title: Ciscomani Hosts Local Faith Leaders to Discuss Strengthening Our Communities
text:
Oro Valley, AZ - U.S. Representative Juan Ciscomani hosted pastors and faith leaders from across Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District, along with their spouses, for a roundtable discussion about the challenges facing their congregations and to explore ways Congress can better support faith-based organizations serving Arizona families.

The discussion focused on strengthening communities through faith-based partnerships, expanding access to affordable housing, improving public safety, and ensuring families feel secure in their places of worship.

"I was honored to welcome pastors and faith leaders from across Arizona’s Sixth District for an important conversation about their organizations and its needs," said Rep. Juan Ciscomani. "Faith-based organizations are often the first to answer the call, providing food, shelter, counseling, and hope to those who need it most. As Arizona’s only appropriator in Congress, I will continue fighting for policies and investments that empower these organizations, strengthen public safety, protect places of worship, and ensure they have the resources to continue their indispensable mission."

As Arizona’s only member of the House or Senate serving on the House Appropriations Committee, Rep. Ciscomani has championed investments that empower faith-based organizations to better serve their communities. During U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Secretary Scott Turner’s recent visit to Arizona’s Sixth District, Rep. Ciscomani reaffirmed his strong support for HUD’s Center for Faith, which partners with faith-based organizations to expand affordable housing opportunities and strengthen local communities.

Faith-based organizations play a vital role in addressing housing needs by partnering with HUD through the Center for Faith. These partnerships help support affordable housing, shelters, community development projects, and the redevelopment of underutilized church property to better serve local families.

The conversation, which took place at Oro Valley Church of the Nazarene, also highlighted the importance of protecting houses of worship and ensuring faith-based organizations have the resources they need to keep their congregations safe. As part of this year’s appropriations process, Rep. Ciscomani successfully championed increased funding for the Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP), which helps nonprofit organizations at high risk of terrorist attacks strengthen physical security through infrastructure improvements, security enhancements, and emergency preparedness. The program also fosters greater coordination between nonprofit organizations and state and local agencies to safeguard communities and better protect places of worship.

"We are grateful to Congressman Ciscomani for bringing faith leaders together and creating an opportunity for meaningful dialogue on the issues that matter most to our congregations and communities," said Pastor Eli Moreno. “The Congressman’s willingness to listen and work alongside local pastors reflects a genuine commitment to strengthening families, supporting faith-based organizations, and advancing solutions that will have a lasting impact across Southern Arizona."

"Faith communities are uniquely positioned to meet people where they are, offering compassion, hope, and practical support during life’s most difficult moments," said Pastor Craig Coulter. "We truly appreciate Congressman Ciscomani’s leadership in recognizing the vital role churches play in strengthening our communities and his commitment to protecting religious liberty, enhancing the safety of our places of worship, and partnering with those who serve others every day."

title: Congressman Cleaver Sounds the Alarm Regarding Potential Closure of Missouri Farm Service Agency Offices
text:
(Washington, D.C.) – Today, U.S. Representative Emanuel Cleaver, II (D-MO) raised concerns about plans to close or reduce services at Farm Service Agency offices throughout the state of Missouri. In a letter to Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins, Congressman Cleaver highlighted the significant challenges confronting American farmers and demanded answers regarding the extent to which FSA operations will be scaled back across the state.

Employing over 460,000 people, agriculture remains Missouri’s number one industry, with soybeans and corn representing the state’s top commodities. Notably, Missouri is home to nearly 88,000 farms, which account for 66% of the state’s total land use. Over the last two years, however, the USDA reports that profit margins for U.S. soybeans and corn have been negative, all while the costs of fertilizer, fuel, seeds, labor, and equipment maintenance have skyrocketed. Moreover, according to a February report from the American Farm Bureau Federation, Chapter 12 farm bankruptcies surged by 46% in 2025, the second consecutive year of increased bankruptcies.

“American farmers are facing an economic crisis that’s made it nearly impossible for many of them to continue producing crops or raising livestock,” said Congressman Cleaver. “The Midwest led the nation last year in the number of farmers declaring Chapter 12 bankruptcy, and Missouri alone saw sixteen farms reach that point in 2025. When you factor in all the families who don’t qualify for Chapter 12, the picture becomes even more dire. Given the current situation, it makes absolutely no sense for the USDA to start unexpectedly closing and reducing services at FSA County Offices. In many respects, the wellbeing of this country depends upon the wellbeing of our farmers, and we know for a fact that Missouri farmers are struggling right now. The FSA is a lifeline to programs needed to keep midwestern farms afloat,” Congressman Cleaver continued, “and reducing the agency’s presence in this state will add yet another burden to the long list of challenges that Missouri farmers are dealing with right now. Closing the local FSA office at a time like the present is akin to kicking our farmers when they’re down.”

Currently operating 97 County Offices across the state of Missouri, the FSA assists farmers with disaster relief, crop insurance, loans, and income support programs. Congressman Cleaver was recently notified that the USDA intends to close or reduce services at several Missouri FSA County Offices starting on October 1, 2026. Early reports indicate that a number of offices will begin operating on an appointment-only basis, while other offices will see their dedicated staff transferred to other locations.

In addition to emphasizing the profound hardships that farmers have faced in recent years, Congressman Cleaver requested additional information regarding the following:

The number of FSA offices slated for closure between now and the end of the next fiscal year (September 30, 2027).

The locations of the proposed office closures.

The date(s) by which the FSA County Offices in question will cease operations.

The extent to office closures will be done in conjunction with FSA staff reductions.

The locations of FSA County Offices that will become open by appointment only.

The offices to which staff will be transferred if their original places of employment are closed.

The plans in place to ensure that FSA programs continue to be administered without delay.

title: Congress Members Introduce Bills to Support Corpus Christi Army Depot
text:
Bills in Congress could benefit Corpus Christi Army Depot

Corpus Christi Caller Times

Olivia Garrett | August 10th, 2026

Three members of the U.S. Congress representing the Coastal Bend have joined to introduce a bill to improve funding transparency for installations like the Corpus Christi Army Depot.

U.S. Rep. Michael Cloud, Sen. John Cornyn, Rep. Vicente Gonzalez and Sen. John Fetterman introduced the bipartisan, bicameral Depot Data Transparency Act. Cloud, Cornyn and Gonzalez all represent the Coastal Bend. Fetterman is from Pennsylvania.

Over the past decade, the civilian workforce and workload at the Corpus Christi Army Depot has shrunk, alarming community and military leaders concerned about the impact on the local economy, as well as national defense and strategic resiliency.

“Over the past decade, Corpus Christi Army Depot’s highly-trained civilian workforce has dropped by thousands due to the Army’s increasing reliance on private companies for helicopter repair work,” Gonzalez said in a news release. “This is a federal issue hurting depots across the country and requires a federal solution; it starts with bringing greater transparency to the Army’s maintenance and overhaul schedule.

“Our bill builds on bipartisan language we secured in the House-passed National Defense Authorization Act, and would ensure we protect South Texas’s military competitiveness and the thousands of workers it employs.”

If made law, the Depot Data Transparency Act would require the U.S. Department of Defense to submit annual reports for military installations detailing how maintenance and repair work is divided between private companies and military depots.

Another bill, the DEPOTS Act, would authorize the U.S. secretary of defense to use surpluses to write off internal Department of Defense debts affecting depots because of planned government work that has been canceled. This would not apply to payments owed to commercial contractors.

“Texas’ two extraordinary Organic Industrial Base sites, the Corpus Christi and Red River Army Depots, make immeasurable, ongoing contributions to our nation’s defense readiness, from remanufacturing and sustaining rotary-wing aircraft to remanufacturing and overhauling tactical wheeled vehicles,” Cornyn said in a news release. “We must provide budgetary flexibility so they are not hampered by financial losses from cancelled government work.”

“The DEPOTS Act is a commonsense flexibility for a real problem,” Cloud said in a news release. “Depots shouldn’t face the adverse effects alone due to mission changes by the Department of War and Congress. Corpus Christi Army Depot does critical work keeping our service members’ aircraft safe and reliable, and this practical reform keeps our Army’s and the nation’s rotary aircraft operational and, in the fight.”

Cornyn and Gonzalez visited the Corpus Christi Army Depot in March with Army Under Secretary Mike Obadal, local leaders and a representative from Cloud’s office.

title: Crow Celebrates Opening of Project Worthmore’s Roots Community Hub
text:
AURORA — Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO) and leaders from Project Worthmore opened the new Roots Community Hub in Aurora, a center that provides resources to new immigrant and refugee families. Congressman Crow secured $4 million in federal Community Project Funds that helped ensure necessary renovations to the building and allowed Project Worthmore to expand the programs and resources they offer.

Project Worthmore has been serving Coloradans since 2011. They offer services to help immigrant families find jobs, healthcare, and education; navigate public benefits; learn English; and access food, legal counsel, and medical care.

“We are a community of immigrants and refugees,” Congressman Crow said at the ribbon-cutting. “About 20 percent of the people that I represent were born outside of the United States. We have over 130 languages spoken in this community. It makes us one of the most diverse communities in the nation, and it makes us stronger. It makes us more vibrant, it makes us more prosperous, and it makes us the wonderful, beautiful place that we call home and that we are so proud of. I will never back down from telling the story to this country and to the world about what the community of Aurora, Colorado, really is and really looks like, and who we are.”

“Part of that is a recognition of the very difficult time that we are in and we will continue to be in for the foreseeable future,” Crow continued. “People will come at our community. They will attack us. They will try to tear us apart. They will target the immigrant and refugee community. And my message to those folks is that we will not let them do that. We protect our own in this community, and if you're going to come at our families, you're going to have to come through all of us to do that. I will fight like hell to protect this community, and to protect the folks who are here today, and to protect the folks who aren't here today. We will not let them get at our community.”

Congressman Crow has led efforts to support and protect the immigrant community in Aurora and across Colorado. That includes fighting back against mass deportation campaigns for immigrants and suing the Trump Administration when they tried to block his oversight of federal immigration detention centers. He previously introduced bipartisan legislation guaranteeing Members of Congress the right to conduct unannounced, in-person oversight visits of ICE detention facilities. He has also led the charge calling for the end to private for profit immigration detention facilities. Since 2019, Crow and his staff have visited the GEO facility in Aurora more than 100 times to conduct oversight. Public reports of such visits, along with conditions at the facility, are published on Crow’s website.

title: Dingell, Kim Introduce Bill to Include Long-Term Care as Part of Medicare
text:
U.S. Representative Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) and U.S. Senator Andy Kim (D-NJ) introduced bicameral legislation to establish long-term care services benefits as part of the Medicare program. The Medicare At Home Act would help older adults and people with disabilities remain safely in their homes and communities by expanding home care coverage under Medicare Part B. Medicare Part B usually covers doctor visits and everyday medical care; this bill would also cover in-home support so people don't have to leave their homes.

Currently, Medicare does not cover long-term care at home. As a result, families across the country face staggering out-of-pocket expenses, forcing many to deplete their savings to qualify for Medicaid or rely heavily on unpaid family caregivers. The Medicare At Home Act eliminates these financial barriers by making home-based care an accessible, affordable part of Medicare coverage.

"Whether seniors are aging at home or individuals with disabilities need daily support, care should be accessible and affordable. This bill gives families peace of mind by ensuring Medicare covers the essential in-home support people need to live with independence and dignity. It is a common-sense solution that makes care more affordable for people on Medicare," said Congresswoman Dingell.

The Medicare At Home Act:

Expands Medicare Coverage: Adds comprehensive home-based personal care benefits to Medicare Part B.

Lowers Financial Burden: Eliminates the need for families to drain life savings or go into debt for basic home care support.

Keeps People in Their Homes: Gives older adults and people with disabilities the choice to remain in their homes and communities.

“Whether it was his last few months living alone in his own place or now at a care facility, my top priority is making sure my dad can live with dignity and comfort. Like so many Americans though, too often that question becomes what care we can afford. Whether seniors are aging at home or elsewhere, this bill gives them and their families the options they deserve by making home care an affordable and accessible option everywhere. These moments of life are hard enough without having to worry about cost,” said Senator Kim.

Endorsing organizations include the Service Employees International Union (SEIU), Caring Across Generations, Justice in Aging, Allies for Independence, National Domestic Workers Alliance, Care in Action, and LeadingAge.

“The Medicare at Home Act finally closes the gap between what people believe Medicare covers and what it actually does, and does it in a way families will feel immediately. Right now, needing help at home means paying out of pocket at costs that can top $60,000 a year, spending down into poverty to qualify for Medicaid, or leaving a family member to do it all unpaid. This bill changes that calculus. The supports from this bill will allow older adults and disabled people to stay safely in their own homes and communities, which is exactly what they’ve told us they want. This isn’t a fringe idea: 93 percent of adults believe Medicare should cover home care, and most already assume it does. The Medicare at Home Act makes the policy match that expectation,” said Nicole Jorwic, Chief Program Officer, Caring Across Generations.

“Long-term care is one of the most significant expenses older adults and their families face. Yet, Medicare does not provide a comprehensive, accessible home care benefit. As a result, far too many older adults are forced to spend down their savings and fall into poverty to access essential care. Justice in Aging proudly supports the Medicare at Home Act because it would help older adults get the assistance they need with daily activities before they experience financial hardship, allowing them to age with dignity and independence,” said Natalie Kean, Managing Director of Health Advocacy at Justice in Aging.

"LeadingAge applauds Congresswoman Dingell and Senator Kim's longstanding leadership in advancing access to care in the home and community. The Medicare at Home Act sets an agenda and important focus for the future by expanding Medicare coverage to include personal care services in the home–a critical need that many older adults and families mistakenly assume is paid for by the current Medicare benefit. We look forward to working with Congresswoman Dingell and Senator Kim to address this shortcoming in access and affordability while also ensuring our nonprofit and mission-driven members are equipped to deliver high-quality care wherever people call home," said Katie Smith Sloan, President and CEO of LeadingAge.

"Home care is essential to families of all backgrounds, our healthcare system, and our economy. Integrating long-term home care into Medicare ensures that seniors and people with disabilities can age safely at home without shouldering the immense financial burden on their own. A federal investment in home care can help transform these lifesaving jobs into good jobs that workers can afford to keep. We are proud to support this legislation from Senator Kim and Congresswoman Dingell, which would help make quality home care more accessible for those who need it,” said Leslie Frane, SEIU Executive Vice President.

“The need for long term services and supports (LTSS) in the home has been a discussion for far too long in this country. Finally, we have a leader willing to address the issue by supporting individuals with functional limitations to be the best they can be in their homes and communities," said Connie Garner, Executive Director, Allies for Independence.

title: DelBene Delivers $500,000 for Bellevue Wastewater Improvement Project
text:
Today, Congresswoman Suzan DelBene (WA-01) delivered a $500,000 ceremonial check to the City of Bellevue to replace old pipes and upgrade the wastewater management system along Lake Washington. DelBene secured the investment in the FY26 federal funding law.

This federal investment will be dedicated to the Lake Washington Sanitary Sewer Lines Program. First installed in the 1950s and 1960s, the wastewater management system’s pipes are aging and need to be updated. They currently serve approximately 1,900 residents in the Hunts Point, Yarrow Point, Evergreen Point, Medina South, Meydenbauer Bay, Killarney and Newport South areas. Without repairs and modernization, the “Lake Lines” will begin to fail and could release raw sewage into Lake Washington. This federal funding will aid the City of Bellevue in developing a plan to manage and update the system, which will protect public health and the local ecosystem.

“Lake Lines serve 1,900 members of our community, but the aging pipes’ location along the shoreline and in Lake Washington create challenges for upgrades,” said DelBene. “Bellevue has worked tirelessly to come up with a strategy to update these pipes to preserve access, protect public health, and avoid harm to Lake Washington. This funding will make a difference in the development and eventual implementation of this critical project.”

“Most people never think about the sewer lines running along Lake Washington - and that’s a good thing. But some of this infrastructure has been serving Bellevue since the 1950s and 60s, and now it is our responsibility to plan for what comes next,” said Bellevue Mayor Mo Malakoutian. “We are grateful to Congresswoman DelBene for helping secure this federal investment and for recognizing that a $1.2 billion challenge will require continued partnership. This funding helps us start that work now, protect Lake Washington and plan responsibly for the generations that will depend on it.”

DelBene secured over $22.2 million for 15 community projects across Washington’s 1st Congressional District in the FY26 federal funding package. Only non-profit, city, county, and Tribal entities are permitted to receive funding.

title: Evans Introduces Bill to Build More Accessible, Affordable Housing
text:
PHILADELPHIA (Aug. 10, 2026) – U.S. Rep. Dwight Evans (D-PA-3) introduced the Visitable Inclusive Tax Credits for Accessible Living (VITAL) Act to strengthen the Low Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) to expand the supply of affordable, accessible housing for older adults and people with disabilities.

Evans’ lead House co-sponsor is Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA-1), and U.S. Sens. Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) and Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), ranking member of the Senate Special Committee on Aging, introduced companion legislation in the Senate.

Evans said, “About 26 percent of people in the United States have a disability, yet less than 6 percent of the national housing supply is designed to be accessible at even a basic level. This bill would change that by expanding low-income housing tax credits to make affordable housing more accessible for seniors and people with disabilities. The need for accessible housing will only continue to grow as America’s senior population grows! I want to thank Congressman Fitzpatrick and Senators Klobuchar and Gillibrand for partnering on this much-needed bill.”

“As we work to increase housing supply and make homes more affordable, we must also build with the needs of our seniors and Americans with disabilities in mind. The VITAL Act uses the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit to promote accessible, adaptable homes in communities connected to transportation and essential services. This legislation reflects the kind of housing policy I will always champion — one that strengthens independence, expands opportunity, and helps every person live with dignity,” Fitzpatrick said.

“For far too many Americans living with disabilities and older adults with mobility issues, safe housing is out of reach due to a lack of affordable and accessible options,” Klobuchar said. “This legislation would increase the number of new homes that are located in walkable or wheelchair-friendly communities to increase access to housing for all.”

“As our aging population continues to grow, it is critical that we invest in affordable housing units with accessible features,” Gillibrand said. “The VITAL Act would help ensure that affordable housing meets the mobility and accessibility needs of New York seniors and people with disabilities, allowing them to age comfortably in the communities of their choice. As the top Democrat on the Senate Aging Committee, I am proud to lead this bill, and I encourage my colleagues to support it.”

The LIHTC is a federal program providing tax credits to developers who build new housing for low-income renters. The VITAL Act would increase state LIHTC allocations, provide an enhanced tax credit for qualifying affordable housing developments that include accessible units for people with disabilities in walkable communities, and incentivize state housing finance agencies to prioritize the development of more accessible housing.

The VITAL Act is endorsed by The Kelsey, LeadingAge, Pathways to Housing PA, TriageCancer, National Low Income Housing Coalition, Liberty Housing Development Corporation, National Council on Independent Living, National Disability Rights Network, Autistic Self Advocacy Network, The Arc of the United States, Disability Rights Education & Defense Fund, Justice in Aging, National Housing Law Project, National Council on Aging, National Association of Councils on Developmental Disabilities, Association of Assistive Technology Act Programs, Muscular Dystrophy Association, National NeighborWorks Association, Paralyzed Veterans of America, TASH, ANCOR, Bazelon Center for Mental Health Law, The Amputee Coalition, Christopher & Dana Reeve Foundation, Colorado Cross-Disability Coalition, YIMBY Action, Disability Empowerment Center of Lancaster PA, American Foundation of the Blind, America Walks, National Homelessness Law Center, Caring Across Generations, National Association of the Deaf, Community Solutions, Center for Law and Social Policy (CLASP), American Council of the Blind, HDC MidAtlantic, New Disabled South, and Autism Speaks.

title: Fitzpatrick, Ukraine Caucus Co-Chairs, McCaul Lead Bipartisan Sanctions Effort to Cut Off the Lifelines Sustaining Putin’s War
text:
Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act targets Russia’s banks, energy revenues, shadow fleet, and global enablers while strengthening the path to a just and lasting peace

WASHINGTON – Today, Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-1), Co-Chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus and a longtime leader in Congress on Ukraine and confronting Russian aggression, introduced the bipartisan Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, a comprehensive sanctions package designed to strike at the financial architecture sustaining Vladimir Putin’s war against Ukraine, hold accountable the governments and institutions enabling his aggression, and strengthen the leverage necessary to secure a just and lasting peace.

Named in honor of the late Senator Lindsey Graham, the legislation carries forward more than a year of bipartisan work to deprive Putin of the resources necessary to sustain his war and increase the economic and strategic pressure required to bring it to an end.

Additional co-sponsors include House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Emeritus Michael McCaul (R-Texas), Congressman Steny Hoyer (D-Md.) fellow Congressional Ukraine Caucus Co-Chairs Joe Wilson (R-SC) and Marcy Kaptur (D-OH), House Baltic Caucus Co-Chair Don Bacon (R-NE), House Armed Services Committee Chairman Mike Rogers (R-AL), and Representatives Jake Auchincloss (D-MA), Jill Tokuda (D-HI), Mike Turner (R-OH), Gabe Vasquez (D-NM), Ann Wagner (R-MO), Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ), Andy Barr (R-KY), Ed Case (D-HI), Eugene Vindman (D-VA), Nathaniel Moran (R-TX), and Chrissy Houlahan (D-PA).

“Senator Graham believed, as I do, that American strength remains the surest guardian of peace,” said Fitzpatrick. “That conviction guided our work together on this legislation. Putin’s war machine runs on oil, money, and the willingness of others to look the other way—and the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 attacks all three. It isolates Russia’s banks, shuts down the networks financing its aggression, and forces every government and company enabling this war to make a choice. By increasing the cost of Putin’s war and reducing his ability to sustain it, this legislation strengthens the path to a just and lasting peace—one determined by Ukraine, not imposed by Moscow. The most fitting tribute Congress can offer Lindsey is to finish the work he began, carry forward the cause of freedom he championed, and make clear that America will not reward aggression, subsidize it through indifference, or abandon those defending their sovereign right to live free.”

Earlier this month, an overwhelming bipartisan majority in the Senate voted to pass companion legislation, by a vote of 86-11, led by Sens. Darline Graham (R-S.C.), Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Katie Britt (R-Ala.), Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.), Chair of the Senate Armed Services Committee Roger Wicker (R-Miss.), and Chair of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee Jim Risch (R-Idaho). The text of the House bill is identical to the text that passed the Senate.

“This legislation was deeply important to my brother, Lindsey, and I’m grateful that it has achieved such a wide coalition of support. Lindsey was committed to achieving a peaceful resolution to this war, and I’m confident that these sanctions will pave the way,” said Sen. Darline Graham. “I’m grateful to Rep. McCaul for leading this effort in the House. The Senate came together in a strong, bipartisan fashion to pass the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, and I hope the House of Representatives will do the same. Russia has waged war against Ukraine for far too long, and this bill assists President Trump in his noble efforts to bring it to a close.”

“Representatives McCaul, Hoyer, Wilson, Kaptur, and Fitzpatrick are longtime champions of Ukraine’s cause and I am glad to have them leading our legislation in the House of Representatives. After a massive bipartisan vote in the Senate, we are eager to turn to the House as we fight to get this legislation across the finish line. There is immense urgency in getting this done – July set a record for Russia’s use of ballistic missiles, killing and wounding dozens of Ukrainians, including many children. Cutting off the source of funding – profits from oil and gas – for these deadly weapons and Russia’s war machine is essential to ending the bloodshed,” said Sen. Blumenthal.

The legislation establishes a broad sanctions framework aimed at the principal sources of political, financial, and commercial support sustaining Russia’s war. Among its provisions, the bill would:

Target Russia’s political and economic power structure, including senior Russian officials, oligarchs, entities supporting Russia’s defense industrial base, and foreign actors materially assisting Moscow’s military operations or efforts to undermine Ukraine’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, democratic institutions, and critical infrastructure.

Strike at Russia’s financial system, including sanctions against major Russian financial institutions and certain foreign financial institutions conducting significant transactions with sanctioned Russian banks.

Disrupt Russia’s shadow fleet and sanctions-evasion networks by targeting vessels used to move Russian oil and other sanctioned goods, as well as owners, operators, insurers, ports, and other actors knowingly facilitating those operations.

Restrict Russia’s access to capital and energy investment by prohibiting new U.S. investment in Russia, limiting investment in Russia’s energy sector, prohibiting purchases of Russian sovereign debt, and targeting financial messaging services used to circumvent sanctions.

Increase pressure on Russia’s energy revenues by authorizing duties of up to 500 percent on goods imported from Russia and targeted duties of up to 100 percent on goods from countries that rank among the largest purchasers of Russian-origin crude oil or natural gas or the leading facilitators of Russian oil sanctions evasion.

Preserve critical sanctions authorities against Iran by extending the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996 through 2031.

Importantly, the legislation also establishes a clear standard for lifting Russia-related sanctions. Under the bill, the President may terminate those sanctions only after certifying to Congress that Russia has signed a peace agreement accepted by the free and independent Government of Ukraine and has ceased military hostilities and activities aimed at overthrowing, dismantling, or subverting the Ukrainian government.

“Senator Graham was a national security giant, a statesman of unmatched conviction, and a personal friend and mentor. We shared a fundamental worldview: America is strongest at home when it projects strength abroad. That’s why he fought so hard for this bill, which I promised him months ago I would introduce in the House,” said McCaul. “As President Zelensky told me last month when I visited Ukraine, he is ready for a ceasefire — ready to negotiate, as he has been for years. Putin, on the other hand, consistently defies President Trump and the international community by refusing to come to the table. I can think of no better way to honor Senator Graham’s life and legacy than by passing these tough sanctions, which will help force Putin into negotiations and bring us closer to securing Lindsey’s vision of enduring peace in two critical regions of the world.”

“Democracy is presently under threat from despotism, and Congress must act to defend democracy and help Ukraine defeat Vladimir Putin’s effort to extinguish its liberty and sovereignty. Our legislation goes after multiple sources of Russian war funding, including its oil and gas sectors, shadow fleet, and financial institutions. I’m encouraged that the Senate passed the companion legislation last week with overwhelming support, and I thank former Chairman McCaul for partnering with me to facilitate action by the House. This action has been delayed too long and will, hopefully, accelerate Ukraine’s success and the ending of this war, one that was initiated illegally by Putin and that has resulted in tens of thousands of deaths of Russians and Ukrainians. I hope that we can secure bipartisan consensus in the House and enact a sanctions package that will stem the flow of money to Russia’s war machine and contribute to a Ukrainian victory," said Hoyer.

"Senator Lindsey Graham and I shared the belief that opposing dictators in defense of freedom and liberty is always the right thing to do. War criminal Putin is losing his invasion of sovereign Ukraine and the threat to humanity posed by the Iranian regime is dire. It is time for Congress to give President Trump the strongest tools available to choke off Russia's war machine for the good of mankind and cripple the ability of Tehran to continue sowing chaos in the region and beyond. My friend and colleague worked tirelessly in championing these critical initiatives, and I am grateful to help advance them across the finish line in the House,” said Wilson.

“Dictator Vladimir Putin’s illegal invasion of Ukraine is failing—Ukraine is battering Russian war infrastructure and the Kremlin is losing tens of thousands of troops each month. Now is the time to intensify pressure on Putin through crippling sanctions while surging support for our Ukrainian allies,” said Kaptur. “Putin will not make peace until he is forced to. I have been a supporter of every bipartisan sanctions bill on the table to pressure Russia to end its illegal full-scale invasion, and I am confident that the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 will accomplish that mission. Designed to protect our allies who aid Ukraine while squeezing Putin and the countries that enable his invasion, the sweeping sanctions and targeted tariffs in this bill are the best chance we have to get bipartisan legislation signed into law to hold Russia accountable and achieve peace.”

“Putin’s illegal war is failing, but he will not choose peace until the cost becomes too high for Russia and those helping fund his brutality,” said Bacon. “Senator Lindsey Graham was one of Congress’s clearest voices for Ukraine, understood that Putin only responds to strength, and worked until his final days to advance the toughest sanctions package yet against Russia’s war machine. The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia Act would impose crippling pressure on Russia and those enabling Putin’s aggression, honor Sen. Graham’s commitment to Ukraine’s fight for freedom, and make clear that America stands with Ukraine.”

“Since 2022, I have called on both Biden and Trump to empower Ukraine to win this war through both strikes and sanctions on Russian oil infrastructure. The strikes are finally happening, and with this bill the sanctions are coming,” said Auchincloss.

"I am proud to join in introducing this legislation to sanction Vladimir Putin and his thugs as well as the Iran and its terrorist regime,” said Rogers. “Every dollar denied to Vladimir Putin weakens his war machine. By choking off the oil and gas revenue fueling Russia's aggression, this legislation gives President Trump powerful leverage to force Putin into serious negotiations that deliver a truly lasting peace. Including additional sanctions on Iran is equally critical given the terrorist regime’s continued threats to freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and its role in enabling Russia’s war against Ukraine. This legislation strengthens America’s hand against adversaries who threaten American security, our allies, and global stability.”

"Vladimir Putin and the regime in Tehran are two of the gravest threats to America and our allies. For far too long, they've bankrolled their aggression by selling oil and gas to whoever will buy it,” said Gottheimer. "This bipartisan legislation cuts off those funding streams: holding accountable anyone who fills Putin's war chest as he wages his brutal, illegal war against Ukraine, and choking off the money that fuels Iran's weapons programs and its terror proxies. I was proud to see the Senate pass this bill with an overwhelming, bipartisan majority, and now it's on the House to finish the job. I can think of no better tribute to Senator Lindsey Graham — a national security champion — than enacting the tough sanctions he fought so hard for. Standing up to tyrants isn't a Democratic or Republican issue; it's an American one."

“By targeting the energy revenues and financial networks that fuel Putin’s war machine and enable the Iranian regime’s terrorist activities, this bipartisan legislation strengthens America’s ability to impose real economic consequences on our adversaries,” said Barr. “Senator Graham understood that harnessing America’s full strength from our financial system to our military is essential to deterring aggression, defending our allies, and advancing peace. I’m proud to join my colleagues to help carry forward that legacy.”

“Supporting a strong, free Ukraine is imperative for the national security of our communities here at home. Sanctioning Russia and Putin sends a direct message to the world: the United States will not sit by while brutal regimes bankroll aggression against democratic nations,” said Vindman. “I am proud to be a co-sponsor of this essential legislation. We must continue to escalate the economic pressure on the Kremlin and strengthen our resolve for the Ukrainian people as they fight for their freedom, sovereignty, and security.”

"Russia is perpetrating a war of aggression, and we must keep the pressure on Vladimir Putin. This action is long overdue, but we are finally moving forward with the resolve this moment demands. These sanctions will erode Russia's war machine by cutting off the revenue that funds it. We must hold those who are fueling this war accountable. These sanctions focus on Russia but will also target dangerous Chinese entities which support the Russian defense industrial base. Peace is the goal, and these mechanisms give the President the tools to achieve that goal,” said Moran.

“To end Russia’s unprovoked and deadly invasion of Ukraine, we must enact maximum financial pain on Vladimir Putin and his cronies. I will not stand idly by while countless people are killed due to Putin’s doomed quest to reconstitute the Soviet Union. I am beyond proud to join my colleagues in introducing this sweeping sanctions legislation that will enact severe financial penalties against Putin, his allies, and those who choose to do business with him. The largest war in Europe since World War II must come to an end, and I am confident these measures will accelerate that process. I am also pleased this bill extends the Iran Sanctions Act to ensure all available measures are available to cripple the terrorist Iranian regime. These necessary sanctions are a fitting legacy to honor the late Senator Lindsey Graham, a friend and colleague who continually fought for freedom, democracy, and against tyrannical regimes like Russia and Iran,” said Wagner.

“For more than four years, Ukrainians have courageously defended their freedom against Putin’s brutal invasion. The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act would increase pressure on the Kremlin, hold those supporting its war accountable, and strengthen Ukraine’s position in pursuit of a just peace," said Houlahan. “The bill also extends longstanding sanctions against Iran. Sanctions cannot replace a clear strategy or the President’s obligation to seek congressional authorization for war, but they remain an important diplomatic tool. I am proud to cosponsor this legislation.”

Click here to read full text of the legislation.

Background:

Today’s introduction builds on Fitzpatrick’s broader work to advance a Ukraine policy rooted in peace through strength: sustaining Ukraine’s ability to defend itself, increasing pressure on Putin and those enabling his war, and ensuring that any path to peace protects Ukraine’s sovereignty and is accepted by the free and independent Government of Ukraine.

As Co-Chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus, Fitzpatrick has helped lead bipartisan efforts to hold Russia accountable, informed by his firsthand visits to Ukraine and meetings with the leaders, servicemembers, and civilians confronting Putin’s aggression. From the Peace Through Strength Against Russia Act and the Countering Russia’s War on Faith Act to efforts addressing Russia’s attacks on civilians and abducted Ukrainian children, his work has followed a consistent principle. The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act advances that same strategy by targeting the financial and energy networks sustaining Putin’s war machine and strengthening Ukraine’s position to secure a just and lasting peace.

title: Fong Moves to End California's Hidden Climate Tax on American Consumers
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Last week, Congressman Vince Fong (CA-20) introduced a Congressional Review Act (CRA) resolution to overturn the EPA’s 2023 authorization of amendments to the California's Air Resources Board’s (CARB) At-Berth Regulation. Senator Dan Sullivan (R-AK) is leading an identical Senate companion resolution.

California’s Ocean-Going Vessels At-Berth regulation imposes costly and unworkable mandates on ports, shipping companies, and critical industries, including requirements for technology that is not yet viable. These regulations threaten the reliable operation of California’s refineries, increase the cost of moving goods through our ports, and ultimately drive-up prices for consumers. They also make California’s ports less competitive, putting cargo, jobs, and private investment at risk as businesses look to move operations to states with less burdensome regulations.

This action was instituted in 2020 by CARB, an unelected state agency, and approved by the Biden Administration’s Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) in 2023. The mandate worsens California’s affordability crisis and harms California's fuel supply that is already under severe strain. Additionally, after this EPA authorization, other states across the country may choose to follow in implementing this unfeasible rule which will harm the U.S. economy.

“At a time when California families are already paying the highest gas prices and facing one of the highest costs of living in the nation, the last thing they need is another costly mandate from Sacramento,” said Congressman Vince Fong. “This onerous regulation will increase shipping costs, raise prices for consumers, and put California’s ports, businesses, and workers at a competitive disadvantage. With refinery closures already straining our fuel supply, this unworkable regulation only adds more uncertainty while relying on technology that isn’t ready. We can improve air quality without making California less affordable or driving jobs and investment out of our state.”

“I am glad to partner with Rep. Fong on this effort, because West Coast supply chains don't stop at state lines,” said Senator Sullivan. “When California imposes onerous and costly mandates, hard-working Alaskan families pay the price. Nearly half of Alaska’s crude oil is processed in California refineries. By restricting which ships can call at its ports and driving up operating costs for those that do, California is artificially inflating costs across our entire region. Alaskans shouldn't be forced to foot the bill for California’s abuse of its Clean Air Act waiver authority.”

Background

California ports handle roughly 40% of the nation's containerized imports, meaning California’s regulation on docked vessels doesn't just affect California. It raises costs for consumers in all 50 states.

The CARB At-Berth Regulation requires ocean-going vessels docked at California ports to cut diesel emissions by plugging into the electrical grid, installing state-approved technology, or paying into a state remediation fund. Ships that cannot comply face penalties of approximately $50,000 per vessel per day. Those costs are passed onto freight rates, wholesale prices, and ultimately what consumers pay at checkout.

The Biden Administration's EPA authorized CARB to expand this regulation to ocean-going tankers in October 2023 without submitting it to Congress for review. The Congressional Review Act gives Congress the authority to nullify that authorization with a majority vote. Congress used this exact mechanism last year to strike down three EPA waivers behind California's electric vehicle mandates.

"We applaud Representative Fong for leading this effort to overturn California's Ocean-Going Vessels at Berth mandate. California ports handle roughly 40% of U.S. containerized imports and significant volumes of crude oil and refined fuels. As a result, the costs of this mandate would ripple through supply chains and energy markets, raising prices for American families and consumers. Congress must act to stop California from imposing unlawful, unachievable policies that raise costs for every American and threaten U.S. energy security along our coasts," said Chet Thompson, American Fuel & Petrochemical Manufacturers (AFPM) President and CEO.

“California should not be allowed to make an already constrained West Coast energy market more costly and less reliable,” said Kristin Whitman, Senior Vice President of Federal Relations, American Petroleum Institute. “By imposing burdensome new requirements on maritime operators, this rule threatens to disrupt the integrated supply chain that moves crude and other vital energy supplies through the region. We welcome Congressman Vince Fong’s resolution to overturn this misguided mandate and protect consumers from further supply constraints and higher costs.”

“For years, CARB’s At-Berth Regulation has created significant challenges and uncertainty for California refiners and importers at a time when stabilizing the industry is a top priority,” said Jodie Muller, President and CEO, Western States Petroleum Association (WSPA). “Policymakers and regulators have been unable to solve the many problems related to the At-Berth Regulation and Congress has decided that it is time to move forward. California consumers should not have to bear the brunt of a further constrained fuel supply.”

“Manufacturers strongly support the introduction of H.J.Res.210 by Rep. Vince Fong to nullify the At-Berth Rule,” said Chris Phalen, Vice President of Domestic Policy, National Association of Manufacturers. “The rule injected needless uncertainty into the regulatory process by granting a federal waiver for this sweeping state regulation. A patchwork of conflicting state laws drives up costs and undermines manufacturing growth across America, and we welcome this legislation to ensure a more straightforward, standardized regulatory process.”

Rep. Fong’s CRA is endorsed by the American Fuel & Petrochemical Manufacturers (AFPM), American Petroleum Institute (API), Western States Petroleum Association (WSPA), and National Association of Manufacturers (NAM).

title: Goodlander and Bicameral Group of Lawmakers Slam Trump Admin Efforts to Deport Military Families
text:
Senate investigation revealed ICE has attempted to deport 282 veterans and their relatives; could be violating law that prevents the use of military against civilians

Washington, D.C. — Congresswomen Maggie Goodlander (D-N.H.), Chrissy Houlahan (D-Pa.), Delia Ramirez (D-Ill.), and Lizzie Fletcher (D-Texas), along with U.S. Senators Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), and Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) led dozens of their colleagues in a bicameral letter pressing the Trump administration on its efforts to coordinate the arrest, detention and deportation of hundreds of veterans and military families.

The letter follows an April 2025 move from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to rescind its long-standing policy that treated military service a “significant mitigating factor” when deciding whether to pursue immigration enforcement, replacing it with a new policy stating that military service alone “does not automatically exempt” non-citizens from enforcement actions.

You can read the full letter and list of signers here.

“These efforts imperil military readiness, weaken service members’ morale, and betray America’s promises to the people who put their lives on the line for our nation,” write the lawmakers.

Alarmingly, DoD has been reportedly targeting individuals at military installations, detaining them on military property, and turning them over to ICE — effectively converting military bases into “traps” for noncitizens. For example, a 22-year-old military wife was recently detained while attempting to obtain a military spouse I.D. Military officials allegedly called DHS and held her in a room until ICE agents arrived to take her to a detention center.

The lawmakers continue, “DoD’s participation in civil immigration enforcement activities raises both ethical and legal concerns, including potential violations of the Posse Comitatus Act, which prohibits using the armed forces of the military for civilian law enforcement.”

A 2025 investigation revealed that ICE has attempted to deport 282 veterans and their relatives. DHS refused to disclose the number of active-duty troops and their families who have been threatened by the administration’s policy. But new reports indicate that DoD and DHS appear to be coordinating to convert military bases into “traps” for individuals this administration deems deportable and has detained non-citizens during routine check-ins, visits, and drop-offs at or near military installations. At the same time, DoD has continued to recruit new service members with the promise of immigration protections.

Recent reporting by the Associated Press reveals that, since January 2025, more than 50 parents and spouses of active-duty service members have been detained, and at least six have been deported. ICE’s statistics show that the agency has arrested 16 non-citizen armed forces members since the beginning of Fiscal Year 2026. Some service members have reportedly needed to take leave or delay deployment because ICE detained their families.

The coalition warned that if service members were to be swept up in any of these enforcement actions, it could separately constitute a violation of the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, which provides protections to all members of the United States military on active duty, including non-citizens, from civil actions—such as immigration proceedings—that interfere with their military duties.

“Service members must have confidence that their sacrifices will be honored, not used against them or to target their loved ones,” wrote the lawmakers. “DoD’s new anti-immigrant practices risk deterring future recruits and damaging the credibility of military recruitment efforts—which promised to care for service members even after their time in uniform.”

The lawmakers requested that the agencies explain the enhanced coordination between DoD and DHS, restore long-standing immigration protections for family members of service members, and explain what steps they are taking to protect troops, veterans, and their families from unjust immigration enforcement by August 23, 2026.

The letter was endorsed by the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), Immigration Defenders Law Center, the Seattle Clemency Project, Common Defense, Repatriate Our Patriots, and League of United Latin American Citizens.

“It is hard to imagine a more profound betrayal than targeting service members, veterans, and military families for deportation,” said Jennie Pasquarella, interim executive director of the Seattle Clemency Project. “This administration is abandoning decades of bipartisan policies that recognized a simple truth: protecting those who serve makes our military stronger and our nation safer. Targeting the very communities that have sacrificed for this country is not just morally indefensible, it is a direct attack on military readiness, recruitment, and trust.”

“This administration has made a conscious decision to abandon its promises to military families and fail those who put their lives on the line for our nation,” said Amanda Schuft, director of legal services at Immigrant Defenders Law Center. “We have seen the devastating human cost firsthand. Our client, the father of an active-duty Army service member, was detained by ICE despite suffering from terminal renal failure, forcing his son to take leave from military service to plead for his release and provide evidence of his grave medical condition. The government ignored those pleas. After his health deteriorated in detention, our client was eventually released, only to die within weeks.”

“Family readiness directly impacts mission readiness. Behind every military spouse or parent in detention is a servicemember who could deploy at any moment. Without a strong homefront, we cannot have a ready force. Our government must honor its commitments to those who serve,” said Danitza G. James, MSW, President, Repatriate Our Patriots.

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Hosts Roundtable, Claws Back More Than $1 Million in Federal Resources to Help Stop Domestic & Community Violence in North Jersey
text:
Above: Gottheimer announces funding to help stop violence in North Jersey.

HACKENSACK, NJ — Today, August 10, 2026, U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) hosted a roundtable at Bergen’s Promise in Hackensack with leaders from Hackensack Meridian Health (HMH), law enforcement, local elected officials, and community stakeholders to discuss domestic violence, shootings, stabbings, and other forms of community violence, and the expansion of hospital-based violence intervention services in Bergen County. Gottheimer clawed back more than $1 million in federal resources to expand HUMC’s Community Health Worker Violence Intervention Program (HVIP). The roundtable discussion focused on the expansion of the program, how the federal funding will expand services for victims and their families, and how it will help reduce community violence in North Jersey.

Watch Gottheimer’s announcement here.

“Keeping Jersey families safe is about as common sense and bipartisan as it gets — and it starts with making sure our hospitals and communities have the tools they need to break the cycle of violence,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “This is exactly the kind of partnership between the federal government, our hospitals, and our community organizations that actually gets things done for people. I’m proud to have fought for this funding. I’m proud it’s coming back to Bergen County where it belongs, and I’m ready to work with all of you to make sure this program succeeds.”

“Community violence isn’t just a public safety issue – it is a public health crisis. At Hackensack Meridian Health, we see the real-world impact of this every day, which is why we are building out our community health worker violence intervention program. By reaching people where they are and providing trauma-informed support, our goal is to break the cycle of violence before it repeats. I want to thank Congressman Gottheimer for pulling this group together. Real, lasting safety happens when healthcare systems, law enforcement, and local advocates sit at the same table and tackle this together,” said Dr. Nicole Harris-Hollingsworth, SVP, Social Impact and Population Health at Hackensack Meridian Health.

Hospital-based violence intervention programs (HVIPs) are multidisciplinary programs that identify patients at risk of repeat violent injury and connect them with hospital and community-based services to support recovery, address underlying risk factors, and work to reduce future victimization. HVIPs begin working with patients while they are still in the emergency department or hospital, then provide intensive community-based case management and support in the months following an injury.

From 2021 through 2026, Hackensack University Medical Center in Bergen County treated almost 3,000 victims of shootings, stabbings, beatings, and domestic violence — accounting for roughly 25 percent of the more than 11,400 violence victims treated across the entire Hackensack Meridian Health network in New Jersey. And these violence intervention programs work: just 5 percent of victims who participate are rehospitalized for another violent injury, compared with 36 percent of those who do not.

The federal funding clawed back by Gottheimer will support trained professionals, technology and supplies, and transportation costs needed to serve victims and families across North Jersey.

Gottheimer was joined by Bergen County Sheriff Anthony Cureton; Bergen County Prosecutor Mark Musella; Bergen County Commissioner Steven A. Tanelli; Dr. Nicole Harris-Hollingsworth, SVP Social Impact and Population Health, HMH; Ms. Sarah Lechner, SVP Chief of External Affairs, HMH; Ms. Leslie Eaddy, Manager, Social Impact and Population Health, HMH; Ms. Angelica Santomauro, Community Health Worker, Social Impact and Population Health, HMH; Ms. Katelyn Segilia, Supervisor, Social Impact and Population Health, HMH; Ms. Omna Syed, Manager, Government Relations, HMH; Dr. Abby Lowe, Assistant Director of Quality, Department of Emergency Medicine, HMH; Dr. Aakash Shah, Program Director, Violence Intervention Programs, HMH; Melissa DeBartolo, Director, Bergen County Department of Human Services; Mr. Dean Paskas, CEO, Bergen’s Promise; Shelisa Foster, Chief Operating Officer, Bergen’s Promise; Ms. Kathryn Werheim, Director of Community Resources, Bergen’s Promise; Ms. Shekinah Williams, Youth Justice Operations Manager, Bergen’s Promise; Ms. Jacqueline Yeboah, Behavioral Health Home Nurse Manager, Bergen’s Promise; Ms. Kelly Kopec, Health Promotion Manager, Bergen’s Promise; Mr. Jacques Hryshko, CEO, Family Connections; Dr. Amanda Santana, COO, Family Connections; Ms. Latisha Miller, Program Coordinator, Family Connections; Ms. Lil Corcoran, CEO, Women’s Rights Information Center; Ms. Lisa Maurer, Associate Executive Director, Women’s Rights Information Center; Ms. Dania Hochberg, Licensed Associate Counselor, Women’s Rights Information Center; Mr. William Salcedo, CEO, Big Brothers Big Sisters of Coastal and Northern New Jersey; Ms. Shannon Orefice, Director of Programs, Big Brothers Big Sisters of Coastal and Northern New Jersey; Ms. Helen Archontou, CEO, YWCA Northern New Jersey; Ms. Monique Joseph, Health Equity Specialist, YWCA Northern New Jersey; Ms. Simaza Sadek, Program Director of healingSPACE, YWCA Northern New Jersey; Ms. Kristine Pendy, CEO, Center for Hope and Safety; Beth Ostuni, Deputy Director of the Division of Alternatives to Domestic Violence; and Kate Gerathy, Advocacy Coordinator, Division of Alternatives to Domestic Violence.

Below: Gottheimer hosts roundtable to help stop violence in North Jersey.

Gottheimer’s remarks as prepared for delivery:

Thank you so much, everybody, for being here today. And a special thank you to the whole team at Hackensack Meridian Health for helping organize today’s discussion, and to Bergen’s Promise for opening up your doors and hosting us. For those of you who don’t know, Bergen’s Promise is a nonprofit that connects children and families with critical mental health, behavioral health, and other support services. We are all very grateful for them.

I want to start by saying how thankful I am to sit down with the people doing this work every single day. The best ideas often don’t come from Washington — they come from the people on the front lines. The doctors, the community health workers, the folks who see community violence up close. You understand these challenges better than most around the country because you’re helping patients and families during some of the most difficult moments of their lives. Let’s talk about why we’re here.

Hackensack University Medical Center is one of the busiest and best hospitals in the state of New Jersey and the country.

In fact, it was just recognized once again by U.S. News & World Report as the number one hospital in New Jersey — a testament to the outstanding care and leadership right here in Bergen County. You provide that top-notch care at your facilities across our great state.

But even one of the nation’s top hospitals, in the ninth safest county in the country, sees the devastating impact of community violence every day. Between 2021 and 2024, Hackensack in Bergen County alone treated more than 2,100 victims of violence — people who came through your doors after shootings, stabbings, and beatings.

In other words, nearly one-quarter of all violence victims treated at HUMC hospitals statewide were treated right here in Bergen County. The bottom line: we are not immune from violence.

Now, the good news: violent crime is down nationally, and it’s down in Jersey. Across the country, violent crime dropped by 5.6 percent this year, and here in New Jersey, violent crime is down more than 16 percent. Two Bergen County communities — Emerson and Allendale — were named among the top ten safest in the entire country.

That’s real progress, and law enforcement and community organizations across Bergen County deserve a lot of credit for helping make our communities safer. As a side note, I also proudly represent most of Sussex County, which is also one of the safest counties in America, with Vernon Township, which has been ranked the safest municipality in our state for three years running. Some of the towns I represent in Passaic County — Ringwood and Wanaque — are always recognized as among the safest, too.

But here’s the thing. Even with crime on the decline, we still have thousands of people walking through the doors of HUMC every year who are victims of violent crime, whether that’s a gunshot wound, a stabbing, or domestic violence. Across the country, more than 44,000 Americans are killed by gun violence every year, and nearly 97,000 more are shot and wounded. In New Jersey, in 2024, 778 people were shot — that’s more than two people every day. Nationally, unintentional and violence-related injuries still cause more than 300,000 deaths a year.

So, the question isn’t whether we’ve made progress. The question is what we do for the people who are still walking through that emergency room door today, and how we stop them from walking back through it again.

That’s what this program is about.

We know that if you were treated for a violent injury once, you are at a much higher risk of being injured again. It’s called repeat victimization, and it’s one of the most frustrating cycles in public health. Hospitals see the same patients come back, again and again. Intervention works — if there is intervention, we see only 5% of victims rehospitalized versus 36% who do not receive these services.

So, the question is: what can you do about it? How do you help break the cycle of violence? Well, that’s why we are here today.

Working closely with Hackensack University Medical Center, I helped claw back more than a million dollars from Washington to Jersey for a new, federally-funded hospital-based violence intervention program, or an HVIP, here in Hackensack. This is a big deal.

HVIPs aren’t new to other hospitals in our state or to Hackensack’s hospitals — but they’ll be new to Hackensack Medical in Bergen County.

With an HVIP, instead of just stitching someone up and sending them back out the door, doctors, nurses, and trained community health workers will meet them right in the emergency department, at their bedside, in the moments immediately after an act of violence, when they’re most vulnerable and most open to accepting help and changing the course of their lives. Hospitals are uniquely positioned to do this work because they’re often the first place victims receive care after experiencing violence.

By connecting patients with support at these critical moments, hospital-based violence intervention programs play a key role in breaking the cycle of repeat victimization before it starts again.

HVIPs work. Since 2021, Project HEAL at Jersey Shore University Medical Center has used this approach in Monmouth and Ocean Counties, and it’s made a real difference. It has helped hundreds of victims of violence access counseling, emergency assistance, transportation, legal services, and other resources that reduce the likelihood of future violence.

What we’re talking about today is bringing that same proven model here to North Jersey, where it’s needed just as much.

Here’s how it works. This funding adds twelve community health workers through the hospital across Bergen County, plus a team leader to coordinate the whole effort. These aren’t bureaucrats. These are trusted, competent, trained professionals — many of them from the very same communities they’re serving — who go to a patient’s bedside, build trust, and then stay with that family long after they leave the hospital.

They assist with housing assistance, food assistance, job training, and mental health support — whatever it takes to help a victim of violence actually recover, not just physically, but mentally, emotionally, and economically, too.

Just to reiterate, of the $1,028,000 we clawed back from Washington to Jersey, $988,000 goes directly to the community health workers, $30,000 will help cover the costs of technology and equipment, and $10,000 to transportation. Every dollar has a purpose, and every dollar makes a difference.

This money isn’t coming out of your state, county, or property taxes. These are your federal tax dollars coming back to Jersey to cover our costs — instead of hitting our local property taxes. And it’s coming back here — not to some Moocher State like Mississippi or Alabama, that often gets back far more than it puts into the federal kitty.

As many of you know, when I first got to Congress, I made it a mission of mine to get more federal dollars back to Jersey. Historically, Moocher States like Mississippi would get about $4.38 back for every dollar they sent to Washington. West Virginia got about $4.23 back.

But New Jersey? We got about 67 cents on the dollar. Now, here in the Fifth Congressional District, we are up more than 357 percent. In the end, that helps lower your taxes and get more bang for the buck. Why should Moocher States get our money instead of it coming back home to you?

My job, and something I take really seriously, is making sure that when your tax dollars go to Washington, as much as possible comes back to North Jersey instead of disappearing into some other state’s budget or some other member’s pet project.

So, when HMH needed additional funding to take on violence and expand this program, I didn’t ask Trenton to raise a tax or ask the county to find room in its budget. I went and got this money back from Washington — dollars that were already yours to begin with.

And I’ll say this, too. HMH isn’t just relying on the federal government to fund this critical work. They’re already investing about $2.2 million a year into violence intervention, with more than 30 team members working on this across the network. That tells you everything you need to know about their commitment.

This federal funding isn’t replacing that. It’s building on top of it, giving them the extra capacity they need to reach the hardest-hit communities.

So, what does success look like a year from now? It looks like fewer repeat victims walking back through that emergency room. It looks like victims and their families getting connected to housing, to jobs, to counseling, instead of falling through the cracks. It looks like Bergen County becoming a model — the same way Project HEAL became one in Monmouth and Ocean Counties — that HMH can expand to other hospitals across its entire network.

To everyone at Hackensack Meridian Health, to everyone at Bergen’s Promise, and to everyone at this table today doing the hard work on the ground — thank you. This is exactly the kind of partnership between the federal government, our hospitals, and our community organizations that actually gets things done for people. I’m proud to have fought for this funding. I’m proud it’s coming back to Bergen County where it belongs, and I’m ready to work with all of you to make sure this program succeeds. There is nothing partisan about it.

If we keep working together to improve our community and keep people safe, in the greatest country in the world, I know that our best days will always be ahead of us.

Thank you.

title: Rep. Grijalva Op-Ed in the Patagonia Regional Times: The Hermosa Mine Approval Sets a Dangerous Precedent for the Entire Country
text:
Patagonia, AZ – Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva penned an op-ed in the Patagonia Regional Times responding to the Forest Service’s Final Record of Decision allowing the Hermosa Mine project to move forward. As Rep. Grijalva writes, this project “is the first critical minerals project in the nation to move through the federal FAST-41 permitting framework, making it a testing ground for how mining projects are approved across the country.”

You can read the full op-ed online or below:

My constituents have made it clear that the recent federal approval of the Hermosa Mine Project poses serious risks to natural resources, public health, and the local economy in Patagonia and Santa Cruz County. I previously urged the U.S. Forest Service to extend the public review and comment period on this complex and controversial mining project so community members could have enough time to provide meaningful feedback.

Unfortunately, the agency proceeded in approving the submitted plan. Not only will this project have lasting consequences for the surrounding communities, but the rushed approval process also sets a dangerous precedent for how large-scale mining projects are reviewed and approved across the country.

The Hermosa Mine is the first critical minerals project in the nation to move through the federal FAST-41 permitting framework, making it a testing ground for how mining projects are approved across the country. The Forest Service’s fast-track approval of this project – despite several unresolved questions about the mine’s public health and environmental impacts – establishes a dangerous precedent that prioritizes speed over science and expediency over meaningful public participation. Communities should not be testing grounds for a sped up permitting process, and South32’s Hermosa project should not become the model for weakening environmental review under the banner of critical minerals development.

The concerns that my constituents have raised throughout this process – including effects on groundwater, public health, wildlife, and compliance with the Coronado National Forest Plan – remain unresolved.

This remarkable area attracts birders, hikers, hunters and campers from across the United States and around the world, making ecotourism a significant and vital aspect of the local economy. The mining operation threatens this critical economic mainstay.

The Forest Service provides South 32 a total of 24 “exceptions” to the Coronado Forest Plan to accommodate the company’s mining plans. The Forest Plan is not just a list of suggestions: it lays out critical standards to protect forest health and resilience, wildlife, recreation, and other uses of our public lands.

One of the exceptions, for example, allows South32 to destroy wetlands that the Plan acknowledges as essential to Forest health. According to the agency’s own analysis, the mine operations’ groundwater pumping would dry 12 Forest springs and streams. How could this possibly be acceptable? The Forest Service should require South32 to meet the Coronado Plan’s well-reasoned and scientific standards instead of carving out special exceptions whenever compliance is inconvenient.

South 32 wants to discharge treated mining process water into Goldbaum Canyon, Mowry Wash South, and Harshaw Creek, which flows through the Town of Patagonia. Although South32 revised portions of its proposal, including alternative water discharge locations, important questions remain about how treated mine water could affect downstream water quality and nearby communities. Preliminary tests already found antimony, a toxic heavy metal, in Harshaw Creek at levels beyond state and federal health standards. If the mine was operating, its discharges also would contain sulfites and traces of the metals its processes extract – lead, zinc, manganese and silver.

Also concerning is the company’s proposal to conduct water quality testing downstream from the mine, instead of at its discharge point. Nearby residents deserve to know that their surface water and groundwater will be safe.

These concerns are not new. In 2020 and 2021, the Town of Patagonia formally requested that the Coronado National Forest conduct a comprehensive groundwater study of the Patagonia Mountains because of the potential impacts of the Hermosa Mine.

My dad, Congressman Raúl M. Grijalva, supported those requests. Despite repeated calls from local leaders, that study was not conducted. Moving forward without this fundamental scientific analysis leaves significant uncertainty about how the project could affect groundwater supplies and undermines confidence in the environmental review.

Many mines such as the proposed Hermosa Mine also emit dangerous substances to the air from ore processing, blasting, excavating, windblown tailings, haul-road dust, and truck and heavy equipment diesel fumes. These emissions can seriously impair public health. Community advocacy organizations including Patagonia Area Resource Alliance (PARA) have been critical of the Forest Service’s responses to these concerns, stating that the federal documents do not quantify the total air emissions of the proposed mining operations or analyze their cumulative impacts.

The Forest Service’s approval will allow South32 to construct a new 138-kilovolt electric transmission line through seven miles of pristine Forest land to reach the mine. In addition, the company wants to build 4.7 miles of new “primary access road” through the Forest. Together, these projects would fragment wildlife habitat, increase wildfire danger through the proposed transmission line, and threaten the habitat of endangered species such as jaguars and Mexican spotted owls. To make matters worse, South32 wants to dump mine tailings that contain pollutants on more than 225 acres of Forest Service land. It remains unclear whether South32 has the legal authority to do so.

The Forest Service has not evaluated the cumulative environmental impacts of these proposals, instead considering each in isolation. The bottom line is that the Forest Service should never have allowed this project to move forward until the input of affected communities, Tribal leaders, and local residents were fully addressed. My constituents—and future generations of Southern Arizonans—deserve nothing less. Unfortunately, the flawed approval process for the Hermosa Mine is just a preview of what is to come in other parts of the country if there are not serious reforms to FAST-41.

title: Comisionado Residente anuncia más de $1.5 millones en fondos federales para fortalecer los museos de Puerto Rico.
text:
CAGUAS, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, anunció hoy la otorgación de $1,535,801 en fondos federales del Instituto de Servicios de Museos y Bibliotecas de Estados Unidos (IMLS, por sus siglas en inglés) para fortalecer cuatro instituciones culturales y educativas en Puerto Rico.

Las subvenciones apoyarán proyectos dirigidos a capacitar profesionales de museos, incorporar herramientas de inteligencia artificial de manera ética, mejorar la preservación de colecciones, ampliar programas educativos y facilitar el acceso público al patrimonio histórico y cultural puertorriqueño.

“Nuestros museos preservan la historia de Puerto Rico, educan a nuevas generaciones y crean espacios para la ciencia, la cultura y el aprendizaje. Estos fondos permitirán que cuatro instituciones amplíen sus programas, fortalezcan sus equipos de trabajo y utilicen nuevas tecnologías para llevar nuestro patrimonio a más personas dentro y fuera de la Isla”, expresó Hernández.

Las otorgaciones incluyen:

$100,000 para el EcoExploratorio: Museo de Ciencias de Puerto Rico, que desarrollará un programa de capacitación en inteligencia artificial, gerencia de proyectos y prácticas éticas para profesionales de museos STEM.

$449,601 para el Museo de Historia Natural y Conservación de Puerto Rico, que capacitará a su personal en paleontología, documentación digital, manejo de colecciones, exhibiciones y programas educativos.

$486,200 para Caribbean University, que liderará talleres para profesionales de varios museos sobre preparación ante desastres, tecnologías digitales, desarrollo de exhibiciones y turismo cultural.

$500,000 para la Fundación Luis Muñoz Marín, que creará una plataforma digital gratuita para preservar y divulgar hasta 4,000 piezas de la Colección Teodoro Vidal-Santoni.
