title: Comisionado Residente destaca más de $1.7 billones en fondos federales para municipios durante encuentro con alcaldes.
text:
AGUADA, Puerto Rico – El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, destacó que su oficina ha anunciado más de $1.7 billones en fondos federales para municipios de la Isla, durante su participación hoy en un encuentro de la Asociación de Alcaldes de Puerto Rico celebrado en Aguada.

Durante el encuentro, el Comisionado Residente dialogó con los alcaldes sobre las necesidades prioritarias de sus comunidades y las oportunidades disponibles para financiar proyectos de infraestructura, desarrollo económico, turismo y servicios municipales mediante programas federales.

“Los municipios conocen de primera mano las necesidades de sus comunidades. Nuestro trabajo es ayudarlos a convertir esas prioridades en proyectos competitivos y conectarlos con los recursos federales necesarios para hacerlos realidad”, expresó el Comisionado Residente.

La agenda reunió a representantes del Cuerpo de Ingenieros del Ejército de los Estados Unidos (USACE), Rural Development del Departamento de Agricultura federal (USDA), Estudios Técnicos Inc, Invest Puerto Rico y Discover Puerto Rico, entre otras entidades.

Las conversaciones se concentraron en identificar oportunidades de financiamiento, fortalecer la coordinación entre los municipios y las agencias, y adelantar iniciativas relacionadas con infraestructura, turismo, innovación tecnológica y crecimiento económico.

"Hasta la fecha, hemos anunciado más de $1.7 billones en fondos federales para municipios de Puerto Rico. Mi compromiso es seguir trabajando para que esos recursos continúen llegando a las comunidades y se traduzcan en más oportunidades para nuestra gente", expresó el Comisionado Residente.

La cifra incluye subvenciones y otras asignaciones provenientes de la Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias (FEMA), destinadas a proyectos y servicios municipales.

Como parte de su gestión en Washington, la oficina del Comisionado Residente continuará ofreciendo apoyo a los municipios para identificar programas federales, atender obstáculos en los procesos de solicitud y promover proyectos que mejoren la infraestructura y los servicios que reciben los ciudadanos.

###

title: Comisionado Residente expresa solidaridad con Colombia
text:
SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, emitió la siguiente declaración:

title: Comisionado Residente participa en inauguración del nuevo Complejo Head Start en Mayagüez
text:
MAYAGÜEZ, Puerto Rico – El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, participó hoy en la inauguración del nuevo Complejo de Servicios Integrados de Educación Preescolar del Programa Head Start del Municipio de Mayagüez, una moderna instalación que fortalecerá los servicios de educación temprana para niños y familias de Mayagüez, Añasco, Maricao y Las Marías.

El nuevo complejo alberga seis centros preescolares con capacidad para atender a 120 niños y niñas mediante horarios regulares y extendidos. Además de educación temprana, el programa ofrece servicios integrales de salud, nutrición, trabajo social y apoyo especializado para promover el desarrollo integral de los participantes y acompañar a sus familias.

Durante la actividad, el Comisionado Residente destacó la importancia de Head Start como una de las principales inversiones federales para el desarrollo de la niñez y reafirmó su compromiso de continuar defendiendo estos programas durante el proceso de asignaciones presupuestarias en el Congreso.

Durante el proceso de asignaciones federales, el Comisionado Residente defendió el financiamiento de Head Start en el presupuesto federal. Como parte de esa gestión, desde su oficina ha anunciado más de $73 millones en fondos federales para fortalecer programas Head Start y Early Head Start en municipios y organizaciones de toda la Isla.

"Los $73 millones que hemos anunciado para Head Start han permitido ampliar servicios, modernizar instalaciones y brindar mayores oportunidades a miles de niños y niñas", expresó el Comisionado Residente.

El nuevo Complejo de Servicios Integrados del Programa Head Start del Municipio de Mayagüez cuenta con seis centros preescolares, una cocina de gran capacidad para la preparación y distribución de alimentos, un anfiteatro multipropósito para actividades educativas y comunitarias, áreas para la capacitación del personal y espacios de apoyo para las familias. Asimismo, sus instalaciones fueron concebidas para servir como un recurso para la comunidad en caso de emergencias o desastres naturales.

El Comisionado Residente reiteró su compromiso de continuar impulsando iniciativas que fortalezcan la educación temprana y garanticen que Puerto Rico siga contando con los recursos federales necesarios para ampliar las oportunidades de desarrollo de la niñez y apoyar a las familias puertorriqueñas.

###

title: Comisionado Residente propone cinco medidas para atender la crisis de agua
text:
SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández presentó un plan de cinco puntos dirigido al gobierno federal para atender la crisis de agua que afecta a cientos de miles de puertorriqueños, que incluiría préstamos federales para pequeños negocios y agricultores.

En un video publicado en redes sociales, el Comisionado Residente hizo un llamado a la gobernadora para que solicite al presidente de los Estados Unidos una declaración federal de emergencia ante la crisis de agua en Puerto Rico.

Bajo la Ley Stafford, la gobernadora tiene la facultad de presentar formalmente esa solicitud. Hernández reiteró su disposición a buscar respaldo congresional para fortalecer la petición y aumentar sus probabilidades de éxito, tal como hizo con la declaración de emergencia energética en 2025.

De lograrse, dicha declaración aumentaría la disponibilidad de recursos de FEMA para atender la escasez de agua, incluyendo la distribución de agua almacenada y el reembolso de gastos de emergencia para los municipios y la AAA.

El Comisionado Residente además pidió que la solicitud incluya asistencia individual, lo cual habilitaría préstamos de la SBA para los negocios afectados por la sequía.

Por separado, el Comisionado Residente recomendará al Departamento de Agricultura federal que emita la designación de emergencia por sequía que las condiciones actuales incluyendo la sequía extrema ya registrada en el sur de la isla — ameritan bajo sus propios criterios, lo cual proveería ayuda para nuestros agricultores.

Finalmente, el Comisionado Residente indicó que deben iniciarse las gestiones necesarias para el regreso de los cientos de puertorriqueños de la Guardia Nacional actualmente desplegados en Washington, D.C., de manera que puedan apoyar la respuesta a esta crisis en la isla.

“Como reflejan estas cinco medidas, el gobierno estatal y federal pueden hacer más, y estoy en la mejor disposición de ayudar para que así sea”, concluyó el Comisionado Residente.

title: Hoyer, McCaul, Colleagues Introduce the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026
text:
Today, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Emeritus Michael McCaul (R-Texas) and Congressman Steny Hoyer (D-Md.) introduced the bipartisanLindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026alongside 16 of their colleagues. This legislation — which honors the late Senator Lindsey Graham, who worked on the bill for more than a year and secured the White House’s support — will hold major purchasers of Russian oil and gas accountable for supporting Russia’s war against Ukraine and extend sanctions that restrict funding for Iran’s energy and weapons sectors.

“Democracy is presently under threat from despotism, and Congress must act to defend democracy and help Ukraine defeat Vladimir Putin’s effort to extinguish its liberty and sovereignty. Our legislation goes after multiple sources of Russian war funding, including its oil and gas sectors, shadow fleet, and financial institutions. I’m encouraged that the Senate passed the companion legislation last week with overwhelming support, and I thank former Chairman McCaul for partnering with me to facilitate action by the House. This action has been delayed too long and will, hopefully, accelerate Ukraine’s success and the ending of this war, one that was initiated illegally by Putin and that has resulted in tens of thousands of deaths of Russians and Ukrainians. I hope that we can secure bipartisan consensus in the House and enact a sanctions package that will stem the flow of money to Russia’s war machine and contribute to a Ukrainian victory," said Congressman Hoyer (MD-05).

“Senator Graham was a national security giant, a statesman of unmatched conviction, and a personal friend and mentor. We shared a fundamental worldview: America is strongest at home when it projects strength abroad. That’s why he fought so hard for this bill, which I promised him months ago I would introduce in the House,” said Congressman McCaul (TX-10). “As President Zelensky told me last month when I visited Ukraine, he is ready for a ceasefire — ready to negotiate, as he has been for years. Putin, on the other hand, consistently defies President Trump and the international community by refusing to come to the table. I can think of no better way to honor Senator Graham’s life and legacy than by passing these tough sanctions, which will help force Putin into negotiations and bring us closer to securing Lindsey’s vision of enduring peace in two critical regions of the world.”

Earlier this month, an overwhelming bipartisan majority in the Senate voted to pass companion legislation, by a vote of 86-11, led by Sens. Darline Graham (R-SC), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT.), Katie Britt (R-AL), Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Chair of the Senate Armed Services Committee Roger Wicker (R-MS), and Chair of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee Jim Risch (R-ID). The text of the House bill is identical to the text that passed the Senate.

“This legislation was deeply important to my brother, Lindsey, and I’m grateful that it has achieved such a wide coalition of support. Lindsey was committed to achieving a peaceful resolution to this war, and I’m confident that these sanctions will pave the way,” said Senator Darline Graham (R-SC). “I’m grateful to Rep. McCaul for leading this effort in the House. The Senate came together in a strong, bipartisan fashion to pass the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, and I hope the House of Representatives will do the same. Russia has waged war against Ukraine for far too long, and this bill assists President Trump in his noble efforts to bring it to a close.”

“Representatives McCaul, Hoyer, Wilson, Kaptur, and Fitzpatrick are longtime champions of Ukraine’s cause and I am glad to have them leading our legislation in the House of Representatives. After a massive bipartisan vote in the Senate, we are eager to turn to the House as we fight to get this legislation across the finish line. There is immense urgency in getting this done – July set a record for Russia’s use of ballistic missiles, killing and wounding dozens of Ukrainians, including many children. Cutting off the source of funding – profits from oil and gas – for these deadly weapons and Russia’s war machine is essential to ending the bloodshed,” said Senator Blumenthal (D-CT).

Joining Hoyer and McCaul as original cosponsors are Co-Chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus Joe Wilson (SC-02); Co-Founder and Co-Chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus Marcy Kaptur (OH-09); Co-Chair of the House Baltic Caucus Don Bacon (NE-02); Congressman Jake Auchincloss (MA-04), House Armed Services Committee Chairman Mike Rogers (AL-03), Representatives Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Mike Turner (OH-10), Gabe Vasquez (NM-02), Ann Wagner (MO-02), Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05), Andy Barr (KY-06), and Ed Case (HI-01); Co-Chair of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01); and Representatives Eugene Vindman (VA-07), Nathaniel Moran (TX-01), and Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06).

"Senator Lindsey Graham and I shared the belief that opposing dictators in defense of freedom and liberty is always the right thing to do. War criminal Putin is losing his invasion of sovereign Ukraine and the threat to humanity posed by the Iranian regime is dire. It is time for Congress to give President Trump the strongest tools available to choke off Russia's war machine for the good of mankind and cripple the ability of Tehran to continue sowing chaos in the region and beyond. title: Hoyer Statement After Introducing Bipartisan Russia Sanctions Bill in the U.S. House of Representatives
text:

Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 in the U.S. House of Representatives, which requires a package of sanctions and financial restrictions that would cut off support for Russia’s war machine and restrict funding for Iran’s energy and weapons sectors:

“I’m proud to join former Chairman McCaul to introduce this legislation in the House, a companion to the Sanctioning Russia Act, which the late Sen. Lindsey Graham negotiated in his final days, along with Sen. Blumenthal, Ranking Member Shaheen, and other Democratic and Republican senators, and which recently passed with bipartisan support in the Senate. For more than four years, Ukrainians have courageously defended their free democracy against Russia’s determined effort to stamp it out and impose despotism on its people. Every day Ukraine fights on is a win for liberty as well as for American values and security.

“It has been an honor to help lead this fight in Congress, including working to discharge the Ukraine Support Act from committee and partnering with former Chairman McCaul, Ranking Member Meeks, and others to pass it through the House in June – a strong signal of support for Ukraine and for NATO and our Baltic allies. We must ensure that Ukrainians have every tool needed to see this war to victory. In doing so, we keep the faith with Ukraine and with international law.

“This bill would impose the toughest sanctions we can on Putin’s inner circle, Russia’s oil and gas oligarchs, its shadow fleet of oil tankers, and its financial sector – all of which have sustained Russia’s war machine. It reflects a bipartisan consensus on key issues, and I believe we can continue coming together on final details as this bill moves through the legislative process, including limiting presidential authority on tariffs to eight specific nations whose imports are funding Russia’s ongoing operations. title: Huffman, Buchanan Re-Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Address World Extinction Crisis
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Representatives Jared Huffman (D-CA) and Vern Buchanan (R-FL) re-introduced the Critically Endangered Animals Conservation Act, a bipartisan bill to support conservation efforts for highly endangered species around the world.

Huffman. “Our bill will bring the U.S. back as a partner on the global stage to reverse the extinction crisis and support conservation projects for the world’s most vulnerable species. The competitive grant program created by this bill will ensure that every dollar goes towards worthwhile projects that protect endangered wildlife,” said Rep. Buchanan.

This legislation would establish funding for the Critically Endangered Animals Conservation Fund, to be administered by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service as part of the successful Multinational Species Conservation Funds. title: Huffman, Dexter Open Investigation into Insider Trading at Energy Fuels After Trump Guts Bears Ears
text:
Energy Fuels CEO bought 74,000 shares days before the monument was cut by 90 percent, the largest insider purchase in company history

Washington, D.C. – Today, House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.) and Oversight & Investigations Subcommittee Ranking Member Maxine Dexter (D-Ore.) opened an investigation into potential insider trading at Energy Fuels Inc., after the company's CEO and Chairman of the Board bought company stock days before President Trump announced he was shrinking Bears Ears National Monument by more than 90 percent.

On July 7, 2026, CEO Ross Bhappu purchased 74,000 shares, the largest insider purchase of stock in the company's history, increasing his ownership by 41 percent. Chairman Bruce Hansen purchased 4,000 shares the next day. On July 13, Trump opened nearly 3 million acres of federal land to mining, including uranium-rich areas of the San Juan Basin that had previously been protected.

“The timing of these stock purchases indicate that nonpublic information was potentially available to both you and Mr. Hansen,” the lawmakers wrote to Bhappu.

The lawmakers argue Energy Fuels' relationships with the administration put its executives in position to learn of the decision early and potentially profit from it. The company hired outside lobbyists that included a former Trump Interior official, identified strong government support as a selling point to investors in its expansion plans, and cited ongoing discussions with government sources as a way to close its financing gap.

The lawmakers write that this “demonstrates close coordination and communication with the Trump administration, which may have enabled you to receive privileged information about when the Bears Ears announcement would occur.”

The new boundaries opened uranium and vanadium districts the company had been eyeing for years. In a 2017 letter to the Trump administration, Energy Fuels wrote that the monument “could affect existing and future mill operations” and pointed to “many other known uranium and vanadium deposits located within the [original boundaries] that could provide valuable energy and mineral resources in the future.”

The reduction opened districts including White Canyon and Elk Ridge, areas holding multiple ore deposits west of Blanding, Utah. Ore mined there would be trucked to White Mesa, the only conventional uranium mill operating in the country.

Two Utah laws took effect in May that fast-track permits and fund critical mineral processing where the company's mill already operates. On June 18, Energy Fuels secured a $725 million loan from the Defense Department's Office of Strategic Capital, the largest that office had issued at the time. Two weeks after the monument shrank, the company broke ground on a mill expansion.

“After the recent passage of favorable state laws and securing funding from DOD, the final leg in Energy Fuels' quest to gain strategic position in domestic uranium extraction and processing was to attack protections for the land and the sovereign Tribal Nations that steward it,” the lawmakers wrote.

The letter argues the company standing to profit from the monument reduction has spent decades harming the community next door. White Mesa sits a mile from the former boundary and the lawmakers describe a facility that “has become a radioactive dumping ground, taking in waste from Superfund sites, the Manhattan Project, and even foreign countries, all while storing more than 700 million pounds of toxic material in outdated, single-liner pits that threaten nearby tribal communities and groundwater.”

“Energy Fuels cannot credibly claim to be a responsible operator while the nation's last uranium mill functions like an unregulated, bargain-bin waste dump on the doorstep of an Indigenous community,” the lawmakers wrote. “Instead of respecting the Tribes for whom Bears Ears is sacred, you appear to be enriching yourself from their devastation.”

Huffman and Dexter are demanding communications between Energy Fuels and Interior, Agriculture, and Defense officials, both executives' calendars, the company's lobbying contract with Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck LLP, and internal revenue projections tied to redrawing the boundaries.

Read the full letter to Energy Fuels CEO Ross Bhappu here.

title: Huffman, Garcia Demand Documents from Vulcan Elements After White House Pushed Through $620 Million Loan to Company Tied to Donald Trump Jr.
text:
Huffman, Garcia Demand Documents from Vulcan Elements After White House Pushed Through $620 Million Loan to Company Tied to Donald Trump Jr.

Washington, D.C. – Today, House NaturalResources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.) and House Oversight and Government Reform Committee Ranking Member Robert Garcia (D-Calif.) sent a letterto Vulcan Elements CEO John Maslin demanding overdue documents after ProPublica reporting revealed that the company’s $620 million Department of Defense loan resulted from direct White House intervention, contradicting assurances Maslin gave Committee staff and reporters that his company received no political favoritism.

“We write regarding serious concerns about corruption in government contracting, from which your company may have benefited,” the Ranking Members wrote. “According to ProPublica, the $620 million loan your company, Vulcan Elements, received from the Department of Defense’s Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) was the result of direct White House intervention. This is the opposite of what you told us—and reporters—happened.”

The loan, the largest in the Office of Strategic Capital’s history, came three months after 1789 Capital, the venture capital firm where Donald Trump Jr. serves as a partner, took an equity stake in Vulcan Elements. According to ProPublica, the deal was initiated by Peter Navarro, a senior White House adviser and close personal friend of Trump Jr., and Pentagon staff were directed to complete the deal in a matter of weeks at an “unusually rapid pace.”

“The ProPublica reporting indicates that Mr. Navarro’s intervention on behalf of a company in which the President’s son held a financial stake was not coincidental to the award process; it was the extent of the award process,” the Ranking Members wrote. “The American people deserve a full accounting of this apparent political favor, which was funded by their taxpayer dollars.”

The Ranking Members laid out a four-month timeline. In July 2025, Maslin met with 1789 Capital, where Donald Trump Jr. was a subject of discussion. In August, the firm bought an ownership stake in Vulcan Elements, then a 30-employee startup. Within about a month, the White House directed the Pentagon to treat a loan to Vulcan Elements as a top priority, and staff were told to expedite the loan. By November, the company had won the largest loan in the Office of Strategic Capital’s history at the time, plus a $50 million equity stake from the Department of Commerce.

“Within the span of four months, your company went from a small startup with 30 employees to the top investment priority of the White House,” they wrote.

The letter also raises questions about ReElement Technologies, Vulcan Elements’ intended supply chain partner, which withdrew from an $80 million conditional loan process in July 2026 after Pentagon due diligence reviews raised serious doubts about the company’s ability to scale, only to receive a new $25 million federal investment three days later.

“Questions about the viability of your partner company, ReElement Technologies, have since emerged, illustrating why political favoritism in the federal government’s award processes is not only corrupt; it is also bad for business: it undermines competition in the market and burdens taxpayers with the costs of avoidable business failures,” the Ranking Members wrote.

During an April 16, 2026, meeting with NaturalResources Committee Democratic staff, Maslin assured staff, as he had assured reporters, that Vulcan Elements received no political favoritism in connection with its federal awards. ProPublica’s reporting contradicts that assurance. A Pentagon official confirmed that the Vulcan Elements deal was the only one initiated by a top aide to the president, with one person directly involved saying,

“The call came from the White House: We have to get this done.” That aide was Peter Navarro, who calls Donald Trump Jr. “brother” and whom Trump Jr. called “my boy” on a public broadcast one week before the Pentagon announced the loan.

At that same meeting, Maslin committed to producing four sets of documents, including the company’s “anti-corruption policy.” None have been shared with the Committee. Today’s letter restates those four requests and adds thirteen more, including all communications between Vulcan Elements and 1789 Capital, Peter Navarro, the White House, the Department of Defense, and the Department of Commerce since January 20, 2025.

Read the full letter to Vulcan Elements CEO John Maslin here.

Background

Ranking Members Huffman, Garcia, and Heinrich opened a formal congressional inquiry on February 2, 2026, into the Trump administration’s decision to commit billions of dollars in public funds to minerals companies in exchange for equity stakes, after waiving critical requirements for transparency and accountability. Multiple beneficiaries of those equity deals have documented connections to top administration officials, including Vulcan Elements and its supply chain partner ReElement Technologies.

In March 2026, Natural Resources Committee Democrats forced a vote on a subpoena motion that would have compelled Donald Trump Jr. to testify under oath about whether he profited from his father's presidency. Committee Republicans voted it down, blocking transparency around the use of hundreds of millions of taxpayer dollars.

title: Smith Visits Iron County to Survey Flood Damage
text:
IRON COUNTY, Mo. – Congressman Jason Smith (MO-08) sat down with Iron County Commissioners Josh Campbell, Jim Scaggs, and Dustin Hinkle in Ironton recently for an update on the county’s recovery from recent flooding, which the National Weather Service has classified as a 1-in-1,000-year event.

Congressman Smith said, “Iron County has taken a brutal hit. Fourteen roads across the county sustained damage, and one of them, County Road 65, took five straight days of work just to become passable again. This kind of destruction is far beyond what a county this size can handle on its own, and I’m committed to making sure Iron County gets every bit of federal support it needs to recover.”

Commissioners presented Congressman Smith with a damage assessment showing $12.4 million in infrastructure damage countywide, a figure that grew to $19 million following a joint Preliminary Damage Assessment with FEMA and the State Emergency Management Agency. The western part of Iron County, the hardest-hit area, sustained an estimated $15.3 million in damage alone, with roughly 23 miles of roadway losing an average of 2 to 3 feet of roadbed and some stretches losing as much as 6 feet.

Iron County’s total annual revenue is only $1.4 to $1.6 million, and the county’s financial reserves have been depleted in recent years by other much needed investments and repairs to county infrastructure. Because FEMA only reimburses public entities after funds have already been spent, commissioners say the county will need to spend more than $3 million upfront before seeing any reimbursement. Neighboring Washington and St. Francois Counties, along with Brockmiller Construction, have supplied equipment and manpower to assist with recovery efforts, and Congressman Smith’s office previously helped secure the release of $200,000 in FEMA funds still owed to Iron County from last year’s tornado damage.

“Senator Graham believed, as I do, that American strength remains the surest guardian of peace,” said Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01). “That conviction guided our work together on this legislation. Putin’s war machine runs on oil, money, and the willingness of others to look the other way—and the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 attacks all three. It isolates Russia’s banks, shuts down the networks financing its aggression, and forces every government and company enabling this war to make a choice. By increasing the cost of Putin’s war and reducing his ability to sustain it, this legislation strengthens the path to a just and lasting peace—one determined by Ukraine, not imposed by Moscow. The most fitting tribute Congress can offer Lindsey is to finish the work he began, carry forward the cause of freedom he championed, and make clear that America’s resolve will endure until that peace is secured.”

“Supporting a strong, free Ukraine is imperative for the national security of our communities here at home. Sanctioning Russia and Putin sends a direct message to the world: the United States will not sit by while brutal regimes bankroll aggression against democratic nations,” said Congressman Eugene Vindman (VA-07). “I am proud to be a co-sponsor of this essential legislation. We must continue to escalate the economic pressure on the Kremlin and strengthen our resolve for the Ukrainian people as they fight for their freedom, sovereignty, and security.”

"Russia is perpetrating a war of aggression, and we must keep the pressure on Vladimir Putin. This action is long overdue, but we are finally moving forward with the resolve this moment demands. These sanctions will erode Russia's war machine by cutting off the revenue that funds it. We must hold those who are fueling this war accountable. These sanctions focus on Russia but will also target dangerous Chinese entities which support the Russian defense industrial base. Peace is the goal, and these mechanisms give the President the tools to achieve that goal,” said Congressman Nathaniel Moran (TX-07).

“For more than four years, Ukrainians have courageously defended their freedom against Putin’s brutal invasion. The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act would increase pressure on the Kremlin, hold those supporting its war accountable, and strengthen Ukraine’s position in pursuit of a just peace," said Congresswoman Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06). “The bill also extends longstanding sanctions against Iran. Sanctions cannot replace a clear strategy or the President’s obligation to seek congressional authorization for war, but they remain an important diplomatic tool. I am proud to cosponsor this legislation.”

title: A250 Field Trip Winner’s Visit
text: Attina Louresse Rosario, a fourth-grade student from Sinapalo Elementary School in Rota won a first place prize in the national America’s Field Trip ("A250") contest. This week, we welcomed her and her mother, Maria Pobeda, to their Washington congressional office. The America Field Trip Contest invites students in grades 3–12 from across the country to reflect on what America means to them through artwork and writing. As part of her prize, Attina explored our nation’s capitol, including visits to the National Mall, the Smithsonian museums, and even a tour of the Capitol. Congratulations, Attina. Thank you for stopping by, and I hope you'll visit again soon.

title: Catching up with the Media and You
text: I spent Friday morning with the good folks at NMI News Service and Marianas Press for a back-to-back set of interviews on the work we have been doing in Washington, what is coming next, and, of course, a little bit about life. What happens in Washington can feel a world away from home, and I always appreciate the opportunity to come back and download that information to all of you. Whether it's legislation moving through Congress, the work happening behind the scenes, or the challenges and opportunities ahead for the CNMI, I think it's important that you know not only what is happening, but why it matters for our islands. Thank you to both news organizations for the opportunity to sit down and have these conversations. I look forward to continuing to keep you informed about the work we're doing on your behalf.

title: Celebrating Chamorro Language and Culture
text: I was honored to attend the Chamorro Culture and Language Research Training Program hosted at the Joeten-Kiyu Public Library. Events like this are an important reminder that preserving our language, history, and traditions is not only about honoring our past, but also about investing in future generations. It was wonderful to see local researchers and students sharing their work and contributing to a deeper understanding of Chamorro language and culture. Thank you to the organizers, presenters, and everyone involved for your commitment to preserving an important part of who we are and ensuring that this knowledge continues to be passed on for generations to come.

title: CJPA Awarded Over $750K for Violence Prevention
text: The Commonwealth’s Criminal Justice Planning Agency has received two significant grants from the Department of Justice Office on Violence Against Women. The FY 2026 STOP Formula Grant Program has awarded $620,987 to strengthen partnerships among law enforcement, prosecution, courts, and victim services, enhancing strategies to combat violent crimes against women and support victims of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, and stalking. Additionally, the Sexual Assault Services Formula Program has provided $129,268 to expand intervention, advocacy, and support services for victims of sexual assault and their families. These grants will empower local organizations and ensure comprehensive care for survivors across our community. Congratulations to CJPA

title: Congratulations to a Friend of the Marianas
text:
Congratulations to Jordan Roiland on his appointment as the University of California’s 2027-28 Student Regent-designate. Jordan will represent students from across the University of California system, serving on the Board of Regents, which governs all 10 UC campuses. Jordan lived and worked in the CNMI from 2022 to 2024, serving with the Commonwealth Healthcare Corporation through the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s Public Health Associate Program. During his time here, he supported cancer prevention initiatives and helped our community through the Covid-19 pandemic. I had the pleasure of welcoming Jordan to my Washington office in April of this year, where he reflected on how much his time in the Marianas shaped him, both professionally and personally. He shared his interest in possibly returning to the CNMI to practice medicine after completing his training. We congratulate Jordan on this historic honor as the first medical student selected to serve as a University of California Student Regent and wish him continued success as he prepares for a career in medicine.

title: Honoring Peace on Tinian
text:
Image

I had the great honor of delivering remarks at the 2026 Tinian Peace Ceremony commemorating the 81st anniversary of the atomic bombing of Hiroshima on August 6th. The ceremony is a powerful reminder of Tinian's unique place in world history and of our responsibility to remember both the events that took place here and the lives forever changed by them. In my remarks, I reflected on growing up on Tinian, where history was never something found only in books, but something that lived beneath our feet and shaped the conversations we had as children. I also spoke about the people of Tinian who rebuilt their island after the war and demonstrated that even after unimaginable conflict, communities can choose reconciliation, friendship, and peace. It was a privilege to join veterans, our friends from Japan, and our local community in honoring the past while reaffirming our shared hope for a more peaceful future.

title: Meeting with Mayor Aldan
text: While on Tinian, I appreciated the opportunity to sit down with Mayor Edwin P. Aldan to discuss the island’s ongoing recovery from Super Typhoon Sinlaku, the federal response, and the work still ahead. We talked about the progress that has been made, the challenges that remain, and how we can continue working together to make sure Tinian’s needs are heard in Washington. Recovery is not just about repairing damage. It is about making sure our communities have the resources and support they need to come back stronger. I appreciate Mayor Aldan’s partnership and his continued leadership on behalf of the people of Tinian. I look forward to continuing our work together as recovery efforts move forward.

title: Postal Duty Collection Changes Published in the Federal Register
text: New federal regulations governing duty collection on certain mail sent from the U.S. Territories to the customs territory of the United States have now been published in the Federal Register. The changes implement new procedures following the suspension of the federal de minimis exemption and may affect certain shipments from the CNMI, Guam, American Samoa, and the U.S. Virgin Islands. Under the proposed process, mailers may be required to prepay applicable duties, taxes and fees before mailing items to the fifty states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico. This is an issue I have been raising since the de minimis exemption was suspended. In November 2025, I and my fellow territorial delegates introduced the Territorial De Minimis Exemption Act, that would permanently restore de minimis treatment for shipments originating from the territories and help ensure that future nationwide trade policy changes do not inadvertently treat U.S. territories as though they were foreign countries. The Postal Service is accepting public comments on these regulations through August 31, 2026. I encourage individuals, businesses, and organizations in the Commonwealth to review the proposal and submit comments. As these regulations move forward under current law, I will continue to advocate for a permanent legislative solution that recognizes our unique states and that removes unnecessary burdens on commerce between the CNMI and the rest of the United States.

title: Krishnamoorthi Blasts Trump Executive Order Advancing Debunked Anti-Vaccine Conspiracy Theories and Endangering Children
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi, Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Health Care and Financial Services on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, issued the following statement after President Donald Trump signed an executive order seeking to reduce the number of vaccines routinely recommended for children and space out their administration across separate medical visits:

Decades of research and an overwhelming scientific consensus show that vaccines work and have saved millions of lives, and that there is no credible link between vaccines and autism. America’s children deserve vaccine recommendations based on science and the judgment of the medical community, not discredited conspiracy theories promoted by Donald Trump and RFK Jr.”

title: Krishnamoorthi Urges USPS Board to Remove Postmaster General Over Effort to Implement Trump’s Election Mail Order Federal Courts Have Held Violates the Constitution
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), a senior member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, today urged the United States Postal Service Board of Governors to remove Postmaster General David Steiner for pursuing implementation of President Trump’s mail-ballot executive order despite federal court rulings that key provisions violate the Constitution. Krishnamoorthi also cited Steiner’s failure to provide Congress with a clear accounting of USPS’s implementation efforts or whether they stopped after the courts intervened.

In the letter, Krishnamoorthi writes:

“I write to urge the United States Postal Service Board of Governors to remove Postmaster General David Steiner for pursuing implementation of President Trump’s mail-ballot executive order, despite federal courts’ rulings that key provisions violate the Constitution. Steiner’s failure to provide Congress with a clear accounting of USPS’s implementation efforts, or whether they ceased after the courts intervened, undermines the transparency, neutrality, and public trust his office requires.”

President Trump’s March 31 executive order directed USPS to withhold delivery of mail ballots to voters whose eligibility could not be confirmed against a federally compiled voter list. Twenty-three states and the District of Columbia challenged the order. A federal district court in Massachusetts blocked key provisions, the First Circuit upheld that injunction on July 25, and the Trump Administration subsequently asked the Supreme Court to allow the order to take effect before the November midterm elections.

Despite those rulings, Steiner has indicated that USPS intends to carry out key aspects of the executive order. During June 24 testimony before the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, Steiner confirmed that USPS would withhold mail ballots from states that declined to provide requested voter data. The letter also points to an apparent contradiction between USPS’s implementation efforts and the Department of Justice’s characterization of the executive order before the Supreme Court as merely “general policy guidance.”

Krishnamoorthi continues:

“Postmaster General Steiner has not responded to requests for that accounting. He has failed to respond to multiple congressional requests for information and my request to appear voluntarily before the full House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform. A Postmaster General who will not tell Congress whether his agency is complying with a federal court order, and who will not appear to answer for that silence, has forfeited the trust required to hold the office.”

The letter notes that millions of eligible Americans rely on mail voting, including military personnel serving overseas, seniors, rural voters, individuals with disabilities, and working families. Krishnamoorthi requested a response from the Board by August 24, 2026.

Krishnamoorthi concludes:

“The Board has both the authority and the responsibility to act. I urge you to remove David Steiner as Postmaster General and ensure that USPS follows the law, complies with federal court orders, and stays out of deciding who is eligible to vote. I request a response to this request by no later than August 24, 2026.”

title: LaHood, Colleagues introduce Bipartisan Bill to Expand Access to Low-Interest Mortgages for First-Time Homebuyers
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Representatives Darin LaHood (IL-16), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), Blake Moore (UT-01), and Tom Suozzi (NY-01) introduced the First-Time Homebuyer Affordability Act, bipartisan legislation to expand access to low-interest mortgages for first-time, low- to medium-income homebuyers.

“Rising housing costs are being felt in rural, urban, and suburban communities across Illinois,” said Rep. LaHood. "The First-Time Homebuyer Affordability Act is a commonsense, bipartisan solution that will help more first-time homebuyers access affordable, low-interest mortgages without taking resources away from other critical housing programs. By expanding access to financing, we can help more hardworking families achieve homeownership, strengthen our communities, and build long-term financial security. I'm proud to work with my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to advance practical policies that make the American Dream more attainable." "Too many working families and first-time homebuyers are locked out of homeownership by high mortgage rates and rising housing costs," said Rep. Panetta. "Our bipartisan First-Time Homebuyer Affordability Act would remove Mortgage Revenue Bonds from the Private Activity Bond cap, allowing California to offer qualified homebuyers lower-interest mortgages while preserving resources for affordable rental housing. Housing affordability is no longer just a coastal issue nor just a Democratic issue, but an issue that requires this type of bipartisan solution for working families all across our country.” "Homeownership is becoming increasingly out of reach for young families,” said Rep. Moore. “Removing Mortgage Revenue Bonds from the Private Activity Bond cap will make housing more accessible by allowing states to offer additional lower-interest mortgages to qualifying families, opening the door to homeownership for more Utahns and Americans across the nation. I’m proud to co-lead the First-Time Homebuyer Affordability Act to lower the barrier to entry for homeownership." “Too many Americans are being priced out of homeownership,” said Rep. Suozzi. “The First-Time Homebuyer Affordability Act will make it easier for states and local governments to issue more mortgage revenue bonds, therefore lowering borrowing costs for more first-time and low- and middle-income homebuyers. I’m proud to co-lead this commonsense bill to make homeownership more accessible and affordable for more families.” The legislation is supported by the Illinois Housing Development Authority (IHDA), the National Council of State Housing Agencies (NCSHA), the Council of Development Finance Agencies (CDFA), the Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA), the National Association of Home Builders (NAHB), and RBC Capital Markets. “This year alone, the Illinois Housing Development Authority (IHDA) has helped more than 3,000 families purchase their first home through our down payment assistance programs,” said IHDA Executive Director Kristin Faust. “With the passage of this legislation, IHDA will be able to provide even greater support through enhanced assistance and lower interest rates, doubling the number of homebuyers we can assist in overcoming the hurdles to homeownership. This bill will directly increase buyers’ purchasing power, help the missing middle, and lower monthly mortgage expenses - creating more homes for families, strengthening communities, and stimulating local economies.” “The First-Time Homebuyer Affordability Act is the most significant bipartisan federal legislation to lower the cost of homeownership for first-time home buyers in decades,” said NCSHA Executive Director Stockton Williams. “The bill would provide lower-interest home mortgage loans to hundreds of thousands of working households who are ready to become homeowners but for today’s relatively high-rate environment.” “This bill represents a transformational opportunity for homeownership in America at a time when the affordability crisis has never been greater,” said Cory Hoeppner, Head of National Housing Group at RBC Capital Markets. “The ability for State Housing Finance Agencies to offer significantly more lower rate mortgages to first time homebuyers will help boost the U.S. real estate market.”

“Increasing resources for programs that enable Americans to purchase their first home is critical. The First-Time Homebuyer Affordability Act will ensure that state housing finance agencies can fully fund affordable homeownership programs. We commend Reps. LaHood, Moore, Panetta, and Suozzi for working to make the American dream of homeownership more attainable," said Bill Owens, Chairman of the National Association of Home Builders.

Background:

Mortgage Revenue Bonds are a longstanding financing tool used by state and local housing agencies to support affordable homeownership opportunities – particularly for first-time, low- to moderate-income homebuyers. These bonds help reduce borrowing costs and expand access to below-market mortgage financing.

Under current law, mortgage bonds are subject to annual Private Activity Bond (PAB) volume caps, which limit the amount of financing states can provide each year. In many states, growing housing demand and rising home prices have strained these caps and reduced the availability of affordable mortgage assistance programs.

The First-Time Homebuyer Affordability Act would exempt qualified mortgage bonds from the PAB cap – expanding financing capacity and allow housing agencies to better meet housing needs in their communities.

Full text of the bill can be found HERE.

title: Larson Announces New Bill to Fully Rescind Corrupt Trump “Get Out of Jail Free” Tax Immunity Deal
text:

“Donald Trump’s sham lawsuit was nothing more than an attempt to line his own pocket with your tax dollars,” said Larson. “While his lackeys at the Department of Justice may claim that it is not moving forward, he still secured a sweetheart deal to shield himself and his family from every having to pay the taxes they owe. title: Lofgren, Whitesides Demand Transparency on OSTP Initiative Funded with NSF Money
text:
(Washington, DC) – Yesterday, Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren (D-CA) and Representative George Whitesides (D-CA) sent a letter to the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) Director Michael Kratsios demanding transparency on OSTP’s “Grand Research Challenges” initiative, reported in Nature. During a Science Committee hearing on July 22nd, 2026, Director Kratsios deliberately avoided answering questions about OSTP diverting resources from the National Science Foundation (NSF) to fund OSTP pet priorities, including the “Grand Research Challenges” initiative. Science Committee Democrats are requesting a comprehensive briefing on the “Grand Research Challenges” initiative and on OSTP control of NSF's operations and appropriated funding by August 14, 2026.

“If you believe this is legal, appropriate, and a good use of taxpayer money in order to bring about a ‘golden age of science,’ then you should have been eager to discuss it before the Committee,” the Members wrote in their letter. “Instead, you chose to apparently mislead the Committee about whether you had any understanding of where NSF’s disappearing money is going.”

“No thanks to your testimony, Science Committee Democrats know these facts, based on reporting and well corroborated sources: OSTP is exerting influence over NSF decision making, certainly on Notices of Funding Opportunities and potentially on at least a subset of grant decisions; NSF is 30-40% behind where it was last year at this time on getting money out the door; OSTP intends to spend hundreds of millions of dollars to fund your priority projects, and that money was not appropriated to OSTP by Congress.”

The letter can be accessed here, and below.

Dear Director Kratsios,

Just two weeks ago, you had the opportunity to come before the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology to “examine the priorities of the FY2027 Research and Technology Enterprise.” Sixteen hours before you were due to appear, you chose to release a 123-page report on “Science: A New Golden Age,” which you described as “a blueprint for renewing American scientific leadership for the 21st century.” This release came with no formal notification to the Science Committee, despite your appearance the next day to discuss precisely these issues. We mention this to note that we have no reason to be surprised that you chose to continue this pattern of obfuscation and disrespect of the Committee’s oversight prerogatives at the hearing itself. We write to demand that the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) be transparent with the Committee regarding recent reporting of an OSTP-led initiative called “Grand Research Challenges.”

The July 24 Nature reporting confirmed rumors that have been swirling about OSTP diverting resources from the National Science Foundation (NSF) to fund your pet priorities. These rumors underpinned multiple lines of questions posed to you at the July 22 hearing:

Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren: “Where is the nearly $1 billion that we know is being clawed back from NSF Directorates, and what is the reported $1.5 billion project – to quote Nature’s reporting – that is a ‘brainchild of the White House OSTP?’ And if you could be specific, is any of the $5 billion you announced today coming from the money appropriated to NSF?”

Director Kratsios: “I’m not familiar with those details, I would refer you to NSF.”

It is incomprehensible that, on the morning of July 22, you were unfamiliar with the details of what would be reported just two days later as the exfiltration of $300 million from NSF’s mathematics and physical sciences directorates to fund an OSTP-led program. It is even more incomprehensible when considered alongside what you said just moments later, when responding

to this same question:

Director Kratsios: “As a nation, we should be more deliberative and specific about trying to tackle grand challenges.” [Emphasis added.]

It is deeply strange and disrespectful that you chose to dodge a question about this very program while mockingly referencing its name. Congressional testimony is not a joke. You agreed to testify before the Science Committee about the FY2027 priorities of the scientific enterprise, and then you decided to elide discussion of this expensive program that you are undertaking without

any Congressional authorization or input. If you believe this is legal, appropriate, and a good use of taxpayer money in order to bring about a “golden age of science,” then you should have been eager to discuss it before the Committee. Instead, you chose to apparently mislead the Committee about whether you had any understanding of where NSF’s disappearing money is

going.

We understand that it would be rather uncomfortable to testify comprehensively and truthfully before the Science Committee about how you are in the process of absorbing hundreds of millions of dollars of appropriated money from an agency under the Committee’s jurisdiction. If you were unfamiliar with your obligation to be truthful before Congress ahead of the hearing, you were reminded of this during questioning by Representative George Whitesides about whether and how OSTP is involved in ensuring money it would prefer to use for its own projects is not, instead, spent as Congress intended, on NSF research awards:

Representative Whitesides: “Earlier, you testified that NSF grant approvals have not been reviewed by political officials at OSTP … I want to give you the chance to make sure that that’s what you wanted to testify, because we have been directly informed that this is not true. Is it still your testimony today that no one at OSTP is playing a role in individual NSF grant approvals?”

Director Kratsios: “I am not personally involved in any individual grant approvals.”

Representative Whitesides: “That is a different answer to what I asked.”

Director Kratsios: “I am not aware of anyone at OSTP that is working on individual grant approvals. I have never asked for that, and I would never condone that, and I don’t think any of us are.”

Representative Whitesides: “Ok, for the record, it is a felony to testify falsely before Congress.”

Director Kratsios: “I am well aware of that, and I’m also well aware that no one at OSTP is involved in individual grant-level decisions.”

Representative Whitesides: “Is anyone at OSTP involved in some kind of grouping of grant decisions?”

Director Kratsios: “I’m not familiar with what a grouping of a grant decision is. But when an individual grant for a particular research project is made, we are certainly not involved in that.”

Representative Whitesides: “Ok, sounds a little squishy to me.”

It is, indeed, squishy to direct focus entirely on “an individual grant for a particular research project” when being asked about any broader influence OSTP is attempting to exert on NSF grantmaking. No thanks to your testimony, Science Committee Democrats know these facts, based on reporting and well corroborated sources: OSTP is exerting influence over NSF decision making, certainly on Notices of Funding Opportunities and potentially on at least a subset of grant decisions; NSF is 30-40% behind where it was last year at this time on getting money out the door; OSTP intends to spend hundreds of millions of dollars to fund your priority projects, and that money was not appropriated to OSTP by Congress.

You chose not to be transparent about this reported “Grand Research Challenges” program when you had the chance before the Committee. As Members of the Minority, at this time, we lack the ability to compel you to be forthright via testimony at a hearing. We request that you brief us on the “Grand Research Challenges” program by August 14, 2026. The briefing must include an explanation of the program, a breakdown of how this program is being funded, and a thorough description of how OSTP has been involved in the internal processes at NSF, so the Committee can understand what influence OSTP has exerted in NSF’s failure to spend appropriated money while you have seemingly found enough funding to push forward your pet priorities.

Pursuant to Rule X of the House of Representatives, the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology “shall review and study on a continuing basis laws, programs, and Government activities relating to nonmilitary research and development.” If you have any questions regarding this letter, please contact Sara Palasits or Albert Hinman with the Committee’s Minority staff at (202) 225-6375. Thank you for your attention to this important matter.
