title: SCHUMER CALLS ON USPS TO WORK WITH LOCAL COMMUNITY AND REOPEN WEST PARK POST OFFICE
text:
West Park Post Office Has Served Ulster County Community For More Than 130 Years Until USPS Abruptly Announced Its Closure, Forcing Customers To Travel Five Miles Away To Highland To Collect Mail Instead

Schumer Urges USPS To Restore Postal Operations So Residents And Small Businesses Can Easily Receive Medications, Checks & Bills, Packages, And Other Important Mail

Schumer To USPS: West Park Deserves A Post Office In West Park

After the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) announced its plan to close the West Park Post Office, and then officially closed the facility on July 24, impacting approximately 170 post office box holders, U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer called on the USPS to immediately restore the post office and work with the community to avoid disruptions to reliable mail service. For years, Schumer has fought relentlessly to protect post offices across Upstate New York, demanding accountability from the U.S. Postal Service, ensuring rural residents have a voice in decisions that affect them, and defending the local institutions that keep small communities connected.

“The West Park Post Office is more than a place where residents pick up mail and drop off packages; it’s the center of the community. The abrupt closure of this office, now forcing residents and small businesses to drive miles away to pick up medications, packages, and other important mail, is simply unacceptable,” said Senator Schumer. “Every day this post office remains closed is another day this community is without an essential asset it depends on. West Park deserves a post office in West Park, and that’s why I’m calling on the USPS to work with the community to reopen it immediately.”

"The West Park Post Office has been an important part of our hamlet for generations, providing essential services while serving as a place that connects neighbors and strengthens our community. On behalf of the Town of Esopus, I want to thank Senator Schumer for his continued support and for standing up for the residents of West Park and our entire community toward a solution that restores reliable postal service close to home," said Roscoe T. Pecora, Town Supervisor, Town of Esopus.

Earlier this year, the USPS announced its plan to close the West Park Post Office, forcing approximately 170 post office box holders to travel five miles away to Highland to collect their mail. The West Park community has rallied against the closure of its gathering place, emphasizing that residents and small businesses depend on the post office for medications, checks, bills, packages, and more. The USPS has not provided any updates to the local community, including the details of a new lease or a timeline for the potential reopening. Schumer said the USPS must work with local stakeholders to restore this essential public service for the West Park community.

Schumer’s letter to USPS Postmaster General David Steiner can be found HERE or below:

Dear Postmaster General Steiner,

I write with concern regarding the future of the West Park Post Office, located at 1740 US-9W, West Park, NY 12493. On July 24, 2026, the United States Postal Service (USPS) issued a temporary closure of the West Park Post Office, citing a loss of lease. Since then, USPS has provided no timeline or concrete plans to restore postal operations in West Park and to ensure that the community’s post office remains in West Park. I urge you to act swiftly and diligently to reinstate the post office in West Park, and to work transparently and collaboratively with community stakeholders in that process.

While I appreciate that the Postal Service has provided alternative mail services for West Park residents at the neighboring Highland Post Office, this location is more than five miles away for many residents, postal workers, and small business owners. West Park is a rural community and any disruptions to mail operations pose serious challenges for many of the residents and small businesses who depend on the Postal Service in their daily lives and who will now have to drive to another town to pick up their medications, checks and bills, packages, and other important mail.

Furthermore, in West Park, the post office is not just a place where residents pick up their mail and drop off their packages. The West Park Post Office is the heart and center of the town – it is the place where residents build close-knit connections with their neighbors and postal workers, and where they see West Park’s identity represented in a community space. The closure of West Park Post Office is a real detriment to the community and any further delays in reinstating the West Park Post Office are unacceptable.

Therefore, I urge the Postal Service to immediately act to reinstate the West Park Post Office. Again, I also urge the Postal Service to transparently engage with West Park residents and establish a clear plan to restore the West Park Post Office as quickly as possible. Thank you for your attention to this important matter. I look forward to your response.

title: ICYMI: At Senate Foreign Relations Hearing, Shaheen Highlights Impact of Global Scam Operations in New Hampshire, Urges Passage of Bipartisan SCAM Act
text:
(Washington, DC) – In case you missed it, at a Senate Foreign Relations Committee hearing, U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, highlighted the harmful impacts of online scams in the Granite State and described how overseas scam compounds are spreading rapidly across the globe. The hearing, entitled, “Protecting Americans from Global Scam Operations: Assessing the U.S. Response,” focused on transnational criminal organizations behind online scam operations and the bipartisan Scam Compound Accountability and Mobilization (SCAM) Act.

In her remarks, Shaheen described the proliferation of overseas scam compounds and emphasized how transnational scam operations threaten U.S. national security—exploiting corruption and weak governance while making billions of dollars that are often traced to Chinese criminal syndicates. Shaheen then underscored the importance of passing the SCAM Act to guarantee that coordinated international responses to scam compounds become a fixed part of U.S. policy.

Click HERE to watch Shaheen’s opening remarks.

Key quotes from Senator Shaheen:

“Behind many of the online scams targeting Americans are scam compounds where trafficked workers are forced to defraud victims online. Just a few years ago, these compounds were concentrated in a handful of countries. But today, scam operations have spread to countries across Africa, the Middle East, Asia and even in the Western Hemisphere. Americans lose more than $12 billion dollars—billion with a B—a year from schemes perpetrated by overseas scam compounds[ …] Global losses are now estimated to exceed $100 billion dollars each year. And every senator on this committee has constituents whose lives have been upended by sophisticated online fraud.”

“In Hollis, New Hampshire, one 78-year-old lost about $150,000 after being lured into a fraudulent online investment scheme. And another Granite State resident reported purchasing a vehicle online and lost $6,200 and never received the car, and his calls went unanswered. We’ve had a scam in New Hampshire targeting our EZ pass system that’s gone out to everyone who has an EZ pass in the state. [...] At a time when families are already feeling squeezed, they cannot afford to lose their hard-earned savings to fraud.”

“This hearing looks beyond those individual stories to the transnational criminal organizations behind many of these sophisticated fraud schemes and why law enforcement alone is not going to be able to dismantle them. These networks have direct consequences for U.S. national security—they span multiple countries, often eroding the rule of law and exploiting weak governance. And they thrive on corruption. They rely on victims from over 80 countries who have been trafficked and forced to carry out these scams. And they generate billions for transnational criminal organizations, many with links to China.”

“That’s exactly the approach Senator Cornyn and I put forward in the Scam Compound Accountability and Mobilization, or SCAM Act, which passed the Senate by unanimous consent. The bill would build on the Administration's work by making that coordinated international response a permanent part of U.S. policy.”

Full remarks as delivered:

Thank you, Mr. Chairman. And thank you to our witnesses for being here today. As the Chairman says, behind many of the online scams targeting Americans are scam compounds where trafficked workers are forced to defraud victims online. Just a few years ago, these compounds were concentrated in a handful of countries. But today, scam operations have spread to countries across Africa, the Middle East, Asia and even in the Western Hemisphere.

Americans lose more than $12 billion dollars—billion with a B—a year from schemes perpetrated by overseas scam compounds. We have that poster to just remind everybody about the total. Global losses are now estimated to exceed $100 billion dollars each year.

And every senator on this committee has constituents whose lives have been upended by sophisticated online fraud. In Hollis, New Hampshire, one 78-year-old lost about $150,000 after being lured into a fraudulent online investment scheme. And another Granite State resident reported purchasing a vehicle online and lost $6,200 and never received the car, and his calls went unanswered. We’ve had a scam in New Hampshire targeting our EZ pass system that’s gone out to everyone who has an EZ pass in the state. [...] At a time when families are already feeling squeezed, they cannot afford to lose their hard-earned savings to fraud.

This hearing looks beyond those individual stories to the transnational criminal organizations behind many of these sophisticated fraud schemes and why law enforcement alone is not going to be able to dismantle them.

These networks have direct consequences for U.S. national security—they span multiple countries, often eroding the rule of law and exploiting weak governance. And they thrive on corruption. They rely on victims from over 80 countries who have been trafficked and forced to carry out these scams. And they generate billions for transnational criminal organizations, many with links to China. Fighting them requires diplomacy, support for human trafficking victims, international law enforcement cooperation, sanctions and strong partnerships with foreign governments.

Now, the good news is that the United States has begun responding to this threat. The Administration has elevated countering scam compounds to be a national security priority. It has imposed sanctions on scam operators and human traffickers. And it has pursued criminal prosecutions and launched a government-wide effort to combat these networks.

These are important steps. But the criminal networks are adapting just as quickly. And when one country cracks down, they move somewhere else. Without a coordinated global response, it becomes a game of whack-a-mole. If these criminal organizations operate across borders, our response has to be to operate across borders. That means preventing recruitment, supporting trafficking survivors, working with our allies and partners and holding both criminal organizations and the governments that enable them accountable.

That’s exactly the approach Senator Cornyn and I put forward in the Scam Compound Accountability and Mobilization, or SCAM Act, [...] which passed the Senate by unanimous consent. The bill would build on the Administration’s work by making that coordinated international response a permanent part of U.S. policy.

Today’s hearing is about how we build on that progress. I look forward to hearing from our witnesses about what's working, about where the gaps remain and what it will take to build a response that is every bit as coordinated as the criminal networks we’re trying to defeat.

Again, thank you both for being here.

###

title: Sullivan Welcomes Over $2.3 Million for Seward Shipyard Upgrades
text:
SEWARD, ALASKA—U.S. Senator Dan Sullivan (R-Alaska), chairman of the Senate Commerce Subcommittee overseeing the Coast Guard, and Admiral Kevin Lunday, the 28th Commandant of the Coast Guard, yesterday celebrated the awarding of more than $2.3 million in federal grants to two Seward shipyard operators to expand vessel-handling capacity, modernize equipment, and strengthen Alaska’s maritime infrastructure. The announcement came during an event in the community with Admiral Lunday celebrating the forthcoming homeporting of an icebreaker in Seward.

The Maritime Administration’s (MARAD) Small Shipyard Grant Program awarded $916,223 to Catalyst Marine Engineering, LLC and $1,405,113 to JAG Alaska Inc. Sullivan and his Alaska congressional delegation colleagues supported both grants in letters to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy earlier this year.

The funding will enable Catalyst Marine Engineering to acquire advanced fabrication, welding, and material-handling equipment, and support JAG Alaska’s expansion of its rail system and acquisition of new carts and cradles to move vessels throughout the Seward Shipyard. These investments will also strengthen Seward’s maritime capacity as the community prepares to welcome a new Arctic Security Cutter. In June, the U.S. Coast Guard announced that the third Arctic Security Cutter funded through the Working Families Tax Cuts Act will be homeported in Seward once the necessary infrastructure is ready.

Click here or the image above for photos from the visit to Seward.

Click here to view opening remarks from Sen. Sullivan at the community event.

“These investments are another important part of what I call the ‘virtuous cycle’ in shipbuilding and ship maintenance that we’re delivering across our great state,” said Sen. Sullivan. “We bring more Coast Guard and NOAA vessels to Alaska, and Alaska workers maintain and repair them while generating even more maritime work right here in our state. Through the largest investment in Coast Guard history in the Working Families Tax Cuts Act—which I pushed for as chair of the Commerce Subcommittee that oversees the Coast Guard—we are seeing this cycle accelerate as we bring four icebreakers to Alaska, including one slated to be homeported in Seward, driving good-paying jobs and new investments in workforce development, housing, and infrastructure in our coastal communities. These grants will build on that momentum by expanding capacity and modernizing operations in Seward. I want to thank Secretary Duffy and MARAD Administrator Stephen Carmel for recognizing Seward’s vital role in Alaska’s maritime economy and working with me to support these important investments.”

“The Maritime Administration is deeply committed to supporting the vital maritime infrastructure of Alaska and delivering these grants is a direct reflection of our aggressive dedication to supporting Alaska's working waterfronts. Through these grants totaling over $2.3 million for Catalyst Marine Engineering and JAG Alaska, MARAD is proud to invest in the equipment and infrastructure that will keep Alaska's maritime sector efficient, competitive, and capable of sustaining good-paying jobs for years to come,” said Maritime Administrator Stephen M. Carmel.

title: Tuberville, Britt Work to End Practice of Releasing Illegals from Immigration Detention
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Tommy Tuberville (R-AL) joined U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-AL) in introducing the Keep Our Communities Safe Act of 2026. The legislation would close a legal loophole created by the United States Supreme Court’s 2001 ruling in Zadvydas v. Davis, which generally requires the release of aliens from immigration detention into American communities after six months if no country has accepted them for deportation.

“Joe Biden and Kamala Harris allowed millions of illegals to INVADE our country—and now law-abiding Americans are paying the price,” said Sen. Tuberville. “We need to do everything we can to deport every single one of these criminals. I’m proud to cosponsor the Keep Our Communities Safe Act to close this legal loophole and allow these illegals to be detained and sent home for good.”

“America is a nation of laws, and if you violate our laws and are subject to removal from the United States, you should remain in detention until the point of deportation,” said Sen. Britt. “Zadvydas v. Davis created a legal loophole that forces the release of aliens into our communities after six months simply because no country has agreed to take them back. This bill would help to close that loophole once and for all.”

Sens. Tuberville and Britt were joined by Sens. Ted Budd (R-NC), Tom Cotton (R-AR), Kevin Cramer (R-ND), Mike Crapo (R-ID), Ted Cruz (R-TX), Deb Fischer (R-NE), John Hoeven (R-ND), Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-MS), Roger Marshall (R-KS), Jim Risch (R-ID), and Mike Rounds (R-SD) in cosponsoring of this legislation.

Read full text of the bill here.

BACKGROUND:

The bill would amend Section 236 of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA), which governs the apprehension and detention of aliens, to expand the Department of Homeland Security’s (DHS) authority to detain criminal aliens, deny bond to criminal aliens, and generally limit the availability of bond unless an alien can establish by clear and convincing evidence that they’re not a flight risk or a risk to another person or the community.

It would also amend Section 241 of the INA, which governs the removal of aliens, to allow for extensions of detention in a number of cases, including in cases where an alien is a threat to national security or has committed an aggravated felony or crime of violence.

Senator Tommy Tuberville represents Alabama in the United States Senate and is a member of the Senate Armed Services, Agriculture, Veterans’ Affairs, HELP and Aging Committees.

title: Van Hollen Joins Padilla, Colleagues in Demanding State Department Process Student Visas Without Delays
text:
U.S. Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) joined Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.) and 28 of their Senate colleagues in expressing concern about the unavailability of student and exchange visitor visa appointments in time for the start of the academic year and demanding answers regarding delays in processing of these applications at U.S. embassies and consulates.

“We urge the State Department to ensure timely processing of F, M, and J student and exchange visitor nonimmigrant visas, consistent with the approach taken by administrations of both parties in the past, and to implement other measures to avoid diminishing U.S. competitiveness,” wrote the Senators. “Specifically, we are hearing from constituents and stakeholders that no timely visa appointments are available for students at some embassies and consulates. This only exacerbates uncertainty about whether students’ visas will be processed in time for them to travel to the United States to begin their studies.”

The Senators highlighted the vital contributions international students make to universities and communities nationwide, including expanding opportunities for American students, generating economic activity, strengthening the U.S. workforce, and building international partnerships.

“International students are critical to the success of our universities, including contributing nearly $43 billion annually to local communities and supporting more than 355,000 American jobs during the 2024-2025 academic year. Even though international students make up only six percent of the total higher education population, their enrollment creates opportunities for American students,” continued the Senators. “International students also improve our national security by fostering global relationships, cross cultural understanding, and long-lasting diplomatic ties. These benefits are at risk if visa processing delays persist.”

The Senators urged the State Department to ensure the timely review and processing of student and exchange visitor visas, extend interview waivers for vetted returning student applicants, provide sufficient staffing for visa processing, and improve transparency and engagement with stakeholders. The Senators also requested an explanation within 30 days about the causes of the delays and the measures being implemented to ensure student and exchange visitor visa applications are processed in a timely manner moving forward.

In addition to Van Hollen and Padilla, the letter was signed by U.S. Senators Dick Durbin (D-Ill.), Angela Alsobrooks (D-Md.), Michael Bennet (D-Colo.), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Chris Coons (D-Del.), Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.), Mazie Hirono (D-Hawaii), Tim Kaine (D-Va.), Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Angus King (I-Maine), Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.), Ben Ray Lujan (D-NM), Ed Markey (D-MA), Patty Murray (D-WA), Gary Peters (D-MI), Jack Reed (D-RI), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.), Tina Smith (D-Minn.), Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-Ga.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Peter Welch (D-Vt.), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), and Ron Wyden (D-Ore.).

The full text of letter is available here and below.

Dear Secretary Rubio,

We write to express our concerns regarding the ongoing unavailability of visa appointments during the peak visa application season for students and scholars seeking to enter the U.S. in time for the start of classes and the academic year. We urge the State Department to ensure timely processing of F, M, and J student and exchange visitor nonimmigrant visas, consistent with the approach taken by administrations of both parties in the past, and to implement other measures to avoid diminishing U.S. competitiveness. Specifically, we are hearing from constituents and stakeholders that no timely visa appointments are available for students at some embassies and consulates. This only exacerbates uncertainty about whether students’ visas will be processed in time for them to travel to the United States to begin their studies.

These challenges come at a time when major academic institutions need skilled, international talent to begin their semesters. Without a fix, the repercussions will be felt across the academic and skilled-technical talent pipeline.

International students are critical to the success of our universities, including contributing nearly $43 billion annually to local communities and supporting more than 355,000 American jobs during the 2024-2025 academic year. Even though international students make up only six percent of the total higher education population, their enrollment creates opportunities for American students. For every additional international undergraduate enrolled at a U.S. public university, two additional in-state freshman students can enroll. Most international students pay out-of-state tuition, injecting vital revenue into our colleges and universities and helping keep costs down for domestic students. International students also improve our national security by fostering global relationships, cross cultural understanding, and long-lasting diplomatic ties. These benefits are at risk if visa processing delays persist.

The case-by-case nature of availability for access to expedited appointments or National Interest Exception requests is neither efficient nor sustainable. Instead of diverting already limited personnel resources, the State Department should ensure that its consular sections restore priority to interview, adjudicate, and process student visas in time for the upcoming school year.

In addition to the above, we urge the State Department to extend interview waivers for vetted returning student applicants; ensure adequate staffing for timely visa vetting and processing; and meaningfully engage with stakeholders to promote greater transparency.

International students bolster the American workforce, drive innovation, and better position our country to maintain its competitive edge. Therefore, we request a written response answering these questions within 30 days:

1. What resources has the Department devoted to processing the backlogs and streamlining processing of F, J, and M visas?

2. Have consular process priorities changed since the spring and summer of 2025? What visa interview categories are currently prioritized by the Bureau of Consular Affairs and where do student visas fall within that list? Provide the list of visa interview prioritization.

3. What guidance has been sent to embassies and consulates regarding prioritization or deprioritization of student and exchange visitor visa processing? Provide a copy of all guidance regarding the prioritizing or deprioritizing of student and exchange visitor visas since August 2025 until the present day.

4. How are interview slots being allocated at embassies and consulates and where do student and exchange visitor visa appointments fit within that allocation?

5. How often are consular post websites and the main State Department website updated for relevant and current information regarding current U.S. consulate operations including visa appointment availability and approximate processing times?

6. When will you resume publicly posting monthly, accurate visa issuance data by category?

7. Will the Department commit to implementing regular, ongoing outreach and collaboration with stakeholders and relevant agencies about the student and exchange visitor visa process and ensure the timely processing of F, J, and M visas?

8. How do you ensure that embassies and consulates are accurately and timely informed of any regulatory or policy changes regarding student and exchange visitor visas?

9. What are the average processing times for F, M, and J visas at the top five locations processing these visas from September 2025 to date, disaggregated by month?

10. Last year, the Department of State announced new vetting, including online presence vetting, of all student and exchange visitor applicants in the F, M, and J nonimmigrant classification

title: Warner, Husted Lead Bipartisan Package of Bills to Strengthen U.S. National Security and Hold China Accountable
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Sens. Mark Warner (D-VA) and Jon Husted (R-OH) introduced a package of four bipartisan bills to strengthen America’s national security and close loopholes that foreign adversaries, including China, can exploit.

“The U.S. must continue to lead in the technologies that will define the future, and we cannot allow China or other foreign adversaries to exploit American innovation and turn our own technologies against us. These bipartisan bills make commonsense improvements that will strengthen America’s national security, protect our technological edge, and bolster our global competitiveness.” said Sen. Warner. “I’m proud to introduce this legislative package that would give us greater insight into our adversaries’ capabilities and better prevent advanced U.S. technologies from falling into the wrong hands.”

“America must continue to compete and win in the technology race, but we know that communist China’s strategy has never been to compete, but to steal and exploit. This bipartisan package would strengthen our understanding of China’s action, improve enforcement and protect American companies, workers and innovations from Chinese espionage,” said Sen. Husted.

The lawmakers introduced the following bills:

The China AI Power Report Act to require the Secretaries of Commerce and State, in consultation with relevant federal agencies, to provide an annual report on the People’s Republic of China’s efforts to indigenize its artificial intelligence (AI) stack. This report would include information on Beijing’s progress to develop home-grown chip design and production, semiconductor manufacturing equipment, subcomponent production, model development and deployment competencies.

The ECRA Statute of Limitations Extension to amend Sections 1760 and 1774 of the Export Control Reform Act (ECRA) to extend the statute of limitations for prosecuting violations of ECRA from five years to 10 years. ECRA currently lacks an explicit statute of limitations and is thus subject to the five-year federal period, even as Chinese technology smuggling operations frequently take years longer to uncover and prosecute.

The Addressing Dangerous Vulnerabilities in Exports and Research to Strategic Adversaries, Regimes and Industrial Entities of Security Concern (ADVERSARIES) Act to direct the Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) to study whether U.S.-domiciled affiliates of designated Chinese companies allow these companies to circumvent export controls to access controlled technologies.

The Bureau of Industry and Security Strategic Talent Recruitment to Enhance National Guardrails for Technological Handling (BIS STRENGTH) Act to grant BIS temporary hiring authority to recruit highly qualified subject matter experts to guide BIS management of advanced technology export controls and fill BIS technical expertise gaps.

All four of these bills have been introduced on a bipartisan basis in the U.S. House of Representatives. The China AI Power Report Act passed the House Committee on Foreign Affairs 47-0 on Jan. 21, 2026.

title: Warnock Secures Two-Year Extensions of AGOA, Haiti HOPE/HELP in Bipartisan Funding Bill
text:
Senator Reverend Raphael Warnock, Ranking Member of the Senate Finance Subcommittee on Trade, Customs, and Global Competitiveness, helped secure two-year extensions of AGOA, Haiti HOPE/HELP in last week’s bipartisan continuing resolution

The extension of the trade programs maintains duty-free access on more than 1,800 products from AGOA participating nations. It also extends the HOPE and HELP trade programs, which provide duty-free access for apparel and textile products from Haiti

Senator Reverend Warnock: “This extension is a win-win for Georgians and our trading partners in Haiti and Africa. It will lower the cost of everyday goods and improve our national security by helping stabilize the economies of our global partners”

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-GA), Ranking Member of the Senate Finance Subcommittee on International Trade, Customs, and Global Competitiveness, helped secure two-year extensions of the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), the Haiti Economic Lift Program (HELP), and the Haitian Hemispheric Opportunity through Partnership and Encouragement (HOPE) in last week’s bipartisan continuing resolution (CR). The extension of the trade programs maintains duty-free access on more than 1,800 products from eligible countries and extends the HOPE and HELP trade programs, which provide duty-free access for apparel and textile products from Haiti.

“This extension is a win-win for Georgians and our trading partners in Haiti and Africa,” said Senator Warnock. “It will lower the cost of everyday goods and improve our national security by helping stabilize the economies of our global partners. This victory shows what is possible when we center the people in policymaking.”

In the aftermath of the devastating 2010 earthquake in Haiti, Congress passed the HELP Act to broaden the types of goods eligible for duty-free status to over 5,000 types of apparel and footwear. The law, which helped rebuild some of Haiti’s domestic industry, expired October 1, 2025. In February 2025, Senator Warnock helped lead the reintroduction of the Haiti HELP Act. The legislation supports stable, safe jobs in Haiti while ensuring U.S. consumers have access to goods free from state-sponsored forced labor.

Senator Warnock uses his oversight role and jurisdiction in the global commerce space as a check against the Trump administration’s reckless trade and tariff policies and their devastating impact on Georgia’s families, farmers, small businesses, and thousands of hardworking Georgians. Last week, Senator Warnock secured a written commitment from the Trump administration that would limit the President’s tariff authorities in the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026. In March, Senator Warnock joined the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) for a fireside chat on the path forward for AGOA alongside Chairman of the Ways and Means Subcommittee on Trade Congressman Adrian Smith (R-NE).

title: Whitehouse and RI Law Enforcement Leaders Push for New Commander-Level Police Training Bill
text:
Promoting Police Leadership Act will provide better training for the police leaders running day-to-day operations

Barrington, RI – U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse today joined RI Police Chiefs Association President Michael Correia, David Lambert, Director of the Roger Williams University Justice System Training and Research Institute, and Family Service of RI CEO Margaret Holland McDuff to push for final passage of Whitehouse’s Promoting Police Leadership Act.

“Rhode Island’s captains, majors, and precinct commanders know that proper training for their officers is key to making decisions that keep our communities safe. They, too, deserve training programs that keep pace with the new demands constantly placed on them,” said Whitehouse. “I’m grateful to Rhode Island’s finest for joining me today, and for their support in getting this bill passed in the Senate.”

The Promoting Police Leadership Act would support the development of commander-level law enforcement leadership training and education curricula to enhance police operations, increase officer accountability and wellness, improve resource management, and strengthen community relations.

The bipartisan bill would task the U.S. Attorney General and Department of Justice with developing a broad training curricula framework for commander-level personnel in consultation with state, local, and tribal law enforcement agencies, academic institutions, and other relevant partners. The legislation would also establish a voluntary certification process for the Attorney General to identify high-quality training programs that align with the broader DOJ framework and provide instruction to police departments. The legislation unanimously passed the Senate in June and now awaits a vote in the House.

“We are grateful for Senator Whitehouse’s leadership in advancing the Promoting Police Leadership Act through the Senate,” said Colonel Michael Correia, Chief of Police for Barrington and President of the Rhode Island Police Chiefs Association. “Strong police departments depend on strong leaders, and this legislation will help ensure that the next generation of law enforcement leaders has the training and preparation needed to meet the challenges ahead. We hope today’s event will help build the support necessary to pass this important legislation in the House and ultimately make it law.”

“De-escalation isn’t about asking law enforcement to do less — it’s about giving officers more tools to keep everyone safe. After more than 20 years of working alongside police and training professionals through FSRI’s Go Team and Trauma Informed Policing Center, we know that when officers understand trauma and have the skills to slow a crisis down, the outcome can change dramatically for a child, a family, and the officer,” said Margaret Holland McDuff, CEO of Family Service of Rhode Island.

“The Promoting Police Leadership Act is essential in the development of professionalism in policing and assisting police leaders in translating evidence-based practices such as community policing, problem solving, crime analytics, trauma-informed practices and risk management into an agency’s business processes,” said David Lambert, Director of the Roger Williams University Justice System Training and Research Institute.

The legislation is endorsed by Law Enforcement Action Partnership, Major County Sheriffs of America, and National Narcotic Officers’ Associations’ Coalition.

Whitehouse has previously teamed up with Senator John Cornyn (R-TX) on the Law Enforcement De-escalation Training Act, a 2022 law that required the Department of Justice to work with experts to develop comprehensive trainings on de-escalation tactics, alternatives to use of force, safely responding to mental, behavioral, and suicidal crises, and making referrals to community-based mental and behavioral health services and other social programs.

title: Rep. Aguilar Delivers Over $1 Million to Expand Affordable Housing and Address Homelessness in Fontana
text:
Press Releases

Rep. Aguilar Delivers Over $1 Million to Expand Affordable Housing and Address Homelessness in Fontana

The funding will help address affordable housing shortages in the City of Fontana and give more low-income Fontana residents pathways to permanent housing

FONTANA, CA – Rep. Pete Aguilar announced that he secured $1.2 million in community project funding for the City of Fontana’s Aldea Apartments Acquisition Phase II project. This grant funding will help expand affordable housing and address homelessness in the Inland Empire by purchasing 2.4 acres of land adjacent to the Aldea Apartments building, where 80 additional housing units will be built. Additionally, the funding will support much-needed upgrades to the existing building’s outdoor amenities to improve residents’ quality of life, including the construction of a children’s playground, dog park and parking lot.

Once complete, the Aldea Apartments will serve as a bridge between temporary shelter programs and permanent housing, giving individuals and families at risk of falling into homelessness a stable, low-cost place to live. You can watch the full video of the press conference here and find photos from the event above and here.

“Here in the Inland Empire, we know how important it is for our neighbors to have access to safe and affordable homes for their families, even when they fall on hard times,” said Rep. Pete Aguilar. “That’s why I’m proud to deliver $1.2 million for the City of Fontana to upgrade and expand the Aldea Apartments, giving families at risk of homelessness a stable, low-cost and comfortable place to call home. I’ll keep fighting to lower the cost of housing and deliver more resources that help families in our community build brighter futures.”

“Support from our partners, like Congressman Pete Aguilar, serves as a foundation for building a strong, thriving community,” said Mayor Acquanetta Warren, City of Fontana. “This funding for the next stage of the Aldea Apartments reflects Fontana’s vision of a community where all residents can find housing stability and opportunities. Congressman Aguilar’s leadership will have a lasting impact in Fontana.”

As a Member of the House Appropriations Committee, Rep. Aguilar secured $19.7 million for 15 projects in California’s 33rd Congressional District in the Fiscal Year (FY) 2026.

title: Congressman Al Green Hosts Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Inc. Slavery Remembrance Legislative Update and Assembly in the Capitol Visitor’s Center Auditorium
text:
(Washington, D.C.) — On Saturday, August 15, 2026, Congressman Al Green will host Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Inc. for a historic Slavery Remembrance Legislative Update and Assembly to implement a National Day of Slavery Remembrance on August 20th annually. The annual event will help ensure the evils of slavery are never forgotten and thus never repeated. The assembly will be held in the Capitol Visitor’s Center Auditorium located at 2 U.S. Senate Drive, Washington, D.C., 20510, at 11:00 a.m. ET.

The theme of this year’s Slavery Remembrance Day is “Harder Yet May Be the Fight.” The event will spotlight key legislative initiatives, including the legislation establishing Slavery Remembrance Day. Congressman Green will highlight efforts to secure Congressional Gold Medals for the enslaved, recognizing their immense contributions as the foundational mothers and fathers of America’s economic greatness. This effort also seeks to address a historical disparity in congressional recognition, as Congress authorized medals honoring Confederate veterans in 1956 while no comparable honor has been bestowed upon the enslaved persons whose uncompensated labor helped build the nation.

“Today, there is a national effort to erase or negate the sacrifices, struggles, and contributions of African Americans,” said Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Inc. General President Brother Lucien J. Metellus, Jr. “Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Inc. recognizes the importance of a National Slavery Remembrance Day and refuses to allow the evils of slavery to be forgotten or our ancestors not properly honored.”

Congressman Al Green stated, “I am honored to stand with my brothers of Alpha Phi Alpha Fraternity, Inc., an organization with a proud history of leadership in the continuing struggle for justice and equality, as we advance the cause of Slavery Remembrance Day. Together, we seek to honor the millions of enslaved persons whose sacrifices and uncompensated labor helped lay the economic foundation upon which America’s greatness was built. Remembrance requires more than reflection; it requires us to confront our history and pursue reconciliation, repair, and reparations."

title: Barrett Meets with Mid-Michigan Farmers to Discuss Trade, Joins Effort to Strengthen USMCA
text:
St. Johns, Mich. — Congressman Tom Barrett (MI-07) on Tuesday met with mid-Michigan farmers, producers, and agricultural industry leaders to discuss trade policy and hear their priorities for negotiations around extending the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA).

A few days prior to the roundtable discussion, which was hosted by Farmers for Free Trade at AgroLiquid in St. Johns, Barrett joined a majority of House Republicans in sending a letter to U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer pushing for improvements to the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) before agreeing to an extension.

“The farmers and producers in our mid-Michigan agricultural community work tirelessly to raise the animals and grow the food we all rely on,” said Congressman Tom Barrett. “Thanks to Farmers for Free Trade for bringing so many of them together. It was great to meet with them to hear how competitive access to trade markets in Canada and Mexico will help give them the certainty they need to continue fulfilling that mission. That goal — and leveling the playing field — must remain a top priority as the Trump administration begins renegotiating the USMCA.”

“We appreciate Congressman Tom Barrett for meeting with mid-Michigan agriculture leaders to discuss the importance of North American trade for our industry,” said Michigan Agri-Business Association President Chuck Lippstreu. “Michigan agriculture benefits greatly from exports and relies on strong trading relationships with Canada and Mexico. North American agricultural trade remains a top priority for our organization because exports are a key ingredient in the success of our state’s agricultural sector and broader rural economy.”

“Thank you to Congressman Tom Barrett for meeting with mid-Michigan farmers and agriculture leaders to discuss the ongoing USMCA negotiations,” said Jacob Smith, Michigan Farm Bureau Associate National Legislative Counsel. “A strong trading relation with our neighbors is vital to Michigan agriculture and ensures a dependable agriculture market across North America.”

“Canada and Mexico are Michigan's top two agricultural markets, and more than $1.7 billion in Michigan farm and food exports depend on them,” said Brian Kuhel, Executive Director of Farmers for Free Trade. “Congressman Barrett gave producers a direct line into that conversation today, and that is what the Joint Review needs. We are encouraged by the work underway to extend and strengthen USMCA, and we want farmer voices shaping that work.”

The letter, which 168 House Republicans signed, supports the Trump administration’s approach to the Joint Review process, which prioritizes outcomes over a set deadline to secure an extension.

“We believe that the USMCA has delivered many positive benefits, but there are key improvements that can and should be made through the Joint Review process,” said the lawmakers. “Thus, while our desired result is an extension agreed to by the United States, Mexico, and Canada, we support the decision to prioritize outcomes over a deadline. We hope that Mexico and Canada work constructively and expeditiously to achieve that result.”

They continued, “Those outcomes should include securing market access that was promised six years ago but not meaningfully delivered; addressing new actions taken by Mexico and Canada that harm American manufacturers, agriculture, service providers, and workers; confronting unfair trade and investment practices from third countries that seek to undermine the North American economy and threaten American jobs; and rationalizing tariff structures to strengthen regional competitiveness in the global marketplace.”

July 1 marked the first USMCA Joint Review, in which the U.S., Mexico, and Canada met to decide whether to extend the agreement for 16 more years. Mexico and Canada agreed to an extension, while the U.S. did not.

The USMCA remains in force until 2036 as the three sides continue to discuss improvements to the agreement.

title: Congressman Bell Hosts Women Veterans Roundtable to Address Issues Facing Veteran Communities
text:
The discussion brought together women veterans and veteran advocates from across the St. Louis region

The roundtable addressed problems specific to women veterans

Women are among the fastest-growing groups in the armed forces and veteran community

Congressman Bell during the discussion: “Your [female servicemembers] experiences are not a footnote to the veteran story. They are central to it”

St. Louis, Missouri – On Monday, Congressman Wesley Bell (D-MO-01) hosted a roundtable event for women veterans in the St. Louis region. During the discussion, the group of veterans addressed unique problems they have faced as women in a historically male-dominated field.

“Women are among the fastest-growing groups of veterans in this country,” said Congressman Bell during the roundtable. “And for too long, the systems meant to serve you were built without you in mind. Too many women veterans have been asked whether they're really the veteran in the family. Too many have struggled to get health care designed for their needs. Too many have navigated the benefits process, the disability claims process, the transition home, feeling like they had to fight a second battle just to receive what they earned. This is simply unacceptable.”

Additionally, Congressman Bell noted that this conversation was about large-scale women veterans’ issues and that his office remained available for specific problems people faced with their benefits or care.

“We have an obligation to ensure we do everything we can to fight for our vets when they return home. This includes fighting for proper healthcare, housing, and resources,” said Rep. Bell. “While today’s conversation is about the big-picture issues facing our veteran community, if you're dealing with a specific problem, my office is here for you. My casework team is the best, and they can sit down with you one-on-one to assist with whatever specific issues you are facing. No one should leave here today without knowing where to turn.”

Missouri has a long history as a military state, home to multiple installations and training centers spanning several branches of the armed forces. The St. Louis region boasts a significant defense industry footprint. As a member of the House Armed Services Committee, Congressman Bell has been a steadfast supporter of the military community and our nation's veterans. Legislatively, Bell has championed bills like the Healthy Servicemembers Act, the Veterans Career Connection Act, the Forward Act, the Improving Menopause Care for Veterans Act, and the Guard VA Benefits Act, all pieces of legislation aimed at improving services and support for veterans, specifically women veterans.

###

Wesley Bell is the U.S. Representative for Missouri's First Congressional District, which includes St. Louis City and a portion of St. Louis County. He is a member of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee, House Armed Services Committee, and House Foreign Affairs Committee.

title: CONGRESSWOMAN BOEBERT WELCOMES DOE DECISION TO CANCEL SOUTHWESTERN GRID CONNECTOR CORRIDOR
text:
Lamar, CO — Congresswoman Lauren Boebert (R-CO) issued the following statements on the Department of Energy’s decision to cancel three proposed National Interest Electric Transmission Corridors (NIETCs):

“I welcome the Department of Energy’s decision to cancel the three previously proposed National Interest Electric Transmission Corridors, including the Southwestern Grid Connector Corridor. This is a smart course correction,” said Rep. Boebert.

A NIETC is a narrow geographic area where DOE has determined that transmission constraints or congestion are raising costs or hurting reliability for American consumers. The designation is meant to help prioritize urgently needed transmission projects — not dictate specific routes or override local communities.

After extensive public feedback from landowners, local governments, Tribes, and other stakeholders, DOE rightly recognized that the process for these three corridors had created confusion and concern. The canceled proposals are the Lake Erie–Canada Corridor, the Southwestern Grid Connector Corridor, and the Tribal Energy Access Corridor.

"American families and businesses need a strong, reliable electric grid—not federal processes that create more uncertainty than progress. As a strong advocate for rural Colorado, I will continue fighting to protect consumers, private property rights, and local input,” said Rep. Boebert.

Background: DOE reviewed extensive public feedback and determined that the current NIETC designation process for these three proposed corridors was not effectively supporting transmission development. In some regions, the process created confusion, concern, and misunderstandings about DOE’s authorities and intentions. Moving forward, DOE will pursue transmission planning strategies that are more effective, better aligned with state and local priorities, and consistent with Administration policies focused on affordability, reliability, and security.

Importantly, DOE is not ending the NIETC program. It is recalibrating the process to better align with state and local priorities, the upcoming 2026 National Transmission Needs Study, and a clear focus on affordability, reliability, and energy security.

title: Burlison Unveils Trillion-Dollar Pay-For in Great American Healthcare Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Eric Burlison (MO-07) today unveiled the pay-for included in his Great American Healthcare Act: a provision targeting a Federal Reserve payment stream that outside research projects will exceed $1 trillion over the next decade. The Foundation for Government Accountability produced the projection, which was subsequently incorporated into the Heritage Foundation’s 2026 American Opportunity Agenda.

The legislation would repeal the Federal Reserve’s broad authority to pay interest on reserve balances while preserving a narrower earnings mechanism for supplemental reserves. The projected savings would offset reforms designed to put patients back in control of their healthcare dollars.

“Every healthcare proposal eventually runs into the same question: How do you pay for it?” Burlison said. “My bill answers that question. By reforming the Federal Reserve’s authority to pay interest on reserve balances, we can use the savings to help offset the cost of putting patients back in charge of their health care.”

The Great American Healthcare Act would allow every American to have a health savings account (HSA), raise the annual contribution limit to the same level as a 401(k), expand qualified HSA expenses, create new healthcare options, strengthen price transparency and improve access to prescription drugs. The bill would also allow families to transfer up to $5,000 tax-free from an HSA into a Trump Account, helping the next generation begin building long-term savings.

“Americans already spend enough on health care,” Burlison continued. “The problem is that patients rarely control the money. This bill changes that dynamic—and includes a real pay-for to make it possible.”

title: Castro, San Antonio Delegation Urge Cities to End Their 287(g) Agreements with ICE
text:
“They want to wreck families. They know what they are doing.”

San Antonio, TX — Today, Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20), Congressman Greg Casar (TX-35), and Texas Reps. Trey Martinez Fischer, and Barbara Gervin-Hawkins announced they have asked six San Antonio area municipalities—Balcones Heights, China Grove, Hollywood Park, Saint Hedwig, Sandy Oaks, and Von Ormy— to withdraw from their 287(g) agreements with ICE. These agreements surged under the Trump Administration and allow local police officers to act as ICE agents and conduct immigration enforcement.

Congressman Castro led 14 of his colleagues, including state legislators and county commissioners, in a letter to the mayors of these municipalities urging them to end their harmful contracts and publicly release the details of their participation in the program.

Watch press conference here.

“Cities in Bexar County should reconsider their cooperative agreements with ICE. Parents have stopped sending their kids to school, people are afraid to show up to their places of worship, and businesses are losing their employees. U.S. citizens, legal permanent residents, and folks who have work authorizations get locked up because of President Trump and Governor Abbott’s mass deportation machine. They are racially profiling folks and wrecking families. Bexar County residents deserve leadership that protects them from an abusive and rogue agency,” said Congressman Castro.

"These agreements take cops off of their local beat to prioritize separating immigrant families instead," said Congressman Casar. "To every Bexar County mayor: don't balance your budget through harassment, discrimination, and separating families. Read our letter, answer our questions, and end these agreements."

“Today, I stood with my Federal and State Colleagues to speak out against the injustice and inhumanity of the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement's 287(g) program,” said Rep. Gervin-Hawkins. “The negative impacts this program will have in our communities of color are detrimental and unacceptable. Most importantly, it erodes community trust and public safety. Our communities will be afraid of first responders, unreported crimes will increase, victims of crimes will be revictimized, racial profiling will intensify, the number of unlawful and prolonged detention of individuals will rise. This is not what our forefathers envisioned for our country. I will continue to fight against injustice and stand for the humane treatment of all.”

Read the letter to the mayors of Balcones Heights, China Grove, Hollywood Park, Saint Hedwig, Sandy Oaks, and Von Ormy.

The letter is co-signed by: Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20), Congressman Greg Casar (TX-35), Texas Senator Ronald Gutierrez, Texas Senator Jose Menendez, Texas Rep. Diego Bernal, Texas Rep. Philip Cortez, Texas Rep. Barbara Gervin-Hawkins, Texas Rep. Elizabeth Campos, Texas Rep. Josey Garcia, Texas Rep. Trey Martinez Fischer, Texas Rep. Ray Lopez, Bexar County Commissioner Justin Rodriguez, Bexar County Commissioner Rebeca Clay-Flores, Bexar County Commissioner Tommy Calvert, and Bexar County Judge Peter Sakai.

Congressman Castro’s remarks as delivered:

I'm Congressman Joaquin Castro, and very proud to represent our hometown of San Antonio in the U.S. House of Representatives. And want to say a special thank you today to the representatives who have joined me, my colleague in the U.S. House of Representatives, who also represents a big part of San Antonio, Greg Casar, also two state representatives, Trey Martinez Fisher, who represents the West and the Northwest Side, and also Representative Barbara Gervin-Hawkins, who represents big parts of the East Side and the Northeast side.

I want to say thank you to them for being here today.

Myself and 14 of my colleagues are asking that China Grove, Balcones Heights, Hollywood Park, Saint Hedwig, Von Army, and Sandy Oaks cities within Bexar County end their 287(g) agreements with ICE. For those that aren't familiar, 287(g) refers to Section 287(g) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, a federal law that lets ICE deputize state and local police officers to carry out federal immigration enforcement. These six cities signed on to what's called a task force model, specifically the version that allows local officers to stop, question, and detain people based on nothing more than suspicion that they may be in the country illegally.

Now, this, as y'all can imagine, has led to a lot of racial profiling within Bexar County and around the country, and it effectively turns a hometown police department into an arm of federal immigration enforcement. So they're turning local law enforcement into ICE agents and receiving money to do that.

In fact, after talking to some council members and at least one of the mayors of the cities, I believe that a big part of the reason that they're doing this is they're trying to balance their budgets with this money, because they receive money for each officer that is trained to carry out this partnership with ICE. Bear in mind that ICE has become a rogue, abusive organization under Donald Trump. We've seen their brutality on their on the streets, but also ICE seen their brutality, as has Greg, behind the closed doors of places like the Dilley Trailer Prison.

We've seen this cruelty in San Antonio as well, and as I said, they're racially profiling folks. So if you are someone who has brown skin, who speaks Spanish in public, or who works a certain job or goes to a certain place, they've been staking out places like Home Depot and Lowe's and other places where hardworking men and women will go to get supplies, and bear in mind, we shouldn't forget that Greg Abbott is a full partner in Donald Trump's mass deportation campaign. The excess, the cruelty, the warrantless searches, the guns drawn, the masks—all of it—Greg Abbott is just as responsible as Donald Trump in Texas.

He's partnered with the Trump Administration and flooded our streets with ICE officers and also DPS officers who are working hand in hand with what has become a rogue, abusive agency. They're going after children, and folks who have not, who have no criminal record, and who have done nothing wrong, and that includes, as you all know, U.S. citizens who have been ensnared in this, legal permanent residents, and even folks who have permission to be in the country and work authorization. So let me be clear: these agreements should end because people like 20-year-old Herbert Ibarra Castro end up locked up.

This was a story of Herbert, who was a mariachi performer. What started out as a routine traffic stop for the San Antonio mariachi student turned into his family's worst nightmare. He was pulled over for speeding in China Grove. Minutes later, ICE showed up and took him. Herbert was married to a U.S. citizen and had just filed paperwork for his green card. Since then, Herbert's been released, but he should have never been locked up in the first place. And over a month ago, Texas DPS stopped Jesus Bracho on his way to work, he was with his nine-year-old daughter Katherine. DPS called ICE, took Jesus, and minutes later returned for Katherine so that they could take her as well. And ICE forced Jesus to lure his daughter out of his boss's house.

And I posted that video, and others have as well on social media, she was scared and didn't know where she was being taken, and they are both still sitting at the Dilley Trailer Prison. Because of these 287(g) agreements, local law enforcement officers are essentially partners in ICE's cruelty, and our community. In many places, folks are scared and terrified. Some students in San Antonio stop showing up at school. Folks are afraid to show up to their places of worship, or even go to work. Businesses have lost employees. Some businesses have told me that either they've shut down, or they're on the verge of shutting down and going broke.

And that's why we're calling on the mayors of Balcones Heights, China Grove, St. Hedwig, Von Army, Sandy Oaks, and Hollywood Park to reconsider and to withdraw these contracts. Our communities deserve police who protect them, not law enforcement that troll that fuels Donald Trump and Greg Abbott's mass deportation machine.

title: Lakewood Alerts article on Smith-led letter to U.S. Postmaster General'Jackson Officials Push USPS to Address Overcrowding, Traffic and Safety Concerns at Post Office'
text:
By Lakewood Alerts

Published August 12, 2026

Jackson Township officials are pressing the United States Postal Service for action over longstanding concerns at the Jackson Post Office on Bennetts Mills Road, including overcrowding, lengthy wait times, inadequate parking, staffing shortages and growing traffic and safety issues.

Residents have repeatedly raised concerns about vehicles backing onto Bennetts Mills Road, traffic extending beyond the post office property and difficulties safely entering and exiting the busy facility.

On August 7, a formal letter was sent to U.S. Postmaster General David Steiner requesting a meeting to address what local officials described as an ongoing postal service crisis in the rapidly growing township.

The effort is being backed across multiple levels of government, with Congressman Christopher Smith, State Senator Owen Henry and Assemblymen Alex Sauickie and Robert Clifton joining Jackson Township officials in calling for improvements.

Among the solutions being urged are the establishment of a second full-service post office in Jackson, a significant expansion and modernization of the existing Bennetts Mills Road facility, and immediate operational changes to improve staffing, reduce wait times and address traffic and public safety concerns while a permanent solution is developed.

Officials stressed that the situation has grown beyond an issue of inconvenience and has become a public safety concern.

Jackson has experienced tremendous population growth in recent years, while its postal infrastructure has failed to keep pace with the increased demand. Officials said residents deserve safe and reasonable access to essential postal services and vowed to continue working with USPS toward a long-term solution.

title: Shore News Network article on Smith-led letter to U.S. Postmaster General'Jackson Post Office is Overwhelmed and Understaffed, Congressman Calls for Change'
text:
By Phil Stilton

Published August 12, 2026

Jackson, NJ – Anyone who has ever been to the Jackson Township U.S. Post Office on Bennetts Mills Road knows the place is a nightmare, especially after the federal agency closed the town’s other post office many years ago.

With the rise in population in Jackson, people often cite their visit to the Jackson post office as not-so-pleasant experience…and it’s getting worse.

Now, a coalition of elected officials is urging the U.S. Postal Service to take immediate action to address longstanding service problems at the Jackson Township Post Office, including considering the construction of a second full-service postal facility to meet the needs of one of New Jersey’s fastest-growing communities.

They say the location is now a public safety risk.

Jackson is expected to hit 200,000 residents within 9 years, according to county officials. Things are going to get worse.

Cassville Post Office – 2013. Shut down by USPS in 2012.

In an August 7 letter to Postmaster General David Steiner, Congressman Chris Smith, State Senator Owen Henry, Assemblymen Alex Sauickie and Robert Clifton, and Interim Mayor Jennifer Kuhn requested a formal meeting with USPS leadership to discuss solutions to what they describe as an ongoing postal service crisis.

The officials said residents have repeatedly voiced concerns about long wait times, overcrowding, inadequate parking, traffic congestion and staffing shortages at the Bennetts Mills Road post office.

“Our residents and businesses have repeatedly expressed grave concern over deteriorating service conditions, unsafe access, excessive wait times, and the inability of the current postal facility to adequately serve its residents,” the delegation wrote. “As their elected representatives, we have a responsibility to ensure their concerns are heard and addressed.”

Congressman, lawmakers say growth has overwhelmed postal system

The letter notes Jackson Township has experienced decades of rapid growth, with its population increasing from about 25,600 residents in 1980 to nearly 61,000 today. Officials argue the township’s postal infrastructure has not kept pace with that expansion.

In fact, it has shrunk. The Cassville Postal Station at 520 West Veterans Highway in Jackson, New Jersey, was suspended in December 2012 after its lease expired and could not be renewed. Operations were officially moved to the main Jackson Post Office at 915 Bennetts Mills Road.

That building now operates as a pet crematorium and funeral home.

“The postal infrastructure serving our community has not kept pace with the growth and needs of your postal customers,” the officials wrote.

The facility at 915 Bennetts Mills Road now experiences routine overcrowding, lengthy customer waits, insufficient parking and traffic backups that extend onto Bennetts Mills Road.

The officials said the situation has evolved beyond customer inconvenience.

“This is no longer simply an issue of customer convenience; it is a matter of public safety and government responsibility,” the letter states.

Officials seek second post office and facility expansion

Among the recommendations, the officials urged USPS to evaluate opening a second full-service post office in Jackson Township, modernizing and expanding the existing Bennetts Mills Road facility, and implementing immediate operational improvements to staffing and customer service.

The letter also points out that Jackson once had two postal facilities. The Cassville Post Office, located on West Veterans Highway, closed in 2012 because of lease-related issues, leaving the township dependent on a single location.

The local officials argue that today’s population and commercial growth far exceed what the remaining facility was designed to handle…and it definitely will not accomodate the anticipated growth level of 200,000 residents, even as the need for postal services declines.

“We strongly believe the time has come for decisive action,” the delegation wrote, specifically requesting USPS evaluate establishing “a second full-service postal facility within Jackson Township,” while also expanding parking, improving traffic flow, increasing staffing and modernizing the existing location.

Interim Mayor Jennifer Kuhn said she has visited the Bennetts Mills Road facility and witnessed traffic congestion and safety concerns firsthand. However, the request is presented as a joint effort led by the township’s congressional, state and municipal delegation.

title: Ciscomani Announces $2 Million in Preliminarily Secured Funding for Rural Health Care, Benefiting Benson Hospital and Chiricahua Community Health Center
text:
Benson, AZ - U.S. Representative Juan Ciscomani today saw firsthand how the $2 million federal investment he preliminarily secured for Benson Hospital will expand access to critical health care in rural Cochise County.

The $2 million preliminarily secured for Benson Hospital is part of 20 other Community Project Funding requests totaling $42.7 million that Ciscomani has advocated for in this year’s House appropriations bills to strengthen communities across Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District.

The funding for the Benson Hospital Emergency Department and Laboratory Modernization Project is included in the Fiscal Year 2027 Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies (LHHS) Appropriations bill, which Ciscomani voted to advance out of the Appropriations committee. The funding is set to expand the hospital’s emergency department and construct a modern laboratory to meet increasing demand for medically underserved parts of Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District.

"As Arizona’s sole appropriator in either the House or Senate, I have made it my mission to relentlessly advocate for Southern Arizona by listening to the needs of our communities and fighting to bring those priorities to Washington," Rep. Ciscomani said after touring Benson Hospital. "This $2 million investment will be a game-changer for Cochise County and the families who rely on Benson Hospital for critical care. I was proud to advocate for this funding on the House Appropriations Committee and to see firsthand how this investment will strengthen the hospital, reaffirming why it was worth fighting for. Hardworking Arizonans drive every Community Project Funding request I champion, ensuring taxpayer dollars are invested where they will have the greatest impact. I will continue working to strengthen rural health care and ensure Southern Arizona families have access to quality care close to home."

The congressman’s efforts are praised by local rural health care leaders.

"Congressman Ciscomani has been a strong partner in helping TMC Health meet the growing health care needs of our community. His advocacy at the federal level will help us expand our emergency department and construct a modern laboratory at Benson Hospital, strengthening access to critical care and essential health infrastructure in our rural community. We are grateful for his leadership and continued commitment to rural hospitals in our region," said Julia Strange, Vice President of External Affairs and Brand for TMC Health.

"Benson Hospital plays a vital role in providing emergency and specialty care to residents across southeastern Arizona. As a designated Critical Access Hospital and Level IV Trauma Center, we serve not only local families, but also residents, travelers, and communities along a major highway corridor between Tucson and New Mexico. Congressman Ciscomani understands how important this access to care is for our rural communities, and we appreciate his commitment to helping us expand our emergency department and build a modern laboratory to meet the growing needs of our local community," said Gary Kartchner, CEO of Benson Hospital.

Ciscomani’s visit to Benson and the Chiricahua Community Health Center also highlighted his broader efforts to expand access to quality care in medically underserved communities. The FY2027 House LHHS Appropriations bill, which Ciscomani voted to advance, includes $55 million for primary care training programs in rural and underserved areas, including $5 million to support medical school partnerships with Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs).

​Ciscomani is also a co-sponsor of the CONNECT for Health Act of 2025, which would permanently expand access to telehealth services for Medicare beneficiaries and ensure that FQHCs are reimbursed by Medicare for providing those services. Together, these efforts reflect Ciscomani’s ongoing commitment to strengthening rural health care and ensuring families have care close to home in Southern Arizona.

title: Ciscomani Urges HHS Secretary Kennedy to Keep Tucson Indian Health Services Open
text:
Tucson, AZ - U.S. Representative Juan Ciscomani is urging the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services to suspend plans to close a federal health care facility in Tucson that serves nearly 28,000 members of the Pascua Yaqui Tribe and Tohono O’odham Nation.

In a letter to the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert Kennedy Jr., Ciscomani called the Tucson Area Office of the Indian Health Service an essential lifeline for the two Southern Arizona tribes.

"For tribal communities across Arizona’s Sixth District, Tucson Indian Health Services is a critical health care lifeline, serving nearly 28,000 members of our local community. Closing this facility would have damaging effects that ripple throughout Southern Arizona, forcing patients to travel farther for care and placing additional strain on the Phoenix office. I am urging Secretary Kennedy to carefully reconsider the proposed consolidation and ensure tribal communities are fully consulted before any final decisions are made surrounding the Tucson IHS. Arizona’s tribal communities deserve continued access to the quality care and services they have relied on for decades," said Representative Ciscomani.

Under the proposed HHS plan, administrative and oversight functions currently based in Tucson would move to Phoenix. This would require patients, tribal health staff, and administrators to travel more than 100 miles to access services and support that have been available locally in Arizona’s Sixth District for nearly 20 years.

The proposed consolidation has also raised concerns about the future of specialized services, including dedicated diabetes care, which could be disrupted by the reorganization.

The Pascua Yaqui Tribe applauded Congressman Ciscomani’s leadership in raising concerns about the potential closure and advocating for continued access to critical health services in Southern Arizona.

"On behalf of the Pascua Yaqui Tribe, I thank Congressman Ciscomani for reaching out directly to Secretary Kennedy and advocating for Arizona’s Tribal communities; preserving the Tucson Area IHS Office is critical to protecting the health care and federal services our people depend on," said Pascua Yaqui Chairman Julian Hernanadez.

​In his letter to Secretary Kennedy, Representative Ciscomani urged the IHS to take a closer look at the proposed consolidation and consider the concerns raised by tribal leaders and health care providers.

"Specifically, I am writing regarding the Indian Health Service’s (IHS) proposal to eliminate the Tucson Area Office and consolidate its functions into the Phoenix Area Office. I represent Arizona’s Sixth District, which borders tribal communities of Southern Arizona, and I have heard from tribal leaders, health care providers, and constituents who are concerned about what this change would mean for their access to care.

"I wanted to bring their perspective to your attention and ask that IHS take a closer look before moving forward. The Tucson Area Office coordinates health services for approximately 28,000 patients, the great majority of whom are tribal citizens of Southern Arizona. Under the proposed consolidation, administrative and oversight functions currently based in Tucson would move to Phoenix, which could require patients, tribal health staff, and administrators to travel more than 100 miles, and in some cases up to two hours, for services and support that are currently available locally. I have also heard concerns that specialized programs such as diabetes care could be disrupted as part of this reorganization."

Congressman Ciscomani has made strengthening Arizona’s tribal communities and protecting their access to critical resources a priority during his time in Congress. He has championed the Northeastern Arizona Indian Water Rights Settlement Agreement (NAIWRSA) Act (H.R. 2025), legislation that addresses one of Arizona’s longest-running water challenges by securing water rights for the Navajo Nation, Hopi Tribe, and San Juan Southern Paiute Tribe.

The agreement also provides the Navajo Nation and Hopi Tribe with opportunities to lease their water rights, creating new economic opportunities, while authorizing $5 billion to build and maintain critical water infrastructure throughout the region. The legislation also establishes a homeland for the San Juan Southern Paiute Tribe.
