title: Neguse Succeeds in Urging NSF to Restore Full Funding for Quantum Center at CU Boulder
text:
Lafayette, CO — Today, Colorado Congressman Joe Neguse announced that the National Science Foundation (NSF) has reversed its planned 22% reduction to the University of Colorado Boulder’s JILA Physics Frontiers Center (JILA-PFC), restoring the center’s full award. For more than twenty years, JILA-PFC has been foundational to quantum research and training, helping cement Colorado’s position as a leader in quantum science and innovation. The proposed reduction would have exacerbated the quantum industry’s talent shortage, not only in Colorado, but across the nation, and undermined the nation’s competitiveness in quantum science.

Rep. Neguse and his office contacted NSF in early July to oppose the proposed cuts and urge the agency to fully fund the center. NSF has since informed CU Boulder that it will provide the full amount of funding for the grant's upcoming fourth year.

“Colorado’s research institutes and laboratories are central to the fabric of our state and our nation, and I’m proud to see the NSF heed our calls and follow through on their commitment to provide critical funding for CU Boulder’s barrier-breaking JILA Physics Frontiers Center. The hardworking scientists, researchers, and students at this institution have made groundbreaking advances in quantum that drive not only our state’s economy, but also America’s standing on the global stage. We must continue to support their work—for the development of the next generation of scientists and to ensure that the benefits of their discoveries reach every American,” said Congressman Neguse.

“CU Boulder is grateful to Congressman Neguse and Colorado's congressional delegation for their leadership in supporting the JILA Physics Frontier Center and sustained investment in quantum research,” said Massimo Ruzzene, senior vice chancellor for research and innovation and dean of the institutes. “For more than two decades, the JILA Physics Frontier Center has advanced the frontiers of quantum science while training the scientists, engineers and entrepreneurs who are shaping the future of this critical field. This restored funding will strengthen that mission by supporting pioneering research and the development of the quantum workforce that Colorado and the nation need.”

Congressman Neguse has forcefully worked to protect Colorado’s scientific institutions, including opposing plans to dismantle the National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCAR) in Boulder and successfully protecting funding for vital programs at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

###

title: Nunn Hosts Treasury Secretary Bessent, House Leaders as Trump Accounts Reach 7 Million Children
text:
“Iowa’s small businesses and community banks are the backbone of our state’s economy, and today’s conversation made clear that the Working Families Tax Cuts are delivering for the families and businesses they serve,” said Rep. Nunn. “We wrote this law to reward hard work, put more dollars in the pockets and paychecks of hardworking Iowans, and give families new ways to save for the future. Secretary Bessent has been a true partner in making that vision a reality. With this week’s guidance, Iowa employers can now contribute directly to their employees’ children’s accounts, while parents can save for their kids’ futures straight from their paycheck.”

“In Iowa, I joined Congressman Nunn, House Majority Leader Steve Scalise, Ways and Means Committee Chairman Jason Smith, Iowa Superintendent of Banking James Johnson, the Iowa Bankers Association, and local banking leaders to discuss how President Trump’s economic agenda is delivering for American families and Main Street,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “From providing certainty through the Working Families Tax Cuts and supporting financial literacy with Trump Accounts to fighting financial crime and cutting unnecessary regulatory burdens, this Administration continues to encourage investment, unlock capital, and ensure community banks can serve the families, entrepreneurs, and small businesses that drive the American economy.”

“I worked closely with Zach Nunn to pass the Working Families Tax Cuts to help make life more affordable not just for American families today, but for the next generation,” said House Majority Leader Steve Scalise. “With 7 million children already enrolled in Trump Accounts, parents across the country have a new opportunity to start saving and building wealth for their children. I appreciate Congressman Nunn bringing us together with Secretary Bessent and Chairman Smith here in Iowa to discuss how we can build on that progress and create more opportunities for hardworking families. That’s what the American Dream is all about: working hard, building a better life, and giving your children even greater opportunities than you have.”

“Two years ago, the Ways and Means Committee became the first committee to hold an official committee hearing at the Iowa State Fairgrounds to hear directly from Iowa families, farmers and small business owners, who were Republicans’ number one priority when writing the Working Families Tax Cuts,” said Chairman Smith. “Congressman Nunn spoke at that hearing about his interest in families getting tax relief from an expanded child tax credit, Iowa farmers benefitting from an extended biofuels tax credit, small businesses benefitting from the same tax treatment that large corporations receive, and adoption being made more affordable for working families. We achieved all of those things in our tax bill, thanks in part to Congressman Nunn’s leadership. I was also proud to join Congressman Nunn for a telephone town hall in June where we spoke directly with thousands of Iowans about the new tax relief available. Congressman Nunn fought to deliver this tax relief for the people he represents, and he’s fighting just as hard to make sure folks know about the results: permanent relief for family farms facing the Death Tax, a small business deduction, full, immediate expensing to help Main Street businesses grow and hire, and more of every paycheck staying in workers’ pockets through No Tax on Tips and No Tax on Overtime. None of that happens without a Congressman like Zach Nunn, who’s never been afraid to break from the pack in Washington and keeps advocating for the people of Iowa.”

“Iowa’s banking leaders appreciated the opportunity to meet with Secretary Bessent and Congressman Nunn to thank them for their leadership in financial services policy, to discuss the impacts of the Working Families Tax Cuts, to share our insights on the Iowa economy, and to provide suggestions on how to continue to improve the regulatory environment,” said Adam Gregg, President & CEO, Iowa Bankers Association. “The accessibility of both of these leaders is remarkable and appreciated.”

The roundtable came as the Administration advances new policies designed to help build wealth, strengthen community banks, and reduce unnecessary red tape for America’s small businesses. Earlier this week, the Treasury Department also issued new guidance allowing employers to contribute to Trump Accounts and permanently ended burdensome federal beneficial ownership reporting requirements for America’s small businesses.

Building Savings for the Next Generation

Trump Accounts, created by the Working Families Tax Cuts, officially launched on July 4, 2026. Every child born from 2025 through 2028 is eligible for a $1,000 federal contribution, and 7 million children have enrolled nationwide since the program launched, according to the Treasury Department.

New guidance issued this week gives families and employers additional ways to build on that foundation. Employers can contribute up to $2,500 per year, tax-free, to an employee’s child’s Trump Account, while parents can direct pre-tax dollars from their paychecks into the children’s accounts.

At today’s roundtable, Iowa banking and financial services leaders discussed how Trump Accounts can help families establish a culture of saving, strengthen financial literacy, and give the next generation a stronger financial foundation.

Cutting Red Tape for Iowa’s Small Businesses

The Treasury Department’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) also finalized a rule this week permanently ending beneficial ownership information (BOI) reporting requirements for American companies and U.S. citizens, and committed to deleting information previously filed by U.S. persons. Foreign entities registered to do business in the United States remain subject to reporting requirements.

Rep. Nunn led the legislative response to the BOI mandate, authoring the Protect Small Businesses from Excessive Paperwork Act, which passed the House 408-0 in February 2025.

The legislation addressed a federal reporting requirement that subjected small business owners to daily fines and up to two years in prison for failing to complete paperwork many business owners were unaware they were required to file. According to the National Federation of Independent Business, 80% of its members were unaware of the requirement, while the National Small Business Association estimated first-year compliance costs of roughly $8,000 per business. By FinCEN’s own accounting, ending the mandate eliminates more than 91 million hours of annual paperwork and approximately $9 billion in annual compliance costs nationwide.

Rep. Nunn’s Financial Services Agenda

Rep. Nunn has advanced four bills through the House Financial Services Committee this Congress, with three also passing on the House floor. At today’s roundtable, he highlighted three priorities for strengthening Iowa’s financial economy:

Bringing capital to the heartland. Rep. Nunn’s ELEVATE Act makes it easier for growing companies to access public markets by allowing them to provide two years of audited financial statements, rather than three, when going public, and permitting confidential draft registration. The bipartisan legislation passed the House by voice vote in June 2025 and was later incorporated into a broader bipartisan capital formation package that passed the House 302–123 in December.

Protecting Iowans from financial fraud. The GUARD Act gives state, local, and tribal law enforcement the tools and resources to combat elder financial fraud and “pig butchering” scams, and authorizes federal agencies to share blockchain tracing tools. The bipartisan legislation advanced unanimously, 52-0, through the Financial Services Committee in May.

Cutting red tape for independent financial advisors. The Clarity for Compensation Act gives independent financial advisors the same ability to route compensation through their own business entities that lawyers, accountants, and insurance agents already have. The bipartisan legislation passed the Financial Services Committee unanimously in June.

Photos from the roundtable are available here.

title: Pallone Presses U.S. Airlines for Answers on Surveillance Pricing
text:
Washington, D.C. – Energy and Commerce Committee Ranking Member Frank Pallone, Jr. (D-NJ) requested details from the eight major U.S. airline companies as part of the Committee’s ongoing inquiry into corporate surveillance pricing practices.

“I am very concerned about companies potentially using Americans’ personal data to determine what prices they see and pay, and I am continuing an inquiry into just how widespread this practice is,” Pallone wrote. “Consumers deserve to know if businesses are using their personal information to manipulate the prices they pay or experiment with algorithms to set the prices they see.”

In May, Pallone launched a Committee inquiry into surveillance pricing with an initial round of letters to 25 major corporations, including information on whether they’re using surveillance pricing based on consumers’ personal data to charge customers different prices for the same goods, particularly for online shopping.

The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) defines surveillance pricing as a form of personalized dynamic pricing where companies use a consumer’s online data—location, demographics, browsing history, shopping habits, or device type—to set individualized prices, often charging higher amounts based on an inferred willingness to pay.

“The airline industry specifically has faced several public allegations of surveillance pricing,” Pallone continued. “One study found that an airline boosted its own revenue by as much as six percent by leveraging AI pricing based on consumer information, an increase that comes at the expense of consumers. Lawsuits have been filed against airlines alleging the use of consumers’ information to set prices and in 2025, an airline came under scrutiny after appearing to announce that they were implementing artificial intelligence to assist with pricing.”

Ranking Member Pallone wrote to the following companies and requested answers by August 25, 2026:

Alaska Airlines

American Airlines

Delta Air Lines

Frontier Airlines

title: Rep. Panetta Announces Federal Funding for Martial Cottle Park
text:
San Jose, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) brought together Santa Clara County officials and community partners to announce $250,000 in federal funding that he secured for the Martial Cottle Park Improvements Project. The community project funding, provided through the Department of Housing and Urban Development’s Economic Development Initiative, supports the implementation of Phase I of the park’s 31-acre Historic Ranch Site Plan.

“Here in the Silicon Valley, we’re very proud of our innovation and technology, but we’re also proud of our roots in agriculture and the hard work that has defined the Santa Clara Valley. There is no greater place to experience that heritage than Martial Cottle Park, which embodies both the beauty and the bounty that make the 19th Congressional District so special,” said Rep. Panetta. “The significant federal funding secured will carry forward the Cottle family’s legacy by helping repurpose historic buildings, expand opportunities for agricultural education and recreation, and strengthen the park as a gathering place for the entire South San Jose community.”

“With Congressman Panetta’s leadership in securing $250,000 in federal funding, we open a new chapter in honoring the agricultural legacy of the Martial Cottle Park Deed through the implementation of Phase I of the Martial Cottle Historic Ranch Site Plan,” said Supervisor Sylvia Arenas, Vice President of the Santa Clara County Board of Supervisors representing District 1. “This project is a testament to our efforts to preserve Santa Clara County’s agricultural roots and farms while expanding agricultural education and agritourism for future generations.”

“The Santa Clara County Parks Department is looking forward to celebrating the completion of Phase I of the Cottle Lester Historic Ranch project and opening of the perimeter trail with the public in November,” said Julie Andersen, Deputy Director of Planning, Development, and Land Stewardship. “This project is a significant milestone in preserving the agricultural heritage of the Santa Clara Valley, and the Department thanks Congressman Panetta for the generous funding contribution that helped make this project possible.”

The funding is helping repurpose historic ranch buildings and create educational spaces, outdoor classrooms, community gathering areas, reservable picnic areas, accessible pathways, restrooms, and a large outdoor event space. The full Historic Ranch Site Plan will transform the 31-acre site while preserving its agricultural character and historic structures. The project carries forward the Cottle family’s decision to preserve the ranch for public use, education, and future generations, while creating new opportunities for residents and visitors to learn about the region’s agricultural heritage.

Rep. Panetta worked for this federal funding to be included in the most recent appropriations package. For FY 2026, he secured $3.75 million in community project funding for local projects across Santa Clara County, and a total of over $15 million to fund 14 local projects in California’s 19th Congressional District.

title: Rep. Panetta Convenes Local Leaders to Discuss Impacts of the Administration’s Mass Deportation Policy
text:
Aptos, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) convened education, housing, health care, food assistance, and law enforcement professionals from Santa Cruz and Monterey counties for a roundtable discussion at Cabrillo College on the local impacts of the Administration’s mass deportation policies. Participants discussed how federal enforcement actions are affecting access to and use of essential services, trust in law enforcement, and the daily lives of families throughout the Monterey Bay region.

The discussion also focused on the more than $200 billion increase in federal funding for immigration enforcement, the need for commonsense guardrails and accountability, and the Administration’s continued attacks on constitutional rights and lawful immigration programs. Rep. Panetta addressed his opposition to unchecked funding for U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and his support for demands to reform federal immigration enforcement and commonsensical immigration reform. He also highlighted his efforts to protect Dreamers, oppose the potential ICE facility near Gilroy, and safeguard birthright citizenship.

“Our discussion made clear that this Administration’s mass deportation policies are affecting our communities, from schools, health care, and housing to public safety and the rule of law,” said Rep. Panetta. “I support a strong and secure border, but that does not require mass deportations, unchecked funding for immigration enforcement, unaccountable federal agents, or unconstitutional attacks on Americans. Congress must impose guardrails, oversight, and accountability while pursuing commonsense reforms to improve our asylum system, protect Dreamers, and provide earned legalization for hardworking immigrants. I will continue working in Congress and with our local partners to protect those who contribute so much to our communities.”

“Cabrillo College stands firmly with all of our students and we will continue to prioritize safety, support and access to education. We want every family in Santa Cruz County to know that Cabrillo campuses in Aptos and Watsonville remain safe and welcoming where student privacy is protected,” said Jenn Capps, Ph.D., President/Superintendent, Cabrillo College.

“Every child, regardless of immigration status, has a fundamental right to a free public education in an environment where they feel safe, protected, and supported. Our schools are sanctuaries of learning and stability, and immigration enforcement concerns should never compromise a student’s ability to attend class, grow, and thrive. We are proud to stand with Representative Panetta to reaffirm our unwavering commitment to keeping our campuses safe, protecting our students, and ensuring our schools remain places of hope and opportunity for every family,” said Deneen Guss, Ed.D., Monterey County Superintendent of Schools, Monterey County Office of Education.

“Every student deserves to come to school feeling safe, welcomed, and supported. Our schools remain committed to creating environments where every child can learn without fear or distraction. We will continue to provide our students, families, and staff with accurate information and timely resources regarding immigration enforcement activities in and around our school communities, while ensuring that our focus remains on the safety, well-being, and success of every student,” said Dr. Ernesto Vela, Assistant Superintendent, Monterey County Office of Education.

“Public safety depends on trust. Whether someone is experiencing domestic violence, a child is missing, or a family is facing a crisis, no one should be afraid to call for help because of their immigration status. Our undocumented residents are part of our communities, and when they call for help, we are here to help them. Our public safety professionals are here to protect everyone we serve. I appreciate Congressman Panetta bringing us together to strengthen that trust,” said Monterey County Sheriff Tina Nieto.

“HUD’s proposal to require every resident in federally assisted housing to establish citizenship or eligible immigration status would be devastating for families and could have profound consequences for housing stability in our communities. Mixed-status families are families, and when we put one member of a household at risk of losing access to housing assistance because of their immigration status, we put the stability of the entire family at risk, including U.S. citizen children. At a time when housing is already out of reach for far too many families, we should not be creating additional barriers that could push people into displacement and homelessness. Housing is the foundation of family and community stability, and our policies should reflect that,” said Elaine Johnson, Executive Director, Housing Santa Cruz County.

“At Santa Cruz Community Health, we care for everyone who walks through our doors, regardless of language spoken, personal identity, or ability to pay,” said Anita Aguirre, CEO, Santa Cruz Community Health.

Last year, Rep. Panetta opposed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which provided more than $75 billion to ICE and $65 billion to CBP. In June, the Secure America Act provided nearly $70 billion more for ICE, CBP, and Department of Homeland Security (DHS) immigration enforcement operations through Fiscal Year 2029. Rep. Panetta voted against the Secure America Act and has voted at least seven separate times this Congress against providing ICE and CBP with additional funding without meaningful guardrails, oversight, or accountability.

Rep. Panetta has supported Democratic demands to require federal immigration agents to wear body cameras and clearly display identification, prohibit non-tactical masks that conceal their identities, strengthen warrant requirements, establish enforceable standards for the use of force and de-escalation, and ensure independent investigations of serious incidents, among other reforms. He is supporting the No Secret Police Act and the Protecting Sensitive Locations Act, which would restrict immigration enforcement at schools, hospitals, houses of worship, courthouses, and other sensitive locations.

In July, DHS briefly paused most vehicle stops by ICE deportation officers after agents fatally shot two men during separate operations in Houston, Texas, and Biddeford, Maine, while searching for other individuals. The White House overturned that pause the following day before the agency completed its review and additional training. Rep. Panetta joined nearly 200 House lawmakers in calling for independent investigations into both deaths, protection for witnesses, and the immediate deployment of body cameras to ICE and CBP agents. The three men traveling with Lorenzo Salgado Araujo when he was shot and killed in Houston each filed for U Visa protection. Rep. Panetta’s Immigrant Witness and Victim Protection Act would strengthen the U Visa program for immigrant survivors and witnesses of serious crimes who cooperate with law enforcement. The legislation would lift the cap on U Visas, protect eligible applicants from detention and deportation while their cases are pending, and allow them to work during the application process.

Earlier this year, Rep. Panetta joined Bay Area lawmakers in a letter to DHS and ICE opposing the proposed immigration detention and processing facility near Gilroy and demanding information about the project. Following the lawmakers’ calls, construction at the site was temporarily paused while legal challenges proceed. Rep. Panetta also joined a letter to DHS and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services demanding an explanation for the spike in delays affecting Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) renewal applications and urging the agencies to accelerate processing. The delays have caused Dreamers to lose employment authorization, miss work, and face disruptions to their income and daily lives despite filing timely renewal requests.

In February, after the Department of Housing and Urban Development attempted to override the intent of Congress by taking federal housing benefits away from mixed-status homes, Rep. Panetta joined his colleagues from the Congressional Asian, Black, and Hispanic Caucuses to assert Congressional intent and oppose this misguided rule. Congress has made it clear that federal housing benefits should be prorated for any eligible residents in a unit, and forcing people to choose between their eligible benefits and their loved ones would only cause further turmoil in California’s 19th District.

title: Congressman Patronis Fights to Defend the Second Amendment
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On Tuesday, Congressman Jimmy Patronis (R-FL) joined nearly 50 of his Republican colleagues in Congress in signing a bicameral letter led by Congressman Andrew Clyde and Senator Steve Daines urging Attorney General Todd Blanche and the Department of Justice (DOJ) to defend a landmark victory for the Second Amendment.

The lawmakers are calling on the Department of Justice to stand with the Constitution and not appeal a major Second Amendment victory. On August 5, a federal court in Texas ruled that the federal government can no longer require registration of suppressors, short-barreled rifles, short-barreled shotguns, and certain other firearms after Congress eliminated the related National Firearms Act taxes. The lawmakers are urging the DOJ to let the ruling stand nationwide, end unnecessary federal red tape, and protect the constitutional rights of gun owners.

“Law-abiding Americans shouldn’t have to beg the federal government for permission to exercise a constitutional right,” said Congressman Patronis. “This is consistent with everything I’ve fought for in Congress, from national reciprocity for concealed carry to repealing the Hughes Amendment. The Second Amendment ‘shall not be infringed,’ and I’ll continue fighting every day to stop Washington from putting unnecessary restrictions on our rights. The DOJ should respect the Constitution and let this historic ruling stand.”

Congressman Patronis remains committed to fighting federal overreach and to ensuring the constitutional rights of Americans are protected.

title: Congressman Pat Ryan Joins Community Leaders, Parents, Educators for Roundtable Discussion on Childcare Affordability & Accessibility in the Hudson Valley
text:
Congressman Ryan joined Hudson Valley parents, childcare providers, educators and other community stakeholders at DAY ONE in Poughkeepsie to discuss the cost and availability of local childcare

In 2025, 70% of parents reported that raising children had become “too expensive,” a 13-point increase from the previous year

The conversation comes as Hudson Valley families continue to face the high cost environment across the board; it also follows a Trump Administration attempt earlier this year to withhold critical childcare funding from New York State

POUGHKEEPSIE, NY – Congressman Pat Ryan – a father of two and member of the Congressional Dads Caucus – joined local parents, childcare providers, educators, and other community stakeholders at DAY ONE in Poughkeepsie to discuss the cost and availability of childcare in the Hudson Valley.

The conversation follows a Trump Administration attempt earlier this year to withhold critical childcare funding from New York and other Democratic-led states – despite the fact that in 2025, 70% of parents reported that raising children had become “too expensive,” a 13-point increase from the previous year.

Among the main concerns discussed were the rising cost of care, retention in the childcare industry, and parents struggling to remain in the workforce and raise their children.

The meeting also comes as Hudson Valley families continue to face the high-cost environment across the board. Throughout his time in office, Congressman Ryan has made lowering costs his number one priority – whether it’s groceries, utilities, housing, or healthcare.

“I know as well as anyone that being a parent is beyond a full-time job. At a time when Hudson Valley families are working as hard as they can, doing everything right, but still can’t afford basic necessities, the last thing they should have to worry about is making sure their kids are well taken care of,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “I fought back hard when Trump tried to rip away childcare funding from our community – but there’s still a lot of work to do. I heard from parents unsure how much longer they can make ends meet and from providers who love taking care of kids but are left with no option but to switch professions in order to pay their bills. Childcare isn’t a luxury item – it’s a necessity for so many parents, but the system is broken. I’m proud and grateful to get to collaborate with these community members on how we can lower costs for families in the Hudson Valley and beyond.”

“Parents, providers and teachers from both sides of the river described the same impossible math: families who can’t find care they can afford, and providers who can’t pay their teachers enough to keep the doors open,” said Geraldine Laybourne, co-founder of DAY ONE Early Learning Community. “Congressman Ryan came to listen, creating space for participants to speak openly and honestly about what they’re experiencing. What he heard in Poughkeepsie is being lived in communities across this country, and affordable, high-quality childcare is an issue where both parties find common ground. New York is treating childcare as public infrastructure, and Dutchess is one of the first three counties building it. What gets solved here can become a template everywhere else.”

"High-quality early childhood education is the foundation that allows children, families, and communities to thrive. At Community Family Development, we see every day that investing in early childhood education is not simply an investment in our youngest children—it strengthens families, supports working parents, and builds a stronger local economy. We are grateful to Congressman Ryan for his ability to listen, learn and work towards tangible solutions that make affordable childcare accessible to folks in the Hudson Valley,” said Jaime Hyla, CEO of Community Family Development.

“For the first time, the people working hands-on in childcare were given the opportunity to speak directly about the challenges they see every day for providers and families with young children. It was refreshing to have the ear of a congressman who was genuinely willing to listen and hear our concerns. Having a seat at that roundtable was significant, because meaningful change in childcare can only happen when we listen to those on the front lines. Ultimately, our goal is to create a system that truly serves the best interests of our most vulnerable population—our babies and young children,” said Marisol Hoffman of Feels Like Home Childcare.

In early 2026, several states, including New York, faced freezes on Child Care and Development Fund (CCDF) dollars due to bogus Trump-originated federal fraud investigations, threatening subsidies for over 10 billion dollars in social services.

For many American families, childcare is now the single largest household expense, often exceeding mortgage or rent payments. The national average for full-time center-based care for an infant has reached $14,802 per year in the US. Childcare costs in New York are among the highest. While the Department of Health and Human Services suggests childcare should cost no more than 7% of a family’s income, single parents currently spend an average of 35% of their income on care, and married couples spend approximately 10%. In 2025, 70% of parents reported that raising children had become “too expensive,” a 13-point increase from the previous year.

The lack of child care is a primary driver of workforce participation issues – approximately 81% of parents who struggled to find care in 2025 reported that it directly impacted their ability to work.

The supply of care is dwindling as providers struggle to remain solvent while paying competitive wages. More than 50% of Americans live in a “childcare desert,” where there are more than three children for every one available slot. Nearly 40% of childcare providers report current staffing shortages. The median hourly wage for child care workers remains stagnant at $15, leading to a 70% difficulty rate for workers in meeting their own basic needs like food and housing.

title: Congresswoman Pou Announces $125,000 Federal Award for Kearny Drug Prevention
text:
PATERSON, NJ – Congresswoman Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09) today announced that the Town of Kearny has been awarded $125,000 to support the Kearny Prevention Coalition and its work to prevent substance use.

The federal award comes through the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s Drug-Free Communities Support Program. The funding will support the Kearny Prevention Coalition Drug-Free Communities Support Project over the coming year. The grant is a continuation of federal support for the program, whose current project period runs through September 2027.

“Preventing substance use starts with strong communities and making sure our young people have the support they need,” said Congresswoman Pou. “This $125,000 federal award will help the Kearny Prevention Coalition continue its vital work with young people and families. I am proud to have helped secure this funding and will keep fighting to bring federal dollars home to Kearny and communities across our district.”

“Fighting drug dependence and abuse is one of the most important responsibilities of government and a team effort. Federal support like this is critical. I thank Congresswoman Pou for helping secure this money for Kearny,” said Kearny Mayor Carol Jean Doyle.

The Drug-Free Communities Support Program provides federal funding to community coalitions working to prevent and reduce substance use among young Americans. This award is administered by the CDC’s National Center for Injury Prevention and Control.

Since taking office, Congresswoman Pou has worked to bring federal resources back to the 35 cities and towns within New Jersey’s Ninth District. Her office collaborates directly with mayors, municipalities, local agencies and community organizations to identify federal funding opportunities and aggressively support grant applications.

Pou has secured over $24 million in federal Community Project Funding for infrastructure, public safety, flood mitigation and other local priorities across Bergen, Hudson and Passaic counties.

title: NEWS: In Hyde Park, Pressley, Markey, Advocates Celebrate $850,000 Delivered for LGBTQ+ Senior Housing at The Pryde
text:
Funds Have Supported the Construction of 74 Units of High-Quality, Service-Enriched Affordable Housing for Seniors in Boston

Photo | Video

Markey (D-MA) visited Hyde Park to celebrate the $850,000 in federal community project funding they helped deliver, in partnership with Senator Elizabeth Warren, for The Pryde, an affordable housing development for LGBTQ+ seniors in Hyde Park. title: Raskin, Beyer, DeGette Led 68 Colleagues Demanding AHRQ Reverse Cancellation of More Than $200 Million in Health Care Research Grants
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.– Representatives Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Don Beyer (D-VA) and Diana DeGette (D-CO) led 68 House Democrats in demanding that the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ) immediately reverse the cancellation of more than 150 grants supporting over $200 million in critical health care research. Among the research projects affected by the cancellations are efforts to integrate behavioral health services into routine pediatric care; use telehealth to expand access to care and reduce costs, including in rural communities; improve postpartum care for patients with chronic medical conditions; and reduce the overuse of antibiotics following hospital discharge to combat antimicrobial resistance.

In a letter to AHRQ Director Roger Klein, the lawmakers noted that Congress provided AHRQ with $345.38 million in funding as part of the Fiscal Year 2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act, reflecting bipartisan support for the agency’s work to improve health care access, affordability, and quality. The lawmakers warned that the mass cancellation of grants may constitute an illegal impoundment of Congressionally authorized and appropriated funding and raised concerns that the agency failed to follow federal regulations governing the termination of awards.

“Given the disastrous impact of these notices, the potential procedural defects in issuing them, and our concerns surrounding AHRQ’s use of Congressionally-appropriated funds, we ask that you immediately withdraw these notices and fully fund the grantees that have waited for committed funds for over a year,” the lawmakers wrote. “Additionally, we ask that you provide Congress with a comprehensive list of all awards for which notices referenced above have been issued and, for each of the canceled grants, list grant-specific information regarding the grantee’s progress, management practices, and other factors considered before issuing the notice.”

The letter is also signed by Representatives Jake Auchincloss (MA-4), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Joyce Beatty (OH-03), Wesley Bell (MO-01), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Julia Brownley (CA-26), Troy Carter (LA-02), Kathy Castor (FL-14), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Steve Cohen (TN-09), Herb Conaway (NJ-03), Angie Craig (MN-02), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Jacon Crow (CO-06), Danny Davis (IL-07), Madeleine Dean (PA-04), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Debbie Dingell (MI-06), Dwight Evans (PA-03), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), John Garamendi (CA-08), Jesús "Chuy" García (IL-04), Dan Goldman (NY-10), Maggie Goodlander (NH-02), Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Van Hoyle (OR-04), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Robin Kelly (IL-02), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Greg Landsman (OH-01), Summer Lee (PA-12), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), John Mannion (NY-22), Doris Matsui (CA-07), April McClain Delaney (MD-06), LaMonica McIver (NJ-10), Grace Meng (NY-06), Gwen Moore (WI-04), Kelly Morrison (MN-03), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Jerry Nadler (NJ-12), Richard Neal (MA-01), Brittany Pettersen (CO-07), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05), Kim Schrier (WA-08), Terri Sewell (AL-07), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Haley Stevens (MI-11), Tom Suozzi (NY-03), Mark Takano (CA-39), Bennie Thompson (MS-02), Dina Titus (NV-01), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Ritchie Torres (NY-15), James Walkinshaw (VA-11), Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12), Frederica Wilson (FL-24) and Congresswoman Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL).

Full text of the letter follows below, and a signed copy is available here.

Dear Director Klein:

We write to request the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ) Grants Management Office immediately reverse the mass cancellation of grants issued July 15, 2026. AHRQ has a statutory responsibility to support research to improve the quality and effectiveness of health services for the American people. The cancellation of more than 150 meritorious grants violates this duty and is likely an illegal impoundment of Congressionally-authorized and appropriated funds. The Grants Management Office also failed to follow federal regulations governing the termination of awards. We urge you to realign your Agency with federal law and the best interests of the American people and reverse these grant cancellations.

On July 15, 2026, AHRQ reportedly sent an estimated 150 cancellation notices to grant recipients. This action is expected to eliminate more than $200 million in lifesaving healthcare research that AHRQ funds as the lead federal agency directing studies into delivering care efficiently, effectively, and safely. At a time when the United States spends $5.3 trillion on healthcare annually, accounting for 18% of national gross domestic product, it is shocking that AHRQ would choose to end its support of that critical research.

Congress consistently authorizes and appropriates federal dollars to AHRQ, and most recently received $345.38 million in the FY26 Consolidated Appropriations Act, demonstrating bipartisan support for improving healthcare access, affordability, and quality, including in areas of priority for AHRQ like rural healthcare, artificial intelligence, and the prevention of healthcare associated infections. Examples of canceled research grants include programs to:

The above list is a small sample of the myriad topics addressed through canceled AHRQ grants that would improve healthcare quality, safety, and cost for the American people.

Withholding federal dollars from grant recipients across nearly 30 states without seeking Congressional approval under the Impoundment Control Act of 1974 is likely illegal and continues what is now a multi-year violation of federal law. The cancellation notices issued on July 15 fail to meet basic standards for grant cancellation notices. The notices cite 42 C.F.R. § 67.17(d) and 42 C.F.R. § 67.17(e), styling the notices as “non-awards” of future funding, rather than cancellations of ongoing research. However, the notices then assign recipients specific obligations under 2 C.F.R. § 200.344, which only applies when grants are canceled. The authorities to cancel ongoing grants provided under 42 C.F.R. § 67.17 require that specific factors are taken into account to cancel individual awards, including “the grantee's progress and management practices and the availability of funds.” Applying blanket language across up to 150 grants covering more than $200 million in awards is not consistent with careful consideration of individual grantees’ progress or performance.

Given the disastrous impact of these notices, the potential procedural defects in issuing them, and our concerns surrounding AHRQ’s use of Congressionally-appropriated funds, we ask that you immediately withdraw these notices and fully fund the grantees that have waited for committed funds for over a year. Additionally, we ask that you provide Congress with a comprehensive list of all awards for which notices referenced above have been issued and, for each of the canceled grants, list grant-specific information regarding the grantee’s progress, management practices, and other factors considered before issuing the notice. We request an update on AHRQ’s plans to withdraw these notices, as well as the full list of requested grantee information, no later than August 21, 2026.

title: ICYMI: Congresswoman Schrier Joins Roundtable Discussion with Local Health Leaders, Patients on Social Media’s Impacts on Youth Mental Health
text:
SEATTLE, WA - On Tuesday, Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) joined scholars, patients, and healthcare leaders to discuss the impacts of social media on youth mental health, and policy solutions to protect children and hold Big Tech accountable.

Included in the discussion were Seattle Children’s CEO Christopher Longhurst, MD, MS; Founding Director of the Stanford Social Media Lab Jeff Hancock, PhD; former Seattle Children’s patient Emme Leonard; Children’s Alliance Executive Director Soleil Boyd, PhD; Seattle Children’s Chief of Psychiatry & Mental and Behavioral Health Services Ray Hsaio, MD; and Seattle Children’s Adolescent Medicine Division Head Yolanda Evans, MD, MPH.

BACKGROUND: Congresswoman Schrier is the first and only pediatrician in Congress, and has used her experience to advocate for the safety, health, and security of children online. This Congress, Congresswoman Schrier introduced Sammy’s Law – a bill that would improve kids’ online safety by requiring social media companies to cooperate with third-party watchdog apps that would alert parents if their children have been exposed to harmful messages or interactions online. Congresswoman Schrier additionally introduced the Kids Off Social Media Act, which prohibits kids under the age of 13 from being on social media and bans companies from recommending content using algorithms for users under the age of 17.

Congresswoman Schrier also recently joined her colleagues in the House of Representatives to advance the KIDS Act, a bipartisan bill that takes historic steps to protect our kids and their data online and hold Big Tech accountable.

“As a pediatrician and member of Congress, I have seen first-hand the dangerous impacts social media has on our kids’ mental, physical, and emotional health,” said Congresswoman Schrier. “Finding solutions to protect kids online and hold Big Tech accountable has always been a top priority of mine, and I was glad to join local healthcare leaders, scholars, and patients today to hear about their experiences working directly to address this public health and safety crisis. I look forward to continuing my work in Congress to keep our children safe from the many harms social media platforms are causing in Washington state and across our country.”

“The evidence is clear: social media has a profound impact on youth mental health, and the data reinforces what we see in young people seeking care at Seattle Children’s,” said Christopher Longhurst, MD, MS, CEO at Seattle Children’s. “Protecting our youth is a responsibility we all share, and I’m grateful Representative Schrier, Attorney General Brown, state legislators and other community partners have joined Seattle Children’s in discussing the issue and necessary solutions to keep our children and teens safe.”

title: SPARTZ ANNOUNCES LONG-OVERDUE PRESIDENTIAL UNIT CITATION FOR INDIANA RANGERS
text:
Noblesville, IN – U.S. Representative Victoria Spartz (IN-05) announced that Company D (Ranger), 151st Infantry Regiment of the Indiana Army National Guard - the legendary “Indiana Rangers”- will receive the Presidential Unit Citation for their extraordinary heroism during the Vietnam War.

The recognition comes more than 50 years after the Indiana Rangers returned home from Vietnam in 1969. The unit was the only Army National Guard ground maneuver unit to serve in Southeast Asia during the Vietnam War and became one of the most decorated units of the war, earning hundreds of individual awards for valor and service.

“It has been a tremendous honor to help recognize these incredible Hoosier heroes,” said Rep. Spartz. “The Indiana Rangers demonstrated extraordinary courage under some of the most dangerous conditions imaginable. While their individual heroism was recognized many times over, recognition of the unit as a whole has been overdue since the Nixon era. More than half a century later, our nation is finally honoring what these brave men accomplished together.”

“The Indiana Rangers of the 151st Infantry Regiment set a standard of excellence that continues to inspire our force today,” said Maj. Gen. Larry Muennich, Adjutant General of the Indiana National Guard. “They lived the Warrior Ethos in the most unforgiving conditions, demonstrating a fierce loyalty to their brothers in arms and an unwavering commitment to the mission. We could not be prouder of this historic heroism. The Presidential Unit Citation is a testament to their grit, their sacrifice, and a legacy that will never be forgotten.”

The Presidential Unit Citation is the highest military decoration awarded to a unit for extraordinary heroism in combat. For the Indiana Rangers, the award recognizes not only individual acts of valor, but the extraordinary courage, teamwork, and sacrifice of the entire company.

Company D deployed to Vietnam in December 1968 and conducted hundreds of dangerous long-range reconnaissance missions, often operating deep in enemy-controlled territory. The Rangers returned to Indiana in November 1969, but for decades surviving members continued their efforts to secure appropriate recognition for the unit as a whole.

“Many of these heroes waited more than five decades for this day, and sadly, some did not live long enough to see it,” Spartz continued. “I am grateful to President Trump, Secretary Hegseth, Maj. Gen. Muennich, and everyone at the Indiana National Guard and Department of War who worked with us to finally make this long-overdue recognition a reality. Our nation must never forget the courage and sacrifice of these Hoosier heroes.”

The award will be given to the Indiana Rangers at the National Guard Association of the United States Conference & Exhibition in Indianapolis during the opening ceremony on August 29, 2026. Media must RSVP to Lauren Houck at lauren.a.houck.nfg@army.mil in order to receive media credentials.

title: Stanton, Colleagues to FTA and OMB: Stop Holding Infrastructure Dollars Hostage
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Representative Greg Stanton (D-AZ) joined Ranking Member of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure Rick Larsen (D-WA), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) and 39 congressional Democrats in demanding that Federal Transit Administration (FTA) Acting Deputy Administrator Matthew Cahill and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Director Russell Vought stop delaying the advancement of public transportation projects funded by the Capital Investment Grants (CIG) program.

Currently, FTA has access to more than $1.9 billion in unobligated and unallocated funds ready to be spent; however, the Trump administration continues to hold up significant projects instead of spending its infrastructure dollars.

We have watched for months as the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) and the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) have stonewalled the progress of worthy transit projects while President Trump and Department of Transportation Secretary Duffy are proclaiming a commitment to a 'golden age of transportation,'” the members wrote.

“The growing backlog of projects in limbo due to FTA and OMB inaction is unacceptable,” the members continued. “We are very concerned that delaying the CIG project pipeline, while advancing only the Utah project, is potentially rooted in partisan political considerations, which could further violate statutory requirements.”

“Every $1 invested in transit generates $5 in long-term economic value. Conversely, failing to deliver on long-promised transit investment carries serious economic consequences,” the members continued.

“Should this egregious trend continue,” the members noted, “11 projects in 10 states…that anticipate signing a CIG grant agreement this year could be subjected to senseless delay.”

The members concluded by reminding the administrators of the historically bipartisan nature of CIG-funded projects and demanded that their agencies immediately advance the stalled projects—regardless of a state’s 2024 election results.

title: Congresswoman Lee Hosts 4th Annual Southern Nevada Water Summit, Highlight Colorado River Crisis
text:
Watch video from the summit here

LAS VEGAS, NV – Today, Congresswoman Susie Lee (NV-03) hosted her fourth annual Southern Nevada Water Summit at the Springs Preserve. Alongside John Entsminger, General Manager of the Southern Nevada Water Authority and lead negotiator for the State of Nevada on Colorado River matters, and national and regional water experts, Congresswoman Lee discussed the Western water crisis.

“Whether I’m in my district or in Washington, D.C., someone always asks me what we’re doing to protect our water. Nevadans know all too well that our water is a precious resource, and I’m always proud to say that southern Nevada has demonstrated that meaningful conservation is possible,” said Colorado River Caucus Vice-Chair Congresswoman Susie Lee. “Today’s Water Summit highlighted that continued collaboration and innovation will be critical as we consider the future of the Colorado River Basin. The limitations on this precious resource have made Nevadans into pioneers once again, and we will continue blazing the trail toward a sustainable Western water future.”

Congresswoman Lee hosts her annual Southern Nevada Water Summit each year to convene advocates and experts for an all-hands-on-deck discussion on how Nevada can meet the Western water crisis with the urgency it demands. This year, the summit featured remarks and Q&A sessions focused on the future of the Colorado River System, the state of water recycling and reuse across the Colorado River Basin, and ongoing efforts to prioritize water supply and conservation within the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.

Congresswoman Lee was joined by John Entsminger, General Manager of the Southern Nevada Water Authority; Mike Connor, Senior Water Resources Official for the Biden, Obama, and Clinton Administrations; Noah Garrison, Environmental Science Practicum Director for the UCLA Institute of the Environment and Sustainability; and Dave Mitamura, Executive Director of the National Water Supply Alliance.

“Water supply reliability in the arid West requires collaboration, innovation, and leadership. Fortunately, there's ample supply in Nevada as demonstrated by Congresswoman Lee's action to bring together people with diverse backgrounds and experience to assess how best to make progress in securing our water future. The Southern Nevada Water Summit demonstrates that solutions are available even in the face of immense challenges,” said Mike Connor, Senior Water Resources Official for the Biden, Obama, and Clinton Administrations.

“We're facing a hotter, drier future across the Colorado River Basin and we need to more aggressively pursue the suite of solutions available - including water recycling - in order to ensure a safe, sustainable supply of water for the region,” said Noah Garrison, Environmental Science Practicum Director for the UCLA Institute of the Environment and Sustainability.

“Rep. Lee is on the march. She is looking for solutions big and small, obvious and not so obvious. Her support of efforts to strengthen the US Army Corps of Engineers water supply program may seem unconventional for a state with zero Corps water supply. She recognizes the benefit to help fellow basin states such as California to implement innovative Corps tools to develop new water supply and reduce reliance on the Colorado River,” said Dave Mitamura, Executive Director of the National Water Supply Alliance.

Lee’s work to protect southern Nevada’s water:

Lee helped pass the Inflation Reduction Act — the most significant action on the climate crisis in our history, including $4 billion in investments specifically for water conservation along the Colorado River Basin.

Lee’s Large-Scale Water Recycling Project Investment Act was signed into law as part of the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law.

She introduced the bipartisan Large-Scale Water Recycling Reauthorization Act to extend a federal grant program for large-scale water recycling projects in the Colorado River Basin and throughout the West.

Lee secured a pair of provisions in the Water Resources Development Act (WRDA) of 2024 to improve Laughlin’s water system and enhance the Las Vegas Wash program.

Last year, Lee fought to defeat proposals to sell Nevada’s public lands and send the proceeds back to Washington to offset permanent tax breaks to billionaires.

Since 1998, the Southern Nevada Public Land Management Act (SNPLMA) has ensured that the revenue from federal land sales in Southern Nevada stays in the state. 10 percent of SNPLMA funds go directly to SNWA — and, to date, SNPLMA has generated more than $368 million to fund Nevada’s water priorities and infrastructure needs.

Lee is co-championing a lands bill with Senator Catherine Cortez Masto that would enable Clark County to responsibly pursue new development across the next half-century while maintaining and building upon SNPLMA.

Lee and Cortez Masto’s bipartisan, bicameral Help Hoover Dam Act was signed into law. As mandated by the bill, the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation released $52 million in funding for the Hoover Dam.

These long-stranded funds can now be used for Hoover Dam operations, maintenance, and improvement projects, including installing the turbines needed to create hydroelectric power at lower lake depths, which have become necessary due to ongoing drought conditions.

title: Congresswoman Tenney Releases 2026 Agriculture Plan to Strengthen New York Farms and Rural Communities
text:
Oswego, NY — Congresswoman Claudia Tenney (NY-24) today released her 2026 Agriculture Plan, laying out her priorities to strengthen New York’s farm economy, support dairy and specialty crop producers, expand market opportunities, protect American farmland, and ensure farmers have the resources and certainty they need to succeed.

Agriculture is a cornerstone of New York’s 24th Congressional District, the largest agricultural district in the Northeast and the fifth largest dairy producing district in the nation. Rep. Tenney’s 2026 Agriculture Plan prioritizes a strong and reliable farm economy by expanding access to domestic and international markets, strengthening the agricultural workforce, and supporting partnerships between local farmers and their communities. It also focuses on the industries that make NY-24 unique, including dairy, apples, grapes, maple syrup, and other specialty crops. The plan further calls for protecting American farmland from hostile foreign interests, improving federal support for producers, and pushing back against burdensome policies that make it more difficult for family farms to remain competitive.

“Farming is not just an industry in Upstate and Western New York. It is a way of life that supports our families, small businesses, and entire rural communities,” said Congresswoman Tenney. “Our farmers work every day to put high-quality food on our tables, yet rising costs, unfair trade practices, workforce challenges, and burdensome mandates continue to make their jobs more difficult. This plan puts our farmers first by opening new markets, supporting our dairy and specialty crop producers, protecting American farmland, and giving family farms the stability they need to grow and pass their operations on to the next generation.”

title: Trahan Announces $161K in Federal Funding to Support Local Law Enforcement
text:
Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03) announced a total of $161,035 in federal funding secured to support law enforcement initiatives in Lawrence, Lowell, Haverhill, Fitchburg, and Marlborough. The funding was awarded through the U.S. Department of Justice’s Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (Byrne JAG) Program.

“Our police officers show up for us every day, and this funding helps us show up for them. Byrne JAG grants put real tools in the hands of local departments so officers can do their jobs as safely and efficiently as possible. That means safer communities for all of us to call home,” said Congresswoman Trahan. “I fought for this funding because our local departments asked for it, and I'll keep working to deliver what they need to protect our communities.”

Specific funding allocations include::

Lawrence: $43,500 to enhance public safety and combat violent crime by modernizing its patrol technology and improving officers’ ability to respond quickly and effectively in the field. By providing officers with reliable, modern technology, the project aims to improve operational efficiency, support data-driven crime prevention, and strengthen the safety of Lawrence residents and businesses.

Lowell: $41,462 to support the Lowell Police Department’s goal of strengthening its crime prevention, intelligence, and community engagement efforts by investing in personnel, training, and resources that support data-driven and evidence-based policing. Byrne JAG funding will support a Crime Analyst in the Crime Analysis and Intelligence Unit, as well as a Grant Research Analyst and Program Manager in the Research and Development Unit, helping the Department better identify crime trends, develop effective strategies, and maximize available resources.

Haverhill: $39,354 for the City’s goal to enhance officer and community safety by strengthening de-escalation capabilities and providing officers with effective, less-lethal options when responding to volatile or aggressive situations. Continued investment in the Taser 10 program will help reduce use-of-force incidents and associated injuries, ensure officers have the training and equipment necessary to respond safely and proportionally, mitigate legal liability and associated costs, and strengthen community trust through safer, more measured policing practices.

Fitchburg: $20,134 for the Fitchburg Police Department’s goal of enhancing officer safety and emergency response capabilities by providing officers with modern protective equipment for high-risk and rapidly evolving incidents. This investment will strengthen the Department’s readiness to respond to violent encounters and emergencies, reduce risks to responding personnel, and improve the Department’s ability to protect both officers and community members.

Marlborough: $16,585 to improve operational efficiency, strengthen internal coordination, and enhance public safety through the continued use and expansion of the City’s Systemsworks Detail Tracking System. Continued investment in this technology will also support data-driven personnel deployment, reduce payroll errors, strengthen compliance with labor agreements, and ensure the Department can maintain efficient, coordinated operations while continuing to provide high-quality service to Marlborough residents.

Since taking office in 2019, Trahan has consistently supported increased funding for the Byrne JAG program and the Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS) program, the two main initiatives that direct federal funding to local police departments. In 2024, she helped bring over $140,000 to MA-03 police departments. In 2025, Trahan supported legislation containing $964 million in funding for the Byrne JAG program, a $417 million increase from when she first took office, and $800 million for the COPS program, a $457 million increase since 2019.

title: Rep. Vasquez Stands With Veterans in Socorro, Marking PACT Act Anniversary
text:
SOCORRO N.M. – To mark the fourth anniversary of the PACT Act, U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) met with veterans in Socorro to discuss pressing issues including access to healthcare, affordable housing, and ensuring that veterans in rural areas continue to have access to the benefits they’ve earned.

“Socorro veterans have come together to build a network of community and support, and I’m grateful to be able to sit down with them and talk shop about the federal issues that impact veterans and their care and benefits,” said Vasquez. “I’ve made supporting veterans a cornerstone of my work in Congress and I’ll continue to go to bat for them in the face of extreme cuts and changes at the VA to strengthen their access to healthcare, housing, reintegration, education and workforce opportunities — especially in rural communities.”

“What struck me, I’ve only been in Socorro for about a year and 8 months, but Congressman [Vasquez] you’re the first one to come out and talk, to my knowledge, to veterans to hear their concerns. So pretty awesome that we’re celebrating that,” said Manny Gonzales, CEO of Socorro Electric and Sergeant Major (Ret.). “As a recipient of the PACT Act, I didn't know it was the anniversary date – it really means a lot for you to come out here.”

The PACT Act passed in 2022 and expanded VA healthcare and benefits for millions of veterans exposed to burn pits, Agent Orange, radiation, and other toxic substances during their military service.

Rep. Vasquez sat down with:

Ravi Bhasker, Mayor of Socorro

Manny Gonzales, CEO of Socorro Electric and Sergeant Major (Ret.)

Sergeant Major Eugene McPeek (Ret.), VFW 1389 Commander

Mack Dyer, NM VFW Army Department Commander

Roxann Scott, Co-founder of Forget Me Not Veterans Park

Daun Medaris, Co-founder of Forget Me Not Veterans Park

Joe Gonzales, Socorro County Commissioner Chairman

Peter Romero, Socorro City Councilor

Rep. Vasquez’s advocacy reflects his ongoing commitment to supporting veterans and active-duty servicemembers. His previous work includes:

Spearheading the TRICARE Travel Improvement Act, which Vasquez led and got passed into law with bipartisan support through the FY26 National Defense Authorization Act. The bill lowers the mileage requirement for TRICARE travel reimbursement from 100 miles to 75 miles — helping military families in rural communities more easily access medical care.

The Feed Our Veterans Act, legislation Vasquez introduced and fought for during the most recent Farm Bill markup, to combat food insecurity among veterans and protect them from new burdensome SNAP work requirements introduced under the Republican tax law last summer.

Signed a bipartisan discharge petition to require a House vote on the Major Richard Star Act, legislation that would allow combat-injured veterans to receive both their full military retirement pay and VA disability compensation.

Voted in support of the Fiscal Year 2027 Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act to obtain critical funding that would improve the quality of life for veterans and make substantial investments in infrastructure to support the readiness of active-duty servicemembers in New Mexico.

title: Vindman Announces New Legislative Efforts to Tackle Corruption, Lower Utility Costs for Virginians
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) — introduced two pieces of legislation today that would lower costs for Virginians, tackle corruption in the utility industry, and hold utility companies accountable.

“Families are already struggling with the rising cost of living. Virginians shouldn’t have to pay junk fees just to keep the lights on, and they shouldn’t have to wonder if their monthly bills are jacked up due to corruption and colluding between regulators and utility companies,” said Vindman. “Banning utility junk fees and closing the revolving door between utilities and regulators will restore trust and lower costs.”

The No Utility Junk Fees Act would establish the first federal ban on utility junk fees by prohibiting utilities from charging excessive fees to customers who pay their bills by credit or debit card. Additionally, it would keep families from having to pay unreasonable fees to access an essential service, especially when monopoly utilities leave them with nowhere else to turn.

The Energy Utility Lobbying Ban Act would end the revolving door between monopoly utilities and the regulators responsible for holding them accountable. It prevents state utility regulators from leaving public service and immediately lobbying for the electric companies they once oversaw. The bill also creates a lifetime ban on lobbying the agency for cases a regulator personally worked on, along with a two-year cooling-off period before lobbying on other utility matters.

BACKGROUND

Vindman was the first member of the Virginia Delegation to come out in opposition to the proposed merger between NextEra Energy and Dominion Energy. Earlier in August, he sent a letter to members of the Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC) urging them to reject the proposed merger. In the letter, Vindman warned that the deal would put Wall Street profits ahead of Virginia families, weaken local accountability, and increase costs for consumers.

Vindman has been a champion for lowering utility bills in Congress and making life better for working families. In May, Vindman heard from more than 800 Virginians through a district-wide survey who said they were feeling the effects of rising utility bill.

Also in May, Vindman introduced two pieces of legislation that would lower costs for families and hold utility companies accountable. The Home Energy Affordability Act would help protect consumers from repeated utility rate hikes by limiting electric utilities to one rate change request every 365 days. The Utility Hikes Transparency Act would create the first comprehensive, machine-readable federal database of retail utility rate changes in the United States.

Vindman also was joined by 14 lawmakers in launching the Congressional Lowering Utility Bills Caucus to find legislative solutions to the ongoing energy affordability crisis in Virginia and around the country. The caucus will convene House Members around oversight strategies and tools to hold utility companies accountable for skyrocketing rates.

title: Sen. Banks Calls on Secretary Hegseth to Blacklist Chinese Engine Maker with Ties to PLA
text:
Weichai engines are used in rocket systems supplied to the Chinese military

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Senator Jim Banks (R-Ind.) sent a letter to Secretary of War Pete Hegseth urging the Department of War to add Weichai Holding Group Co. Ltd. to its Chinese Military Companies list.

Weichai is wholly-owned by a Chinese state-controlled enterprise and works with blacklisted Chinese defense companies. China North Industries Corporation (NORINCO)—a Chinese state-owned defense manufacturer—uses Weichai engines in a multiple-launch rocket system supplied to the People’s Liberation Army, and Weichai has also partnered with a subsidiary of the blacklisted China Aerospace Science and Industry Corporation.

In the letter, Banks argues that Weichai’s ownership structure, defense partnerships and role in China’s military-civil fusion strategy meet the criteria for designation as a Chinese military company. He urges the Department of War to add Weichai to the 1260H List to protect U.S. national security and prevent Chinese military-linked companies from operating in the United States without appropriate scrutiny.

Read the full letter here.

Dear Secretary Hegseth:

I am writing to bring to your attention the U.S. national security risk posed by Weichai Holding Group Co. Ltd. (Weichai) and urge you to add it to the Department of War’s Chinese Military Companies List (1260H List). Weichai, based in the People’s Republic of China (PRC), manufactures diesel engines that are sold in more than 150 countries including the United States.

As you know, Section 1260H of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 requires the Secretary of War to publish a list of “Chinese military companies.” Under the statute, a Chinese military company includes entities identified as a military-civil fusion contributor to China’s defense industrial base. Among the statutory criteria, an entity qualifies as a military-civil fusion contributor if it is affiliated with China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) or the State-Owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council (SASAC). Weichai’s ownership structure, state backing, and partnerships with entities of concern appear to satisfy these criteria.

Weichai is wholly owned by Shandong Heavy Industry Group, a state-owned enterprise supervised and controlled by the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (SASAC) of the Shandong Provincial Government. This body maintains control over the company’s strategic direction, and SASAC praised Weichai for “building a ‘Benchmark’ or High-Quality Development among State-Owned Enterprises.” In 2019, Shandong Heavy Industry Group established a People’s Armed Forces Department (PAFD) that reports to the Shandong Provincial Military District, and this group owns or holds controlling stakes in companies worldwide including the French diesel engine manufacturer Baudouin Motors. At a minimum, this ownership structure provides access to strategic resources and assets held by its overseas subsidiaries. Like all major state-owned enterprises (SOEs), Weichai also houses an active internal CCP committee that oversees major business decisions to ensure they align with the party’s political directives.

Weichai’s collaborations with PRC defense companies are equally concerning. NORINCO, a blacklisted Chinese military company that supplies the People’s Liberation Army (PLA), procures Weichai engines for use in the PHL-11 Multiple Launch Rocket System (MLRS). Weichai also signed a cooperation agreement with Hubei Sanjiang Space Wanshan Special Vehicle Co., a subsidiary of the blacklisted China Aerospace Science and Industry Corporation (CASIC), further demonstrating its integration into China’s defense industrial base.

Moreover, Weichai supports the State Key Laboratory of Engine and Powertrain System, one of the PRC’s more than 500 State Key Laboratories (SKL). SKL’s are part of a PRC government-directed research network that seeks to reduce its reliance on foreign technologies. PRC central government planning documents describe SKLs as “vital components of China’s innovation ecosystem.” SKLs receive central government funding to advance strategic technologies for both commercial and military use, making Weichai a key participant in China’s military-civil fusion strategy.

In addition to its role in military-civil fusion, Weichai works directly with foreign defense entities of concern and firms that have been sanctioned by the U.S. government. In 2016, Weichai signed a cooperation agreement with Belarus’ MAZ group – sanctioned by the Treasury department in 2023 – to build diesel engines. It also established a joint venture with Kamaz, a Russian supplier of trucks to the Russian Ministry of Defense, and signed a cooperation agreement with Hubei Sanjiang Space Wanshan Special Vehicle Co., a wholly owned subsidiary of the blacklisted China Aerospace Science and Industry Corporation (CASIC).

Equally alarming is Weichai’s subsidiaries and members that maintain extensive ties to Chinese government industrial initiatives, state-funded research programs, and defense-linked institutions:

Shaanxi Heavy Duty Automobile Co., a Weichai subsidiary, participates in multiple national high-tech and Ministry of Science and Technology research programs.

Shaanxi Fast Gear Co., a Weichai subsidiary, explicitly identifies the Belt and Road Initiative and “Made in China” strategy as key drivers for its growth.

Shaanxi HanDe Axle Co., founded by Weichai, has received funding from the Baoji Municipal Bureau of Industry and Technology Provincial Fund for automotive industry development. It also has partnered with Xi’an Jiaotong University, a defense-linked institution supervised by the State Administration for Science, Technology and Industry for National Defense (SASTIND) that conducts classified military research and has strategic partnerships with major Chinese defense contractors. HanDe Axle has also received provincial science and technology awards, underscoring its integration into China’s state-directed innovation ecosystem.

Collectively, these relationships between Weichai’s members and the CCP demonstrate its connections to the CCP’s industrial policy, government support, and collaboration with institutions that directly advance China’s military-civil fusion strategy and defense industrial base. Weichai’s work has even earned the praise of General Secretary Xi Jinping, who remarked in 2018 that “Weichai has handed in a brilliant result with ten years of development.” The information above seems to indicate that Weichai meets the definition of a Chinese military

company and thus should be listed on the 1260H list.

Thank you for your attention to this critical national security matter. I am ready to work with the Department of War to ensure that our nation’s industry remains secure from potential foreign threats.

Sincerely,

Jim Banks

U.S. Senator
