title: The Hutchinson News: Artemis II crew visit Cosmosphere, the 'best space museum in world'
text:
Artemis II crew visit the Cosmosphere, the 'best space museum in world'

The Hutchinson News | August 12, 2026

Kansas is home to the best space museum in the world, at least that's what Commander Reid Wiseman of the Artemis II mission reassured the audience gathered Aug. 11 at the Cosmosphere.

Wiseman was joined by fellow Artemis II crew member Christina Koch for a visit to the museum and science center in Hutchinson, after accepting an invitation from Sen. Jerry Moran while aboard Integrity, the Orion capsule that housed the crew on its way to and from the moon in April.

The astronauts joined Moran and NASA administrator Jared Isaacman for a tour of the facility, which includes the artifacts from previous American, Soviet and Russian missions in its Hall of Space museum, as well as facilities for education that were being used by camp students during the visit.

Astronauts thankful for support throughout mission

Following the tour, all four spoke to a crowd or around 200 who were invited to the event, including campers with the summer programs at the Cosmosphere.

"Today, our astronauts represent that whole set of people that our country desperately need and provides, particularly so today," Moran said in introducing them.

While the senator noted that often people look to athletes or performers as role models, the United States is privileged to have a lot of other choices as well.

"I don't think being an astronaut, that there is anything more compelling or life changing than that," he said. "That's what happens when that occurs, both with adults and children."

After introductions from the senator, Wiseman and Koch presented a video of the mission from launch to splashdown, speaking of the significance of it and the importance of people back on Earth, even in Kansas, in sending and bringing them home.

Wiseman said this part of being a crew member on Artemis was one of the best parts of the journey.

"We get to inspire the youth, get to work with the men and women working on this vehicle, the engineering support and the folks who sent us to the moon and brought us back safely," he said.

Koch said the launch and splashdown were some of the more important moments to her, as it was a reminder of the people on Earth who were with them for the entirety of the mission, including those at the Cosmosphere and around the nation.

"While we were on the (launchpad), you heard us say, 'We are going for our teammates,'" she said. "You may have thought we were talking about someone else, but we were also talking about you. Because the people that build lovers of space, the people that foster an industry here in aerospace and love exploring, you are our teammates."

NASA head and Sen. Moran speak on importance of space funding

Isaacman said the task of exploring the unknowns of space in missions like Artemis and others that NASA takes part in isn't something that is easy, or inexpensive, and having funding from resources including the federal government, is important.

"There is often no obvious business case or economic return," he said. "We're going out and seeking answers to questions that we've had for a very long time. It's important that there are contributions across the nation ... for all that it might reveal for the future."

Moran, who chairs the Senate Aviation, Space and Innovation Subcommittee, said he sees funding NASA as a priority.

"There is the reason for public support, governmental support, taxpayer support for the exploration of space," he said. "It's not about benefiting NASA itself or benefiting Congress, but what the future of our country holds because we accomplished these outcomes."

Isaacman promises Cosmosphere artifacts from Artemis

Wiseman and Koch, as well as their boss Isaacman, spoke of the importance of the place that is the Cosmosphere.

"Both Christian and I flew on Russian vehicles (as well as American)," Wiseman said. "To my knowledge, this is the only place where you can see the power (of both). You can look through the Russian side and the American side of space travel. It's special to be able to relive the entire space journey under one roof."

Isaacman, who visited the museum during the Artemis II mission, said the Cosmosphere is one of the best places that honors preserves the history of spaceflight.

"In the years ahead, artifacts from the Artemis mission will arrive here to take a place of honor next to those of Mercury, Gemini and Apollo," he said. "To all of you, especially the young folks here, continue to stay curious, keep visiting, keep exploring and never forget the greatest days of exploration are ahead of us."

title: Moreno, Hegseth Travel to Panama to Bolster Alliance Against Cartels
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Senator Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) traveled with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to Panama to meet with President José Raúl Mulino and Ambassador Cabrera, and Colombian officials. During the event, Senator Moreno delivered remarks on the importance of strengthening cooperation with our Latin America allies to combat cartels and other illicit activities within the Western hemisphere.

Senator Moreno’s remarks as prepared are below:

“President Mulino, Secretary Hegseth, Ambassador Cabrera, distinguished ministers, commanders, and friends of the Americas:

“Thank you for the honor of joining you today and thank you especially to President Mulino for hosting this critical gathering in Panama. Ambassador Cabrera, your leadership here continues to strengthen the vital partnership between our two nations, and you continue to set the bar for Ambassadors around the globe.

“I speak to you not only as a United States Senator, but as someone born in Latin America. My family left Colombia seeking the American dream: opportunity, safety, and the rule of law. And we found just that. The United States gave me every opportunity for success, and I could not have achieved what I did anywhere else on earth. That personal journey shapes everything I believe about this fight. There is a reason the American dream does not exist throughout all the Americas. Narco terrorist organizations pillage, corrupt, and rob Latin Americans of their god given rights to live freely and securely. These cartels crush families, whether in the neighborhoods of Colombia, along the routes through Panama, in the cities of Ohio, and across our entire hemisphere.

“Cartels have no borders. They spread their poison, their corruption, and their destruction of economic prosperity with total impunity. They recruit our young people, murder our citizens, corrupt our institutions, and steal the future from the next generation. We have lived through too much murder, too much crime, and too much insecurity. Enough is enough.

“We can end this downward cycle of decay by offering an alternative to drug trafficking and other illicit activities. A permanent end to this tragedy starts with prosperity. That is why economic security is inseparable from national security. Prosperity is one of the strongest weapons we have against these criminal networks. When legitimate businesses thrive and young people see real opportunity for a good life, the cartels lose their recruiting base and their hold on communities. That is why the United States must reward our closest allies — the nations gathered in this room today — with favorable trade agreements that allow them to take full advantage of America’s decoupling from China. As we reshore supply chains and reduce dependence on Beijing, our trusted partners in the Americas should be the first to benefit. Stronger economies in free nations mean weaker cartels.

“President Trump created the Americas Counter Cartel Coalition for one clear purpose: a coordinated, determined response that wipes these terrorists out forever. Panama has already shown under President Mulino what focused leadership and real cooperation can achieve. Now we must scale that resolve across the hemisphere. Colombia, with its unique geography and its new direction, must play a leading role. No strategy succeeds without closing the production and transit corridors that feed this poison.

“Thanks to the leadership of President Trump and Secretary Hegseth, the time is now. The tools are in our hands. The will is building. The opportunity is here.

“Let us seize this moment. Let us act with clarity, with courage, and with unity. The families of the Americas are counting on us.

“Thank you.”

title: Moreno Presses DHS to Crack Down on Illegal Chinese Transshipment
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Senator Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) sent a letter to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin calling for action against illegal transshipment schemes used predominantly by Chinese manufacturers to disguise their goods’ origins and evade U.S. tariffs. The CCP’s scheme costs American taxpayers billions of dollars in tariff revenue and threatens American manufacturing jobs, predominantly in the auto industry.

“Illegal transshipment is a deliberate scheme by foreign manufacturers, overwhelmingly based in the People’s Republic of China, to falsify where their goods are made, launder them through a third country, slap on a new label, and dump them into the American market, eluding tariffs and other duties imposed on the true country of origin. Every one of these shipments represents a company breaking American law and stealing competitive advantage from American businesses,” wrote Senator Moreno.

“This sustained act of trade fraud against the American economy is costing taxpayers billions in lost revenue and threatening law-abiding American businesses and the jobs they provide,” Senator Moreno continued.

Read the full text of the letter HERE or below.

August 12, 2026

The Honorable Markwayne Mullin

Secretary

U.S. Department of Homeland Security

2707 Martin Luther King Jr. Avenue, SE

Washington, D.C. 20528

Dear Secretary Mullin,

Thank you for your leadership at the Department of Homeland Security (the “Department”). The Trump Administration’s America First Trade Policy has put the American economy, the American worker, and U.S. national security first, a vital realignment from the previous administration. Specifically, U.S. Customs and Border Protection (“CBP”) has a strong track record of upholding and reinforcing this Policy with its efforts to enhance customs enforcement and ensure that American companies can compete on fair terms in the global marketplace. I write to bring your attention to a substantial fraud scheme hampering this policy’s effectiveness: circumvention of U.S. trade law via illegal transshipment and other mechanisms.

Illegal transshipment is a deliberate scheme by foreign manufacturers, overwhelmingly based in the People’s Republic of China, to falsify where their goods are made, launder them through a third country, slap on a new label, and dump them into the American market, eluding tariffs and other duties imposed on the true country of origin. Every one of these shipments represents a company breaking American law and stealing competitive advantage from American businesses. The numbers make clear this is not a marginal problem. Trade data from earlier this year shows a record $112 billion gap between what China reported exporting to the United States and what CBP recorded as actually arriving on our shores last year. That means as much as a quarter of everything China shipped to America last year may have slipped past our tariff enforcement entirely.

This sustained act of trade fraud against the American economy is costing taxpayers billions in lost revenue and threatening law-abiding American businesses and the jobs they provide.

For Ohio, the stakes could not be higher. The auto industry is a cornerstone of our economy, supporting over 329,400 jobs and contributing $41.43 billion to Ohio’s gross state product. Notably, transshipment has already threatened this critical industry in my home state. In January 2024, Homeland Security Investigations (“HSI”) executed a federal search warrant at the Moraine, Ohio plant of Harco Manufacturing Group, the U.S. subsidiary of Qingdao Sunsong, a Chinese auto parts manufacturer. Qingdao Sunsong has been previously identified in Congressional investigations for circumventing Section 301 tariffs. The investigations alleged that Qingdao Sunsong transshipped its products with limited transformation through Thailand to the United States. This is what illegal transshipment looks like: Chinese companies setting up shadow operations in other countries to cheat U.S. trade laws while American businesses play by the rules.

I wholeheartedly support the Administration’s tariff agenda. However, tariffs only work if they are collected and enforced without exception. I appreciate the Department’s work so far, including the adoption of Al to enhance visibility into supply chains, the continued Enforce and Protect Act investigations, and the work of HSI’s Global Trade and Investigations division.

The Department has already taken considerable steps to promote economic fairness, protect domestic industry, and uphold the integrity of U.S. supply chains, and I urge the Department to continue leveraging innovative methods to better uphold U.S. trade laws. Additionally, I recommend that the Department look into any additional authorities needed to go after those who knowingly and blatantly violate U.S. law. Congress stands by to aid you in punishing tariff evaders.

title: Murray Joins Senate Colleagues in Demanding State Department Process Student Visas Without Delays
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, joined 29 of her Senate colleagues in expressing concern about the unavailability of student and exchange visitor visa appointments in time for the start of the academic year and demanding answers regarding delays in processing of these applications at U.S. embassies and consulates.

“We urge the State Department to ensure timely processing of F, M, and J student and exchange visitor nonimmigrant visas, consistent with the approach taken by administrations of both parties in the past, and to implement other measures to avoid diminishing U.S. competitiveness,” wrote the Senators. “Specifically, we are hearing from constituents and stakeholders that no timely visa appointments are available for students at some embassies and consulates. This only exacerbates uncertainty about whether students’ visas will be processed in time for them to travel to the United States to begin their studies.”

The Senators highlighted the vital contributions international students make to universities and communities nationwide, including expanding opportunities for American students, generating economic activity, strengthening the U.S. workforce, and building international partnerships.

“International students are critical to the success of our universities, including contributing nearly $43 billion annually to local communities and supporting more than 355,000 American jobs during the 2024-2025 academic year. Even though international students make up only six percent of the total higher education population, their enrollment creates opportunities for American students,” continued the Senators. “International students also improve our national security by fostering global relationships, cross cultural understanding, and long-lasting diplomatic ties. These benefits are at risk if visa processing delays persist.”

The Senators urged the State Department to ensure the timely review and processing of student and exchange visitor visas, extend interview waivers for vetted returning student applicants, provide sufficient staffing for visa processing, and improve transparency and engagement with stakeholders. The Senators also requested an explanation within 30 days about the causes of the delays and the measures being implemented to ensure student and exchange visitor visa applications are processed in a timely manner moving forward.

In addition to Senator Murray, the letter was signed by Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), and Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), Michael Bennet (D-CO), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Chris Coons (D-DE), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Andy Kim (D-NJ), Angus King (I-ME), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Ben Ray Luján (D-NM), Ed Markey (D-MA), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Gary Peters (D-MI), Jack Reed (D-RI), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Tina Smith (D-MN), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-GA), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Peter Welch (D-VT), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), and Ron Wyden (D-OR).

Full text of the letter is available HERE and below:

Dear Secretary Rubio,

We write to express our concerns regarding the ongoing unavailability of visa appointments during the peak visa application season for students and scholars seeking to enter the U.S. in time for the start of classes and the academic year. We urge the State Department to ensure timely processing of F, M, and J student and exchange visitor nonimmigrant visas, consistent with the approach taken by administrations of both parties in the past, and to implement other measures to avoid diminishing U.S. competitiveness. Specifically, we are hearing from constituents and stakeholders that no timely visa appointments are available for students at some embassies and consulates. This only exacerbates uncertainty about whether students’ visas will be processed in time for them to travel to the United States to begin their studies.

These challenges come at a time when major academic institutions need skilled, international talent to begin their semesters. Without a fix, the repercussions will be felt across the academic and skilled-technical talent pipeline.

International students are critical to the success of our universities, including contributing nearly $43 billion annually to local communities and supporting more than 355,000 American jobs during the 2024-2025 academic year. Even though international students make up only six percent of the total higher education population, their enrollment creates opportunities for American students. For every additional international undergraduate enrolled at a U.S. public university, two additional in-state freshman students can enroll. Most international students pay out-of state tuition, injecting vital revenue into our colleges and universities and helping keep costs down for domestic students. International students also improve our national security by fostering global relationships, cross cultural understanding, and long-lasting diplomatic ties. These benefits are at risk if visa processing delays persist.

The case-by-case nature of availability for access to expedited appointments or National Interest Exception requests is neither efficient nor sustainable. Instead of diverting already limited personnel resources, the State Department should ensure that its consular sections restore priority to interview, adjudicate, and process student visas in time for the upcoming school year.

In addition to the above, we urge the State Department to extend interview waivers for vetted returning student applicants; ensure adequate staffing for timely visa vetting and processing; and meaningfully engage with stakeholders to promote greater transparency.

International students bolster the American workforce, drive innovation, and better position our country to maintain its competitive edge. Therefore, we request a written response answering these questions within 30 days:

What resources has the Department devoted to processing the backlogs and streamlining processing of F, J, and M visas?

Have consular process priorities changed since the spring and summer of 2025? What visa interview categories are currently prioritized by the Bureau of Consular Affairs and where do student visas fall within that list? Provide the list of visa interview prioritization.

What guidance has been sent to embassies and consulates regarding prioritization or deprioritization of student and exchange visitor visa processing? Provide a copy of all guidance regarding the prioritizing or deprioritizing of student and exchange visitor visas since August 2025 until the present day.

How are interview slots being allocated at embassies and consulates and where do student and exchange visitor visa appointments fit within that allocation?

How often are consular post websites and the main State Department website updated for relevant and current information regarding current U.S. consulate operations including visa appointment availability and approximate processing times?

When will you resume publicly posting monthly, accurate visa issuance data by category?

Will the Department commit to implementing regular, ongoing outreach and collaboration with stakeholders and relevant agencies about the student and exchange visitor visa process and ensure the timely processing of F, J, and M visas?

How do you ensure that embassies and consulates are accurately and timely informed of any regulatory or policy changes regarding student and exchange visitor visas?

What are the average processing times for F, M, and J visas at the top five locations processing these visas from September 2025 to date, disaggregated by month?

Last year, the Department of State announced new vetting, including online presence vetting, of all student and exchange visitor applicants in the F, M, and J nonimmigrant classification.

What resources has the Department of State devoted to these new vetting procedures?

In developing these new vetting procedures, what steps has your Department taken to ensure our national security interests of welcoming bona fide international students in our communities can still be achieved through timely processing of F, J, and M visas.

How many applications have been refused pursuant to the new enhanced vetting procedures? Please disaggregate these numbers by the basis for refusal.

Sincerely,

###

title: Padilla, Murphy, Democratic Colleagues Demand Answers from HHS Secretary RFK Jr. on Potential $150M Contract Award to Trump-Aligned Law Firm to Represent Unaccompanied Children in Court
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Chris Murphy (D-Conn.), and 14 of their Democratic colleagues demanded answers from the Trump Administration on its intent to award a no-bid contract to a Trump-aligned law firm with no apparent immigration law experience, allowing them to represent unaccompanied children who are in the care and custody of the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR).

“Given the political connections between the firm’s senior leadership and the Trump Administration, we have concerns about why you sidestepped the competitive bidding process to select this firm to provide legal services for children who are in ORR care and custody, and demand transparency into whether all federal procurement processes were followed,” wrote the Senators. “Children deserve competent representation by attorneys who practice at the intersection of child welfare and federal immigration law, but Americans also deserve to know why their federal dollars are being doled out to Trump’s friends and allies.”

The Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS), through ORR, has an obligation to ensure that unaccompanied children are provided competent legal aid as they navigate the immigration process. Despite this, HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has cut legal services funding for 26,000 unaccompanied children, potentially shifting funding to the Trump-aligned Burke Law Group, despite the firm’s lack of experience protecting the rights of immigrant children.

“The firm appears to have little relevant experience with the legal and practical challenges that children face, raising serious concerns about the firm’s ability to provide not just representation but adequate, zealous representation,” wrote the Senators. “Within hours of the notice in the Federal Register, the firm appears to have updated their website to include content about immigrant youth that didn’t exist on the website the previous day. At best, this is concerning, and at worst, it is a part of a coordinated scheme to paper over the firm’s lack of experience.”

Burke Law Group’s inexperience in the complexities of immigration law could result in serious harm for the nearly 2,000 children in ORR’s care. The firm employs just 26 people in total, adding an additional concern about the firm’s capacity to provide adequate legal representation to vulnerable children, some of whom are victims of trafficking or other abuse, let alone its competency to do so. Instead, the only clear outcome of this contracting award is that another Trump-aligned business will receive millions from the Trump Administration.

In the letter, the Senators demanded that Secretary Kennedy provide transparency as to why the Burke Law Group received this contract and details about the firm’s plans to provide legal assistance to unaccompanied children.

In addition to Padilla and Murphy, the letter was signed by U.S. Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Mazie Hirono (D-Hawaii), Tim Kaine (D-Va.), Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.), Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Patty Murray (D-Wash.), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), and Ron Wyden (D-Ore.).

Full text of the letter is available here and below:

Secretary Kennedy,

We are alarmed by the recent news that the Trump administration intends to award $150 million to a Houston law firm with close ties to President Trump and no apparent expertise in immigration law, to provide legal representation to unaccompanied children. Given the political connections between the firm’s senior leadership and the Trump administration, we have concerns about why you sidestepped the competitive bidding process to select this firm to provide legal services for children who are in the Office of Refugee Resettlement’s care and custody, and demand transparency into whether all federal procurement processes were followed. Children deserve competent representation by attorneys who practice at the intersection of child welfare and federal immigration law, but Americans also deserve to know why their federal dollars are being doled out to Trump’s friends and allies.

Most Americans agree children should not be forced to navigate the complex immigration process without adequate counsel, and Congress has enacted several provisions and funded counsel for these children for many years. The Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act (TVPRA) directs the Secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), through the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR), to “ensure, to the greatest extent practicable . . . that all unaccompanied alien children . . . have counsel to represent them in legal proceedings or matters and protect them from mistreatment, exploitation, and trafficking.” Recently, ORR moved to withhold funding from over 100 legal services providers that had provided counsel to children for decades, which essentially cut off all funding for representation of approximately 26,000 unaccompanied children currently navigating the immigration court process. Yet, seemingly overnight, ORR bypassed the competitive bidding process entirely, awarding the Burke Law Group (“theDear …, firm”) a one-year single-source cooperative agreement. We are awaiting final details, but the new agreement appears to cover around 1,800 children currently in ORR custody.

The firm appears to have little relevant experience with the legal and practical challenges that children face, raising serious concerns about the firm’s ability to provide not just representation but adequate, zealous representation. Within hours of the notice in the Federal Register, the firm appears to have updated their website to include content about immigrant youth that didn’t exist on the website the previous day. At best, this is concerning, and at worst, it is a part of a coordinated scheme to paper over the firm’s lack of experience. Furthermore, the firm’s senior leadership has political ties to the Trump administration. One of the founders of the firm was a Trump appointee – to an agency with no involvement in either child welfare or immigration law – and still another founding partner now serves as Principal Deputy Assistant Administrator in the Office of Enforcement and Compliance Assurance (OECA) for Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and has a questionable connection to harms perpetuated against detainees at immigration detention centers.

Consistent with the TVPRA, Congress has funded, and ORR administered, robust legal services to unaccompanied children under past Republican and Democratic administrations alike. Counsel for children should have at a bare minimum, experience and knowledge of the complex laws, policies, and dynamics of the intersection of immigration and child welfare law. Beyond the professional duty of legal competence, there is long-standing concern about adequate representation by qualified counsel for this vulnerable population, which is why Congress authorized and funded the program originally. HHS has yet to clarify how a 26-person Houston-based law firm will be able to adequately satisfy the TVPRA’s mandate to provide representation for unaccompanied children in ORR’s care and custody.

For these reasons and our deep concern regarding the treatment and protection of unaccompanied children, we call for an independent, timely, transparent, and public investigation at both the state and federal level into this award, with the full cooperation of ORR and HHS. We request the following information and responses to questions by August 25, 2026.

Please provide:

Names of all legal services providers considered for this cooperative agreement. Please include the type of provider (e.g., law firm, nonprofit) and their qualifications.

A copy of the firm’s application for the award.

A copy of the cooperative agreement and justification for single-source funding.

All communications between employees of the firm and agency personnel at ORR and HHS.

Copies of the merits determination for this agreement and the compliance justification for why the agreement is in line with the grants policy agreement.

Questions:

Nothing in this agreement discusses how children who were already represented will be supported by the firm or how such children will be transferred to attorneys of the firm.

What is the firm’s plan to ensure adequate continuity, experience, and knowledge in taking these cases, including its anticipated case-per-attorney ratio?

What, if any, subcontractors will the firm employ or plan to employ to handle the workload?

Describe the firm’s coordination, if any, with the supplemental cooperative agreement awardee, the U.S. Committee for Refugees and Immigrants.

There are currently only two attorneys at the firm listed as having any immigration experience. How is the cooperative agreement expected to ensure proper legal representation of approximately 1,800 children in ORR custody?

Will firm attorneys be required to convey a represented child’s sensitive personal information, or information of the represented child’s family members or prospective sponsors, to ORR or DHS without specific and credible reason to believe such information-sharing is in the best interest of the represented child?

Please explain what the firm is expected to share with ORR or HHS, including who will have access to such information, the cadence by which that information will be shared, and the purpose of such information-sharing.

Please also explain how the firm will be in compliance with ABA Model Rule 1.6 and Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct 1.05 and 1.06, involving a client’s informed consent.

How will this firm be handling ‘Know Your Rights’ presentations and legal consultations? How will they be providing these services to children not in Texas? Please clarify whether these services will be provided in-person or virtually.

Sincerely,

###

title: ON THE JOB FOR MICHIGAN: Local Leaders Highlight Peters’ Work to Support Michigan Communities After 2020 Midland Flood
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – In a new “On the Job” video from U.S. Senator Gary Peters’ (MI) office, local leaders highlight Peters’ efforts to help Michiganders recover in the wake of the catastrophic 2020 Midland flood. After the Edenville and Sanford dams failed in May 2020, many communities in the Great Lakes Bay Region faced widespread destruction of homes, businesses, and properties from the historic floodwaters. In response, Peters secured more than $30 million in federal funding to help these communities recover and rebuild. Peters also authored bipartisan legislation to improve the process of applying for federal disaster assistance to support communities like Sanford and others that were devastated by the flooding. The video is part of the On the Job for Michigan series, which highlights Peters’ leadership and advocacy on behalf of Michigan constituents and communities.

“The senator’s office was the most helpful in dealing with FEMA. It was extremely helpful to have the senator in our corner,” said Bridgette Gransden, Midland County Administrator. “We’re continuing to work with our state legislators, our federal legislators, to improve infrastructure in the community. I really think it’s important to acknowledge what the senator has done as far as advocating for the Midland community, the Great Lakes Bay Region.”

“We actually began some work in fall of 2020 to help very localized areas to recover and rebuild. If that entire process were streamlined, that would take a huge layer right off of the work that these people are doing, literally, with their sleeves rolled up and their mud boots on,” said Diane Middleton, Vice President of Advocacy, Midland Business Alliance.

“I remember Senator Peters had been here during the flood. We decided to contact Senator Peters’ office to see if he could help simplify the communications and help us get to the right person,” said Dolores Porte, Village of Sanford President. “When you're in the middle of a disaster, a lot of paperwork to fill out. It’s pretty daunting. If that simplification act had been in place, we wouldn't have had to fill out two different sets of paperwork with two different sets of people.”

Porte continued, “Small towns are about seeing people face to face and about relationships. So, having your staff come here pretty regularly to check on things, sit down over ice cream in the ice cream store, and have Senator Peters come through on his [motorcycle] tour. It meant a lot to have people actually come here.”

Watch the “On the Job” video here.

“The catastrophic flooding and destruction caused by those dam failures was absolutely devastating for the region, and it was worsened by the fact that we were in the middle of a pandemic,” said Senator Peters, Ranking Member of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee. “But one thing was clear then and remains true now: Michigan communities are tough and resilient. I was proud to stand alongside them during that difficult time, and I won't stop fighting to ensure all Michiganders have the resources they need to rebuild and emerge stronger in the face of disaster.”

As Ranking Member of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, Peters has led several efforts to help Michigan communities prepare for and recover from natural disasters. Peters’ Disaster Assistance Simplification Act would establish a universal application across federal agencies for those seeking federal assistance to recover from natural disasters such as severe storms, floods, wildfires, and more. Currently, individuals must fill out separate and detailed applications depending on what agency they need help from, a process that can take weeks or even months. Peters’ legislation, which passed the Senate, would significantly streamline this process to reduce the burden on disaster survivors.

In addition to leading the Disaster Assistance Simplification Act, Peters also authored legislation that was signed into law to merge the application deadlines for two key Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) programs that provide federal disaster assistance to individuals. Peters’ Disaster Assistance Deadline Alignment Act helps prevent confusion for disaster survivors and aims to reduce the burden on people who need to rebuild their lives after disasters. He also authored bipartisan legislation that was signed into law to protect FEMA Reservists from losing their full-time employment when called upon to assist with disaster response.

Peters also passed into law the bipartisan Safeguarding Tomorrow through Ongoing Risk Mitigation (STORM) Act, which helps states establish revolving loan funds for local governments to carry out mitigation projects that reduce natural disaster risk. Peters then secured $500 million for the program to help communities address the impacts of natural disasters. Michigan has been awarded $22.5 million in federal funding through the program to date.

Finally, in 2022, Peters’ bill to help protect pets and other animals during and in the aftermath of natural disasters and emergencies was also signed into law.

title: In Las Vegas, Rosen Celebrates Landmark Bipartisan Housing Law with Nevada Housing Leaders
text:
Senator Rosen Recently Helped Pass the Bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act into Law

LAS VEGAS, NV – Today, U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen visited Golden Rule Apartments, a new local apartment complex for seniors, with housing leaders from Southern Nevada to celebrate the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act that she helped pass into law. This law is the biggest housing package passed in decades, containing over 40 provisions to increase housing supply and lower costs for hardworking families. The act also includes provisions that limit the corporate buy-up of single-family units.

“The lack of available housing Nevadans can afford, along with the rising costs of homeownership and rent, is squeezing hardworking Nevada families. Addressing this crisis and lowering costs is a top priority for me, which is why I worked with Democrats and Republicans to pass the largest housing package in decades into law,” said Senator Rosen. “Today’s visit to Golden Rule Apartments and discussion with Southern Nevada housing leaders highlighted just how important this bipartisan law is, and the fact that it cannot be the end of our work to lower housing costs. I’ll keep fighting to address the housing crisis from all angles so Nevadans can afford a place to call home.”

“I remain hopeful that the ROAD Act can be another tool to help move housing solutions forward, especially for working families who keep Southern NV going every day. We know there are still real barriers in front of us. Land availability, limited or decreased funding, rising construction costs, and the growing gap between wages and housing prices. But progress does not happen all at once. It happens when we keep showing up, building partnerships, and finding ways to do more with what we have,” said Michelle Merced, CEO of Neighborhood Housing Services of Southern Nevada. “For the NHSSN team, this is an opportunity to remain “having a seat” at the table, continue to advocate for our community, and be part of the solutions that give more families a safe, stable place to call HOME.”

“We are grateful to Nevada’s federal delegation for their leadership and action in advancing the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act and recognizing that addressing our housing crisis requires meaningful federal action. This bipartisan legislation gives Nevada and communities across the country additional tools to increase housing supply, reduce barriers to development, preserve existing affordable housing, and improve access to rental assistance programs,” said Maurice Page, Executive Director of the Nevada Housing Coalition. “For Nevada, this cannot be the finish line. We must build on this federal action with state and local policies that increase housing production while addressing the needs of extremely low-income households, seniors, working families, and people experiencing homelessness. Our next step is making sure Nevada puts these tools to work in ways that reflect the needs of our communities and create lasting housing opportunities across the state.”

“Southern Nevada continues to face significant housing supply challenges, and we appreciate Senator Rosen’s leadership in advancing solutions that will help increase the supply of homes and expand housing opportunities for Nevadans,” said Tina Frias, CEO of the Southern Nevada Home Builders Association. “At SNHBA, we know that addressing housing affordability starts with increasing supply and ensuring builders can deliver a diverse range of housing options to meet the needs of our community. We must continue working to remove barriers to new housing development, so more Nevada families have a place to call home.”

Senator Rosen has been fighting to make housing more affordable in Nevada. She introduced legislation to exclude homebuilding materials from Trump’s tariffs and called on the administration to crack down on corporate price gouging in the housing market. Senator Rosen has also introduced a bipartisan bill to support small businesses in the housing industry and bipartisan legislation to help grow the construction workforce, making it easier to build more houses and bring down costs. Senator Rosen has helped secure millions in federal funding for housing projects all across Nevada. In August, she successfully pushed the Trump Administration to release more than $3.3 million in federal funding it was withholding for affordable housing across Nevada.

title: ICYMI: Sen. Schiff Calls Out Trump Prioritizing Self-Enrichment Over Addressing Affordability During Conversation at San Francisco’s Commonwealth Club
text:
Schiff: “And central to that objective, I think, is making the economy work for people again …The problem today is that people are working, and they can barely afford to get by. And I don’t think our democracy will ever be on a secure footing until our economy is on a secure footing. Until people feel it’s working for them.”

San Francisco, CA – U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) spoke at the Commonwealth Club World Affairs of California on President Trump’s self-enrichment schemes, highlighting that Trump’s choices are making cost of living issues worse for the American people.

Schiff spoke with moderator San Francisco Chronicle reporter Hannah Wiley on how he is fighting back against the Trump administration and taking steps to address the affordability crisis and pushing to end the war with Iran.

View the full interview here.

Key Excerpts:

On the importance of repairing the Department of Justice:

What is the cost to the American people. Now, I would prioritize, and this is a cost that is more difficult to measure. But I would prioritize the corruption that we have seen within the Justice Department itself, and maybe that’s because I come out of the Justice Department. I have a certain reverence for that department, but also because I think the damage to that department has been the most wide-scale of all the agencies. Certainly, things like USAID have been devastated. But it will take years, if not decades, to restore the reputation of the department for independence and nonpartisanship and the rule of law. But that department continues to do great damage. So, in the case of the slush fund for cop beaters, that’s 1.776 billion dollars of taxpayer money. That’s a direct cost to taxpayers if that is allowed to go on.

On Trump’s corrupt dealings:

[…] They don’t get a pass any more than anyone else. I saw the president recently was asked about the ethics language that I’ve been fighting to get into any market structure bill overseeing crypto. And the president making the false claim to reporters that they want to treat me differently than everybody else. No, actually, the problem for him is we want to treat him the same as everybody else. He wants to be treated differently. He doesn’t want rules to apply to him. And they should apply to him, and they should apply to his kids, just like they should apply to anyone and their family if they’re engaged in corrupt conduct. We simply don’t know when this administration is making decisions of foreign policy. Are they with the best interests of the public in mind, or are they because the president got a $400 million dollar jet from Qatar? Are we making decisions vis-a-vis Saudi Arabia because they’re in the best interests of the country, or because the Saudis are investing billions in Jared Kushner’s investment fund, or because they’ve invested billions in Trump properties or crypto enterprises or that of their kids. There is simply no way of knowing, and to protect the country, we really do need to know. So, I would say no one is excluded, no one is included just because of who they are, whose family they’re in.

On the values of the Democratic Party:

[…] We have a whole generation of young people that wonder if they’ll ever be able to buy a home. The year that I was born, the average new home buyer was 28 years old. The average home buyer today is 40 years old. If you were going to have an equivalent circumstance to my dad’s, then and be able to buy a home in California for your annual income. You would need an annual income of about a million dollars. And it doesn’t have to be that way in this country. And I think the Democrats should hit the ground rolling with an agenda that brings down the cost of housing, and the cost of childcare, and the cost of health care, and expands access to health care, with bold, non-incremental ideas about how to do it. One of the things that the Republicans have demonstrated that I think we should take a page from that book is if you have the courage of your convictions, you can move the country far and fast. In our case, in the right direction; in their case, horribly backward.

[…] And I think when millions of people start to see the life they have as less than their parents for the first time in our history. All too many are willing to entertain any demagogue who comes along, promising they alone can fix it. So, we have got to address these big economic challenges, and I make that priority number one.

On making housing affordable:

[…] There are mechanisms that we have; we don’t have to invent them. Things called the low-income housing tax credit, for example, that really work that help incentivize the development of low-income housing and middle-income housing, or could, but those tax incentives are capped. And so the funds available under those programs are quickly limited and reach capacity, and then new housing projects cannot qualify because they’re gone. I’ve introduced a bill called the Housing BOOM Act that would lift that cap, that would triple the amount of housing you could build under this program, if not more. It has a whole other sorts of pieces to it that focus on middle-income housing and workforce housing. But these are just things that the federal government can do, and that is change the tax incentives.

On what Congress can do to protect the Justice Department in the future:

[…] And in terms of what the Congress can do, we can certainly do oversight of the Justice Department. They will resist it. It won’t be easy to do. We will be heavily reliant on whistleblowers. One of the other legislative proposals I think that ought to be early on our agenda when we take over the House and Senate and White House. It is a bill that I’ve introduced. It’s called the Protecting Our Democracy Act.

[…] We need to enshrine these protections in law, and so we will need to introduce a newer version at the end of this horror show that addresses each of these things that tries to once again rebuild the wall of independence between the White House and the Justice Department.

On building an economy that works for everyone:

[…] It shouldn’t be that young people have to become horribly saddled in debt to afford an education. It shouldn’t be that health care is unaffordable for people. If people are working hard, they should be able to afford a good quality of life in this country. And if they’re not able to afford a good quality of life, it’s not their fault; it’s ours, as policymakers. And I think any elected official who does not recognize that and is not advocating for things that are big and bold that will address that, things like Medicare for all that would bring down the cost of healthcare. I think people who are not embracing bold solutions are going to be in trouble.

[…] We just have to stay laser focused on the economy, and the needs of the American people, and the need to make the economy work for people, and to bring home how this president is so oblivious. The only thing he cares about, the only economy he cares about, is his own damn personal wealth. And he’s made more money as president in a year and a half, two years than in his whole life combined.

On the way to bring an end to the Iran War:

[…] The way to bring an end to the war is by not funding it. And if we had some of the Republicans willing to go with us to say we are going to cut off funding for this. Then it would dramatically bring about an end to the war. This war was ill considered from the very beginning. It’s already had the most tragic consequences. We’ve lost 18 servicemembers. It has escalated the cost of living for American families. It has empowered Iran already tragically. Prior to the war, the Iranians may have theorized that they had the power to close the Strait, notwithstanding the force the United States might use to reopen it. They may have known that in theory. Now they know it in practice, and that is already a strategic defeat for the United States. I don’t know how the administration ends this war, except I think, for their part, they’re going to look for any face-saving way they can. Which means that the resolution is not going to be a good one. It will not, I think, bring about any meaningful guarantee of an end to the Iranian nuclear program.

title: In the Los Angeles Times, Sen. Schiff: How Democrats Can Repair the Broken Supreme Court
text:
Schiff: “Future Democratic majorities in Congress — perhaps starting as soon as January — should make repairing the court and reforming the judicial branch a priority to make sure it does not continue to operate as a partisan and retrograde institution.”

Read the full op-ed here.

Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), a member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, published an op-ed with the Los Angeles Times on the urgent need for Supreme Court reform and how it should be a top priority for Democrats in 2027.

“It’s no secret that the Supreme Court has become an extension of our partisan politics over the past decade. The decisions handed down in the 2026 session prove just how broken the court has become and how unrepresentative it is of the views of the American people,” wrote the Senator.

In the op-ed, Senator Schiff unpacks how the Supreme Court and the federal judicial system is broken, and why we must take action to ensure the Court does not continue operating as a partisan and retrograde institution. He lays out how the Court’s rulings this year demonstrate its partisanship and dysfunction, against the backdrop of a festering culture of corruption in our judiciary. Schiff outlines his vision of how Democrats can and should unite around a simple and popular agenda to reform the Court and restore faith in our justice system.

Background: Last month, Senator Schiff launched his push for Congress to pass legislation to strengthen accountability, transparency, and ethical standards across the federal judicial system. His proposed reforms are necessary in addition to other significant reforms to the Supreme Court and judiciary, including term limits, expanding the Court, and enforcing a code of ethics.

Read the full op-ed here and below:

Los Angeles Times: How Democrats can repair the broken Supreme Court

By U.S. Senator Adam Schiff

It’s no secret that the Supreme Court has become an extension of our partisan politics over the past decade. The decisions handed down in the 2026 session prove just how broken the court has become and how unrepresentative it is of the views of the American people. Reactions show how little confidence the public has in its fairness.

Future Democratic majorities in Congress — perhaps starting as soon as January — should make repairing the court and reforming the judicial branch a priority to make sure it does not continue to operate as a partisan and retrograde institution.

One need look no further than the court’s recent decisions for evidence of its partisanship and dysfunction.

President Trump’s handpicked court continued to gut the Voting Rights Act, greenlighting Republican gerrymandering to tip the scales of this upcoming and future elections, and undermining a half century of precedent and the hard-fought battles of the civil rights era. After professing their abiding respect for precedent during confirmation hearings, a partisan majority of the court has no trouble striking down any precedent when it disfavors GOP control of Congress.

Trump’s justices have allowed federal immigration agents to arrest and detain individuals, without the requisite standard of cause, based on their apparent ethnicity, perceived jobs or spoken language. This nod to the conservative agenda to roll back civil rights also required the disparagement of any precedents to the contrary.

The court gave Trump the power to fire heads of independent agencies, including federal trade commissioners, clearing the way for him to assert political influence on additional independent government bodies intended by Congress to be insulated from such pressures. This required overturning more than nine decades of precedent. Only when it came to the Federal Reserve was the court willing to sustain the independence of one of these bodies, and then only because wealthy financial interests (and the economy more generally) collided with the personal whim of the president.

A full third of the court is now so extreme that it almost allowed Trump to overturn the Constitution with an executive order, which attempted to claim he alone had power to do away with birthright citizenship.

These attacks on the Constitution and decades of established American law have not taken place in a vacuum. Their backdrop is a festering culture of corruption in our courts — with undisclosed luxury gifts and glaring conflicts of interest, and members of our judiciary refusing to recuse themselves from cases tied directly to their benefactors’ financial or political advantage, or their own.

It is not surprising then that the American public has abandoned reverence for those who are meant to be our independent arbiters of the law. Chief Justice John Roberts claimed that his court would merely “call balls and strikes.” But decisions to overturn Roe vs. Wade and dismantle the Voting Rights Act have led more than half of Americans to disapprove of how the court is doing its job, with almost half of Americans believing that the court “is ruling on President Trump’s policies based on ideology, rather than the law.” Who can blame them?

Democrats should unite around a simple and deeply popular agenda to fix the court.

We must enact term limits for Supreme Court justices to promote predictability and stop institution-defeating gamesmanship around depriving presidents of hearings and votes on their nominees.

We need to expand the number of justices sitting on the court to reflect the expanded size of our nation and to prevent this court — now otherwise fixed for a generation in its steadfast partisanship — from further destroying the hard-fought system of rights the American people have come to rely on.

And we must create an enforceable code of ethics, bringing this court under the same set of rules of accountability as other leaders privileged to be in public service.

I’ve drafted legislation to build on these three core tenets, to ensure transparency and ethical standards across the federal judicial system.

After being called out for repeated conflicts of interest, the Supreme Court established a toothless code of conduct in November 2023 with no external body to enforce it. Under these unenforced and unenforceable guidelines, justices act as their own ethical arbiters with no accountability.

To rectify this, I’ve proposed extending the conflict of interest statute that already applies to executive branch employees to include federal judges and justices, preventing them from participating in cases relating to their own financial interests.

So long as judges and justices know where their investments lie — and therefore where they may profit — it is fair to question the impartiality of their decisions. The law I propose, called the Justice Is Blind Act, would require judges, justices and their immediate family to put their financial assets into a blind trust. Members of Congress should be required to do the same, if not divest their assets entirely.

Lastly, we need to bring much-needed transparency to our judiciary. By expanding the Freedom of Information Act to the judiciary, we would create an explicit right of public access to administrative records so the American people and the press can access judicial complaints, investigation records, meeting minutes and more.

Passing these reforms will be difficult in a Congress where Republicans have become rubber stamps for the president’s priorities, but it’s important for Democrats to push for legislation that tells the country what we stand for, and what we’re willing to do when we flip majorities in Congress and take back the White House.

If Justice Samuel Alito retires soon — as some have speculated he will — that may open the door for Trump to appoint a fourth Supreme Court justice — and yet another political ally poised to advance the president’s agenda rather than the rule of law or justice. This should be a warning to all Americans of how much is at stake if we don’t act to fix this system.

These proposals would help restore balance and credibility to the court. It has been packed, and it should be unpacked. It has become an agent of partisan and cultural warfare, and it should become a neutral arbiter of the law. It has shredded precedent to achieve political objectives, and it should respect precedent once more. It has become beholden to wealthy financial interests, and it must disentangle itself from the personal economic benefit of its decisions.

The American people’s trust in the judicial system might be battered, but when Democrats control Congress again, they will have the opportunity to rebuild that trust and should not miss what could be the last best chance to restore some measure of integrity to the courts.

Adam Schiff represents California in the U.S. Senate.

###

title: SCHUMER URGES ARMY TO SELECT FORT DRUM FOR NEXT-GENERATION NUCLEAR POWER PROGRAM TO STRENGTHEN ENERGY RESILIENCE AT DOMESTIC MILITARY INSTALLATIONS
text:
Last Year, Fort Drum Was Among Nine Sites Shortlisted For Army’s Next-Generation Nuclear Microreactor Program To Protect Domestic Military Bases From Grid Failures, Critical Energy Deficiencies, And Other Threats

Fort Drum’s Strategic Mission Sets, Wheeler-Sack Army Airfield, Skilled Personnel, And Existing Infrastructure Make It The Best-In-Class To Demonstrate Safe And Secure, On-Site Nuclear Power Generation

Schumer To Army: Fort Drum Needs Reliable Power To Protect National Security

After the U.S. Army named Fort Drum as one of nine domestic Army installations under consideration to host the Janus Program, U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer today urged U.S. Secretary of the Army Dan Driscoll to select Fort Drum for the Army’s effort to deploy a commercial nuclear microreactor to strengthen the installation’s energy resilience and support critical military operations. Schumer explained that the effort is to ensure military sites have secure, reliable power if the commercial power grid goes down and that after analyzing sites across the United States, including energy requirements and power infrastructure, that the Army shortlisted Fort Drum.

“Fort Drum’s facilities, personnel, and infrastructure make it uniquely positioned to spearhead the Army’s Janus Program and demonstrate this important, innovative nuclear microreactor technology. Fort Drum is top-of-class to lead in advanced nuclear development. Bringing a safe and secure nuclear energy source to Fort Drum is a win-win for strengthening the base’s energy security and protecting our Army from vulnerabilities like grid failures,” said Senator Schumer. “As one of the most advanced and strategic military installations in the country, Fort Drum is ready, and the critical missions it carries out to protect our nation demand reliable, resilient, and independent onsite power generation.”

The Department of the Army’s Janus Program is an initiative to deploy commercial nuclear microreactors on domestic military installations. The program will help strengthen the Army’s installation energy resilience, support future mission requirements, and advance next-generation nuclear energy. The program aims to have a working prototype operating on a domestic Army base by the end of 2028. Last year, the Army announced that nine military installations—including Fort Drum—were shortlisted for consideration to host a commercial nuclear microreactor under the Janus Program.

Schumer explained that Fort Drum, home to Wheeler-Sack Army Airfield, which serves as the primary mobilization airfield for the 10th Mountain Division, is one of the most strategic military installations in the United States. A nuclear microreactor would provide Fort Drum with a reliable, independent, and continuous source of energy for mission-critical support functions, command and control elements, mobilization activities, and other vital capabilities, including during grid-level energy infrastructure outages and the disruption of key power supplies. Schumer added that Fort Drum’s location would allow the Army to assess a microreactor’s performance under harsh weather and other conditions needed to inform its efforts to integrate energy solutions into future operations. Schumer also explained Fort Drum currently uses over 60 megawatts of power, most of which is pulled from the local grid.

Fort Drum is a vital economic and community anchor for the North Country, supporting thousands of military and civilian jobs. Schumer underscored that Fort Drum is well-equipped to demonstrate how nuclear power can reduce vulnerabilities and reinforce critical U.S. defense infrastructure. It is expected that the commercial microreactor would not require significant land use changes and would be designed to produce up to 20 megawatts (MW) of power to support installation operations. Fort Drum officials and the local community have conveyed support for the site’s selection for the Janus Program.

Schumer’s letter to U.S. Secretary of the Army Dan Driscoll can be found HERE or below:

Dear Secretary Driscoll:

Late last year, the U.S. Army announced a list of nine domestic military installations—including Fort Drum, New York—to be considered for the deployment of a commercial nuclear microreactor under the Army’s Janus Program. The Janus Program is a critical opportunity to strengthen the Total Army’s installation energy resilience through the deployment of next-generation nuclear energy and support future mission requirements consistent with the goals of the National Defense Strategy. I write to encourage you to select Fort Drum, given the installation’s distinct combination of operational need, personnel, and existing infrastructure that make it an optimal site to spearhead the Janus Program.

Fort Drum is one of the most advanced and strategic military installations in the United States. Fort Drum has the facilities, personnel, and infrastructure needed to be the best-in-class site to field a nuclear microreactor. The garrison is home to Wheeler-Sack Army Airfield, which serves as the primary mobilization airfield for the 10th Mountain Division and is a strategic asset and power projection capability for the Joint Force. Moreover, Fort Drum and the 10th Mountain Division’s operational tempo and strategic importance make the installation the ideal candidate to demonstrate the need for secure, onsite power generation to support military installations and critical mission sets.

As the Army continues to prepare for large-scale combat operations (LSCO) and conflicts in increasingly contested environments, where adversaries will target critical infrastructure, including the potential disruption of highly interconnected key power supplies and grid-level energy infrastructure, military installations must be capable of executing their mission even during prolonged outages and disruptions to the local grid. A nuclear microreactor would provide Fort Drum with a reliable, non-carbon polluting, independent, and continuous source of energy for mission-critical support functions, command and control elements, mobilization activities, and other vital capabilities during contingency operations. It would also allow the Army to validate the operational benefits of advanced nuclear energy while strengthening the resilience of one of its premier power projection platforms.

Furthermore, serving as the home to the 10th Mountain Division—the most deployed conventional Army unit since 2001—Fort Drum has long been a leader in developing, testing, and proving the Army’s cold-weather and expeditionary capabilities, including hosting large-scale training exercises for multi-domain operations in harsh climate and austere environments that simulate conditions warfighters may encounter downrange. Fort Drum’s permissive training environment would allow the Army to assess a microreactor’s performance under realistic operational conditions, enhance the installation’s energy resilience by reducing grid dependency vulnerabilities and interdependencies, and strengthen the Army’s ability to maintain a high readiness posture, including by informing its efforts to integrate resilient energy solutions into future operations.

For these reasons, I urge you to select Fort Drum to host a nuclear microreactor as part of the Army’s Janus Program. I appreciate the careful consideration you will give Fort Drum’s candidacy during the site selection process, and I am confident you will find that Fort Drum has the personnel, infrastructure, resources, and capacity consistent with the Army’s basing criteria under the Janus Program.

###

title: ICYMI: Annual Shaheen-Led Bipartisan Resolution Designating National Fentanyl Prevention and Awareness Day Unanimously Passes Senate
text:
(Washington, DC) – Last week, a bipartisan resolution annually led by U.S. Senators Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH) and Chuck Grassley (R-IA) designating August 21 as "Fentanyl Prevention and Awareness Day” unanimously passed the U.S. Senate. The bipartisan push aims to raise awareness around dangers of fentanyl, highlight prevention efforts, encourage drug-free lifestyles and recognize the lives lost to drug overdoses.

“I’m glad the Senate came together to unanimously pass our bipartisan resolution designating August 21 as National Fentanyl Prevention and Awareness Day and memorializing those who have lost their lives to drug overdoses,” said Senator Shaheen. “There’s always more work to be done to address the substance use disorder crisis in New Hampshire, and driving more awareness in our communities around the dangers of fentanyl use is one important way we can prevent the loss of more lives.”

A copy of the bipartisan resolution can be read HERE.

As a senior member of the U.S. Senate Appropriations Committee and Ranking Member of the Senate Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration and Related Agencies (Ag-FDA) Appropriations Subcommittee, Shaheen is committed to fighting the substance use disorder crisis in New Hampshire. Earlier this year, Shaheen renewed a years-long effort to authorize billions in federal funding for substance use disorder treatment and prevention with the reintroduction of the Turn the Tide Act. Shaheen also leads the bipartisan End Veterans Overdose Act to expand access to naloxone and other overdose reversal agents to our veterans, which went on to unanimously clear the Senate Veterans’ Affairs Committee—a significant step toward passing the bill into law. In the Fiscal Year 2026 Military Construction, Veterans Affairs and Related Agencies Appropriations bill that was signed into law, Shaheen secured provisions that will ensure veterans can better access health care, including substance use disorder treatment. In 2025, Senator Shaheen introduced the Keeping Drugs Out of School Act alongside Senator Grassley to establish a new grant program to educate students about the dangers of synthetic opioids.
