title: Republican Reps. Steve Scalise, John James visit Temple Israel in show of support for Jewish community
text:
A top member of Congress visited Michigan on Thursday to show support to the Jewish community following an attempted mass casualty attack that happened in March.

House Majority Leader Steve Scalise (R-LA) visited Temple Israel in West Bloomfield. The congregation was the target of an attack by a gunman who rammed his truck, loaded with fireworks and gasoline, into the building and began shooting. The attack failed in part because the vehicle became jammed and the attacker was unable to get out of the burning vehicle, and he shot himself.

Around 140 children and staff were reportedly in the building at the time of the attack; had the attacker been able to exit the vehicle, the incident likely would have been far worse.

Scalise is the second highest-ranking member of the U.S. House of Representatives, behind just the Speaker of the House. He was joined at Temple Israel by Rep. John James, who represents parts of Oakland and Macomb counties in Congress.

James co-sponsored the Jewish American Security Act (H.R. 9211), which would help protect members of the Jewish community and other faith groups. One of the ways it would do that is by authorizing a significant increase in funding for the Nonprofit Security Grant Program that supports security at synagogues and other at-risk nonprofits.

“I appreciate Leader Scalise coming here to see the site of the attack first-hand, and to talk with community leaders,” said James, R-Shelby Township. “To have a top member of Congress visit signals that we are treating the rise in threats seriously, and that this is an urgent national concern.”

James immediately spoke in support of the congregation following the failed attack.

James also visited Israel in Nov. 2023, following the Oct. 7 terrorist attack in which Hamas militants raped and murdered innocent civilians, many of them young people peacefully enjoying a music festival.

“There is a sickness in a certain segment of our population that reacted to the Oct. 7 terrorist attack with sympathy for the attackers, and which has spent the past few years irrationally targeting members of the Jewish community here in Michigan with hateful words and actions,” James said. “I fought extremists in Iraq; we cannot let that kind of violent thinking take root here in Michigan. Everyone should be able to live and worship in peace.”

title: Kaptur Applauds Additional Investment Of $289,597 For Northwest Ohio Airports
text:
Toledo, OH — Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee, announced that two Northwest Ohio airports will receive United States Department of Transportation Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) awards for critical upgrades and improvements. The Defiance County Regional Airport Authority will receive $192,887 for pavement reconstruction, while the Put-in-Bay Township Port Authority will receive $96,710 for an airport-wide obstruction survey.

“Ohio’s strong aviation history shines bright across our Great Lakes region, and it is a privilege to build upon it by investing in local airport innovation and expansion,” said Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09). “Creating partnerships between Federal agencies and our local communities is vital to Northwest Ohio’ continued success. Working together to deliver these awards makes our airports safer and more efficient for all aviation staff, customers, and the businesses that rely on them. Together we are creating a standard of excellence that will help our region thrive for all the generations to come.”

Called Northwest Ohio’s “gateway to business and community,” Defiance County Memorial Airport has been undergoing many improvements over recent years to enhance its infrastructure. Today’s $192,887 investment will help the airport complete the final phase of reconstructing 1,091 square yards of East Apron pavement that has reached the end of its useful life. The Put-in-Bay Airport is located on South Bass Island and services both small commercial carriers and private aviators carrying freight or vacationers to the area. Its $96,710 award will help the airport conduct an airport-wide obstruction survey for the purpose of collecting detailed aeronautical and environmental data. Comprehensive data will make landing and takeoff safer and can help with future airport planning.

These new federal investments build on previous awards to airports across our Northwest Ohio region in recent years. In July of this year, Congresswoman Kaptur secured over $3.67 Million for Toledo-area airports and over $7.8 Million for three Northwest Ohio regional airports, including Erie-Ottawa International Airport, Toledo Executive Airport, and Fulton County Airport. On May 18th, Congresswoman Kaptur announced a $1.4 Million Award for Eugene F. Kranz Toledo Express Airport. On May 12th, 2026, Congresswoman Kaptur announced over $1 Million in federal investment for infrastructure improvements at Williams County Regional Airport, Defiance Memorial Airport, and Sandusky County Regional Airport.

title: Kean Hosts Eagle Scout and Girl Scout Gold Award Event
text:
(August 14, 2026) READINGTON, NJ – Yesterday, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) held his third Eagle Scout and Girl Scout Gold Award Event. Scouts from New Jersey's 7th Congressional District who achieved the rank of Eagle Scout or completed their Girl Scout Gold Award in 2025 and 2026 were invited to attend. Family, Scoutmasters and other adult scout leaders from across the district were also welcome to join the celebration with their Scouts.

Eagle Scout is the highest rank attainable in the Boy Scouts of America organization. To become an Eagle Scout, one must earn a total of 21 merit badges and demonstrate scout spirit, service, and leadership. This includes an extensive service project that scouts plan, organize, lead, and manage.

The Girl Scout Gold Award is the highest and most prestigious achievement in Girl Scouting, requiring Seniors and Ambassadors in grades 9–12 to complete a rigorous, sustainable community service project of at least 80 hours. They must identify a community issue, research its root cause, build a team of volunteers and community experts, and create a sustainable, long-lasting solution.

“Very few receive the rank of Eagle Scout or earn the Girl Scout Gold Award, and those who do deserve to be recognized for this achievement,” said Congressman Kean. “Through their generosity and creativity, they are laying the groundwork for lives that will be directed by the values of volunteering, leadership and civic duty, which will impact the world around them in distinct and impactful ways.”

“As an Eagle Scout myself, I was pleased to participate in Congressman Kean’s Scout recognition ceremony, where I had the opportunity to say a few words and introduce him,” said Eagle Scout and Readington Township Committeeman Adam Mueller. “Congressman Kean has been a consistent and genuine supporter of Scouting in our district. His commitment to recognizing the hard work, leadership, and service of our Scouts strengthens these programs and the young people who benefit from them. We’re fortunate to have a representative who understands the value of Scouting and actively invests in its success.”

“Being an Eagle Scout takes years of commitment, leadership, and hard work. It is a challenge that most kids, even Scouts, do not achieve,” said Eagle Scout Christopher Forzani. “Because of this, it was an honor to learn about the Eagle Projects of other local Scouts and to meet Congressman Tom Kean, who gifted each Scout a flag that had been flown over the Capitol.”

“I appreciate Congressman Kean and his staff hosting this event to recognize those who have earned the highest awards in Scouting,” said Girl Scout Gold Award recipient Faith Feldman. “It was really cool to receive a flag that has been flown at the US Capitol.”

The event honored 20 Eagle and Girl Scouts who represented all six counties in New Jersey’s 7th Congressional District. More than 55 people attended this event, including parents, grandparents, siblings, and adult scout leaders.

title: Release: Rep. Khanna’s Statement on New Yale Analysis Finding Medicare for All Could Save More Than $1 Trillion Annually
text:
Washington, DC – Representative Ro Khanna (CA-17) released the following statement on a new analysis from researchers at the Yale School of Public Health finding that Medicare for All could save the United States more than $1 trillion in annual health care spending while providing universal coverage.

The updated analysis was released by researchers at Yale’s Center for Infectious Disease Modeling and Analysis in response to an inquiry from Rep. Khanna about the economic impact of a single-payer universal health care system. The researchers updated their peer-reviewed 2020 Lancet analysis using the most recent national data and accounting for coverage retractions enacted in 2025.

In a letter to Rep. Khanna, the researchers project that Medicare for All would reduce annual national health expenditures from $5.28 trillion to $4.24 trillion - a savings of $1.04 trillion, or nearly 20 percent of current health spending. The researchers also estimate that lowering the Medicare eligibility age to 50 would cost the federal government approximately $180 billion annually, after accounting for existing federal health spending, employer-sponsored insurance offsets and premiums paid by beneficiaries.

The analysis also found that Medicare for All could strengthen hospital finances and allow for higher reimbursement rates where needed. Hospitals currently provide approximately $52 billion in uncompensated care each year, which would be reimbursed in full under a single-payer system. Services currently reimbursed at Medicaid rates would rise to Medicare rates, while hospitals and health care providers would save on administrative costs associated with navigating insurers and prior authorization requirements. The researchers found that the more than $1 trillion in overall savings would provide room for additional targeted increases in reimbursement rates for certain hospitals or medical specialties where needed.

“Americans are drowning in medical debt while insurance companies and big pharma make huge profits. This analysis shows we can guarantee health care to every American and save our country more than $1 trillion every year. We can also strengthen our hospitals by ensuring they are paid for care that currently goes uncompensated and reducing the enormous administrative costs of our current system,” said Rep. Ro Khanna. “The case for Medicare for All has never been clearer or more urgent. Congress must pass Medicare for All and finally guarantee health care as a right for every American.”

title: Congressman Nick LaLota Presents over $2 Million in Federal Funding for Suffolk County Law Enforcement
text:
YAPHANK, NY — Congressman Nick LaLota (R-Suffolk County) yesterday presented $2.025 million to the Suffolk County Police Department and Suffolk County Sheriff’s Office for vehicle fleet improvements which he secured through the Fiscal Year 2026 appropriations process.

LaLota was joined by Suffolk County Executive Ed Romaine, Suffolk County Police Commissioner Kevin Catalina, Suffolk County Undersheriff John Becker, and local officials for the check presentations at Suffolk County Police Department headquarters.

The $825,000 for the Suffolk County Police Department will support the acquisition of new police vehicles. The $1.2 million for the Suffolk County Sheriff’s Office will support fleet enhancements and help ensure deputies have reliable vehicles to carry out their duties.

“Our men and women in Law Enforcement put their lives on the line every day to keep Suffolk County one of the safest counties in America. We must make sure they have the resources to do that job safely and effectively. This $2 million in federal funds brings more of our tax dollars back to Suffolk County. As a member of the Appropriations Committee, I have a front-row seat to how Washington spends your money, and I’m going to keep bringing it back here to support our Cops, our Sheriffs, our public safety and our way of life,” said Congressman Nick LaLota.

“This congressman has fought for Suffolk County. We are so appreciative of this. This strengthens our effort to keep everyone in Suffolk County as safe as possible. You delivered for Suffolk County. We are deeply appreciative of this,” said Suffolk County Executive Ed Romaine.

“The $2 million that is going to Law Enforcement today is going to go a long way in helping to augment a severely depleted force of vehicles that we have in the Suffolk County Police Department. We're now going to be able to purchase 15 vehicles as a result of the over $800,000 that Congressman LaLota and his staff were generous enough to give to us. That's going to help the men and women of Suffolk County Police Department not only be safer but keep the people of Suffolk County safer as well,” said Suffolk County Police Commissioner Kevin Catalina.

“On behalf of both Sheriff Toulon and the men and women of the Suffolk County Sheriff's Office, I want to thank Congressman LaLota for his continued support of Law Enforcement and for securing this $1.2 million grant. This funding is a significant investment in the sheriff's office fleet and will allow us to purchase approximately 15 vehicles, both marked and unmarked. Our vehicles are one of the most important tools that our Deputy Sheriffs utilize every single day. Our personnel need safe and reliable vehicles to do their jobs effectively,” said Suffolk County Undersheriff John Becker.

Background:

The funding is part of LaLota’s broader effort to bring federal resources back to Suffolk County.

title: Representative John W. Mannion Announces Federal Public Safety Funding for Syracuse and Onondaga County
text:
SYRACUSE, N.Y. – Representative John W. Mannion today announced that the City of Syracuse will receive $151,005 in federal funding to support public safety initiatives carried out by the Syracuse Police Department and the Onondaga County Sheriff’s Office.

Representative John W. Mannion said, “Everyone deserves to live in a safe community, and this funding will provide local law enforcement with additional tools to protect residents and respond to emergencies. It will strengthen security at public facilities and large gatherings while supporting the specialized officers and equipment needed to keep Syracuse and Onondaga County safe. I’ll continue working to ensure our region receives its fair share of federal funding and that local law enforcement agencies have what they need to do their jobs.”

The Syracuse Police Department will use its portion of the award to purchase hardened security barriers for the newly renovated Public Safety Building, mobile security barriers for mass gathering locations, equipment for its SWAT team, replacement parts for its drone fleet, and support for emergency management incidents.

The Onondaga County Sheriff’s Office will use its portion of the funding to purchase a snowmobile for its Snowmobile Unit and critical equipment for its SWAT team.

City of Syracuse Mayor Sharon Owens said, “Sustaining and modernizing our public safety capabilities is essential to protecting our residents, visitors, and first responders. Thanks to Congressman Mannion, this funding will allow the Syracuse Police Department to take proactive steps to ensure we are prepared for emerging threats, equipped for complex incidents, and able to maintain a high standard of public safety across our City.”

Onondaga County Sheriff Toby Shelley said, “Congressman John Mannion remains a steadfast champion for Central New York law enforcement. From securing initial funding for the Sheriff’s Office’s first wellness program during his tenure as State Senator to delivering critical federal funding for a new mobile command vehicle since he has been in Congress, Congressman Mannion consistently ensures local officers have the resources needed to protect our community. That unwavering commitment holds true today with his latest funding announcement, further strengthening our regional public safety operations.”

Representative Mannion recently secured over $2 million for new mobile command units for the Syracuse Police Department and Onondaga County Sheriff’s Office. He is also requesting additional funding in FY27 Community Project Funding to help the Sheriff’s Office replace aging patrol vehicles.

The funding was awarded by the Department of Justice’s Bureau of Justice Assistance through the Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant Program. The program provides federal resources to state and local governments for law enforcement, crime prevention, emergency response, technology, and other public safety initiatives.

title: McCaul Returns from Bold Visit to Taiwan
text:
WASHINGTON – House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Emeritus Michael McCaul concluded his third visit to Taiwan. While there, he gave a keynote speech at a forum focused on Indo-Pacific security and met with high-level officials including President Lai, who conferred the Order of Brilliant Star with Special Grand Cordon on him for his support of Taiwan. Chairman Emeritus McCaul released the following statement on his trip:

"At a time when the stakes couldn't be higher, I was proud to visit Taiwan for the third time to reaffirm the United States' unwavering support. The increasing belligerence of the Chinese Communist Party poses a direct threat — not only to Taiwan, but to the entire global balance of power. That's why I've been proud to support Taiwan, from championing the 2024 supplemental bill to spearheading AUKUS legislation to bolstering U.S.-Taiwan economic ties. I'm honored to receive the Brilliant Star from President Lai and will continue standing with Taiwan as we pursue a free and democratic future in which peace through strength prevails."

McCaul delivered the keynote speech at Taiwan's Ketagalan Forum, a conference on security across the Indo-Pacific. In his remarks, he emphasized how the U.S. is honoring its commitments to Taiwan under the Taiwan Relations Act.

Image

Click to watch McCaul's keynote speech

Next, McCaul met with President Lai Ching-te, who conferred the Order of Brilliant Star with Special Grand Cordon on him for his support of Taiwan. McCaul previously visited President Lai immediately after his inauguration. In response, the CCP conducted war games around the island throughout that visit and sanctioned McCaul. During this week's meeting, McCaul spoke about how the CCP's aggression has only reinforced his commitment to support a free and peaceful Taiwan.

McCaul receives the Order of Brilliant Star with Special Grand Cordon from President Lai (photos courtesy of the president's office)

McCaul gifts President Lai a Texas A&M baseball jersey in recognition of Taiwan's love of baseball

McCaul also met with Taiwan's Vice President Bi-khim Hsiao, who discussed Taiwan's efforts to integrate artificial intelligence into its defense technologies.

McCaul with Vice President Hsiao at the Grand Hotel in Taipei

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs hosted a luncheon with McCaul, during which he and Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung discussed the ties between Texas and Taiwan — particularly Taiwan's recent investments in the semiconductor and technology industries in the Lone Star State.

McCaul with Foreign Minister Lin and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs

McCaul also met with members of Taiwan's parliament — the Legislative Yuan — and its speaker, President Han Kuo-yu, who presented McCaul with an array of Taiwanese fruits. In the meeting, legislative members discussed Taiwan's recent defense budget and the importance of drone production and coproduction with Taiwan.

McCaul with President Han and other members of the Yuan

Before departing Taiwan, McCaul participated in meetings with Taiwan's National Security Council and Ministry of National Defense to discuss strengthening Taiwan's defenses against the CCP's malign agenda in the region.

He also visited Shield AI, a U.S. drone company operating in Taiwan, and Taiwan's Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI). ITRI is the first organization outside the U.S. to certify that its drones contain no parts made in Communist China — a tremendous step toward freedom from CCP influence in their defense industry.

title: Reps. McGarvey, Jayapal Demand Trump Administration Reverse Rule to Fast-Track ICE Detention and Deportation Proceedings for Asylum Seekers
text:
Congressional Democrats say new DHS rule will push more asylum seekers into ICE detention and deportation as arrests at airports surge nationwide

WASHINGTON, D.C. (August 14, 2026) – Today, Representatives Morgan McGarvey (KY-03) and Pramila Jayapal (WA-07) led 69 Congressional Democrats in a letter to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) calling on the Trump administration to withdraw its new rule allowing asylum officers to reject an affirmative asylum seeker’s case without an interview and refer him or her directly to immigration court for deportation proceedings.

The rule comes as ICE ramps up arrests of individuals at airports, including those with legal status or pending applications.

Last month Sarafinah Bukirwa, one of McGarvey’s constituents with a valid visa and active asylum application, was detained by ICE at Louisville’s Muhammad Ali International Airport.

“USCIS’s failure to adjudicate such applications in a timely manner is now being weaponized by ICE, which, in collaboration with the Transportation Security Administration (TSA), is arresting individuals as they attempt to fly domestically,” the Members wrote.

McGarvey and Jayapal argued eliminating these interviews – a standard practice since 1990 – will deny those arrested under the new DHS rule from receiving full and fair consideration of their case, especially for asylum seekers who’ve faced persecution and violence and for survivors of gender-based violence.

The Members also rejected the administration’s claim that the rule would help address the asylum backlog, arguing it simply moves cases a USCIS officer could have decided into immigration courts, which already have 2.3 million pending asylum cases and keeps asylum seekers waiting in ICE detention even longer.

Instead, they called for increasing the number of asylum officers and resources for USCIS to process applications faster.

“Given the fact that Congress has given the administration $240 billion for immigration enforcement, moves like this call into question the Department’s ability to deploy those additional resources responsibly,” the Members continued.

Read the full letter here.

title: Congressman Griffith’s Weekly E-Newsletter 8.14.26
text:
The 118th Congress served as a launching pad for numerous actions taken in the 119th Congress.

House Republicans reintroduced commonsense policies that first secured House passage in the 118th Congress.

One bill, the Laken Riley Act which I repeatedly voted for, makes it easier for law enforcement to arrest criminal illegal aliens for certain crimes. This bill received swift consideration and passage in both the House and Senate.

A second bill is the HALT Fentanyl Act. I was the proud House sponsor of this legislation to permanently designate lethal fentanyl-related substances as Schedule I drugs. The bill also made researching Schedule I drugs easier so that we can work to better understand the impacts of these substances on human health.

Like the Laken Riley Act, this bill received swift consideration in both chambers of Congress.

Both of these bills not only won support in the 119th Congress, but from the President as well. President Trump signed these bills into law to help protect American communities.

Some of my actions in the 118th Congress have influenced further action at the federal level.

During that time, I served as the Chairman of the Oversight & Investigations Subcommittee for the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

Moreover, I was a leading Energy and Commerce member on the Select Subcommittee on the Coronavirus Pandemic.

During my leadership on these panels, I routinely participated in oversight of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), with particular interest in American public health agencies engaged in risky research and gain-of-function research projects.

Our investigative work demanded answers from public health officials like Dr. Anthony Fauci.

My findings led me to introduce the Risky Research Review Act. This bill outlines key reforms to make American-funded research more safe, more transparent and more accountable.

To continue momentum on this front, I reintroduced the bill in the 119th Congress with Senator Rand Paul. But the Trump Administration is actively responding to my concerns.

In July 2026, the Trump Administration announced a new government policy for stopping high-risk life sciences research.

The federal policy prohibits American funding of dangerous gain-of-function research in both domestic and foreign settings and aims to establish stronger oversight for life sciences research that could present significant risks to human health.

The Trump Administration further limits federal support for research in countries or institutions that lack appropriate biosafety, biosecurity and oversight standards.

While I will still push for my legislation to enshrine necessary guardrails into law for federally funded risky research, these federal actions are steps in the right direction.

A separate health care policy I investigated under my Chairmanship in the 118th Congress concerned the implementation and oversight of the organ donation and transplant system.

I led a hearing to spotlight issues with our organ transplant programs and discuss the failures of the groups responsible for the procurement of organs, Organ Procurement Organizations (OPOs).

In particular, I highlighted alarming allegations that were previously raised to my Subcommittee’s attention.

We received reports that an OPO had planned to operate on prospective organ donors who showed signs of life!

Another allegation claimed that somebody mouthed the words “help me” just before doctors were ready to commence an organ harvesting procedure.

The patient survived, but this disturbing detail reinforced Congressional desires to make the organ transplant process more safe and less risky.

These reports reflected concerns about Network for Hope, one federally designated OPO, and its management and operating procedures.

Upon hearing these troubling allegations, my Oversight Subcommittee brought in medical experts to understand the organ transplant health care landscape and determine the frequency at which these incidents happen.

Following my investigation on the issue, the Trump Administration has worked to protect prospective organ donors and patients awaiting lifesaving treatments.

In August 2026, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services made steps to decertify Network for Hope! This means the OPO can no longer do business with the federal government, and it loses a primary source of income.

This action is another critical federal step in working to ensure the safety and integrity of organ donation and securing U.S. health care programs to better protect patients.

I am proud to have been an early advocate on these issues to help sway federal action. I will continue to shine a light on issues that deserve attention from Congress, the President and the American people.

If you have questions, concerns, or comments, feel free to contact my office. You can call my Abingdon office at 276-525-1405 or my Christiansburg office at 540-381-5671. To reach my office via email, please visit my website at https://morgangriffith.house.gov/. Also on my website is the latest material from my office, including information on votes recently taken on the floor of the House of Representatives.

title: WATCH: Pressley, McGovern, Lynch Conduct Unannounced Oversight Visit of Plymouth ICE Facility, Renew Calls for Accountability
text:
Pressley Has Conducted Oversight of ICE Facilities in MA and Acrossthe Country, Advocated for Children Detained by ICE, Named Impacted Families as Honorary State of the Union Guests

Pressley Has Stood in Vigorous Defense of Immigrant Communities, Fought to Bring Detained Neighbors Home, and Led Efforts to Address Childhood Trauma

Media Availability (YouTube) | Photos (Dropbox)

PLYMOUTH, MA – Today, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), alongside Congressmen James P. McGovern (MA-02) and Stephen F. Lynch (MA-08), conducted an unannounced Congressional oversight visit of the Plymouth County Correctional Facility—the only facility in Massachusetts currently holding civil immigration detainees on a long-term basis. Federal law gives members of Congress the authority to conduct unannounced oversight visits of ICE detention facilities without providing advance notice.

Following their visit, the lawmakers held a media availability calling for the release of individuals unlawfully imprisoned there and accountability for the harm and trauma caused by Trump and ICE’s campaign of terror. Congresswoman Pressley also called for the release of her constituent Darwin, whose fiancée joined the lawmakers following the visit, and who has suffered from traumatic physical injuries and treatment in prior ICE custody and reported lack of access to health assistive devices, potable water, and nourishing food at the Plymouth facility.

“Under this cruel, lawless Trump administration, families are being separated, children are traumatized, and our communities are suffering,” said Congresswoman Pressley. “I came to Plymouth to conduct an oversight visit of a major detention facility in our state, check on my constituents, and demand accountability of ICE as they deny the humanity and rights of our community members. Learning of the trauma experienced by innocent individuals like my constituent Darwin and his fiancé are a damning reminder of the injustice of these detentions and the need to abolish ICE, end qualified immunity for ICE agents, and stop Trump and ICE’s campaign of terror. Today, I am more resolute than ever in my fight for the freedom, dignity, and humanity of our immigrant neighbors.”

“In 2018, I became the first Member of Congress to demand that we abolish ICE,” said Congressman McGovern. “After hearing heartbreaking stories today at the Plymouth detention facility from folks who were abducted by ICE on their way to work and ripped away from their families, my resolve to abolish ICE has never been stronger. Under orders from the Trump administration, masked federal agents are terrorizing our communities, stalking our streets, and executing American citizens in broad daylight with impunity. Any American with a conscience must join us in calling for this rogue agency to be abolished, for ICE agents to be held accountable, and for the human rights and dignity of immigrants to be respected without condition.”

“While President Trump claims that ICE operations are targeting the “worst of the worst,” the individuals in ICE custody that we met with today included a police officer and construction workers who were on the job with valid work permits and active Social Security numbers. In fact, many of the individuals in ICE detention at the Plymouth Correctional Facility have open immigration cases and prior to their arbitrary arrests, were seeking to comply with the formal processes governing applications for immigrant visas, asylum, and humanitarian parole. Absent substantive reforms including body camera requirements, a prohibition on agents wearing masks, the termination of arbitrary enforcement operations, and the adoption of humane use of force standards, ICE will continue to operate outside the law and we must keep fighting to oppose agency funding,” said Rep. Lynch. “We must also keep exercising our legal right, as Members of Congress, to conduct unannounced oversight inspections of ICE detention facilities to better ensure that individuals in custody are treated humanely and that ICE is transparent and accountable to the American people.”

In Congress, Congresswoman Pressley has been a leading voice in pushing back against Trump, defending our immigrant neighbors, and calling for ICE to be abolished. Rep. Pressley has visited individuals behind the wall at detention facilities in Texas, Louisiana, and Massachusetts and leads legislation to bring accountability to families whose loved ones have been murdered and harmed by ICE agents, including the DHS Use of Force Transparency Act and the Qualified Immunity Abolition Act.

A transcript of Congresswoman Pressley’s remarks is available below and the video from the media availability is available here. Photos from the visit are available here.

Transcript: Rep. Pressley’s Remarks Following Unannounced Oversight Visit of Plymouth ICE Facility

U.S. House of Representatives

August 14, 2026

Well, and let me just, you know—I know technically they are characterized as detainees—but just to center their humanity, today we met with Jose, we met with Alexis, we met with Darwin.

These are sons. These are fathers. These are husbands. Men who are loved by their families, whose labor is valued and essential to the functioning of our communities and our economies. They are sorely missed by their families, and they desperately miss their families.

Jose, for example, 30 years old, has a four-year-old and a two-year-old. He’s never met his two-year-old daughter Ariella—Ariela, rather. And as Jim mentioned, he was a police officer in Ecuador, and in his time spent here, he has worked in construction.

We met with, with Darwin and Alexis, and both talked about how they miss working, and they’re, they’re eager to get back to work. They find dignity in their work, they take pride in their work. They take pride in the role that they play, many of them as the sole breadwinners in their families, not only their families here, but money that they are sending back to countries like Ecuador, Honduras.

I asked about where are most of the detainees from, and the countries were Guatemala, El Salvador, Ecuador, and Honduras, with some rare exceptions.

But what is very clear is that this is a waste of money and a waste of time. And for what? We have separated families. We are causing trauma, and we have people that are providing valuable contributions to community, of which we are all being denied.

So it is a tremendous injustice to these families and a great disservice to our communities writ-large.

One of the, one of the men that we met with, Darwin. This is his fiancé Angelina, and I’m going to turn things over to her in a moment. But I want to say two things.

I’ve said repeatedly that our strategy as a Democratic caucus is litigation, legislation, agitation, when necessary, and mobilization.

The reason we could do this unannounced visit today is because of litigation initiated by our task force, and because that, the court sided with Joe Neguse, Congressman Neguse, and the rest of us who signed on to that—that is why we could do this today.

So, although the work of litigation can move more slowly than we would like, that is why we could do this unannounced visit today.

Secondly, I reinforced for Jose, Alexis, and Darwin that there are people who’ve never met them, who care about them, and are fighting for their freedom. And they all expressed the relief that they felt in knowing that, that they had not been forgotten.

And so, in that aim, I also want to acknowledge that since two of the gentlemen here who were arrested and detained were picked up in Vermont, and so we made sure they knew that Senator Welch and Senator Sanders, that we were here, you know, in their stead, and again that there are people working vigorously on their behalf.

And so I now turn it over to Angelina to tell more of Darwin’s story.

title: Quigley, Durbin, Duckworth, Davis Announce More than $696 Million for Amtrak Upgrades in Chicago
text:
U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), and U.S. Representatives Mike Quigley (D-IL-05) and Danny Davis (D-IL-07) today announced that the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) has awarded $696,250,000 in federal funding to Amtrak projects based in Chicago. One of the three projects receiving funding—the South Bridge Rehabilitation—is part of the Chicago Hub Improvement project (CHIP), a multi-phased project to revitalize Chicago Union Station and its surrounding infrastructure, as well as revolutionize Midwest passenger rail.

The funding was awarded through the Federal-State Partnership for Intercity Passenger Rail (Fed-State) grant program, which supports capital projects that repair, improve, or expand intercity passenger rail service.

“Our state’s top-notch rail system keeps our economy moving while allowing Illinoisans to travel from Chicago to Carbondale. This latest federal investment into Chicago’s Amtrak facilities and infrastructure reflects the city’s status as a thriving transportation hub,” Durbin said. “I look forward to seeing this funding turn into concrete improvements to our rail infrastructure, and in turn, delivering an even better experience to Amtrak riders.”

“Investments in our rail infrastructure are investments in our economy, making sure our rail network is safer, faster and more efficient for people and goods to get where they need to go,” said Duckworth. “This funding will help support critical upgrades to our rail infrastructure and strengthen our city’s role as a national hub for Amtrak. I will continue working alongside Senator Durbin, Congressman Quigley, Amtrak leadership and our local leaders to ensure our communities have the support they need to modernize our rail network, improve reliability and keep trains moving safely and efficiently for generations to come.”

“Safe, affordable, and accessible rail travel is critical to the success of Chicago and the Illinois region. This grant will make improvements and repairs that will modernize passenger rail service in our area for the millions of people who utilize these services. I have talked about the dangers of disrepair in our rail system for many years, and I have particularly called out the damaged bridges in the region that are long past the need for repair. I am pleased that this grant will help address these issues and improve access to safe and efficient rail services for Chicagoland residents for many years to come. I will continue working with my colleagues in the House and Senate to bring home more funding to achieve these goals,” said Quigley.

“The 7th District has long felt the impact of aging infrastructure, and our residents deserve a rail system that is safe, reliable, and built to last. This funding is not just an investment in steel and concrete — it is an investment in the working families who depend on Amtrak to get to their jobs, their schools, and their loved ones every day. I am proud to have fought alongside my colleagues to secure these resources, and I will keep pushing to ensure Chicago's West Side and communities across our region benefit from the good-paying jobs and safer travel this project will bring,” said Davis.

The three Amtrak projects receiving a portion of the announced $696,250,000 are:

Midwest Maintenance Facilities Modernization P3 ($572,000,000). The proposed project was selected for Right of Way Acquisition and includes activities to improve efficiency and safety at Amtrak’s Chicago-area Midwest Maintenance Facilities by relocating certain maintenance facilities from Amtrak’s 14th St. Yard to the to-be-acquired Canal St. Yard to support ongoing operations. The project will improve service and system performance because it will provide a modern, efficient maintenance and inspection facility and increase the ability to meet anticipated demand. The project will benefit Blue Water, Borealis, Hiawatha, Illini/Saluki, Illinois Zephyr, Lincoln, Pere Marquette, Wolverine routes.

Chicago Rail Bridge Renewal P3 ($87,000,000). The proposed project was selected for Project Development, Final Design, and Construction to rehabilitate or replace approximately 17 aging viaducts, bridges, and ancillary structures at Chicago’s Canal Street Yard as part of Amtrak’s Chicago Rail Bridge Renewal P3 Project. The project will enhance safety and improve system and service performance because it will correct critical structural deficiencies and eliminate hazards for rail operations, drivers, and pedestrians. The project will benefit Blue Water, Borealis, Hiawatha, Illini/Saluki, Illinois Zephyr, Lincoln, Pere Marquette, Wolverine routes.

South Branch Bridge Rehabilitation ($37,250,000). The proposed project will rehabilitate the existing South Branch Bridge and Project Development activities for a future bridge replacement. Activities will support the immediate state of good repair including the replacement of missing fasteners, defective hardware, and replacement parts to balance, support machinery and plan for a future replacement. The project will enhance safety and increase reliability by bringing the over-110-year-old South Branch Bridge into a state of good repair. The project will benefit Amtrak’s Blue Water, Lincoln, Pere Marquette, River Runner, and Wolverine routes.

In 2023, Durbin and Duckworth announced $93.6 million in secured federal funding for CHIP through the U.S. Department of Transportation’s (DOT) Federal-State Partnerships for Intercity Passenger Rail grant program, which received funding through the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act.

Durbin worked to bring parties together—local officials, the State, Amtrak, and other stakeholders including labor, environmental groups, and businesses—to ensure there was a unified push for the project. In September 2023, Durbin, Duckworth, and Quigley (D-IL-05) led 29 Midwest colleagues in a bipartisan, bicameral letter to Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg and Federal Railroad Administration Administrator Amit Bose expressing their support for Amtrak’s Fed-State grant application for CHIP.

In May 2025, Durbin raised the issue of CHIP funding with Transportation Secretary Duffy, urging the DOT to obligate the remaining funds for the $93.6 million grant awarded in 2023. The Members also sent a letter of support to Secretary Duffy for this round of Fed-State grant applications.

Durbin, Duckworth, Quigley, and Davis will continue to build upon previous investments in the CHIP and lead stakeholders in advocating to advance the improvement of Chicago Union Station, cementing its critical importance to both Illinois and the Midwest.

title: Rep. Salinas Introduces Bill to Tax Data Centers, Reinvest in Housing, Conservation, and Infrastructure
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representative Andrea Salinas (OR-06) introduced the Data Center Community Reinvestment Act, a bill that would tax the electricity data centers use and send that money to programs that build affordable housing, protect public lands and waterways, clean up hazardous waste sites, fund clean energy projects, and repair roads and bridges.

“As AI use expands and the demand for data centers grows, we need to ensure our communities aren’t left footing the bill,” said Rep. Salinas. “This bill taxes the energy used by data centers and reinvests that money in the programs our communities rely on, from affordable housing to conservation to cleaning up hazardous waste sites. Every community deserves to drive a hard bargain with data center developers, and at the end of the day, every community deserves to share in the benefits from data center growth.”

As data center demand grows, so will the strain on local infrastructure. Rep. Salinas’ bill would place a 1-cent-per-kilowatt-hour excise tax on electricity used by any data center with more than 1 megawatt of power capacity, whether that power comes from the grid or is generated on-site. Based on current data center electricity use nationwide, the tax is projected to raise about $1.76 billion a year.

The bill would split that revenue equally five ways among the following federal programs and funds:

The Land and Water Conservation Fund, which protects public lands and waterways. It would receive about $352 million more a year, an increase of nearly 40 percent.

The Housing Trust Fund, which builds and preserves affordable housing for the lowest-income households. It would receive about $352 million more a year, more than doubling its current funding.

The Hazardous Substance Superfund, which pays for the cleanup of hazardous waste sites when no responsible party can be identified.

The Highway Trust Fund, which funds road, bridge, and transit projects nationwide.

The Energy Technology Trust Fund, which would fund federal loan guarantees for clean energy, advanced nuclear, and grid infrastructure projects. Last year, Republicans rescinded funding for this loan guarantee program. Rep. Salinas' bill would restore a dedicated funding source for it.

title: SCHNEIDER, DURBIN, DUCKWORTH, ANNOUNCE MORE THAN $7.95 MILLION IN FEDERAL FUNDING FOR ILLINOIS AIRPORTS
text:
The Chicago Executive Airport and the Decatur Airport will receive a combined total of $7.95 million in federal funding for runway improvements, sound mitigation

SPRINGFIELD – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), and U.S. Representative Brad Schneider (D-IL-10) today announced a total of $7,951,873 in federal funding for the Chicago Executive Airport and the Decatur Airport. This funding stems from the Federal Aviation Administration’s (FAA) Airport Improvement Program, which supports the planning and development of public-use airports.

“Investing in our airports is laying the foundation for increased connectivity and reliability. With this grant announcement for Decatur Airport, Illinoisans will see upgraded airport infrastructure, making travel safe and more efficient. Additionally, this funding will ensure that Illinoisans who live near the Chicago Executive Airport can mitigate the sounds of flyovers while still having access to a quality airport,” Durbin said.

“Illinois airports are critical economic engines for our state,” Duckworth said. “This major investment will help modernize infrastructure, install new runway safety measures and support noise mitigation for surrounding neighborhoods. Together, we will continue working to make air travel safer and more reliable for all passengers while ensuring that our airports are receiving the much-needed federal resources they deserve.”

“I’m glad to work alongside my colleagues and local leaders in Illinois to announce more than $3.8 million in federal funding to support noise mitigation around Chicago Executive Airport,” said Schneider. “This project will support the health and well-being of nearby residents while ensuring the airport can continue to serve Cook County. In Congress, we will continue working to deliver funding that supports local priorities and projects.”

Specifically, this grant funding will go toward:

Decatur Park District ($4,081,873). This funding will go the construction phase of the Decatur Park District’s project to reconstruct existing runway signage at the airport; acquire and install three new wind cone navigational aids to provide pilots with critical airfield information; and reconstruct existing runway lighting.

Chicago Executive Airport ($3,870,000). This funding will go toward the state’s project to install sound installation mitigation measures for 2,202 residences impacted by airport noise exposure. This funding allotment will support the project’s current phase, which consists of program planning, design services, and sound insulation for 110 residences.

title: SCHNEIDER, TENNEY LEAD 36 LAWMAKERS URGING SECRETARY MULLIN TO DROP ONEROUS GRANT FUNDING RULES THAT LEAVE SYNAGOGUES, CHURCHES, AND MOSQUES LESS SAFE
text:
LINCOLNSHIRE, IL – Today, Congressman Brad Schneider (IL-10) and Congresswoman Claudia Tenney (NY-24) led a bipartisan group of members calling for Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin to remove onerous guidelines that deter applicants from accepting Nonprofit Security Grant Program funding, leaving synagogues, churches, mosques less safe.

The Nonprofit Security Grant Program is a FEMA grant program that provides funding for physical security enhancements and activities to nonprofit organizations that are at high risk of terrorist attack. It is designed to integrate and promote coordination and collaboration in emergency preparedness activities among public and private community representatives, as well as state and local government agencies.

“American religious groups, and especially Jewish communities, have seen record increases in violent incidents and hate-filled threats,” said Schneider. “I'm grateful to partner with Rep. Tenney to push back against onerous new rules that make our synagogues, churches, and mosques less safe. We will continue to root out hate and discrimination in all forms, so everyone can observe their faith safely and without threat of harm.”

“The Nonprofit Security Grant Program is an essential resource that helps faith-based organizations and nonprofit institutions protect the people they serve,” said Tenney. “As threats against houses of worship and community organizations continue to rise, it is important that these institutions have confidence that the program will provide the support they were awarded. Our letter encourages DHS to provide that certainty by ensuring the program remains focused on its core mission of enhancing security for vulnerable communities.”

“As antisemitism and threats against faith communities remain at historic levels, NSGP is more essential than ever to help at-risk communities protect themselves from threats,” said Lauren Wolman, ADL’s senior director of government relations and strategy. “We are grateful to Representatives Schneider and Tenney for their bipartisan leadership in championing this lifesaving program and ensuring organizations can access those resources quickly, with confidence, and without unnecessary delays.”

Rep. Schneider led two letters calling for updated guidance for the Nonprofit Security Grant Program – one in January, as Co-Chair of the Congressional Jewish Caucus, and one in February as part of a larger bipartisan call for action. In response, the Department of Homeland Security stated they were “actively developing clarifying guidance.” Such guidance has still not been put forward.

During Secretary Mullin’s confirmation hearing, Mullin said he would work to “streamline the process” for grants, including the Nonprofit Security Grant Program.

View the full letter here and below.

Dear Secretary Mullin,

Thank you for your continued support for the Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP), which provides critical grants for the protection of at-risk faith-based and nonprofit organizations, including Jewish institutions and many others, facing a troubling rise in targeted violence and antisemitism. In recent years, attacks in San Diego, West Bloomfield, Jackson, Boulder, Washington, D.C. and other communities have shown that no faith tradition or religious institution is immune to violence or hate-motivated threats. According to the Anti-Defamation League, 2025 was one of the most violent years for American Jews, with 203 assaults, including 32 incidents involving a deadly weapon, the highest number ADL has ever recorded. Additionally, ADL recorded 1,129 antisemitic incidents at Jewish institutions in 2025. While incidents on college campuses decreased, they remained nearly three times higher than before October 7th.

As representatives of communities that include vibrant religious institutions, we appreciate how important these grants are to ensuring that synagogues, churches, mosques, schools and other high-risk nonprofits, and the people they serve, are safe and secure.

On February 5, 2026, we wrote to then-DHS Secretary Noem to express our concern that the Standard Terms and Conditions promulgated by DHS on April 18, 2025, created new compliance requirements for NSGP recipients that were unrelated to the security of grant recipients and their communities. As we stated in our previous letter, these Standard Terms and Conditions would divert limited funds and burden the institutions the NSGP is meant to protect. At that time, we urged DHS to issue clarifying guidance and, where appropriate, waive any terms and conditions unrelated to the grant’s core security purpose.

In DHS’ response to us on February 27, 2026, then-DHS Secretary Noem stated that DHS and FEMA were “actively developing clarifying guidance tailored for the NSGP, including examples relevant to houses of worship and other faith-based nonprofits.” Unfortunately, such guidance has not yet been put forth.

We are writing again today because the FY 2026 Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO), as issued by FEMA on June 24, 2026, maintains these concerning new compliance requirements. Ascurrently structured, the FY 2026 NOFO carries forward the compliance requirements we previously identified and adds a new ground for termination not present in the FY 2025 terms: the authority to end an award “for convenience,” upon a FEMA determination the award no longer advances the “national interest.” This vague and expansive standard gives applicants little guidance about what is expected of them and raises concerns about mid-project terminations without warning. As NSGP requires organizations to front the costs of their security projects, the possibility of mid-award termination and, therefore, no reimbursement, may deter applicants from accepting the grant, leaving their institution vulnerable to attack.

We have always believed that NSGP should be as streamlined and effective as possible, with minimal red tape and compliance requirements focused squarely on security. You rightly expressed this same belief during your confirmation hearing. That is why we urge you to revise the FY 2026 NOFO and issue new guidance that removes or waives terms and conditions unrelated to the security of grant recipients, eliminates the new overly broad termination authority and ensures that the NSGP remains accessible to all eligible faith-based and community organizations.

In this time of rising antisemitic attacks and violence against diverse faith-based institutions, we believe it is crucial that NSGP remains a critical resource for all who seek to worship in safety and free from requirements unrelated to security.

title: Report: Stanton Earns “A” for Bipartisanship in Congress, Highest-Ranked Arizona House Democrat
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Representative Greg Stanton (AZ-04) was ranked the most bipartisan Democrat in Arizona’s U.S. House delegation, earning an “A” grade and a 95 out of 100 Bridge Score in the latest Bridge Grades report. The nonpartisan organization evaluates how collaboratively or divisively members of Congress govern compared with their peers.

“Proud to earn an A from Bridge Grades for being one of the most effective, bipartisan legislators in Congress. When it comes to lowering costs and supporting working families, I'll work with anyone — Democrat or Republican. That's the job, and Arizonans expect nothing less,” said Rep. Stanton on X.

Stanton’s 95.0 Bridge Score is one of the highest among House Democrats in the 119th Congress, earning him an “A” for bipartisanship. The House average is 44.9, and of the 435 members evaluated by Bridge Grades, just 76 received an A—36 Democrats and 40 Republicans.

Bridge Grades describes itself as a nonpartisan “polarization report card” and compiles third-party public data on lawmakers’ legislative records and public rhetoric, including whether members introduce and co-sponsor bipartisan legislation, discuss bipartisanship and avoid personal attacks. Scores are measured relative to other members of the same chamber.

title: Ranking Members Subramanyam and Garcia Demand Answers About Conditions on USS Lincoln
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Representatives Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10), Ranking Member of the Military and Foreign Affairs Oversight Subcommittee, and Robert Garcia (CA-42), Ranking Member of the House Oversight Committee, are demanding answers from the Department of Defense (DOD) about conditions on the USS Lincoln.

“Secretary Hegseth has claimed the rumors of overboard attempts and food rationing are overblown. If conditions are what he says they are and he has nothing to hide, then we will see if the information matches his claims. Our servicemembers are being asked to be away from family for months on end with inadequate conditions. That is unacceptable,” said Ranking Member Subramanyam.

"Sailors on the USS Abraham Lincoln are going without food, dealing with contaminated water, and attempting suicide after hundreds of days at sea due to President Trump’s incompetent and disastrous war with Iran. Secretary Hegseth must answer for and improve these unacceptable conditions immediately," said Ranking Member Robert Garcia.

There have been reports for months about food rationing and insufficient food on the USS Lincoln. There have also been more recent reports of several servicemembers attempting to jump off the ship. The USS Lincoln has been deployed for more than 250 days, setting modern records for deployments without port calls.

In a letter to DOD Secretary Hegseth, the Ranking Members asked for information on the inventory of food, medical supplies, and other critical resources for the sailors and Marines. They also asked for clarification on the timeline of when the USS Lincoln would be relieved by another aircraft carrier.

The letter can be found HERE and below.

###

Dear Secretary Hegseth:

We write regarding the conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, specifically, the living conditions and access to mental health resources for the sailors. Recent reports have revealed disturbing sanitation conditions, food shortages, and deteriorating mental health among those deployed on the aircraft carrier, including multiple suicide attempts, with one sailor jumping overboard. Our sailors deserve better while they serve our country, and these deplorable conditions negatively impact morale and readiness. As Members of Congress, we have a duty to support our troops, and it is clear that additional oversight is needed aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln.

The USS Abraham Lincoln holds more than 5,000 sailors and Marines and departed San Diego last November. Now redirected to the Middle East to support the Iran War in Operation Epic Fury, the carrier has been deployed for over 250 days and has spent a record-setting 200 consecutive days at sea. At a town hall with Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, families of those aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln voiced their concerns directly. Among them were food shortages, water contamination, and disruptions in mail.

As the Ranking Members of the Oversight Committee and the Oversight Committee’s Subcommittee on Military and Foreign Affairs, we request a classified briefing on the USS Abraham Lincoln’s conditions and answers to the following questions by August 28, 2026:

What is the current inventory of food aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln?

Please detail the food supply and delivery schedule over the course of the carrier’s deployment.

What sanitation issues have been identified aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, including broken bathroom facilities?

What health care, including mental health care, are available to the sailors aboard?

What behavioral health care professionals are on board and accessible to those seeking help?

How quickly can someone on board the ship meet with a behavioral health care professional after seeking help?

What steps can be taken to mitigate the disruptions to the mail system that sailors have experienced?

Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao reportedly told family members that the USS Theodore Roosevelt is preparing to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln. Without jeopardizing national security, what details can be shared about the timeline for the ship’s relief?

The Committee on Oversight and Government Reform is the principal oversight committee of the House of Representatives and has broad authority to investigate “any matter” at “any time” under House Rule X. If you have any questions about this request, please contact Committee Democratic staff at (202) 225-5051. Thank you for your prompt attention to this request.

title: Texas Democrats Demand Gov. Abbott Act on Extradition of ICE Agent Charged in Minneapolis Shooting
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C — Today, Congresswoman Sylvia Garcia (D-TX-29) and Congressman Vicente Gonzalez (D-TX-34) led Texas Democrats in demanding that Texas Governor Greg Abbott authorize the extradition of Christian J. Castro, an ICE agent charged in connection with a January shooting during an immigration enforcement operation in Minneapolis. Castro is accused of firing into a home, shooting Venezuelan immigrant Julio C. Sosa-Celis in the leg, and later lying about the circumstances surrounding the shooting.

Castro, 52, was arrested in South Texas on May 29, 2026, after a warrant was issued in Hennepin County. He remains in custody in Cameron County, Texas. Castro is charged with four counts of second-degree assault and one count of falsely reporting a crime.

“The Texas Rangers and the prosecuting authority in Cameron County have done their jobs and collaborated with the necessary Minnesota authorities,” the lawmakers said in a letter to Abbott.

“The last step to begin the long-awaited court proceedings for the victims is for you to sign the paperwork. Mr. Castro has already been in custody for two months, and the paperwork, according to Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty, is in order. There is no reason to delay,” the lawmakers wrote.

“When an ICE agent is charged with shooting into a home and lying about what happened, the answer cannot be delay or special treatment. We have watched this administration’s out-of-control immigration enforcement turn deadly, while official accounts unravel as the facts come out,” said Congresswoman Garcia. “We saw it in Minneapolis and Maine, and we are seeing it here in Houston as we demand the truth about ICE’s killing of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo. Governor Abbott should sign the extradition paperwork and let the justice system do its job.”

“Texans are firm believers in law and order, which is why accountability must be delivered in the case of Christian J. Castro. Governor Abbott has an immediate responsibility to uphold the extradition process and not interfere with our nation’s justice system. We cannot normalize criminal actions, including those committed by rogue ICE agents under this Administration’s hyperaggressive immigration policies,” said Congressman Gonzalez.

The charges stem from a Jan. 14, 2026, immigration enforcement operation in north Minneapolis. Prosecutors allege Castro and other ICE agents pursued Alfredo Alejandro Aljorna to the home he shared with Sosa-Celis. After both men made it inside, Castro allegedly fired through the closed front door, striking Sosa-Celis in the leg. The bullet traveled through the home and lodged in the wall of a child’s bedroom.

title: U.S. Rep. Dina Titus, RTC and Boulder City officials highlight Nevada Way improvements
text:
Congresswoman Dina Titus, Regional Transportation Commission of Southern Nevada (RTC) and Boulder City officials held a news conference today to provide details about the upcoming Phase II Nevada Way Reconstruction Project to upgrade this key roadway in Boulder City, including safety improvements for vulnerable roadway users.

The project is being made possible by an $850,000 federal grant secured by Congresswoman Titus.

“Nevada Way is a main thoroughfare through Boulder City, providing a gateway to Lake Mead National Recreation Area and other tourist destinations around Boulder City,” Congresswoman Titus said. “This project will contribute to Boulder City’s economic vitality while providing additional pedestrian safety measures for its residents.”

“RTC is proud to partner with Boulder City and Congresswoman Titus to advance improvements that make Nevada Way safer and more welcoming for residents, businesses, and the customers they serve,” said Andrew Kjellman, RTC Deputy CEO. “We are grateful for Congresswoman Titus’ leadership and commitment to bringing resources back to Southern Nevada.”

The project will rehabilitate Nevada Way from Colorado Street to Park Street through the historic downtown area of Boulder City and reconstruct Colorado Street from Nevada Way to Utah Street, and Park Street from Nevada Way to Utah Street. The project will repave, restripe, and replace deteriorating asphalt on the roadway. The improvements include raised crosswalks with pedestrian-activated flashing beacons. The project also includes upgrades to ADA and pedestrian access, especially where sidewalks and ramps are currently limited.

The news conference was held at The Coffee Cup Café on Nevada Way and featured speakers were Andrew Kjellman, Deputy CEO, RTC, Boulder City Mayor Joe Hardy, Gary Poindexter, Public Works Director, Boulder City, and Congresswoman Titus.

title: Trahan Celebrates $140 Million in Federal Funding for Haverhill Line Improvements
text:
Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03) joined Governor Maura Healey in announcing a $139.6 million investment from the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) to the Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority (MBTA) to make major improvements to the Haverhill Commuter Rail line, helping deliver faster, safer and more reliable service for thousands of riders every day.

The funding will support the final design and construction of the Haverhill Double-Track Project, a major upgrade project that will add approximately 6.8 miles of new track between Reading and Andover to allow trains traveling in opposite directions to keep moving instead of waiting for one another. The project will also upgrade four stations in Reading, North Wilmington, Ballardvale and Andover with high-level platforms, to make those stations more accessible, and will modernize signals to improve safety at 15 rail crossings.

The federal funding will be matched by $34.9 million from the MBTA, bringing the total investment in the Haverhill Line project to $174.5 million.

“This is a significant federal investment in the future of commuter rail across the Merrimack Valley. This funding will deliver faster, more reliable service for riders in Haverhill, Lawrence, and communities throughout the region, along with safer crossings and modernized stations that are fully accessible to seniors and riders with disabilities,” said Congresswoman Lori Trahan. “I've been proud to fight alongside Governor Healey for federal funding like this because Massachusetts families deserve a transit system they can count on.”

“Since taking office, we’ve made historic investments to turn the T around, and riders are seeing the difference with fewer slow zones and more reliable service,” said Governor Maura Healey. “Now we’re keeping that momentum going. This $140 million award will help us make major improvements to the Haverhill Line that mean fewer delays, safer and more accessible stations, and better service for riders. We’re grateful to our federal delegation for helping us bring this funding home to Massachusetts.”

“This $140 million investment is not only going to make major safety, reliability, and accessibility impact along the Haverhill Commuter Rail Line, but it will also directly support Amtrak Downeaster operations and freight rail,” said Interim Secretary and MBTA General Manager Phillip Eng. “New double track gives us more operational flexibility and the ability to decrease commute time along the line. Upgrading four stations with high-level platforms is another step closer to a fully accessible MBTA system, and modernizing our signals will help to move trains more safely and reliably through the intercity area. Improving freight allows for more efficient movement of goods and helps to control costs for the public. I’m grateful for the leadership of Governor Healey to make these continued improvements possible and for our Congressional Delegation, MassDOT, and the MBTA for advocating for this funding with the foresight that it will have benefits for decades to come. I also want to thank the Federal Railroad Administration for their partnership and ability to move this project forward and through construction.”

What This Means for Riders

Today, parts of the Haverhill Line have only one track, which means a train sometimes has to wait for another train traveling in the opposite direction to pass. If there is a problem with a train or the track, that single-track section can also cause delays to ripple across the line.

This project will add nearly seven miles of second track between Reading and Andover, allowing trains to move in both directions at the same time and giving the MBTA more options to keep service moving when problems arise. It will also make it easier for crews to perform maintenance without disrupting service or requiring shuttle buses.

Approximately 10 miles of new fencing will also be installed along the corridor between Andover and Reading to help prevent unauthorized access to the tracks.

The project will also make Reading, North Wilmington, Ballardvale and Andover stations more accessible by adding high-level platforms that allow riders to step directly between the platform and train. The MBTA will improve signals at 15 rail crossings, eliminate the Tewksbury Street crossing in Andover and install approximately 10 miles of new fencing to improve safety along the tracks.

The improvements will benefit not only MBTA Commuter Rail riders but also Amtrak’s Downeaster service, which operates between Boston and Brunswick, Maine, and CSX freight service. By removing delays and increasing capacity, the project will strengthen passenger and freight rail connections throughout the region and support future improvements to rail service.

This funding is the latest championed by Congresswoman Trahan to support transportation-related projects throughout the district. Just this year, Trahan secured $1.2 million in federal funding for bridge improvements in Lawrence. Last year, she celebrated alongside Governor Maura Healey $251 million in federal funding secured through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law for the Rourke Bridge Replacement Project in Lowell. Trahan also secured $7,158,564 for the Lowell Regional Transit Authority and $7,194,360 for the Merrimack Valley Regional Transit Authority to purchase new buses and improve service, helping better connect communities across the district.

title: Vindman Announces Thousands of Dollars in Funding to Support Law Enforcement and Strengthen Public Safety
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) today celebrated the U.S. Department of Justice’s (DOJ) award of thousands of dollars in federal funding to communities across Virginia’s Seventh Congressional District to strengthen local law enforcement operations and improve public safety.

“As a former prosecutor, I care deeply about ensuring our communities remain safe. That’s why I work with local law enforcement to ensure they get the tools and resources they need to do their jobs effectively,” said Vindman. “I’m proud to see Virginia’s Seventh Congressional District receive this federal funding to strengthen public safety. I’ll keep fighting to bring federal resources back home, supporting the dedicated public servants who work every day to respond to emergencies and keep families safe.”

All three grants were awarded through the Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (JAG) Program. Administered by the DOJ’s Bureau of Justice Assistance (BJA), the program provides non-competitive formula grants to support personnel, equipment, training, and technology across the criminal justice system.

Spotsylvania County was awarded $29,500 in funding that will enable the Spotsylvania County Commonwealth’s Attorney’s Office to purchase up to nine portable, high-performance forensic laptops for the secure and efficient review of large volumes of digital evidence, including social media content, body-worn camera footage, cellphone extractions, and data from other electronic devices.

These specialized laptops are designed to support forensic software and applications, allowing prosecutors to review evidence more effectively and prepare cases more efficiently. The laptops will be assigned to prosecutors to enhance case preparation and litigation.

The City of Fredericksburg was awarded $16,552 in funding, which will allow the city to replace an all-terrain vehicle (ATV) used to patrol the City’s watershed, which spans thousands of acres.

The ATV enables officers to efficiently patrol rugged, hard-to-reach areas, including hills, muddy trails, and undeveloped land that are inaccessible to standard patrol vehicles. Replacing the ATV will help improve patrol coverage and support faster response times in remote areas.

Stafford County was awarded $37,657 in funding to enhance public safety, emergency response, and officer safety by purchasing critical equipment for its ATV Team, Traffic Safety and Volunteer Unit, and SWAT Team. It will also support the acquisition of a new all-terrain vehicle to improve search and rescue operations and response in difficult terrain, portable jump starter packs to reduce response times for disabled motorists, and advanced night vision equipment to strengthen tactical operations during low-light incidents.

title: Ranking Member Maxine Waters Applauds Federal Court for Blocking Trump’s Cruel Attack on Los Angeles Homelessness Funding

title: Baldwin, Blumenthal Lead Colleagues in Demanding Trump Admin Rescind Cancelation of Lifesaving Research Grants That Improve Patient Safety & Care
Baldwin, Colleagues Introduce Bill to Stop Trump from Hiding Troop Deaths and Injuries from Iran War
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – As the Trump Administration attempts to hide the true cost of the Iran war from the American people, U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) and her colleagues introduced the Honoring the Sacrifices of Our Troops in War Act to stop President Donald Trump’s attempt to dishonor the sacrifice of our troops injured and killed in combat. This comes after the Pentagon recategorized recent casualties suffered in Trump’s Iran war – including four killed and over 200 wounded servicemembers – under a separate category outside of Operation Epic Fury to downplay the damage done and evade accountability to the American people.

“Donald Trump launched an unpopular war of choice wholly unprepared, and now he is doing everything he can to lie and deceive the American people about its consequences. This war has sent costs skyrocketing, taken the lives of 18 American service members, and wounded hundreds more”, said Senator Tammy Baldwin. “Now, rather than take responsibility and bring this war to an end, the Trump Administration is pulling the wool over the American people’s eyes. This is an insult to the servicemembers wounded and those who perished – and all of their families who have sacrificed alongside them. I’m pushing to make sure our servicemembers and their families get the respect and dignity they earned and to hold this reckless president accountable for this haphazard and spiraling war in Iran.”

To ban the Secretary of Defense from hiding the true cost of war, the Honoring the Sacrifices of Our Troops in War Act specifically:

Bans Arbitrary, Unjustified Recategorizing of Designated Contingency Operations by prohibiting redesignating an ongoing conflict if the Administration continues to mobilize forces against the same enemy;

Prevents Manipulation of Casualty Records by prohibiting manipulation of casualty records by falsely redesignating a contingency operation;

Restores Casualty Records of Our Fallen and Wounded Heroes in the Iran War by requiring restoration of casualty records for Iran-related operations since February 28, 2026, and notify next-of-kin about the correction;

Bans Cutting Hard-Earned Benefits for Troops and Civilian Personnel by prohibiting the modification of eligibility for deployment-related personnel benefits on the basis of falsely redesignating a contingency operation; and

Restores Benefits to Personnel Supporting Iran War by retroactively restoring all covered benefits entitled to members of the Armed Services and civilian employees who have supported Iran-related operations since February 28, 2026.

Senator Baldwin has been an outspoken critic of President Trump’s illegal war with Iran and has repeatedly forced votes in the Senate to end Trump’s war of choice that is hurting Wisconsinites. For months, Senator Baldwin has been raising the alarms on the Trump Administration’s inadequate preparation, which put American troops in harm’s way and led to insufficient care for injured servicemembers, including two Wisconsinites who went weeks without proper screening and treatment for traumatic brain injuries.

The bill is led by U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) and also co-sponsored by Senators Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Gary Peters (D-MI), John Hickenlooper (D-CO), Mazie K. Hirono (D-HI), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Michael Bennet (D-CO), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Andy Kim (D-NJ), Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), John Fetterman (D-PA), Brian Schatz (D-HI) and Jacky Rosen (D-NV).
