title: Rep. Roy Demands Answers from Texas State University After Hiring H-1B Employee Over Americans
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congressman Chip Roy (TX-21) sent the following letter to Texas State University, demanding answers after the university renewed an employment contract with a foreign worker on an H-1B visa.

The Daily Caller wrote an exclusive report on the letter, which you can read here.

Read the full letter here or below:

Dr. Kelly R. Damphousse

President, Texas State University

601 University Drive

San Marcos, Texas 78666

Dear Dr. Damphousse,

It has come to my attention that Texas State University clarified its decision to file a notice of intent to hire an H-1B nonimmigrant worker for a Public Relations Specialist position at the university, as it is a renewal for an existing Texas State H-1B visa holder employee and graduate, not a new petition.

While the explanation behind Texas State’s occupation listing provided some clarity on the H-1B nonimmigrant posting, it raises questions about the extent to which the university may be prioritizing the hiring of foreign nationals over American graduates and workers, and whether it made good-faith efforts to recruit a qualified U.S. citizen for the position. As you are likely aware, Texas State offers a Bachelor of Science degree in Public Relations and could have hired one of its own U.S. citizen graduates, as it awards an estimated 140 degrees to its students in this field annually.

Further, universities can sponsor an F-1 student visa holder who enrolls in the Optional Practical Training program for an H-1B visa, allowing them to remain in the country longer. The explanation details that the referenced H-1B visa holder was an F-1 student at Texas State who later graduated and found employment at the university, raising questions about Texas State’s role in sponsoring international students for long-term stay and employment rather than recruiting local applicants.

On January 27, 2026, Governor Greg Abbott directed all state agencies and universities to freeze new H1B petitions until May 31, 2027, and launch a review of the visa program statewide after noting how the H-1B visa program is used to replace American workers with cheap unskilled foreign labor, often working for low wages. More recently, on August 19, 2026, Gov. Abbott called on the state legislature to ban higher education institutions from employing H-1B recipients statewide.

Relatedly, recent data show Texas as a leading state in Labor Condition Applications filed to hire H-1B workers, raising concerns that businesses, employers, and colleges may be overlooking Texans who are qualified, talented, and, in many cases, being displaced to employ cheaper foreign alternatives who likely do not possess unique or specialized skills.

Further, a 2019 academic evaluation of the program found that “most H-1B workers have no more than ordinary skills, skills that are available in the U.S. labor market”, as applicants are only required to hold a bachelor’s degree, which countless Americans possess, which undermining the narrative that H-1B visa holders are skilled, specialized, or “the best of the best”.

Most H-1B visa holders are also paid lower on average than their American counterparts, often leading to the latter unfairly competing for occupations and decent salaries in specialty occupations despite existing statute requiring employers to pay the prevailing wage.

In 2024, over 90 percent of employer-submitted prevailing wage claims for approved H-1B visas were below the Bureau of Labor Statistics’ prevailing wage for the occupation and location. Another result of hiring large numbers of H-1B visa holders is the routine mass firing of white-collar workers who are often required to train their replacements to receive a severance package.

The H-1B visa program does not serve the interests of Texas nor the nation. The Trump administration has rightly ordered stricter scrutiny on H-1B visa applicants to determine if they offer unique skills to the nation and to counter outsourcing by IT firms that petition for these foreign workers only to displace local white-collar workers.

As such, I respectfully request clarity and a detailed accounting of the following questions by September 3, 2026:

How many H-1B visa holders does Texas State University currently employ? Please disaggregate by the following:

The occupations listed on their H-1 B petitions and where they currently work within the university.

The educational and specialty skills these individuals possess and how they pertain to the occupation in which they currently work.

Please provide the salary offered to H-1B recipients and the current salary paid to them from their hiring date to the present.

Please provide the prevailing wage for the respective occupations.

Does Texas State assist international students who enter the U.S. and enroll at the university on an F-1 student visa or J-1 nonimmigrant visa in adjusting to the Optional Practical Training program and eventually the H-1B program to subsequently sponsor and employ them?

Please explain the extent to which this occurs and provide data on the visa adjustment stated above.

How many of the H-1B visa holders at Texas State are from the capped lottery or are cap-exempt?

How many H-1B visa holders have Texas State employed since fiscal year 2020?

Please break down each figure by fiscal year.

Please provide a detailed explanation of how Texas State has tried to recruit U.S. citizens through public postings, salary offered, or other means.

How many other employment postings by Texas State have solicited H-1B workers?

Please explain the extent to which Texas State University is complying with Gov. Abbott’s January 27, 2026, directive for state universities to halt new H-1B petitions.

Respectfully,

Chip Roy

Member of Congress

title: Congressman Dr. Raul Ruiz and Congressman Troy Carter Demand Answers From HHS, ICE, CBP, and ORR On Plans To Expand Child Detention Capacity and House Unaccompanied Children at Contaminated Former Air Force Base
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congressman Dr. Raul Ruiz (CA-25) and Congressman Troy Carter (LA-02), joined by 75 additional Members of Congress, today led a formal letter to Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) Commissioner Rodney Scott, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) Acting Director David Venturella, and Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) Acting Director Angie Salazar, demanding immediate answers on reports that the Administration is preparing to dramatically expand federal detention capacity for unaccompanied children, including at a former Louisiana military installation with a documented history of environmental contamination.

The letter cites a federal solicitation seeking a contractor capable of housing up to 3,000 unaccompanied children per facility, with capacity for at least 400 children within 30 days of contract award, and reports that the former England Air Force Base in Louisiana is under consideration as a detention site. According to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, portions of the former base have tested for the "forever chemical" (PFAS) contamination at levels among the worst of any military site in the country, with groundwater still being remediated for chlorinated solvents. No cleanup plan for the PFAS contamination has been completed.

"When the federal government takes custody of a child, it takes on full responsibility for that child's safety," said Rep. Ruiz. "As an emergency physician, I know exactly what chronic exposure to these chemicals can do to a developing child. PFAS chemicals do not break down and they do not leave the body quickly, they bioaccumulate. In a growing child, that can mean weakened immune systems, developmental delays, a lifetime of elevated cancer risk, thyroid and liver problems, and a weaker response to routine childhood vaccines. Children breathe, drink, and eat more relative to their body weight than adults, and their organ systems are still developing, so these risks compound. Layer in the solvents still being cleaned up in the groundwater, and you have a facility where the water and soil themselves could be a health hazard, in addition to the psychological trauma of detention itself. Before a single child is sent to a site with this kind of contamination history, HHS owes Congress and the American people real answers. No physician would sign off on housing a healthy child there without a complete, independent environmental health assessment. Right now, we don't have those answers, and neither does the public."

"Everyone, but especially children, deserves to be treated with dignity and respect as they pursue immigration to America. Legally, we recognize that unaccompanied minors are uniquely vulnerable and require special care when in federal custody. It's imperative that the administration guarantees these children have a safe place to sleep, access to medical care, and safe living conditions," said Congressman Troy A. Carter, Sr. (LA-02).

"This is not a routine capacity planning, it is a rapid, large-scale expansion of child detention, and it demands real oversight," Ruiz continued. "Congress passed the Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act because unaccompanied children are among the most vulnerable people in our custody. That law is clear: children must be cared for in child-appropriate settings and released to qualified sponsors without unnecessary delay. I am going to make sure HHS, ICE, and CBP are held to that standard."

The letter comes amid a broader pattern of preventable deaths in federal immigration custody. According to a July 2026 report by Physicians for Human Rights, at least 52 people died in ICE custody in the first 500 days of the current administration, a mortality rate more than double that of the first Trump Administration and nearly four times the rate under the Biden Administration. Reps. Ruiz and Carter warned that expanding detention capacity for children, at facilities with unresolved environmental and safety questions, risks repeating and compounding that pattern.

In the letter, Reps. Ruiz and Carter request written responses within 30 days to a series of questions, including:

What factors led HHS to determine that capacity for up to 3,000 additional beds per facility is necessary, and what the agency's current shelter capacity and occupancy rates are;

What alternatives HHS considered before selecting the former England Air Force Base, and what environmental and public health reviews were conducted;

What short- and long-term health effects children could face from exposure to site contaminants, and whether personnel previously stationed there have experienced adverse health effects;

What steps HHS is taking to prioritize licensed, child-appropriate placements and timely release to qualified sponsors, consistent with the TVPRA; and

How HHS, ICE, and CBP are coordinating to minimize the time children spend in federal custody.

Reps. Ruiz and Carter also request a staff briefing within 30 days on the Administration's plans for the care of unaccompanied children and the standards that will govern any expansion of detention capacity.

title: Salazar Joins Acting Labor Secretary Sonderling to Highlight No Tax on Tips, Address Restaurant Workforce Crisis
text:
MIAMI, FL — Today, Congresswoman María Elvira Salazar (FL-27) joined Acting U.S. Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling and South Florida restaurant leaders for a roundtable focused on No Tax on Tips, the pressures facing locally owned restaurants, and the industry’s need for a stable, legal workforce.

“Miami gathers around its restaurants, from the morning cafecito to the last table of the night. Behind every one of those tables is someone working hard for every tip they earn,” said Congresswoman Salazar.“That is why I helped turn No Tax on Tips into law. It allows servers, bartenders, and other restaurant workers to keep more of their earnings for the bills waiting at home, without asking small restaurant owners, already operating on tight margins, to absorb another cost.”

Under the new law, eligible workers may deduct up to $25,000 in qualified tip income from their federal taxable income. The law also provides a deduction for eligible overtime compensation.

The roundtable then turned from immediate tax relief to a longer-term challenge raised by restaurant owners: maintaining a stable and legal workforce.

According to the National Restaurant Association, nearly one in four restaurant and food-service employees (23 percent) was born outside the United States. Restaurant operators struggled to fill nearly 900,000 open positions each month in 2025, and the industry is expected to add approximately 1.7 million jobs over the next decade.

The National Restaurant Association has endorsed Salazar’s bipartisan Dignity Act (H.R. 4393), and restaurant owners participating in the roundtable expressed support for the legislation as a practical answer to the workforce uncertainty affecting their businesses.

“Restaurant owners told us directly that they have positions they cannot fill and no reliable legal workforce to fill them. At the same time, experienced workers who have lived here for years remain unable to work legally,” Salazar said. “The Dignity Act brings those realities together under strict rules. That is why the National Restaurant Association and restaurant owners support it: it replaces uncertainty with a permanent workforce solution that restaurants nationwide can use and trust.”

The Dignity Act would allow eligible, longtime undocumented immigrants to earn renewable legal status and work authorization after meeting strict requirements. Combined with nationwide E-Verify, it would help restaurants build a stable, verified workforce while protecting businesses that follow the rules. The Dignity Program provides no federal benefits or pathway to citizenship.

During the roundtable, local operators described how rising costs, narrow margins, and staffing shortages shape decisions about hours, service, and expansion. Salazar underscored her message: No Tax on Tips delivers immediate relief to restaurant employees, while the Dignity Act addresses the staffing instability holding their employers back.

Salazar thanked Acting Secretary Sonderling for bringing the conversation directly to Miami and hearing firsthand from the restaurant leaders affected by federal labor and workforce policies.

Participants included representatives from the National Restaurant Association, the Florida Restaurant and Lodging Association, Rusty Pelican, Texas Roadhouse, Chick-fil-A, Grove Bay Hospitality, VE Hospitality, SuViche, Novecento, Outback Steakhouse, Anna Management, Meat N’ Bone, and Wagyu Bar.

title: Rep. Andrea Salinas’ Statement Following Supreme Court Ruling Allowing Trump to Advance Voter Suppression Plan
text:
SALEM, OR — Today, Congresswoman Andrea Salinas (OR-06) released the following statement in response to the Supreme Court’s decision that clears the way for President Trump to move forward with parts of his executive order restricting mail-in voting.

“The Supreme Court just cleared the way for President Trump to move forward with his plan to restrict mail-in voting, a thinly veiled attempt at voter suppression.

“For decades, Oregonians have voted entirely by mail, and our elections have been safe, secure, and accurate. Today’s ruling is an attack on every Oregonian’s right to vote, but it’s not the end of the fight. Every Oregonian has a right to cast their ballot and have it counted. I will keep supporting the legal battle against Trump’s unlawful executive order, and I will keep fighting to protect our vote-by-mail system.

“The more Trump tries to silence Oregonians, the more we will make our voices heard. Come November, Oregonians will vote overwhelmingly to hold Trump, Congress, and every other institution that has enabled his corruption, accountable.”

title: Rep. Stansbury Demands Answers on Project Jupiter’s Water Use as New Mexico Supreme Court Issues Emergency Orders
text:
ALBUQUERQUE — Congresswoman Melanie Stansbury (NM-01) is requesting answers from New Mexico state officials regarding the water use, water rights, permitting, quality, and compact compliance associated with Project Jupiter, a 1,400-acre artificial intelligence data center campus under construction near Santa Teresa in Doña Ana County, New Mexico. Stansbury’s calls for answers come as the New Mexico Supreme Court issued two emergency orders Sunday night regarding the project’s emergency well permit, used for construction of the project, and a proposed air quality permit.

Stansbury is directing the public request for information by close of business this Friday, August 28, as the Court has ordered the parties to respond to its orders by Wednesday of next week. Stansbury’s letter, addressed to the New Mexico Attorney General, the State Engineer, the State Environment Secretary, and the Chair and Director of the New Mexico Interstate Stream Commission, requests information about the project’s proposed water use, analysis of potential impacts, and compliance requirements under the Rio Grande Compact.

The request comes as New Mexico confronts unprecedented water challenges and works to meet its obligations under a court-supervised settlement following litigation with Texas over the Rio Grande Compact. Under the settlement, New Mexico must reduce groundwater pumping in the Lower Rio Grande Basin by 18,200 acre-feet annually by 2036.

Project Jupiter is expected to become a significant industrial water user in the basin, with estimates putting its water use at over a million gallons a day. Stansbury is asking the Office of the State Engineer (OSE) and others to provide a clear public accounting of how the project’s water needs will be met and what water rights and permits support those needs.

"In New Mexico we know water is life and our communities are facing a historic water crisis,” Rep. Stansbury said. "Every new major water use deserves a transparent accounting of where its water is coming from and how that use fits within our state’s obligations to our tribes and Pueblos, acequias, farmers and ranchers, the communities who already depend on these waters, and our surrounding neighbors. New Mexicans demand and deserve to know how their water is being used, how those rights may be obtained or transferred, and what permits the State has approved. This is about transparency, accountability, and protecting New Mexico’s water future."

In her letter to the OSE, Stansbury requests information on four key areas:

Project Jupiter’s water use: Estimated and reported daily and annual water consumption during construction and future operations, including the intended end uses of the water, such as cooling, power generation, and domestic use, and potential consumptive use and return flows.

Project Jupiter’s water rights: The water rights currently associated with the project, their origin—including whether they derive from prior agricultural use—and the legal process through which any transfer or change of use was reviewed and approved. The request also asks whether any new groundwater appropriations have been sought or granted.

Project Jupiter’s permits and applications: A complete list of applications and permits filed with or issued by OSE, including filing dates, current status, and any protests or objections submitted.

Analyses Conducted on Project Jupiter’s Water Impacts: Any analysis performed of the project’s proposed water use or discharge on state water supplies, water quality, other users, and compliance with in-state, interstate, and international laws, agreements, and management requirements on the Rio Grande.

“The scale of Project Jupiter makes this an important test case for how New Mexico evaluates major industrial water users in a water-scarce future,” Stansbury said. “The public should have a clear accounting of what water resources are being proposed for this project, the process by which those decisions are being made, and must have a say on how water in New Mexico is used.”

This request follows two unanimous orders from the New Mexico Supreme Court on August 23rd, 2026, pausing Project Jupiter proceedings. One order temporarily halts a scheduled September 14th air quality permit hearing at the New Mexico Environment Department on Project Jupiter’s proposed natural gas fuel cell system. The second order directs the Office of the State Engineer to pause an emergency permit for a specific well being used for the data center’s construction. These orders follow concerns from environmental groups alleging a lack of due process in the state's permitting processes. The New Mexico Supreme Court gave the parties involved until September 2, 2026, to respond to their orders.

Find a recording of the press call on this topic here.

Find a copy of the letter here or read the full letter below:

Dear Attorney General Torrez, State Engineer Anderson, Secretary Kenney, Chair Sanchez, and Director Riseley-White:

I am writing to urgently request information from applicable state agencies regarding the water usage, water rights, water permitting, and potential impacts to water quality and interstate river compact compliance associated with Project Jupiter, a 1,400-acre artificial intelligence data center campus under construction near Santa Teresa in Doña Ana County, New Mexico. While the New Mexico Supreme Court has stayed the administrative proceeding on the project’s air quality permit and the use of its emergency water-well authorization this week, we remain deeply concerned about the proposed water usage by this facility. Specifically, we are concerned about whether it has obtained the proper water rights and/or permits to operate in compliance with New Mexico water law and the state's obligations under the Rio Grande Compact and interstate agreements.

This request comes at a critical moment for New Mexico’s water future. As you know, the state is currently experiencing one of its worst water years on record: water curtailments have hit users and farmers statewide following record-low snowpack, Elephant Butte Reservoir has fallen to its lowest storage level since 1971, and the Rio Grande has now run dry through the middle reach for more than three months—one of the longest such stretches on record. While we are hopeful that weather conditions will improve this year to provide increased precipitation, we understand that these conditions represent a longer-term trend and shift in our water supplies due to climate change—which raise significant concerns about the impacts of this project.

With increasing constraints on our water supply, New Mexico is already experiencing significant pressures to restrict and reduce existing uses. Following litigation with Texas over the Rio Grande Compact, New Mexico is now under a binding, court-supervised settlement requiring a reduction in groundwater pumping of 18,200 acre-feet annually in the Lower Rio Grande Basin by 2036—the very basin from which Project Jupiter draws its water. Given New Mexico’s record-breaking drought and ongoing water availability crisis, your agencies’ decisions governing the allocation, permitting, and oversight of our limited water resources deserve the utmost public accountability and transparency. This is especially true when the State is legally obligated to bring into balance a large new industrial water user entering the basin—one that is currently reported to require over a million gallons of water a day.

The questions Project Jupiter has raised matter to and affect New Mexicans statewide. Given the size of this project and the precedent it may set for how similar large-scale industrial water developments will be reviewed in the future, the public deserves a clear and complete record of the water resources at stake and how water rights and permitting determinations will be made.

This request follows significant public concern raised regarding the project’s water requirements at several local proceedings. At the Doña Ana County Board of Commissioners meeting in September 2025, commissioners voted to approve $165 billion in industrial revenue bonds for Project Jupiter. That meeting drew several hundred residents, many of whom requested that the vote be delayed, to allow more time for questions about water and other impacts to be answered. Subsequently, on October 29, 2025, the New Mexico Legislature’s Water and Natural Resources Committee met in Artesia and received a briefing on Project Jupiter, during which committee members raised concerns regarding water use and the availability of information about the project to the public.[4] Similar concerns were also raised in recent public listening sessions held by New Mexico lawmakers over the last several weeks and have been raised by federal state, tribal, and local leaders across New Mexico.

At this time, a full accounting of Project Jupiter’s proposed water usage, permits and water rights has not been made publicly available nor has any analysis of its potential impacts on New Mexico’s water supply, water quality, and compliance with interstate compacts, agreements, and court orders been made public. To shed light on these issues we are respectfully requesting that each of your agencies provide the following information as it pertains to your agency, office, or commission and any relevant information your office may have on the matter:

Project Jupiter’s estimated and reported water usage, in daily and annual volumes, for both the construction phase and ongoing/future operations, including the intended end uses of that water (e.g., cooling, power generation), potential consumptive use, and potential return flows.

Any proposed or confirmed water rights or permits currently associated with Project Jupiter, including their origin (e.g., prior agricultural use) and the legal and/or administrative processes by which any transfer or change of use was reviewed and approved—and whether any new groundwater appropriations have been sought or granted for the project, including quantities, places of use, and relevant dates of administrative action.

A list of all permits and applications filed with or issued by OSE for Project Jupiter, including dates and status of each and any protests or objections filed against them.

Any analysis performed of the project’s proposed water use or discharge on state water supplies, water quality, other users, and compliance with in-state, interstate and international laws, agreements, and management requirements on the Rio Grande.

Given the level of public concern regarding this project and its potential water impacts, and considering imminent court decisions regarding project completion, we request your responses in writing to my office no later than close of business Friday, August 28. We also request that your office make all non-privileged information available to the public.

Thank you for your attention to this request.

###

title: Rep. Steube Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Protect Nonprofits’ Tax-Exempt Status
text:
Rep. Steube Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Protect Nonprofits’ Tax-Exempt Status

WASHINGTON–U.S. Representative Greg Steube (R-Fla.) and Representative Suzan DelBene (D-Wash.) today introduced the Safeguarding America’s Nonprofits Act, legislation to amend the Internal Revenue Code and clarify that a nonprofit’s federal tax-exempt status does not constitute federal financial assistance.

“Nonprofits across the country depend on their tax-exempt status to carry out their work. That status should never be treated as a form of government assistance,” said Rep. Steube. “The Safeguarding America’s Nonprofits Act puts a clear, permanent rule in statute so nonprofits do not have to worry about their tax exemption being reinterpreted as a government handout.”

“Nonprofits across the country rely on clear, consistent federal rules to continue serving their communities effectively. In recent years, conflicting court decisions have created uncertainty by suggesting that nonprofits could be subject to regulations that Congress never intended for them. This bipartisan legislation would clarify that an organization’s tax-exempt status is not federal financial assistance. It would protect charities, philanthropies, community‑based organizations, and religious institutions from unnecessary regulations so they can stay focused on delivering critical services,” said Congresswoman Suzan DelBene.

“Nonprofit organizations are the heart of our communities. They play an essential role in supporting families and hardworking Americans, advancing research, educating students, and providing countless other public benefits, often stepping in where government and business can’t or shouldn’t. Their strength lies in their independence. The Safeguarding America’s Nonprofits Act protects tax-exempt organizations independent from the federal government from unnecessary and burdensome risks of litigation or bureaucratic overreach. We appreciate Congressman Greg Steube (R-FL) and Congresswoman DelBene for their bipartisan leadership so nonprofits can continue to focus on their missions,” said Community Impact Coalition Co-Chairs: Tommy Goodwin and Mary Wheatley.

“Associations are among the most trusted institutions in American life,” said Michelle Mason, FASAE, CAE, President and CEO, American Society of Association Executives. “They set the standards that keep products safe and professions credible, train and credential the workforce, and convene the people who solve problems no single company or agency can solve alone. That work depends on their independence. The Safeguarding America’s Nonprofits Act makes clear what has always been true: tax exemption is not federal financial assistance, and it should never become a lever for government control over organizations that accept no federal dollars. ASAE thanks Congressman Steube and Congresswoman DelBene for introducing this important legislation and urges members of Congress to support it.”

“Representing family forestry businesses across Rural America, the Forest Landowners Association understands firsthand the important role nonprofit organizations play in strengthening communities and advancing the interests of the people and industries they serve,” said Scott Jones, CEO, Forest Landowners Association. “Tax-exempt status is not a government grant or subsidy, and it should not be treated as federal financial assistance. The Safeguarding America’s Nonprofits Act provides important clarity and protects organizations like FLA from unnecessary regulatory burdens that could hinder our ability to carry out our missions. FLA is proud to support this bipartisan legislation.”

“Community Associations Institute (CAI) is proud to support the Safeguarding America’s Nonprofits Act,” said Dawn M. Bauman, CAE, CEO of CAI. “Nonprofit organizations like CAI play an essential role in providing important resources to support the integrity and strength of America’s communities. This legislation helps ensure CAI can continue to prioritize our members and provide the education, advocacy, and resources they need to support thriving community associations. We thank Congressman Steube and Senator Lankford for their leadership on this important legislation.”

The bill amends Section 501 of the Internal Revenue Code to state that a federal income tax exemption does not count as federal financial assistance for organizations described under sections 501(c), 501(d), or 401(a).

There are roughly 2 million nonprofit organizations in the United States. Many operate without any direct government assistance, thereby avoiding the compliance burdens that federal subsidies often impose. When the tax code was written, Congress intended for a clear distinction between nonprofits that do and do not accept government assistance. This bill affirms Congress’ intent and limits legal uncertainty.

The legislation is supported by a broad coalition of nonprofit organizations, including the Community Impact Coalition, Career Education Colleges and Universities, American Society of Association Executives, National Scleroderma Foundation, Women in Trucking, Florida Association of Free and Charitable Clinics, Community Associations Institute, The Handcrafted Soap & Cosmetic Guild, Inc., Household and Commercial Products Association, American Rental Association, American Council of Academic Physical Therapy, Bostrom, National Association for Regulatory Administration, Association Management Services, Inc., Association CEO, American Society for Nondestructive Testing, American Society for Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics, and the National Emergency Number Association.

The full text of the Safeguarding America’s Nonprofits Act is available here.

title: Lee, Horsford Introduce Bill to Ensure Yucca Mountain is Never Used as Nuclear Waste Repository
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Susie Lee (NV-03) and Congressman Steven Horsford (NV-04) introduced legislation to ensure Yucca Mountain will never be used as a repository for nuclear waste. The Jobs, Not Waste Act follows the Trump Administration’s proposal to scrap Yucca Mountain as the nation’s sole nuclear waste repository and instead allow other states to willingly host such facilities.

“I will continue to work to never let Yucca Mountain become the nation’s dumping ground for nuclear waste. Time and time again, Nevadans have clearly opposed storing waste at Yucca Mountain—now we have a chance to make sure Yucca stays dead for good,” said Congresswoman Susie Lee. “I’m fighting to pass this bill so we can explore other uses for the site to grow our economy instead of turning it into a nuclear waste dump.”

“Nevadans have said no to nuclear waste storage at Yucca Mountain for decades, and that answer hasn't changed,” said Congressman Steven Horsford. “This fight has shaped the lives of my constituents for a generation; the uncertainty, the threat, the toll it's taken on our communities never went away. It's time to end it permanently. The Jobs, Not Waste Act closes the door on nuclear waste at Yucca Mountain and opens the door to real jobs and economic opportunity for Southern Nevada instead. I'm proud to co-lead this bill for the Nevadans who have carried this fight for far too long.”

The Jobs, Not Waste Act would repeal the law that established Yucca Mountain as a repository for nuclear waste, require the Department of Energy (DOE) to withdraw and terminate the licensing proceeding for Yucca Mountain at the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, require DOE to reclaim and mitigate any adverse environmental impacts to the site, and require the Office of Management and Budget to determine the viability and benefits of other uses for the site.

title: Tonko, Schumer, Gillibrand Raise Alarm Amid Impending Closure of Schenectady Veterans Affairs Community Based Outpatient Clinic
text:
NEW YORK, NY — Today, U.S. Representative Paul Tonko (D-NY-20), Senate Democratic Leader Charles Schumer (D-NY), and U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), following continued concern from local Capital Region veterans, called on Secretary of Veterans Affairs Doug Collins to provide more information about the planned closure of the Schenectady Veterans Affairs (VA) Community Based Outpatient Clinic (CBOC) at the end of the month. When the closure was announced in March 2026, the lawmakers immediately called on the VA to halt the closure and provide immediate answers to ensure that healthcare for the over 1,500 Capital Region veterans who rely on this clinic would not be disrupted. Now, five months following their original letter and with the closure looming, few questions have been answered.

In the letter, the members addressed the lack of communication from the VA and the confusion that Capital Region veterans are experiencing with little to no guidance as to the future of their care. They wrote, “Since the closure was announced this past spring, vanishingly little detail or communication has been made available to veterans or the broader public in the Capital Region. The lack of communication has raised concerns about the burden this disruption will place on veterans with ongoing care. Five months since the announcement of the closure, we continue to hear from veterans and non-profit organizations working to cover gaps in care and transportation for veterans, who find themselves less informed, more confused, and in greater precarity.”

The members noted that this would be the second CBOC closure in the Capital Region in five years, forcing veterans to seek out alternative care in places that may be even farther from their homes. They continued, “The communities we represent have expressed significant doubt regarding the VA’s claim that transportation time to the new clinics will be shorter for 80% of veterans. Many older veterans in the area are reliant on public transportation, ride-share services, and friends, family, and their communities for transportation to VA appointments. We are especially concerned that the decision to shift care away from the Schenectady CBOC does not account for the additional bus routes, ride-share costs, and time commitments from friends and families to ensure that veterans have regular access to care at a different facility.”

In a series of questions, the members demanded immediate transparency and requested that the VA release concrete data and outreach plans regarding the facility's closure by August 27th. The inquiry pushes the VA to detail its justification for the closure and the projected impact on veterans in the region, as well as the VA’s plans for ensuring that patients maintain their access to high-quality care.

The lawmakers stressed that not a single local veteran or advocacy group had reached out to their offices to voice support for the clinic’s closure. They concluded, “The lack of clear communication and proper planning has caused significant anxiety for veterans in the Schenectady region who place their trust in the VA to manage their care. We urge the VA to listen to the community that would be most immediately affected by this plan, halt the closure of this clinic until all the questions posed in this letter can be properly addressed, and work with us to rebuild trust among veterans in the Capital Region.”

title: Representative Derek Tran Raises Alarm on the Cost of the Iran War for American Families
text:
Washington, DC – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) led a letter with his National Security Task Force co-chairs Representatives Jason Crow (CO-06) and Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) to President Trump and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth demanding a full public accounting of the economic costs of the war with Iran as prices rise for American families nationwide.

Read the full letter HERE.

"What was billed as a two-week operation is now a full-scale war that has lasted for over 150 days, cost at least $37 billion, and claimed the lives of 18 servicemembers. At the same time, prices across the country have gone up significantly, placing the burden of this conflict on American families. By June 9, you had claimed that the war in Iran was almost over 38 times. Instead, the war has continued, leaving Americans across the country with no idea when this war will come to an end and when prices will come down. This uncertainty, and the months of higher costs have taken a toll, impacting Americans’ ability to budget, plan, and save for the future. These costs are untenable, and the American people deserve better," wrote the members.

The letter details a request for information on the cost of operations, changes in the oil and energy markets, and macroeconomic impacts. It comes following the Department of Defense’s supplemental request for tens of billions more to fund the ongoing war in Iran and concerns about the risks to American economy, personnel, and safety overtime.

An Army Veteran, Representative Tran is a member of the powerful House Armed Services Committee and serves as a member of the Readiness Subcommittee and the Intelligence and Special Operations Subcommittee. Tran has voted for or cosponsored multiple War Powers Resolutions to reassert Congressional authority over the war, includingH.Con.Res. 40,H.Con.Res. 38, andH.Con.Res. 86, and joined the Democratic Veterans Caucus in aletter to President Trump calling for the same. In May 2026, Tran joined fellow members of the Lowering Costs Caucus in aletter urging the Trump Administration to address skyrocketing energy prices.Tran serves as Co-Chair of the House Democratic Caucus National Security Task Force.

title: Representative Tran Issues Statement on GKN’s $100 Million Fund for Families Impacted by the Hazmat Incident
text:
Garden Grove, C.A. – Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) released the following statement in response to an announcement by GKN Aerospace that it is creating a $100 million fund for families, small businesses, and community members impacted by the hazmat incident and evacuation over Memorial Day Weekend:

“Today’s announcement from GKN Aerospace is a step in the right direction. Committing $100 million in grant funding to aid the families, workers, and small business owners impacted by the recent evacuation is part of corporate accountability. This substantial commitment is a crucial and welcome step toward helping our community recover from the severe disruption, unexpected financial burdens, and stress caused by this crisis.

Our residents and local businesses showed incredible resilience during the evacuation and they deserve to be made whole by way of direct financial relief to help cover missed wages, temporary housing, and lost business revenue. I commend GKN for stepping up to take meaningful responsibility for the hardship experienced by our neighbors.

At the same time, we must recognize that the full economic impact of an emergency involving over 50,000 displaced residents and 5,000 local businesses is complex and still unfolding. While $100 million represents significant progress, I am calling on GKN Aerospace leadership to remain open to evaluating the true long-term costs. If this initial fund proves insufficient to make every affected family and business whole, GKN must be prepared to step up with additional support.

Full accountability means ensuring no single resident or small business owner is left absorbing the financial toll of this incident. I look forward to working closely with GKN, local officials, and community leaders to ensure these grant funds are distributed swiftly, equitably, and transparently,” said Representative Tran.

On Thursday, May 21, the Orange County Fire Authority reported a leak of methyl methacrylate, a volatile and flammable chemical, from a 34,000-gallon storage tank at the GKN Aerospace plant in Garden Grove. The risk of a toxic leak or catastrophic explosion prompted over 50,000 evacuations across Garden Grove, Westminster, Buena Park, Cypress, Anaheim, and Stanton. On May 29, Representative Tran urged Administrator Kelly Loeffler to issue a disaster declaration and expedite small business loans. The Small Business Administration issued a disaster declaration on June 11, providing small businesses adversely affected by the crisis with access to low-interest federal disaster loans. On August 18, Representative Tran introduced the Hazardous Materials Transparency Act, to mandate that facilities like GKN properly and regularly notify the communities they operate in about the safety measures that are taken to avoid danger to residents and small businesses.

###

title: Congressman Van Drew: Gov. Sherrill Responds to Election Integrity Questions with Political Hit Piece
text:
Washington, DC - Today, Congressman Jeff Van Drew responded to Governor Mikie Sherrill's letter attacking members of the Republican Study Committee who joined Congressman Van Drew's effort to get answers about the failure that placed thousands of individuals who identified themselves as noncitizens on New Jersey's voter rolls.

"When we first raised this issue, we did so because we were genuinely concerned about what happened in New Jersey and wanted to understand exactly how it happened," said Congressman Van Drew. "For years, those of us who raised concerns about the integrity of our voter rolls were dismissed as conspiracy theorists. Then New Jersey admitted that thousands of individuals who said they were not citizens were registered to vote, and many registered through the error went on to cast ballots.

"We did not blame Governor Sherrill for a failure that occurred under the previous Murphy administration. We did not attack her personally or drag unrelated Democratic politicians into our letter. With the help of my colleagues in the Republican Study Committee, we asked basic, fact-finding questions about how the system failed mechanically and electronically, why the safeguards did not catch it, and what is being done to make sure it never happens again.

"Instead of answering those questions, Governor Sherrill responded with Democratic talking points, attacks on President Trump, and personal attacks against me and the Republican Study Committee members who joined me in seeking answers. None of the Members who signed our letter deserved to be demeaned for doing their jobs. Her response was a political hit piece, and it was beneath the Office of the Governor.

"This was never about Governor Sherrill or any one political party. It is about New Jersey and the integrity of our country's elections. Our mutual constituents deserve fair and secure elections, and they deserve the truth about how something this serious was allowed to happen. We are going to keep pursuing the facts, demanding accountability, and making sure this does not happen again. We will not give up until the people of New Jersey get the answers they deserve."

title: Rep. Whitesides Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Investigate Insider Trading Within the Department of Defense, Urges Prediction Markets to Crack Down on Harmful Practice
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. – Today, Reps. George Whitesides (D-CA), Don Bacon (R-NE) and Seth Moulton (D-MA) introduced the bipartisan No Insider Trading on National Security Act of 2026, legislation that investigates insider trading within the Department of Defense during the war in Iran. Rep. Whitesides introduced the bill following evidence of suspicious trades being made on prediction markets during Operation Absolute Resolve in Venezuela and Operation Epic Fury in Iran.

“Profiting off of events like war and human suffering by using insider information is a blatantly corrupt and unacceptable practice that cannot be allowed to continue,” said Rep. Whitesides. “We must crack down on anyone who uses private information to pad their pockets at the expense of our soldiers. This legislation will help us root out bad actors within the administration and restore sanity and trust to our government.”

“While Trump’s war of choice with Iran makes everyday life unaffordable for the American people, Trump and his associates are busy getting rich off of this war,” said Rep. Moulton. “The American people deserve to know how this administration uses public announcements as opportunities for market manipulation, insider trading, and self-enrichment. This legislation is the first step towards much-needed accountability from the most corrupt administration in history.”

On prediction markets like Polymarket, the average win rate for most categories on the site is about 18 percent. For military and defense actions, that number jumps to 52 percent. One user, under the account name “MAGA-my-man,” made close to $600,000 by betting on the timing of U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran. Another group of traders placed roughly $500 million on an energy market in future oil trades. Minutes later, an announcement was made postponing strikes in Iran. In April, a U.S. Army special forces soldier was charged with making more than $400,000 betting on the ouster of Nicolas Maduro on Polymarket.

The No Insider Trading on National Security Act instructs the Department of Defense’s Inspector General to investigate insider trading on both energy and prediction markets during Operation Epic Fury, assess risks posed by the potential trading, and recommend safeguards for future use.

Additionally, Rep. Whitesides wrote to top prediction market CEOs this week urging them to work with the Trump Administration to crack down on this practice, citing documented instances of irregular trading during military incidents.

title: Baldwin, Takano, Merkley Lead 179 Colleagues in Urging Supreme Court to Protect Preschoolers from Discrimination
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Senator Tammy Baldwin (WI), Rep. Mark Takano (D-CA-39) and Senator Jeff Merkley (D-OR) led their colleagues in filing an amicus brief at the Supreme Court in the case of St. Mary Catholic Parish v. Roy advocating to the Justices that preschools that receive state dollars should not be able to discriminate against children and families. At issue in the case are religious preschools seeking an exemption from the nondiscrimination provision in Colorado’s universal preschool program so they can refuse to admit LGBTQ+ children or the children of LGBTQ+ people while still receiving public funding. The members’ brief urges the Supreme Court to uphold the nondiscrimination provision and not grant a religious exemption.

“Discriminating against anyone – let alone preschoolers – is simply wrong and betrays some of our most fundamental and enduring beliefs as Americans,” said Senator Baldwin. “No child or family should face discrimination in a program supported by taxpayer dollars. Our country has taken great strides in the march toward true equality, and the Supreme Court should stop such blatant discrimination that would take us an unmistakable step backwards.”

This upcoming term, the Supreme Court will hear arguments in St. Mary’s Catholic Parish v. Roy, where the court will be considering when to apply which of its standards for granting religious exemptions from nondiscrimination laws. In 2020, Colorado voters passed a ballot proposition to establish state funding for preschool. In response, the Colorado legislature passed legislation to codify a universal preschool program. The law includes a nondiscrimination provision, stating that the quality standards for the program must include “a requirement that each preschool provider provide eligible children an equal opportunity to enroll and receive preschool services regardless of race, ethnicity, religious affiliation, sexual orientation, gender identity, lack of housing, income level, or disability, as such characteristics and circumstances apply to the child or the child's family.”

Two Catholic parishes that operate preschools, among other plaintiffs, sued claiming that this nondiscrimination policy violates their First Amendment rights. Specifically, the preschools want a religious exemption in order to receive taxpayer dollars while discriminating against LGBTQ+ students and children of LGBTQ+ parents.

The members’ brief argues that:

The Supreme Court defers to legislatures and the political process when assessing exemptions from neutral, generally-applicable laws;

Petitioners’ rule would endanger a myriad of federal nondiscrimination laws that Congress has carefully crafted over decades; and

The Court should be mindful not to destabilize or undermine that legislative role by effectively legislating ad hoc exemptions to nondiscrimination laws.

“I don’t just fear a Democrat majority. I fear a Democrat-Socialist majority because the [DSA] who control today’s Democrat Party support wide open borders, they support eliminating ICE, they are anti law enforcement, they want to defund the police,” Banks said.

“I cannot believe that the Democrats are so radical and extreme today that they’re OK with what’s happened to our country [with] illegals taking jobs for Americans or allowing illegals to be behind the wheel of semi-trucks,” Banks said, pointing to his “Dalilah Law.”

The bill honors Dalilah Coleman, a first-grader who was critically injured when an illegal immigrant driving a big rig caused a multi-car pileup on an Indiana highway. Partap Singh, an Indian national licensed in California, was driving the truck. Coleman suffered catastrophic injuries, spent months in the hospital and had a craniectomy.

Proponents have argued such changes would give American graduates a better chance of entering the job market after college.

Other bills in the package would provide additional border security funding to the War Department, restrict chain migration and target grants to colleges employing illegal immigrants.

“These seven bills are common sense, everything from stopping illegals from driving semi-trucks to banning birthright citizenship, to stopping chain migration, to cracking down on those who misuse the H-1B visas for cheap labor,” Banks said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., for comment on the package and to ask whether any of the bills will be expedited ahead of the midterms.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Sen. Banks, Gary Mayor Melton talked to President Trump about Storm Recovery on Monday
text:
Click here for the full story from The Times of Northwest Indiana or read below:

EXCLUSIVE: U.S. Sen. Jim Banks, R-Indiana, and Gary Mayor Eddie Melton spoke to President Donald Trump over the phone on Monday, providing him with an update about “the good things going on in Gary,” while also keeping him in the loop about storm damage and the impacts being felt on the ground by residents.

Trump approved a Presidential Emergency Declaration for Indiana at Gov. Mike Braun’s request on Aug. 15.

Banks said on Monday that Trump knows about another request from the Indiana Congressional delegation requesting direct assistance to families, homeowners, renters and others who have been impacted by the Aug. 11 derecho.

“The president loves Gary and has a long history in Gary,” Banks said. Trump was behind the riverboat Princess Casino, which opened in 1996 at Buffington Harbor.

“In my conversation with President Trump, I made it clear that Gary needs immediate access to FEMA resources to support our recovery,” Melton said in a statement shared with The Times. “This federal assistance is critical to restoring our neighborhoods, rebuilding our community and making sure Gary emerges from this storm stronger and more resilient than before.”

Banks told The Times about the call with Trump in an interview while in Gary early Monday afternoon. Banks said he, Trump and Melton also discussed the Nippon deal for U.S. Steel, which his administration approved last summer.

Melton and Banks took a “comprehensive tour of impacted areas” in Gary, according to a release from the city.

“The devastation our city has experienced demands swift, decisive and unified action at every level of government,” Melton said in a statement, adding that he was grateful to Banks for visiting Gary’s residents.

“The people here step up to help each other,” Banks said.

Banks also visited the Salvation Army’s Gary location before meeting with Pastor Eric Boone of the Tree of Life Missionary Baptist Church, whose congregation has served food to thousands in recent days.

“I think that says a lot about this community,” Banks said. “Pastor Boone has such a giant heart and what he’s been doing and what the other churches are doing in the area is really important.”

When asked about NIPSCO and the governor’s request for an investigation into the company’s preparedness for and response to recent storms, Banks said he believes it’s “important to learn from a situation like this.”

“What could we have done to avoid it and then learn from it to make sure it doesn’t happen again?” Banks said. “For sure, we should definitely investigate that.”

But, Banks said, his focus right now remains on getting the final few thousand customers without power in Gary and elsewhere across the Region. As of 2:30 p.m. on Monday, over 9,000 NIPSCO customers were without power. About 6,500 of those customers were in Gary, or about 72% of all remaining outages.

“It’s a long road ahead, but when you see leadership like that,” Banks said, referring to Melton, “It makes you hopeful that we can all pull together and work together and hopefully, Gary will come out of this better and stronger than ever before.”

title: Bennet Leads Entire Colorado Congressional Delegation in Support of Presidential Major Disaster Declaration Request for Colorado Wildfires
text:
Denver — Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet, a senior member of the U.S. Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry, and Representative Jeff Hurd, led the entire Colorado Congressional delegation – Senator John Hickenlooper and U.S. Representatives Brittany Pettersen, Diana DeGette, Joe Neguse, Jason Crow, Lauren Boebert, Jeff Crank, and Gabe Evans – in a letter to President Trump expressing strong support for Governor Jared Polis’ request for a Presidential Major Disaster Declaration for Pueblo, Custer, and Ouray Counties in Colorado. This request comes in response to more than $18 million in Federal Emergency Management Agency validated damages from Colorado’s Aspen Acres and Gold Mountain fires.

In June, Colorado experienced two large, destructive fires within 48 hours, the Aspen Acres Fire and Gold Mountain Fire, due to prime wildfire conditions including high winds, extreme heat, and prolonged drought. These fires burned over 140,000 acres collectively across Pueblo, Custer, and Ouray Counties and destroyed hundreds of homes and structures and energy and water infrastructure. The burn scars left by these fires also contributed to significant post-fire flooding and debris flows that led to one fatality in Beulah, Colorado.

Summer is peak tourism season for Colorado, and the fires and subsequent flooding caused major disruptions to transportation, lodging, recreation, hospitality, outfitter, and guide businesses. They also damaged the operations of agricultural producers who lost livestock, fencing, and grazing lands. Several rural communities were also affected by road closures, which made accessing work, school, healthcare, or essential services extremely difficult. State and federal emergency response officials state that they expect disruptions to continue through the remainder of the summer season.

“Successful recovery is essential to restoring the counties’ economies, which depend on clean drinking water, tourism, agriculture, outdoor recreation, and hunting and fishing. Without additional support, residents could face potentially insurmountable barriers to rebuilding homes and businesses, increased drinking water and electric utility costs, and the loss of important habitat and grazing lands. In addition, these communities face ongoing hazards from the post-fire burn scars, including debris, burned trees, and threats to water quality and drinking water infrastructure,” wrote the lawmakers.

“[…] a Presidential Major Disaster Declaration unlocks federal assistance programs, including Hazard Mitigation Assistance Grants, that are indispensable to recovery, mitigation, and long-term resilience. These communities urgently need federal relief to rebuild. We thank you in advance for your expedited review and approval of the Governor’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration,” concluded the lawmakers.

Bennet has actively fought against President Trump’s decision to deny Major Disaster Declarations for the Lee and Elk Fires in August 2025 and Southwest Colorado flooding in October 2025. This month, Bennet called on Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) and Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) to launch immediate investigations into the Trump administration’s use of federal agencies, grants, and personnel to carry out the President’s political vendetta against Colorado, including the denial of federal disaster funding for the Lee and Elk Fires and Southwest Colorado flooding. In January 2026, Bennet led the full Colorado Congressional delegation in support of Governor Jared Polis’ appeal to Trump’s decision to deny Major Disaster Declarations for the Lee and Elk Fires as well as Southwest Colorado flooding.

As Ranking Member of the Senate Agriculture Subcommittee on Conservation, Forestry, Natural Resources, and Biotechnology, Bennet has made wildfire resilience, forest health, and watershed protection a central focus of his work for Colorado. This month, he led Senators Hickenlooper, Mike Lee, and John Curtis to introduce a bipartisan resolution honoring this season’s wildfire casualties and all those who serve on the front lines of wildland firefighting efforts in the United States. Bennet and Hickenlooper also introduced the Emergency Mountain Pine Beetle Response and Coordination Act to mitigate the growing mountain pine beetle outbreak in Colorado. In February 2025, Bennet reintroduced the Protect the West Act to make a $60 billion investment in forest health and watershed restoration.

The text of the letter is available HERE and below.

Dear Mr. President:

We strongly support Governor Jared Polis’ request on August 23, 2026, for a Presidential Major Disaster Declaration with Public and Individual Assistance for Custer and Pueblo Counties, Colorado, in response to the Aspen Acres Fire and Public Assistance for Ouray County in response to the Gold Mountain Fire. Both fires burned during June, July, and August 2026. As part of this request, Governor Polis has also requested the Hazard Mitigation Assistance Grant Program for the affected counties.

In June 2026, extreme heat, prolonged drought, and high winds up to 100 miles per hour contributed to two mega fires in Colorado within 48 hours. The Gold Mountain Fire burned approximately 40,000 acres in Ouray County, Colorado, and the Aspen Acres Fire burned over 102,000 acres across Custer County and Pueblo County, Colorado. Together, these fires destroyed drinking water and electric utility infrastructure, and over 800 structures and 324 homes. The burn scars from both fires contributed to significant post-fire flooding and debris flows that destroyed additional homes, buildings, and electric, water, and transportation infrastructure. On August 16, a significant rain event resulted in one fatality in Beulah, Colorado.

Both fires occurred immediately before the Fourth of July during the summer’s peak tourism season, disrupting lodging, recreation, hospitality, outfitter, and guide businesses. Repeated fire, flood, and debris flow closures have limited visitation and disrupted tourism along the U.S. 550 corridor in Ouray and San Juan Counties, and in Beulah, Rye, and Westcliffe, Colorado. State and federal emergency response officials expect these disruptions to continue through the remainder of the summer season, with flood warnings and business closures continuing to cause cancellations while agricultural producers lose livestock, fencing, and grazing lands. In already isolated rural communities, the ongoing road closures are limiting access to work, schools, pharmacies, medical care, and other essential services.

Governor Polis has requested a Presidential Major Disaster Declaration for the Aspen Acres Fire and Gold Mountain Fire. With over $17 million in validated damages, and with significant gaps in private insurance coverage, the Aspen Acres Fire meets the Federal Emergency Management Administration’s threshold for both Public and Individual Assistance. Losses incurred due to the Gold Mountain Fire meet FEMA’s threshold for Public Assistance.

Successful recovery is essential to restoring the counties’ economies, which depend on clean drinking water, tourism, agriculture, outdoor recreation, and hunting and fishing. Without additional support, residents could face potentially insurmountable barriers to rebuilding homes and businesses, increased drinking water and electric utility costs, and the loss of important habitat and grazing lands. In addition, these communities face ongoing hazards from the post-fire burn scars, including debris, burned trees, and threats to water quality and drinking water infrastructure.

As you are aware, a Presidential Major Disaster Declaration unlocks federal assistance programs, including Hazard Mitigation Assistance Grants, that are indispensable to recovery, mitigation, and long-term resilience. These communities urgently need federal relief to rebuild. We thank you in advance for your expedited review and approval of the Governor’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration.

###

title: Booker Continues Annual 21-County Tour with Stops in Essex and Somerset Counties
text:
NEWARK, N.J. — Today, U.S. Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ) continued his annual 21-County Tour with stops in Essex and Somerset Counties. In Essex County, he visited medical researchers and students at Hackensack Meridian Health’s Center for Discovery & Innovation and School of Medicine. He then traveled to Somerset County, where he met with community leaders and families at the Franklin Food Bank for a roundtable on the importance of the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) for New Jersey families.

In Essex County, Senator Booker toured the Hackensack Meridian School of Medicine’s amphitheaters and simulation lab, where students receive hands-on medical training, and the Center for Discovery & Innovation’s laboratories, where researchers conduct immunology and cancer research and work to translate scientific discoveries into clinical care. He met with researchers and medical leaders about their work advancing cancer research, training the next generation of health care professionals, and developing new treatments.

This visit comes as the Trump administration has cut federal support for medical research, including right here in New Jersey, a global leader in life science innovation and world-class medical research that relies on millions of dollars in NIH grants. Senator Booker has consistently fought to protect federal investments in medical research. He introduced the NIH IMPROVE Act, which would provide consistent funding for NIH’s maternal health research initiative, and cosponsored legislation to expand Medicare-funded medical residency positions to help address the nation’s physician shortage. He also leads annual funding requests for colorectal, esophageal, ovarian, and Von Hippel-Lindau cancer research through the Department of Defense’s Peer-Reviewed Cancer Research Program.

“Senator Booker has been a tireless advocate for education, research, and high-quality, accessible healthcare for all communities,” said Robert Garrett, FACHE, CEO of Hackensack Meridian Health. “We are proud to host him at the Hackensack Meridian School of Medicine and the Center for Discovery and Innovation, to show how by training doctors of the future and making new scientific discoveries, we are working toward a better and healthier future for all of New Jersey, and beyond.”

In Somerset County, Senator Booker joined families and the leaders of New Jersey’s five major food banks at the Franklin Food Bank for a roundtable discussion on SNAP and food insecurity. Participants discussed the role SNAP plays in supporting nearly 850,000 New Jerseyans and the challenges communities face as federal policymakers consider cuts to the program. An estimated 44 percent of food-insecure residents in New Jersey do not receive SNAP benefits, making the work of organizations like the Franklin Food Bank critical to ensuring families have access to food.

Earlier this year, Senator Booker introduced his Food is Medicine: HEAL America Agenda, which calls for strengthening nutrition assistance and expanding access to healthy foods, including by expanding SNAP incentives for fresh fruits and vegetables and connecting federal food programs with American family farmers.

"Today, the Franklin Food Bank was honored to welcome U.S. Sen. Cory Booker and leaders from New Jersey’s five Feeding America food banks for an important conversation about the devastating impact of recent SNAP cuts on families in Franklin Township and communities across New Jersey.As food insecurity grows, we’re leaning on strong and integrated partnerships at the local, county, and state levels to meet these challenges head-on. Together, we’re working to ensure our most vulnerable neighbors have access to healthy, nutritious, culturally relevant food and the social services they need to thrive with dignity. Our greatest strength is our people. Our staff and volunteers are resilient, creative, and resourceful. Like palm trees, we may bend in the fiercest storms, but we don’t break. Our roots run deep—and our partnerships run even deeper and we’ll continue to adapt, respond, and stand with our neighbors," said Derek Smith, Executive Director, Franklin Food Bank.

“Today’s conversation between Senator Booker, New Jersey’s five food banks, and several of our pantry partners was an important opportunity to discuss the future of SNAP and what’s at stake for families in need,” said Elizabeth McCarthy, President & CEO of the Community FoodBank of New Jersey. “Since the SNAP cuts included in H.R. 1 took effect, we have seen increased demand for food assistance as families struggle to keep meals on the table with fewer resources. Shifting an additional $90 million in SNAP administrative costs to the state would put even more pressure on communities already working to meet growing needs. We urge Congress to delay this cost shift for two years and to roll back the harmful cuts enacted under H. R. 1. Thank you to Senator Booker for listening to those on the front lines of hunger relief and advocating with us to protect this critical program.”

"Families across South Jersey face an affordability crisis. Food, utilities, healthcare – it's all rising while federal support is shrinking," said Jane Asselta, President & CEO of the Food Bank of South Jersey. "We thank Senator Booker for meeting with us to raise awareness of how SNAP cuts are impacting food insecurity, increasing the need for additional federal food resources."

“Norwescap has seen demand more than double over the last three years. With the SNAP benefits changes and coming Medicaid changes we are going to be stretched beyond capacity to help our vets, seniors and lower-income families put food on the table,” said Mark Valli, CEO of Norwescap.

“Across Monmouth and Ocean counties, nearly 148,000 people are experiencing food insecurity, and the changes to SNAP enacted through H.R. 1 are creating new challenges for many of the neighbors we serve,” said Triada Stampas, President & CEO of Fulfill. “Our Navigation team, one of the most experienced in the country, is already seeing widespread confusion around expanded work requirements. Some people who still need help may lose benefits simply because they cannot navigate the new requirements or document an exemption. When that happens, their need for food does not disappear. They turn to food banks and local pantries that are already experiencing increased demand and cannot replace the scale of SNAP. We are grateful to Senator Booker for listening to what our communities are experiencing and for his continued advocacy to protect this critical program.”

"Hunger is not a failure of character. It is often the result of a family facing impossible choices. Our responsibility is to make sure those choices become less impossible," said Randall West, CEO of Mercer Street Friends.

“At a time when the Trump administration and congressional Republicans are pursuing cuts to federal investments in medical research and SNAP, today’s conversations reaffirmed how critical both of these programs are to the health of New Jerseyans and the importance of standing up against these chaotic and cruel policies that are hurting the people of our state. At the Center for Discovery and Innovation, I saw researchers who work every day to find new breakthroughs in cancer research, develop better treatments, and turn discoveries in the lab into care for patients. At the Franklin Food Bank, I heard from New Jerseyans feeling the squeeze of rising grocery costs and from the people working tirelessly to make sure their neighbors have enough to eat. We cannot afford to turn our backs on this work or on the people who depend on it. I will continue fighting for every dollar I can to make sure New Jerseyans doing this critical work have the support they need,” said Senator Booker.

Senator Booker’s Annual 21-County Tour continues tomorrow with stops in Middlesex, Union, and Hudson Counties.

title: Cantwell Statement on SCOTUS Decision Enabling Trump Admin to Restrict Mail-In Ballots
text:
Cantwell Statement on SCOTUS Decision Enabling Trump Admin to Restrict Mail-In Ballots

EDMONDS, WA – Today, the United States Supreme Court ruled that President Donald Trump could proceed to restrict mail-in voting, allowing implementation of an executive order despite rulings of lower courts finding the president’s order unconstitutional. The executive order would enable the United States Postal Service (USPS) and other agencies to have a role in determining whether voters receive ballots or a ballot will be counted.

U.S. Senator Maria Cantwell (D-WA) gave the following statement:

“Today’s Supreme Court decision gets the Trump Administration one step closer to implementing its voter suppression order and forcing states to hand over personal voter data to the federal government. This is wrong. The Constitution clearly says the States should administer elections. The federal government should not weaponize the US Postal Service to decide who will receive a mail-in ballot and whose vote will be counted. The Administration must not be allowed to take the right of Washingtonians to vote by mail or interfere with our free and fair elections.”

Sen. Cantwell has been a stalwart defender against overreach of the Trump administration into our elections:

On August 5, she sent a letter to Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche and Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin demanding the Trump Administration adhere to the National Voter Registration Act’s (NVRA) “quiet period” that prohibits systematic voter purges within 90 days of an election, pushing back against the Administration’s ongoing voter suppression efforts.

On July 29, she wrote to Blanche, Mullin, and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth demanding to know whether the Trump administration plans to illegally deploy armed federal law enforcement officers at polling sites during the November 2026 elections.

On July 28, Sen. Cantwell sharply criticized the Trump administration’s request that the Supreme Court allow him to seize control of state-run elections and implement an anti-vote-by-mail executive order. Lower courts have repeatedly rejected the president’s arguments and stated that his executive order is unconstitutional.

On July 2, Sen. Cantwell sent a letter to the Postmaster General about the U.S. Postal Service’s (USPS) proposed illegal rule to implement President Trump’s March 31 executive order to interfere with vote-by-mail. Sen. Cantwell’s letter specifically noted the recent decisions of multiple federal courts that found Trump’s executive order unconstitutional and enjoined the USPS from implementing the proposed rule – including in separate cases brought by the State of Washington with other states and the NAACP – and demanded the USPS comply with those court orders.

On June 29, she celebrated the Supreme Court’s ruling in Watson v. Republican National Committee against an effort to stop states from counting mail-in ballots that are received after Election Day, even if they’ve been postmarked in time. The case, brought by the Republican National Committee, threatened the election administration practices of states like Washington.

On June 24, Sen. Cantwell co-sponsored the Right To Vote Act, legislation to create the first-ever affirmative federal voting rights guarantee for all eligible citizens.

On June 24, she also denounced President Trump’s announcement that he would not sign the 21st Century Road to Housing Act – an overwhelmingly popular, bipartisan bill that passed both the House and Senate earlier in the week and would have increased housing supply and brought down housing costs – until Congress passes the SAVE America Act. That legislation, which Trump has repeatedly demanded, would eliminate vote-by-mail and impose onerous new restrictions on voting and registering to vote. It would disenfranchise millions of Americans in the name of a voter fraud “crisis” that, even by the standards of the right-wing Heritage Foundation, straightforwardly does not exist. President Trump again demanded Congress pass the restrictive bill following the Supreme Court’s ruling in Watson v. Republican National Committee. Despite President Trump’s refusal to sign the bipartisan housing bill, it became law on July 11, since he failed to act on the bill within the time period prescribed by the Constitution after Congress sent him the legislation.

On June 23, she joined the entire Democratic Caucus in sending a letter to the USPS demanding the USPS abandon attempts to restrict voting by mail called for by President Trump in an illegal and unconstitutional March 31 executive order attacking mail and absentee ballots.

On June 23, she also delivered a speech on the Senate floor calling out the Trump Administration’s war on mail-in voting as the latest frontier in a long history of voter disenfranchisement in the United States.

On June 17, she joined several of her Senate Democratic colleagues for a spotlight forum highlighting President Trump’s illegal overreach into our free and fair elections.

On June 8, she joined 23 of her Senate colleagues in demanding answers over the Trump Administration’s decision to remove the most recent version of the Federal Prosecution of Election Offenses manual from DOJ’s website without explanation.
