title: Barrett Hosts Energy Roundtable to Highlight Work to Expand Energy Production, Lower Costs
text:
Lansing, Mich. — Congressman Tom Barrett (MI-07) on Monday joined leaders from Michigan’s energy industry for a roundtable conversation to highlight his work and discuss additional solutions to increase domestic energy production and lower costs for Michigan families.

Barrett voted to spur American energy dominance in the Working Families Tax Cuts Act last year, and he has long championed policies to promote competition and encourage production of affordable, reliable energy.

“The pain at the pump is real for all of the families like mine that are crisscrossing mid-Michigan to get from school to soccer practice and everywhere in between,” said Congressman Barrett. “In Congress, I’ve proudly led the charge to increase American energy production and strengthen competition in the market by advocating for permitting reform and rolling back burdensome regulations that have driven costs through the roof. It’s going to take all of us working together with the private sector to bring down energy prices, and I hope Democrats in Lansing can set aside their Green New Deal Mandates to join me in that effort.”

Under a state law passed in 2023 by Democrats along party lines, Michigan will require electricity production to use 100% green energy sources by 2040. Due to the cost of building the wind turbines and solar farms necessary to comply with the mandate, electric rates in Michigan are projected to double. Electric rates in the state are already the highest in the Midwest.

“Michigan’s oil and natural gas industry plays a critical role in powering millions of homes and businesses, supporting hundreds of thousands of jobs and strengthening the state’s economy,” said Chris Zeigler of the American Petroleum Institute, who spoke at the roundtable. “Modern, predictable permitting processes are essential to helping advance critical energy infrastructure projects and improve access to reliable, affordable American energy, and we applaud Congressman Barrett for his leadership on energy issues.”

Background:

The Working Families Tax Cuts Act (H.R. 1) boosted American energy production by authorizing new oil and gas leases and undoing red tape imposed during the Biden administration. The historic law removed subsidies and carveouts for special interests, providing a level playing field to allow companies producing oil, natural gas, wind, solar, nuclear, or other energy sources to compete, innovate, and provide more efficient, affordable energy.

At a time when the ongoing Iran conflict has throttled the worldwide energy market, Barrett has voted three times to end the conflict unless the people’s representatives in Congress provide clear authorization for military force in the region.

title: BEATTY CELEBRATES GROUNDBREAKING OF 166 NEW AFFORDABLE HOMES IN DOWNTOWN COLUMBUS
text:
COLUMBUS, OH — This week, Congresswoman Joyce Beatty (OH-03) joined Columbus State Community College, Woda Cooper Companies, local leaders, and community partners to celebrate the groundbreaking of Opportunity Pointe, a $51 million development that will bring 166 new affordable homes to the Columbus State campus in Downtown Columbus. Additionally, Congresswoman Beatty convened community partners and local leaders for a roundtable conversation on the monumental housing wins included in the recent 21st Century Road to Housing Act and the future of housing reform.

The new development comes as Central Ohio faces an estimated shortage of more than 53,000 affordable housing units and families continue to grapple with housing costs that are rising faster than incomes.

“As Central Ohio grows, affordable housing must be part of that growth,” said Congresswoman Beatty. “Opportunity Pointe is exactly the kind of investment we need. These 166 affordable homes, plus additional units dedicated to Columbus State students, will connect more people to education, jobs, transportation, and opportunity. This project also shows what is possible when federal investment and strong public-private partnerships come together. I’m proud to have fought for the HOME program, Low-Income Housing Tax Credits, and the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act to help communities build more affordable housing and turn projects like Opportunity Pointe from plans into reality.”

Prior to the groundbreaking, Congresswoman Beatty partnered with the Coalition on Homelessness and Housing in Ohio (COHHIO) to convene a roundtable conversation with the following community partners and local leaders. Together, they discussed how the landmark 21st Century Road to Housing Act will increase access to affordable housing across the country and identified key areas for future reform building off of the recent legislative win.

Amy Riegel, Executive Director of the Coalition on Homelessness and Housing in Ohio (COHHIO)

President David Harrison of Columbus State Community College,

Jeffrey Woda, Founder and CEO of Woda Cooper Company,

Amy Rosenthal, Vice President of National Church Residences, and

Carlie Boos, Executive Director of the Affordable Housing Alliance of Central Ohio (AHACO)

This conversation also highlighted the ongoing housing challenges Ohioans face as costs continue to rise and America’s affordable housing supply dwindles — specifically spotlighting the unique challenges of homelessness, affordable campus housing for college students, and the importance of permanent supportive housing.

“Columbus is growing, and we must make sure that growth creates opportunities for everyone. Opportunity Pointe is an important investment in that vision, bringing much-needed affordable housing to our Downtown while giving families, workers and students the opportunity to live close to jobs, education, transportation and other community amenities,” said Mayor Andrew J. Ginther, City of Columbus. “Through strong public-private partnerships like this one, we can continue building a city where everyone participates in and benefits from Columbus’ success.”

“Monday’s roundtable discussion reinforced just how critical it is for communities, policymakers, government officials, the private sector, and other stakeholders to work together to address the growing need for affordable housing. We know that housing affordability affects families, workers, students, seniors, and the economic health of our communities,” said Jeffrey J. Woda, Founder & CEO, Woda Cooper Companies, Inc. “That is why we are especially proud to break ground on Opportunity Pointe here in downtown Columbus. This is what can happen when we come together around a shared vision to make quality, affordable housing more accessible to the people who need it most.”

“Housing costs are increasing faster than incomes. Columbus, and communities throughout Ohio, are seeing the effects of the affordable housing shortage every day, from families struggling to pay rent to shelters operating beyond capacity,” said Amy Riegel, Executive Director, Coalition on Homelessness and Housing in Ohio. “We’re grateful to Congresswoman Beatty and all of her bipartisan colleagues for passing the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act. Now we need to fully implement this legislation to fulfill its potential for expanding access to affordable homes.”

“Opportunity Pointe will meet an urgent need for affordable housing, both for our students and for the broader Central Ohio community,” said President David T. Harrison. “This is a great example of how public-private partnerships can make a difference in people’s lives. Columbus State is proud to partner on this innovative solution to a regional challenge. Along with the YMCA and the recently announced ALDI, we are helping our students with housing, childcare, and food insecurity. These have been longstanding barriers to success for many of our students.”

“OHFA is proud to be a financial partner in Opportunity Pointe through the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit program,” said Bill Beagle, Executive Director of OHFA. “This housing development is a result of the shared vision of the city, Columbus State, and Woda Cooper to increase access to affordable, quality housing in Columbus.”

FEDERAL INVESTMENTS HELPING BUILD MORE HOUSING

Opportunity Pointe is supported in significant part by federal housing investments championed by Beatty in Congress, including funding through the HOME Investment Partnerships Program and Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTC).

Beatty leads the annual congressional appropriations request for the HOME program and has fought to protect and strengthen LIHTC, two critical federal tools that help leverage public and private investment to build and preserve affordable housing.

The groundbreaking also follows enactment of the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, a major housing reform package that includes six bills championed by Beatty.

The legislation provides communities with additional tools to expand housing supply, unlock investment, strengthen housing counseling and financial literacy, support community financial institutions, and make it easier to move affordable housing projects from planning to construction.

Opportunity Pointe represents a public-private partnership among Columbus State Community Partners, Woda Cooper Companies, the City of Columbus, the Ohio Housing Finance Agency, the Columbus-Franklin County Finance Authority, Ohio Capital Corporation for Housing, Rocky Mountain Community Reinvestment Corporation, and other community and financial partners.

title: Congressman Biggs Calls on Governor Hobbs to Give Arizonans Access to Education Freedom Tax Credit
text:
GILBERT, ARIZONA- Today, Congressman Andy Biggs (AZ-05) joined U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon at the East Valley Institute of Technology for a tour and press conference, highlighting the Education Freedom Tax Credit, which was included in the One Big Beautiful Bill signed into law last year.

The Education Freedom Tax Credit provides individuals in participating states with a dollar-for-dollar federal tax credit, up to the applicable limit, for contributions to approved K-12 scholarship-granting organizations. The program gives taxpayers greater control over how their dollars support educational opportunities while expanding choices for students and families.

Scholarship funds can help K-12 students cover a variety of educational expenses, including tuition, tutoring, technology, special education services, and therapies.

States must opt into the program for their students to receive scholarships funded through the tax credit. To date, thirty states—including some led by Democrat governors—have opted into the program. If a state declines to participate, its taxpayers may still claim the federal tax credit, but their contributions will benefit eligible students in participating states rather than students in their own state.

“I was pleased to vote for this tax credit, which expands educational freedom for thousands of parents who want a better education and a brighter future for their children,” said Congressman Biggs. “It’s a win for families, students, and taxpayers—and it was made possible by Republicans in Congress and the Trump Administration.

“Unfortunately, Arizona families are being denied the full benefits of this program because Governor Katie Hobbs has refused to opt our state in,”continued Congressman Biggs. “Because of her failure, Arizona students will miss out on scholarship dollars that could help pay for tuition, tutoring, technology, special education services, and other educational needs. That’s why I’m calling on Governor Hobbs to join the thirty states that have already opted in and give Arizona families access to the Education Freedom Tax Credit. Arizonans should not have to watch their tax dollars create educational opportunities for students in other states simply because their governor refuses to participate.”

title: Bresnahan, Secretary Duffy Push for Infrastructure Improvements at Nanticoke Bridge
text:
Today, U.S. Representative Rob Bresnahan, Jr. (PA-08) welcomed U.S. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy to Northeastern Pennsylvania for a tour of the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton International Airport (AVP) and visit to the Nanticoke Bridge.

“Bridges don’t care if you are a Republican or a Democrat, everyone needs to get from point A to point B,” said Rep. Bresnahan. “Since the Nanticoke Bridge closed, businesses have been cut off, commuters and families are stuck in traffic, and emergency response times have nearly doubled. But this is not an isolated incident; nearly one in four bridges in NEPA have been deemed structurally deficient. That’s why I’m fighting to put more federal infrastructure dollars directly in the hands of local communities. I thank Secretary Duffy for coming to NEPA and seeing firsthand why these investments matter, and I look forward to continuing the fight to keep Pennsylvania moving.”

“The Trump Administration is excited about all the ways transportation infrastructure is being strengthened here in the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton area,” said Secretary Duffy. “From investing nearly $18 million into the air traffic control system and $3 million into family-friendly infrastructure at AVP to meeting with local leaders on the Nanticoke bridge, we’re making sure Pennsylvanians have the state-of-the-art transportation they deserve. Thanks to local leaders like Rep. Bresnahan, the needs of northeast Pennsylvania will not be overlooked.”

The Nanticoke Bridge, which closed to traffic in March 2025, connects the communities of West Nanticoke and Plymouth Township to Nanticoke. While it has the funding necessary to build, the bridge stands empty, awaiting the proper permitting that can take years to be approved.

Nearly 700,000 passengers traveled through AVP last year. While on a tour of the airport, Rep. Bresnahan and Secretary Duffy highlighted the $12.5 billion in air traffic control modernization passed through the Working Families Tax Cuts and the significant technology upgrades coming to AVP.

title: Buchanan Named Most Bipartisan Member in Florida in National Congressional Scorecard
text:
Earns an “A” Grade in Bridge Grades Nonpartisan Congressional Scorecard

WASHINGTON — Congressman Vern Buchanan has earned an “A” grade with a score of 96.9 out of 100 from Bridge Grades, a nonpartisan scorecard that rates members of Congress on their record of bipartisan collaboration. Buchanan’s score is more than double the House average of 44.9 and earns him the title of the most bipartisan member in the Florida congressional delegation.

“Floridians didn’t send me to Washington to fight for the sake of fighting,” said Buchanan. “They sent me to get things done and deliver results for all Americans. For nearly 20 years, I have worked across the aisle for Southwest Florida and this score reflects that approach. I believe in leading bills that bring people together, build coalitions and avoid the personal attacks that get in the way of real progress for our communities.”

Bridge Grades evaluates members of Congress based on their record of introducing and cosponsoring cross-partisan legislation, their public rhetoric around bipartisanship and whether they avoid personal attacks on colleagues, with bonus consideration for political courage and coalition building. Buchanan’s “A” grade places him among the highest-rated members of the House on the scorecard. This grading also earns Buchanan the title of the most bipartisan member of the Florida congressional delegation.

Buchanan has represented Florida in Congress since 2007 with nearly two decades of service marked by a consistent focus on creating real results for all Americans. This work includes bills such as the ASAP Act (H.R. 6130) on Alzheimer’s screening, the SAFE Act (H.R. 1661) on animal welfare, the bipartisan Stop Insider Trading Act (H.R. 7008) and continued work on the Sunshine Protection Act (H.R. 139).

title: Calling upon U.S. Postmaster General SteinerSmith leads push with state and local officials to urge USPS to resolve ongoing postal issues in Jackson Township
text:
Rep. Chris Smith (R-NJ-04) is leading state and municipal officials representing Jackson Township, New Jersey in a new push to address and resolve the ongoing postal service crisis at the Jackson Post Office.

In a joint letter to U.S. Postmaster General David Steiner, Smith and his fellow elected officials—NJ-LD-12 Senator Owen Henry, NJ-LD-12 Assemblymen Alex Sauickie and Robert Clifton, and Jackson Township Mayor Jennifer Kuhn—call attention to the “overwhelming concerns voiced by… the residents and businesses of Jackson Township, [who] have repeatedly expressed frustrations over deteriorating service conditions, unsafe access, excessive wait times,” and inadequacies of the existing facility.

“While the USPS has previously stated that they are aware of and looking into the ongoing challenges facing the Jackson Post Office, these issues have only intensified in recent years, resulting in poor customer service, and above all, serious public safety risks,” said Smith. “As Jackson Township’s population continues to grow, so do the shortcomings and limitations of its only postal facility.”

The letter notes that “Jackson Township is the third-largest municipality in New Jersey by land area, encompassing approximately 100 square miles,” and stresses that the town’s population has grown exponentially in recent decades.

“According to the U.S. Census Bureau, Jackson's population increased from 25,644 residents in 1980 to 58,544 residents in 2020, with more recent estimates placing the population at nearly 61,000 residents,” the officials write. “This growth has been accompanied by continued residential and commercial development, significantly increasing the demand for postal services.”

“The Jackson Post Office has proven to be woefully ineffective in adequately serving the needs of its booming population,” Smith continued. “Postal customers at this facility have been repeatedly subjected to overcrowded conditions, extended wait times, inadequate parking, severe traffic congestion, and insufficient staffing.”

The letter specifically cites eyewitness accounts from Mayor Kuhn, who stated that she “has personally visited [the facility] on numerous occasions and has witnessed firsthand the unsafe conditions created by vehicles backing onto Bennetts Mills Road, traffic congestion extending beyond the property, and residents struggling to safely access postal services.”

These conditions, the lawmakers argue, “create legitimate public safety concerns, not only for postal customers, but also for motorists, pedestrians, emergency responders, and the community as a whole.”

Moreover, the authors of the letter note that Jackson Township was historically served by two postal facilities—the Cassville Post Office, located at 520 West Veterans Highway, and the Jackson Post Office, located at 915 Bennetts Mills Road—that helped distribute customer demand and provided residents in different sections of the municipality with reasonable, effective access to postal services; however, in 2012, the Cassville facility closed its doors, forcing Jackson Township’s tens of thousands of residents to now rely upon a singular, ill-equipped facility for all of their postal needs.

In the conclusion of their letter, the lawmakers call for “decisive action” from the USPS and urge the agency to seriously evaluate:

The establishment of a second, full-service postal facility within Jackson Township to restore adequate access for residents and businesses;

The significant modernization and/or expansion of the existing Bennetts Mills Road facility, including improvements to parking, traffic flow, customer service areas, accessibility, and operational capacity; and

The immediate operational improvements to address staffing levels, customer wait times, and public safety concerns while long-term solutions are being evaluated.

title: Lakewood Alerts article'Congressman Chris Smith Joins Ocean County, Manchester Officials in Strong Opposition to AI Data Centers'
text:
By Lakewood Alerts

Published August 25, 2026

Rep. Chris Smith is joining Ocean County and Manchester Township officials in opposing the development of AI data centers in the area, citing concerns over their potential impact on local resources, the environment and residents.

Smith met Thursday, August 20, with Manchester Township Mayor Joseph Hankins, Public Works Director Al Yodakis and Ocean County Commissioner Rob Arace to discuss their shared opposition to data center development in Manchester Township and across Ocean County.

“AI data centers pose critical environmental risks and impose undue stresses on local resources—including water and electricity—which place significant financial burdens on ratepayers and residents,” Smith said.

Smith also voiced strong support for a recently adopted Ocean County Board of Commissioners resolution encouraging municipalities to conduct comprehensive due diligence and establish appropriate land-use safeguards before approving data center projects. The resolution raises concerns about the environmental and resource impacts associated with the construction and operation of the facilities.

“The people who will have to endure the negative consequences of data center development in their communities deserve to have their voices heard,” Smith said. “The reasonable concerns of local residents must no longer be steamrolled by tech companies seeking profit over Americans’ quality of life—not on my watch.”

title: Texas Port Looks to SMRs
text:
Nuclear Engineering International

August 25th, 2026

Anew US partnership focused on small modular reactor (SMR) technology for maritime applications has been launched by US Secretary of Transportation Sean P Duffy with the Port of Corpus Christi in Texas. Duffy, Maritime Administrator (MARAD) Stephen M Carmel, US Representative Michael Cloud and Port leaders kicked off the initiative which aims to revitalise US shipbuilding, cut fuel costs, and restore US maritime dominance.

It is the second agreement the Department has signed since Secretary Duffy launched the SMR initiative in May. The first agreement was signed by MARAD, the Department of Energy (DOE) and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) in June with the Port of Long Beach in California. That agreement directly complemented a separate lease at the port with BlueCore Energy, a nuclear startup developing floating, barge-mounted SMRs.

The Port of Corpus Christi is the largest US port for petroleum exports and a national leader in liquefied natural gas (LNG) shipments. In the first half of 2026, energy-related cargo movements at the port included 11.5 m tonnes of LNG, a 36.3% increase year-over-year, 17.1m tonnes of refined products, 8.2m tonnes of bulk liquids, 914,606 tonnes of natural gas liquids, and 66m tonnes of crude oil. In June, the port handled 110.3m tonnes of cargoes making the first half of 2026 the best first half of the year in the port’s history.

Through a memorandum of cooperation (MOC), MARAD and the Port of Corpus Christi agreed to work together to explore opportunities to advance maritime energy systems, including through the potential integration of SMR technologies, resilient port microgrids, shoreside power architecture, infrastructure capable of supporting emerging vessel propulsion concepts, and related workforce development opportunities.

“Small modular reactors have the potential to reshape America’s maritime sector, lower shipping costs, and bolster our supply chains,” said Duffy. “I’m thrilled that the Port of Corpus Christi is embracing this exciting partnership with the Trump Administration to ensure the United States leads the way in innovation. Maritime dominance starts with rebuilding America’s fleet with this state-of-the-art technology.”

Maritime Administrator Carmel noted: “This agreement with the Port of Corpus Christi demonstrates that the leading energy port in the nation understands the significance of this technology. SMR integration has the potential to drive down costs and guarantee that our critical Gulf Coast maritime supply chains remain resilient against any contingency, from extreme weather to power grid disruptions, while training the next generation of high-skilled American mariners.”

The four pillars of MOC expand into concrete operational goals: SMR technology integration; resilient port microgrids; shoreside power architecture; and advanced vessel propulsion infrastructure.

SMR technology integration – the primary objective is to evaluate how SMRs can be physically and legally safely housed within a major commercial hub. The port signed a complementary study with UK ship-based nuclear company Core Power to evaluate the feasibility of hosting floating nuclear barges. Power generated from SMRs will support both port operations and the surrounding industrial complex, which is heavily reliant on petroleum and LNG production. Initial phases will map out safety perimeters, emergency handling, and legal compliance required for commercial nuclear facilities.

Resilient port microgrids – major Gulf Coast ports face severe vulnerabilities from weather anomalies and external energy blackouts. The integration of SMRs intends to sever the port’s dependence on the main Texas electrical grid. The targeted microgrid architecture will isolate port power, ensuring critical supply chain operations remain active during hurricanes or regional grid collapses. The baseload power provided by SMRs will ensure steady energy supply required for massive industrial operations.

Shoreside power architecture – “cold ironing” or plugging ships into the port electrical grid while docked, requires vast amounts of clean electricity. The research outlines shore-based support infrastructure needed to service nuclear-powered commercial ships when they call on the port. SMR power grids will connect directly to docks, enabling ships to shut down diesel auxiliary engines and transition to zero-emission shore power smoothly.

Advanced vessel propulsion infrastructure – the ultimate long-term horizon for the Department of Transportation is transforming commercial shipping logistics. The study will examine what a port needs to refuel, service, and maintain civilian vessels propelled by onboard marine SMRs. Rather than immediate deployment, this groundwork maps the future supply chain requirements for a new, modernised domestic merchant fleet. The agreement explicitly outlines joint technical training programmes to educate the next generation of American mariners and port technicians in nuclear maritime tech.

Earlier in August, Core Power issued its response to Marad’s original SMR request for information outlining the company’s Project Pathfinder programme for designing, building, and placing into service a US-flagged nuclear-powered commercial vessel. The Port of Corpus Christi has now signed a memorandum of collaboration with Core Power to study opportunities for firm, reliable power from floating nuclear power plants (FNPPs) and readiness for future calls by nuclear-powered commercial ships.

The study evaluates how a major energy gateway prepares for two distinct scenarios: hosting a FNPP to supply power to the port and region and serving as a safe harbour/gateway for nuclear-powered commercial ships. Core Power will use the busy Texas petroleum and LNG export hub to map out practical requirements such as grid connections, customer needs, predictable transit routes, and berthing arrangements. The initiative aligns with Core Power’s broader Liberty programme, which targets bringing commercial floating nuclear power to the US market by the mid-2030s.

“Port Corpus Christi, as the preeminent energy gateway in North America, is committed to remaining a leader in the global energy marketplace, even as that marketplace expands and evolves, said Jeff Pollack, Chief Strategy & Innovation Officer of the Port of Corpus Christi Authority. This collaboration will help us understand what would be required technically, environmentally, operationally and commercially for floating nuclear power plants and future calls by nuclear-powered commercial ships to be considered in the real-world context of the Port. It is about gathering evidence and keeping our region competitive for future investment, industry, and high-value jobs.”

Core Power CEO Mikal Bøe noted: “Ports are where energy systems and global trade meet. For floating nuclear power plants, we need to understand sites, grids, customers, operating models and long-term service arrangements. For nuclear-powered commercial ships, we need safe and predictable pathways for transit, berthing and routine port operations. Port Corpus Christi gives us a real operating environment in which to assess both pathways separately, but as parts of the complete industrial and regulatory system needed to make maritime nuclear commercially deployable. This is how we move from promising technology to products and infrastructure capable of supporting US energy and maritime competitiveness.”

Core Power said the proposed work covers two related but distinct product pathways. Under the Energy track, the parties intend to assess the site-specific technical, environmental, regulatory, operational and commercial requirements for the potential deployment of an FNPP. The work is expected to consider marine and site conditions, water use and discharge, grid connection, potential customer and offtake requirements, candidate locations and mooring, safety and security, permitting, operations, maintenance and long-term service support.

Under the Propulsion track, the parties intend to examine what would be required for the Port to receive nuclear-powered commercial ships safely and routinely in the future. The work is expected to consider a reference vessel and power-system envelope, transit and berthing, port-stay safety and security, cargo interfaces, emergency preparedness, liability, classification and the roles of U.S. and international maritime and nuclear authorities.

UK-based Core Power formally entered the US market in November 2021 when it established its US subsidiary, Core Power (US) and opened its first American office in Washington DC. This move was specifically designed to begin direct engagement with US maritime and nuclear regulators, such as NRC. Around the same time, Core Power teamed up with major American energy players Southern Company and TerraPower on a Molten Chloride Fast Reactor project, which secured cost-share funding from DOE.

In February 2025 Core Power drastically upscaled its US footprint. At a summit in Houston, Texas Bøe announced a “US-anchored” maritime civil nuclear programme under which the company committed to building its primary manufacturing yard for Floating Nuclear Power Plants (FNPPs) inside the US.

title: Rep. Crank, Colorado Congressional Delegation Urge President Trump to Approve Presidential Major Disaster Declaration Request in Response to Recent Wildfires
text:
COLORADO SPRINGS, C.O. -- Representative Jeff Crank (CO-05) along with the full Colorado Congressional Delegation sent a letter to President Trump urging the President to approve Governor Polis' request for a Presidential Major Disaster Declaration in response to Colorado's Aspen Acres and Gold Mountain Fires.

In June, Colorado experienced two large, destructive fires within 48 hours, the Aspen Acres Fire and Gold Mountain Fire, due to prime wildfire conditions including high winds, extreme heat, and prolonged drought. These fires burned over 140,000 acres collectively across Pueblo, Custer, and Ouray Counties and destroyed hundreds of homes and structures and energy and water infrastructure. The burn scars left by these fires also contributed to significant post-fire flooding and debris flows that led to one fatality in Beulah, Colorado.

Summer is peak tourism season for Colorado, and the fires and subsequent flooding caused major disruptions to transportation, lodging, recreation, hospitality, outfitter, and guide businesses. They also damaged the operations of agricultural producers who lost livestock, fencing, and grazing lands. Several rural communities were also affected by road closures, which made accessing work, school, healthcare, or essential services extremely difficult. State and federal emergency response officials state that they expect disruptions to continue through the remainder of the summer season.

“Successful recovery is essential to restoring the counties’ economies, which depend on clean drinking water, tourism, agriculture, outdoor recreation, and hunting and fishing. Without additional support, residents could face potentially insurmountable barriers to rebuilding homes and businesses, increased drinking water and electric utility costs, and the loss of important habitat and grazing lands. In addition, these communities face ongoing hazards from the post-fire burn scars, including debris, burned trees, and threats to water quality and drinking water infrastructure,” wrote the lawmakers.

“[...] a Presidential Major Disaster Declaration unlocks federal assistance programs, including Hazard Mitigation Assistance Grants, that are indispensable to recovery, mitigation, and long-term resilience. These communities urgently need federal relief to rebuild. We thank you in advance for your expedited review and approval of the Governor’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration,” concluded the lawmakers.

The text of the letter is available here and below.

Dear Mr. President:

We strongly support Governor Jared Polis’ request on August 24, 2026 for a Presidential Major Disaster Declaration with Public and Individual Assistance for Custer and Pueblo Counties, Colorado, in response to the Aspen Acres Fire and Public Assistance for Ouray County in response to the Gold Mountain Fire. Both fires burned during June, July, and August 2026. As part of this request, Governor Polis has also requested the Hazard Mitigation Assistance Grant Program for the affected counties.

In June 2026, extreme heat, prolonged drought, and high winds up to 100 miles per hour contributed to two mega fires in Colorado within 48 hours. The Gold Mountain Fire burned approximately 40,000 acres in Ouray County, Colorado, and the Aspen Acres Fire burned over 102,000 acres across Custer County and Pueblo County, Colorado. Together, these fires destroyed drinking water and electric utility infrastructure, and over 800 structures and 324 homes. The burn scars from both fires contributed to significant post-fire flooding and debris flows that destroyed additional homes, buildings, and electric, water, and transportation infrastructure. On August 16, a significant rain event resulted in one fatality in Beulah, Colorado.

Both fires occurred immediately before the Fourth of July during the summer’s peak tourism season, disrupting lodging, recreation, hospitality, outfitter, and guide businesses. Repeated fire, flood, and debris flow closures have limited visitation and disrupted tourism along the U.S. 550 corridor in Ouray and San Juan Counties, and in Beulah, Rye, and Westcliffe, Colorado. State and federal emergency response officials expect these disruptions to continue through the remainder of the summer season, with flood warnings and business closures continuing to cause cancellations while agricultural producers lose livestock, fencing, and grazing lands. In already isolated rural communities, the ongoing road closures are limiting access to work, schools, pharmacies, medical care, and other essential services.

Governor Polis has requested a Presidential Major Disaster Declaration for the Aspen Acres Fire and Gold Mountain Fire. With over $17 million in validated damages, and with significant gaps in private insurance coverage, the Aspen Acres Fire meets the Federal Emergency Management Administration’s threshold for both Public and Individual Assistance. Losses incurred due to the Gold Mountain Fire meet FEMA’s threshold for Public Assistance.

Successful recovery is essential to restoring the counties’ economies, which depend on clean drinking water, tourism, agriculture, outdoor recreation, and hunting and fishing. Without additional support, residents could face potentially insurmountable barriers to rebuilding homes and businesses, increased drinking water and electric utility costs, and the loss of important habitat and grazing lands. In addition, these communities face ongoing hazards from the post-fire burn scars, including debris, burned trees, and threats to water quality and drinking water infrastructure.

As you are aware, a Presidential Major Disaster Declaration unlocks federal assistance programs, including Hazard Mitigation Assistance Grants, that are indispensable to recovery, mitigation, and long-term resilience. These communities urgently need federal relief to rebuild. We thank you in advance for your expedited review and approval of the Governor’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration.

title: Davids Announces New Grant to Strengthen Olathe Head Start Programs
text:
Today, Representative Sharice Davids announced that the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) has awarded Olathe Public School’s Head Start program with a new federal grant. The $1.9 million award will be used to continue providing early education opportunities and family support services to children and families in the Olathe area.

“These programs provide affordable early education and care that working parents can count on, help children build the skills they need to succeed, and create good-paying jobs for educators right here at home,” said Davids. “Head Start is incredibly important to our community and I am fighting to preserve funding so kids have the resources they need.”

"Olathe Public Schools is proud to have been a Head Start grantee for 65 years," said Dr. Kim Hawkins, Director of Early Childhood, Olathe Public Schools. "The continuation of this funding reflects a longstanding commitment to supporting children and families throughout our community. Through high-quality early learning, strong family partnerships, and connections to important resources, Olathe Head Start helps support the whole child and the whole family. We are grateful for the partnership between Head Start, our school district, and the families we serve, and we are excited to continue building strong foundations for our youngest learners!"

Students in early childhood education programs are 25 percent more likely to graduate high school and are four times more likely to complete a bachelor’s degree in comparison to non-Head Start students. Children in Head Start are also healthier and have better social and emotional skills. In adulthood, statistics show that former Head Start students experience greater economic stability and earn higher wages.

title: Dingell Statement on U.S.-Canada Trade War
text:
U.S. Representative Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) released the following statement in the wake of a growing trade war between the United States and Canada:

“It is a dark moment for our country when the president is more comfortable cozying up to dictators and autocrats than working together to find common ground with our closest friend and ally. Canada and the United States share the longest international border in the world; we are bound together by generations of friendship, family, culture, and common democratic values, and yes, even Great Lakes,” said Congresswoman Dingell. “The values that unite us are stronger than any policy disagreement that divides us. title: Deluzio Presses IRS for Answers on High Call Volumes, Lack of Live Support
text:
CARNEGIE, PA — Today, Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17) shared a recent letter that he sent to the CEO of the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), Frank J. Bisignano, pressing for answers about the wide range of issues Western Pennsylvanians face when trying to contact the agency.

The Congressman and his office hear regularly from constituents receiving notices in the mail that request time-sensitive, personal information. Western Pennsylvanians tell Congressman Deluzio’s team that they face hour-long wait times on the phone or get a message telling them to try again at a different time. This has even prompted some to request time off work in the hopes of finally reaching a live agent on the phone for assistance.

Congressman Deluzio’s letter to the IRS reads, “Constituents receive no answers and waste an unreasonable amount of time trying to fulfill their duties to pay taxes and to address their issues with the IRS.”

The letter continues, “Americans should be able to have their questions answered and receive assistance in a timely manner without spending days and weeks at a time trying to get connected to an agent by phone.”

In his letter, Congressman Deluzio requested information regarding any steps the IRS is taking to address high call volumes, whether the agency is prioritizing automated systems over human agents, and if there are any technology and staffing improvements in the works. He requested a response by September 4, 2026.

Read the full letter HERE.

Congressman Deluzio’s congressional office offers casework services to constituents of Pennsylvania’s 17th Congressional District who have problems and questions with federal programs or agencies. title: Reps. Garamendi, Crow and House Democrats, Demand Trump Administration Reveal True Cost of War with Iran
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman John Garamendi (CA-08), a senior member of the House Armed Services Committee joined Congressman Jason Crow (CO)-06, a combat veteran and Co-Chair of House Democrats’ National Security Task Force, in demanding the Trump Administration provide a full and transparent update to the American people about how much the war with Iran is costing taxpayers.

In a new letter to President Donald Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, the lawmakers demanded an accounting of operational costs placed on the Department of Defense; effects on the oil and energy market; and impacts on inflation, supply chains, and consumer prices, as American families continue to shoulder the cost of this conflict.

Joining Garamendi and Crow in the letter are fellow members of the House Armed Services Committee, like Congressman Derek Tran (CA-45) and Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02), along with 44 other House colleagues.

During a July appropriations hearing, Secretary Hegseth testified that the estimated cost of the Administration’s war with Iran was $37.5 billion. Independent estimates place the figure much higher, surpassing $100 billion. The Trump Administration and Republicans now want Congress to approve another $88 billion funding package for the war.

Working families have been forced to pay more as a result of this war. Energy costs have skyrocketed, making gas, travel, groceries, and goods cost more. If gas prices remain at or above $4 per gallon, which the President has said is “okay” and that he “will never apologize” for, American families will spend at least $90 billion more at the pump this year.

The lawmakers wrote, “What was billed as a two-week operation is now a full-scale war that has lasted for over 150 days, cost over $37 billion, and claimed the lives of 18 servicemembers. At the same time, prices across the country have gone up significantly, placing the burden of this conflict on American families. By June 9, you had claimed that the war in Iran was almost over 38 times. Instead, the war has continued, leaving Americans across the country with no idea when this war will come to an end and when prices will come down. This uncertainty, and the months of higher costs, have taken a toll, impacting Americans’ ability to budget, plan, and save for the future. These costs are untenable, and the American people deserve better.”

To read the full letter, click here.

title: ICYMI: Rep. Grijalva Hosts Town Hall on Border Wall Construction in Ajo
text:

The town hall followed Rep. Grijalva’s site visit to Quitobaquito Springs, a cultural and sacred site in the ancestral homeland of the Tohono O’odham Nation. The area is also home to three endangered species and is at risk of being damaged as the Trump administration prepares for construction of a second meaningless border wall.

“For the Tohono O'odham Nation, this is not just a border. The border cuts through an ancestral homeland that existed long before the United States or Mexico, long before the international boundary was drawn where it is today. It separates communities and families. It makes traditional practices more difficult. It places enormous pressure on lands and places that hold cultural and spiritual significance.” said Rep. Grijalva

During the town hall, Rep. Grijalva announced that she had led a letter with Congressman Raul Ruiz and other border-region Members of Congress to the Department of Homeland Security and the Department of the Interior urging the agencies to suspend construction until meaningful Tribal consultation has taken place.

She also announced plans to introduce legislation that would end DHS’s sweeping authority to waive federal laws to expedite border-wall construction.

title: Rep. Grijalva, Ruiz Call for Immediate Halt to Border Wall Construction on Tribal Lands
text:
TUCSON, AZ — Today, Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva and Congressman Raul Ruiz (CA-25) alongside Representatives Vernonica Escobar (TX-16) and Juan Vargas (CA-52) called on the Departments of Homeland Security (DHS) and the Interior (DOI) to immediately suspend construction of secondary border walls until the federal government has meaningfully consulted with the Tohono O’odham Nation.

“As Members of Congress representing communities along the U.S.-Mexico border, including districts directly impacted by border enforcement operations and infrastructure construction, we write to express our serious concerns regarding the Department of Homeland Security’s (DHS) ongoing construction of secondary border walls. We are deeply concerned by federal government’s failure to meaningfully consult with Tribal Nations regarding projects that may impact sacred sites, cultural resources, and ancestral homelands,” the Members wrote.

The letter also raises concerns about the use of taxpayer dollars on secondary border barriers and urges DHS to pursue more effective, cost-conscious approaches to border security, including modernizing and strengthening ports of entry.

“We are also concerned these projects are wasting an extraordinary amount of taxpayer resources. The overwhelming majority of narcotics interdictions occur at ports of entry, where illicit drugs are typically smuggled through vehicles and commercial cargo rather than between ports of entry. At a time when Congress faces difficult funding decisions, DHS should be able to demonstrate that costly border wall construction is both operationally necessary and a responsible use of taxpayer dollars.”

We urge DHS and the Department of the Interior (DOI) to immediately suspend further construction activities until meaningful government-to-government consultation has occurred with the Tohono O’odham Nation and Congress has received a full accounting of the project’s impacts on Tribal lands, cultural resources, and surrounding communities,” the Members wrote.

The Members’ letter comes in the wake of the destruction of the Las Playas Intaglio, a sacred cultural resource and significant Indigenous site. The incident underscores the urgent need for the federal government to respect Tribal sovereignty and ensure that future border infrastructure projects do not irreparably damage Tribal lands, cultural resources, and sacred sites. Sites like Quitobaquito Springs are already at risk of destruction, making it critical that the federal government take immediate action to protect these irreplaceable places and the Tribal communities to whom they hold deep cultural and spiritual significance.

title: Congressman Rogers Joins State Sen. Stivers & Rep. Wilson to Deliver Infrastructure Funds in Williamsburg
text:
WILLIAMSBURG, KY (August 25, 2026) – U.S. Rep. Harold “Hal” Rogers (KY-05) joined Kentucky Senate President Roberts Stivers and State Rep. Nick Wilson at the Williamsburg Tourism and Convention Center on Tuesday to deliver funding for local infrastructure projects in Whitley County.

Congressman Rogers delivered a $3 million check to Williamsburg Mayor Roddy Harrison and Whitley County Judge Executive Pat White for the water improvement project in Downtown Williamsburg. Congressman Rogers secured the funding through the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Section 531 Program, created exclusively to expand water and wastewater resources in Southern and Eastern Kentucky. When complete, the $15 million project will impact more than 8,800 homes and 460 businesses.

“Just last week, there was a boil water advisory in downtown Williamsburg. This funding will go a long way to eliminate water problems downtown. It will repair and replace deteriorating waterlines and build a new water tank for the city,” said Congressman Rogers, a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee. “Water projects don’t often get big headlines, but strong infrastructure systems are essential to economic development, our schools, our businesses, our homes and our health. I was proud to work with Mayor Harrison and Judge White on this important project in Whitley County.”

“The total project will cost $15 million, but thanks to Congressman Rogers, Sen. Stivers and Rep. Wilson, we already have $9 million covered,” said Williamsburg Mayor Roddy Harrison. “We’ll be able to take care of the citizens of Williamsburg, the University of the Cumberlands, and then out to the county. This is going to make a huge difference without raising any taxes. We can go directly to work on replacing our oldest water lines.”

Sen. Stivers and Rep. Wilson also presented four checks in state funding, including:

$1.5 million to the replace the water tank in Downtown Williamsburg;

$1.5 million to support the renovation and expansion of the local jail;

$950,000 for development of an innovation hub; and

$6.4 million for a runway addition at the Williamsburg-Whitley County Airport.

“I love these big checks because it means we’re getting things done for our community. With support from Congressman Rogers and our state officials, we’re able to do far more than we could on our own,” said Whitley County Judge Executive Pat White. “We’re adding 100 beds onto the Whitley County Detention Center, which will get us close to 300 beds, making it more efficient, and I’m proud to say that construction is moving ahead of schedule. All of these projects are great for our county and our neighbors.”

“These projects come to fruition through thoughtful collaboration between the local, state and federal levels, and strategic investments,” said Sen. Stivers, President of the Kentucky Senate. “We’ve made great strides over the last ten years in the state legislature, allowing us to get better bond ratings, while also reducing state income tax from 6% to 3.5%. The state legislature has created the wave for this growth and prosperity by the policies we have enacted.”

“We have strategically been working on ways to bring more jobs and businesses to our region, and this funding will pave the way for the economic development and innovation we need,” said State Rep. Nick Wilson.

“I’m really proud of the things we’ve been able to do together, across Whitley County,” said Corbin Mayor Suzie Razmus. “Congressman Rogers and our state legislators know how to tackle a problem, and they continue to work with us day after day. I’m grateful for our collective partnership.”

For more information about Congressman Rogers’ work in Washington and at home in Kentucky, visit halrogers.house.gov and follow him on social media.

title: LEADER JEFFRIES ON CNN: “WE’RE GOING TO HOLD THE CROOKS ACCOUNTABLE”
text:
Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries appeared on CNN’s The Situation Room, where he emphasized that with 70 days until the midterm elections, Democrats are committed to lowering the high cost of living and holding Donald Trump and his administration accountable for their unprecedented corruption and extremism.

WOLF BLITZER: Joining us now to discuss this and more in an exclusive interview is the House Minority Leader, Hakeem Jeffries of New York. Leader Jeffries, thank you so much for joining us. Can you explain what was the specific objective of this meeting you had with Jared Kushner in New York?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, good morning, Wolf. Great to be with you. And as we’ve repeatedly indicated as House Democrats, from the beginning of this Congress, we’re committed to pushing back against the extremism that has been unleashed on the American people every day, every week, every month, year after year, until we can end this national nightmare. At the same period of time, of course, we have a responsibility to solve problems, and sometimes that means meeting with people on the other side of the aisle to figure out what the opportunities will be in order to address the things that the American people definitively want us to address, which from our standpoint is the reality that the cost of living in this country is way too high. Far too many people are working hard, they’re playing by the rules, they can’t thrive and they can barely survive. That’s not an acceptable situation, and we’ve got to address that affordability crisis, which is not a hoax. It’s very real. I hear about it every day here in Brooklyn and across the country, and we’re determined to do something about it.

WOLF BLITZER: So did you accomplish anything specific during this meeting with Kushner?

LEADER JEFFRIES: No, it was just a high-level topical conversation, particularly focused on affordability as well as the housing bill that was recently passed and enacted into law as a foundation for the type of thing that perhaps can be built upon moving forward. By the way, that housing affordability bill that ultimately became law, notwithstanding the President’s refusal to sign it, was driven by the strong leadership of Maxine Waters on the House side and Senator Elizabeth Warren on the Senate side of the Capitol, because Democrats are committed to getting things done whenever and wherever possible. At the same period of time, as I’ve mentioned, nobody’s getting a pass because we’re determined to make sure, beginning on day one, that we hold every single member of the Trump cartel accountable beginning on day one.

WOLF BLITZER: Well, beginning on day one, you mean if the Democrats become the majority in the House of Representatives and you potentially could be the Speaker. Is that what you’re suggesting? On day one of that event, you will begin to hold everyone in the Trump cartel, your words, accountable?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, what I’m suggesting is that if folks have been shortchanging the American people, screwing over the American people or stealing from the American people, yes, our commitment very publicly is that we’re going to hold the crooks accountable. We’re going to follow the facts, we’re going to apply the law and we’re going to be guided by the Constitution. Now, that work is going to be led by Jamie Raskin and House Committee Democrats on the Judiciary Committee, as well as Robert Garcia, who’s also doing a tremendous job, and Democrats on the Oversight Committee. But let’s be clear about something. Our commitment to the American people has been we’re going to fight to make life more affordable. We recognize that the cost of living is out of control and we need to lower the cost of groceries, lower the cost of gas, lower the cost of housing. We’re also going to fight to make healthcare affordable for every single American because we recognize that, in this great country, access to high-quality, affordable healthcare can’t simply be a privilege available only to the wealthy, the well-off and the well-connected. It’s got to be a right available to everyone. That’s a principle that unites Democrats all across the ideological spectrum.

WOLF BLITZER: Do you have any plans, at least right now, to start meeting with the White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles or even President Trump himself before the midterm elections in November?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, that depends on what legislative business may be in front of us as it relates to the things that need to be done for the American people prior to the midterms. I haven’t frequently engaged with Susie Wiles, though we’ll see what happens as we move forward in that regard. And of course, Leader Schumer and myself had one high-profile meeting with President Trump in the Oval Office in advance of the 43-day government shutdown, which, by the way, occurred because Democrats have made clear we’re not going to support partisan Republican spending bills, in that instance, that gutted the healthcare of the American people. And we’re going to continue to battle them on tariffs as we’ve done, battle them on Medicaid, battle them on the Affordable Care Act, battle them on Epstein, battle them on ICE funding, battle them on the reckless and costly war of choice in the Middle East and, of course, battle them on the unprecedented corruption that has been unleashed on everyday Americans. But as I travel the country, Wolf, I also know that the American people want us in Washington to solve problems. And I’m not simply here to make a point, but I’m also here to make a difference. And we have a commitment to the American people to make a difference in their lives so that they can live an affordable life, a comfortable life and live a good life, which we know what that should look like—it’s a good-paying job, good housing, good healthcare, good education for your children and, when it’s all said and done, a good retirement.

WOLF BLITZER: I know you’ve argued that Democrats can indeed address the issue of affordability, that crisis that’s unfolding, and take on President Trump’s tariffs while simultaneously conducting oversight of this Trump administration. Let’s watch what you said in a video posted on social media just yesterday. Listen to this.

VIDEO OF LEADER JEFFRIES: No one is going to get a pass. We’re going to hold every single member of the Trump cartel accountable, beginning on day one.

WOLF BLITZER: So what exactly does it mean, and what do you suggest it means when you use the phrase ‘Trump cartel?’

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, listen, Donald Trump has conducted himself like an organized crime boss. These people have unleashed unprecedented corruption on the American people. And here’s our problem with that: that if you’ve got people in high office that are so focused on enriching themselves, their family members, their friends and their donors, then they’re not focused on actually making life better for the American people. And so, our commitment to combating corruption and to holding the crooks accountable beginning on day one is a commitment actually to make sure that we’ve got people in government focused on doing the things necessary to address the affordability crisis, to make sure that healthcare is affordable for every single American, to fix our broken immigration system, to restore the damage that’s been done to voting rights in the United States of America, including by passing the John Robert Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act and, of course, to ending this reckless and costly war of choice in the Middle East, which, by the way, has skyrocketed gas prices on everyday Americans while at the same time putting Iran in a stronger position. So there’s a lot of challenges that we’ll continue to confront as House Democrats through the balance of this Congress and, of course, into the next Congress.

WOLF BLITZER: If you become the Leader or the Democrats become the majority in the House, are you open to pursuing impeachment of President Trump or are you ruling that out?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’ve made clear we haven’t ruled anything in and we haven’t ruled anything out. And certainly, as I’ve indicated, Jamie Raskin and House Judiciary Committee Democrats—I was a proud member of the House Judiciary Committee for 10 years—as well as Robert Garcia and Democrats on the Oversight Committee are going to take the lead. And as we’ve done in the past, whenever there have been moments of accountability that we’ve had to lead on, we are guided by three principles: follow the facts, apply the law and be guided by the United States Constitution.

WOLF BLITZER: On another important issue, Leader Jeffries, you issued a statement yesterday slamming what you called ‘the malicious claim that American Jews are inviting violence against themselves’ as ‘dangerous and antisemitic.’ Was that in reference to far-left influencer Hasan Piker and his recent very controversial comments?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Yes, those comments were dangerous, malicious and antisemitic and should not be tolerated by anyone in the public square. What we’ve seen is a startling rise of hate crimes all across the United States of America, but particularly in this moment directed against our Jewish brothers and sisters. And everybody, regardless of ideological perspective, should be willing to denounce this rise of antisemitic rhetoric, hate crimes and bigotry and actually try to move us to a society where we embrace everyone. Even where there are differences on issues, be they foreign or domestic, the notion that people should be targeted because of their religious beliefs or ethnicity or race, whatever the case may be, that’s fundamentally inconsistent with who we are in this country.

WOLF BLITZER: Yes, indeed. Hasan Piker’s clout among Democrats, though, particularly some younger Democratic voters, seems to be growing. We saw, for example, his prominence in the Michigan Senate Democratic primary. So why not call him out by name in your statement, if you feel so passionately about this issue?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I’ve just addressed Hasan Piker’s comments as it relates to the Jewish community as forcefully as I can, and I will continue to do that.

WOLF BLITZER: Yes, but in your original statement, he was not addressed by name. That’s why I was raising the question. Leader Jeffries, you want to give me a final thought before I let you go? And we’re grateful to you for joining us.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, there are 70 days until the midterm elections, and we’re either going to move the country forward, or we’re going to turn back the clock. And Donald Trump’s administration has been a disaster for the American people. That is clear. And we have an opportunity to take back control of the House and the United States Senate so we can begin the process of ending this national nightmare. And look, our commitment as Democrats is going to be to fight every day, every week, every month to actually address the problems that matter here in this country while pushing back against the extremism that has been unleashed on the American people that’s unprecedented in nature and needs to end.

WOLF BLITZER: And a final thought: will the Democrats be the majority in the House and the Senate?

LEADER JEFFRIES: We have a good chance of taking back both the House and the Senate, but we’ve got 70 days. And we’ve got to knock on every door, we’ve got to encourage everybody to vote. And we’re going to make sure that, notwithstanding the Supreme Court’s efforts, that it’s going to be the American people who decide who’s in the Congress after November 3.

WOLF BLITZER: Leader Jeffries, thanks once again for joining us. Appreciate it very much.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Thank you.

Full interview can be watched here.

title: Krishnamoorthi Condemns Supreme Court Ruling on Trump Mail-Voting Restrictions, Renews Call for Postmaster General Steiner to Resign or Be Removed
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi issued the following statement after the Supreme Court lifted an injunction against President Trump’s executive order restricting mail voting while a separate nationwide injunction remains in effect:

“Today, the Supreme Court’s conservative majority moved Donald Trump one step closer to upending mail voting just weeks before Americans begin receiving ballots. By throwing out the challenge from 23 states and the District of Columbia on standing without deciding whether Trump’s order is lawful, the Court opened the door to forcing states to turn over voter lists and allowing USPS to withhold ballots from eligible Americans who do not appear on them. A separate nationwide injunction still blocks implementation, yet Postmaster General David Steiner has already pushed ahead with rules to carry out Trump’s restrictions despite a federal judge expressly ordering him not to complete that rulemaking. As a senior member of the House Oversight Committee, I am renewing my call for Steiner to resign and, if he refuses, for the Postal Service Board of Governors to remove him. The Postal Service should deliver ballots, not decide who gets to vote, and I will fight every effort by this Administration to disenfranchise the American people.”

title: Krishnamoorthi, Cook County Clerk Gordon, Voting Rights Leaders Highlight Threats to Voting Access Posed by Trump Administration Ahead of November Elections
text:
CICERO, IL — Today, Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi joined Cook County Clerk Monica Gordon and Illinois voting rights leaders at the Cook County Elections Processing Center for a tour and roundtable discussion on threats to voting access and election administration ahead of the November elections.

Congressman Krishnamoorthi, Clerk Gordon, Becky Simon of the League of Women Voters of Illinois, Christian Harris of Common Cause Illinois, and Ed Yohnka of the ACLU of Illinois discussed President Trump’s efforts to restrict mail voting and reports that his Administration could deploy as many as 1,000 Department of Justice personnel in connection with the November elections.

“Donald Trump is trying to seize powers over our elections that the federal government does not have, including turning the Postal Service into a gatekeeper for who receives a ballot,” said Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi. “Our elections belong in the hands of the state and local professionals who administer them, not Donald Trump and his political appointees. I will keep fighting every attempt to interfere with Americans’ right to vote. The Postal Service should deliver ballots, not decide who gets to vote.”

Congressman Krishnamoorthi has led efforts to challenge the Trump Administration’s restrictions on mail voting, repeatedly pressing USPS to comply with federal court orders finding that Congress never gave the Postal Service authority to determine which voters receive mail ballots. Yesterday, he renewed his call for Postmaster General David Steiner to resign after USPS finalized its election-mail rule despite a court order barring him from completing that rulemaking. Following yesterday’s Supreme Court ruling allowing parts of the Administration’s plan to move forward while litigation continues, Krishnamoorthi stressed that the fight is far from over: the Court did not rule that Trump’s restrictions are lawful, a separate nationwide injunction remains in place, and legal challenges to the policy are continuing.

title: LaLota Presents Nearly $1 Million in Federal Funding for Law Enforcement on the South Fork
text:
HAUPPAUGE, NY - On Tuesday, August 25th, Congressman Nick LaLota (R-Suffolk County) presented two checks totaling nearly $1 million to Law Enforcement agencies on the South Fork.

The $782,100 LaLota presented to the Southampton Town Police Department will upgrade technology within its Mobile Command Van to expand the department’s monitoring capabilities and communications during emergencies. The $206,751 he presented to the Village of Sag Harbor Police Department will support vehicle enhancements to give Officers reliable vehicles to carry out their duties.

LaLota secured the funding for these municipalities through the Fiscal Year 2026 Community Project Funding Appropriations process, a discretionary process that allows Members of Congress to direct federal funding toward critical local projects.

“Delivering nearly $1 million in federal funding to the Southampton and Sag Harbor Police Departments strengthens public safety while sparing local taxpayers the expense, which is exactly how I’m making sure Long Islanders send less money to Washington and get more in return,” said Congressman Nick LaLota. “Whether it’s quadrupling the SALT cap to cut the average Long Island family’s federal taxes by about $3,000 or bringing home $27.1 million for public safety, water quality and infrastructure projects across Long Island, I’m focused on my mission to make sure Long Islanders keep and get back more of their hard-earned tax dollars, while seeing those dollars put to work in their communities.”

“My district is completely within the First Congressional District, so every dollar that the Congressman brings home to us, to our local towns and communities, is a dollar saved by our taxpayers. Many people mistake these beautiful, bucolic communities on the east end as a place for the rich and famous, but those aren't the people who typically live here. The people who do certainly need this kind of support,” said Senator Anthony Palumbo.

“Today's a major victory for our taxpayers. Long Island families send a tremendous amount of hard-earned money to the federal government, and today it's about bringing that money back home to New York where it belongs. These federal dollars directly lower the burden on local property owners. Instead of funding these vital upgrades through town taxes, we're utilizing federal money to protect our community,” said Town of Southampton Supervisor Maria Moore.

“I want to thank the congressman for his continued support of the Southampton Town Police Department and public safety in general. And I thank him for allowing us to move forward with this project. Our command van is 25 years old. It's in very sound mechanical condition, and there is no reason to get rid of something that is old but working fine. So, what we plan to do is refurbish it and get equipment where we can serve the community better,” said Town of Southampton Police Chief James Kiernan.

“These federal funds are important to us. They help bridge the gap so the taxpayers are not overburdened. And I just wanted to thank Congressman LaLota for understanding that and for showing support in Washington for the local municipalities and Law Enforcement,” said Village of Sag Harbor Mayor Thomas Gardella.

“Maintaining a safe and reliable fleet is also one of the larger recurring expenses faced by a small municipal Police department. This funding will allow us to replace aging vehicles with modern, reliable Police vehicles while significantly reducing the financial burden that would otherwise fall directly on the taxpayers of the Village of Sag Harbor. And while Sag Harbor may be a small community, demands placed on our department are anything but small,” said Village of Sag Harbor Police Chief Robert Drake.

Background:

The funding is part of LaLota’s broader effort to bring federal resources back to Suffolk County.

title: Congressman Langworthy Announces $20 Million USDA Purchase of Concord Grape Juice Following Advocacy to Support Lake Erie Growers
text:
Washington, D.C.—August 25th… Congressman Nick Langworthy today announced the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s decision to purchase $20 million worth of Concord grape juice, providing critical support to growers across the Lake Erie Grape Belt following months of advocacy urging USDA to intervene in a rapidly deteriorating market.

The USDA purchase comes after Congressman Langworthy pressed Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins to use the department’s authority under Section 32 to conduct a bonus purchase of surplus Concord grape juice to help stabilize the market and protect growers. This is the third federal buyback purchase Congressman Langworthy has facilitated with amounts totaling $85 million.

The Concord grape industry has faced significant challenges following Refresco’s decision earlier this year to cancel grower contracts across Western New York, Pennsylvania, and Ohio. Approximately 126 growers representing roughly 2,600 acres of primarily Concord grapes were impacted, leaving many farmers without a buyer for their crop after making substantial investments to prepare for the 2026 growing season.

“Keeping our Concord grape industry strong and thriving is a top priority, and I am extremely pleased to see USDA take this important step to support our growers,” said Congressman Nick Langworthy. “When Refresco walked away from its contracts, it put hardworking family farmers across the Lake Erie Grape Belt in an incredibly difficult position. I immediately pressed USDA to act, and this $20 million purchase will help provide much-needed stability and relief to growers while reducing excess inventory and strengthening the market. I will continue fighting to make sure our grape growers have the support they need to keep their farms productive and pass them on to the next generation.”

The Concord grape market was already under significant pressure due to declining juice grape consumption, elevated carryover inventories and a large 2025 harvest. Congressman Langworthy’s June letter to USDA warned that without timely intervention, growers could be forced to mothball or abandon vineyards, creating lasting economic consequences for farmers, processors, suppliers and communities throughout the region.

Congressman Langworthy concluded, “The Lake Erie Grape Belt is an important part of our agricultural heritage and a major economic driver for communities across Western New York. Our family farms have weathered difficult markets before, and we are going to do everything we can to make sure this industry has a future here. I appreciate Secretary Rollins and USDA for listening to our concerns and taking action to help our growers.”

title: Lofgren Presents $850k Check to Establish Agricultural Resource Center in Santa Clara County
text:
SAN JOSÉ, CA — Yesterday, Congresswoman Zoe Lofgren (CA-18) visited the Santa Clara County Government Center to deliver a check for $850,000 as one of her 13 community projects she submitted for the Fiscal Year 2026 congressional appropriations cycle. This funding for the County of Santa Clara will be used to establish an Agricultural Resource Center in Gilroy that will provide personal and professional supportive services that address the needs of agricultural workers and their families.

“Agriculture is such a vital part of our regional economy, and it’s important that we’re doing all that we can to support the people working day after day to put food on our tables,” said Rep. Lofgren. “This new resource center in Gilroy is going to help expand opportunity for our ag workforce. I’m proud to select this project for funding this year, and I applaud Santa Clara County for taking the initiative to make sure resources are reaching ag workers."

“Funding for the new Agricultural Resource Center will help our current generation of farmers thrive in delivering locally sourced foods that better serve our communities and our environment,” said Santa Clara County Executive James Williams. "This endeavor by Representative Lofgren demonstrates what is possible when a strong partnership exists between federal elected officials and local governments,” said James R. Williams, County Executive for the County of Santa Clara. “We thank Representative Lofgren for her commitment to the more than 8,000 agriculture workers in Santa Clara County who ensure we have a safe and bountiful food supply, both locally and across the nation.”

“For too long, local farmworkers have been left to fend for themselves in terrible living conditions, without proper health care, and without equal access to the support services that our tax dollars already pay for,” said Supervisor Sylvia Arenas, who represents Santa Clara County’s agricultural heartland in District 1. "That’s why I'm so appreciative of Congresswoman Zoe Lofgren’s partnership and leadership in securing $850,000 in federal funding that will allow us to create an Agricultural Resource Center and provide a lifeline for the farmworkers facing housing insecurity, health inequities, and social hardship in Santa Clara County. As the daughter of farmworkers – I cannot express enough my appreciation for the Congresswoman making this happen for these families.”

The agricultural industry in Santa Clara County employs over 8,000 workers and contributes around $830 million annually to the national economy. Most of the farmland is concentrated in the southern portion of the county, around Gilroy, Morgan Hill, and south San José. This funding will be used to acquire a fixed asset to support the establishment of an Agricultural Resource Center. Services offered at the resource center may include: referrals to external service providers; assistance with completing and filing applications for government programs; and information regarding programs related to labor and employment rights, education, housing, utilities, mental health, immigration, food security, workforce training and education, or childcare assistance.

In addition to securing this funding, Rep. Lofgren has led on agricultural labor issues by introducing the Farm Workforce Modernization Act, a bipartisan bill that reforms the H-2A program to provide more flexibility for employers, while ensuring critical protections for agricultural workers. This legislation was negotiated over nine months with input from employers and the United Farm Workers union, and it passed the House with strong bipartisan support in 2019 and 2021.

Rep. Lofgren has delivered multiple checks this year to community project funding recipients, totaling $64,006,000 across California’s 18th district.
