title: In New Letter, Murray and Senate Democrats Slam the Trump Administration’s Anti-Women Agenda and Threats to Abortion, Reproductive Care
text:
***LETTER HERE***

ICYMI: AtSpotlight Forum on Dobbs Anniversary, Murray Highlights How Republicans’ Efforts to Rip Away Reproductive Health Care Has Harmed Women & Families

Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), a senior member and former chair of the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP), led her colleagues in sending a letter to Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. expressing outrage over the Trump administration’s efforts to ban abortion nationwide and limit access to reproductive health care for women across the country. The senators called out this administration’s harmful restrictions on mifepristone as well as their moves to threaten access to essential preventative care, contraceptives, and abortion care.

“The decades-long Republican attacks on reproductive health, rights, and justice have culminated in a nation where women today have less autonomy over their bodies and their medical care than their grandmothers did,” writes Senator Murray. “And with women already suffering and dying as a result of your policies, you are doubling down with an even more aggressive and dangerous anti-women agenda.”

In the letter, Senator Murray calls out the Trump Administration’s “pro-family” claims, highlighting their hypocrisy. “Despite proclaiming to be a “pro-family” administration, the Trump administration has orchestrated a coordinated attempt to limit access to reproductive health care and move closer to a national abortion ban by whatever means necessary. From partnering with Congressional Republicans to defund clinics that provide preventive care like annual physicals and cervical cancer exams, because they also provide abortion care; terminating women’s health research at the National Institutes of Health; withholding millions in already awarded and appropriated Title X funding, the only federal stream solely dedicated to family planning; to terminating more than 50 Teen Pregnancy Prevention Grants, a program that has shown great success in lowering the teen birth rate; this administration has stopped at nothing to strip access to providers, basic services, and health information.”

Senator Murray continues by outlining the administration’s ongoing attacks on every possible aspect of reproductive health care, including: spreading misinformation, politicizing federal funding and grants, attempting to restrict access to mifepristone, and implementing regulatory strategies that grossly violate women’s privacy and autonomy.

“Women are less safe, less free, and less able to see a doctor today because of the choices this administration has made. Senate Democrats will keep fighting in every way possible to protect every woman’s right to the care they need and the freedom to make their own decisions about their own body and their own future,” Senator Murray concludes.

In addition to Senator Murray, the letter was signed by U.S. Senators Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), John Hickenlooper (D-CO), Edward J. Markey (D-MA), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Adam B. Schiff (D-CA), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Ben Ray Luján (D-NM), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Ron Wyden (D-OR), Angela D. Alsobrooks (D-MD), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Michael F. Bennet (D-CO), Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Richard J. Durbin (D-IL), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Brian Schatz (D-HI), Christopher A. Coons (D-DE), Gary C. Peters (D-MI), Tina Smith (D-MN), Mazie K. Hirono (D-HI), Jack Reed (D-RI), Cory A. Booker (D-NJ), Bernie Sanders (I-VT), and Elizabeth Warren (D-MA).

The full letter is available HERE and below:

Dear Secretary Kennedy,

We write with outrage over the numerous actions taken by the Trump administration to threaten and limit access to reproductive health care for women and girls across the country, including essential preventive care, contraceptives, and abortion care. The decades-long Republican attacks on reproductive health, rights, and justice have culminated in a nation where women today have less autonomy over their bodies and their medical care than their grandmothers did. And with women already suffering and dying as a result of your policies, you are doubling down with an even more aggressive and dangerous anti-women agenda.

The decision in Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization that overturned Roe v. Wade and removed the constitutional right to an abortion has had life-threatening consequences for women across America, especially in states with abortion bans. We know that Republicans’ ultimate goal is to ban all abortions nationwide. Currently, women in 13 states live under total abortion bans and those in 28 other states live under gestational bans, some as early as six weeks—often before a woman even knows she is pregnant. These bans create a system in which women can’t get the health care they need, requiring them to travel across state lines when abortion care via telehealth is unavailable, and in some circumstances forcing them to carry a pregnancy to term. In too many devastating cases, these bans have forced women to wait until their lives are at risk before they can receive adequate care. A 2025 report released by the Gender Policy Equity Institute showed that women living in states that banned abortion were nearly two times as likely to die during pregnancy, childbirth, or soon after giving birth, compared to women living in states where abortion is legal and accessible.

Despite proclaiming to be a “pro-family” administration, the Trump administration has orchestrated a coordinated attempt to limit access to reproductive health care and move closer to a national abortion ban by whatever means necessary. From partnering with Congressional Republicans to defund clinics that provide preventive care like annual physicals and cervical cancer exams, because they also provide abortion care; terminating women’s health research at the National Institutes of Health; withholding millions in already awarded and appropriated Title X funding, the only federal stream solely dedicated to family planning; to terminating more than 50 Teen Pregnancy Prevention Grants, a program that has shown great success in lowering the teen birth rate; this administration has stopped at nothing to strip access to providers, basic services, and health information. Instead, the Trump administration has promoted, through moms.gov, “crisis pregnancy centers” that spread misinformation and employ deceptive practices to further an anti-abortion agenda. People cannot make informed decisions about their bodies if they do not have medically accurate information to begin with, or access to providers who can provide that education. Furthermore, the recently proposed Office of Management and Budget (OMB) regulation on federal financial assistance will politicize the entire grants process, undermining federal agencies’ ability to carry out the programs enacted by Congress and significantly hampering the grantees’ work on programs and services related to women’s and reproductive health. The dismantling and politicization of reproductive health care programs is a thinly veiled attempt at ensuring politicians have even more control over women’s bodies.

The administration has also systematically attacked mifepristone, one of the medications commonly used for abortion care. Mifepristone is safe and effective, has been used for decades by over 7.5 million people since its approval by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in 2000, and is part of the two-drug regimen used in more than 60% of abortions in the U.S. each year. In September 2025, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) announced that it would conduct, through the FDA, “its own review of the evidence” on the safety and effectiveness of mifepristone, despite the overwhelming evidence already proving this. This exercise seeks to disregard the vast safety evidence of mifepristone and further politicize the medication as part of your attempts to limit abortion access nationwide. The Department of Justice has repeatedly cited the FDA’s baseless “review” in ongoing litigation brought by anti-abortion extremists in an attempt to gut access to mifepristone, including in a brief filed at the Fifth Circuit just last month. In November 2025, all Democratic Senators sent a letter to you and then-Commissioner Makary demonstrating our concern over this review and requesting additional information. We have yet to receive a response.

Congressional Republicans and the Trump administration often pretend these restrictions to reproductive health care are designed to give power back to states. However, the Trump administration continues to undermine this argument and attack states that do protect access to reproductive health care. Most recently, the then-Acting Attorney General of the United States, Todd Blanche stated on a private call that the Trump administration’s anti-abortion efforts are “taking longer than we want” and promised that the Department of Justice (DOJ) is working hand in hand with HHS, the FDA, the White House, and President Trump’s team to get permanent solutions. And in Blanche’s July confirmation hearing before the Senate Judiciary Committee, he doubled down on restricting abortion, committing DOJ’s resources to an effort clearly aimed at further limiting access to mifepristone. In March 2026, the Trump administration misused the Weldon Amendment, a harmful refusal of care law, to launch an investigation into 13 states with laws that require state-regulated insurance plans to cover abortion care. In April, the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO), at the request of the Republican Speaker of the House, House Majority Leadership, and other Members of Congress, sent interview requests to a number of states that require abortion coverage in their Affordable Care Act (ACA) Marketplace Plans. If the administration’s goal is to make abortion care a state issue, the federal government should not be interfering and investigating states with lawful abortion protections.

On July 3, the Trump administration released its 2026 Unified Agenda and annual Regulatory Plan. This agenda includes regulatory actions that seek to entrench “fetal personhood,” the idea that fertilized eggs, embryos, and fetuses should receive full rights and legal protections. Granting “fetal personhood” could have enormous consequences, and could ultimately lead to criminal charges and conviction of pregnant and postpartum women for seeking necessary health care.4 The agenda also includes a regulatory action that may roll back access to abortions for unaccompanied immigrant children in detention, a policy that the first Trump administration tried to implement in 2017.5 After legal proceedings, the 2017 policy was eventually abandoned and replaced with a new policy that prohibited the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) staff from interfering with unaccompanied pregnant minors’ access to abortion.

The attacks on reproductive health care don’t stop there. Just last month, on July 7, the Department of Justice asked the Third U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals to allow any employer to opt out of the ACA’s requirement that insurance plans include coverage of the full range of birth control without additional cost, a provision that has helped millions of people to use contraceptives more consistently and effectively, furthering their health and wellbeing. The FDA has also newly imposed a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) on two birth control products, adding new burdensome certification, reporting, and dispensing requirements. Of note, the use of REMS is extremely rare; of the over 20,000 FDA-approved drugs, there are only 73 drugs that have a REMS. This administration has imposed REMS on these products under the guise of ensuring the benefits of the device outweigh its risk of complications, however the agency has failed to answer detailed questions about the research that informed its actions. We believe that, just as politicians shouldn’t be able to make decisions about women’s bodies, neither should their employers. Decisions about birth control, pregnancy, and abortion should be made between a patient and their provider.

If this administration was truly committed to helping families, President Trump would work to lower the cost of living and make health care and child care more affordable and accessible. Instead, the President has stated on the record that we must prioritize “fighting wars” and that we simply cannot afford to address these issues. In fact, in the year and a half they’ve been in charge, President Trump and Congressional Republicans have made the largest cut to Medicaid in our nation’s history. This action directly impacts reproductive health care access for women, as Medicaid pays for more than half of the births in our country and has already led hospitals to close their doors and cut services.

From the moment Donald Trump returned to office, this administration has waged a relentless, coordinated assault on women’s health and the freedom to make their own medical decisions. Stripping away the emergency-room protections that guarantee women can get life-saving care, moving to restrict access to safe and effective medication like mifepristone, gutting the maternal health programs that keep moms and babies safe, and so much else—your policies constitute serious attacks on women’s health that are not rooted in safety or science, but would simply advance an extreme ideological agenda that is wildly out of touch with America’s pro-choice majority.

Women are less safe, less free, and less able to see a doctor today because of the choices this administration has made. Senate Democrats will keep fighting in every way possible to protect every woman’s right to the care they need and the freedom to make their own decisions about their own body and their own future.

Sincerely,

###

title: PHOTOS: Peters Stops in Alpena on Day 2 of 10th and Final Motorcycle Tour
text:
ALPENA, MI – U.S. Senator Gary Peters (MI) stopped at the Thunder Bay National Marine Sanctuary during his annual motorcycle tour across Michigan. Peters, a longtime supporter of the Thunder Bay Marine Sanctuary, highlighted the sanctuary’s importance to local tourism, the regional economy, Michigan’s maritime heritage, and Great Lakes preservation efforts. Peters also received a briefing on the sanctuary’s current research priorities and mapping efforts.

“Thunder Bay National Marine Sanctuary is a critical tourism destination and an integral part of Michigan’s cultural landscape. So, I’m thrilled to be back in Alpena to get an update on the exciting work happening right here,” Peters said. “We must invest in special places like this so that researchers and scientists at Thunder Bay can continue their conservation and research efforts. That's why I've long worked to secure federal funding for the great work done here at Thunder Bay, and I’ll keep pushing to ensure they get the support they need.”

To view photos from Senator Peters’ stop in Alpena, click HERE.

Peters has led numerous efforts to protect and strengthen the Thunder Bay National Marine Sanctuary. Throughout his time in Congress, Peters has secured robust federal funding to enhance the sanctuary’s Great Lakes restoration, mapping, and historical preservation efforts. Peters also led the bipartisan Great Lakes Maritime Heritage Assessment Act to recognize historically significant underwater areas in the Great Lakes as National Marine Sanctuaries, aiming to increase local tourism and boost Michigan’s economy.

Located in Lake Huron, Thunder Bay National Marine Sanctuary was established in 2000 to protect one of the nation’s most historically significant collections of shipwrecks. In 2014, the sanctuary expanded from 448 to 4,300 square miles, making it the nation’s largest marine protected area focused on underwater cultural heritage sites. Within this new boundary, approximately 100 known shipwreck sites exist, while historic research indicates as many as 100 additional sites in the area remain undiscovered.

Peters – an avid and longtime motorcycle rider – kicked off his “Thank you, Michigan” tour in Bay City. After Alpena, he will make stops in Marquette, Traverse City, Grand Rapids, and East Lansing. He will ride more than 1,000 miles across the state on this year’s tour – which is Peters’ 10th and last official motorcycle tour.

“I've always said the best way to travel across our state is on a motorcycle,” Peters said. “Representing Michigan in the U.S. Senate has been the absolute honor of my lifetime. So, this year’s tour is about saying thank you to all of the amazing people and communities I’ve been able to partner with during my career to help make Michigan an amazing place to work, live, and raise a family.”

title: Reed & Magaziner Help Peace Dale Library Write Its Next Chapter with Opening of SK Community Learning Center
text:
WAKEFIELD, RI – After delivering over $3.5 million in federal funding for major upgrades to the Peace Dale Library, U.S. Senator Jack Reed and U.S. Representative Seth Magaziner today joined Governor Dan McKee along with South Kingstown Town officials, project partners, and community members for a special ribbon cutting ceremony for a new community learning center housed within the library.

Located on the upper floor of one of the oldest libraries in Rhode Island, the new learning center utilized $2,893,891 from the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) as well as a $700,000 federal earmark that Senator Reed and Congressman Seth Magaziner secured through the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development’s (HUD) Economic Development Initiative.

The initial federal ARPA funds were allocated to the Peace Dale Library by Governor McKee. As the cost of the project escalated, Reed and Magaziner were able to secure additional federal funds to help take the community project to the ‘next level’ and ensure the underutilized top floor of the library could be renovated to offer brand new community space and resources.

The historic building now known as the Peace Dale Library first opened in 1891 and today serves as the largest and most utilized public library within the South Kingstown library system, which also includes the Kingston Free Library and the Robert Beverly Hale Library.

Blending history with modern amenities, the renovated space preserves the building’s architectural character and original construction while offering tech-equipped workspaces and services. The following new spaces are now open: two new conference rooms; two new study/privacy rooms; a multipurpose use classroom/open space; two counters for individual use; a new second floor Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) compliant bathroom; the Community Paramedic Office; and a new Director’s Office, along with storage. There is also a new stairwell connecting the community learning center area to the parking lot lobby entrance and it is also serviced by an elevator.

The Community Paramedic Program (CPP) is a service provided by South Kingstown Emergency Services to guide patients towards general health and well-being, connect patients with appropriate healthcare services, and provide tele-health, educational or training opportunities.

“Public libraries are about so much more than books. They are places where people can go to transform their lives and this project has certainly transformed this space and added a new chapter to the library’s history. Here, Rhode Islanders can unlock opportunities, discover new passions, and create new connections,” said Senator Reed, the leading Congressional champion of public libraries and a member of the Senate Appropriations Committee, says. “This federal funding will help take patrons of the Peace Dale Library to new heights and hopefully unlock opportunities for learning, growth, and building community.”

“When people have access to quality public spaces, they have more opportunities to learn, grow and connect with one another,” said Rep. Magaziner. “By securing more this federal funding for the Peace Dale Library, we are creating a welcoming space that will serve Rhode Islanders of all ages for generations to come.”

The community learning center renovations began on September 15, 2025 and were completed this month.

Throughout the process, the library placed a great emphasis on respecting, reusing, and restoring the historic character of the building. Parking lot improvements were also made to improve accessibility, which included preserving and moving a historic stone wall.

You do not need to be a South Kingstown resident to use the new library space. All members of the public are welcome.

title: Reed Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton
text:
PROVIDENCE, RI -- Today, U.S. Senator Jack Reed (D-RI) paid tribute to the life and legacy of American music legend Dolly Parton, who, in addition to her career as an entertainer and entrepreneur, was a noted philanthropist, humanitarian, and a champion of literacy and public libraries:

“Dolly Parton will forever be the big-hearted Queen of country music. She truly made the world a better place, sharing her talent and warmth with countless people.

“On stage and screen, Dolly Parton entertained and inspired generations of Americans. She uplifted people and communities through her philanthropic efforts and by serving as a model for kindness, hard work, and bringing people together. She helped kids in Rhode Island and other states through her Imagination Library, which gives free books to families in need.

“Her legacy as an artist is matched only by her legacy for good deeds, caring for others, and bringing out the best in people. She was proud of her humble beginnings and always remained grounded while stressing the importance of education and opportunity for all. She was a great American and her legacy lives on."

According to Dolly Parton’s web site: “When I started the Imagination Library, it was to honor my Daddy. My Daddy was so smart but he felt crippled with the fact that he couldn’t read and write.”

While Parton’s father, Robert Lee Parton, never had a chance to go to school because he had to help his parents make a living for the family, he joined his daughter in launching the program to help others develop a love of reading.

title: ICYMI: Sen. Schiff Joined 30th Annual Lake Tahoe Summit, Underlined Bipartisan Progress in Keeping Tahoe Blue
text:
View the full Summit HERE

Lake Tahoe, CA – In case you missed it, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) joined the 30th Annual Lake Tahoe Summit where he highlighted key priorities to safeguard Lake Tahoe through supporting scientific research necessary to protect the lake, preserving the forests and supporting firefighters, protecting against invasive species and securing consistent and reliable funding for projects across the lake.

“I will be working diligently with my colleagues to continue to bring resources back [to Lake Tahoe] to make sure that these brave firefighters have what they need to do the job and come home safely, that we continue to support all of the good scientific research that is necessary to protect the lake and that we make sure this remains a public-private, nonpartisan partnership for another 30 years,” said Senator Schiff at the Lake Tahoe Summit.

U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.) hosted the summit this year and U.S. Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.) and Alex Padilla (D-Calif.); U.S. Representatives Mark Amodei (R-Nev.-02) and Kevin Kiley (I-Calif.-06); Nevada Governor Joe Lombardo; and Chairman Serrell Smokey of the Washoe Tribe of Nevada and California were in attendance.

Background: Senator Schiff hosted the 29th annual Lake Tahoe Summit, “Protecting Lake Tahoe: Balancing Sustainable Recreation and Conservation,” where he emphasized that protecting the environment, improving fire response, addressing the insurance crisis and balancing outdoor recreation and conservation are key priorities to help safeguard Lake Tahoe. The 29th Summit honored the legacy of former California Senator Dianne Feinstein, who created the Summit in 1997 with former Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid.

Most recently, Schiff, Rosen, Padilla, and Cortez Masto introduced bipartisan, bicameral legislation to deliver more funding to protect the Lake Tahoe Basin with no new costs to taxpayers.

Schiff secured $2.2 million in federal funding for South Lake Tahoe projects that support critical infrastructure development that ensures water sustainability, and for the development of essential affordable housing.

Schiff also led his California and Nevada colleagues in requesting the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) and U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI) ensure Lake Tahoe Basin benefits from the bipartisan Expanding Public Lands Outdoor Recreation Experiences (EXPLORE) Act.

Schiff and Padilla introduced the Golden Mussel Eradication and Control Act of 2026, legislation to expedite the control and eradication of golden mussels – harmful invasive species.

Schiff also secured an increase in the authorization of appropriations for Army Corps Lake Tahoe Basin restoration activities in the 2026 Senate Water Resources Development Act (WRDA) bill from $50 million to $60 million. This bipartisan bill was reported out of committee in July.

title: Schiff, Blumenthal and Welch Demand Answers after DHS Pays $464 million for Luxury Jets and Airplanes via a No-bid Contract with Company Owned by Prominent Trump Supporter
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), and Peter Welch (D-Vt.), today demanded answers from Secretary of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Markwayne Mullin, about DHS’s wasteful purchase of 10 airplanes for $464 million via a no-bid contract. In a letter to Mullin, the Senators called out the Department’s growing and alarming reliance on no-bid contracts since the beginning of the second Trump Administration and raised concerns that the owner of the company that received the award also runs a company alleged to have solicited kickback payments to former DHS official Corey Lewandowski.

“Recent reporting reveals that, beginning in the fall of 2025, DHS pursued and eventually awarded a no-bid contract to purchase 10 aircraft, including three ‘luxury business jets’ and seven ‘Boeing 737 passenger jets,’ and that most of these aircraft have sat idle for months since DHS acquired them. Although DHS claims that the contract was undertaken during Secretary Noem’s tenure, contracting records indicate that the cost of the contract ‘increased by $303 million on the day that Mr. Mullin was sworn in as secretary,’” the Senators wrote.

The Senators continued, “The apparent waste generated by idle, multi-million-dollar government assets belies the Department’s claim of urgency. To date, there is no public indication that any of these aircraft have ever been used for DHS’s claimed purpose of removing noncitizens from the United States. One of the luxury jets was leased to the FBI for use by Director Kash Patel who, in February 2026, incurred estimated costs of $75 million to fly to the Olympic Winter Games in Italy, using the same make of luxury aircraft as the one reportedly leased to the FBI.”

The Senators continued, “DHS purchased the aircraft through a $464 million no-bid contract to Daedalus Aviation Corporation (Daedalus), a Virginia-based company led by chairman William Walters…In fact, Mr. Walters has allegedly created ‘a web of companies,’ that subsequently received government contracts despite having no prior government contracting experience. Companies with ties to Mr. Walters include Salus Worldwide Solutions Corporation (Salus), which, in 2025, received a hastily-awarded contract worth $915 million ‘for air operations to support the administration’s effort to persuade millions of undocumented immigrants to ‘self-deport.’ Public reporting alleges that a representative of Salus repeatedly approached a prospective subcontracting firm with proposals to undertake work for DHS only if the firm would direct millions in kickbacks to Corey Lewandowski or consulting firms connected to him.”

“Congress and the American people deserve the Department’s full and prompt transparency with respect to the shocking waste of taxpayer funds and potential corruption involved in the Department’s aircraft purchase and widespread no-bid contracting,” the Senators concluded.

The full text of the letter can be found here and below.

Dear Secretary Mullin:

We write to request documents and information regarding the Department of Homeland Security’s (“DHS” or “the Department”) purchase of 10 airplanes for $464 million via a no-bid contract.[1] DHS justified this purchase by claiming that these aircraft were urgently needed to operate noncitizen removal flights, but recent reporting reveals that most of these airplanes have sat idle, and one was made available to Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director Kash Patel.[2] That these aircraft have been parked for months or redistributed for purposes inconsistent with DHS’s claimed reason for acquiring the planes significantly undermines the Department’s explanation for bypassing a full and fair competitive contracting process and raises troubling questions about whether DHS overpaid for these aircraft, as well as about the Department’s growing and alarming reliance on no-bid contracts since the beginning of the second Trump Administration. We are also concerned that DHS awarded this no-bid contract to a company led by William Walters. A separate company that Mr. Walters has ties to, engaged in contract dealings with DHS that have raised allegations of solicitation of corrupt kickback payments to former DHS official Corey Lewandowski.

Recent reporting reveals that, beginning in the fall of 2025, DHS pursued and eventually awarded a no-bid contract to purchase 10 aircraft, including three “luxury business jets” and seven “Boeing 737 passenger jets,” and that most of these aircraft have sat idle for months since DHS acquired them. Although DHS claims that the contract was undertaken during Secretary Noem’s tenure, contracting records indicate that the cost of the contract “increased by $303 million on the day that Mr. Mullin was sworn in as secretary.” DHS justified “the enormous price tag” for the aircraft by claiming “it had no time to consider other offers” because “[t]he planes were needed urgently for deportation flights.” The apparent waste generated by idle, multi-million-dollar government assets belies the Department’s claim of urgency. To date, there is no public indication that any of these aircraft have ever been used for DHS’s claimed purpose of removing noncitizens from the United States. One of the luxury jets was leased to the FBI for use by Director Kash Patel who, in February 2026, incurred estimated costs of $75 million to fly to the Olympic Winter Games in Italy, using the same make of luxury aircraft as the one reportedly leased to the FBI.

The waste generated by parking most of these aircraft compounds the loss of taxpayer funds involved in the suspect, no-bid process the Department hurriedly implemented to buy these jets. DHS purchased the aircraft through a $464 million no-bid contract to Daedalus Aviation Corporation (“Daedalus”), a Virginia-based company led by chairman William Walters. Mr. Walters “has emerged as a vocal Trump supporter” who made at least one $10,000 donation to a political action committee supporting former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem during her tenure as governor of South Dakota. Former Secretary Noem and Corey Lewandowki reportedly traveled the country in 2025 on a separate, $70 million luxury 737 MAX 8 that was leased to DHS by a separate company with ties to Mr. Walters, Valkyrie Aviation Holdings Group. In fact, Mr. Walters has allegedly created “a web of companies,” that subsequently received government contracts despite having no prior government contracting experience. Companies with ties to Mr. Walters include Salus Worldwide Solutions Corporation (“Salus”), which, in 2025, received a hastily-awarded contract worth $915 million “for air operations to support the administration’s effort to persuade millions of undocumented immigrants to ‘self-deport.’” Public reporting alleges that a representative of Salus repeatedly approached a prospective subcontracting firm with proposals to undertake work for DHS only if the firm would direct millions in kickbacks to Corey Lewandowski or consulting firms connected to him.

The no-bid contract awarded to purchase these aircraft is only the latest in the Department’s growing abuse of a contracting shortcut designed to meet genuinely urgent necessity. The “urgency exception” permits bypassing full competition only when an agency’s “need for the supplies or services is of such an unusual and compelling urgency that the Government would be seriously injured” unless permitted to move forward on a no-bid basis. Despite the narrow set of circumstances when bypassing money-saving competition might be justified, “[t]he exemption accounts for nearly two-thirds of the $34 billion that [DHS] has spent on contracts signed in 2026,” which “is up sharply from past years.” In 2024, only one percent of DHS contracts were awarded under the urgency exception.

Congress and the American people deserve the Department’s full and prompt transparency with respect to the shocking waste of taxpayer funds and potential corruption involved in the Department’s aircraft purchase and widespread no-bid contracting. Our offices are reviewing allegations of misconduct arising from federal contract awards to assess whether and the extent to which laws and regulations governing honest services and federal procurement may require legislative reform. In order for us to better understand the award of this contract, plans for these airplanes moving forward, and remedial measures for the American taxpayer, please provide the following information by September 7, 2026:

How did DHS initiate conversations with Daedalus to act as broker for the purchase of 10 airplanes?

Which DHS officials were involved in initiating these conversations?

How did DHS ascertain the number and type of airplanes necessary for purchase?

How did DHS evaluate and conclude that purchasing aircraft would be more cost effective than leasing or otherwise engaging a contractor to operate removal flights?

What metrics did DHS evaluate for cost effectiveness before arriving to its decision to purchase these aircraft?

How does DHS plan to use the 10 purchased airplanes moving forward?

How much has DHS spent to store, retrofit, convert, move, and maintain the 10 aircraft since their purchase?

Has DHS implemented changes to its contracting procedures as it relates to the use of exemptions for full and open competition?

Please also provide the following records by September 7, 2026:

All communications regarding the award of the $464 million contract to Daedalus, including but not limited to communications with Daedalus, William Walters, Secretary Mullin, former Secretary Noem and Corey Lewandowski or any of their staff;

All communications regarding the purchase of each individual airplane, including but not limited to communications with Daedalus, William Walters, Secretary Mullin, former Secretary Noem and Corey Lewandowski or any of their staff;

All communications regarding plans for the use of each airplane after purchase;

All flight logs and passenger logs for each airplane purchased under the contract.

Please contact our offices if you have questions about responding to this request. Thank you for your attention to this matter.

title: SCHUMER, AFTER VISITING CHAUTAUQUA COUNTY TO LAUNCH PUSH TO HELP WESTERN NEW YORK GRAPE FARMERS AFTER MAJOR CONTRACTS WERE CANCELED, AND GILLIBRAND ANNOUNCE USDA HAS AGREED TO PURCHASE $20 MILLION IN...
text:
“Bonus Buy” Will Help Local Western NY Farmers After Major NY Grape Processor Abruptly Canceled Contracts Earlier This Year After They Had Already Invested In Preparing Their Vineyards For The Season

Last Week Schumer Stood With Western New York Grape Farmers And Called On USDA To Use Authority To Purchase Excess Grapes For Domestic Food Assistance Programs & Help Keep Upstate Concord Grape Farmers Growing

Schumer, Gillibrand: Grape Purchase Is Win-Win For Local Farmers And Putting American-Grown Grapes To Good Use

After Schumer stood with Western New York grape farmers just last week – after their contracts for this season were suddenly terminated – to call on the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) to purchase Concord grape juice for use by domestic nutrition programs across the country, U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer and U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand today announced the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) has heeded their call and will purchase $20 million in surplus product to ensure the continued success of Concord grape growers in New York. Earlier this year, Refresco suddenly canceled contracts with approximately 126 farmers across New York and Pennsylvania after they had already invested in preparing their vineyards for this season, leaving local growers in a lurch. The senators explained today’s announcement provides much-needed relief for Western New York grape farmers who were facing growing uncertainty amid rising costs and the loss of a major client.

“Everyone knows the best Concord grapes come from Upstate New York. But when Refresco cancelled contracts with many grape farmers earlier this year, growers were left in a lurch with nowhere to sell their harvests. That’s why, last week, I stood shoulder to shoulder with Western New York grape farmers in Chautauqua County and urged the USDA to buy extra Concord grape juice for nutrition programs,” said Senator Schumer. “I’m proud to announce that USDA has heeded my call to purchase Concord grape juice. This is a win for Upstate farmers, families, and New York’s economy. I’ll keep fighting for our growers and a stronger domestic food supply chain.”

“Earlier this year, New York State Concord grape farmers were left stranded after having their contracts suddenly canceled,” said Senator Gillibrand. “That is why I called on the USDA to step in and purchase surplus Concord grape juice for federal nutrition programs. I am thrilled that the USDA answered our call by enacting Section 32 of the Agricultural Adjustment Act to support Western New York’s growers during this critical time. This decision delivers relief to our local farming families and protects a critical part of New York’s agricultural economy."

Chautauqua County is the leading grape-producing county in the state and the largest grape-growing county in the country outside of California. Every year, about 800 growers produce 150,000 tons or more of grapes on more than 22,000 acres on the Lake Erie Plain across northern Pennsylvania and Western New York. Products like juices and jellies that come from Concord grapes are processed locally and sold across the world. The Cornell Cooperative Extension estimates that the Lake Erie Grape Belt region supports about 2,000 jobs, contributes upwards of $300 million in economic impact, and supports a fruit and vegetable processing industry that employs over 5,000 workers.

Western New York’s grape sector is an economic anchor for the state’s agricultural industry, as Lake Erie’s shallow depth extends the growing season by moderating temperatures as it keeps air moving when grapes are at risk for frost. The region extends far beyond Chautauqua County. Niagara County is home to the Niagara Escarpment American Viticultural Area, which contains nearly 60 farms across more than 1,000 acres of vineyard. The Niagara grape was created in Niagara County by cross-breeding Concord and Cassady grapes and is now a staple for making white grape juice.

In March, Refresco, a major processor for many New York grape farmers, canceled all of its contracts with grape growers. Refresco bought from 126 grape growers across New York and Pennsylvania in the Lake Erie region. Since then, New York’s grape growers have been struggling in the face of an uncertain future. In early June, over two months ago, Schumer sent a letter to USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins and explained that purchasing grapes for use by domestic nutrition programs would alleviate stress for Concord grape growers in Western New York.

Section 32 funds, which are the source of funding for the grape buy announced today, are authorized by Section 32 of the Agricultural Adjustment Act of 1933 and used by USDA to purchase agricultural products, which are in turn used for nutrition programs such as the school lunch program. These “bonus buys” have been used by USDA in the past to stabilize agricultural markets, support communities, and deliver nutritious food to those who need it most. In fact, earlier this year, Schumer and Gillibrand fought to secure exactly such a purchase by USDA to stabilize prices for New York grape farmers. Section 32 has also been deployed successfully for Concord grapes in 2006, 2007, 2009, 2014, 2017, and 2024.

title: Sen. Tim Scott supports resolution to celebrate National Park Week
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Senator Tim Scott (R-S.C.) joined Sen. Steve Daines (R-Mont.) in introducing a resolution to designate August 22 through August 30 of 2026 as National Park Week. The Senate passed the resolution by unanimous consent.

“America is the greatest country on earth, and our national parks contribute immensely to that greatness. From the natural beauty of Congaree to the historic grounds of Fort Sumter and Fort Moultrie, South Carolina is home to some of the most beautiful places in God’s creation,” said Sen. Scott. “As we celebrate National Park Week, I welcome Americans across the country to spend time outdoors and learn more about why we are blessed to call this land our home.”

“America’s national parks are true national treasures worth protecting. I’m thrilled to commemorate this week as National Park Week with Senator King. These parks are America’s crown jewels, and we will cherish them for generations to come,” said Sen. Daines.

Congress established Yellowstone National Park as the first national park in 1872. Since then, the United States government has worked to protect and support national parks. In 1916, Congress established the National Park Service to protect and manage the landscapes, battlefields, and historical sites across the country, so that future generations may enjoy them and learn from their rich history.

title: Shaheen Underscores Commitment to Rural Economies at Century-Old Small Business in Intervale, Discusses Conversation Efforts at Loon Preservation in Moultonborough
text:
(Moultonborough, NH) – U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), a senior member and former Chair of the U.S. Senate Small Business Committee, today visited Limmer Boots, a century-old custom bootmaker in the Mount Washington Valley, to highlight her longstanding commitment to helping New Hampshire’s rural entrepreneurs build and grow their small businesses. After, at the Loon Preservation Committee in Moultonborough, Shaheen discussed efforts to restore and maintain a healthy population of loons in New Hampshire.

Photos from today’s events can be found HERE.

At Limmer Boots, Shaheen spoke with employees about the challenges and opportunities facing small rural manufacturers and received a tour of the shop floor to see the process firsthand.

"Since 1919, Limmer Boots has crafted durable boots enjoyed by hikers in New Hampshire and across the country. It was an honor to see the shop floor in action and discuss how we’re working to support rural entrepreneurs at the federal level,” said Senator Shaheen.

Limmer Boots has been the beneficiary of support from the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) and was the SBA’s 2026 New Hampshire Small Business Manufacturer of the Year and New England Rural Business of the Year.

In Moultonborough, Shaheen toured the grounds of the Loon Preservation Committee (LPC) before embarking on a boat tour on Lake Winnipesaukee for loon viewing. During her visit, Shaheen discussed LPC’s efforts to restore and maintain a healthy population of loons throughout New Hampshire.

"Loons are staples of New Hampshire’s iconic wildlife, but they are uniquely vulnerable to human activities,” said Senator Shaheen. “I was pleased to see firsthand the extraordinary work the Loon Preservation Committee is doing to protect loons and their habitats to ensure the beautiful outdoor spaces that make the Granite State so great are enjoyed by generations to come.”

The LPC was created in 1975 in response to concerns about a dramatically declining loon population and the effects of human activities on loons. For over 40 years, the Loon Preservation Committee has undertaken state-wide monitoring, research, management and outreach to preserve loons and their habitats.

title: Welch Hosts ‘Common Grounds with Senator Welch’ Listening Session in Essex County
text:
ISLAND POND, VT – U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.) this morning hosted a ‘Common Grounds with Senator Welch’ listening session at the scenic outdoor pavilion at Lakeside Park in Essex County. Vermonters joined Senator Welch for a discussion about how Washington can work better for the Green Mountain State.

“The world we’re in is completely different than the world we grew up in and that we inhabited only five or ten years ago. You know, we all have political points of view on health care, on the environment, on poverty, on education—and we debate those. But in the past, we also had common reference points—we believed in the rule of law, we believed in courtesy to our neighbors, we believed in free and fair elections and accepted the outcome of those elections. Those days are behind us. And it’s a jump ball as to what happens when we come out on the other side. And that’s the real contest of what’s going on in our country right now. The basic norms that all of us depended on to help us get through our differences have been shattered,” said Senator Welch.

“The biggest challenges that we have here—like health care, housing, education, social media—are not unique to Vermont, and they’re not unique to blue states or red States,” the Senator continued. “They’re shared problems. And in Vermont we look at what the challenges are and we face them together. Sure, we’ll have a debate about how best to address them. But we always start from the proposition that the problems we have to solve are shared, and that we want to solve them for the well-being of our community and for the future of our kids.”

Senator Welch has hosted Common Grounds events in Addison, Bennington, Caledonia, Franklin, Grand Isle, Lamoille, Orange, Orleans, and Windsor counties, and will host listening sessions in every county of Vermont in 2026. title: Bipartisan Members of Congress Call on Commerce Department to Block Americans from Working For Russian and Chinese Intelligence Agencies
text:
Wyden, Cornyn, Welch, Harrigan, Jacobs and McCaul Urge Secretary Lutnick to Implement Rules Passed by Congress in 2022 to Stop American Companies and Citizens from Supporting Intelligence Agencies in Foreign Countries of Concern

Washington, D.C. –Bipartisan members of Congress today called on the Commerce Department to stop American companies and citizens from aiding Russian and Chinese civilian intelligence agencies, by implementing a 2022 bipartisan law that the executive branch has never fully enforced.

U.S. Senator Ron Wyden, D-Ore., Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, Sen. Peter Welch, Rep. Pat Harrigan, R-N.C., Rep. Sara Jacobs, D-Calif., and Rep. Michael McCaul, R-Texas, urged Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to close loopholes in U.S. export control rules that currently allow Americans to work with civilian intelligence agencies in China, Russia and other countries of concern. Without new controls against helping adversary nations, U.S. national security could be at risk.

“As a result, foreign intelligence agencies in many countries can still legally hire consultants in the United States and buy advanced U.S. surveillance, cyber, and artificial intelligence technology, for use in their intelligence operations to target Americans, and operate against American national security and foreign policy interests,” the members wrote.

The Trump Administration imposed export controls on U.S. persons doing business with military intelligence agencies in China, Russia, and other countries of concern in 2021. But the law at the time only allowed such restrictions to be applied to military intelligence agencies. In 2022, Congress closed the civilian intelligence loophole in a 2022 law, allowing the government to impose export controls on foreign civilian intelligence and security agencies too. While the Biden Administration proposed draft regulations imposing export controls in 2024, those regulations were never finalized.

“Implementing these crucial enhancements to fully close this loophole is vital to preventing foreign adversaries from leveraging American tools and expertise against the U.S. government, our citizens and strategic interests,” the members wrote.

The members urged the administration to include recommendations by Wyden, national security and human rights experts, including:

Extending export controls to cover all serial human rights abusers and espionage threats. The country lists proposed by the last administration omitted numerous repressive regimes and nations that conduct espionage against the United States. BIS should establish a “trusted countries list” composed of nations with strong track records of respecting human rights and that do not surveil the United States. A license should be required for U.S. persons to do business with intelligence and security agencies in all countries not on that list

Close due diligence loopholes for private surveillance contractors. Private spyware and cyber-surveillance firms frequently mask their client lists to bypass regulations. BIS must close this loophole by explicitly applying export restrictions to all foreign surveillance technology companies unless they provide their U.S. suppliers with a sworn attestation confirming that their clients do not include any intelligence or security end-users outside the trusted countries list.

Control the export of all biometric surveillance and classification technologies: Although the 2024 draft rule proposed adding facial recognition to the EAR’s Commerce Control List (CCL), oppressive regimes rely on a wider array of digital tracking tools. The final regulations must expand this category to include broader biometric identification technologies—such as gait or cardiac signature recognition—as well as biometric classification technologies used to sort individuals by demographic traits such as race, sex, or ethnicity.

A copy of the full letter sent to the GAO is available here.

title: Wyden, Merkley, Bonamici, Hoyle, Dexter, Colleagues Oppose Rescission of Key Energy Leasing and Public Lands Protections
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley, along with U.S. Representatives Suzanne Bonamici, Val Hoyle and Maxine Dexter, today opposed the recent rescission of two key Bureau of Land Management (BLM) oil and gas rules on leasing and waste prevention that will harm public lands, reduce community input, increase pollution, and raise taxpayer costs.

In the first of two letters, the Oregon lawmakers denounce the BLM’s proposal to rescind the 2024 Fluid Mineral Leases and Leasing Process rule (the 2024 Onshore Leasing Rule).

“[...] BLM’s newly proposed rule threatens to dismantle this common-sense progress. We are deeply concerned that the proposed changes shift cleanup liabilities back to the public, restrict community and private landowner participation, and distort the balance required to manage America’s public lands responsibly,” the Senate and House members wrote to Department of Interior Secretary Doug Burgum.

The 2024 Onshore Leasing Rule ensured that the concerns of states, Tribes, and local communities were included in decision-making and was a long-overdue correction to decades of BLM policies that favored oil and gas development over other uses. This led to tens of thousands of dangerous abandoned wells that became the financial responsibility of taxpayers instead of the oil and gas companies. The 2024 rule had immense public support and established a balanced framework that saved taxpayer money, ensured multiple use management of public lands and protected cultural resources and rural communities that depend on public lands. In their letter, the lawmakers ask that the administration specifically reconsider oil and gas bonding requirements; public participation, Tribal consultation, and landowner involvement; and leasing preference criteria.

The first letter was led by U.S. Senators Michael Bennet, D-Colo., and U.S. Representative Jared Huffman, D-Calif. In addition to Wyden, Merkley, Bonamici, Hoyle and Dexter, the letter was signed by U.S. Senators Ben Ray Luján, D-N.M., Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I., John Hickenlooper, D-Colo., Martin Heinrich, D-N.M., Catherine Cortez Masto, D-Nev., Edward J. Markey, D-Mass., Tammy Duckworth, D-Ill., Jacky Rosen, D-Nev., Cory Booker, D-N.J., as well as U.S. Representatives Yassamin Ansari, D-Ariz., Julia Brownley, D-Calif., Salud Carbajal, D-Calif., Ed Case, D-Hawaii, Steve Cohen, D-Tenn., Diana DeGette, D-Colo., Debbie Dingell, D-Mich., Adelita Grijalva, D-Ariz., Sara Jacobs, D-Calif., Raja Krishnamoorthi, D-IlI., Susie Lee, D-Nev., Mike Levin, D-Calif., Seth Magaziner, D-R.I., Betty McCollum, D-Minn., Dave Min, D-Calif., Joe Neguse, D-Colo., Frank Pallone, D-N.J., Emily Randall, D-Wash., Mary Gay, Scanlon, D-Pa., Lateefah Simon, D-Calif., Paul Tonko, D-N.Y., and Juan Vargas, D-Calif.

The Oregon lawmakers outlined in the second letter their strong opposition to BLM’s proposal to overturn the 2024 Waste Prevention, Production Subject to Royalties, and Resource Conservation rule. The BLM’s reversal of this rule will increase pollution on public lands, reduce domestic energy supply, expose nearby communities to avoidable health risks and waste publicly owned natural gas costing Americans tens of millions in foregone revenue.

“We strongly urge BLM to reject this proposed rescission and maintain the 2024 Waste Prevention rule. The oil and gas resources on these lands belong to the American public and Tribal nations, and they deserve to benefit from the full value and benefits of responsible resource stewardship,” the lawmakers wrote.

The second letter was led by Bennet and Huffman. In addition to Wyden, Merkley, Bonamici, Hoyle and Dexter, the letter was signed by U.S. Senators Luján, Angus King, I-Maine, Whitehouse, Hickenlooper, Heinrich, Markey, and Booker, as well as U.S. Representatives Ansari, Brownley, Carbajal, Sean Casten, D-IlI., Cohen, Jasmine Crockett, D-Texas, DeGette, Dingell, Grijalva, Jacobs, Krishnamoorthi, Magaziner, McCollum, Min, Seth Moulton, D-Mass., Neguse, Pallone, Scott Peters, D-Calif., Randall, Scanlon, Simon, and Vargas.

The text of the letter opposing the rescission of the 2024 Onshore Leasing Rule is here.

title: Smith Urges Admin to Support America's Ranchers
text:
Today, Congressman Adrian Smith (R-NE), a senior member of the House Ways and Means Committee and Chair of the Subcommittee on Trade, released the following statement in response to the Trump Administration’s move to increase foreign beef imports:

Moving forward, I will continue to encourage the administration to pursue policies that give America’s ranchers the assurance they need to make long-term decisions for their operations.”

title: Rep. Aguilar Announces $1 Million for Comprehensive GeoAI Education at San Bernardino Valley College
text:
Press Releases

Rep. Aguilar Announces $1 Million for Comprehensive GeoAI Education at San Bernardino Valley College

The funding will create opportunities for students to train with emerging technology, preparing them to effectively use artificial intelligence in high-demand technical careers.

SAN BERNARDINO, CA – Today, Rep. Pete Aguilar (CA-33) announced $1,000,000 in grant funding for San Bernardino Valley College (SBVC) to enhance the school’s geospatial artificial intelligence (GeoAI) curriculum, which integrates AI tools into geographic information sciences (GIS), ultimately setting up students for successful careers in technical fields. Rodriguez, Chancellor of the San Bernardino Community College District. “We’re grateful to the National Science Foundation for investing in San Bernardino Valley College and supporting this partnership with the University of Redlands and our local K-12 schools. By working together, we can open more doors for students and help prepare the skilled professionals our region and our country will need in the years ahead.”

title: Carbajal Highlights $20 Million Federal Grant for UCSB Advanced Research Lab
text:
On Friday, August 21, U.S. Representative Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24) hosted a press conference at UC Santa Barbara’s (UCSB) OASIS Facility to highlight a $20 million grant from the National Science Foundation (NSF). The NSF grant will go towards UCSB’s COAST PCL, one of 20 facilities in a new national network of programmable cloud laboratories. Carbajal was joined by Dr. Rachel Segalman, Vice Chancellor for Research at UCSB; Dr. Ram Seshadri, Associate Dean for Research in The Robert Mehrabian College of Engineering; Dr. Javier Read de Alaniz, Co-Director of COAST PCL; and Dr. Chris Bates, Co-Director of COAST PCL.

Following the speaking program, Carbajal and the university leaders toured the COAST PCL laboratory.

Download photos here.

The $20 million grant will be used to create a remotely accessible, AI- and robotics-enabled laboratory for discovering new polymers and soft materials. Researchers anywhere in the country will be able to design experiments online, have robots conduct the experiments at UCSB, and receive and analyze the results without having to travel to the university.

The initial research focus will be sequence-defined polymers and biomolecular materials, with potential applications in medicine, energy, electronics, aerospace, and other advanced technologies. Additional background is available here.

“As a proud Gaucho, I am thrilled to highlight this $20 million grant from the National Science Foundation to support UC Santa Barbara’s COAST PCL project,” said Rep. Carbajal. “With this federal investment, UC Santa Barbara will host state-of-the-art programmable cloud laboratories, allowing researchers from across the country to perform experiments completely remotely. The work conducted right here on the Central Coast will revolutionize materials research and lay the foundation for breakthroughs across many industries, from medicine and construction to advanced aerospace and energy technology. I will keep fighting in Congress to bring our tax dollars back home to support world-changing projects like this one.”

"We are grateful to Congressman Salud Carbajal for his unwavering support of UC Santa Barbara and the pioneering research made possible through federal investment," said Rachel Segalman, UC Santa Barbara’s vice chancellor for research and a professor of materials and chemical engineering,” said Rachel Segalman, UC Santa Barbara’s vice chancellor for research and a professor of materials and chemical engineering. “AI is changing how we approach scientific discovery, but it cannot discover new materials on its own. AI needs high-quality experimental data to learn from and validate its predictions. COAST creates a powerful connection between AI, computation and experimentation, allowing researchers to generate new data, learn from it, and move more quickly toward materials that could have applications ranging from medicine and water purification to microelectronics.”

“COAST PCL is a testament to The Robert Mehrabian College of Engineering’s proud tradition of materials discovery,” said Ram Seshadri, the associate dean for research and a distinguished professor of materials, and chemistry & biochemistry. “For decades, our faculty have advanced the fundamental understanding of materials while building a culture of collaboration and shared infrastructure that allows ambitious ideas to flourish. This new investment builds on that legacy and on Dean Umesh Mishra’s vision for OASIS as a bridge between laboratory discovery and real-world impact. COAST PCL will be a key part of realizing that vision and shaping how the next generation of materials are discovered.”

“What excites me most about COAST PCL is the opportunity to rethink how experiments are designed and carried out,” said materials professor Chris Bates, who will serve as co-director of COAST PCL. “By automating workflows and making them remotely accessible, we can move toward a model where sophisticated materials research is available to anyone, anywhere, at any time. That has the potential not only to accelerate discovery, but to fundamentally change how the next generation of scientists and engineers approaches experimentation.”

“COAST PCL is about changing what is possible in materials research. A researcher anywhere in the country will be able to design an experiment remotely, have our automated systems carry it out here at OASIS, and use the resulting data to decide what to test next,” said Javier Read de Alaniz, co-director of COAST PCL and a professor of chemistry & biochemistry. “By combining remote access, robotics, and standardized data, we can accelerate discovery while giving a much broader community of researchers access to capabilities they otherwise might never have.”

title: Smith leads bipartisan congressional letterSmith calls on Pakistan to protect and return abducted Christian woman Neha Faqir to her family
text:
Rep. Chris Smith (R-NJ), the Co-Chair of the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission (TLHRC), today called upon the government of Pakistan to protect the safety and fundamental rights of Neha Faqir, an 18-year-old Pakistani Christian woman, who was allegedly abducted in March and subsequently converted to Islam. A Pakistani court has rejected a petition brought by her family seeking her return.

“The circumstances surrounding Neha Faqir’s disappearance and subsequent conversion raise profoundly troubling questions about her safety, freedom of religion, and ability to exercise her rights without coercion or intimidation,” said Smith.

On August 20th, Smith and ten other Members of Congress sent a letter to Pakistan’s Federal Minister for Law and Justice Azam Nazeer Tarar, expressing concerns over Faqir’s case and urging “the Government of Pakistan to take appropriate action to ensure a just resolution of this matter.”

In addition to Smith, the bipartisan letter was also signed by Reps. James P. McGovern (D-MA), French Hill (R-AR), Gus Bilirakis (R-FL), Andy Harris (R-MD), María Elvira Salazar (R-FL), Riley Moore (R-WV), Randy Weber (R-TX), Michael Cloud (R-TX), Brad Sherman (D-CA), and Blake Moore (R-UT).

In the letter, the lawmakers urge Pakistani authorities to take the necessary steps within their judicial system to “ensure Ms. Faqir’s physical safety and well-being; ensure she has confidential access to independent legal counsel and an opportunity to communicate freely and privately with her family; and ensure that any further judicial proceedings are conducted under conditions that allow her to express her wishes freely and without intimidation or undue influence.”

The Members also refer to Pakistan’s own constitutional protections, including Article 20, which guarantees freedom to profess, practice, and propagate religion, and Article 25, which guarantees equality before the law.

“Pakistan’s Constitution protects religious freedom and equality before the law—but this means little if a young woman cannot safely and freely express her own beliefs,” continued Smith.

“This case is particularly important for Pakistan’s religious minorities, who have been subject to abduction, forced conversion and forced marriage.”

Christian Solidarity International (CSI) brought international scrutiny to Faqir’s case on June 10th, reporting that she disappeared on March 24th after attending a sewing course. She was later found at a madrassa in Lahore, where she had been converted to Islam.

According to CSI, Faqir appeared before the Lahore High Court on June 9. Her family requested an opportunity to speak with her privately, but the request was denied, and the court subsequently rejected the family’s petition seeking her return.

CSI also highlighted Faqir’s case at a June 16th hearing at the Palace of Westminster on coerced conversion and marriage of religious-minority women, sponsored and chaired by Lord Alton.

A leading religious freedom lawmaker, Smith has long raised concerns about the abduction and forced conversion of religious-minority women and girls, as well as the failure of authorities to hold perpetrators accountable.

Smith is the author of the Frank R. Wolf International Religious Freedom Act of 2016 (PL 114-281), which significantly enhanced and upgraded the State Department’s toolkit to better promote and advance religious freedom throughout the globe. In July of 2025, Smith chaired a TLHRC congressional hearing on human rights in Pakistan.

title: Patch article'Data Center Ban Introduced In Manchester'
text:
By Karen Wall, Patch Staff

Published Wed., August 26, 2026 at 5:34 am ET

MANCHESTER, NJ — The Manchester Township Council took the first step to banning artificial intelligence data centers in the township on Monday night with the introduction of an ordinance to do just that.

The ordinance, No. 26-48, was introduced before another overflow crowd that carried dozens of signs and chanted its message: "No Data Centers. No Means No."

The council had been faced with an overflow crowd at the Aug. 10 council meeting, where residents turned out in force because of rumors that a developer had approached the town about building one in the midst of the Pine Barrens.

Of particular concern was an ordinance approved in August 2025 by the council that designated a property owned by the Stavola Corporation off South Hope Chapel Road for redevelopment and included a provision that specifically included data centers as an acceptable use.

(Karen Wall/Patch)

The ordinance introduced Monday night repeals the 2025 measure. It also includes a definitive statement banning data centers in any part of Manchester.

The ordinance is scheduled for a second reading, public hearing and final vote on Sept. 14, township attorney Lauren Staiger said. It will take effect 20 days after publication of the ordinance following the final vote, in early October, Staiger said.

Council President Michele Zolezi announced the repeal ordinance at the start of the public meeting session, after the council returned from executive session discussions.

Mayor Joseph Hankins was absent from the meeting due to a prior commitment in Whiting. Zolezi said he attended the executive session to reiterate his opposition to data centers, which Hankins had expressed in a statement after the Aug. 10 meeting.

"Tonight the Council took an important step toward listening to the concerns our residents have raised," Hankins said after the meeting. "Repealing this provision removes data centers from our redevelopment plan entirely, and reflects our commitment to ensuring that future development in Manchester Township aligns with the character, resources, and priorities of our community."

"I want to thank the Council for their thoughtful consideration and swift action on this issue. Their willingness to listen and respond to the community speaks to their dedication to serving the residents of Manchester Township," Hankins said. "I also want to thank the residents who have shown up to meetings, written letters, and made their voices heard throughout this process. Local government works best when it responds to the people it serves, and this ordinance is a direct result of that engagement."

Hankins and members of the township administration had met with Ocean County Commissioner Robert Arace and U.S. Rep. Chris Smith, who represents Manchester as part of New Jersey's 4th District in the House of Representatives.

"AI data centers pose critical environmental risks and impose undue stresses on local resources — including water and electricity — which place significant financial burdens on ratepayers and residents," Smith said in a statement Monday afternoon. "The reasonable concerns of local residents must no longer be steamrolled by tech companies seeking profit over Americans’ quality of life — not on my watch."

At the meeting, residents applauded the introduction of the ordinance, but some questioned whether it will prevent a developer from getting plans for one in place before the ban takes effect.

Carl Block, Manchester's business administrator, reiterated statements from the Aug. 10 meeting that no plans have been presented to the township for any data center.

He said the 2025 ordinance that addressed redevelopment of the specific site had created the only place in the township where a data center was possible under the township's zoning, and by repealing that ordinance, that option was completely removed because it was specific to the redevelopment.

The ordinance repealing it adds a section completely banning data centers, removing any possibility in the town.

Block also said that the only way a proposal could have been considered is if a developer had filed a complete application for one with the township's planning board. Getting a planning application deemed complete is a process that doesn't happen quickly in the vast majority of cases.

Block also said following the process and the rules for putting the ordinance in place is important, because rushing the process out of fear that someone will try to sneak in a project under the wire would backfire and give the courts reason to reject it.

One man warned that the ban may be put in place, but that it doesn't mean the fight will be over.

"These guys will keep coming at us," the man said, "not just New Jersey, not just Manchester Township, but the whole country."

As happened at the Aug. 10 meeting there was a diverse range of residents who came out in opposition to data centers.

That included the "Jersey Devil," a man who came in costume with a sign urging the council to ban data centers and to protect the Kirkwood-Cohansey Aquifer, a massive underground reserve of freshwater that provides drinking water to millions of New Jersey residents.

At the microphone the man identified himself only as "JD," to the dismay of Zolezi, but he thanked the council for taking the first step to ban the centers.

He then took it a step farther, urging the council to seek more parcels to protect as open space in connection with the Ocean County Natural Lands Trust program, to avoid issues in the future.

The "Jersey Devil" made an appearance at the Manchester Township Council on Monday to advocate for a ban on data centers. (Karen Wall/Patch)

title: Ciscomani Again Recognized Among Most Bipartisan and Effective Members of Congress, Highlights Record of Results for Arizona
text:
Tucson, AZ - U.S. Representative Juan Ciscomani has once again been recognized as one of the most bipartisan and effective members of Congress, earning the highest Bridge Score among Arizona’s congressional delegation. Congressman Ciscomani continues to deliver results for Arizonans on critical issues including water, veterans, public safety, national security, and economic development.

"My focus from day one has been to deliver common-sense, lasting results for my constituents in Arizona’s 6th Congressional District," Ciscomani said. "That means working with anyone willing to find solutions, regardless of party. From preserving our water to protecting public lands and advocating for veterans, my job is to get things done. I'm proud of my record of successfully bringing federal funds to the communities I represent - funds to support our first responders in Huachuca City and Oro Valley, as well as to expand workforce training and improve our roads. These are real wins that will directly improve the quality of life in southeastern Arizona."

This recognition builds on a proven record. During his first term, the nonpartisan Center for Effective Lawmaking named Ciscomani the most effective member of Arizona’s congressional delegation and the 15th most effective member of the U.S. House in the 118th Congress. In the 119th Congress, he earned an "A" grade and a Bridge Score of 97.5 out of 100 from Bridge Grades, placing him among the highest-rated members of the U.S. House. Bridge Grades evaluates members using third-party data focused on bipartisan legislation.

In the 119th Congress, 32 substantive bills were introduced, with nine passing the U.S. House of Representatives, according to the Center for Effective Lawmaking. Legislative efforts have focused on policies that uniquely impact southern Arizona, put veterans first, and address growing concerns about water security.

Among Congressman Ciscomani's key accomplishments, the Chiricahua National Park Act(H.R. 6380) passed the House unanimously by voice vote and advanced through the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee. This legislation would designate Chiricahua National Monument as a national park, preserving one of Southern Arizona’s most treasured landscapes while helping drive tourism and economic opportunity in rural Arizona.

"Washington is full of career politicians who talk a good game about problems but go radio silent when it comes to finding real solutions," said Ciscomani. "The hardworking people I represent deserve leaders who are willing to work with anyone, roll up their sleeves and do what’s necessary to score tangible wins."

Water security remains a central priority. The bipartisan Colorado River Caucus was launched with Rep. Joe Neguse to bring together members from all seven Colorado River Basin states. Bipartisan legislation has advanced to improve federal water monitoring, expand water recycling, and strengthen watershed management, while ensuring Arizona’s fair share of the Colorado River. The WATER Data Improvement Act (H.R. 5770) passed both chambers and was signed into law in 2024. This work has continued during the 119th Congress, with increased support for federal investments in Western water conservation and ongoing collaboration with local, state, and federal stakeholders to address Southern Arizona’s long-term water challenges.

In addition to legislative accomplishments, the congressman is set to secure $42.7 million for 20 federal investments in all five counties of Arizona’s 6th Congressional District: Cochise, Graham, Greenlee, Pima, and Pinal.

title: Representative Ciscomani Highlights $1 Million for Rural Cochise County Law Enforcement
text:
Sierra Vista, AZ - Representative Juan Ciscomani today visited the Cochise County Sheriff’s Office to highlight $1 million in federal funding preliminarily secured to strengthen the department’s communications capabilities and provide local law enforcement with the tools they need to keep Cochise County communities safe.

​The funding would support the purchase of four mobile communications trailers equipped to provide 5G data and P25-compliant radio coverage for Cochise County Sheriff’s Department operations.

Cochise County is home to nearly 126,000 residents, and reliable communication can be challenging for local law enforcement due to the county spanning over 6,000 square miles. These mobile trailers can be moved to wherever they are needed, helping deputies stay connected without the cost of building permanent communications infrastructure. The investment is also expected to save the department approximately $140,000 in annual communications costs.

"I am incredibly proud to be fighting to deliver $1 million to the Cochise County Sheriff’s Department," said Rep. Ciscomani. "Our local law enforcement officers deserve the tools and resources necessary to carry out their mission and keep our communities safe. This targeted investment will improve communications for drone operations, search-and-rescue command and control, and high-definition video surveillance, helping our officers better serve the people of Cochise County. I will always fight for our local heroes, and I am confident this meaningful investment will have a lasting impact on Cochise County residents, visitors, and businesses for years to come."

Cochise County Sheriff Mark Dannels praised Representative Ciscomani’s leadership and partnership in working to secure the $1 million in funding.

"Our office and our entire community is grateful for Representative Ciscomani’s leadership and partnership in working to deliver this $1 million to Cochise County. We saw the need to improve our communications systems, and when we brought that need to Congressman Ciscomani, he didn’t hesitate to make it a priority. We appreciate his efforts to make this investment a reality for our local law enforcement and the people we serve," said Sheriff Mark Dannels.

Prior to his visit to the department, Representative Ciscomani also watched an ATF K-9 demonstration in recognition of National Dog Day which highlighted the vital work K-9 teams in Arizona do to assist federal and local law enforcement and help keep communities safe.

As the only member of Arizona’s congressional delegation serving on the House Appropriations Committee, Representative Ciscomani has made securing federal investments for Arizona’s 6th Congressional District a priority. The $1 million for the Cochise County Sheriff’s Department is part of $42.7 million preliminarily secured for 20 Community Project Funding (CPF) requests across the district.

This builds on the $60 million Representative Ciscomani secured for 28 CPFs between Fiscal Years 2024 and 2026, bringing critical federal investments back to communities across Arizona’s 6th Congressional District.
