title: The Hindustan Times article on Smith-led letter'11 US lawmakers demand Pakistan action after Christian woman "abducted, converted to Islam"'
text:
By Karishma Ayaldasani

Published August 27, 2026, 14:22:12 IST

A bipartisan group of 11 US lawmakers have urged Islamabad to safeguard the fundamental rights of a Pakistani Christian woman who was allegedly kidnapped and converted to Islam.

Neha Faqir, an 18-year-old Pakistani Christian woman was allegedly abducted in March and subsequently converted to Islam. Congressman Chris Smith, the co-chair of the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission, asked the Pakistan government to protect the safety and fundamental rights of Faqir.

"The circumstances surrounding Neha Faqir's disappearance and subsequent conversion raise profoundly troubling questions about her safety, freedom of religion, and ability to exercise her rights without coercion or intimidation," said Smith.

Congressman Chris Smith urged the Pakistani government to protect the safety and fundamental rights of Neha Faqir. (chrissmith.house.gov)

How did the case come to light?

The US reaction comes after Christian Solidarity International (CSI) raised concerns over Faqir's case on June 10 and reported that she went missing on March 24 after attending a sewing course.

Faqir was later found at a madrassa in Lahore, where she had been converted to Islam.

However, a Pakistani court has rejected a petition brought by her family seeking her return.

What US lawmakers said in the letter

Smith, along with ten other members of the US Congress, wrote a letter to Pakistan’s federal minister for law and justice Azam Nazeer Tarar on August 20, expressing concerns over Faqir’s case. They urged the government of Pakistan to take “appropriate action to ensure a just resolution of this matter.”

In addition to Smith, the letter was also signed by Reps James P McGovern, French Hill, Gus Bilirakis, Andy Harris, María Elvira Salazar, Riley Moore, Randy Weber, Michael Cloud, Brad Sherman, and Blake Moore.

The lawmakers also called Pakistani authorities to take the necessary steps within their judicial system to ensure Faqir's physical safety and well-being, and that she has confidential access to independent legal counsel.

They further requested Pakistan to provide Faqir an opportunity to communicate with her family freely and privately. The lawmakers urged Islamabad to ensure that any future judicial proceedings are conducted under conditions that allow her to express her wishes freely, without intimidation or undue influence.

The members also referred to Pakistan’s own constitutional protections, including Article 20, which guarantees freedom to profess, practice, and propagate religion, and Article 25, which guarantees equality before the law.

“Pakistan’s Constitution protects religious freedom and equality before the law—but this means little if a young woman cannot safely and freely express her own beliefs,” Smith added.

He stressed the importance of the case for Pakistan’s religious minorities, who he said, have been subjected to “forced conversions and marriage.”

"This case is particularly important for Pakistan's religious minorities, who have been subject to abduction, forced conversion and forced marriage."

title: 95.9 The Rat article'Manchester Township Introduces Ban on Artificial Intelligence Data Centers'
text:
By J. Mayhew

Published August 27, 2026 at 3:38 PM EDT

Manchester Township Council brought forth an ordinance Monday night. It bans AI data centers in the municipality. The measure, Ordinance No. 26-48, came before a packed crowd who carried signs and chanted "No Data Centers. No Means No."

The ordinance repeals a measure approved in August 2025 that designated a property owned by Stavola Corporation off South Hope Chapel Road for redevelopment. That earlier legislation included a provision listing data centers as an acceptable use.

Council President Michele Zolezi announced the repeal at the start of the public meeting session. Mayor Joseph Hankins was absent due to a prior commitment in Whiting. He attended the executive session to reiterate his opposition.

"Tonight the Council took an important step toward listening to the concerns our residents have raised," Hankins said after the meeting, according to Patch. "Repealing this provision removes data centers from our redevelopment plan entirely, and reflects our commitment to ensuring that future development in Manchester Township aligns with the character, resources, and priorities of our community."

GETTY IMAGES

The ordinance will receive a second reading, public hearing, and final vote on Sept. 14, said township attorney Lauren Staiger. It takes effect 20 days after publication following the final vote in early October.

U.S. Rep. Chris Smith, who represents the area as part of New Jersey's 4th District, issued a statement Monday afternoon supporting the ban. "AI data centers pose critical environmental risks and impose undue stresses on local resources — including water and electricity — which place significant financial burdens on ratepayers and residents," Smith said.

Residents packed the meeting for the second time this month. A packed crowd attended the Aug. 10 council meeting after rumors spread that a developer had approached the town about building a facility in the Pine Barrens.

Carl Block, the township's business administrator, said no plans have been submitted. He said the 2025 ordinance had created the only place where such a facility was possible under zoning rules, and repealing it removes that option completely.

Block said a developer could have moved forward by filing a complete application with the planning board. Getting an application deemed complete is a process that doesn't happen quickly in most cases, he said.

title: Ciscomani Honors Local Heroes at Fifth Veteran Servant Leader Awards, Meets with Veterans Advisory Council
text:
Sierra Vista, AZ - Representative Juan Ciscomani spent time with local veterans this week, holding his fifth Veteran Servant Leader Award Ceremony in Sierra Vista and meeting with his Veterans Advisory Council to provide a legislative update and discuss the unique needs of veterans in Arizona's 6th Congressional District.

"It was an honor to host my fifth Veteran Servant Leader Award Ceremony overall and first in Sierra Vista to recognize 19 incredible veterans for their remarkable leadership, dedication, and continued service, and to award an outstanding civilian who has dedicated years to supporting our local veterans," said Rep. Juan Ciscomani. "The service of these veterans did not end when their time in uniform did. They continued to serve, lead, and make a lasting impact in our communities, and I am proud to recognize their contributions and the role they play in moving Southern Arizona forward. I was also grateful to meet with the Veterans Advisory Council this week to provide them with an update on how I am fighting for our veterans in Congress, and to hear firsthand the needs of our local veteran population. As I prepare to head back to Washington, I look forward to continuing to advocate for the men and women who have sacrificed so much for our country and community."

The congressman's fifth Veteran Servant Leader Awards, and first to be held in Sierra Vista, honored 17 local veterans who served in the Army, Marine Corps, Navy, and Air Force for their continued service and leadership in their communities after leaving the Armed Forces.

The Veteran Servant Leader Award recognizes veterans for their remarkable contributions to their communities and their continued impact in moving Southern Arizona forward. Each honoree received a Veteran Servant Leader Award certificate and a challenge coin from Representative Ciscomani. Additionally, recipients who served in the Vietnam War received a Vietnam Veteran Lapel Pin in honor of their service.

Ciscomani also honored the first recipient of his Veteran Advocate Award, which recognizes civilians for their commitment to supporting and advocating for veterans throughout Southern Arizona.

Following the main Veteran Servant Leader Award ceremony, the congressman recognized two additional veterans who had each been nominated for the award two times but were unable to attend the event. He surprised Dr. Aaron Hannequin and Dr. Victoria Holtz at their Sierra Vista business, Doc’s Watering Hole, to honor both individuals with the Veteran Servant Leader Award and thank them for their tremendous service to our nation and community. With these two veterans being honored, the congressman's Veteran Servant Leader Awards this week recognized a total of 19 veterans.

Sierra Vista Mayor Clea McCaa applauded Ciscomani’s continued leadership and commitment to delivering for local veterans.

"Veterans in Sierra Vista and throughout Cochise County are at the very heart of our communities," said Mayor McCaa. "They play a major role in making this corner of Arizona a great place to live, work, raise a family and do business. I truly appreciate Representative Ciscomani’s leadership in moving the needle for our veterans - from delivering better access to the services they have earned to expanding education and workforce opportunities. He is a champion for our veterans, and it is great to see him making that extra effort to recognize and celebrate their service."

The congressman’s fifth Veteran Servant Leader Awards recognized 20 distinguished honorees:

Mike Rutherford, Civilian, Veteran Advocate Award

Brad Cottrell, U.S. Army

Tom Gross, U.S. Army

Dr. Randy Groth, U.S. Army

Dale Hadfield, U.S. Army

Dr. Aaron Hennequin, U.S. Army

Dr. Victoria Holtz, U.S. Army

Daryl Kling, U.S. Army

Ray Larez, U.S. Navy, Vietnam Veteran

Mayor Clea McCaa II, U.S. Army

Nolan Robert, U.S. Army

Dr. James Perey, U.S. Army

Rodney Preuss, U.S. Army, Vietnam Veteran

David Reno, U.S. Navy

Ron Roberts, U.S. Army, Vietnam Veteran

Wesley Sorce-Zirnheld, U.S. Air Force

Eric Sudhoff, U.S. Navy

Jericho Valle, U.S. Army

Robert Wheeler, U.S. Marine Corps, Vietnam Veteran

Oliver White, U.S. Air Force, Vietnam Veteran

Congressman Ciscomani has held four previous Veteran Servant Leader Awards, in October 2024, April 2025, November 2025, and most recently in May of this year.

In addition to honoring local veterans, the congressman also met with his Veterans Advisory Council this week to discuss the work he is doing in Congress to support and advocate for veterans in Southern Arizona, and to hear firsthand the priorities and needs of the local veteran population.

Ciscomani represents nearly 80,000 veterans in Arizona’s 6th Congressional District and serves on the House Committee on Veterans’ Affairs. Through congressional casework, Ciscomani and his team have returned more than $9 million to local veterans across the district. These funds were owed to veteran constituents but had become stuck in the bureaucracy of federal agencies, including the Department of Veterans Affairs, the IRS, and the Social Security Administration. Ciscomani has worked to cut through red tape, ensuring veterans receive the benefits they have earned.

In the 119th Congress, Ciscomani has introduced three pieces of veterans-focused legislation aimed at improving access to benefits, education, and support for veterans and their families.

The Rural Veterans’ Improved Access to Benefits Act of 2025 (H.R. 3951) expands the types of licensed healthcare professionals who can conduct VA disability examinations and extends that authority through 2031. The legislation reduces travel burdens for rural veterans who lack easy access to VA facilities and passed the U.S. House of Representatives last year.

The VETS Opportunity Act (H.R. 1458) would expand educational benefits under the Post-9/11 GI Bill to include both in-person and partially online, or hybrid, skilled-trade training programs, helping veterans pursue education and training in high-demand vocational careers.

The Prioritizing Veterans Survivors Act (H.R. 1228) would strengthen the Department of Veterans Affairs’ Office of Survivor Assistance, which operates within the Office of the VA Secretary and advocates for veterans’ surviving family members, seeking to ensure that survivors have a strong advocate within the VA.

As a member of both the House Committee on Veterans’ Affairs and the House Appropriations Committee, Representative Ciscomani has a unique opportunity to advocate for veterans through legislation, federal funding, and congressional oversight. His work is directly informed by conversations with veterans across Southern Arizona, helping to ensure their priorities and ideas have a voice in Washington.

title: Rep. Clyde Applauds $93.3 Million Investment to Transform Rural Healthcare Access Across Georgia
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Andrew Clyde (GA-09) applauded the Trump Administration’s announcement that a $93.3 million investment is being delivered to Georgia to help strengthen rural hospitals and improve health outcomes through the federal Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP).

This investment was made possible through Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA), which received Rep. Clyde’s vote and unanimous Democrat opposition, including from Georgia’s Democrat Senators Jon Ossoff and Raphael Warnock. The OBBBA delivered a historic $50 billion investment, known as the Rural Health Transformation Program, to help states modernize rural health.

“I’m deeply thankful for President Trump and his Administration’s implementation of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act’s commitment to invest in and ultimately improve rural healthcare,” said Clyde. “From strengthening the workforce to expanding access to critical care, this investment will make a tremendous impact throughout the Peach State, including in the rural communities across the Ninth District. It’s incredible to see the Rural Health Transformation Program in action, delivering on our promise to make rural America healthy again.”

Background

Today’s announcement, which is just one part of the larger overall funding amount awarded to Georgia for Fiscal Year 2026, completes Georgia’s initial Year 1 award cycle.

Projects supported by this funding include:

Preparing rural hospitals for value-based care: Georgia is supporting 87 rural hospitals with pre-implementation funding to prepare for participation in Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services’ (CMS) AHEAD Model, helping providers build the capacity needed to transition toward more sustainable, accountable models of care.

Strengthening the rural healthcare workforce: Investments are expanding education and training opportunities for nurses, emergency medical technicians, and paramedics, while supporting new approaches to recruiting and retaining healthcare professionals in rural communities.

Expanding access and strengthening the continuum of care: Georgia is investing in telehealth access points, maternal and behavioral healthcare, newborn screening, transportation, and other services designed to better connect rural patients with care.

Modernizing rural healthcare through technology and innovation: Funding is supporting technology-enabled care and infrastructure, including rural hospital cybersecurity, telehealth capacity, surgical robotics, and other tools designed to strengthen rural healthcare delivery and workforce retention.

title: Rep. Cuellar Introduces the Ratepayer Bill of Rights Act of 2026
text:
U.S. Congressman Henry Cuellar, Ph.D. (D-TX-28) introduced the Ratepayer Bill of Rights Act of 2026 earlier this week. Congressman Cuellar’s legislation would require data centers to disclose those demands, protect local water and electric services, and pay the costs created by data center construction and operations.

The legislation would establish ten rights for communities affected by these projects:

1. The Right to Know a Data Center’s Demands.

The public must be told how much electricity and water a covered project expects to use, where those resources will come from, and how demand may grow.

2. The Right to Know the Agreements, Infrastructure Costs, Rate Effects, and Public Support.

Communities must be able to see project agreements, infrastructure costs, possible rate effects, and any taxpayer or public support.

3. The Right to Not Pay a Data Center’s Costs.

Ratepayers cannot be charged for electricity, water, wastewater, infrastructure, mitigation, or related costs caused by a covered project.

4. The Right to Reliable and Affordable Community Water.

A new project cannot come at the expense of dependable and reasonably priced water for the people and businesses already there.

5. The Right to Protection of Rural Water, Aquifers, and Agriculture. Private wells, rural water systems, farmers, and ranchers must receive monitoring, notice, and fair compensation if a project harms their water supply.

6. The Right to Reliable Electricity and Disclosure of On-Site Power and Emissions. Electric reviews would have to confirm the project can be served without materially reducing reliability for existing customers.

7. The Right to Advance Notice, Local Information, and Public Input. Residents and ratepayers must receive advance notice, useful local information, and a public meeting before major commitments are finalized.

8. The Right to Public Information that Cannot be Hidden by Contract. A private agreement cannot conceal information the public is entitled to know. 9. The Right to Protection Against Loopholes and Evasion.

A company cannot avoid the law by dividing one project among separate entities, meters, tenants, parcels, or project phases.

10. The Right to Enforcement, Refunds, and Accountability.

The rules must be enforceable and improper charges to ratepayers must be corrected.

“If a family in Laredo sees a higher utility bill because a billion-dollar project needs a new substation, or a farmer in South Texas loses dependable water without notice and protection, that’s not right,” said Congressman Cuellar. “If the project creates the cost, the project pays the cost. The family ratepayer does not.”

Under the legislation, covered data centers would be responsible for project-driven electricity, water, wastewater, infrastructure, mitigation, and other related costs. Those costs could not be passed on to families and other protected customers through higher utility rates or other charges. The legislation would require independent reviews of a project’s potential effects on local water supplies and electric reliability. Water reviews would consider impacts on households, agriculture, existing businesses, drought conditions, rural wells, and other existing water users. Electric reviews would examine issues including demand, grid reliability, outages, and necessary infrastructure upgrades.

Community members would be required to have ample opportunity to make their voices heard and see their opinions reflected in any project that receives their approval. Relevant information on resource use, costs, public assistance, and potential rate effects would be made available to the public.

“South Texas welcomes economic development and investment, but growth should not mean higher bills for working families or less dependable water for agriculture,” said Congressman Cuellar. “Tell the public what the project will use, protect our water and electric services, and pay the costs your project creates.”

title: Dingell, Lawler Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Expand Sunscreen Access at National Parks

The possible environmental effects of any sunscreen distributed in parks.

“Protecting Americans from skin cancer starts with making basic sun protection readily accessible. I’m proud to lead this bipartisan effort to expand access to sunscreen and other sun-protective measures in our national parks,” said Congressman Lawler, Co-chair of the Extreme Heat Caucus and the Appalachian Trail Caucus.

title: Dingell, Latta Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Reshore American Manufacturing
text:
U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) and Bob Latta (R-OH-05) introduced the bipartisan Biomanufacturing Excellence, Domestic Resilience, Output, and Competitive Know-how Act, or the BEDROCK Act. This legislation would help turn products invented in America into products made in America—supporting American manufacturing jobs, strengthening American supply chains, and reducing American dependence on Communist China.

Biomanufacturing uses biology to make products at industrial scale, such as new materials and medicines. American companies lead the world in discovering these new products, but all too often, the factories, suppliers, and jobs required to produce them at scale move overseas. Communist China has repeatedly made biomanufacturing a national priority; they now dominate the world’s fermentation capacity.

“America's manufacturing might has been hollowed out for decades,” Congresswoman Dingell said. “This bipartisan bill will strengthen and create good-paying jobs, as well as reduce our reliance on China. I am proud to support this effort to invest in America's workers and ensure we do not cede our competitive edge to our adversaries.”

“Northern Ohio knows that manufacturing is the lifeblood of our economy,” Congressman Latta said. “For far too long, America has pioneered new inventions, only for Communist China to build the facilities—stealing the jobs that come with them. The BEDROCK Act would help reshore that work. This bipartisan legislation would create new opportunities for Ohio workers, strengthen the biomanufacturing supply chain, and make it easier for American manufacturers to produce at home.”

The BEDROCK Act would:

Designate a senior Department of Commerce official to lead efforts to strengthen U.S. biomanufacturing competitiveness;

Assess critical supply-chain inputs, domestic production capacity, commercialization barriers, and reliance on China and other foreign adversaries;

Develop a prioritized action plan and consolidate existing federal resources to address the most significant risks and barriers; and

Map federal commercialization processes, establish FDA and EPA points of contact, and publish industry-led practices to help companies scale production.

title: Deluzio, Finstad Reintroduce ‘Water Authority Cybersecurity Protection Act’ Following Recent Hacks on Water Systems Across America
text:
CARNEGIE, PA – Today, Congressman Chris Deluzio (D-PA-17) and Congressman Brad Finstad (R-MN-01) announced the reintroduction of the Water Authority Cybersecurity Protection Act. This now bipartisan bill doubles the amount of funding available in certain grants and technical assistance to local water authorities to strengthen cybersecurity efforts.

Congressman Deluzio first introduced the bill in December 2024 following an Iranian-based hack of the Municipal Water Authority of Aliquippa on November 24, 2023 that suddenly shut down water pressure technologies. Congressman Deluzio led a call for a Department of Justice investigation into the incident.

Since then, hackers have launched cyberattacks on water systems across the country. So far in the summer of 2026, at least 12 states have reported possible cyberattacks to their water systems—with some experiencing flooding and reduced water pressure or going offline completely. At least 100 municipalities have reported potential hacking efforts to their water systems. U.S. intelligence again suggests that Iranian hackers are to blame.

“Any attack on our nation’s critical infrastructure is unacceptable, and the 2023 Iranian hack in Western Pennsylvania should have been a major wake-up call for our federal government,” said Congressman Deluzio. “Especially while the Iran War continues, we need to make sure our local water authorities have the resources and training they need to defend against cyber threats from the Iranians and others. Residents should be able to trust that their drinking water is safe from attacks. I am proud to reintroduce the Water Authority Cybersecurity Protection Act to help local leaders better secure our water system.”

“We have seen far too many instances of cybersecurity threats to our critical water systems,” said Rep. Finstad. “Just this summer, Minnesota experienced over 30 cyberattacks targeting operational technologies that our communities rely on. I am proud to join Congressman Deluzio in introducing this important, bipartisan legislation that will help ensure our local water authorities have the proper capabilities to respond to threats from foreign adversaries."

This legislation would renew the Drinking Water Infrastructure Risk and Resilience Program through 2029 and provide grants to owners and operators of community water systems based on community size. The bill authorizes $50 million each fiscal year to assist local water authorities plan, design, and implement programs for emergency responses. Key among these is improvements for automated and remote systems, and training programs for security and resilience.

The full text of the bill is available here.

title: Edwards Responds to Ethics Committee Findings
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Chuck Edwards sent a letter rebuking the House Ethics Committee's findings that he engaged in sexual harassment and outlining his concerns with the Committee's investigation and conclusions.

In the letter, Edwards directly challenged the Committee's findings and provided his colleagues with his account of the allegations and the context surrounding the evidence and investigation.

The Committee concluded that Representative Edwards did not violate federal sexual harassment law; concluded he engaged in no sexual activity with nor propositioned any staff member; and concluded that the allegations in the matter do not implicate quid pro quo sexual harassment. Yet the Committee used third-party testimony, omitted evidence, and made inferences that his conduct "could" be perceived as something the evidence itself failed to establish.

"Sexual harassment is a serious offense. One that deserves to be defined clearly, investigated fairly, and established by evidence—not inference or speculation. I unequivocally reject the Ethics Committee's findings and its conclusion that I engaged in sexual harassment," said Congressman Edwards. "Those conclusions do not accurately reflect the facts or the full context surrounding these allegations. I sent this letter because every Member of Congress deserved to hear directly from me and have the opportunity to review the facts for themselves."

title: Fedorchak, McMahon spotlight North Dakota model for local education, preview new tax credit
text:
“Sweet Briar School and Bismarck State College serve different students, face different challenges, and succeed in different ways—and that’s the point,” Fedorchak said. “One-size-fits-all solutions for education don’twork. North Dakota parents, teachers, and local leaders know what their students need better than federal bureaucrats in Washington. Secretary McMahon understands that, and I’m grateful she came to see firsthand how local leadership, flexibility, and innovation are preparing our students to succeed."

At Bismarck State College, Fedorchak and McMahon met with students, instructors, administrators, and workforce partners and toured the Polytechnic Institute. Their discussion highlighted BSC’s hands-on approach to education and its partnerships with North Dakota employers to prepare students for high-demand careers. As North Dakota’s polytechnic institution, BSC offers more than 100 certificate, associate, and bachelor’s degree programs. BSC has seen extraordinary growth in recent years, increasing enrollment by 46% since spring 2022.

The visit continued at Sweet Briar School, a rural public school serving students in kindergarten through eighth grade near Mandan. Fedorchak and McMahon visited with teachers, students, and school leaders about the strengths and challenges of rural education and the importance of giving local educators the flexibility to meet the needs of their students.

Secretary McMahon’s visit was part of her nationwide Returning Education to the States Tour. She is visiting all 50 states to hear directly from teachers, parents, students, and community leaders about successful local approaches to education and to identify best practices that can be shared nationwide.

Fedorchak also discussed the implementation of the Education Freedom Tax Credit, which will become available beginning in January 2027. Governor Kelly Armstrong announced in January that North Dakota will participate in the program.

The credit will allow individual taxpayers to receive a dollar-for-dollar federal tax credit of up to $1,700 per year for cash contributions to an approved Scholarship Granting Organization. Those nonprofit organizations will use the contributions to provide scholarships for eligible K–12 students in North Dakota.

Parents can use the scholarships for educational expenses at public, private, or religious schools, including:

Eligible students must be able to enroll in a public elementary or secondary school and come from a household earning no more than 300 percent of the area median income. Scholarship amounts will be determined by participating Scholarship Granting Organizations and are not limited to $1,700.

“This new tax credit will bring more educational opportunities within reach for many North Dakota students,” Fedorchak said. “It encourages private donations that can help families pay for tutoring, special-needs services, technology, career training, tuition, and other educational expenses. Most importantly, it gives parents more freedom to choose opportunities that fit their child.”

Before taxpayers can claim the credit, North Dakota must submit a list of approved Scholarship Granting Organizations to the U.S. Department of Treasury. Treasury is scheduled to release the full list of rules governing the program by the end of September, and Fedorchak is urging them to complete the guidance soon, so the state has time to prepare for the January implementation.Taxpayers may begin claiming the credit for qualifying contributions made in January 2027.

title: Fitzpatrick Introduces Bipartisan American Mariner Tax Fairness Act to Strengthen U.S. Maritime Workforce
text:
Targeted tax relief would help address mariner recruitment and retention challenges and strengthen national readiness

WASHINGTON, D.C. —Today, Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-1), joined by Representatives Tom Suozzi (NY-3), Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11), and Brendan Boyle (PA-2), introduced the bipartisan American Mariner Tax Fairness Act, legislation to strengthen America’s merchant mariner workforce by providing targeted tax relief to qualifying U.S. mariners serving aboard U.S.-flag vessels in international trade.

America’s U.S.-flag deep-sea fleet has declined from roughly 1,100 oceangoing vessels in 1950 to fewer than 200 today, shrinking with it the pool of credentialed mariners available to crew commercial vessels and sustain the sealift capacity our nation depends on. Federal maritime readiness reviews have consistently identified recruitment and retention as a central challenge to maintaining that capability.

“America’s maritime strength depends first on the men and women who crew our ships,” said Fitzpatrick. “Our merchant mariners spend months away from their families doing demanding, essential work that keeps commerce moving and preserves a capability our nation cannot afford to lose. Yet the workforce we depend on is shrinking, and recruitment and retention remain a serious challenge. Good governing means identifying the pressure point and delivering a practical solution. This bill brings greater fairness to the tax code, reflects the realities of service at sea, and helps make these careers more sustainable. If we are serious about strengthening our economy, national security, and America’s maritime future, we have to start with the men and women who make that mission possible.”

“America’s economic and national security depend on a strong maritime industry with skilled mariners to crew our ships. This bipartisan bill recognizes the sacrifices mariners make in entering such a demanding profession by providing targeted tax relief through extending the foreign earned income exclusion to members of this essential workforce. My district is home to the U.S. Merchant Marine Academy and Webb Institute of Naval Architecture, so I know firsthand how vital our mariners are to America’s economy and global security. I’m proud to support the men, women, and legislation that keep our commerce moving,” said Suozzi.

“I’m proud to help lead this effort for mariners in Philadelphia and across the country. America’s merchant mariners are essential to our economy and our national security, and our tax code should recognize the critical role they play. This commonsense legislation will help recruit and retain the next generation of mariners,” said Boyle.

"AMC thanks Congressman Fitzpatrick for his leadership in supporting U.S. Merchant Mariners - the unheralded backbone of American sea power. By offering targeted tax relief for international service, this bipartisan legislation combats our mariner shortage, strengthens the U.S.-flag fleet, and bolsters national security,” said Elizabeth O’Connor, Executive Director of American Maritime Congress.

“Recruiting and retaining mariners is one of the most pressing national security vulnerabilities facing the maritime industry today, and this bill addresses it head-on. The American Mariner Tax Fairness Act simply extends the same treatment already given to other Americans working abroad to mariners sailing in international waters, bringing us in line with how every other major maritime nation treats its seafarers. I want to thank Representatives Fitzpatrick and Suozzi for their bipartisan work in advancing this legislation and delivering on a key objective of a strong U.S. maritime policy,” said Adam Vokac, President, Marine Engineers’ Beneficial Association (MEBA).

The American Mariner Tax Fairness Act would extend the existing foreign earned income exclusion to qualifying U.S. merchant mariners who spend at least 90 days during a 12-month period working aboard qualifying U.S.-flag vessels engaged in foreign trade. The exclusion would apply only to income earned during qualifying periods of service, providing targeted tax relief that better reflects the international nature and unique demands of maritime work while helping address the recruitment and retention challenges facing America’s maritime workforce.

title: Rep. Foster Leads Bipartisan Group to Demand Answers Regarding Insufficient USCIS Correspondence
text:
Washington, DC — Today, Congressman Bill Foster (D-IL) led a bipartisan coalition of 70 Members of Congress in demanding answers from DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) Director Joseph Edlow regarding an alarming pattern in Congressional casework over the past several months.

Despite increased funding for USCIS under H.R. 1, the agency’s correspondence with congressional offices has become increasingly problematic. Congressional caseworkers are receiving responses from USCIS liaison services that reference the wrong constituent or case number, fail to address the questions raised in their inquiries, and provide no clear avenue for staff to ask follow-up questions or request additional information.

Congressional USCIS casework often involves children without a parent or guardian and nowhere to go, spouses who are facing separation, or families that have escaped warfare or other traumatic instability. Additionally, USCIS deals with work permits, meaning insufficient correspondence from the agency impacts local businesses.

In the letter to Secretary Mullin and Director Edlow, the Members wrote:

“Congressional caseworkers have become trapped in a frustrating, never-ending cycle that undermines their ability to effectively assist constituents. The Congressional inquiry process is meant to facilitate communication between USCIS and Members of Congress on behalf of the people they represent.

“When inquiries are met with these inadequate responses—and there is no meaningful avenue for follow-up—that purpose is defeated.”

A copy of the letter and a list of cosigners are available here.

title: Grothman Leads Wisconsin Delegation in Urging President Trump to Approve Major Disaster Declaration
text:
Congressman Glenn Grothman (R-WI) is leading every member of Wisconsin’s Congressional delegation in urging President Donald Trump to approve Wisconsin’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration following the severe storms and tornadoes that struck the state on July 27, 2026.

The storms caused extensive damage across Forest, Outagamie, Vilas, and Winnebago Counties. A powerful EF3 tornado tore through Wisconsin’s Fox Valley region, leaving a broad path of devastation across Appleton, Menasha, Neenah, and Fox Crossing. Preliminary findings from the National Weather Service indicate that the tornado remained on the ground for more than 20 minutes, traveled approximately 12 miles, and reached nearly one mile in width, with estimated winds of 136 to 165 miles per hour. The tornado left thousands of homes and businesses destroyed or severely damaged and caused widespread damage to infrastructure.

Damage assessments conducted by FEMA and Wisconsin Emergency Management found 2,346 residential structures impacted, including 84 destroyed and 412 with major damage, with estimated losses exceeding $8.2 million. Public-sector damage exceeded $13.8 million, surpassing Wisconsin’s per-capita threshold by more than $2.4 million.

The bipartisan delegation is urging President Trump to make Individual Assistance, Public Assistance, and Hazard Mitigation assistance available to affected Wisconsinites.

title: Harshbarger Introduces Legislation to End Federal Ban on Home Distillation
text:
Image

Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Diana Harshbarger (R-TN) today introduced the Freedom to Home Distill Act, legislation that would end the federal prohibition on home distillation and extend to distillers the same tax-free, personal-use exemption that home brewers of beer and wine have enjoyed since Congress updated the tax code in 1978.

“It makes no sense that Americans can legally make beer and wine at home for personal consumption, but not a small batch of spirits,” said Congresswoman Diana Harshbarger. “Distilling has deep roots in Tennessee and across Appalachia, tied to self-reliance and craftsmanship that go back generations. It's long past time we modernize this outdated federal law. My bill restores an important piece of that tradition and puts personal responsibility back where it belongs: with the American people.”

Image

Eric “Digger” Manes, star of the reality television series Moonshiners on the Discovery Channel and native of Tennessee’s First Congressional District:

“It would be an understatement to say that it was an honor to be involved in authoring the Freedom to Home Distill Act. When I initially approached Congresswoman Diana Harshbarger to explore the possibility of introducing a bill that would allow hobby distillers to engage in their craft without the fear of law enforcement intervention, it was a monumental step. The apprehension of prosecution has been a persistent concern for illegal distillers since George Washington participated in the same process that is now being carried out in these Appalachian hills. My hope is that everyone who reads this will contact their federal representatives, regardless of whether they intend to pursue the hobby themselves, and request their support for this bill. Given that multiple states have legalized marijuana, it appears logical that we should be permitted to engage in our hobby without facing repercussions. Congresswoman Harshbarger has dedicated three years of research and effort to the development of this bill solely because one of her constituents inquired about her interest in becoming a hero to four million citizens. The moonshine community cannot express its gratitude enough to Representative Diana Harshbarger!”

Reps. Tim Burchett (R-TN) and Riley Moore (R-WV) joined as original cosponsors.

“Nationwide prohibition ended nearly a century ago, yet the federal government continues to regulate domestic distilling operations. There is no reason to keep antiquated and inefficient laws on the books, nor is there any reason that this should not be state-level issue. I support the “Freedom to Home Distill Act” and any legislation that reduces red-tape and strengthens individual liberties,” said Congressman Tim Burchett.

“West Virginia has a proud tradition of craftsmanship, independence, and yes, moonshining. The federal government shouldn’t stand in the way of responsible adults distilling spirits for personal use in their own homes. The Freedom to Home Distill Act is a commonsense bill that protects Americans’ individual liberties,” said Congressman Riley Moore.

BACKGROUND:

Under current law, home brewers can produce up to 200 gallons of beer or wine per household each year tax-free for personal use. Home distillation of spirits, however, remains fully banned under federal law. The restriction predates Prohibition by more than 50 years and has not been substantively updated since, even as commercial distilling has grown into a legitimate and expanding industry.

The Freedom to Home Distill Act:

Creates a tax exemption for spirits produced at a qualifying home distillery, defined as a private residence, or a connected shed, yard or enclosure, used solely for personal or family consumption.

Sets production limits mirroring current homebrewing limits: up to 10 proof gallons per year for single-adult households and up to 20 proof gallons per year for households with two or more adults age 21 or older.

Prohibits any sale or transfer for sale of home-distilled spirits.

Exempts qualifying home stills from federal registration and notice requirements, provided the equipment has a pressure release and vacuum relief valve and a capacity no greater than 50 gallons.

Removes criminal penalties under the tax code for distilling within a qualifying home distillery establishment.

Preserves state authority. The bill applies only to federal law, and states retain full power to regulate or prohibit home distillation as they choose.

title: Huffman, Dexter Demand Records from Corporate Sponsors of Freedom 250
text:
Letters to 23 sponsors and partners follow interim report finding the White House turned the nation’s 250th birthday into a fundraising operation for the President

Washington, D.C. – Today, House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.) and Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee Ranking Member Maxine Dexter (D-Ore.) sent letters to 23 corporate sponsors and partners of Freedom 250, LLC, demanding documents and communications related to their donations to the entity at the center of the White House’s takeover of the nation’s 250th celebration.

In the letters, the lawmakers point to the Committee’s July interim report, From Vanity to Insanity: How the White House Cheated the American People out of their 250th Birthday, which “found that the White House hijacked the nation’s semiquincentennial celebration, converting a once-in-a-generation national commemoration into an apparatus for raising and spending money in service of the President’s political ideology and vanity projects. Freedom 250, a wholly owned subsidiary lodged within the National Park Foundation, was created as a new entity to facilitate this takeover.”

“As a sponsor or partner, your organization possesses documents and information essential to this investigation,” the lawmakers wrote.

The lawmakers are investigating “whether, how, and to what extent Freedom 250 and those acting in concert with it solicited donations by trading on official access, by misrepresenting the recipient or intended use of funds, or by leveraging donors’ business before the federal government.” They wrote that the inquiry “will inform potential legislation, including to ensure that the hijacking of the semiquincentennial does not become a template for further wrongdoing.”

The letters were sent to corporate sponsors of Freedom250, which include Boeing, Chevron, Deloitte, Exiger, ExxonMobil, January AI, John Deere, Lockheed Martin, Mastercard, Mosaic, Northrop Grumman, Oracle, Palantir, Penske, Phorm Energy, RTX, SAP, Scotts Miracle-Gro, Softbank, TikTok, UFC, United Airlines, and United Health Group.

Read the full request to one of Freedom250’s corporate sponsors here.

Background

The Committee’s July interim report found that when the congressionally chartered, nonpartisan America250 Commission refused to bend to the President’s demands, the White House built a replacement, Freedom 250, LLC, and declared it the central platform for the national celebration. The White House lodged that entity inside the National Park Foundation so it could draw on the credibility and donor relationships of a public charity while operating outside the transparency rules Congress wrote into law for the commission.

The Committee’s July 2 report found that Freedom 250 circulated sponsorship packages starting at $500,000 and climbing above $10 million, backed by the promise of a photo opportunity with President Trump. Its CEO solicited foreign governments and corporations at Davos. Fundraisers appear to have misled donors who meant to give to America250, handing them Freedom 250’s banking information instead, conduct the report found could amount to wire fraud. The report also found that Freedom 250 harvested Americans’ personal data, routing event registration through Campaign Nucleus, the firm founded by Trump campaign operative Brad Parscale, which scores visitors with artificial intelligence to target “persuadable voters.”

The report concluded that Freedom 250 has created a blueprint for corruption, not a one-time abuse, pointing to the Department of Agriculture, where the administration steered companies with business before the government to donate through a conservation charity into a fund the Secretary controls.

###

title: Kennedy Introduces Bipartisan STORMWATER Act to Strengthen Water Infrastructure and Protect Great Lakes Communities
text:
Legislation Would Reauthorize Federal Grant Funding for Stormwater Infrastructure and Establish New Center of Excellence for the Great Lakes

BUFFALO, N.Y. – Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26), alongside Representatives Debbie Dingell (MI-06) and Nick Langworthy (NY-23), introduced the bipartisan Stormwater Treatment, Optimization, Resilience, and Management with Academic Technological Expertise and Research (STORMWATER) Act, legislation to strengthen communities’ ability to manage stormwater, reduce flooding, and protect local waterways from pollution. This legislation is endorsed by the Great Lakes Commission.

“Every Western New Yorker deserves to know that when the next major storm comes, our communities have the infrastructure and expertise to withstand it,” said Congressman Kennedy. “The STORMWATER Act is about making that investment now – strengthening our water infrastructure, protecting our neighborhoods and businesses, and putting Great Lakes communities at the forefront of the technologies we need to safeguard the critical waters we all call home.”

“It is crucial we have protective measures in place for overflows in our lakes. Michiganders know all too well how drastic weather conditions can cause millions of dollars in damages and risk people’s lives. This reauthorization will not only continue to fund these lifesaving agencies, but will establish a new facility in the Great Lakes Basin,” said Congresswoman Dingell.

“Communities across the Great Lakes region know firsthand the challenges that stormwater runoff and flooding can create for our homes, businesses, farms, and infrastructure,” said Congressman Langworthy. “The STORMWATER Act will strengthen research and innovation, support communities working to address flooding, and establish a dedicated Center of Excellence focused on the unique needs of the Great Lakes Basin. As a member of the Great Lakes Caucus, I’m proud to join Congressman Kennedy in advancing this legislation and ensuring our region has the tools and expertise needed to protect our communities and keep our Great Lakes healthy for generations to come.”

"The Great Lakes Commission commends Rep. Kennedy for introducing the STORMWATER Act, which will ensure the Stormwater Centers of Excellence program continues nationwide while recognizing the Great Lakes as a unique resource increasingly threatened by stormwater impacts,” said Tim Bruno, Chair of the Great Lakes Commission. “Communities across the Great Lakes region are confronting more frequent flooding that threatens public health and water quality, carrying nutrients, debris, chemicals and other pollutants into our waterways. This bill will provide crucial resources to help communities prepare for and address these growing challenges."

The STORMWATER Act would reauthorize federal grant programs established through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law that support stormwater innovation, technical assistance, and flood mitigation. The existing grant programs are currently set to expire in September 2026. The legislation would extend them through fiscal year 2031, providing communities with the resources and continuity needed to plan and implement long-term infrastructure improvements.

Critically for Western New York, the legislation would establish a Stormwater Center of Excellence specifically focused on the Great Lakes region. While four existing Stormwater Centers of Excellence currently provide regional expertise on stormwater infrastructure, there is no federally designated center focused specifically on the Great Lakes basin, a region containing approximately 21 percent of the world’s fresh water and 84 percent of North America’s surface fresh water. This Great Lakes-focused Center would ensure that communities across the region can access technical expertise tailored to their unique stormwater and water-quality challenges, including strategies to improve infrastructure, reduce flooding, and protect the lakes and waterways that are central to the region’s economy and quality of life.

Specifically, the STORMWATER Act would:

Establish a fifth Center of Excellence focused on the Great Lakes region, ensuring the region’s unique stormwater and water-quality challenges receive dedicated expertise;

Reauthorize $5 million annually from fiscal years 2027 through 2031 to support and maintain five Centers of Excellence;

Reauthorize $10 million annually from fiscal years 2027 through 2031 for competitive Stormwater Control Infrastructure Project grants to support communities’ stormwater infrastructure needs.

Background

Stormwater runoff occurs when rain or melted snow cannot absorb into the ground and instead flows over hard surfaces like roads, rooftops, and parking lots. As that water moves rapidly into drainage systems and waterways, it can overwhelm infrastructure, contribute to flooding, and carry oil, debris, fertilizers, chemicals, and other pollutants into local streams and lakes.

For Western New York communities surrounded by the Great Lakes, these challenges are both environmental and economic. Stronger stormwater infrastructure can help protect homes and businesses from flooding, reduce pollution entering local waterways, and preserve the health and economic vitality of the Great Lakes for generations to come.
