title: Kiggans Welcomes Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy to Norfolk International Airport
text:
NORFOLK, VA — Today, Congresswoman Jen Kiggans (VA-02) was joined by U.S. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy for a visit to Norfolk International Airport to highlight the airport’s critical role in Hampton Roads and discuss ongoing infrastructure and air traffic controller staffing needs.

During the visit, Rep. Kiggans and Secretary Duffy met with Norfolk International Airport leadership to discuss the airport’s ongoing projects, infrastructure priorities, and how the transportation hub serves the region’s economic needs. They then toured Norfolk’s Air Traffic Control Tower (ATCT), where Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) personnel provided a briefing on air traffic operations, safety, staffing, and other priorities affecting the airport and the surrounding airspace.

Congresswoman Kiggans said, “As a former Navy helicopter pilot, I know firsthand how vital skilled air traffic controllers and modern infrastructure are to safe, reliable air travel. I was proud to welcome Secretary Duffy to Norfolk International Airport to meet with the professionals who safely manage some of the most complex civilian and military airspace in the country. The $27.3 million investment made possible by the Working Families Tax Cut will help ensure they have the tools needed to carry out that mission. I look forward to continuing our work with Secretary Duffy and the FAA to strengthen aviation safety across Hampton Roads.”

“Virginia’s 2nd Congressional District has a true champion in Congress in Representative Kiggans. Her vote for the Working Families Tax Cut delivered the $12.5 billion down payment the Department needed to revitalize air traffic control, including $27.3 million for Norfolk International Airport. Together, we are delivering a safer and more efficient travel experience for Virginians and providing an economic boost to the Norfolk region”, said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy.

Congresswoman Kiggans previously toured the Norfolk ATCT in 2025 to meet directly with controllers about staffing, infrastructure, and working conditions. At the time, Norfolk had been on the FAA’s critical facility list continuously since January 2023 and faced significant controller shortages. In 2024, controllers at the facility worked approximately 8,724 hours of overtime to help address staffing needs.

“The men and women operating our air traffic control towers have gone above and beyond in keeping our skies safe despite persistent staffing shortages,” Kiggans said. “They deserve the staffing, resources, and infrastructure they need to succeed and I’m committed to ensuring they receive this vital support to keep Hampton Roads and our nation safe.”

Rep. Kiggans’ Advocacy for Norfolk Air Traffic Control Modernization:

In January 2026, Rep. Kiggans voted in favor of a funding package that consisted of the remaining FY26 Appropriations bills, including funds for Transportation, Housing and Urban Development (THUD). The package increased funding for the FAA by $1.588 billion, secured $4.577 billion for airport infrastructure improvements, and provided resources to hire 2,500 new air traffic controllers. Read her press release here.

In March 2025, following the tragic crash over Reagan National Airport, Kiggans and Rep. Tom Barrett (MI-07) introduced the Military Helicopter Training Safety Act of 2025, to direct the Department of Defense to evaluate the feasibility of equipping all U.S. military helicopters with modern collision avoidance systems in an effort to improve safety measures for military rotary-wing aircraft operating near civilian airspace. Certain provisions within the bill were included in the Airspace Location and Enhanced Risk Transparency (ALERT) Act of 2026 and passed the House in February 2026. Read more from WTKR-3 here.

As the representative for Virginia’s Second District and a former Navy helicopter pilot married to a former F/A-18 pilot and current mother of a F/A-18 pilot, Rep. Kiggans remains committed to modernizing Hampton Roads’ transportation infrastructure, addressing air traffic controller staffing shortages, and securing the federal investments necessary to keep passengers moving safely and efficiently.

title: Krishnamoorthi Delivers Nearly $5.8 Million to Upgrade Aging Infrastructure, Protect Communities from Severe Weather Threats
text:
DES PLAINES, IL — Today, Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi joined local leaders from Des Plaines, Elk Grove Village, DuPage County, Bartlett, and Schaumburg to announce nearly $5.8 million in Community Project Funding he secured for five infrastructure projects across the 8th Congressional District. The investments will upgrade aging water infrastructure, reduce neighborhood flooding, improve road and pedestrian safety, and advance major transportation improvements.

“When a water main breaks, a neighborhood floods, or an intersection becomes overwhelmed, families pay the price,” said Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi. “That’s why I’m proud to have secured nearly $5.8 million to help our communities fix aging infrastructure before problems become crises. These investments will protect homes from flooding, keep drinking water reliable, and make our roads and intersections safer. With severe weather putting more strain on the infrastructure we rely on every day, investing now will help keep our communities safer, stronger, and more resilient for years to come.”

The funding includes:

$1.8 million for the City of Des Plaines’ Algonquin Road Grade Separation Project to support Phase II engineering, including final design and preparation of the plans and specifications needed to move the project toward construction. Phase II engineering is expected to take approximately three to four years.

$1.092 million for Elk Grove Village’s Water Main Lining Project to rehabilitate 15 critical sections of the Village’s more than 180 miles of water main, much of which dates to the 1950s and 1960s. The project will be Elk Grove Village’s first use of water-main lining, which requires less roadway excavation than traditional replacement.

$240,000 for DuPage County’s Newton & Second Flood Reduction Project to address recurring flooding in the Nelsons Highview neighborhood near Newton Avenue and Second Street in unincorporated Glendale Heights. Flooding has damaged residential properties and closed roads, limiting emergency vehicle access. Improvements include a detention/retention pond, additional storm sewers, and outlet and downstream improvements.

$1.5 million for the Village of Bartlett’s Route 25/West Bartlett Road Intersection Improvements to add dedicated turn lanes in each direction and a pedestrian crossing bridge to improve traffic flow and safety.

$1.152 million for the Village of Schaumburg’s Hammond Drive/Algonquin Road Intersection Improvements to improve the intersection and mitigate the impacts of industrial traffic on Schaumburg residents.

The five awards total $5.784 million in Fiscal Year 2026 Community Project Funding secured by Congressman Krishnamoorthi for infrastructure projects across the 8th Congressional District.

title: Krishnamoorthi Demands Answers from Trump DOJ Over Reported Hiring of Lawyer Convicted of Hacking Election Websites for Election Monitoring
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), a senior member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, today demanded answers from Attorney General Todd Blanche following reports that a lawyer convicted of hacking election websites joined the Trump Administration’s Civil Rights Division and participated in its election-monitoring operation during Minnesota’s August primary. The reports come as DOJ prepares to deploy as many as 1,000 personnel during the November midterm elections, raising urgent questions about who the Department is entrusting with access to polling locations and voters.

In the letter, Krishnamoorthi writes:

“Reports indicate that David Michael Levin—a Florida attorney who pleaded guilty in 2016 to unauthorized computer intrusions involving two election websites—appears to have joined the Department’s Civil Rights Division and participated in the Department’s monitoring of Minnesota’s August primary. Photographs and video reviewed by reporters reportedly show Mr. Levin standing alongside a Civil Rights Division attorney at a Minneapolis polling location, where a local election judge intervened after the two men positioned themselves too close to the polling place.”

According to Florida investigators, Levin used SQL injection techniques to obtain the login credentials of the Lee County Supervisor of Elections and used those credentials to access the office’s website as an administrator. He also targeted the Florida Division of Elections website. Levin was originally charged with three felonies, ultimately pleaded guilty to two misdemeanors, and served 20 days in jail.

DOJ has not publicly explained Levin’s employment status, his role in the monitoring operation, or how he was selected to participate. Reports have also identified other individuals brought into the Civil Rights Division who have publicly questioned the legitimacy of past elections.

Krishnamoorthi continues:

“These reports raise a fundamental question: What standards is the Department applying when selecting the personnel who will be responsible for protecting Americans’ voting rights?”

The letter follows Krishnamoorthi’s August 19 demand for safeguards against voter intimidation and answers on how DOJ will select, train, and supervise as many as 1,000 election monitors it plans to deploy during the 2026 midterms, nearly twice the size of its 2024 effort.

Krishnamoorthi writes:

“If the reports concerning Mr. Levin are accurate, his presence at a polling location would call that confidence into question. An individual with a documented history of unauthorized access to election systems should not be placed in a position of authority or proximity to voters and election officials without a clear explanation from the Department of the vetting, supervision, and legal authority governing that assignment.”

Krishnamoorthi requested responses to the following questions by September 3, 2026:

Is David Michael Levin currently, or has he previously been, an employee, contractor, detailee, or volunteer of the Civil Rights Division? If so, please identify his position, responsibilities, and dates of service.

What vetting process does the Department require before assigning an individual to election-monitoring duties, including criminal background checks and reviews of an individual’s prior involvement with election systems or election-related activities? Was that process followed in Mr. Levin’s case?

Were Department officials aware of Mr. Levin’s 2016 conviction for unauthorized access to election systems before he participated in the Minneapolis monitoring operation? If so, who approved his participation?

Under what legal authority was Mr. Levin present at the Powderhorn Park polling location? Was he a duly appointed federal election observer, a Civil Rights Division employee, or acting in another capacity?

What training and written guidance are provided to election monitors regarding permissible conduct inside or near polling places, including restrictions designed to prevent voter intimidation and interference with election officials?

What screening criteria will the Department apply to the approximately 1,000 personnel it plans to deploy in November? Will those criteria include an individual’s criminal history, prior conduct involving election systems, and public efforts to undermine confidence in lawful elections?

Will the Department provide Congress with a written description of the vetting, training, supervision, and disciplinary procedures governing its 2026 election-monitoring program before those personnel are deployed?

Krishnamoorthi requested a complete response by September 3, 2026, citing the proximity of the midterm elections and the scale of DOJ’s planned deployment.

title: Krishnamoorthi Demands USDA Action as Trump-Backed SNAP Cuts Put Free School Meals at Risk
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) today demanded immediate action from the Trump Administration to protect children’s access to free school meals as historic cuts to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act take effect. In a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins and Food and Nutrition Administration Acting Administrator Shiela Corley, Krishnamoorthi warned that the cuts are already putting additional pressure on school meal programs in Illinois and across the country.

New data show Illinois has 47 fewer schools and 15 fewer school districts participating in the Community Eligibility Provision (CEP) this school year, with nearly 24,000 fewer Illinois students attending schools that provide free meals to all students through the program. Illinois was one of only three states to experience the largest declines nationwide in the number of schools participating in CEP.

In the letter, Krishnamoorthi writes:

“I am writing regarding the severe impact that cuts under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) are having on children’s access to school meals as students across Illinois and the country return to the classroom. I strongly urge the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) and its Food and Nutrition Administration (FNA) to take immediate action to protect children’s access to nutritious school meals, particularly in Illinois communities already experiencing losses in free meal eligibility as a result of the law’s cuts to SNAP.”

The OBBBA, enacted by Congress and the Trump Administration in July 2025, imposed new SNAP eligibility and work requirements while making the largest cuts to SNAP in the program’s history. Since the law took effect, an estimated 4.5 million people, including 1.5 million children, have lost SNAP benefits nationwide. In Illinois, more than 300,000 people are expected to lose benefits because of the new work and paperwork requirements alone, while SNAP enrollment has already fallen 16 percent in the year since the law’s enactment.

Those losses can follow children directly into the classroom. Students enrolled in SNAP are automatically certified for free school meals without having to submit a separate household application. When families lose SNAP, children can lose that automatic eligibility even when their underlying need for food assistance has not changed.

Krishnamoorthi writes:

“A paperwork failure by one household should not become a food insecurity problem for hundreds of children. If enough families lose direct certification, an entire school can lose access to CEP and its ability to provide free meals to every student.”

Under CEP, schools and districts where at least 25 percent of students are directly certified through SNAP, Medicaid, or other qualifying programs can provide free breakfast and lunch to all students without collecting individual household applications. As families lose SNAP because of new paperwork requirements, schools can fall below that threshold and lose CEP eligibility.

Krishnamoorthi is demanding that USDA and FNA conduct an immediate state-by-state assessment of the impact of the OBBBA’s SNAP eligibility changes on children’s access to school meals and make the results public. He is also seeking answers to the following questions:

How many children have lost direct certification for free school meals as a result of losing SNAP benefits since the OBBBA took effect, both nationwide and in each state?

How many schools and school districts have lost, or are at risk of losing, CEP eligibility as a result of changes in SNAP participation, and how many students attend those schools?

What steps are USDA and FNA taking to prevent children who lose direct certification from losing access to free school meals and to help schools preserve CEP eligibility?

Which states and communities face the greatest risk of reduced access to school meals as a result of these changes, and what assistance are USDA and FNA providing to them?

Krishnamoorthi requested responses to his questions and the results of the state-by-state assessment by September 10, 2026. He also requested that USDA make the assessment public so states, school districts, and families can understand the effects of the changes and the steps being taken to address them.

title: Krishnamoorthi Urges State Department to Support Search for Those Missing After Devastating Floods in Nepal and Tibet
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi today urged the State Department to use every available resource to support ongoing search and rescue efforts following devastating floods in Nepal and Tibet that have left hundreds of people missing, including American citizens. Krishnamoorthi’s office is also working to assist those seeking help locating missing family members and friends.

“My thoughts are with everyone affected by the devastating floods in Nepal and Tibet, including the hundreds of people who remain missing. Reports that American citizens are among those still unaccounted for are deeply troubling, and my office is working to assist those seeking help locating family members and friends. The State Department must use every available resource to support search and rescue efforts and help account for those who remain missing. The United States must continue working closely with authorities in Nepal and the region to provide answers to families awaiting news of their loved ones.”

title: Latta, Dingell Introduce Bipartisan BEDROCK Act to Reshore American Manufacturing
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Congressman Bob Latta (OH-5) and Congresswoman Debbie Dingell (MI-6) introduced the bipartisan Biomanufacturing Excellence, Domestic Resilience, Output, and Competitive Know-how Act, or the BEDROCK Act. This legislation would help turn products invented in America into products made in America—supporting American manufacturing jobs, strengthening American supply chains, and reducing American dependence on Communist China.

Ohio’s Fifth Congressional District is home to over 1,000 manufacturers and more than 86,000 manufacturing jobs. From small family-owned shops to major production facilities, manufacturing offers Ohioans the opportunity to work, support their families, and build the products that the rest of the world needs. The BEDROCK Act would help bring that manufacturing tradition to the next generation of American industry.

Biomanufacturing uses biology to make products at industrial scale, such as new materials and medicines. American companies lead the world in discovering these new products, but all too often, the factories, suppliers, and jobs required to produce them at scale move overseas. Communist China has repeatedly made biomanufacturing a national priority; they now dominate the world’s fermentation capacity.

“Northern Ohio knows that manufacturing is the lifeblood of our economy,” Latta said. “For far too long, America has pioneered new inventions, only for Communist China to build the facilities—stealing the jobs that come with them. The BEDROCK Act would help reshore that work. This bipartisan legislation would create new opportunities for Ohio workers, strengthen the biomanufacturing supply chain, and make it easier for American manufacturers to produce at home.”

“America's manufacturing might has been hollowed out for decades,” Dingell said. “This bipartisan bill will strengthen and create good-paying jobs, as well as reduce our reliance on China. I am proud to support this effort to invest in America's workers and ensure we do not cede our competitive edge to our adversaries.”

The BEDROCK Act would:

Designate a senior Department of Commerce official to lead efforts to strengthen U.S. biomanufacturing competitiveness;

Assess critical supply-chain inputs, domestic production capacity, commercialization barriers, and reliance on China and other foreign adversaries;

Develop a prioritized action plan and consolidate existing federal resources to address the most significant risks and barriers; and

Map federal commercialization processes, establish FDA and EPA points of contact, and publish industry-led practices to help companies scale production.

“For too long, biomanufacturing's importance to both national security and industrial policy has been overlooked,” said Sam Dorn, Vice President of Policy & Government Affairs, the New American Industrial Alliance (NAIA). “By developing a critical biomanufacturing action plan, streamlining government coordination, and mapping key supply chains, the BEDROCK Act would begin to address that dangerous oversight. Rep. Latta and Rep. Dingell are to be commended for their leadership in this important effort.”

“This legislation gives biomanufacturing the clear federal leadership, honest risk assessment, and streamlined pathways it has long needed,” said Brooke Coleman, Executive Director, the American Alliance for Biomanufacturing. “It's a critical piece of the broader push to accelerate commercial deployment here at home and ensure America—not our competitors—leads the world in biomanufacturing. Federal agencies must treat this as the strategic priority it is, and the Department of Commerce must be at the forefront of this effort.”

“A strong domestic biomanufacturing base helps ensure that innovative medicines can be developed and produced reliably in the United States while creating high-value jobs and economic opportunity,” said Dr. Kelvin H. Lee, Institute Director, the National Institute for Innovation in Manufacturing Biopharmaceuticals. “The BEDROCK Act supports these goals by strengthening the capabilities and supply chains that underpin modern biopharmaceutical manufacturing.”

“ITIF supports the BEDROCK Act as a practical step toward strengthening U.S. biomanufacturing competitiveness and reducing reliance on China,” said Stephen Ezell, Executive Vice President, Global Innovation Policy, Information Technology and Innovation Foundation. “As China rapidly expands its state-backed biomanufacturing capacity, the United States needs a clearer picture of its supply-chain vulnerabilities and a more coordinated federal pathway for companies to commercialize. By directing Commerce to assess critical supply-chain dependencies, identify reliance on foreign adversaries, and streamline the federal commercialization process, the BEDROCK Act would help address these gaps and strengthen America’s biomanufacturing ecosystem.”

“LanzaTech’s gas fermentation platform is headquartered in the United States and has been successfully commercialized around the world, proving that U.S.-developed technology can compete, scale, and lead in international markets,” said Dr. Jennifer Holmgren, Chief Executive Officer, LanzaTech. “That global leadership would be reinforced by a stronger domestic biomanufacturing base. Expanding deployment here at home would strengthen U.S. economic and national security, support domestic manufacturing of critical products such as sustainable aviation fuel and other strategic supply chain materials, and create high-quality American jobs across engineering, construction, operations, and advanced manufacturing. By providing a single federal point of coordination, a clear pathway to commercialization, and greater visibility into supply chain dependencies, the BEDROCK Act would help accelerate biomanufacturing investment in the United States while ensuring that American innovation continues to set the pace globally.”

title: Lawler Introduces Bill to Ensure Continuity of Operations at Export-Import Bank
text:
“American businesses should never be put at a competitive disadvantage because the Export-Import Bank is unable to function due to vacancies on its board. Making the quorum solution permanent is a commonsense step that will provide greater certainty for U.S. exporters and ensure they have access to the financing tools they need to compete against foreign companies backed by their own governments. The New Jersey Chamber of Commerce supports this effort to prevent unnecessary disruptions, strengthen American competitiveness and support businesses, workers and supply chains here in New Jersey and across the country,” said the New Jersey Chamber of Commerce.

“It's imperative that businesses across the State of New York have reliable access to financing tools that allow them to be competitive in a global marketplace. To accomplish that, the EXIM Bank must be able to operate responsibly and uninterrupted. We commend Reps. Lawler and Gottheimer for their leadership on this important issue and for advancing legislation that will end future delays,” said Heather Mulligan, President and CEO of The Business Council of New York, Inc.

“Businesses across Ohio and around the country utilize important financing mechanisms like the Export-Import Bank to help ensure they can sell their products to consumers overseas. It is essential to build on investments made by leaders in Washington to support re-industrialization and reshoring by ensuring that the United States does not unilaterally disarm in a global marketplace. Reauthorizing the EXIM Bank is a critical step needed to keep American businesses competing on a level playing field,” said Ohio Chamber President & CEO Steve Stivers.

“Political gridlock left the Export Import Bank of the United States functionally paralyzed for nearly four years, costing American exporters billions of dollars in lost deals while foreign competitors rushed in to fill the void. Freeing the EXIM Bank from this legislative logjam is a bipartisan concern and a pillar of American competitiveness, which is why the EXIM Bank Continuity in Competitiveness Act permanently fixes the quorum requirement and keeps EXIM Bank fully operational. American workers, manufacturers, and small businesses cannot afford to lose another deal simply because Washington failed to staff a board, and the Chamber thanks Representatives Lawler and Gottheimer for their leadership in introducing this commonsense legislation,” said Foxhall Parker, Senior Director, Center for Capital Markets Competitiveness, U.S. Chamber of Commerce.

“Reps. Lawler and Gottheimer's bipartisan legislation delivers an important fix manufacturers have long sought to improve the operations and efficiency of the EXIM Bank and ensure it can use its full authorities to support U.S. manufacturers competing around the world. A strong, efficient EXIM Bank helps level the playing field, giving manufacturers and their customers greater access to critical financing that supports growth, investment and job creation here at home,” said Jay Timmons, CEO of the National Association of Manufacturers.

This bill is also endorsed by the Rockland Business Association.

Full text of the bill can be found HERE.

title: REPS LIEU, FRIEDMAN, CHU, KAMLAGER-DOVE, & WATERS CONVENE LA’S TRANSPORTATION LEADERS ON OLYMPIC READINESS
text:
WEST HOLLYWOOD, CA — On August 26, 2026, Congresswoman Laura Friedman (D-Los Angeles) convened a panel of the region’s top transportation officials alongside U.S. Representatives Ted Lieu (D-Los Angeles), Maxine Waters (D-Los Angeles), Judy Chu (D-Los Angeles), and Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-Los Angeles) to examine what the 2026 FIFA World Cup revealed about Los Angeles County’s readiness to move millions of people during the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games. The panel came just weeks before Congress decides how much federal funding Los Angeles gets for the Games.

The panel brought together the agencies that run public transit across the region:

LA Metro Chief Customer Experience Officer Jennifer Vides, who spoke to what the agency needs to move visitors across dozens of venues over sixteen days, including the buses, operators, and storage capacity a Games-scale operation requires and the capital projects Metro is working to finish before 2028.

Los Angeles Department of Transportation General Manager Laura Rubio-Cornejo, who runs the second largest municipal transportation department in the country and is delivering street and transit improvements before 2028, including an additional zero-emissions bus maintenance facility.

City of Santa Monica Department of Transportation Director Anuj Gupta, who oversees the Big Blue Bus and a department of more than 470 employees in a city that will host no Olympic venues but will be the site of at least a dozen nation houses.

LA Metro Chief of Police and Emergency Management Bill Scott, who led Metro's security coordination during the World Cup and is standing up the agency's new in-house Transit Community Public Safety Department while preparing for the 2027 Super Bowl and 2028 Games.

“I am honored to represent California’s 36th Congressional District, which will host the Olympic Athletes Village at UCLA and the first LA 28 medal event, the Women’s Triathlon in Venice Beach. Ahead of the Olympics, we must ensure that athletes are able to get to and from their events safely and efficiently. Just as importantly, we must make sure the millions of Angelenos and visitors from around the world attending the Games can reliably travel to the venues while minimizing traffic impacts on Los Angeles County residents,” said Congressman Lieu. “I look forward to working with my colleagues to secure the federal funding needed to address Los Angeles’ critical transportation and security needs.”

“The World Cup proved that Los Angeles can deliver, but eight matches at one stadium over five weeks is not the same as sixteen days of events at dozens of venues across the region,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman. “The agencies responsible for moving those visitors have never had to work at that scale together. So, we brought them into one room to tell Congress what they need to pull this off, and when they need it because the window for that closes in weeks, not years. I am going to keep fighting to bring our tax dollars home, and to make sure what this region builds for 2028 is still serving Angelenos long after the Games leave town.”

"The American Decade of Sports is an opportunity for Los Angeles to shine bright on the world stage while leaving our region better than fans found it," said Congresswoman Kamlager-Dove. “Hosting successful games and delivering lasting benefits for our community starts with investing in our transportation infrastructure. The 2026 World Cup was the ultimate test run for the 2028 Olympics, and convenings like today help us learn from the past so we can build a safer, more accessible, and better-connected LA long after the Olympic flame is extinguished."

WHAT THE WORLD CUP SHOWED:

More than 212,000 rides were taken on Metro’s enhanced bus service to and from SoFi Stadium at $1.75 each way.

Enhanced service included direct shuttles connecting the stadium to 15 transit hubs across Southern California.

June system ridership was 2 million riders higher than last June, with Metro recording its highest single-day ridership of the month on June 18.

Metro CEO Stephanie Wiggins has said there were zero major security incidents during the tournament.

WHAT THE 2028 GAMES REQUIRE:

Metro has requested approximately $2 billion for its Games mobility plan. Congress approved only $94.3 million earlier this year.

The House Appropriations Committee approved $875 million for the request in its FY27 Transportation, Housing and Urban Development bill. This has not been signed into law and falls short of what Los Angeles will need to make the games safe and secure.

The President’s FY27 budget request did not include funding.

Metro needs approximately 1,700 additional buses against a current fleet of roughly 2,100, and has secured roughly half of that total to date.

The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act expires September 30, 2026.

Metro has publicly stated that without the full request, the complete scope of the Games Enhanced Transit System would not be feasible.

title: Rhode Island Congressional Delegation Announces $4.6 Million for URI, CCRI Engineering Workforce Development Program
text:
PROVIDENCE, RI — As demand grows for skilled engineers and technicians to power Rhode Island's advanced manufacturing, marine, and clean energy sectors, U.S. Senators Jack Reed and Sheldon Whitehouse and Representatives Seth Magaziner (RI-02) and Gabe Amo (RI-01) announced $4,619,389 of federal funding awarded by the National Science Foundation (NSF) to the University of Rhode Island, in partnership with the Community College of Rhode Island, to support scholarships for high-achieving, low-income students pursuing degrees in engineering and engineering technology.

The program stands to benefit workforce development across multiple sectors, including Rhode Island's blue economy and advanced manufacturing industry. It is set to begin in January.

“This is a wise investment in individuals, Rhode Island’s workforce, and American science and engineering expertise, which is increasingly critical for our economy and national defense. Helping smart kids afford an engineering degree is a win-win. They get the skills that put them on promising career pathways for critical, in-demand jobs and America stays competitive,” said Senator Reed.

“Rhode Island’s institutions of higher education are on the leading edge of STEM innovation and help power the Ocean State’s economic competitiveness,” said Senator Whitehouse. “This federal funding will create opportunities for deserving Rhode Island students to follow their dreams at URI and CCRI.”

"Rhode Island needs more engineers, and this funding will help make sure that talented students across our state have a real shot at that career, no matter their financial background," said Rep. Magaziner. "I am proud to work alongside the Rhode Island Congressional delegation to deliver the funding needed to support workforce training here in the Ocean State.”

"I'm proud to work alongside our Rhode Island Delegation to expand opportunity for talented students at the University of Rhode Island and the Community College of Rhode Island,” said Rep. Amo. "This federal funding will remove financial barriers for students and set them up for good-paying engineering jobs that will power Rhode Island's economy of tomorrow."

“This project will help reduce the financial burden for students pursuing an engineering degree and, ultimately, the amount of debt they may carry after graduation,” said Vinka Craver, associate dean for research at URI’s College of Engineering and Principal Investigator on the NSF grant. “But the program goes beyond financial support. From their first year, students will have access to faculty and industry mentors and opportunities to participate in internships and capstone projects, helping them build the experience and connections they need to be better prepared for their professional careers.”

"Cost should never stand between a talented student and their future. This grant makes that future possible for Rhode Island students pursuing degrees in engineering and engineering technology. Through our partnership with URI, we're building a talent pipeline into the advanced manufacturing, marine, and clean energy jobs that are shaping Rhode Island's economy,” said Rosemary A. Costigan, Ph.D., RN, president of the Community College of Rhode Island. “I'm grateful to Senators Reed and Whitehouse and Representatives Magaziner and Amo for their continued investment in our students and our state's workforce future."

A total of 116 scholars pursuing associate's degrees in engineering technology at CCRI and bachelor's degrees in engineering and engineering technology at URI will receive scholarships for up to five years, along with mentoring and other support services designed to improve retention and graduation rates.

The award is administered by the National Science Foundation (NSF) as part of NSF's Scholarships in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (S-STEM) program, which supports the retention and graduation of academically talented, low-income students with demonstrated financial need in STEM fields. The project, entitled "Collaborative Research: Advancing Pathways through a Multi-Institutional Consortium for Engineering Education and Workforce Development," will be evaluated on an ongoing basis to help identify effective strategies for supporting low-income students in STEM.

title: Rep. Mann Presses ATF For Clarity Following Suppressor Regulations
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representative Tracey Mann (KS-01) sent a letter to Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) Director Robert Cekada requesting clear and timely guidance for law-abiding firearm owners, manufacturers, and federally licensed firearms dealers following the August federal court ruling in Silencer Shop Foundation v. ATF.

The ruling affects federal suppressor registration requirements under the National Firearms Act (NFA) and has created uncertainty regarding existing and pending applications, Form 4 approvals, and the requirements that remain in effect. In his letter, Rep. Mann urged ATF to promptly explain how it will implement the ruling and provide clear direction to Americans and businesses seeking to comply with federal law.

“Law-abiding gun owners and businesses should not be left guessing about what federal law requires of them,” said Rep. Mann. “The Second Amendment is a fundamental constitutional right, and the federal government has a responsibility to provide clear, transparent guidance when a court ruling changes how firearm regulations are enforced. Without clear guidance from ATF, law-abiding Americans and businesses are being left to determine for themselves how this ruling affects their rights, responsibilities, and livelihoods. ATF should work directly with Congress and the firearms community to provide answers and restore certainty as quickly as possible.”

Rep. Mann specifically requested information from ATF regarding:

Steps the agency has taken to implement the Silencer Shop Foundation v. ATF ruling

How the ruling will affect the Form 4 application and approval process

Which federal NFA registration requirements will remain in effect

How ATF will handle existing and pending applications

What procedures firearm owners, manufacturers, and dealers should follow going forward

When ATF intends to publish official, finalized guidance

Rep. Mann is a staunch defender of the Second Amendment. In January 2025, Rep. Mann introduced the RIFLE Act of 2025. Rep. Mann also penned a letter to former ATF Director Steven Dettelbach in January of 2024, pushing back against President Biden's zero-tolerance policy. In June 2023, Rep. Mann voted to block ATF’s rule to reclassify pistols with stabilizing braces as short-barreled rifles and shotguns. Rep. Mann opposed the Biden Administration’s overreaching executive orders that made it harder for law-abiding citizens to own firearms and voted against legislation to establish an unconstitutional assault weapons ban.

title: Representative Mannion Presents Military Medals and Honors to Highly Decorated Vietnam Veteran Joe Pounder of Liverpool
text:
SYRACUSE, NY - Representative John W. Mannion (NY-22) today presented military medals, unit awards, ribbons, and badges to Joe Pounder of Liverpool, a highly decorated U.S. Army veteran who served with the 5th Special Forces Group (Airborne), 1st Special Forces, during the Vietnam War.

Pounder attained the rank of sergeant first class during more than a decade of service in the U.S. Army. His honors include two Bronze Star Medals, including one with a “V” device for heroism; two Purple Hearts; two Army Commendation Medals, including one with a “V” device; and the Air Medal.

Representative John W. Mannion said, “Sergeant Pounder rushed into enemy fire to save four wounded members of his patrol, coordinated their evacuation, and then led his men forward against the enemy. That is extraordinary heroism, and these medals and decorations honor more than a decade of devotion to our country. It’s my privilege to help Joe receive what he earned, ensure his service will always be recognized, and give his family lasting symbols of what he did for our nation.”

On October 25, 1969, Pounder was serving as a Special Forces adviser to a patrol operating from Camp Tra Bong when the unit was ambushed and four members of the patrol were wounded in the open under intense enemy fire. Pounder rushed forward and moved the wounded to cover, rallied the patrol, called for a medical evacuation, coordinated artillery and air support, and then led an assault that routed the enemy. He was awarded the Bronze Star Medal with “V” device for his heroism.

The medals and military honors presented to Pounder include:

Medals

Bronze Star Medal (2) with one bronze oak leaf cluster and bronze “V” device

Purple Heart (2) with one bronze oak leaf cluster

Air Medal

Army Commendation Medal with one bronze oak leaf cluster and bronze “V” device

Army Good Conduct Medal with bronze clasp and three loops

National Defense Service Medal

Vietnam Service Medal with four bronze service stars and one silver service star

Unit Awards

Presidential Unit Citation

Meritorious Unit Commendation

Ribbon

Republic of Vietnam Campaign Medal ribbon with 1960 Device

Badges

Combat Infantryman Badge

Expert Marksmanship Qualification Badge with Pistol and Rifle Bars

Parachutist Badge

Supporting veterans and their families is a priority for Representative Mannion, including helping constituents secure military records, replacement medals, and benefits they have earned. Any NY-22 resident who needs assistance obtaining military service records or replacing medals and decorations can contact Representative Mannion’s office at (315) 233-4333 or visit mannion.house.gov.

title: PHOTO RELEASE: Rep. McBride, Lt. Governor Evans Gay Convene Delaware Childcare Roundtable on Access and Affordability
text:
DOVER, Del. — Today, U.S. Representative Sarah McBride and Lt. Governor Kyle Evans Gay (both D-Del.) brought together advocates, childcare providers, and local leaders for a conversation at Delaware State University on lowering childcare costs, expanding access to care, and strengthening Delaware’s childcare workforce.

Rep. McBride was recently selected by House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries to co-lead the House Democratic Caregiving Working Group, which is charged with helping develop the House Democratic Caucus’s legislative agenda on caregiving. Today’s discussion further informs that work, bringing the experiences and priorities of Delaware families and childcare providers directly into creating bold federal solutions to caregiving challenges facing families in the First State and across the country.

“Childcare costs are increasingly unaffordable for working families in Delaware and across the country,” said Rep. McBride. “Access to affordable, reliable childcare must be at the center of our economic agenda at both the federal and state levels. Today’s conversation brought together providers, advocates, and local leaders to talk about what it will take to lower costs for families, expand access to care, and recruit and retain the childcare workers our communities need. As we develop a caregiving agenda for the next Congress, I’m going to make sure the voices and experiences of Delawareans are front and center.”

The discussion focused on four key challenges facing Delaware families and childcare providers: affordability for families; access to and availability of care; financial, operational, and workforce pressures facing providers; as well as state and federal policies that could help address those challenges. Participants also discussed gaps in infant care, care during nontraditional hours, rural childcare, and care for children with disabilities, as well as barriers providers face in recruiting and retaining workers and expanding capacity to meet demand.

“For too long, we have approached early childhood education in Delaware as a collection of individual programs — each with its own funding stream, requirements, eligibility rules, and priorities. But parents don't experience government that way. Educators don’t. And children certainly don’t,” said Lt. Governor Kyle Evans Gay. “We have an opportunity right now to think differently — to move from fragmented programs toward an aligned and coordinated system with sustainable investments. We have the opportunity to design a system around the people that we serve. As Chair of the IRMC, I am committed to that work—and to making sure the we have the honest conversations about governance, financing, coordination, and accountability that this moment requires so that our youngest Delawareans have access to the education and care they need.”

Affordability was a central focus throughout the conversation as families continue to face high childcare costs. According to a recent report, the national average annual price of center-based infant care was $15,570. In Delaware, families are paying approximately $17,252 per year for center-based infant care.

Joining Rep. McBride and Lt. Governor Evans Gay were representatives from:

Child Care for Every Family Network

Delaware Association for the Education of Young Children

YMCA of Delaware

Delaware State Education Association

Delaware State University's Early Childhood Center

Delaware Department of Education

Delaware Department of Health and Social Services

Representatives shared concerns about workforce infrastructure and the increasing costs of providing care, as well as squeezed bottom lines across the board. Each spoke about challenges facing the affordability of childcare — reinforcing the broad effects across every aspect of the economy and workforce — and shared invaluable perspectives about the way families are navigating childcare access and costs across Delaware.

Rep. McBride has long worked to strengthen support for working families. In Congress, she is a cosponsor of the Child Care for Every Community Act, which would create a universal childcare program, and the American Family Act, which would increase the value of a monthly Child Tax Credit.

While serving as a Delaware State Senator, Rep. McBride passed the Healthy Delaware Families Act with bipartisan support, providing paid family and medical leave to workers across the state. In Congress, she has continued to lead on strengthening the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) and expanding paid leave nationwide. She has introduced legislation including the FAIR Leave Act, the Flexible Leave Act, and is an original cosponsor of the FAMILY Act, helping ensure workers and their families can access leave when they need it most.

Photos from the event can be found here.

title: ICYMI: Conference Chairwoman McClain Attends Michigan Farm Bureau Dinner on the Farm
text:
MICHIGAN – House Republican Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain (R-Mich.) this week joined the annual Michigan Farm Bureau Dinner on the Farm at Zwerk & Sons Farms to highlight the benefits of the Working Families Tax Cuts for Michigan farmers and to discuss ongoing work to pass a long-term Farm Bill.

Attendees included House Agriculture Committee Vice Chairman Austin Scott (R-Ga.); Matt Frostic of Frostic Farms and the National Corn Growers Association; Mike Noll of Noll Farms and Michigan Farm Bureau; and Michigan Farm Bureau President Ben LaCross.

“It was a rewarding evening of honest discussions with Michigan farmers who work tirelessly every day to feed our families and boost our economy. Washington should support their efforts by making their work easier,” Chairwoman McClain said. “I fought to deliver meaningful wins for our farmers through the Working Families Tax Cuts, and I will continue pushing to reduce input costs, cut through excessive red tape, and get a long-term Farm Bill across the finish line to bring much-needed relief to our agricultural community.”

“I want to thank Chairwoman McClain for inviting me to join her at Dinner on the Farm and giving me the opportunity to hear from Michigan’s farmers. Though our commodities may differ, our message remains the same: we will continue the fight in Washington to advance policies that support our producers and rural communities. Across the country, farmers want fair access to markets both domestically and abroad, they want Congress to address rising input costs, and they want to ensure the next generation can succeed on the farm. Chairwoman McClain is a fierce advocate for addressing these issues and I look forward to continuing to work with her on behalf of American agriculture,” House Agriculture Committee Vice Chairman Austin Scott said.

“We always look forward to working with our federal partners to advance crucial ag policies,” said Michigan Farm Bureau President Ben LaCross. “Farm Bureau couldn't be the voice of agriculture without our members coming to events like this, lending their voices and your credibility in the ag discussion. Because of our members, we are able to engage with elected officials in Washington, D.C., and in Lansing who are willing to advocate and listen to us — just like Congresswoman McClain is doing with the farm bill and E15.”

The Working Families Tax Cuts delivered major wins for farmers by strengthening crop insurance, raising reference prices, strengthening dairy coverage, and providing tax relief that helps family farms plan for the next generation.

The House passed the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 in April, but the Senate has yet to advance a Farm Bill to the floor.

title: McDowell Leads Resolution Honoring Gulf War-Era Veterans and Fifth Anniversary of Afghanistan Evacuation
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Addison McDowell (NC-06) introduced a resolution honoring the millions of American veterans who served during the Gulf War era and commemorating five years since the evacuation of Afghanistan.

Approximately 8.4 million veterans served during the Gulf War era, representing roughly 43 percent of all living American veterans and making them the largest single group of living veterans.

“Gulf War-era veterans answered the call to defend our country, confront terrorism, and protect freedom around the world,” said Congressman McDowell. “For more than three decades, they have stood in defense of our nation through war, terrorism, and uncertainty. We are a safer and stronger nation because of their courage and sacrifice. Five years after the evacuation of Afghanistan, we honor their service and reaffirm a simple promise: America will never forget those who stood in her defense.”

For more than three decades, members of the United States Armed Forces have served across the Middle East to defend our Nation and its allies. The Gulf War era began with Operations Desert Shield and Desert Storm in 1990 and 1991, when American service members liberated Kuwait from Iraqi occupation. They later served in Operation Enduring Freedom to dismantle al-Qaeda, Operation Iraqi Freedom to overthrow the Ba’athist government of Saddam Hussein, and Operation Inherent Resolve in response to the rise of the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria.

“The National Guard remains an essential component of America's Total Force. Thousands of Guardsmen continue to support missions at home and abroad, carrying forward the legacy established by those who served throughout the Gulf War era. This resolution sends an important message that Congress remembers their service, honors their sacrifices, and remains committed to supporting veterans and military families,” said Jon “Ice” Eisberg, Vice President of Government Affairs at the National Guard Association of the United States.

“NGAUS thanks Representative McDowell for his leadership on this resolution and urges all Members of the House of Representatives to support H. Res. 1496 to join in recognizing the dedication and courage of Gulf War era veterans. Passage of this resolution will ensure that the service of this generation is properly remembered and that their contributions to our nation's security are never forgotten.”

Tomorrow, August 28, 2026, also marks five years since the evacuation of Afghanistan. Among those remembered are the 13 American service members killed in the terrorist attack at Abbey Gate on August 26, 2021, and all those who sacrificed throughout the Gulf War era. American service in the region continues today, as tens of thousands of members of the Armed Forces remain in the Middle East protecting the United States and its allies from the Islamic Republic of Iran.

Original Cosponsors: Rep. Jim Baird (IN-04) , Rep. Juan Ciscomani (AZ-06), Rep. Matt Van Epps (TN-07) and Rep. Derrick Van Orden (WI-03).

title: ICYMI: McIver and Counsel Paul Fishman Press Call Debriefing Court’s Refusal To Dismiss U.S. v. McIver Case
text:
NEWARK, NJ – Today, on a briefing call, Congresswoman LaMonica McIver (NJ-10) and her counsel, Paul Fishman, broke down Wednesday's Third Circuit decision to not dismiss U.S. v. McIver. The decision carries troubling legal and political implications that threaten separation of powers.

McIver and Fishman discussed the complex ruling— the Court ruled to not dismiss the case on two counts and ruled to vacate and remand the third count— the next steps from the court and the legal team, and the broader implications and consequences of the case for democracy. The case, if not dismissed, would set a precedent for extreme ICE impunity, executive branch overreach, and weaponization of the DOJ.

Below are excerpts from the briefing.

Fishman on the stakes of the case

“Let me make something clear. We are not afraid to try this case, and if we try this case…we will win that trial.

[...]

“This is a fight for Congresswoman McIver and every other member of the House of Representatives and the United States Senate who could be targeted by this administration for speaking out, for conducting oversight of the executive branch… [The case is] designed both to chill her and to chill the other members who want to engage in…the same kind of conduct and hold the executive branch responsible for what they're doing.”

McIver on defending and serving her district

“Making sure that my duties as a member representing the 10th district doesn't fall short at all is something that I was very adamant about when [the Trump administration] charged me. I think that's what they hoped for, that it would cripple me in doing my job… But we’ve delivered thousands of dollars in casework and continue to show up on so many different fronts.

“I'm super just grateful for the support I have in my district… That was the reason that took me to Delaney in the first place. The response that I was getting from my community about the things that they heard and saw happening… So I'm going to continue to… show up for them, and protect them, and fight for them because that's what they elected me to do.”

For additional information on the upcoming developments in McIver’s case, please contact Hanna.Rumsey@mail.house.gov.

title: Moulton Visits Home Base National Center of Excellence to Highlight Veterans’ Mental Healthcare Innovation
text:
CHARLESTOWN, MA—Today, Congressman Seth Moulton (MA-06) visited the Home Base National Center of Excellence to tour its state-of-the-art facilities, meet with leadership, and discuss how federal policy directly impacts mental healthcare for veterans, active-duty service members, and their families.

Guided by retired Brig. Gen. Jack Hammond, Executive Director of Home Base, Congressman Moulton toured Home Base’s outpatient clinic, clinical research labs, and specialized care facilities. The visit focused on addressing the growing pressure on non-profit healthcare providers amid federal funding cuts imposed by the Trump Administration, ongoing staffing shortages at the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), and the urgent need to expand high-impact, innovative treatments for trauma.

"Home Base is filling critical gaps in veteran care by eliminating barriers that too often prevent service members from getting help," said Congressman Seth Moulton. "Whether it's pioneering breakthrough psychedelic research for treatment-resistant PTSD, supporting military families, or delivering care regardless of discharge status, their work sets a national standard. As we face staffing challenges and service reductions across the VA, supporting non-profit leaders like Home Base is essential to keeping our promise to those who served."

Home Base is a partnership between Mass General Brigham, the Red Sox Foundation, and the Wounded Warrior Project’s Warrior Care Network that provides clinical care, intensive treatment programs, and family support services at zero out-of-pocket cost to patients.

title: Nadler, Frost Demand Antitrust Investigation Into Sysco’s $29.1 Billion Acquisition of Restaurant Depot Over Threats of Higher Costs for Restaurants
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman Jerrold Nadler (NY-12) and Congressman Maxwell Alejandro Frost (FL-10) are calling on the Department of Justice (DOJ) and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to closely scrutinize Sysco's proposed $29.1 billion acquisition of Restaurant Depot and investigate its potential anticompetitive effects. In the letter sent to the DOJ and FTC, the Congressmen warn that the deal could reduce competition, drive up costs for independent restaurants, and ultimately make dining out more expensive for consumers:

Restaurant Depot currently operates 166 locations across 35 states and serves more than 700,000 restaurants and food service operators. As a direct competitor to Sysco, Restaurant Depot provides independent restaurants with an important alternative when purchasing food and negotiating prices.

“Soaring food prices are forcing Americans to struggle to put food on the table for their families. The last thing our districts need is another bloated corporation using their unfair market power to raise food prices further. The Department of Justice must take its job seriously by fairly and carefully examining this proposed transaction to ensure that American consumers are protected,” said Congressman Jerry Nadler (NY-12), Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on the Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust Committee on the Judiciary.

“Restaurants are already struggling with rising costs, and eliminating competition in food distribution could make the problem worse. If this merger drives up the cost of food for small restaurants, those costs will ultimately be passed on to consumers. Families can’t afford another hit to their wallets, and that’s why the DOJ and FTC need to closely scrutinize this deal,” said Congressman Maxwell Frost (FL-10).

"Independent restaurants operate on razor-thin margins, and Restaurant Depot gives them an essential alternative to large distributors like Sysco and a critical price benchmark when negotiating with suppliers. If Sysco is allowed to acquire a major competitor, independent restaurants will lose that leverage, face higher food costs, and ultimately have little choice but to pass those costs on to diners. We thank Representatives Frost and Nadler for urging federal regulators to thoroughly investigate this deal before it does lasting harm to independent restaurants and the communities they serve,” said Erika Polmar, Executive Director Independent Restaurant Coalition.

The proposed acquisition would eliminate a major competitor to Sysco, the nation’s largest food distributor, and could give the company greater leverage over the prices restaurants pay for ingredients and supplies. For independent restaurants operating on already-thin margins, even modest increases in food costs can have significant consequences, including higher prices for customers.

Nadler and Frost warned that the impact of the merger could extend beyond restaurant owners to consumers and workers. If restaurants face higher costs, they may have little choice but to pass those costs on to customers at a time when families are already cutting back on dining out because of rising prices.

The proposed acquisition could also have implications for independent farmers and growers. Sysco has touted the increased purchasing power that would result from the acquisition, raising concerns about how greater market concentration could affect the prices paid to producers.

Nadler and Frost are calling on the Department of Justice and Federal Trade Commission to closely examine the proposed acquisition and launch an antitrust investigation into its potential effects on competition, independent restaurants, farmers, workers, and consumers.

Read the full letter here.

title: Nunn, Subramanyam Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Modernize Reserve Organization of America Charter
text:
DES MOINES, IA — Representatives Zach Nunn (IA-03) and Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10) today introduced the Reserve Organization of America Charter Amendments Act of 2026 to ensure federal law recognizes both enlisted servicemembers and commissioned officers serving in America’s reserve forces.

Founded in 1922, the Reserve Organization of America (ROA), formerly known as the Reserve Officers Association, is the only Congressionally chartered organization exclusively dedicated to advocating for America’s Reserve and National Guard — across all ranks and services.

“After more than two decades in uniform, serving in both active duty and the Air Force Reserve, I’ve seen firsthand how our Reserve forces have evolved to meet new challenges and keep our country safe,” said Rep. Nunn. “ROA has evolved right alongside them, expanding to represent servicemembers of every rank, but its federal charter hasn’t kept up. Our bipartisan bill brings that charter into the 21st century, cuts outdated red tape, and gives ROA greater flexibility to serve the men and women who defend our nation.”

The legislation updates ROA’s outdated federal charter to reflect the organization it is today, including its expansion to represent servicemembers of every rank and reserve component. Because ROA is Congressionally chartered, outdated requirements written into federal law can only be changed by Congress. This bipartisan bill gets that done by officially recognizing the Reserve Organization of America name, cutting decades-old red tape, and giving ROA greater control over its own governance, headquarters, and day-to-day operations.

Nearly 9,000 Iowans serve in the Army and Air National Guard, with thousands more answering the call in reserve components across the Armed Forces. Rep. Nunn currently serves alongside them as a Colonel in the Air Force Reserve, continuing more than two decades of military service that began as an airborne intelligence officer.

“Modernizing ROA’s charter will ensure that it can continue to advocate for reservists and their families for the next 75 years and beyond,” said Rep. Subramanyam. “I look forward to continuing to partner together on these efforts and championing impactful legislation to support our servicemembers.”

Specifically, the Reserve Organization of America Charter Amendments Act would:

Recognize every rank that serves by officially changing ROA’s name in federal law from the Reserve Officers Association to the Reserve Organization of America.

Modernize ROA’s federal charter by giving the organization greater control over its own governing structure and headquarters, rather than locking those decisions into federal law.

Cut administrative red tape by replacing burdensome multi-state agent filing requirements with a single registered agent in Washington, D.C.

Maintain strong accountability standards by prohibiting ROA from operating for profit, issuing stock, contributing to political campaigns, or making loans to its officers or governing body members.

The Reserve Organization of America Charter Amendments Act of 2025 is the House companion to bipartisan legislation introduced by Senators Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) and Richard Blumenthal (D-CT).

Text of the bill can be found here.

title: Rep. Omar Statement on One Year Anniversary of the Annunciation Catholic School Shooting
text:
MINNEAPOLIS – Today, Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-MN) released the following statement to commemorate the one year anniversary of the mass shooting at Annunciation Catholic School in her district.

"Today, our community gathers to remember Fletcher Merkel and Harper Moyski, honor the survivors, and stand with every child, family, educator, parishioner, and first responder whose life was forever changed by the tragedy at Annunciation one year ago.

"Fletcher and Harper were targeted while doing something so innocent: sitting in prayer at the first all-school Mass of the school year. As a mother, I cannot imagine the heartbreak their families have endured. As a Minneapolis resident and your representative, my heart remains utterly shattered. I refuse to accept that this is the reality our children must grow up in.

"Annunciation Church has been a fixture of our Southside community for more than 100 years. My district office is just 10 minutes away, and members of my staff have deep ties to this church. They have celebrated weddings, baptisms, and first communions there. This tragedy struck not only a school and a parish, but a community that we hold close to our hearts.

"At the heart of today is a simple belief: one meaningful way we can remember is by showing up for others and moving our feet. Through acts of service and generosity, we can carry forward the love, courage, and care that have surrounded the Annunciation community over the past year. But remembrance must also be coupled with action.

"Gun violence is the number one killer of children and teens. Our leaders at every level of government have an obligation to confront this crisis and keep our children safe. As a legislator, I continue to be ashamed by the lack of political will to act, even after Columbine, Parkland, Uvalde, and far too many other tragedies. We must do whatever is within our power to protect our kids.

"It should not be controversial to pass commonsense lifesaving measures, including banning assault weapons and high-capacity magazines. Our elected leaders should care more about the safety of our children than protecting access to weapons of war.

"We owe it to Fletcher and Harper, to the survivors, and to every single child who deserves to feel safe at school and in a house of worship to do everything in our power to prevent this from ever happening again."
