title: Congresswoman Luz Rivas Introduces Bill to Expand Access to Undergraduate Research STEM Programs
text:
LOS ANGELES – Congresswoman Luz Rivas (CA-29), co-chair of the STEM Education Caucus, introduced the National Science Foundation’s (NSF) Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU) Act of 2026. This bill reauthorizes and modernizes the NSF REU program that has strengthened undergraduate STEM research pathways since 2010.

“Every college student, regardless of their background, deserves the opportunity to engage in STEM research, gain new experiences in the lab, and understand what a potential STEM career could be,” said Congresswoman Rivas. “Opportunities for STEM education experiences should not be limited because of where students go to school. My NSF REU Act expands access to undergraduate research experiences and opportunities to students at minority-serving institutions, community colleges, emerging research institutions, and rural-serving institutions. By strengthening learning opportunities for all students, we can develop a more inclusive and robust STEM workforce that will keep the United States a leader in innovation and technology.”

Background:

The National Science Foundation’s (NSF) Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU) Act of 2026 strengthens pathways into STEM careers by prioritizing first-time research participants and students from underrepresented and underserved backgrounds. It expands NSF’s flexibility to support student professional development, mentor training, institutional partnerships, and long-term program evaluation. The legislation reinforces the role of experiential learning in building the STEM workforce, while improving access for students at minority-serving institutions, community colleges, emerging research institutions, and rural-serving institutions.

The NSF REU Act of 2026 would expand access to high-quality undergraduate research experiences and modernize program implementation. Key aspects of this legislation include:

Updates statute to be consistent with NSF’s current implementation of the program;

Provides NSF further flexibility to support undergraduate research, including support for student professional development, faculty supplements to promote community college participation, mentorship training to broaden participation in STEM, and program evaluation and data collection activities;

Clarifies one of the primary intents of the program is to provide first-time research experiences to individuals with limited or no prior experience in STEM or individuals belonging to groups; and

Authorizes an appropriation sum of $100 million per year for fiscal years 2027 through 2032.

title: Congressman Dr. Ruiz Honors FIND Regional Food Bank CEO Debbie Espinosa with Congressional Record Entry
text:
INDIO, CA — In mid-July, Congressman Dr. Ruiz (CA-25) gave remarks on the floor of the United States House of Representatives in Washington, DC, honoring Debbie Espinosa, outgoing CEO of FIND Regional Food Bank, for her years of dedicated service to California's 25th Congressional District. These remarks were entered in the nation’s Congressional Record and on Thursday, August 27, Congressman Dr. Ruiz joined the Coachella Valley community for a surprise celebration marking Espinosa's departure, held at FIND's Indio headquarters, where he presented her with a framed copy of those remarks as a lasting tribute to her leadership. The event brought together an intimate group of community members, FIND staff, and local leaders to celebrate Espinosa's contributions to our communities. Espinosa is departing the Coachella Valley to lead Harvesters, a regional food bank network serving Missouri and Kansas.

During her tenure, Espinosa led FIND through a period of significant growth, including the groundbreaking and ribbon-cutting of a new 40,000-square-foot warehouse that expanded the food bank's storage capacity and created new workforce development pathways. Under her leadership, FIND organized emergency food distributions for federal employees affected by government shutdowns and helped bring the stories of farmworker families to Washington, D.C., where Espinosa briefed members of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus.

"Debbie has been more than a community partner to me and to this district. She has been a trusted collaborator, someone I could call in the middle of a crisis and know she would show up," said Congressman Dr. Ruiz. "She never simply distributed food. She built bridges, connecting federal resources to local solutions, connecting policymakers to the families they serve, and connecting our communities to hope in their hardest moments. She did it with compassion, and she did it with professionalism, and she never lost sight of the people at the center of it all.

title: FOLLOWING 50% TARIFF LEVIED ON CANADA, REP. SCHNEIDER, SENATORS GILLIBRAND AND WELCH INTRODUCE BILL TO REPEAL SECTION 338 AND REFUND TARIFFS
text:
LINCOLNSHIRE, IL – Today, Congressman Brad Schneider, a member of the House Ways and Means Trade Subcommittee, together with Senators Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) and Peter Welch (D-VT), introduced the Banning Antiquated Duties and Delivering Equitable American Levies (BAD DEAL) Act to repeal Section 338 and refund all duties paid under this authority. Over the weekend, trade talks between the United States and Canada broke down, resulting in the U.S. imposing 50% tariffs on Canada under Section 338. In response, Canada is pledging dollar-for-dollar retaliatory tariffs slated to come into effect after Labor Day. Canada is Illinois’ largest export market, with over $19 billion in exports in 2024.

In 2025, Rep. Schneider introduced the Repealing Outdated and Unilateral Tariff Authorities Act which would repeal Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930. A recent report from the Midwest Economic Policy Institute shows that average household costs for Illinois families have increased by $2,200 as a result of Trump’s tariffs.

Earlier this year, Rep. Schneider brought the CEO Learning Resources, the named plaintiff in the Supreme Court case on Trump’s tariffs, as his State of the Union Guest days after the Supreme Court ruled Trump’s tariffs under IEEPA were illegal.

“Every American deserves a fair shot to get ahead, and Trump’s capricious and costly tariffs are making it exceedingly difficult to simply make ends meet,” said Schneider. “President Trump’s brazen and counterproductive trade war only damages the long-standing, mutually beneficial relationship with our neighbor, and second largest trading partner, Canada. This is a bad deal! It’s a bad deal for American families, and it’s a bad deal for American small businesses. I’m proud to work with my colleagues to introduce the aptly named BAD DEAL Act to repeal this outdated tariff authority AND refund the tariff duties paid. We will continue fighting to rein in Trump’s costly tariffs and reassert Congress’ authority before his on-again, off-again trade policy damages our international relationships for years to come.”

“President Trump and Republicans promised to lower costs and make life more affordable, but they’ve used their total power in Washington to make life more expensive than ever,” said Gillibrand. “Let’s be clear: the latest tariffs against Canada are a bad deal for New York families. I’m proud to introduce this legislation to end these costly tariffs and refund Americans. It’s past time for President Trump to stop the political games, get back to the negotiation table, and make a deal that lowers costs and strengthens our economy.”

“No good will come of this trade war with Canada. The only thing these tariffs will create is economic pain on both sides of the border, especially for Vermont and the other 33 states that rely on Canada as their largest trading partner,” said Welch. “Imposing on-again, off-again tariffs is the opposite of how we should treat our close friends and longtime allies, but it’s endemic to how the Trump Administration operates. I’m proud to join my colleagues in leading the BAD DEAL Act to repeal these reckless tariffs and reclaim Congress’ constitutional role in setting our trade policy.”

Cosponsors of the BAD DEAL Act include Reps. Don Beyer (VA-08), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), Tim Kennedy (NY-26), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), Terri Sewell (AL-07), Greg Stanton (AZ-04), and Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10).

title: Rep. Peters and Healthcare, Childcare Providers Denounce Trump Administration’s Threats to Child Welfare
text:
San Diego, CA – Today, Rep. Scott Peters convened children’s healthcare and childcare providers to increase awareness of President Trump and HHS Secretary Kennedy’s recent changes that threaten children’s health and wellbeing.

In early August, the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) announced proposed rule changes to Head Start, the nation's early education program for children from low-income families. The move would diminish the program's federal standards and give states and parents more control. A few weeks later, President Trump signed an Executive Order that alters the childhood vaccine schedule and promotes his widely discredited theories about vaccines.

“Back to school season should be an exciting time with new opportunities for kids to learn and grow. But this year, too many parents are forced to worry about the welfare of their children thanks to recent changes from the Trump Administration that threaten their ability to thrive,” said Rep. Peters. “The bottom line is that vaccines keep kids healthy. Head Start ensures every child has an equal opportunity to succeed. Yet from every angle, the Trump Administration’s deregulation efforts set kids up for failure.”

“My message is simple: San Diego Unified will continue following the advice from early childhood medical experts, not politically influenced directives that are in no way based on scientific evidence,” said San Diego Unified School Board Vice President Sabrina Bazzo. “We will keep advocating, alongside Congressman Peters, for full Head Start funding and for vaccine guidance based on data, not ideology. Because we are committed to doing everything in our power to ensure the health and safety of our students.”

“August is back-to-school season for children across California, where they'll spend time learning, playing, and yes, sharing germs,” said Pia Pannaraj, MD, MPH, American Academy of Pediatrics - California Chapter 3 (AAP-CA3). “Non-expert changes to child and adolescent immunization recommendations needlessly put the health and well-being of kids and our communities at risk and create more confusion for parents and caregivers. Here's what I tell parents who come to my clinic with questions: despite the confusing and conflicting information out there, the science hasn't changed. Your pediatricians continue to follow the American Academy of Pediatrics' immunization recommendations because they help keep kids healthy, in the classroom, and ahead of serious, preventable diseases. I encourage parents with questions or concerns to talk with their child's pediatrician.”

“We must keep the promise and build Head Start for what’s next. Fewer rules cannot equal fewer results,” said Damon Carson, General Manager, Neighborhood House Association. “Fewer hours, more turnover, or less experienced staff may save money on one line of a budget, but they create costs somewhere else – for programs, families, and children. And the more resources we have, the earlier we can identify a concern, and the earlier a family can act. Neighborhood House Association staff, families, and partners can submit their own comments on the proposed rules at regulations.gov before the October 6 deadline.”

“The YMCA of San Diego County is dedicated to community well-being and belonging. Alongside critical community partners, we support wholistic family health, which includes access to early care and education,” said Courtney Baltiyskyy, Vice President of Policy & Advocacy, YMCA of San Diego County. “As one of the largest childcare and after school providers in the county, the Y strengthens the broader childcare landscape by supporting families, providers, and employers while advancing systems that work better for everyone. When we think about a thriving San Diego, we know a continuum of quality care and education includes our valuable Head Start programs.”

President Trump's most recent Executive Order on childhood vaccines would stagger the administration of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine. Public health experts have raised concerns that this creates an increased risk of infection. As kids begin the new school year and during National Immunization Awareness Month, Rep. Peters is calling attention to these changes and encouraging parents to speak out and protect their children.

Simultaneously, the regulatory changes to Head Start would deregulate the program’s student-teacher ratios, staff qualifications, child development screenings, background checks, and safety rules. These rules are not final and are currently in a public comment period until October 6, 2026. San Diegans can share their thoughts on the proposed changes here.

A livestreamed recording of the press conference can be viewed here. Additional photos from the event, courtesy of the office of Rep. Scott Peters, can be viewed here.

title: Rep. Sewell Celebrates the FDA Approval of a New Drug for Pancreatic Cancer
text:
Birmingham, AL - Today, U.S. Rep. Terri Sewell (AL-07) celebrated the Food and Drug Administration's approval of daraxonrasib, a new drug for treating advanced pancreatic cancer. This drug, taken as two pills a day, is the first treatment that substantially extends the lives of patients with pancreatic cancer.

"This is incredible news," celebrated Rep. Sewell. "No family in America has been spared the scourge of cancer, including my own. Having lost my mother, the late Nancy Gardner Sewell, to pancreatic cancer, I know firsthand the heartbreak and devastation this disease can bring to a family. That is why I am overjoyed to join millions of Americans in celebrating this historic victory which will help revolutionize the way we treat pancreatic cancer."

"The FDA’s approval of daraxonrasib offers new hope to pancreatic cancer patients and their loved ones, and represents a remarkable step forward in our fight against one of the deadliest forms of cancer," continued Rep. Sewell. "Breakthroughs like this one highlight why we must continue investing in lifesaving research - so that one day we will not only be able to treat pancreatic cancer, but cure it!”

Pancreatic cancer is one of the deadliest major cancers, with a five-year survival rate below 20%. This cutting-edge drug, which will be sold under the brand name Rasonque, was approved for patients who have metastatic pancreatic cancer and have already tried chemotherapy. In clinical trials, participants who received daraxonrasib lived for a median of over 13 months, compared with less than seven months for those who received chemotherapy. Some patients who have gotten the drug through clinical trials have lived for years.

This new breakthrough comes just months after the passage of the Nancy Gardner Sewell Multi-Cancer Early Detection Act, a bipartisan law that ensures seniors on Medicare can get access to the latest lifesaving cancer screening tests. Co-sponsored by Rep. Terri Sewell (D-AL) and Rep. Jodey Arrington (R-TX), the bill was one of the most sponsored bill in the 199th Congress with 339 House co-sponsors and 68 Senate co-sponsors and was signed into law by President Trump on February 3, 2026.

title: Brown, Wyden Call for GAO Investigation After DOT Fails to Protect Airline Passenger Data
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Shontel Brown (OH-11) and U.S. Senator Ron Wyden (D-OR) are urging the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to investigate the Department of Transportation’s (DOT) ongoing failure to protect passenger privacy using its authority to regulate the practices of commercial airlines and ticket agents. Brown serves as Ranking Member of the House Oversight Subcommittee on Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation.

A copy of the full letter sent to the GAO is available here.

For over four decades, the DOT has held exclusive jurisdiction over safeguarding passenger data; nonetheless, a Congressional Research Service evaluation reveals the agency has failed to execute a single privacy enforcement measure, despite severe breaches impacting hundreds of millions of commuters. This prolonged inaction exposes confidential travel information to corporate data mining, federal monitoring, and security risks from hostile foreign nations.

“DOT’s abdication of its role as a privacy regulator has left the sensitive personal information of hundreds of millions of Americans exposed to corporate exploitation, warrantless government surveillance, and warrantless seizure of money and other property,” the lawmakers wrote in letter to Acting Comptroller General Orice W. Brown. “In addition to harming the public, DOT’s regulatory inaction also potentially threatens national security. Travel data held by airlines and travel agencies may be of interest to foreign adversaries, who could exploit such information to track U.S. military, diplomatic, and other U.S. government personnel.”

Historically, DOT has taken a reactive approach to airline privacy, relying on consumer complaints instead of proactively auditing airlines’ privacy practices. In March 2024 Senator Wyden partnered with the DOT to launch a first-ever industry-wide review into the privacy practices of the nation’s 10 largest airlines. More than two years later, DOT has not publicly released its findings or announced any enforcement actions.

The need for stronger DOT oversight is clear. For years, a data broker collectively owned by major U.S. airlines, the Airline Reporting Corporation (ARC) provided federal agencies access to roughly 722 million passenger travel records without warrants or judicial oversight. ARC shut down the program in November 2025, but DHS has since sought a replacement passenger-surveillance system.

Brown and Wyden asked the GAO to launch a comprehensive investigation into the DOT’s systemic failure to fulfill its consumer privacy enforcement responsibilities, by answering the following questions:

Status of the 2024 Airline Privacy Review: Provide a full accounting of the status, findings, and disposition of the industry-wide review launched on March 21, 2024.

Audit of Agency Personnel and Technical Expertise: Identify the exact number of full-time personnel within the OACP currently dedicated exclusively to privacy enforcement, including the number of technologists.

Audit of Interagency Coordination on DEA Informants: Review the interagency coordination between DOT and the Department of Justice (DOJ) over airline employees selling passenger data to the Drug Enforcement Agency (DEA), including any delays and actions taken to hold airlines accountable.

Agency Response to Widespread Public Scandals: Evaluate whether DOT independently investigated ARC’s sale of passenger records or took action only after congressional and media pressure led to the program’s closure in November 2025.

Structural Nature of the Complaint-Driven Model: Examine why DOT relies on a complaint-driven model instead of routine privacy audits.

Assessment of Insider Threat Mitigation and Data Governance: Evaluate whether the DOT has established guidelines regarding airlines’ protection of Passenger Name Record (PNR) databases against insider threats.

International Data Commitments: Explain how DOT’s domestic privacy enforcement since July 2023 aligns with its commitments to the European Commission under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework (DPF).

The lawmakers asked GAO to respond with legislative recommendations to strengthen DOT’s enforcement authority and better protect travelers’ privacy rights.

“If the DOT continues to neglect its domestic regulatory obligations, it risks undermining the integrity of this entire agreement, potentially collapsing transatlantic data flows and destroying vital economic benefits for U.S. companies,” the law makers concluded.

title: Congresswoman Simon Secures Federal Funding to Create New Community Plaza Adjacent to Ashby BART and Expand Open Space in South Berkeley
text:
BERKELEY, CA – Congresswoman Lateefah Simon (D-CA-12) recently secured $850,000 in federal Community Project Funding (CPF) for the City of Berkeley to design new public open spaces along Adeline Street, including a new main plaza adjacent to the future transit-oriented development on the west parking lot of the Ashby Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) station.

The federal funding will support the design of a vibrant community plaza and other public open spaces for South Berkeley that will complement new housing, including affordable housing, as well as new commercial and community spaces. The project will also improve access to the BART station, including pedestrian and ADA access.

Last week, the Congresswoman announced the funding alongside Mayor of Berkeley Adena Ishii, Berkeley City Councilmember Ben Bartlett, BART General Manager Bob Powers, BART Board Director Barnali Ghosh, and community partners.

As a disability and transit justice advocate, Congresswoman Simon has long to create vibrant communities where there is equitable housing development near affordable and accessible transit. Additionally, during her time as BART Board President, she led on redeveloping the Ashby BART station. In Congress, Congresswoman Simon has also introduced the Connecting Communities Through Transit Planning Act, which would make permanent and expand the Pilot Program for Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Planning to support housing projects near new or existing transit corridors.

“I helped jumpstart and plan the Ashby BART station transit-oriented development project when I served as BART Board President – and I am extremely proud to now secure nearly a million in federal funding to further the process on a new plaza that will complement the Ashby BART transit-oriented development,” said Congresswoman Simon. “Transforming this public space along Adeline Street into a plaza where people can live, work, and play near affordable and accessible transit will be game changing and create more vibrant, connected communities that succeed both economically and culturally.”

“I'm proud to join Congresswoman Simon in announcing this $850,000 investment in South Berkeley. It's one of our most diverse communities, and it's been underinvested in and underserved for too long. Now, we're changing that,” said Mayor of Berkeley, Adena Ishii. “This project looks to create a future of greater economic opportunity and better access for people with disabilities, complementing the new housing already planned for Adeline Street.”

This Community Project Funding (CPF) is a part of the $11.2 million dollars that Congresswoman Simon secured for 15 projects across the East Bay in Fiscal Year 2026. Each fiscal year, members of Congress can submit Community Project Funding requests for consideration with the House Committee on Appropriations.You can read about the 15 projects that Congresswoman Simon secured funding for in her first year here.

title: Rep. Simpson Advances Funding for Aberdeen Research and Extension Center
text:
WASHINGTON—Idaho Congressman Mike Simpson highlighted the inclusion of $5,000,000 in funding for the USDA-ARS University of Idaho Aberdeen Research and Extension Center Potato Breeding Facilities Project in Aberdeen, Idaho, at his request through Community Project Funding (CPF) in the House-passed Fiscal Year 2027 Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration Appropriations Bill.

“Potatoes are one of Idaho’s most important crops, and our state leads the nation in production,” said Rep. Simpson. “The University of Idaho has conducted phenomenal research on various crops and provided valuable information to producers about these key agricultural products. As the University continues to expand its research to meet industry needs, it is crucial that funding keeps pace with the research efforts. I am proud to support this project, and as we continue to support the potato industry, we should strive for the goal that ten out of ten Americans associate potatoes with Idaho, rather than just nine out of ten!”

“We are thankful for Congressman Simpson’s continued support and advocacy for Idaho agriculture,” said Leslie D. Edgar, J.R. Simplot Endowed Dean of the University of Idaho College of Agricultural and Life Sciences. “Funds secured by Congressman Simpson will allow us to make critical updates to potato storage and greenhouse facilities at our Aberdeen Research and Extension Center, advancing the essential research we conduct in partnership with USDA-ARS. These updates will allow us to better support Idaho’s $8.5 billion potato industry and ensure the U.S. has resilient potato varieties for the future.”

“Congressman Simpson’s support for the Aberdeen Research and Extension Center represents a meaningful investment in the future of Idaho agriculture. Advances in potato breeding and research are vital to improving productivity, sustainability, and resilience for our growers, and this funding helps ensure they remain competitive in a rapidly changing environment,” said Matt Dorsey, Idaho Farm Bureau Federation President.

“On behalf of Idaho's potato industry, I extend my heartfelt thanks to Congressman Simpson and the House Appropriations Committee for advancing the Fiscal Year 2027 Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration Appropriations Bill that includes critical funding for the Aberdeen Research and Extension Center. This investment ensures Idaho will continue to lead the nation—and the world—in cutting-edge potato research, supporting our growers, strengthening our Nation’s food security, and driving innovation for years to come,” said Jamey Higham, Idaho Potato Commission President.

This funding will be used to update federally owned storage and greenhouse facilities at the Aberdeen Research and Extension Center to ensure it can continue conducting the necessary research needed by the potato industry. The Aberdeen Research and Extension Center is home to several potato research projects investigating potato-related diseases and disease management techniques; potato pests; potato cropping systems and weed biology, control, and herbicide resistance; and potato variety development. The center plays a crucial role in the development of potato varietals that are higher-yielding, more disease-resistant, and have better end-use qualities than past varieties.

As Idaho’s only appropriator, Rep. Simpson has a unique opportunity to fight for Idaho’s priorities and ensure Idahoans’ hard-earned tax dollars return to Idaho.

title: Rep. Steube Introduces SHIELD Act to Protect Parental Rights in Schools
text:
Rep. Steube Introduces SHIELD Act to Protect Parental Rights in Schools

WASHINGTON – U.S. Representative Greg Steube (R-Fla.) today introduced the School Health and Instructional Environment Limits and Disclosure (SHIELD) Act, legislation requiring local educational agencies to notify parents before distributing or disseminating information about abortion or abortion-related services to students. The bill also prohibits abortion providers and their subsidiaries from distributing or disseminating such information to students on school grounds or through a school’s virtual platforms, including social media. The SHIELD Act is endorsed by Students for Life Action, a leading national organization fighting to protect the unborn and defend the right to life.

“I believe every child, born and unborn, is made in the image of God and deserves to be protected, not managed behind their parents’ backs. No school employee should ever schedule an abortion for someone else’s daughter and tell her to keep it a secret from her own mother and father,” said Rep. Steube. “I’m fighting for the unborn and I’m fighting for parents, because those two fights are the same fight. The SHIELD Act keeps abortion providers out of our classrooms and puts parents back in charge of these conversations with their kids.”

“‘School Health and Instructional Environment Limits and Disclosure Act,’ better known as the SHIELD Act, provides long-overdue protections for students from a predatory abortion industry infiltrating classrooms to push deadly abortions – without any parental involvement. Rep. Greg Steube’s bill has SFLAction’s full support as he works to ensure that when it comes to talking with kids about life-ending abortions, parents are engaged. Planned Parenthood’s own annual report makes it clear that they start marketing early, infiltrating schools to build a customer base for life. Parents need to know what schools are teaching their children and need to be sure that when they send a child to school, their grandchildren are not being targeted by school officials who cut those who care most from a life-and-death decision. We all saw the chaos in Fairfax County, Virginia, just outside of Washington, D.C., where Students for Life rallied against secret school abortions. We will fight to ensure that schools do not become another place for Planned Parenthood to push for abortion deaths for profit and that parents are fully informed about what their children are learning,” said Kristan Hawkins, President, Students for Life of America & Students for Life Action.

This legislation is also co-sponsored by Reps. Harriet Hageman (R-Wyo.), Sheri Biggs (R-S.C.), and Diana Harshbarger (R-Tenn.).

The need for greater parental transparency has been underscored by incidents such as one in Fairfax County, Virginia, where a public high school social worker reportedly scheduled an abortion appointment for a 17-year-old student, paid the associated clinic fees, and instructed the student to conceal the matter from her parents. The U.S. Department of Education has since opened an enforcement action against Fairfax County Public Schools.

Federal law already gives parents the right to inspect instructional materials used in their child’s curriculum and requires parental notice for certain nonemergency, invasive physical examinations or screenings administered by schools. However, no comparable requirement specifically exists when schools distribute or disseminate information about abortion or abortion-related services to students.

Organizations such as Planned Parenthood have used sex education programs, educator training, and classroom instruction to reach K-12 students on abortion-related issues, often with limited parental awareness of the content being presented. Taxpayer-funded schools should not serve as a venue for abortion providers or their affiliates to promote abortion-related information to minors without parents being informed.

The SHIELD Act closes that gap by amending the General Education Provisions Act to require parental notification before abortion-related information is distributed or disseminated to students. The legislation also prohibits abortion providers and their subsidiaries from using K-12 schools or school-operated virtual platforms to distribute abortion-related information to students. The bill defines an “abortion-related service” as any medical, surgical, or support care directly related to terminating a pregnancy.

The full text of the SHIELD Act is available here.

title: Subramanyam, Nunn Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Modernize Reserve Organization of America Charter
text:
Ashburn, VA – U.S. Representatives Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10) and Zach Nunn (IA-03) today introduced the Reserve Organization of America Charter Amendments Act of 2026 to ensure federal law recognizes both enlisted servicemembers and commissioned officers serving in America’s reserve forces.

Founded in 1922, the Reserve Organization of America (ROA), formerly known as the Reserve Officers Association, is the only Congressionally chartered organization exclusively dedicated to advocating for America’s Reserve and National Guard — across all ranks and services.

“Modernizing ROA’s charter will ensure that it can continue to advocate for reservists and their families for the next 75 years and beyond,” said Rep. Subramanyam. “I look forward to continuing to partner together on these efforts and championing impactful legislation to support our servicemembers.”

The legislation updates ROA’s outdated federal charter to reflect the organization it is today, including its expansion to represent servicemembers of every rank and reserve component. Because ROA is Congressionally chartered, outdated requirements written into federal law can only be changed by Congress. This bipartisan bill gets that done by officially recognizing the Reserve Organization of America name, cutting decades-old red tape, and giving ROA greater control over its own governance, headquarters, and day-to-day operations.

Nearly 9,000 Iowans serve in the Army and Air National Guard, with thousands more answering the call in reserve components across the Armed Forces. Rep. Nunn currently serves alongside them as a Colonel in the Air Force Reserve, continuing more than two decades of military service that began as an airborne intelligence officer.

“After more than two decades in uniform, serving in both active duty and the Air Force Reserve, I’ve seen firsthand how our Reserve forces have evolved to meet new challenges and keep our country safe,” said Rep. Nunn. “ROA has evolved right alongside them, expanding to represent servicemembers of every rank, but its federal charter hasn’t kept up. Our bipartisan bill brings that charter into the 21st century, cuts outdated red tape, and gives ROA greater flexibility to serve the men and women who defend our nation.”

Specifically, the Reserve Organization of America Charter Amendments Act would:

Recognize every rank that serves by officially changing ROA’s name in federal law from the Reserve Officers Association to the Reserve Organization of America.

Modernize ROA’s federal charter by giving the organization greater control over its own governing structure and headquarters, rather than locking those decisions into federal law.

Cut administrative red tape by replacing burdensome multi-state agent filing requirements with a single registered agent in Washington, D.C.

Maintain strong accountability standards by prohibiting ROA from operating for profit, issuing stock, contributing to political campaigns, or making loans to its officers or governing body members.

The Reserve Organization of America Charter Amendments Act of 2025 is the House companion to bipartisan legislation introduced by Senators Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) and Richard Blumenthal (D-CT).

Text of the bill can be found here.

title: Rep. Sykes Presents $1,000,000 Ceremonial Check for Cuyahoga Falls Water Treatment Plant Improvement Project

title: Rep. Sykes Presents a $450,000 Ceremonial Checks for Guise Park Lodge Renovation
text:
MUNROE FALLS, OHIO — Yesterday, U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) presented a $450,000 ceremonial check to the City of Munroe Falls for upgrades at the Guise Park Lodge.

“This funding is about making sure everyone, regardless of age or ability, can experience the beauty of Guise Park. These improvements will strengthen local tourism, support our community, and create a more inclusive outdoor space for residents and visitors alike,” said Rep. Sykes. “I will continue to work to secure federal funding to support projects like this that directly benefit residents of Ohio’s 13th Congressional District.”

“I would like to express my appreciation for the grant provided by Emilia Sykes’ Office for funding extended renovations to the Guise Park Lodge,” said Mayor Mavrides. “Thank you for seeing the potential in the project and all of the benefits it will bring to the residents of the City of Munroe Falls.”

This federally funded project would support renovations to Guise Park Lodge and its surrounding grounds. Built in 1957, the lodge is in need of a new roof and accessibility improvements, including ADA-compliant restrooms, an accessible kitchen area, additional accessible walkways, and an ADA-accessible parking space. The project will also include a small accessible outdoor patio and pavilion for visitors. The renovations will provide 24-hour, seven-day-a-week access to ADA-compliant restrooms, while revitalizing the lodge and improving accessibility for residents and visitors of all ages and abilities.

The $450,000 for the Guise Park Lodge Renovation Project is one of 15 Community Project Funding awards totaling more than $12 million that Rep. Sykes secured in the Fiscal Year 2026 federal budget for Ohio's 13th Congressional District. The other projects included in this funding can be foundhere.

title: Congresswoman Tenney Celebrates Fort Drum Selection for Army Janus Nuclear Energy Program
text:
Oswego, NY — Congresswoman Claudia Tenney (NY-24) celebrated the U.S. Army’s selection of Fort Drum as one of five initial installations for the Janus Program, bringing advanced nuclear energy technology to Upstate New York to strengthen Fort Drum’s energy security and mission readiness.

The Janus Program is the Army’s next generation nuclear power initiative designed to provide secure, resilient, and reliable energy for defense installations and critical military missions. Through the program, Fort Drum was selected to receive a 1-megawatt commercial microreactor developed by Westinghouse Government Services. The Army is partnering with the Defense Innovation Unit and private industry to invest $2.2 billion for private sector companies to own, construct, and deploy commercially viable microreactors while accelerating the development of advanced American nuclear technology. As one of the five selected sites, the project will provide Fort Drum with a dedicated source of reliable power and strengthen the installation’s energy resilience following the closure of its previous biomass power facility.

“Fort Drum plays a critical role in our national defense, and secure, reliable power is essential to that mission,” said Congresswoman Tenney. “I am honored to represent so many members of the Fort Drum community, and I fought hard to bring Project Janus to Fort Drum because advanced nuclear technology provides the dependable, around-the-clock energy our military needs while strengthening American leadership in nuclear innovation. This investment will help create a pathway towards commercially viable microreactors, with Fort Drum being one of the first recipients of this new transformative technology that can help provide much-needed baseload power. This selection marks an important investment in Fort Drum, the 10th Mountain Division, and Upstate New York, and I look forward to seeing Project Janus advance the future of American nuclear energy.”

title: Congresswoman Tenney Releases 2026 Tax Plan to Deliver Relief for New York Families, Workers, and Small Businesses
text:
Oswego, NY — Congresswoman Claudia Tenney (NY-24) today released her 2026 Tax Plan, setting forth her priorities to lower taxes, reward work, support families and seniors, strengthen small businesses and family farms, and encourage investment and economic growth across New York’s 24th Congressional District.

As a member of the House Ways and Means Committee, the chief tax-writing committee in Congress, Rep. Tenney has worked to advance a tax code that allows Americans to keep more of what they earn while giving businesses the certainty to invest and grow. The Working Families Tax Cuts built on the successes of President Trump’s Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 by codifying permanent relief for individuals and small businesses, a stronger Child Tax Credit and Standard Deduction, protections for family farms from the death tax, and tax relief for tipped and hourly workers, seniors, and families facing childcare costs. Tenney’s 2026 Tax Plan details her vision to continue expanding opportunities for retirement savings, encourage investment in housing and economically distressed communities, and use the tax code to support Main Street businesses and important economic drivers throughout NY-24.

“Families know how to spend their money better than Washington ever will,” said Congresswoman Tenney. “President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts delivered real relief by lowering taxes on workers, families, seniors, farmers, and small businesses. Now we need to build on those wins by creating more opportunities to save, invest, grow a business, and pass a family farm on to the next generation. My Tax Plan is about a simple principle: hardworking New Yorkers should keep more of the money they earn.”

To view Tenney's full 2026 Tax Plan, click here.

title: Congressman Tim Moore Announces $3.8 Million in FEMA Funding for Hurricane Helene Recovery Projects in Lake Lure, Chimney Rock, and Polk County
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. - Today, Congressman Tim Moore (NC-14) announced $3.8 million in federal funding from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) for Hurricane Helene recovery across Lake Lure, Chimney Rock, and Polk County. Projects include critical sewer repairs, dam restoration, and public assistance.

“While it has been nearly two years since Hurricane Helene devastated our communities, significant recovery work remains,” said Congressman Moore. “This additional funding will help restore necessary infrastructure across Lake Lure, Chimney Rock, and Polk County. I appreciate President Trump, Secretary Mullin, and the folks at FEMA for continuing to prioritize Western North Carolina's recovery.”

$1,810,198.80 will go to the Town of Lake Lure for permanent repairs to the sewer collection system following severe damage from Hurricane Helene. This funding is authorized under Section 406 of the Robert T. Stafford Act.

$1,555,804.86 will go to the Town of Lake Lure for permanent repairs to the Lake Lure Dam following Hurricane Helene. The repairs include removing and replacing concrete stairs, chain link fence, dam barrel, traffic signs, crossing sign, and embankment restoration. This funding is authorized under Section 406 of the Robert T. Stafford Act.

$312,717.28 will go to Chimney Rock Village to support management of Public Assistance grants as a result of Hurricane Helene. This funding is authorized under Section 324 of the Robert T. Stafford Act.

$142,298.10 will go to Polk County to support the earthen retention dam and related repairs or replacements following the damage from Hurricane Helene. This funding is authorized under Section 406 of the Robert T. Stafford Act.

title: Underwood Opposes DHS Plans to Spend Millions on Electric Shock Gloves for ICE
text:
WASHINGTON — This week, Rep. Lauren Underwood, a member of the House Homeland Security Appropriations Subcommittee, wrote to the Department of Homeland Security in opposition to recently reported plans to spend up to $20 million to equip U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) personnel with electric shock gloves.

The devices, known as Generated Low Output Voltage Emitters, or G.L.O.V.E., are designed to be worn by officers and administer an electrical shock when an officer makes physical contact with an individual.

“The idea that we would spend millions of taxpayer dollars to put these electric shock gloves on the hands of ICE personnel is disturbing and completely unacceptable,” said Rep. Underwood. “This agency is already out of control, and they cannot be given another tool to terrorize and brutalize our communities. These devices should not be deployed under any circumstances, and I am demanding DHS abandon this procurement.”

The manufacturer of G.L.O.V.E., Compliant Technologies, warns against using the devices on elderly people, small children, pregnant women, and people with severe disabilities. Underwood is demanding answers about what restrictions DHS will place on their use, including protections for vulnerable populations and safeguards to prevent involuntary reactions caused by an electrical shock from being mistaken for resistance and used to justify additional force.

Underwood also raised concerns about accountability, particularly given recent incidents in which DHS’s initial characterization of use of force encounters has been contradicted by video and other evidence, as G.L.O.V.Es can administer shocks without leaving burns, marks, or scars,

The letter comes just weeks after Underwood met with DHS leadership about gaps in body worn camera deployment, where officials cited the significant costs of fully equipping ICE and CBP personnel with cameras. Underwood questioned why DHS is prepared to spend up to $20 million on electric shock gloves while those gaps remain.

title: Rep. Gabe Vasquez Demands Answers on True Cost of Iran War for New Mexican Families
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) sent a letter to President Trump and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth demanding a full public accounting of the economic costs of their cost-raising war of choice with Iran as prices continue to skyrocket for American families.

"What was billed as a two-week operation is now a full-scale war that has lasted for over 150 days, cost at least $37 billion, and claimed the lives of 18 servicemembers. At the same time, prices across the country have gone up significantly, placing the burden of this conflict on American families.” wrote Vasquez. “This uncertainty, and the months of higher costs have taken a toll, impacting Americans’ ability to budget, plan, and save for the future. These costs are untenable, and the American people deserve better."

“The President lied to the American people about no more forever wars. It’s clear there is no exit plan or any sense of a coherent strategy while prices surge at the gas pump and the grocery store, deeply hurting everyday Americans,” said Vasquez. “This war is costing taxpayers billions, skyrocketing our national debt, depleting our critical munitions stockpile, and putting our servicemen and women in continued danger. Americans deserve to know the true cost of this war, and I can already tell you, it’s too damn much.”

The letter demands for information on the cost of military operations, changes in the oil and energy markets, and larger economic impacts. The request follows the Department of Defense’s supplemental request for tens of billions more to fund the ongoing war in Iran and concerns about the risks for American military personnel.

Read the full letter HERE.

title: Vindman Hears from the Virginians on the Merger Between Dominion Energy and NextEra Energy, 80% are Opposed
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) heard from more than 950 Virginians in a district-wide survey, and the results were clear: respondents overwhelmingly oppose the merger between Dominion Energy and NextEra Energy.

“Virginians have made their voices heard loud and clear: they do not want a merger that puts corporate profits ahead of affordable, reliable energy,” said Vindman. “More than 950 people in Virginia’s Seventh District took the time to tell me that they oppose this deal. Many of them are deeply concerned about the impact it could have on their utility bills. I share their concern. Virginians should not be forced to pay more so that Wall Street investors can increase profits. The Virginia State Corporation Commission should listen to the people it represents and reject this merger.”

The survey asked constituents whether they supported or opposed the merger and gauged their level of concern about potential increases in household utility bills. Earlier this month, Vindman sent a letter to members of the Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC) urging them to reject the proposed merger.

Below are responses submitted by Virginia’s Seventh District residents who took the survey:

—

“Large mergers never help the lower and middle class consumers.” – Paul, Spotsylvania

“This change would be a catastrophe for many individuals in this area.” – Gwen, Prince William

“Virginia has enough local monopolies jacking up prices. This will only harm families that are already facing increased energy costs.” – Tristan, Fredericksburg

“We are already paying high utility bills and it would be hard to add more. A lot of people are already having problems bringing food to the table.” – Rose, Prince William

“I oppose this merger. At a time when families are already being asked to absorb the costs, we need greater accountability and competition, not greater consolidation.” – Kristen, Culpeper

“I’m afraid a merger of energy companies this size will raise rates to where the average person will have a difficult time paying for energy.” – Kevin, Caroline

BACKGROUND

NextEra is well-known for having implemented what many recognize as the largest residential electricity rate increase in history at the end of 2025. High energy bills already top the list of concerns for Virginians and Vindman has heard from hundreds of families who will not be able to endure record-setting rate hikes on top of their existing burdens.

Between May 2021-May 2026, Floridians who rely on NextEra’s subsidiary, Florida Power & Light, have seen their utility bills rise by 33 percent.

As a founding member of the Congressional Lowering Utility Bills Caucus, Vindman has been a champion for bringing down utility costs.

In May, he introduced the Home Energy Affordability Act, legislation that would help protect consumers from repeated utility rate hikes by limiting electric utilities to one rate increase request every 365 days. This bill is based on a proposal that has received overwhelming support from constituents across Virginia’s Seventh District and would amend the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 to require states to consider policies restricting how often regulated electric utilities can seek rate increases.

He also introduced the Utility Hikes Transparency Act, legislation that would create the first comprehensive, machine-readable federal database of retail utility rate changes in the United States. The tracker would be updated quarterly which would include approved and effective electric and natural gas utility rate changes for investor-owned utilities, cooperatives, and municipally owned utilities nationwide.

title: Vindman Meets with Leaders from Fredericksburg Health Care Center, Productive Discussion on How to Decrease Wait Times
text:
Fredericksburg, Va. — On Monday, August 24, immediately following a roundtable with veterans in the community, Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) and Senator Tim Kaine (D-Va.) met with key leaders at the Fredericksburg VA Health Care Center (HCC). This meeting was a direct response to Vindman’s repeated calls for action to reduce wait times and improve care at this state-of-the-art facility.

After the productive meeting at the HCC, Vindman released the below statement.

“This week’s meeting with leadership at the Fredericksburg VA Health Care Center was productive and laid the groundwork for continued collaboration between the Department of Veterans Affairs and my office.

“I shared what I heard directly from local veterans at a roundtable earlier that day about staffing, access to care, and communication, and we discussed concrete steps the VA and my office can take together to address these challenges.

“I appreciate VA leadership coming to the table and acknowledging that too many veterans are still facing unreasonable wait times and delays. I feel confident that we will keep fighting, together, to make sure this facility is fully equipped to serve every veteran who depends on it. My office will continue to share updates on the tangible steps we take as a result of yesterday’s conversations.”

BACKGROUND

On Monday, August 24, Vindman hosted a roundtable with veterans from the community to discuss their experiences with the Fredericksburg VA Health Care Center. The roundtable helped highlight veterans’ stories, renewing the call to increase transparency and accountability at the VA.

In mid-July 2026, over 200 Virginians responded to a survey from Vindman about the delays they experienced at the Fredericksburg VA Health Care Center. He personally called over 30 of these veterans to express his commitment to demanding better from the VA.

In June 2026, Vindman introduced bipartisan legislation to increase transparency and accountability at the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), helping address understaffing at facilities across the country, including the Fredericksburg VA Health Care Center, and ensure veterans receive the care they earned.

Prior to that, Vindman called for accountability and a clear timeline to bring the facility to full capacity, ensuring our nation’s veterans receive the care they earned through their service in six different letters.

title: Walkinshaw, Amo, Kelly, Markey Lead 134 Colleagues in Demanding Release of More Than $3 Billion in Lifesaving Global Health Funding
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11), a member of the House Oversight and Government Reform Subcommittee on Military and Foreign Affairs, Congressman Gabe Amo (RI-01), Congresswoman Robin Kelly (IL-02), and Senator Edward J. Markey (D-MA) led 134 of their colleagues in calling on Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought to immediately release $7.5 billion in international affairs funding, to include more than $3 billion in congressionally appropriated global health funding before it expires on September 30, 2026.

In a bicameral letter to Rubio and Vought, the lawmakers warned that approximately $7.5 billion in international affairs funding remains unobligated and at risk of expiring, including more than $3 billion intended for lifesaving global health programs.

The Global Health Programs account supports efforts to combat HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria, maternal and child health, malnutrition, and emerging health threats. According to the letter, OMB has notified Congress that approximately $1.35 billion is being withheld for costs associated with closing the U.S. Agency for International Development instead of being used for the critical global health programs Congress funded.

The lawmakers warned that allowing the funding to expire could contribute to an estimated 121,000 deaths from tuberculosis, 47,600 deaths from malaria, and the loss of lifesaving nutrition products for 22.9 million children.

“This hardship can be prevented if the Administration spends these funds as Congress directed,” the lawmakers wrote. “We call on you to immediately release the remaining lifesaving, bipartisan GHP funding before it expires on September 30, 2026.”

The letter also raises concerns about proposed changes to the President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief, or PEPFAR, which has saved more than 26 million lives. The lawmakers warned that reducing the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s role in the program could disrupt HIV treatment, weaken global disease surveillance, and limit America’s ability to stop outbreaks abroad before they threaten communities at home.

“The Department and OMB’s refusal to spend GHP funding as directed by Congress and the concerning PEPFAR implementation changes defy the law and threaten lives, internationally and in the U.S.,” the lawmakers wrote.

Walkinshaw, Amo, Kelly, Markey, and their colleagues demanded answers by September 9 regarding the Administration’s plans to release the funding, the costs of terminating USAID programs, and the public-health consequences of reducing the CDC’s role in PEPFAR.

The full text of the letter, including the complete list of 138 signers, is available here.

title: Rep. Whitesides Introduces Legislation to Protect the Antelope Valley by Stopping the Dumping of Sexually Violent Predators in Rural Communities
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Rep. George Whitesides (CA-27) introduced the Stop Predator Dumping Act, legislation that would protect rural communities by mandating a new placement framework for Sexually Violent Predators (SVPs). The bill aims to stop communities from being disproportionately impacted by repeated SVP placements, an issue that has historically burdened areas like the Antelope Valley.

“For too long, communities like the Antelope Valley have been treated as dumping grounds for Sexually Violent Predators, while other areas share none of the burden,” said Rep. Whitesides. “This legislation ensures a fair and transparent approach to SVP placements nationwide. We must prioritize the safety of our communities and ensure no single region is forced to bear this burden alone.”

The current approach to SVP placements in many states has allowed for the concentration of offenders in specific regions, straining local resources and impacting community safety. The Stop Predator Dumping Act would overhaul this system by mandating that states adopt a strict placement framework.

Additionally, the legislation directs the Department of Justice (DOJ) to study, compile, and promulgate best practices to states, ensuring that areas like the Antelope Valley do not bear the brunt of these placements through repeated dumping. To help states execute these new guidelines, the bill establishes a federal grant program to fund the implementation of these best practices at the state and local levels.

Specifically, the Stop Predator Dumping Act would:

Establish strict proximity limits, prohibiting any offenders from being placed within 10 miles of each other.

Prohibit repeated placements in a single county subdivision until all other subdivisions within that county have received a placement.

Implement a strict county cap for counties with populations over 1 million people, ensuring that no single county governing district (such as the Antelope Valley at-large) can house more than 25% of the total SVPs in a county like Los Angeles.

Require the DOJ to study and promulgate best practices to states regarding SVP placements to prevent disproportionate dumping in communities.

Create a new federal grant program to assist states in implementing and carrying out these best practices.

title: Wittman Advocates for Community Project Funding for the Gloucester County Colonial Courthouse
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Rob Wittman (VA-01) highlighted the inclusion of a $750,000 funding request for the Colonial Courthouse in Gloucester County through Community Project Funding (CPF) in the Fiscal Year 2027 Transportation, Housing and Urban Development, and Related Agencies Act. This measure has been approved by the House Appropriations Committee and awaits passage on the House Floor.

During the August district work period, Congressman Wittman traveled across the district to meet with local leaders and discuss his efforts in Washington to secure federal investments for Virginia's First District.

“Gloucester County’s Colonial Courthouse is an important piece of Virginia’s history and a way for residents and tourists to discover more about the origins of our democracy,” said Rep. Wittman. “This funding would help preserve the courthouse for future generations while expanding opportunities for students, residents, and visitors to experience history firsthand. Investing in this historic landmark will also strengthen heritage tourism, support local businesses, and ensure this treasured piece of Gloucester’s history remains accessible for years to come.”

“We are very grateful to Congressman Wittman for his continued support of Gloucester County and for recognizing the importance of preserving our historic assets. The 1766 Colonial Courthouse is such an important part of Gloucester’s history and our community. This funding would help us preserve this special property and ensure it remains a place that our residents and future generations can enjoy. We are excited to see this project included in the appropriations package and truly appreciate Congressman Wittman’s advocacy and partnership with Gloucester County.” - Regine Biggers, the Deputy County Administrator

The funding would be used to preserve and restore the Colonial Courthouse. Built in 1766, the courthouse is one of the community’s most historically and architecturally significant public structures. Restoration will expand educational programming, interpretive exhibits, and public access, allowing students, residents, and visitors to engage directly with the sites where early civic life and Revolutionary-era history unfolded. Federal investment will also generate economic benefits by strengthening heritage tourism, increasing visitation to Main Street businesses, and supporting local jobs in retail, hospitality, and skilled trades involved in the restoration work. Given the scale and cost of preserving structures of this age, federal support is critical to ensuring their long-term stability and continued public use, while delivering lasting cultural and economic value to Gloucester County and the surrounding region.

Community Project Funding (CPF) allows Members of Congress to bring tax dollars back home for district-specific priorities. Members have firsthand knowledge of their district’s needs and can prioritize federal funding for the most critical local projects. For Congressman Wittman, these projects address clear and present needs in communities across Virginia and enjoy broad community support. The federal dollars designated for CPF projects exist within existing budget limits. Community Project Funding gives Congressman Wittman the ability to empower Virginians by ensuring they have a critical voice in directing their federal tax dollars back into VA-01 communities.

title: Womack Hosts House Armed Services Committee Chairman Mike Rogers in Arkansas’s Third District
text:
ARKANSAS—August 27, 2026... Senior member of the House Appropriations Defense Subcommittee Congressman Steve Womack (AR-3) welcomed House Armed Services Committee Chairman Mike Rogers (AL-3) to Arkansas’s Third Congressional District this week. Together, they visited key locations and met with individuals who are contributing to a stronger national defense through advancing research and innovation, as well as bolstering military readiness and global alliances.

Congressman Womack said, “It brings me incredible pride to welcome Chairman Mike Rogers to the Third District and showcase how Northwest Arkansas and the River Valley are integral partners in strengthening our national defense. Chairman Rogers’ leadership in guiding defense policy is crucial to Congress’ efforts to meet the evolving needs of our military, and I am proud of the work happening across our region to support our men and women in uniform. From executing critical missions to developing cutting-edge technologies and capabilities, our district is helping ensure our servicemembers are equipped and prepared to meet emerging threats.”

Chairman Rogers said, “I was excited to visit Arkansas’s Third Congressional District with my friend, Rep. Steve Womack. The U.S. defense industrial base is growing for the first time in many years, and districts like ours are the hub of this innovation. I am thankful to Rep. Womack for his leadership and his steadfast support for our nation’s defense.”

Chairman Rogers oversees the drafting of the annual National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) that authorizes defense policy and spending for the next year. As a senior defense appropriator, Rep. Womack builds on the authorities established in the NDAA to allocate funding to the Department of War (DOW). Rep. Womack has worked closely with Chairman Rogers to secure language to strengthen Arkansas defense equities in the annual NDAA. Read more HERE.

Visit Highlights

During a working lunch at the University of Arkansas, Rep. Womack and Chairman Rogers discussed strategies for safely and efficiently transporting troops and the resources they depend on in contested environments—the central focus of the Sam M. Walton College of Business’ upcoming Contested Logistics Consortium. This event will leverage Northwest Arkansas’s supply chain expertise to help address the complex logistics challenges facing our military.

Rep. Womack and Chairman Rogers toured the Grady E. Harvell Civil Engineering Research and Education Center (CEREC) laboratories where students and researchers are developing rapid-setting cement and other innovative solutions to help our military deploy resources and infrastructure quickly and safely.

At the Multi-User Silicon Carbide (MUSiC) Research and Fabrication Laboratory, Rep. Womack and Chairman Rogers saw firsthand how students and researchers are testing the next generation of Silicon Carbide (SiC) electronics to ensure our military always has the technological edge.

Rep. Womack and Chairman Rogers participated in a fireside chat moderated by Arkansas State Chamber of Commerce CEO Randy Zook at the 2026 Mid-America Aerospace and Defense Summit. During their discussion, Rep. Womack highlighted the importance of revitalizing the defense industrial base and maximizing defense spending.

At Ebbing Air National Guard Base, Rep. Womack and Chairman Rogers engaged with commanders of the Arkansas National Guard and 188th Wing—including BG Chad Bridges, CMSgt Scott Manamon, Col. Daniel Wynn, Col. Jonathan Esparza, and CMSgt Jeffrey Weaver—who showcased how the 188th Wing’s current Remote Piloted Aircraft activities and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) F-35 mission are strengthening military readiness and global alliances.

Congressman Steve Womack (AR-3) has represented Arkansas’s Third Congressional District since 2011. He is a member of the House Appropriations Committee.

title: Bennet, Hickenlooper, Luján Demand Trump Administration Comply with Injunction to Ensure Prompt Approvals of Wind and Solar Energy Projects
text:
Denver — Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet, a member of the Senate Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry Committee’s Rural Development and Energy Subcommittee, led Senators John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.) and Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) in a letter to Interior Secretary Doug Burgum to demand that the Department of Interior (DOI) comply with a preliminary injunction to ensure covered wind and solar permitting reviews are conducted promptly without illegal bureaucratic roadblocks.

In July 2025, the DOI released an order requiring Secretary Burgum’s personal approval for routine wind and solar energy project permitting decisions, which led to massive delays in power projects across the West. In November 2025, Bennet, Hickenlooper, and Luján sent a letter demanding answers to the DOI’s order and highlighting its harmful effects to energy prices and reliability, but never received a response.

In April 2026, the U.S. District Court issued a preliminary injunction to prohibit the DOI and its officials from applying the July 2025 order and other internal DOI orders that make wind and solar permitting processes needlessly delayed and difficult while the court case proceeds. Since then, numerous wind and solar developers report that DOI personnel have illegally continued to force project applicants to repeatedly document and prove their eligibility for these court protections.

“[…] Applicants also report that DOI staff have received little or no internal guidance regarding implementation of the Court’s injunction. These reports are not isolated or short-lived: developers continue to describe these delays more than three months after the injunction took effect, indicating an ongoing pattern of noncompliance rather than a transitional implementation issue. DOI’s actions are creating severe regulatory uncertainty, threatening to permanently sideline projects at a time when Western families, farmers, and businesses are facing rising energy demand and higher costs,” wrote the senators.

“Western states depend on reliable and affordable energy to keep our grid secure and our economies competitive. Wind and solar are the least expensive and fastest-to-deploy sources of new electricity generation available. Dragging out permitting timelines in direct violation of a federal court order is not only illegal, but it also needlessly stalls private investment and drives up household energy costs. Furthermore, your recent testimony before the House Natural Resources Committee, where you reportedly rejected the premise of the ruling and called it “absurd” for a judge to dictate internal processes, raises concerns. While DOI has the right to appeal, it is legally obligated to comply with the injunction. Moreover, impeding the deployment of the lowest-cost energy sources directly undermines the administration’s stated goals of unleashing American energy and ensuring affordability,” continued the senators.

Bennet has continuously fought to protect funding for Colorado’s energy projects and condemn partisan project reversals under the Trump administration. In July 2026, Bennet joined Democratic Senate Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) and Senators Patty Murray (D-Wash.), Gary Peters (D-Mich.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), and the entire Senate Democratic caucus in demanding that Director Vought immediately rescind the Office of Management and Budget’s proposed power grab over federal grants and awards. In May 2026, Bennet joined Senator Brian Schatz (D-Hawaii), Schumer, and 18 of their Senate colleagues to introduce legislation to protect public scientific research and reports from the influence of political and special interests.

In October 2025, Bennet issued a statement following the Trump administration’s targeted cancellation of billions of dollars in funding for energy projects across the country. That same week, Bennet led the Democratic Colorado Delegation in demanding answers from Secretary Wright on the Department of Energy’s abrupt cancellation of $7.56 billion in energy project funding, including over $600 million in funding for 38 Colorado-affiliated projects. Additionally, Bennet joined Murray, Heinrich, and 34 Senate colleagues in sending a letter demanding that Secretary Wright and Director Vought restore funding for all 223 energy projects in Democrat-led states that were unlawfully canceled. In November 2025, Bennet also demanded answers from Secretary Burgum on DOI’s recent order requiring Secretary Burgum’s personal approval for routine wind and solar energy project permitting decisions.

The text of the letter is available HERE and below.

Dear Secretary Burgum:

We write to express serious concerns regarding reports of the Department of Interior’s (DOI) failure to fully comply with the U.S. District Court’s April 21, 2026 preliminary injunction in Renew Northeast v. U.S. Department of the Interior, No. 1:25-cv-13961 (D. Mass.). In November 2025, we sent you a letter with questions regarding one of the DOI memos addressed in the case, but never received a response. While this injunction took immediate effect and remains in force, reports from industry participants raise serious questions regarding whether DOI has fully complied with the Court’s injunction.

As you know, the Court’s injunction explicitly prohibits DOI and its officials from applying the DOI Review Procedures Memorandum, the Wind and Solar Fish and Wildlife Service database Ban, Section 4 of the DOI Land Order, Section 4(c) of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Memorandum, and M-Opinion 37086. The Court clearly intended for the covered wind and solar permitting reviews to proceed to timely decisions without these needless bureaucratic roadblocks. Yet, wind and solar developers continue to report that DOI personnel are forcing covered project applicants to repeatedly document and prove their eligibility for these protections, despite the fact that plaintiffs previously provided DOI with a list of covered members. Applicants also report that DOI staff have received little or no internal guidance regarding implementation of the Court’s injunction. These reports are not isolated or short-lived: developers continue to describe these delays more than three months after the injunction took effect, indicating an ongoing pattern of noncompliance rather than a transitional implementation issue. DOI’s actions are creating severe regulatory uncertainty, threatening to permanently sideline projects at a time when Western families, farmers, and businesses are facing rising energy demand and higher costs.

Western states depend on reliable and affordable energy to keep our grid secure and our economies competitive. Wind and solar are the least expensive and fastest-to-deploy sources of new electricity generation available. Dragging out permitting timelines in direct violation of a federal court order is not only illegal, but it also needlessly stalls private investment and drives up household energy costs. Furthermore, your recent testimony before the House Natural Resources Committee, where you reportedly rejected the premise of the ruling and called it “absurd” for a judge to dictate internal processes, raises concerns. While DOI has the right to appeal, it is legally obligated to comply with the injunction. Moreover, impeding the deployment of the lowest-cost energy sources directly undermines the administration’s stated goals of unleashing American energy and ensuring affordability.

To ensure compliance with the law and restore certainty to energy developers and Western stakeholders, we request answers to the following questions:

Internal Guidance – What types of written internal guidance or implementation instructions regarding compliance with the Court’s injunction has DOI provided to staff? Please provide copies of any implementation memoranda, directives, guidance documents, training materials, emails, or other instructions on this topic. If no such materials exist, explain what alternative measures DOI has taken to ensure consistent compliance throughout DOI;

Applicant Identification – What instructions has DOI provided staff for identifying plaintiffs and their members? Please provide communications to DOI staff and explain the steps that DOI is taking to minimize duplicative verification procedures.

Permitting Progress – What steps has DOI taken since the Court injunction to ensure that covered permitting reviews are proceeding to timely agency action? Please identify, by bureau or office where practicable, the number of covered permitting reviews that have advanced since entry of the Court’s injunction, including consultations completed, biological opinions issued, permits or other authorizations issued or denied.

Stalled Reviews – Which covered permitting reviews remain paused or materially delayed following entry of the Court’s injunction? Please provide a list and explain the specific reason for any such delay, including whether it is related to eligibility verification, lack of implementation guidance, application of one of the court-blocked policies, or some other basis. The lists from questions 3 and 4 should add up to the total number of permitting reviews under consideration by DOI between April 21 and now.

We respectfully request a written response to these questions no later than September 1, 2026. We urge you to follow the law and comply with federal court orders to ensure that federal permitting supports, rather than undermines, an affordable and secure energy future.

###

title: Blackburn, Colleagues Introduce Bill to Restore State Authority Over Insurance
text:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. – U.S. Senators Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.), Ted Cruz (R-Texas), Mike Lee (R-Utah), and Rand Paul (R-Ky.) recently reintroduced the Federal Insurance Office Abolishment Act. The legislation would abolish the Federal Insurance Office (FIO) within the U.S. Department of the Treasury, returning sole regulatory authority over the insurance industry to the states.

“Insurance regulation has long been, and should remain, a responsibility of the states,” said Senator Blackburn. “The Federal Insurance Office Abolishment Act would eliminate unnecessary federal overreach, cut red tape, and return power to the states.”

“The Federal Insurance Office is a redundant, ever-expanding, unaccountable entity that infringes upon states’ authority to regulate the insurance industry,” said Senator Cruz. “This legislation will rein in bureaucratic overreach by the federal government and empower state regulators to focus on what is best for consumers in their states.”

“The Federal Insurance Office does not need to exist. It’s an Obama-era expansion of the federal bureaucracy created to intrude on states’ rights,” said Senator Lee. “Our bill will formally abolish this needless expense and return insurance regulation to the states, where it has always belonged.”

BACKGROUND

In 1945, Congress passed the McCarran-Ferguson Act, solidifying states’ regulatory authority over the insurance industry. Following the 2008 financial crisis, the Federal Insurance Office (FIO) was created by the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, which granted the FIO specific financial stability, monitoring, and international responsibilities. However, these responsibilities duplicate functions within an industry that has long been regulated at the state level and traditionally overseen by state insurance regulators.

The Federal Insurance Office Abolishment Act would eliminate the FIO and restore primary regulatory authority over the insurance industry to the states.
