title: CORREA SECURES $850,000 IN FEDERAL FUNDING FOR SANTA ANA COLLEGE WORKFORCE TRAINING PROGRAMS
text:
Investment will expand hands-on training in automotive, diesel-electric transportation, and robotics manufacturing/welding for 200 additional students each semester

SANTA ANA, CA — U.S. Representative Lou Correa (CA-46) today presented a check for $850,000 in federal funding to Santa Ana College. These dollars were used to create infrastructure for its Automotive Technology, Diesel-Electric Transportation Technology, and Robotics Manufacturing/Welding programs. The funding, secured by Rep. Correa through the FY26 appropriations process, will allow the college to serve 200 additional students each semester in training for in-demand, good-paying careers.

“Santa Ana College has always been a launching pad for opportunity in our community, and this funding makes sure it stays that way,” said Rep. Correa. “Families in Orange County want access to good jobs that don’t require a four-year degree and a mountain of debt — like jobs in the trades, in manufacturing, and in transportation. This investment means 200 more students a semester get hands-on training and a real shot at those careers.”

"I want to extend my sincere gratitude to Congressman Lou Correa for his continued investment in our students and our community. This $850,000 investment will directly elevate our Automotive, Diesel-Electric Transportation Technology, and Robotic Manufacturing/Welding programs, giving our students access to the modern, hands-on training spaces they need to succeed in high-demand technical careers. We are not just expanding a facility, we are expanding opportunity for the workforce Orange County depends on. I am deeply thankful for Congressman Correa's partnership and his belief in the power of community colleges to change lives," said Dr. Annebelle Nery, President of Santa Ana College.

The programs have at times had over 400 students on waitlists, and the trades they train for pay median hourly wages of roughly $28 to $41. The funding will support retrofitting a vacant lot and adjacent classroom space, part of a $4.865 million project expected to add five automotive, two diesel technology, and three welding courses each semester once complete.

Rep. Correa has long been a champion for workforce training at Santa Ana College, securing $2,000,000 in FY23 to help dislocated and at-risk members of our community gain skills essential for employment, $850,000 in FY24 to renovate workforce training facilities, and $1,031,000 in FY26 for the college’s Criminal Justice Academies to enhance regional training programs and facilities to meet the current and future demand for correctional and peace officers.

title: Rep. Crane Touts Rural Healthcare Win, Hosts Secretary Burgum
text:
Recently, Rep. Eli Crane (R-AZ) attended several engagements to advocate on behalf of rural Arizonans. With the annual district work period drawing to a close, he used the time to strengthen partnerships, host Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum, and meet with stakeholders at key sites across the Grand Canyon State.

Last week, Rep. Crane visited the Gila River Indian Community as the University of Arizona and Gila River Health Care announced a new partnership. The initiative aims to expand medical education and improve physician recruitment in the community. This new Doctor of Medicine-granting program marks a national first by establishing a rural regional branch in partnership with a federally recognized Tribe on Tribal land.

Students will begin their foundational science coursework in Phoenix before continuing clinical training at Gila River Health Care and regional sites. This structure is designed to draw future physicians into rural and Tribal communities that depend on reliable access to care. Rep. Crane called the program a strong step toward building a long-term physician workforce from within the community.

The visit came on the heels of his support for the Ak-Chin Indian Community’s selection under the Indian Health Service Joint Venture Construction Program. That collaboration will fund a new health center offering primary care, dental services, behavioral health, and specialty care close to home.

Rep. Crane pointed to these two announcements, along with recent investments through the Rural Health Transformation Program, as meaningful progress for rural healthcare. That program has already directed more than $160 million to Arizona for clinics, workforce development, and infrastructure. He views the combined efforts as significant movement toward closing longstanding gaps in essential services.

Click here to see more.

On Tuesday, Rep. Crane joined Secretary Doug Burgum of the U.S. Department of the Interior for visits to both the North and South Rims of Grand Canyon National Park. The trip allowed park staff to brief the Secretary on the current challenges facing the region, including ongoing recovery from the Dragon Bravo Fire and strain on core water and infrastructure systems.

At the North Rim, stakeholders outlined the scope of the 2025 fire’s damage, which destroyed or severely harmed critical facilities and left the area grappling with erosion, flash flooding, water-system disruptions, and long-term needs. Rep. Crane discussed his North Rim Restoration Act of 2025, which would streamline federal contracting to help the National Park Service move quickly on rebuilding. He also highlighted his amendment to the 2026 Farm Bill, which provides similar support for the Forest Service as it continues its response to the White Sage Fire. Both measures passed the House unanimously and await further consideration in the Senate.

Rep. Crane appreciated Secretary Burgum’s willingness to meet with personnel on the ground. He remains hopeful the Senate will finalize these solutions and deliver much-needed support for park staff, concession operators, small businesses, and gateway communities.

Click here to see more.

The next morning, Rep. Crane and Secretary Burgum traveled to Theodore Roosevelt Dam on the Salt River northeast of Phoenix. The site supports Arizona’s water system by providing storage, flood control, hydropower, and recreation on Roosevelt Lake, the largest lake located entirely within the state. The team at Salt River Project (SRP) described how recent dry winters and shifting runoff patterns have increased the importance of reliable in-state storage. They also reviewed ongoing work with state and federal partners to keep the system resilient.

During the engagement, officials reviewed the 2024 decision by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers allowing SRP to hold water in a portion of the dam’s Flood Control Space for up to 120 days instead of the previous 20-day limit. The added flexibility allows substantially more water to be kept on site after major runoff events rather than being released downstream before it can be put to beneficial use. SRP estimates the change could support water needs for hundreds of thousands of households during eligible periods.

Although Roosevelt Dam is not part of the Colorado River system, it plays an important role as Arizona prepares for potential reductions to Lower Basin allocations beginning in 2027. Rep. Crane reiterated concerns about the disproportionate projected cuts for Lower Basin states and noted previous letters he cosigned to Secretary Burgum and House Leadership urging assistance as the drought continues.

He discussed several ongoing issues in the negotiation process with Secretary Burgum, including ways to avoid costly litigation, ensure adequate storage capacity, and support potential desalination projects. While the Governor’s team drives the interstate negotiations, Rep. Crane made clear his opposition to the proposed cut share for Lower Basin states and pressed for federal involvement if the states’ discussions fail to reach a balanced agreement.

Later that afternoon, Rep. Crane, Secretary Burgum, and Rep. Andy Biggs (R-AZ) visited the Miami Smelter, a century-old copper processing facility in Claypool operated by Freeport-McMoRan. The site is a key component in the domestic copper supply chain, processing concentrate from Freeport’s Arizona mines and serving as the company’s most significant U.S. source of sulfuric acid for its leaching operations. As America works to strengthen domestic mineral and critical-mineral production, the facility’s role has only grown more important.

During the tour, Freeport leaders outlined recent developments at the smelter, including the 2025 maintenance turnaround and the roughly 821,200 metric tons of copper concentrate processed that year. They also discussed the approximately 209,300 metric tons of copper anodes produced and the nearly $73 million in maintenance and idle-facility costs tied to that work. Company officials noted they are evaluating an expansion of the site, citing existing infrastructure as a more practical route than permitting and constructing an entirely new domestic smelter.

Rep. Crane discussed federal regulatory barriers that have obstructed the facility’s competitiveness. He noted the Environmental Protection Agency standards for primary copper smelters finalized in May 2024, which Freeport had warned could impose significant costs and equipment changes. Rep. Crane welcomed the two-year regulatory relief the Trump administration granted to the facility in October 2025 while emphasizing the need for a permanent, pro-growth solution that supports American production rather than reliance on foreign suppliers. He appreciated the Secretary’s feedback and renewed his support for continued operations and future expansion in the region.

title: Crow on Six Months of Iran War
text:
AURORA—Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO), a combat veteran and member of the House Armed Services Committee and House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, released the following statement on the six-month mark of President Trump’s reckless and illegal war with Iran:

“Six months ago, Donald Trump launched a reckless war of choice with Iran, with no plan, no strategy, and no endgame. Six months later, 18 servicemembers are dead, hundreds more are wounded, and American taxpayers have spent billions of dollars on a war that has not made them safer and that has only raised their prices at home.

“Trump campaigned on ending wars in the Middle East. As someone who fought in Iraq and Afghanistan as a paratrooper and Army Ranger, I shared this goal. But since taking office, the President has done the exact opposite of what he campaigned on. He started new conflicts abroad. Now Coloradans and the American people have paid the price.

title: De La Cruz Hosts Farm Bill Panel in Beeville
text:
WASHINGTON – This week, Congresswoman Monica De La Cruz joined agricultural leaders from the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Texas Farm Bureau, and Texas and Southwestern Cattle Raisers Association in Beeville for a panel discussion focused on the passage of the Farm Bill and priorities for Texas farmers, ranchers, and rural communities.

The discussion centered on the importance of passing a comprehensive Farm Bill that protects producers, safeguards crop and livestock production, and invests in rural Texas.

De La Cruz joined panelists Dan Hunter from USDA, James Redfield from USDA, Scott Frazier from Texas Farm Bureau, Stephen Diebel from Texas Southwestern & Cattle Raisers Association, and Jody Brown from Texas Farm Service Agency for a panel discussion on the importance of passing a strong Farm Bill.

Background:

In April, Congresswoman De La Cruz voted to advance the Farm Bill, which includes four of her legislative initiatives:

Texas Agricultural Producers Assistance Act: Addresses the significant economic losses suffered by Texas agricultural producers due to the Mexican government’s non-compliance with the 1944 Water Treaty.

Southern Border Farmers and Ranchers Protection Act: Authorizes payments under the Environmental Quality Incentives Program (EQIP) to assist farmers and ranchers with repairing damages to farming infrastructure caused by illegal criminal activity along the Southern border.

Cattle Fever Tick Eradication Program Enhancement Act: Mandates the USDA to enter into a contract to evaluate the Cattle Fever Tick Eradication Program with a land-grant college or university or a non-land-grant college of agriculture.

Amendment to establish a permanent, interagency working group to protect South Texas farmers and producers from the impacts of the Mexican government's failure to comply with water deliveries under the 1944 Water Treaty.

title: Deluzio Celebrates Groundbreaking of New Churchill Playground With $500,000 in Federal Funding

title: Ahead of Labor Day, Elfreth Reconvenes Local Labor Leaders
text:
ANNAPOLIS, MD – Yesterday, Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth (MD-03), a member of the Labor Caucus, hosted her annual roundtable discussion with labor leaders in Maryland’s Third District at the Maryland State & DC AFL-CIO. This was the second annual convening since the Congresswoman first took office last year.

“As a proud member of the Labor Caucus and daughter of a union rail worker, I know firsthand the hard-fought protections, rights, and dignity that unions have secured for working families across this country,” said Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth. “I reconvened this roundtable to hear directly from our Third District union leaders as to how we can best support their members and workers across Maryland. Especially as this Administration deepens the affordability crisis, attacks collective bargaining rights, and strips back commonsense worker safety regulations, it is all the more important to stand with our brothers and sisters in organized labor in the fight for workers’ rights on the job.”

At the roundtable, Elfreth delivered an update from Congress, including progress on NDAA amendments and other legislative initiatives to restore the collective bargaining rights of hardworking federal employees and expedite the process of securing labor contracts. The roundtable was an opportunity to hear directly from the representatives of the over 340,000 union workers across the state and 45,000 federal employees in the District. In addition to collective bargaining, the conversation focused on federal funding cuts, healthcare, affordability, and workplace safety for rail, maritime, and emergency responders.

Elfreth was joined by various labor unions from across Maryland’s Third District, including the Maryland State and DC AFL-CIO, Maryland State Education Association (MSEA), Carroll County Education Association (CCEA), Service Employees International Union (SEIU) Local 500 and 32BJ, Howard County International Association of Fire Fighters (IAFF) Local 2000, International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers (IBEW) Local 24 and Local 26, International Alliance of Theatrical Stage Employees (IATSE) Local 487, Amalgamated Transit Union (ATU) Local 1300, International Union of Painters and Allied Trades (IUPAT) DC51, the International Organization of Masters, Mates & Pilots, the Maritime Institute of Technology and Graduate Studies (MISTAG), American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees (AFSCME) Maryland Council 3, the National Active and Retired Federal Employees (NARFE) Chapter 1734, Laborers’ International Union of North America, American Federation of Government Employees (AFGE), American Maritime Officers, United Association of Plumbers and Pipefitters, Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen - B&O, and the Baltimore-DC Building Trades Council.

“SEIU Local 500 is eager to join Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth alongside our labor partners to discuss the real issues facing Maryland workers. As a state legislator, she was a labor champion. In the face of rising costs and attacks on labor rights by the current administration, we are glad to have her in the United States Congress championing the needs of working people,” said Christopher Cano, Director of Political & Legislative Affairs, SEIU Local 500.

“As an association dedicated to federal workers and retirees, NARFE appreciates Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth’s work to protect the merit-based civil service system and our earned benefits. We pledge to stand with her to fight ongoing threats to public health, food safety, worker rights, and the myriad ways in which the federal workforce protects and enhances the lives of all Americans,” said Teresa Baker, First Vice President, NARFE Maryland Federation.

“IATSE Local 487 is proud to attend this AFL CIO roundtable discussion with Congresswoman Elfreth. Being given the opportunity to discuss the state of the film & television industry in the US, and more specifically the Mid-Atlantic region, allows our skilled craftworkers a voice in how we can bring back the work that supports our families and local industries in Maryland. Our hope is that this conversation highlights the vital importance of a national tax incentive and legislative support for the I.A.T.S.E. workforce—the skilled craftworkers whose labor powers the entertainment industry,” said Vice President Steve Saada, IATSE Local 487.

“Congresswoman Elfreth has been a longtime advocate for Maryland’s firefighters. Her accessibility and commitment to our members are unmatched, whether making time to meet with our leaders in her office on Capitol Hill or visiting local fire stations. Most recently, she co-sponsored H.R. 1269, the Honoring Our Fallen Heroes Act, which extends federal Public Safety Officers’ Benefits to the families of firefighters who die from occupational cancer,” said Adam Nolder, Vice President of IAFF Local 2000.

“The issues that are top of mind for our union today include the Administration’s Jones Act waiver, which is giving American maritime jobs to foreign seafarers while doing nothing to lower gas prices,” said MM&P President Captain Don Josberger. “We are also advocating strongly on Capitol Hill for passage of the Faster Labor Contracts Act, which would ensure that unscrupulous companies cannot indefinitely hinder workers’ legal right to form a union.”

“Public services from our state and local governments, and the public service workers who make them happen, are more important now than ever. Right now, workers face significant challenges on the job, and our union appreciates the partnership and collaboration with Congresswoman Elfreth to ensure public service workers have a voice in Congress fighting for them,” said President Jack Hughes, AFSCME Maryland Council 3.

As the daughter of two civil servants and the representative of over 45,000 federal employees, Congresswoman Elfreth has been laser-focused on protecting and advancing the rights of workers and civil servants. Elfreth has voted in favor of numerous bills to ensure workers receive the benefits they deserve, including the Faster Labor Contracts Act to speed up the process for workers to secure labor contracts and the Protect America’s Workforce Act (PAWA) to repeal a presidential executive order that stripped union rights from 1.5 million federal workers. She has also spoken out in support of legislation like theRailroad Retirement Fairness Act to eliminate provisions that unfairly reduce retirement payments for certain railroad retirees and spouses. On the House Armed Services Committee, Elfreth has fought for civilian DoD civil servants and proudly supported Congressman Donald Norcross’ amendment in each year’s annual defense bill to restore the collective bargaining rights that the President’s executive order stripped.

title: Finstad, Deluzio Introduce the Water Authority Cybersecurity Protection Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Brad Finstad (MN-01) and Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17) introduced the Water Authority Cybersecurity Protection Act. This bipartisan legislation would double the amount of funding available in certain grants and technical assistance to local water authorities to strengthen cybersecurity efforts.

In July, Minnesota faced more than 30 cyberattacks on water systems potentially linked to Iran. At least 11 other states have reported possible cyberattacks to their water systems—with some experiencing flooding and reduced water pressure or going offline completely. At least 100 municipalities across the country have reported potential hacking efforts to their water systems.

“We have seen far too many instances of cybersecurity threats to our critical water systems,” said Rep. Finstad. “Just this summer, Minnesota experienced over 30 cyberattacks targeting operational technologies that our communities rely on. I am proud to join Congressman Deluzio in introducing this important, bipartisan legislation that will help ensure our local water authorities have the proper capabilities to respond to threats from foreign adversaries.”

title: ICYMI: Rep. Gillen Delivers Millions in Federal Funding, Meets with Law Enforcement and Long Islanders Throughout August

Supporting Local Businesses and Entrepreneurs

She will bring the stories she heard at the roundtable and throughout Nassau County with her back to Washington as she continues to fight for Long Islanders.

Bipartisanship Top Grades

title: VETERANS: Harder Demands Answers on Restoration of Union Rights at NorCal VA
text:
Federal judge ruled in March that collective bargaining rights at the VA must be reinstated

AFGE Local 1206 reports that months later, these rights have still not been restored

STOCKTON – Today, Rep. Josh Harder (CA-09) called on the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to respond to concerns that union rights at local VA facilities are not being upheld. Harder led nine regional colleagues in a letter to VA Secretary Doug Collins demanding answers on the VA’s progress to comply with a federal order requiring collective bargaining rights to be restored.

In March, a federal district court judge ordered the Department of Veterans Affairs to reinstate its Master Collective Bargaining Agreement with the American Federation of Government Employees (AFGE). Those agreements provide for collective bargaining rights like official time for authorized union representatives and access to union office space and equipment. However, AFGE Local 1206, which represents bargaining unit employees within the VA Northern California Health Care System, has raised concerns that these rights have still not been fully restored.

“We take seriously the concerns raised by union representatives, particularly in light of the ongoing litigation regarding the termination of the Master Collective Bargaining Agreement. Indeed, on August 7, 2026, the federal district court issued a further order requiring the agreement to remain in effect pursuant to its continuation provisions,” wrote the Members. “To better understand the circumstances and VA Northern California Health Care System's implementation of the reinstated agreement, we respectfully request responses to these concerns.”

Key demands of the Members to be provided no later than September 11, 2026:

Steps taken to fully implement the March court order and restore collective bargaining rights at the VA Northern California Health Care System.

Details of any incidents of union representatives being denied pay or access to union space and equipment while performing union representational duties.

Steps taken to resolve outstanding disagreements between the VA Northern California Health Care System and AFGE Local 1206 regarding the bargaining agreement.

Read the full letter here.

title: RELEASE: REP. HILL AWARDS USPS HIS GOLDEN FLEECE AWARD FOR FAILING TO STOP FRAUDULENT POSTAGE
text:
Today, Rep. French Hill (AR-02) announced the United States Postal Service (USPS) is the latest recipient of his Golden Fleece Award for failing to properly identify and stop fraudulent postage.

The United States Postal Service Inspector General found that the USPS struggled to intercept packages and letters going through its sorting and shipping process that had invalid or fraudulent postage. This puts the USPS and the services it provides at risk as over $1.7 billion is estimated to be lost yearly to fraudulent stamps or postage. This is revenue that the USPS could be using to reduce its $9 billion loss posted in 2025.

Rep. Hill said, “The USPS no doubt provides important services, especially for rural central Arkansans who rely on it to deliver everything from letters to medicine. But at a time when the USPS is posting yearly losses and the package transportation industry is becoming more dynamic, the USPS must adapt. Commonsense steps can be taken to stop the bleeding, and USPS already has statutory authorities to do so. While I am encouraged to see USPS agree with the recommendations the Inspector General has made, they must go further and rigorously follow through.”

In his letter to Postmaster General David Steiner, Rep. Hill writes:

Dear Postmaster General Steiner

I am writing today to inform you that the United States Postal Service (USPS) is this month’s recipient of my Golden Fleece Award. I am awarding this to USPS because of its inability to detect and properly stop counterfeit postage.

USPS is an important facilitator of connection and commerce for the United States. A secure and effective USPS benefits all Americans. That is why I am troubled by reports that the USPS has insufficient controls in place to detect and stop counterfeit postage from being used. This includes postage for small envelopes and larger packages.

Reports from the Inspector General of the USPS estimate that $1.7 billion could be lost due to counterfeit stamps. It may be that the USPS Advanced Facer Canceller Systems (AFCS), which is used to read stamps and labels, is not adequate by itself to detect and intercept fraudulent postage. In fact, during an audit conducted by the Inspector General of the USPS, the AFCS did not catch a single piece of fraudulent postage when running in its low-revenue protection mode. This mode improves mail processing speed, but it checks only one of two possible tests and is clearly not effective.

Other alerts by the Inspector General of the USPS have indicated that the USPS also struggles to detect counterfeit labels and postage for larger packages. These findings are especially troubling since criminals could exploit this loophole to ship illegal or illicit materials at no cost and courtesy of the USPS. From 2024 to 2025, package and shipping revenue made up roughly $9 billion of the $22 billion USPS generated in revenue, the largest single line of service by revenue. If the USPS cannot adequately capture revenue from this service, it will be increasingly difficult to maintain its viability, and commerce will suffer as a result.

Despite technical limitations like the AFCS, the USPS also appears to struggle with prosecuting the creators of fraudulent postage. I am pleased that USPS will be improving its fraudulent postage enforcement activities under existing legal authorities like the Lanham Act. Under this authority, the USPS has prosecuted individuals who used USPS logos without authorization. To tackle this challenge, the USPS will need to use all of its statutory authorities.

The challenges faced by the USPS are existential. In 2025, the USPS reported a $9 billion net loss and a $2.7 billion controllable net loss. While this is an improvement over 2024 financial results, this is not sustainable, and the USPS must do everything it can to ensure its long-term viability.

While I recognize some of the Inspector General of the USPS’ recommendations to tackle fraudulent postage will cost money, implementing them would improve the USPS’ ability to capture revenue and offset some of this loss. That said, I urge the USPS to seriously heed the Inspector General's concerns and implement their recommendations immediately.

While the USPS is funded by its sales and operations, it should be a better steward of its resources to ensure those funds are not wasted. Should you require additional authority from Congress, I ask that you notify me. I look forward to working with you.

Sincerely,

French Hill

Member of Congress

CC: Inspector Gary Barksdale, Chief Postal Inspector; Inspector General Tammy Hull, Inspector General of the United States Postal Service

title: Horsford Demands Congress Close Prediction Markets Loophole After Court Win: ‘The Fight Is Not Over’
text:
Rep. Steven Horsford issued the following statement in response to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit's ruling against prediction markets offering sports betting.

“Today, the Ninth Circuit affirmed what Nevadans have always known: prediction markets are gambling. This ruling is an important victory for States’ and Tribes’ authority to regulate gambling.

But the fight is not over. We must continue working to protect consumers, ensure young people aren't targets, preserve state and Tribal rights, and safeguard gaming workers across the country. This issue is far from settled and will likely make its way to the U.S. Supreme Court. Congress must act now to make clear, once and for all, that sports betting - and gambling at large - belongs under state and Tribal gaming laws.

“It is time to stop unelected regulators from bypassing states by passing my bipartisan Prediction Markets Are Gambling Act. This legislation would close the loophole that allows prediction market platforms to offer sports betting and casino-style games. Prediction markets must play by the same rules as traditional gaming operators, including the same consumer protections and licensing requirements.

“The message from the Ninth Circuit is clear. Now it is time for Congress to act and make this principle the law of the land.”

The unanimous ruling was issued by a three-judge panel consisting of judges appointed by President Donald Trump. The case originated in Nevada, where state regulators sought to prohibit Kalshi from offering prediction-market contracts tied to sporting events. Additionally, new analysis by CNN found that young adults between 18 and 21 - who are legally barred from most gambling in the United States - have traded an estimated $5.4 billion so far this year on Kalshi.

title: Horsford: Nevadans Didn't Create This Crisis, and They Shouldn't Have to Pay for It

LAS VEGAS, NV- Congressman Steven Horsford (NV-04) spoke today at the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee Democrats' Shadow Hearing on President Trump's attack on affordability.

"Oversight Democrats could have held this hearing anywhere, but they chose Las Vegas because we are feeling the impacts of this affordability crisis more than any other place in this country," Rep. Horsford said. "The Trump slump has caused grocery prices to go up, gas to go up, and housing to be further out of reach. When you have an administration that believes affordability is a scam, their priorities reflect that. That’s why we're seeing permanent relief for billionaires but not for working families. We're seeing it with illegal tariffs that have cost Nevada nearly $2.5 billion since January 2025, which forced small businesses to close their doors for good. Affordability is not a scam. It's life or death for so many Nevadans, especially in my district, where people are living paycheck to paycheck and deserve not just to survive, but to get ahead."

As Nevada's only representative on the Ways and Means Committee, Horsford has been a leading voice in Congress for lowering costs and putting money back in families' pockets. Las Vegas tourism, including nearly 3.1 million visitors from Canada alone, supports thousands of hospitality workers who are now feeling the impact as visitor numbers soften. Tariffs have cost roughly $2,053 per household. That’s money that could otherwise go toward groceries, gas, and rent.

Congressman Horsford continues to advocate for Nevadans on affordability, introducing legislation to help bring down costs, including:

The RELIEF Act, which would require refunds within 90 days of enactment

The TIP Improvement Act, which would make tips permanent and close the subminimum wage, currently as low as $2.13/hour

The HOME Act, key provisions of which were incorporated into the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act

An amendment to permanently extend the Advanced Premium Tax Credit, relief that supported more than 96,000 working Nevadans, offered during markup of the One Big Beautiful Bill

title: Congressman Brian Jack Hosts Fireside Chat  from President Roosevelt’s Little White House
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

August 28, 2026

Contact: Joseph Brannan

WARM SPRINGS, GA – Today, Congressman Brian Jack hosted a Fireside Chat for more than 100,000 constituents across Georgia's 3rd Congressional District from President Roosevelt’s historic Little White House in Warm Springs.

President Franklin Delano Roosevelt started the tradition of speaking directly to the American public through his famous “Fireside Chats,” and Congressman Jack carried that spirit forward this afternoon, utilizing the historic setting to discuss key legislative priorities and hear firsthand from families across Georgia’s 3rd Congressional District.

President Roosevelt visited the Little White House 16 times during his Presidency, leaving a legacy that resonates beyond Georgia today.

Congressman Brian Jack said, “I had a wonderful time hosting a Fireside Chat for over 100,000 constituents from President Franklin Delano Roosevelt’s beloved Little White House in Warm Springs this afternoon.

President Roosevelt ​​pioneered the concept of a “Fireside Chat”, and I was honored to continue that tradition, as I deeply care about preserving the rich history, values, and culture of Georgia’s 3rd Congressional District, especially as we celebrate our Country’s 250th anniversary.

When President Roosevelt left the Yalta Conference he told his aides – who were worried about his ailing health – ‘If I can just make it back to Warm Springs, I’ll be OK.’

President Franklin Delano Roosevelt left an indelible mark on our Congressional District, and we are proud to have been the home away from home for a President.”

Throughout the Fireside Chat, Congressman Jack fielded questions from constituents on the economy, immigration, values, and election integrity.

title: LEADER JEFFRIES ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF THE MARCH ON WASHINGTON: “IT’S TIME FOR US TO GET INTO SOME GOOD TROUBLE
text:
Today, joined by members of the Congressional Black Caucus, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries delivered remarks at the 63rd Anniversary event for the March on Washington hosted by the National Action Network and Drum Major Institute.

LEADER JEFFRIES: It’s a high honor and a distinct privilege to stand with my colleagues in the Congressional Black Caucus, Reverend Sharpton, the King family, the National Action Network and the civil rights community as we commemorate the 63rd anniversary of the March on Washington and prepare for the battles ahead.

We certainly have come a long way in the United States of America, but we still have a long way to go. These are challenging times in this country right now. We have a hater in the White House, a reckless and costly war of choice raging in the Middle East, a Supreme Court that’s out of control. Black unemployment is up, Black home ownership is down and Black political representation is under assault with Jim Crow-like tactics all throughout the South. Challenging times. Wickedness in high places. But we’re not distressed because our community knows how to make a way out of no way.

We’re facing a crossroads right now here in the United States of America. The question is which direction will we choose? We want to move America forward. The extremists are trying to turn back the clock. We’re working hard to bring people together. The extremists are tearing the country apart. We believe in truth and reconciliation. The extremists want to erase our history, but Black history is American history. Our story will never be erased.

And so we come today in the spirit of Frederick Douglass. We come today in the spirit of Sojourner Truth. We come today in the spirit of Jackie Robinson. We come today in the spirit of Rosa Parks. We come today in the spirit of Martin Luther King, Jr. We come today in the spirit of Muhammad Ali. We come today in the spirit of Fannie Lou Hamer. We come today in the spirit of Adam Clayton Powell, Jr. We come today in the spirit of Shirley Chisholm. And we come today in the spirit of the great John Lewis, because it’s time for us to get into some good trouble. Necessary trouble. Good trouble.

We fight for liberty and justice for all. We fight for equal protection under the law. We fight for free and fair elections. We fight for work, wages and wealth creation. We fight for jobs and freedom. We fight for racial justice. We fight for economic justice. We fight for social justice. We fight for civil rights. And we fight to pass the John Robert Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act so we can end the era of voter suppression in the United States of America once and for all.

So let’s continue to show up, to stand up and to speak up to make this country the best version of herself. And when we do, together, I’m confident that we will win the day, win the week, win the month, win the year, win the hearts and minds of the American people and then on November 3rd, win back control of the United States House of Representatives so we can end this national nightmare and continue our march toward a more perfect union.

Full remarks can be watched here.

title: Save the Alewife Brook: A Federal Partnership for a Cleaner, Safer Alewife.
text:
Today was a milestone for Alewife Brook. Congresswoman Katherine Clark met at the Brook with Save the Alewife Brook and our state and local delegation to see the sewage, sediment, and flooding crisis for herself. We talked with her about engaging the Army Corps of Engineers for a project to dredge, dechannelize, and restore Alewife Brook.

“Protecting our environment means protecting our neighbors. I’m grateful for the incredible advocates at Save the Alewife Brook for their continued work to eliminate sewage pollution, safeguard our local ecosystem, and build the cleaner future our kids deserve. I’m looking forward to partnering with them and with leaders at every level of government to keep moving the ball forward.” Democratic Whip Katherine Clark (MA‑5)

Joining the Congresswoman at the Brook were State Senator Pat Jehlen and State Representatives Christine Barber, Dave Rogers, Sean Garballey, and Steve Owens. From the Town of Arlington, we were joined by Town Manager Jim Feeney and Select Board members Diane Mahon and Steve DeCourcey. Save the Alewife Brook was represented by steering committee members Kristin Anderson, Gene Benson, Ann McDonald, George Laite, and Mike Lonetto.

Why this visit matters

A portion of the Alewife Brook is confined to a 27-foot-wide concrete channel that receives untreated sewage from six active Combined Sewer Overflow (CSO) outfalls. In 2021, MWRA, Cambridge, and Somerville dumped 51 million gallons of untreated sewage into the Brook.

The Brook has accumulated 2 1/2 to 3 1/2 feet of contaminated sediment and, according to the 2024 Inter-Fluve Sediment Study, will lose its remaining capacity as sediment continues to fill in.

The public health toll is already severe. During CSO discharges, E. coli levels in Alewife Brook reach roughly 950 times the EPA safe standard. A Boston University School of Public Health study found that even living near CSOs can increase the risk of illness serious enough to require an ER visit.

Roughly 5,000 residents of Arlington, Cambridge, and Belmont, many in Environmental Justice neighborhoods, live in the Alewife Brook 100‑year floodplain.

—

title: Kean Hosts Roundtable on Preventing Nitrous Oxide Misuse
text:
(August 28, 2026) WASHINGTON, D.C. – Yesterday, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) held a roundtable with constituents, first responders, medical professionals, non-profit representatives, and local leadership to discuss the prevention of nitrous oxide misuse. The discussion coincided with the introduction of Congressman Kean’s bipartisan legislation, co-led with Congressman Gottheimer (NJ-05), the Mitigating Abuse of Nitrous-oxide Nationwide and Reducing Inhalation-Related Neurological Outcomes (MANNARINO) Act, which aims to save lives and protect Americans by restricting recreational access to hazardous nitrous oxide products. These products can also be known as laughing gas, whippets, or Galaxy Gas.

“Today we honor the memory of John Robert Mannarino by working to prevent other families from experiencing the harms of nitrous oxide misuse,” said Congressman Kean (NJ-07). “Nitrous oxide whippets and tanks, widely available in corner stores and online, pose a danger to the community and must be treated accordingly. After hearing John’s story, I introduced the MANNARINO Act to raise awareness of the dangers of nitrous oxide and prevent future tragedies from occurring. Thank you to the Mannarino family for bringing this important issue forward and attending this roundtable discussion.”

"Nitrous oxide, or ‘whippets,’ are far from harmless — abuse can cause paralysis, nervous system failure, and death. That's why I'm teaming up with Rep. Kean on this bipartisan bill to help states crack down on the sale of nitrous oxide, ban flavored versions marketed to kids, and put real teeth behind these protections. We owe it to every Jersey family to close this loophole before more damage is done and more lives are lost,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05).

“Our family is living with a tremendous loss that can never be replaced because of the misuse of nitrous oxide,” said the Mannarino family. “We lost our loving son, brother, and husband, John, and while we cannot bring him back, we can fight to prevent another family from experiencing this devastating tragedy. We hope Congress will act now to protect lives and ensure that what happened to our family does not happen to another.”

“Thank you to Congressman Kean and the Mannarino family for bringing this issue to our attention,” said Bridgewater Councilman Timothy Ring. “I hope to see more discussion on ways to prevent the misuse of substances from the start rather than only after a crisis has occurred. As a councilman and volunteer EMT of nearly 40 years, I will continue to work towards more education on the symptoms, signs, and effects of nitrous oxide.”

“The courage of the Mannarino family is inspiring, but it’s so sad that it often takes a tragedy to drive change,” said Andi Williams, Executive Director of CiC for Prevention and Recovery. “Education around the risks and availability of these harmful substances is critical and, with the support of leaders like Congressman Kean and with adequate funding from the administration, precious young lives can be saved. At CiC, we have brought about a documented reduction in youth substance use in the communities we serve showing that it is possible to drive that change. I was grateful to be a part of today’s conversation and to witness a group of changemakers committed to these efforts.”

“Congressman Kean is right to raise this important public health issue. Nitrous Oxide abuse is a serious problem, impacting many families and most of all young people,” said Mental Health Association CEO Robert Davison.“Limiting its access and raising awareness about its negative and potentially deadly effects are important first steps in this important conversation. His bi-partisan bill and the highly engaging forum he facilitated today gives me hope we can make progress and protect people from the harmful effects of Nitrous Oxide.”

“As a Family Nurse Practitioner, school nurse, and former mayor, I know we are standing at the base of a public health mountain with nitrous oxide misuse, which has tripled in New Jersey,” said school nurse Lisa Lontai. “Because this gas clears the system in minutes, it is completely invisible on standard drug tests. It is absolutely critical that primary care and emergency clinicians immediately consider nitrous oxide as a differential diagnosis whenever a patient presents with unexplained neurological issues like tingling, numbness, or balance problems. Catching this early and starting aggressive medical treatment is the only way to prevent permanent nerve damage, and we urgently need Congressman Kean’s retail ban passed to stop this crisis from accelerating.”

“Two years ago, members of our youth coalition alerted us to Galaxy Gas after seeing it trending on TikTok,” said Executive Director of Prevention Services Erin Cohen. “Since then, we have been working to educate parents, school personnel, and the broader Hunterdon/Somerset community about the serious health risks involved. We thank Congressman Kean for his leadership on this issue and for honoring the Mannarino family's courage in turning their loss into action. Legislation like this is exactly what's needed to protect our community before more families experience this kind of tragedy.”

Background:

Nitrous oxide is being misused for recreational use with its harms largely unrealized. Its abuse can lead to heart attack, nerve damage, muscle spasms, numbness, birth defects, paralysis, and even death.

In November 2025, Bridgewater, New Jersey resident John Robert Mannarino lost his life, with nitrous oxide being a major contributing factor. After outreach from his family, Congressman Kean introduced the MANNARINO Act to restrict access to nitrous oxide by encouraging states to adopt laws restricting the sale of the product for recreational use.

This bill would:

Encourage states to adopt laws restricting the sale of nitrous oxide so that it is only used for legitimate purposes like medicine, dentistry, commercial food production, and others.

Encourage states to ban the sale of all scented/flavored nitrous oxide.

Close the loophole for nitrous oxide to be sold as a standalone “food propellant” to non-commercial users.

Give the HHS Secretary authority to reduce federal grant funding to states that refuse to restrict this dangerous substance. This is a policy tool used to encourage states to set age limits on tobacco and alcohol use.

Last month, Congressman Kean spoke in a Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade subcommittee hearing about the dangers of nitrous oxide. Watch HERE.

In response to constituent concerns about the accessibility of nitrous oxide products, Congressman Kean wrote a letter to corporations expressing concern about the sale of these products in their stores. Read the letter HERE.

A copy of the bill text is available HERE.

title: Kiggans, CMS Administrator Oz Discuss Healthcare Affordability, Access in Coastal Virginia
text:
VIRGINIA BEACH, VA — Today, Congresswoman Jen Kiggans (VA-02) welcomed Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz to Virginia’s Second District for a series of healthcare visits focused on improving patient access, supporting providers, and addressing challenges affecting healthcare delivery across Coastal Virginia.

Congresswoman Kiggans and Administrator Oz began the visit at the Sentara Princess Anne Hospital. There, they toured the facility and met with senior leadership to discuss hospital operations, patient services, workforce needs, and federal healthcare priorities.

Following the visit, Congresswoman Kiggans and Administrator Oz traveled to Tidewater Community College (TCC) for a healthcare roundtable with local healthcare providers. The conversation focused on addressing healthcare affordability, decreasing staffing shortages, navigating Medicaid policy, alleviating administrative burdens on providers, and expanding access to high-quality care throughout the region. Watch Rep. Kiggans and Administrator Oz discuss Medicaid reform following the roundtable here.

Today, CMS celebrated a $122 million investment to improve healthcare outcomes across the Commonwealth of Virginia through the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). Read CMS’s press release here.

Congresswoman Kiggans said, “As a nurse practitioner, I know firsthand that advancing quality healthcare policy starts with listening to the patients and providers who navigate our healthcare system every day. I’m grateful to Administrator Oz for coming to Virginia’s Second District to hear directly from our healthcare community about the successes and challenges they face. I’m proud to have helped deliver critical investments in rural healthcare and preserve the integrity of our social safety net, but there is still more work to be done to lower costs and protect access to care. I look forward to continuing to work with Administrator Oz to advance commonsense solutions that put patients first and expand access to quality, attentive healthcare.”

“Thanks to the Trump Administration’s Rural Health Transformation Program, we’re proud to work with state and local partners to turn bold ideas into lasting improvements for rural communities,” said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “I want to thank Representative Kiggans for her leadership in bringing local leaders and health care providers together to build stronger partnerships. Together, we can Make America Healthy Again.”

During the roundtable, Congresswoman Kiggans and CMS Administrator Oz highlighted the Rural Health Transformation Program, established through the Working Families Tax Cut and signed into law last year, which is providing substantial federal resources to strengthen healthcare accessibility in America’s rural communities. Through this groundbreaking program, the Commonwealth of Virginia will receive over $189 million a year for the next five years to expand telehealth and virtual care options, as well improve maternal care and workforce development. Watch Rep. Kiggans and Administrator Oz highlight this monumental investment here.

“Access to high-quality healthcare should never be dictated by where you live,” said Rep. Kiggans. “The Rural Transformation Program will bring care directly to our rural communities and was made possible by the Working Families Tax Cut. I’m proud to have supported this program and its efforts to strengthen our healthcare workforce and give providers the tools they need to better serve their patients.”

As the Representative for Virginia’s Second District and a former adult-geriatric nurse practitioner, Rep. Kiggans remains committed to lowering healthcare costs, strengthening America’s healthcare workforce, expanding access to high-quality care, and ensuring patients and providers have the resources they need to achieve better health outcomes.

Rep. Kiggans’ Work in the Healthcare Space:

In December 2025, Rep. Jen Kiggans (VA-02) and Rep. Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05), along with a bipartisan coalition of 38 total House Members, introduced the CommonGround for Affordable Health Care Act, a bipartisan bill that included a two-year extension of health insurance premium savings for American families—including a year of the enhanced Premium Tax Credits (ePTCs), with targeted modifications, new guardrails to prevent “ghost beneficiaries” and crack down on fraud, an extension of open enrollment, and PBM reform. Read her press release here.

In July 2025, Rep. Kiggans introduced the Health Care Fairness for Military Families Act, which would allow TRICARE dependents to remain on their parents’ plan until age 26. Read her press release here.

title: Rep. Kiggans Joins Chief of Naval Operations Admiral Daryl Caudle for Visit to Naval Air Station Oceana
text:
VIRGINIA BEACH, VA – Congresswoman Jen Kiggans (VA-02) joined Chief of Naval Operations Admiral Daryl Caudle, Master Chief Petty Officer of the Navy John Perryman, Naval Air Station (NAS) Oceana leadership, and local Sailors for a visit to NAS Oceana. The visit highlighted the installation’s critical role in supporting naval aviation, strengthening operational readiness, and preparing the Navy’s warfighters for missions around the world.

During the visit, Congresswoman Kiggans and Admiral Caudle met with NAS Oceana leadership for a briefing on the installation’s mission, current operations, infrastructure priorities, and future. NAS Oceana Commanding Officer Captain Rob Littman also discussed the installation’s ongoing priorities and the investments necessary to sustain its long-term mission.

Congresswoman Kiggans said, “As the Representative of Virginia’s Second District, I’m always honored to spend time with the Sailors and Aviators that keep our Navy ready to fight and win. I’m grateful to Admiral Caudle and MCPON Perryman for coming to Hampton Roads to hear directly from our warfighters and see firsthand the critical mission happening here every day. NAS Oceana is essential to our national security, and I’ll continue fighting in Congress for the people, infrastructure, and resources needed to strengthen readiness and support Oceana’s mission of mobile air superiority.”

The delegation visited Carrier Air Wing Eight (CVW-8), where Congresswoman Kiggans and Admiral Caudle participated in a simulator experience and spoke with aircrew about their training, operational responsibilities, and readiness. The visit also included an opportunity for MCPON Perryman to meet with the installation’s Chief Selects.

NAS Oceana is the Navy’s East Coast Master Jet Base and plays a vital role in the training and readiness of strike fighter squadrons assigned to the United States Atlantic Fleet. The installation supports thousands of servicemembers, civilian employees, and military families while serving as an important component of both Hampton Roads’ defense community and the region’s economy.

As the representative for Virginia’s Second District and a former Navy helicopter pilot married to a former F/A-18 pilot and current mother of a F/A-18 pilot, Rep. Kiggans remains committed to supporting America’s servicemembers, strengthening military readiness, modernizing defense infrastructure, and ensuring Hampton Roads continues to play a leading role in our nation’s defense.

title: Larsen Urges Supreme Court to Protect LGBTQ+ Students from Discrimination
text:
This week, U.S. Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02) joined more than 180 House and Senate Democrats in filing an amicus brief at the Supreme Court in the case of St. Mary Catholic Parish v. Roy. In this case, religious preschools are seeking an exemption from the nondiscrimination provision in Colorado’s universal preschool program so they can refuse to admit LGBTQ+ children or the children of LGBTQ+ people while still receiving public funding.

“It’s not complicated: organizations accepting taxpayer dollars should not be allowed to discriminate against LGBTQ+ children or parents,” said Rep. Larsen. “I urge the Supreme Court to protect LGBTQ+ families from discrimination, and Icontinue to stand with the LGBTQ+ community in Northwest Washington and across the United States.”

The members’ brief urges the Supreme Court to uphold the nondiscrimination provision and not grant a religious exemption. The brief argues that:

The Supreme Court defers to legislatures and the political process when assessing exemptions from neutral, generally applicable laws;

Petitioners’ rule would endanger numerous federal nondiscrimination laws that Congress has carefully crafted over decades; and

The Court should be mindful not to destabilize or undermine that legislative role by effectively legislating ad hoc exemptions to nondiscrimination laws.

The amicus brief is available to read here.

title: Connecticut Officials Bring Attention to Addiction and Recovery Resources in Advance of International Overdose Awareness Day
text:
Hartford, CT - In advance of International Overdose Awareness Day, which is commemorated annually on August 31, Connecticut officials reaffirmed their commitment to combating the overdose crisis and bringing attention to addiction, recovery, and overdose prevention resources available to people across Connecticut.

International Overdose Awareness Day is a global campaign to end overdose, remember without stigma those who have died, and acknowledge the grief of the family and friends left behind.

“Every community across our state and the nation has been touched by the opioid epidemic. As we recognize International Overdose Awareness Day, we stand together to remember those who lost their lives to addiction and recommit to investing in prevention and treatment services. I will continue to support programs in communities that connect families with the resources they need to combat substance abuse and support those in recovery,” said Congressman John B. Larson.

“Today we mourn the lives lost to overdoses this year and commit to honoring them with action," said Senator Richard Blumenthal. "While Connecticut has made progress over the last few years to reduce the number of these tragic deaths, we need to dismantle the destructive grip addiction has on our communities. I will keep fighting for federal funding to support addiction prevention and recovery efforts.”

“Overdose deaths are on the decline in Connecticut, but addiction and mental health issues still affect the lives of countless individuals and families across the country, including the hundreds who have died from drug overdoses in Connecticut last year," said Congresswoman Rosa DeLauro. "As the lead Democrat on the Appropriations Committee, I have proudly fought for federal investments to address this addiction crisis, including against the unconscionable cancellation of grants earlier this year. I will continue to advocate for the resources necessary for those struggling with addiction.”

“Every life lost to an overdose leaves a hole in the lives of family and friends left behind. On Overdose Awareness Day, we remember those we have lost and stand with the families and communities carrying that grief. We must continue expanding access to treatment and recovery resources and ensuring that anyone struggling with addiction knows they are not alone,” said Congressman Jim Himes.

“In advance of International Overdose Awareness Day, I want to acknowledge the 836 lives we’ve lost over the past year. Each one of these individuals represents a loss in our Connecticut community and an immeasurable impact on their loved ones. Through tireless efforts across the state, countless lives have been saved, but even one overdose is one too many. This fight is not over. On this day, we commit to continuing building a future where no one in the Connecticut community experiences the loss of a loved one to overdose. Our work is not done until every person living with substance use disorder has access to the support they need not just to live, but to thrive,” said Governor Ned Lamont.

“On International Overdose Awareness Day, we reassert our state’s commitment to fighting the impacts of the overdose epidemic in Connecticut," said Lt. Governor Susan Bysiewicz. Today we remember those we have lost over the past year and honor their lives. For everyone living with substance use disorder, you are not alone. We see you and help is available. We will continue working towards creating a community where every person living with substance use disorder has the support they need for their journey towards recovery.”

“On International Overdose Awareness Day, we remember every life taken by the opioid epidemic and recognize the toll this crisis continues to take on our communities," said Attorney General William Tong. "We also stand with those who are battling addiction and the loved ones, advocates, and providers who work tirelessly to make sure they have the support they need to recover. Connecticut has fought to hold the companies that fueled this crisis accountable, helping secure more than $50 billion nationwide, including $600 million for Connecticut, for treatment, prevention, and recovery services. No amount of money will bring back the lives that were lost, but we will continue fighting to keep other families from suffering that same loss.”

“Today, we remember the people we have lost to overdose in the past year and the families and communities who continue to feel that loss," said Comptroller Sean Scanlon. "These tragedies, this epidemic, must always propel us to continue our work to combat substance use disorder in Connecticut. We must lead with compassion to face the challenge ahead and build a better tomorrow.”

“International Overdose Awareness Day is an intentional recognition of the 836 lives that have been lost to overdose in Connecticut over the past year. On this day we stand with the families and communities who carry that loss and reaffirm our commitment to saving lives. DMHAS will continue to make investments in programs focused on prevention, treatment, recovery, and harm reduction. Every person living with substance use disorder is a member of our Connecticut community and deserves our support. We will continue to fight for them to receive the care and resources they need for recovery,” said Connecticut Department of Mental Health and Addiction Services Commissioner Nancy Navarretta.

“International Overdose Awareness Day is a time to remember and honor every life lost to overdose, and to stand with the families, friends, and communities who continue to carry that loss. But remembrance must also inspire action," said Connecticut Department of Public Health Commissioner Manisha Juthani, M.D. "At DPH, we are committed to preventing overdose deaths through evidence-based prevention, harm reduction, strong community partnerships, and efforts to prevent substance use before it begins. We must also continue to replace stigma with compassion and understanding. Addiction is a medical condition, not a moral failing, and everyone deserves the opportunity to seek help, access treatment, and recover. Together, we can save lives and build a healthier future for Connecticut.”

Connecticut has made progress in reducing fatal drug overdoses in recent years. In 2025, 836 individuals died from a drug overdose in Connecticut, representing a 45% decline from the state’s peak in 2021. The number of fatal drug overdoses has declined each year since 2021. While this progress is encouraging, the loss of 836 lives in a single year underscores that the overdose crisis remains a serious public health issue and that continued prevention, treatment, recovery, and harm reduction efforts are essential.

Connecticut has dedicated significant resources toward preventing overdose, expanding access to treatment and recovery services, increasing the availability of naloxone, and reducing the stigma associated with substance use disorder. State officials and community partners continue to encourage residents to learn how to recognize and respond to an overdose, carry naloxone, and connect people struggling with addiction to treatment and recovery supports.

title: Congressman Liccardo Responds to Six Months of the Iran War
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Congressman Sam Liccardo (CA-16) released the following statement on the six month mark of the war with Iran:

“We’re now six months into a war President Trump promised would last six weeks. By the Pentagon’s own estimate, it has already cost taxpayers $37.5 billion—a sum that could house every American experiencing homelessness for roughly four years.

“Meanwhile, Americans pay more at the pump, in the grocery aisle, and at the doctor’s office, while this president pockets every dollar he can through grift after grift.

“While we have exhausted much of our missile interceptor stocks in a war with Iran, making us unable to meet our commitments of defensive weapon deliveries to Taiwan and Japan, China’s and North Korea’s menacing threats to our Pacific allies only grow. title: Lofgren Convenes Experts to Discuss AI’s Potential Impact on Agriculture & Water Conservation
text:
SAN JOSÉ, CA — On Wednesday at San José State University, Congresswoman Zoe Lofgren (CA-18), Ranking Member of the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee, convened a roundtable of civic, academic, agricultural, and technology leaders to discuss the potential impacts artificial intelligence may have on agricultural productivity and water security. California’s 18th district, containing both Silicon Valley and the Salinas Valley, is uniquely positioned at the intersection of technology and agriculture, two of California’s defining economies. Some topics during the discussion included the obstacle of broadband deployment, automated weeding and harvesting technology already at work in strawberry and celery fields, predictive groundwater modeling that could address resource constraints, and expanding ag-tech engineering pathways for students in the area.

“Congress needs to be well-informed and proactive when it comes to addressing artificial intelligence’s role in our agriculture sector,” said Rep. Lofgren. “As with other industries, this new technology presents great possibilities but also valid concerns. I wanted to hold this roundtable to hear from some of the region’s brightest minds about how AI is already shaping agriculture and what should be done to protect and develop our workforce. As the leading Democrat on the House Science Committee, listening to experts is a big part of my role, and I appreciate all of the participants who shared their insights on these important topics which impact both Silicon Valley and the Salinas Valley."

In addition to her committee leadership, Lofgren serves as an Ex Officio Co-Chair of the House Democratic Commission on AI and the Innovation Economy. She has led multiple bipartisan bills in the 119th Congress to support responsible AI innovation with necessary guardrails, including the AI-Ready Federal Data Guidelines Act (H.R. 9341) and the Workforce for AI Trust Act (H.R. 9334). Both pieces of legislation passedunanimously out of the House Science Committee in June.

The roundtable included San José State University President Cynthia Teniente-Matson; SJUSD Board Chair José Magaña; Silicon Valley Leadership Group CEO Ahmad Thomas; Reservoir VC General Partner Nicola Kerslake; Monterey Bay Economic Partnership President and CEO Tahra Goraya; Synopsys Director of Government Affairs Victoria Tung; and San José State University's Dr. Katherine Cushing, Chair of the School of Planning, Policy, and Environmental Studies.

"AI has tremendous potential to help address challenges such as water conservation, precision irrigation, groundwater modeling and crop monitoring,” from Cynthia Teniente-Matson, President of San José State University. "I am proud that so many SJSU faculty members and students are deeply interested in connecting their research with real-world challenges, while helping ensure innovation advances the public good. The opportunity before us is to move from what AI makes possible to what California needs us to make possible. I thank Congresswoman Lofgren and everyone who contributed their expertise to this important conversation."

"Congresswoman Lofgren's leadership on the House Science, Space and Technology Committee and the Democratic Commission on Artificial Intelligence gives Silicon Valley a direct line into how federal AI policy gets made," said Ahmad Thomas, CEO of Silicon Valley Leadership Group. "Conversations like this one aren't just symbolic; they're a chance to make sure the people writing the rules for AI understand what's actually happening on the ground. SVLG is proud to help build a bridge from the Silicon Valley to the Salinas Valley that lifts up the voices of all stakeholders."

"AI has real potential to help Salinas Valley growers manage water, labor, and crop health more precisely, but none of that works without the infrastructure to connect it,” said Tahra Goraya, President and CEO of Monterey Bay Economic Partnership. "At MBEP, we've seen firsthand through our broadband buildout across rural, underserved parts of our region that closing the connectivity gap isn't a side issue to AI adoption in agriculture, it's the prerequisite. Rural broadband is the infrastructure that determines whether the next generation of ag technology reaches every farm in this valley, or just the ones that can already afford to leapfrog the gap."

"AI is going to reshape nearly every career path our students consider, which means the investments we make in TK-12 STEM education today directly determine who gets to participate in that future economy,” said José Magaña, President of the San José Unified Board of Trustees. "Early exposure to STEM changes outcomes, particularly for Latino students who remain underrepresented in these fields relative to their share of California's student population. Conversations like this one, informed by Congresswoman Lofgren's role on the AI Commission, are a chance to make sure that federal AI policy doesn't just focus on innovation but that it focuses on the pipeline of talent that has to exist for that innovation to be built by, and benefit, communities like ours."

“Synopsys provides engineering solutions that help companies design and optimize complex systems, from chips to industrial equipment to digital infrastructure and more,” said Victoria Tung, Director of Government Affairs at Synopsys. "Discussions like this underscore the importance of designing technologies that meet customer requirements while balancing the needs of the communities where they are deployed.”

"AI's intersection with agriculture and water resources raises complex and important issues, requiring an approach that engages multiple research disciplines and sectors in our society,” said Dr. Crist S. Khachikian, Vice President for Research and Innovation at San José State University. "A comprehensive public research university like SJSU is ideally suited to helping us get the governance right, ensure growers of every size can put these tools to use, and prepare the workforce for the changes ahead. California agriculture feeds the nation and the expertise in that room was diverse and palpable. I thank the Congresswoman and everyone around the table for a thoughtful and meaningful conversation.”

title: McClain Delaney, Van Hollen, Alsobrooks Announce $240,000 for Frederick Municipal Airport’s Air Traffic Control Tower
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Congresswoman April McClain Delaney alongside U.S. Senators Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks (all D-Md.) announced $240,000 in federal funding for infrastructure upgrades at Frederick Municipal Airport’s air traffic control tower. The investment will fund the rehabilitation of the tower’s HVAC system. This funding is in addition to $1.6 million in federal support that the lawmakers have secured for other infrastructure projects at Frederick Municipal Airport, which serves as a reliever airport for Baltimore Washington International Airport and supports local business and a range of community-related operations, including emergency medical needs.

"As Frederick County continues to grow, we need infrastructure that grows with it,” said Congresswoman McClain Delaney. “This $240,000 federal investment will modernize Frederick Municipal Airport’s air traffic control tower, strengthen safety and reliability, and support an airport that is critical to our local economy. I’m proud to work with Senators Van Hollen and Alsobrooks to bring federal dollars home and deliver for Frederick County.”

“As Maryland’s second busiest airport, Frederick Municipal Airport serves as a local economic hub, driving regional businesses, bringing visitors to Maryland, and supporting the surrounding community with a broad array of services. That’s why we’ve worked to support the airport’s modernization and deliver federal investments to upgrade its infrastructure. This investment will help ensure the airport’s control tower has the infrastructure it needs to continue providing safe and efficient service to all travelers,” said Senator Van Hollen.

“This $1.6 million in critical federal funding will enable the Frederick Municipal Airport to continue serving Maryland—supporting small businesses, moving goods, and strengthening our health care response. This investment will improve our infrastructure, strengthen our economy, and help keep Marylanders safe,” said Senator Alsobrooks.

This investment is provided through the Federal Aviation Administration’s Contract Tower Competitive Grant Program, which was created and funded at $100 million over five years through the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act passed by Congress in 2021.

###

title: McClain Delaney, Van Hollen, Alsobrooks Announce Over $3 Million in Federal Funding to Improve Water Infrastructure in Western Maryland
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Congresswoman April McClain Delaney with U.S. Senators Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks (all D-Md.) announced $3,340,000 in federal funding to improve water and wastewater infrastructure across Western Maryland. This investment, comprising a $2,779,000 loan for the Town of Emmitsburg to replace a critical Main Street water line, a $465,000 grant for the Town of Luke’s replacement of its sewer collection system, and a $96,000 grant for Garrett County’s planning costs for the Friendsville and Crellin wastewater treatment upgrades, will help Western Maryland communities upgrade critical infrastructure.

“Every rural community deserves reliable water and wastewater infrastructure, no matter its size or ZIP code,” said Congresswoman McClain Delaney. “This more than $3 million federal investment will help replace aging water and sewer systems and lay the groundwork for critical upgrades across Frederick, Allegany, and Garrett Counties. I’m proud to work alongside Senators Van Hollen and Alsobrooks to bring federal resources home and ensure our rural communities have the infrastructure they need to grow and thrive.”

“Aging water systems put the health and safety of communities at risk. That’s why it’s essential we invest in modernizing community water and sewer infrastructure. This federal funding will support these much-needed improvements across Western Maryland and help prevent costly problems for communities, businesses, and residents in the future,” said Senator Van Hollen.

“From Mountain Maryland to the Eastern Shore, I will always work to ensure Marylanders across our state have access to clean and safe drinking water. Investing in clean water – as we are in Frederick, Allegany, and Garrett Counties with this over $3 million federal investment – protects public health, helps us meet our environmental goals, and ensures our infrastructure is modern and resilient,” said Senator Alsobrooks.

The federal funding has been awarded as follows:

$2,779,000 loan to the Town of Emmitsburg in Frederick County to replace a water line along Main Street.

$465,000 grant to the Town of Luke in Allegany County to replace its sewer collection system.

$96,000 grant to the Garrett County Sanitary District to conduct Preliminary Engineering and Environmental reports for the Friendsville and Crellin wastewater treatment plants.

This federal funding is provided through the U.S. Department of Agriculture Rural Development Water and Waste Disposal Loans and Grants Program, which the lawmakers worked to fund at $140 million in the Fiscal Year 2026 appropriations package.
