title: What They’re Saying: Responses to the Third Circuit’s Refusal to Dismiss U.S. v. McIver
text:
“A brazen and unlawful abuse of power, and a direct attack on congressional oversight”

WASHINGTON, DC — On Wednesday, the Third Circuit Court of Appeals threw out Congresswoman LaMonica McIver’s (NJ-10) motion to dismiss her case, U.S. v. McIver. Since the news broke, McIver has received a groundswell of support for the case which she said in a Wednesday statement is “not over.” One thing is clear: The case against McIver is not only baseless, but it poses a threat to democracy. The people are talking and they’re not happy about this outcome. Here’s what they’re saying.

What lawmakers are saying:

“Donald Trump wants Congressmembers to fall in line & not conduct oversight of detention centers. And he wants to make an example out of @RepLaMonica. But we’re not letting up.” (Rep. Ayanna Pressley)

“Criminalizing oversight deters lawmakers from holding Trump accountable—even if Democrats take back Congress. LaMonica is strong and won’t be intimidated, but the continued attacks on her for doing her job is dangerous to our democracy.” (Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman)

“Trump weaponizing the Department of Justice to target members of Congress simply for doing their jobs is straight out of his corruption playbook. It’s a brazen and unlawful abuse of power, and a direct attack on congressional oversight.” (Gov. Mikie Sherrill)

What the press is saying:

“Between going to doctor’s appointments, attending congressional hearings, serving her constituents, meeting with her lawyers, raising money for her defense and continuing to keep a spotlight on the treatment of immigrants in detention, McIver isn’t just fighting for her seat — she’s fighting for her freedom.” (Errin Haines, The 19th)

“McIver faces up to 17 years in prison if convicted in the case. She argued that the charges brought against her were for political reasons, citing numerous statements by the Trump Administration, President Trump himself and former prosecutor Alina Habba, who initially brought federal charges against McIver before leaving her position and becoming an aide in the administration.” (Brandon Caldwell, TheGrio)

What advocacy groups are saying:

“One of the more troubling features of the current administration is its apparent penchant for prosecuting perceived political adversaries of the President. The prosecution of Congresswoman McIver bears the hallmarks of just such a prosecution.” (Washington Litigation Group)

“Today’s decision is a grave miscarriage of justice… What is happening to Rep. McIver is no accident: it is an intimidation tactic aimed at silencing a sitting member of Congress who stood up to protect her community members from human rights violations.” (Fatima Goss Graves, NWLC)

“Weaponizing the DOJ to target a sitting Member of Congress undermines our system of checks and balances and threatens our democracy.” (Amol Sinha, ACLU NJ)

“The Trump administration is using LaMonica McIver as an example. It is a message to all lawmakers– if you stand up to ICE, if you fight back, we’ll come after you. Rep. McIver is showing us what fighting back looks like. Despite a split appeals court declining to drop the case, she is standing strong against these politically motivated charges… We stand with her 100%” (Vote Mama)

McIver and her legal team are currently exploring all options for moving the case forward. Those options include but are not limited to asking for the case to be heard en banc by the Third Circuit or by the U.S. Supreme Court. McIver is running for re-election and is eight months pregnant. For additional information on the upcoming developments in McIver’s case, please contact Hanna.Rumsey@mail.house.gov.

title: THOMPSON APPLAUDS REVERSAL OF DANGEROUS PRAIRIE POTHOLE WETLAND ROLLBACK
text:
St. Helena, CA – Rep. Mike Thompson (CA-04), Chair of the Congressional Wildlife Refuge Caucus and a member of the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission (MBCC), applauded the U.S. Department of the Interior’s decision to halt proposed changes that could have weakened longstanding protections for wetland easements in the Prairie Pothole Region. The announcement came after Rep. Thompson spoke out against the proposal and more than 200,000 Americans submitted comments on the proposal.

The proposed changes could have allowed increased drainage near protected wetlands, threatening critical waterfowl breeding habitat in the region that produces more than half of North America’s migratory waterfowl.

“I'm glad the Administration reversed course on this dangerous proposal. I spoke out against these changes and urged the Administration to maintain these longstanding protections because these wetlands are critical to our migratory birds and waterfowl,” said Rep. Thompson. “The Administration never should have put these protections at risk in the first place. This is a win for conservation, but we must remain vigilant to make sure these wetlands are protected for generations to come.”

“Waterfowl nesting in the Prairie Potholes are critical for the continental migrations. Recent proposed changes from US Fish and Wildlife Service opening up voluntary conservation easements to tile draining could have been disastrous. Thank you to the wise conservation-minded hunters and fishers, and our own Congressman Mike Thompson who spoke up to defeat this sad proposed change,” said Dr. Frederic Reid, Wildlife Ecologist.

BACKGROUND

The Prairie Pothole Region spans portions of Montana, the Dakotas, Minnesota, and Iowa and produces more than half of North America’s migratory waterfowl. For more than 60 years, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) has maintained protections for wetlands covered by voluntary conservation easements.

In July, USFWS opened a 14-day public comment period on potential changes to its drain-tile setback policies. More than 200,000 comments were submitted during the review. On August 14, USFWS announced that “no further action is planned” at this time as it reviews the information received.

Rep. Thompson joined members of the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission in sending a letter to the Administration urging it to maintain the existing protections and reject the proposed changes.

The full text of the letter can be found here and below.

The Honorable Doug Burgum

Secretary

U.S. Department of the Interior

1849 C Street, N.W.

Washington, DC 20240

Dear Secretary Burgum:

As Members of the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission (MBCC), we write to express our strong support for maintaining long-standing and science-based U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service wetland easement protections and the current drain tile setback standards that have allowed for the conservation of wetlands in the Prairie Pothole Region for more than sixty years while providing benefits and certainty to participating landowners. These protections are essential to sustaining North America's migratory bird populations, protecting taxpayer-funded conservation investments, and preserving one of the continent's most important waterfowl breeding landscapes.

Congress established the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission to oversee and advance the conservation of migratory birds and their habitat through strategic federal investments and collaboration and partnership with private landowners. The Commission plays a central role in reviewing and approving land acquisitions, easements, and habitat conservation projects funded through the Migratory Bird Conservation Fund, including revenues generated by the Federal Duck Stamp program, and the North American Wetlands Conservation Fund. Through these authorities, the Commission helps ensure that public conservation investments produce lasting benefits for waterfowl, other migratory birds, sportsmen and women, and the American public.

The Prairie Pothole Region produces more than half of the continent's migratory waterfowl. Wetlands protected through federal easement programs provide critical nesting and brood-rearing habitats that support waterfowl populations across the nation.

As Commissioners, we are concerned by recent actions that call into question the science-based, conservation-focused, and collaborative protections associated with permanent Fish and Wildlife Service wetland easements. These easements were voluntarily entered into by willing landowners and purchased using taxpayer resources to conserve wetlands in perpetuity. The value of these investments depends on maintaining the integrity of protected wetlands. Allowing activities that undermine wetland function would diminish both the biological benefits of these easements and the public return on decades of successful public-private wetland conservation spending.

The Commission has long championed the principle that conservation investments must be durable, provide benefits and certainty for private landowners, and manage vital waterfowl habitat using the best available science. We respectfully urge the Department of the Interior to maintain the science-based drain tile setback standards that have successfully protected Service easements for decades; uphold the integrity of voluntary easement agreements; prevent the drainage of protected wetlands; and provide landowners with legal safe harbor and the certainty necessary to fulfill their conservation commitments. Doing so will honor commitments made to willing landowners, protect taxpayer investments, support healthy migratory bird populations for generations to come, and build upon the success of this conservation model.

Thank you for your continued commitment to conserving America's wetlands and migratory bird resources.

Sincerely,

###

Congressman Mike Thompson is proud to represent California’s 4th Congressional District, which includes all or part of Lake, Napa, Solano, Sonoma and Yolo Counties. He is a senior member of the House Committee on Ways and Means. Rep. Thompson is Chairman of the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force. He is also Co-Chair of the bipartisan, bicameral Congressional Wine Caucus and a member of the fiscally-responsible Blue Dog Coalition.

title: Miller Applauds $750,000 Rural Residency Planning and Development Funds Awarded to Princeton Community Hospital Association
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. - Today, the Health Resources and Services Administration announced a $750,000 award to Princeton Community Hospital Association as part of the Rural Residency Planning and Development program. Funding is used to expand and improve access to health care in rural areas, supporting start-up costs to create new rural residency programs, including Rural Track Programs (RTPs), in qualifying medical specialties.

“The Rural Residency Planning and Development Program is vital to addressing physician shortages in rural communities. By studying and practicing in rural areas, our next generation of physicians can be better equipped to handle the unique challenges these areas bring, and studies show physicians who train in rural areas are more likely to stay there long-term. I was happy to join in colleagues last December in introducing legislation to authorize the Rural Residency Planning and Development Program, and am thrilled to see the Princeton Community Hospital Association receive this award. This funding will improve access to quality, life-saving care in our rural communities, and help Make America Healthy Again,” said Congresswoman Miller.

Background

- In December 2025, Congresswoman Miller introduced the Rural Residency Planning and Development Act, authorizing the Rural Residency Planning and Development Program.

- Only 2% of residency training occurs in rural areas. Training physicians in rural areas improves access to care and also increases the likelihood of practicing in a rural community.

- Nearly 20% of Americans live in rural areas, but only 10% of physicians practice in these communities.

- The United States continues to face a serious physician shortage, especially in rural communities. Current projections show the nation may fall short by up to 124,000 physicians in the next decade, with rural areas alone expecting to face a deficit of more than 20,000 primary care doctors by this year.

- Training, recruiting, and retaining physicians in rural communities is essential to ensuring that people living in these areas have reliable access to comprehensive health care services.

title: Congressman Griffith’s Weekly E-Newsletter 8.28.26
text:
On September 7, Americans will celebrate Labor Day.

The American worker serves as a backbone for our economy. Thanks to the fruits of their labor, our communities reap the rewards of more opportunity, business growth and expanded access to goods and services.

Even in times of hardship where industries face new challenges, and when innovative technologies emerge, the American workforce shows resilience by adapting.

This resilience takes shape in the belief that hard work is central to our communities. We see numerous investments that drive this belief for our region’s workforce.

In the last year, Henry County celebrated various company investments resulting in a cumulative total of more than $100 million.

There is also Narro Trucks which recently launched in Pulaski County. The electric utility vehicle company will power new jobs for the New River Valley.

Further, thanks to a new industrial investment, Bland County’s Virginia Steel and Fabrication is set to expand operational capabilities.

Earlier this year, I toured the Virginia Steel plant in Bastian to receive updates on its operations and leadership.

These industry decisions, among others, will support regional job, generate friendly climates for small businesses and deliver renewed hope for our communities.

Because these investments mean so much, I am an advocate for federal policies that help the American worker access opportunity for work.

From job programs, including ones that develop skills, to friendly tax environments, we can use policy to strengthen this access.

As we rest for Labor Day weekend, join me in celebrating the American worker.

Days after Labor Day, I will join our communities to recognize solemn occasions.

September 10 marks the one-year anniversary of the assassination of a conservative icon. In broad daylight on a college campus, Turning Point USA CEO Charlie Kirk was murdered by an individual seemingly indoctrinated by radical gender ideology.

My family shared the shock and grief with millions of Americans stunned by Kirk’s murder.

Following the slaying, I supported Kirk’s legacy and memory, visiting Virginia Tech with Lieutenant Governor Winsome Sears for a candlelight vigil.

Outside of my DC office along with countless other Congressional offices, I displayed a poster of Kirk.

Additionally, I voted with 309 of my House colleagues to honor Kirk’s life and legacy. It was disappointing to see more than 100 Democrats refrain from supporting the House resolution, but I remain committed to protecting the conservative values and freedoms that Kirk constantly worked to defend.

Perhaps nothing meant more to Kirk’s movement than the freedom of speech, a cornerstone of our country’s founding and the U.S. Constitution.

We must never forget that disagreements, discourse and debate are healthy for our government. Kirk provided a venue for our younger generations to recognize this fundamental truth.

Silencing Americans is never a solution. I will continue to support policies that protect the freedom of speech.

Please join me on September 10 to not only pray for Charlie, but to ask that God helps with healing for Charlie’s widow, Erika, their two young children and the entire Kirk family.

Americans will also reflect on the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks.

To this day, the attacks are a painful memory for millions of Americans as well as many across the entire world.

I have the memory of working that morning in my law office when my bookkeeper, Terry Haynie, grabbed my attention. She informed me that a plane struck a Tower of the World Trade Center.

After turning our eyes to the television to see the events live, we watched the second plane crash into the South Tower.

The Pentagon was also hit, while a thwarted attempt resulted in a plane crash in Pennsylvania.

When passengers of Flight 93 knew the end was coming, they would not allow that plane to be used to attack America. It is believed that plane was headed for the U.S. Capitol where I now work.

In total, more than 3,000 innocent lives were taken from us that day.

While the terrorists sought to strike fear, they failed to break the enduring spirit of the American people.

Following the tragedy, I drove to Salem’s Kmart store to buy an American flag. I proudly displayed it outside my office.

I plan to attend a 9/11 wreath laying with former Governor Glenn Youngkin at the National D-Day Memorial.

With these events on the horizon, it will be an emotional time for many.

But over the Labor Day weekend, we will rejoice that the American worker is the most efficient, hardworking labor force in the world.

If you have questions, concerns, or comments, feel free to contact my office. You can call my Abingdon office at 276-525-1405 or my Christiansburg office at 540-381-5671. To reach my office via email, please visit my website at https://morgangriffith.house.gov/.

title: Pallone Celebrates Next Steps on Beach Replenishment Projects in Monmouth County
text:
LONG BRANCH, NJ — Congressman Frank Pallone, Jr. (NJ-06) today announced that the US Army Corps of Engineers is awarding a $38.3 million contract to Weeks Marine to begin a targeted sand replenishment project in Monmouth County, including sections of the towns of Monmouth Beach, Sea Bright, and Long Branch. With this funding, the Army Corps of Engineers will be able to complete the sections of the project covered by both the base contract and its options.

“Beach replenishment is about keeping people safe,” said Pallone. “With strong coastlines, our residents, businesses, and communities are better equipped to face extreme weather events. I’m glad I was able to secure the federal funding necessary to support this project, which will make these Jersey Shore communities more resilient in the years to come.”

Congressman Pallone secured $37 million in federal funding for the project, which will be matched with a combination of state and local funds. The contract includes a section of Monmouth Beach starting at the Monmouth Beach Bathing Pavilion and going north to the Monmouth Beach Bath and Tennis Club. Sea Bright will see most of their ocean beach front replenished and the area in Long Branch north of Pier Village to Seven President’s Park will also receive sand.

The US Army Corps of Engineers will place 1.3 million cubic yards of sand across these three towns. The project is expected to begin in late fall, finishing by March 2027.

title: Following 50% Tariffs on Canada, Rep. Panetta Joins Introduction of Bill to Repeal Section 338, Refund Tariffs
text:
Monterey, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) joined Rep. Brad Schneider (IL-10) and Senators Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) and Peter Welch (D-VT) in introducing the Banning Antiquated Duties and Delivering Equitable American Levies (BAD DEAL) Act to repeal Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 and refund all duties paid under this authority. Over the weekend, trade talks between the United States and Canada broke down, resulting in the United States’ imposition of 50% tariffs on roughly $20 billion in Canadian goods under Section 338. In response, Canada is pledging dollar-for-dollar retaliatory tariffs slated to come into effect after Labor Day.

The United States and Canada share one of the world’s largest and most integrated trading relationships. In 2025, bilateral trade in goods and services totaled approximately $872 billion, including nearly $426 billion in U.S. exports. Canada is the United States’ second-largest trading partner and the top merchandise export market for 32 states. These new tariffs threaten to disrupt cross-border supply chains, raise costs for American families and businesses, and invite further retaliation against U.S. industries.

“This Administration’s senseless tariff policies and self-defeating trade wars have already hurt American businesses and raised costs for working families. Now, the President’s 40-year fixation on tariffs is producing yet another bad deal for the American people by imposing massive new duties on Canada, our second-largest trading partner and a longstanding ally,” said Rep. Panetta. “I’m proud to join Rep. Schneider and other Ways and Means colleagues in introducing the BAD DEAL Act to repeal this antiquated authority under Section 338 and refund the duties American businesses have already been forced to pay. It is long past time for Congress to reclaim its constitutional authority over trade and put an end to this Administration’s destructive tariff regime.”

“Every American deserves a fair shot to get ahead, and Trump’s capricious and costly tariffs are making it exceedingly difficult to simply make ends meet,” said Rep. Schneider. “President Trump’s brazen and counterproductive trade war only damages the long-standing, mutually beneficial relationship with our neighbor, and second largest trading partner, Canada. This is a bad deal! It’s a bad deal for American families, and it’s a bad deal for American small businesses. I’m proud to work with my colleagues to introduce the aptly named BAD DEAL Act to repeal this outdated tariff authority AND refund the tariff duties paid. We will continue fighting to rein in Trump’s costly tariffs and reassert Congress’ authority before his on-again, off-again trade policy damages our international relationships for years to come.”

In addition to Rep. Panetta, cosponsors of the BAD DEAL Act include Reps. Don Beyer (VA-08), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), Tim Kennedy (NY-26), Terri Sewell (AL-07), Greg Stanton (AZ-04), and Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10).

In 2025, Rep. Panetta joined Rep. Schneider in introducing the Repealing Outdated and Unilateral Tariff Authorities Act, which would repeal Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930.

Full text of the bill is available here.

title: Pappas Announces 43 New Cosponsors of His Bill to End Corrupting Influence of Dark Money in American Elections, Bringing Total to 181
text:
Today Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01) announced that his DISCLOSE Act has gained 43 additional cosponsors since its introduction, bringing the total number of cosponsors to 181 in the House. Pappas introduced this legislation in March alongside U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (RI), House Judiciary Committee Ranking Member Jamie Raskin (MD-08) and House Administration Committee Ranking Member Joe Morelle (NY-25).

The DISCLOSE Act would end the scourge of dark money in our democracy, shine a bright light of transparency on politics, and make government more accountable to the will of voters.

"Trust in our government is nearing historic lows, and we need to take action to bring greater transparency to our elections and restore Americans’ faith that their voices will be heard in our democracy,” said Congressman Pappas. “The DISCLOSE Act would stop billionaires and corporate special interests from secretly buying our elections by requiring dark money groups to disclose who their donors are and shining a light on payments made to social media influencers to promote or attack candidates. I’m thrilled to see support for this legislation grow, bringing us closer to putting the power of our democracy back in the hands of the people.”

Since the 2010 Citizens United decision, secret spending in U.S. elections by corporations, ultra-rich ideological extremists, and secretive front groups has exploded. These dark-money expenditures that corrupt our politics increased from less than $5 million in 2006 to more than $300 million in the 2012 election cycle, and topped $1.9 billion in 2024, shattering the previous record of $1 billion in 2020.

The DISCLOSE Act would restore transparency in American elections and restore fairness and accountability in our political system by:

Requiring super PACs, 501(c)(4) “dark money” groups, corporations, and other organizations spending more than $10,000 in elections and on judicial nominations to promptly disclose donors who contribute more than $10,000;

Shutting down the use of transfers between organizations to cloak the identity of the original contributor.

Strengthening prohibitions against foreign actors participating in election spending in the United States, including in state and local referenda;

Prohibiting the establishment of corporations to conceal election contributions and donations by foreign actors;

Expanding “stand by your ad” disclosure requirements to online ads and ads that may promote or attack a candidate but stop short of expressly advocating for a vote for or against a candidate; and

Requiring identification of top funders of outside groups paying for video, text, or audio political ads.

The bill has been adapted to the modern political ecosystem. The DISCLOSE Act of 2026 would:

Capture payments made to social media influencers to promote or oppose a candidate as political spending that must be disclosed and disclaimed;

Narrow and specify what constitutes threats and harassment to qualify for an exemption to disclosure, and put commonsense guardrails on the process to grant such exemptions; and

Allow more flexibility for disclaimers for short political ads instead of limiting it to hyperlinks.

Several prominent good-government organizations support the bill including Campaign Legal Center, Democracy Defenders Action, Public Citizen, Democracy21, End Citizens United, Common Cause, Center for American Progress, and the Brennan Center.

A summary of the DISCLOSE Act of 2026 can be found here. The House bill text can be found here, and the Senate bill text can be found here.

Background:

Rep. Pappas has been an original cosponsor of the DISCLOSE Act since he came to Congress. He led efforts to pass the DISCLOSE Act in the 118th Congress following the retirement of Rep. David Cicilline.

title: “A TOTAL FIASCO,” AS WAR IN IRAN REACHES SIXTH MONTH, CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN BLASTS REPUBLICANS ENABLING TRUMP’S COSTLY, DEADLY WAR; ESCALATES CALL TO FIRE PETE HEGSETH

Congressman Ryan has been the leading voice of opposition to Trump’s war in Iran; he sits on the House Armed Services Committee, is the first West Point graduate to represent the Academy in Congress, and served two combat tours in Iraq earning him two Bronze Stars

After a March 1st Iranian drone strike killed 6 U.S. servicemembers in Kuwait, Ryan blasted Secretary Hegseth face to face for putting troops in danger, refusing to take accountability, and then calling survivors of the horrific attack liars

As the war in Iran reaches its sixth month – with 18 brave U.S. servicemembers killed and billions in taxpayer dollars spent – Ryan is continuing to demand Hegseth’s resignation and fighting to pass his No Funds for Iran War Act

WASHINGTON, DC – Today marks six months since Trump launched his war in Iran. Throughout the course of the war, Congressman Pat Ryan – who sits on the House Armed Services Committee, is the first West Point graduate to represent the Academy in Congress, and served two combat tours in Iraq earning him two Bronze Stars – has been the leading voice of opposition to the costly, deadly war in Iran. As the administration continues its war with no strategy, Ryan is escalating his calls to end the war and for Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth to resign.

“From Day 1 of this reckless war in Iran, Trump and Hegseth have lied to and betrayed the American people on every level. They lied about the timeline, lied about the cost, and left hardworking Americans to foot the bill for a war they never wanted in the first place,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “18 brave American Patriots have died because of their utter incompetence, and hundreds more have been injured while their families are left in the dark. The entire war has been a total fiasco – and instead of ending it, the chickenhawk President and unfit SecDef are doubling down on a losing strategy. I’m going to keep fighting everyday, with every fiber of my being, to end this war, bring our troops home, and hold everyone accountable – especially Hegseth – for this historic disaster.”

In the first week of the war, President Donald Trump said it would take “four to five weeks” to achieve the war’s objectives. Six months later, 18 brave U.S. servicemembers have been killed – 6 of whom were knowingly sent to an unfortified position and denied additional protection – at least 750 more have been injured, and zero objectives have been achieved.

A Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll found that 61 percent of Americans believe using military force against Iran was a mistake, making Trump’s war as unpopular among Americans as the Iraq War during the peak of violence in 2006 and the Vietnam War in the early 1970s.

The Pentagon’s internal overall cost estimate has exceeded $100 billion. That number doesn’t even account for the cost to the American people. Gas prices have soared, as people across NY‐18 have spent an additional $172 million on gas since the beginning of the war, costing the average family in our district an additional $646 in gas costs over the past six months. Grocery prices have also skyrocketed as the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

Ryan has repeatedly cosponsored and voted in favor of War Powers Resolutions to end the war in Iran five separate times.

In May, amid reports that the Pentagon would seek $200B in supplemental funding for the war, Ryan introduced the No Funds for Iran War Act, which would prohibit the use of additional taxpayer funds for military action against Iran in the absence of an Authorization for the Use of Military Force (AUMF) or official declaration of war from Congress. Ryan introduced the legislation with the support of his fellow Democratic veterans in Congress, and it has continued to grow in support in the enduring months of the war.

In April, Ryan confronted Hegseth himself during a House Armed Services Committee hearing, pressing him on his failure to protect troops at Port Shuaiba. Following new reporting on the strike on Port Shuaiba, Ryan opened an investigation in August into how the Department of Defense failed to provide adequate medical care to service members injured and demanded answers about the Department's lack of preparation for a strike against Port Shuaiba.

Last month, Ryan spoke on the House floor against handing Hegseth’s Pentagon a $1.5 trillion blank check through the FY27 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). He criticized colleagues for again refusing to consider his No Funds for Iran War Act, especially following the successful passage of a War Powers Resolution.

“It's personal to me. Having served twenty-seven months in combat in Iraq. Watching us double down on a losing strategy, year after year, while my friends and fellow soldiers – many of whose names are on this memorial bracelet I wear – fought and died. It's personal to the now eighteen families who lost their loved ones in this reckless war in Iran — sons, daughters, husbands, wives, somebody's whole world. It’s personal to the hundreds more wounded, many carrying injuries that will last their entire lives from this war,” Ryan said on the House floor.

Ryan’s full floor remarks can be viewed here.

Most recently, when the Trump administration tried to downplay the number of casualties in the war, Ryan again joined his Democratic veteran colleagues in demandingthe Administration accurately and transparently account for U.S. servicemembers killed and wounded in the Iran war.

Congressman Ryan is a U.S. Army veteran, served two combat tours in Iraq, and is the first West Point graduate to represent the Academy in the U.S. House of Representatives. Amid recent threats to veterans’ benefits, national security concerns, and rising threats worldwide, Congressman Ryan led his fellow veterans in Congress to create the Democratic Veterans Caucus. He sits on the House Armed Services Committee and has led extensive legislation to deliver relief for veterans, servicemembers, and military families.

title: Amata Highlights National Park of American Samoa During National Park Week
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Uifa’atali Amata is highlighting the beautiful National Park of American Samoa during National Park Week. Typically held in April, park week was moved to August this year to align with this week’s National Park Service’s 110th birthday, celebrated August 25th. National Park Week is an annual celebration of gorgeous natural landscapes, viewpoints, hiking trails, shorelines, historic battlefields, and protected wildlife and woodland areas.

Recent ASG photo with Park Liaison Pua Tuaua, Lt Governor Pulumataala, and Park Superintendent Paul PT Lathrop

“Our National Park of American Samoa emphasizes special places within our beautiful islands, showcases our ancient culture, and protects wildlife and bird habitat,” said Congresswoman Aumua Amata. “Thank you to our entire Park team, and happy birthday to the National Park Service and all its personnel. Thank you also to all our people who take personal care and responsibility in the seemingly small choices that cumulatively do so much to help our islands stay beautiful, whether in or out of the Park borders.”

American Samoa and its National Park has birds such as the Ti’otola (bright-plumed Pacific kingfishers and flat-billed kingfishers of regional varieties that differ from those elsewhere), while rugged Pola Island, offshore from Vatia, is among American Samoa’s nesting sites for tropical seabirds including the Fua’o (brown and red-footed boobies), and Ta’i’o (shearwaters) as part of a rich diversity of species, with local and migratory birds from as far as Alaska, like the Bristle-thighed Curlew.

The National Park of American Samoa has several unique and rare features within the national system. It is the only one in the South Pacific, so it has plants and species not found anywhere else in the United States. It is also a multi-site Park, within several islands, and it protects certain offshore coral reefs.

The NPS is part of the Department of the Interior, under the jurisdiction of the Natural Resources Committee, where Amata serves as Vice Chairman of the Subcommittee on Indian and Insular Affairs, and serves on the Subcommittee on Water, Wildlife and Fisheries. The United States has 63 National Parks and 433 total sites, and National Park Week is an initiative of the NPS and the National Park Foundation.

In related legislation, Amata is an original cosponsor of the Committee-passed bipartisan America the Beautiful Act, H.R. 9250, also known as the Great American Outdoors Act 250, which has since its introduction attracted the public support of well more than half of the House of Representatives. This bill builds on the original GAOA, signed into law in 2020, a landmark generational investment in national parks and public lands, and reauthorizes its Legacy Restoration Fund at $1.9 billion yearly to maintain, restore, and improve parks and related infrastructure. Notably, the bill states that “amounts remaining in the Fund after the allocations required under subparagraph (A) may be allocated for transportation projects of the covered agencies, including paved and unpaved roads, bridges (etc.) …”

Also, Amata is an original cosponsor of the bipartisan EXPLORE Act (Expanding Public Lands Outdoor Recreation Experiences Act), which became law on January 4, 2025. This Congress, the bipartisan Fix Our Forests Act was passed by the House 279-141 and awaits a Senate vote.

title: Ramirez, Garcia, Johnson, Tlaib Lead Congressional Inquiry Into TSA Data Sharing, ICE Enforcement at Airports
text:
Washington, DC – Today, Congresswoman Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Ranking Member of a Subcommittee on the Homeland Security Committee, led 28 colleagues in opening an investigation into a new data-sharing agreement between the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) that has resulted in a spike in immigration enforcement activities at airports across the country. In the inquiry, the members raise the possibility of violations of privacy and civil liberties, as well as safety concerns, for all U.S. residents and international visitors traveling through airports. The letter was co-led by Congressman Robert Garcia (CA-42) — Ranking Member of the Oversight Committee, Congressman Henry C. "Hank" Johnson (GA-04), and Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib (MI-12).

The inquiry directed to the Department of Homeland Security follows American Oversight obtaining a partially redacted memorandum of agreement (MOA) signed in May 2025 that formalized a new data-sharing partnership between TSA and ICE. The agreement documents that TSA is sharing personally identifiable information, including passenger names and birth dates, and other data with ICE to conduct immigration enforcement, contradicting former Acting TSA Administrator Ha Nguyen McNeill’s sworn congressional testimony that TSA does not send such information to ICE.

“Handing travelers' private information over to immigration officers for the purposes of conducting immigration enforcement without warrants or due process violates long-standing safeguards meant to protect the safety and rights of the American people. TSA must acknowledge the dangerous precedent associated with forging secret agreements that allow the government to expand how it uses residents’ personal information absent consent, guardrails, transparency, or oversight,” wrote the Members. “The consequences of such action reach far beyond immigration and raise profound concerns about privacy, civil liberties, and public trust. TSA and ICE must change course immediately.”

According to a Reuters report, as of April 2026, TSA reportedly shared the personal information of more than 31,000 travelers with ICE, which led to more than 800 immigration-related arrests. Since TSA and ICE have not publicly disclosed the unredacted information-sharing agreement, it remains unclear how information is shared and why immigrants are targeted for arrest.

The department has until September 7, 2026, to provide details about the agreement and its effect on immigration enforcement and travelers' privacy.

The letter was signed by Representatives Judy Chu (CA-28), Lou Correa (CA-46), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Danny Davis (IL-07), Diana DeGette (CO-01), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), John Garamendi (CA-08), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Dan Goldman (NY-10), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Jahana Hayes (CT-05), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Robin Kelly (IL-02), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Morgan McGarvey (KY-03), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), Chellie Pingree (ME-01), Emily Randall (WA-06), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Adam Smith (WA-09), and Jill Tokuda (HI-02).

title: SCHNEIDER, BELL, TOGETHER WITH 70+ DEMOCRATIC COLLEAGUES, URGE DEFENSE SECRETARY HEGESETH AND ACTING SECRETARY OF THE NAVY HUNG CAO TO PROTECT LEGACY OF THE FUTURE USS DORIS MILLER
text:
LINCOLNSHIRE, IL – Today, Congressman Brad Schneider (IL-10) and Congressman Wesley Bell (MO-1), joined by 70+ Democratic colleagues, urged Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao to reject any effort to rename the future USS Doris Miller (CVN-81) after reports that the Navy is considering naming the carrier after President Trump.

The future USS Doris Miller will be the first aircraft carrier named for an African American and the first named in honor of an enlisted sailor. Doris “Dorie” Miller remains one of the most celebrated enlisted sailors in American military history for his bravery and courage during the attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941. The potential move to name the carrier after a sitting president would break with longstanding Navy tradition and diminish the recognition of Miller’s extraordinary acts of bravery and his service to our nation.

As home to Naval Station Great Lakes, naval tradition and history run deep throughout Illinois’ 10th District. Every enlisted sailor in the Navy begins their journey at Great Lakes, completing basic training before going on to serve our nation. The 10th District has long been proud to play a role in preparing these sailors for service, and we must continue to honor the legacy of those who have helped shape the Navy and our nation.

“A strong Navy is built on the courage and valor of its sailors, both in times of conflict and peace,” said Schneider. “Doris Miller’s extraordinary service, unwavering loyalty to his fellow sailors, and devotion to his country are a source of pride for all Americans. Honoring his legacy is the right thing to do and an opportunity to inspire future generations. Doris Miller should not be robbed of this rightful honor and am proud to join my colleagues in this effort to urge Secretary Hegseth and Acting Secretary Cao to recognize Miller’s heroism and reject another Trump vanity project.”

“The decision to name CVN-81 for Doris Miller recognized not only one extraordinary sailor, but generations of enlisted servicemembers whose courage and contributions have too often gone unnoticed and unrecognized,” the members wrote.

“We urge you to reject this plan and ensure that CVN-81 bears the name USS Doris Miller, the members concluded. “Our Navy must continue honoring the courage of those that answered their country’s call to service.”

View the full text of the letter here and below:

Dear Secretary Hegseth and Acting Secretary Cao:

We write regarding the recent reporting that the Department of the Navy is considering renaming the USS Doris Miller potentially in honor of President Trump.1 Renaming this ship after a sitting President would be unprecedented and break longstanding tradition. Most importantly, this would diminish the recognition of one of our country’s greatest military heroes. It was during President Trump’s first term that the Navy announced CVN-81 would bear Doris Miller’s name. Reversing that decision now would be a significant step backward in honoring the courage and sacrifice of those who have served our country.

The future USS Doris Miller will be the first aircraft carrier to be named for an African American and the first named in honor of an enlisted sailor. Those distinctions reflect the bravery and courage during the attack on Pearl Harbor by Doris ‘Dorie’ Miller, who was later awarded the Navy Cross, the Navy’s second-highest honor.

On December 7, 1941, Miller was serving aboard the USS West Virginia when Japan’s attack began. At the time, Miller was a Mess Attendant Third Class, and after his station came under fire, despite lacking proper training, he took control of an anti-aircraft gun and fired at incoming aircraft. Even when the ship began to sink, it was only when he ran out of ammunition did he abandon his position. But in the process, he still managed to assist his fellow wounded sailors and help them reach safety. Doris Miller’s story is one of extraordinary bravery, service, and pure patriotism. When he served, segregation restricted the roles available to Black sailors and servicemembers. Yet, when his country came under attack, Miller did not hesitate for one second to put himself in harms’ way to defend his fellow sailors and his nation. This story embodies the finest traditions of the United States Armed Forces.

Black Americans have served in every major American conflict, often defending a country that did not provide or even recognize their equal rights while home. Their service and sacrifice are an integral part of our country’s military history. The decision to name CVN-81 for Doris Miller recognized not only one extraordinary sailor, but generations of enlisted servicemembers whose courage and contributions have too often gone unnoticed and unrecognized.

In 2020, then-Acting Secretary of the Navy Thomas Modly announced the decision to honor Doris Miller by placing his name on CVN-81, the newest and most powerful warship. It was Acting-Secretary Modly who said that the decision honored “the contributions of all our enlisted ranks, past and present, men and women, of every race, religion, and background.”

Our aircraft carriers are among the most visible symbols of American military power. They are stationed all over the world, projecting strength, protecting our national security, and reminding our allies that we will have their backs at their time of need. The names these ships carry should preserve the legacies of Americans whose service, sacrifice, and leadership represent the very best of our democracy and our Armed Services.

There is no question that Dorie Miller meets that standard. His story deserves to be remembered aboard one of the most powerful warships ever constructed. There has never been a time when we have named a warship after a sitting president. Changing course now to satisfy a sitting President’s ego, especially one who dodged military service to his country, would be shamefully wrong.

We urge you to reject this plan and ensure that CVN-81 bears the name USS Doris Miller. Our Navy must continue honoring the courage of those that answered their country’s call to service.

title: Rep. Takano Addresses 63rd Anniversary of March on Washington Rally: “America is an Idea Worth Fighting For.”
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Representative Mark Takano (CA-39) participated in the 63rd anniversary of the March on Washington alongside Minority Leader Representative Hakeem Jeffries (NY-8), Congressional Black Caucus Chairwoman Representative Yvette Clarke (NY-9), Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), and Senator Bernie Sanders (I-VT).

Leaders provided remarks at the steps of the Lincoln Memorial, then participated in a march to the Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial led by Reverend Al Sharpton.

Below are Rep. Taknao’s remarks as prepared:

“We are not here simply to remember history. We are here because the work that began 63 years ago is unfinished. We are here because the battles we thought had been long settled have resurfaced:

“Birthright citizenship is under attack. Americans feel the need to carry a passport to prove they belong. Fascists are using their power to intimidate Americans into silence.

“These are not echoes of some distant past. They are the reality of this moment.

“And this moment is an awakening: norms alone will not protect us.

“Every generation must take up the work of renewing and perfecting the idea of America so that America lives up to its promise. There are those who would have us believe America is about blood and soil. Replacing America’s founding principles with a narrow definition of who belongs and who does not. That being an American is about how many generations your family has lived here, where your parents were born, and what you look like.

“But that is not the America generations of people have struggled, marched, bled, and died for.

“And what is the idea of America?

“It is the idea that all of us are created equal. That government derives its power from the people. That every person deserves liberty and justice. And that being an American is not determined by your race, your religion, or where your parents came from, or who you love.

“The work of renewing and perfecting the idea of America does not happen on its own.

“People had to fight for it.

“John Lewis fought for that idea. At 23 years old he stood here in 1963 and demanded that America live up to it promise. Two years later, on the Edmund Pettus Bridge, police beat him for demanding the right to vote. He knew what awaited him on the other side of the bridge. Yet, he crossed it anyway.

“Because America was an idea worth fighting for.

“Wong Kim Ark fought for that idea. Born in San Francisco to immigrant parents, he challenged the government when it tried to deny him entry into his own country. In 1898, he took his fight to the Supreme Court—and won. If you are born here, you are an American. Period. More than a century later, we are fighting that battle again.

“Because America is an idea worth fighting for.

“And my own family fought for that idea. During World War II, my great-uncle Monzo served in the 442nd Regimental Combat Team. Fighting and bleeding alongside other segregated units like the Buffalo Soldiers and Tuskegee Airmen. He fought for the United States while my parents and grandparents were among more than 120,000 Japanese Americans incarcerated by their own government.

“Think about that contradiction. A country that questioned their loyalty and took away their freedom. And still, Japanese American soldiers fought and died for an America that had not yet lived up to its promise. The motto of the 442nd was simple: Go for Broke. Risk everything. Give everything. And they did.

“Today, we are being called to our own “Go for Broke” moment. To fight for the character of our country. We fight for an America where nobody feels that they have to carry a passport to prove they belong. We fight for an America where citizenship cannot be stripped away because of who your parents are. We must fight for an America where the government does not use fear and intimidation to silence its own people. And we must fight for an America where every eligible citizen can vote and have that vote counted.

“The people who gathered here 63 years ago understood something we cannot afford to forget: Progress is not permanent. Rights do not protect themselves. Democracy does not defend itself.

“Every generation inherits the idea of America—and then must decide whether it is willing to fight for it.

“My great-uncle Monzo made his choice. Wong Kim Ark made his choice. John Lewis made his choice. Dr. King made his choice. Now it is our turn!

“Because America does not belong to one political party. America does not belong to a bloodline. And it certainly doesn’t belong to one man.

“America belongs to all of us. Let’s Go For Broke. Go all in for democracy. Go all in for equality. Go all in for freedom. We cannot turn back. Let’s finish the assignment, make Dr. King’s dream a reality, and fulfill the promise of a better America.”

title: ICYMI: Public Knowledge Calls the FRONTIER Act “the best proposal (so far)” for Reining In Frontier AI
text:
In a new analysis, the consumer advocacy group Public Knowledge backed Congresswoman Lori Trahan (D-MA-03) and Congressman Jay Obernolte’s (R-CA-23) Frontier Risk Oversight, National Transparency, Independent Evaluation, and Reporting (FRONTIER) Act, calling it the strongest proposal yet to manage the risks of the most powerful AI systems.

“The frontier needs real rules, not voluntary guardrails. That requires binding legal regimes for evaluating and managing the risks from frontier models: as they are being developed, before they are deployed, and after they are in widespread use,” wrote Nicholas Garcia, Senior Policy Counsel at Public Knowledge. “The best proposal (so far) to move past frameworks, lists of principles, or nibbling at the edges of this challenge is the ‘Frontier Risk Oversight, National Transparency, Independent Evaluation, and Reporting (FRONTIER) Act’ from Representatives Jay Obernolte and Lori Trahan.”

“For years, Public Knowledge has been one of the most serious and principled voices fighting to protect the public from the risks posed by cutting edge technologies. When they engaged in the discussion draft process, we took their criticisms seriously and worked with them to address their concerns,” said Congresswoman Trahan. “That kind of rigorous, good-faith feedback is a big reason the FRONTIER Act is the strongest frontier AI safety legislation ever introduced. Public Knowledge’s support is critical as we work to broaden the coalition backing this bipartisan bill and push for its consideration. We’re in a race against the clock right now, and Congress needs to act before the next major incident.”

The FRONTIER Act would establish a tiered, risk-based national framework for overseeing the most advanced AI models. It requires the largest developers to publish their safety frameworks, submit to independent third-party audits and verification, and report critical safety incidents to a new Under Secretary of Commerce for AI Security. The bill is an updated version of the Commerce-focused portions of Trahan and Obernolte's Great American AI Act (GAAIA) discussion draft. The sponsors reworked it over seven weeks of stakeholder feedback, narrowing its preemption of state law and sharpening its auditing and reporting provisions.

Public Knowledge's endorsement marks a notable evolution. When the sponsors released the GAAIA discussion draft in June, Public Knowledge opposed it, warning that its preemption clause reached too far and would lock states out of even light-touch AI transparency and evaluation rules. At the same time, the group made clear it was ready to work with the sponsors to get the policy right.

Trahan and Obernolte took that feedback and rewrote the bill. When they introduced the FRONTIER Act in July, the preemption had been narrowed to cover only the catastrophic-risk issues the federal framework itself addresses, leaving state authority over child safety, privacy, consumer protection, and procurement intact. That change answered Public Knowledge's central concern, and the group now backs the bill.

Public Knowledge joins a broad, bipartisan coalition of AI policy experts and organizations that have praised the FRONTIER Act as the strongest federal AI safety proposal introduced to date.

title: Rep. Juan Vargas Statement on Piker Comments

WASHINGTON – Rep. Juan Vargas (D-CA-52) released the following statement on streamer Hasan Piker's recent comments suggesting that American Jews are inviting violence against themselves and warning that “eventually someone will come around and take action” against them.

title: Congressman Veasey Calls on DHS to Immediately Release Iranian Christian Pastor Granted Asylum as Health Deteriorates in Detention
text:
August 28, 2026

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Marc Veasey (TX-33) is calling on the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to expedite the release of Elmira Azizi, an Iranian Christian pastor currently detained at the Prairieland Detention Center in Alvarado, Texas, after she was granted asylum in the United States. Azizi fled Iran after facing persecution because of her Christian faith. According to her attorneys, she has now been granted asylum, has no criminal record, and remains in federal immigration custody while awaiting DHS to complete the process necessary for her release. Azizi suffers from a life-threatening medical condition which she was able to successfully manage prior to detention. During her detention, Azizi’s health has rapidly deteriorated, and her declining health has now left her reliant on a wheelchair. “Elmira came to this country seeking refuge from religious persecution, and the United States granted her asylum. She has no criminal record, and there is no reason for allowing bureaucratic delays to put her life at further risk,” said Congressman Veasey. “Elmira has been detained for months without real justification, all the while her health has been rapidly deteriorating. She is now in a wheelchair, and is still not receiving the necessary medical care. “DHS must act with the urgency her condition demands, complete the remaining process, and release Elmira so she can get the life-saving medical treatment she desperately needs.” Congressman Veasey’s office has previously raised concerns regarding conditions and access to information and services for individuals detained at the Prairieland Detention Center. After several reports of alarming conditions and poor treatment of detainees, Congressman Veasey conducted several oversight inspections and alerted DHS and ICE to the concerns.

title: Congressman Wittman Receives Grade “A” Bridge Grade

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Rob Wittman (VA-01) celebrated earning a Grade “A” rating from Bridge Grades. This award recognizes legislators who put people over party and embrace the spirit of bipartisanship and collaboration.

Serving Virginia’s First District means putting people above party politics and working with my colleagues to find common ground. I’ll continue working across the aisle to deliver results for Virginia and put the interests of my constituents first. Thank you to Bridge Grades for this recognition.”

Background:

Bridge Grades scores members of Congress on how collaboratively or divisively they govern compared to their peers.

They use non-partisan 3rd party data sources to sort legislative “bridgers” from “dividers”.

Bridgers build win-win consensus solutions through collaboration and coalitions for the benefit of cross-partisan interests

Dividers pursue zero-sum game governance, engage in personal attacks, and demonstrate predictably partisan legislative records

Their systems compile multiple trusted 3rd-party data sources into a blended 0-100 index (the “Bridge Score”). They use data that measures what a person does (legislative record: authoring and sponsoring cross-partisan bills) and what a person says (rhetoric: public statements, speeches, social media).

title: ICYMI: Baldwin Wraps Up First Week of “Ending Chaos, Lowering Costs” Statewide Tour
text:
WISCONSIN – Today, U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) wrapped up the first week of her “Ending Chaos, Lowering Costs” statewide tour with stops in Madison, Richland Center, La Crosse, Onalaska, and Eau Claire, meeting with Wisconsin families and small businesses and highlighting how she is fighting to end the high costs and hardship that Congressional Republicans and President Donald Trump have created.

In Madison, Senator Baldwin visited a local Boys & Girls Club to help pack donated school materials and meet with staff and stakeholders to hear how rising costs are hurting families this back-to-school season. Trump’s tariffs and war in Iran have increased back-to-school supplies’ costs for families, with nearly half of parents saying they are cutting back on other household expenses to make room for back-to-school shopping.

In Richland Center, Senator Baldwin stopped by Richland Hospital to learn how $4.5 million in direct federal support she secured is helping update this critical access hospital and medical center. The visit and Baldwin-backed support come as Republicans made historic cuts to the Medicaid program in their signature One, Big Beautiful Bill, which is poised to devastate rural hospitals and threaten the closure of critical access facilities for Wisconsin.

In La Crosse, Senator Baldwin visited with small businesses – including Oh Oh Coffee, Larson's General Store, and Kroner's Hardware – to discuss how President Trump’s trade war with our allies and his illegal war in Iran are driving up costs and squeezing Wisconsin Main Street shops and their consumers. A poll conducted by Small Business Majority in June found that 63% of small business owners reported decreased profit margins this year and 74% reported that they are being impacted by recent increases in fuel and transportation costs.

In Eau Claire, Senator Baldwin hosted a roundtable with local bar and restaurant owners to talk about how her new bill, the For the Fans Act, will save small businesses money and cut through the confusing landscape of watching televised sports. Her legislation would end blackouts and force leagues to provide a free viewing option for local fans. The bill comes as the Packers’ upcoming 2026-27 season schedule has four games on Amazon Prime and Netflix, forcing fans outside of the Milwaukee and Green Bay media markets to pay for games.

The tour comes as Senator Baldwin released a brand-new report earlier this week showing that, from the ongoing trade war, war in Iran, and chaos, Congressional Republicans and President Trump are costing Wisconsin families more than $3,300 for everyday essentials like housing, gas, and groceries.

Key findings from this report can be found below:

Wisconsin Families Spending $3,300+: As of June 2026, the average household in Wisconsin has had to spend more than $3,300 more on goods and services under President Trump, including $794 more on housing costs such as rent and mortgages, $310 more for groceries, and $120 more for electricity.

Back-to-School Essential Cost 20% More: As the cost of essentials like lunch boxes, notepad paper, index cards, and tissues has increased by 20% or more, nearly half of parents say they are cutting back on other household expenses to make room for back-to-school shopping. Additionally, packing lunches will cost families more than $3,800 this school year, up nearly $400 from last year.

Wisconsinites Spent $1 billion More on Gas: Wisconsinites have spent an estimated $1 billion more on gas. Nationwide, 75% of Americans believe that they have faced hardships due to the rising costs of gas.

Farmers Spend 73% More on Diesel: Wisconsin farmers spent $43,800,000 or 73.6% more, on diesel fuel during this year’s planting season than they did last year.

Next week, Senator Baldwin’s tour continues with stops in the Superior area, Wausau, Green Bay, and Monona.

Read the full report here.

title: Blackburn, Duckworth Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Counter Communist China’s ‘Gray-Zone’ Aggression Against Indo-Pacific Partners
text: NASHVILLE, Tenn. – U.S. Senators Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.) and Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.) introduced bipartisan legislation to improve our nation’s capabilities to counter the People’s Republic of China’s (PRC) intimidation and coercion tactics in the Indo-Pacific, which actively threaten the safety of our partners in the region as well as our national security. Known as ‘gray-zone tactics,’ these actions are aimed at disrupting regional stability while stopping just short of armed conflict—a dangerous strategy that sets the stage for even harsher intervention by the PRC in the future. The Senators’ bipartisan Countering Gray Zone Aggression by the People’s Republic of China Act would direct the State Department to enhance cooperation with our Indo-Pacific partners and better address the growing threat of PRC aggression in the region.

title: Senator Blumenthal: Week in Review 8/21/2026-8/28/2026
text:
Supporting Ukraine in its Fight Against Putin’s Invasion

[Hartford, CT] – U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), a member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, traveled to Ukraine as the country continues to fight in the war against Russia. Blumenthal’s trip included a visit to Dnipro, near the eastern front of the war—the furthest east a Congressional Delegation has gone since the invasion. Blumenthal is the first member of Congress to visit Dnipro since the war began in 2022.

“Eye opening, awe-inspiring—my visit to Dnipro, the first congressional trip permitted since the war’s start, showed me the best of humanity, with Ukrainians meeting the worst—Russia’s craven inhumanity. All I met—unspeakably injured soldiers, courageous caregivers, steadfast staffs—are demonstrating professional excellence under demanding conditions, with dedication & dignity,” wrote Blumenthal with an accompanying video on Twitter/X.

In Dnipro, Blumenthal visited a military hospital where we met seriously wounded soldiers and their caregivers.

“Heroes caring for heroes—at the military hospital in Dnipro, near the eastern front, I saw the courage & grit of seriously wounded soldiers & medical warriors helping them regain their lives. An awe-inspiring visit,” wrote Blumenthal with an accompanying video on Twitter/X.

While in Kyiv earlier this week, Blumenthal met with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and attended the National Prayer Breakfast on Ukraine’s Independence Day. He also toured SkyFall, a major Ukrainian defense technology company aiding the country in its fight against Russia.

“Another inspiring meeting with President Zelenskyy at a critical turning point in Ukraine’s fight for freedom, when they are turning the tide against Russia’s savagery & slaughter. They need air defense interceptors, the Russia sanctions bill, Starlink, & aid. I am more determined than ever to redouble our support because their fight is our fight, & our own national security is directly at stake,” wrote Blumenthal on Twitter/X.

“At today’s National Prayer Breakfast, I stated emphatically—we stand with the people of Ukraine in prayer & faith, but also in action. Their fight for freedom & democracy is our fight too,” wrote Blumenthal with an accompanying video on Twitter/X.

“A moving celebration in Kyiv for Ukraine’s Independence Day—a reminder that freedom is never free, & we must redouble our efforts to support this brave embattled nation against Putin’s murderous invasion,” wrote Blumenthal with an accompanying video on Twitter/X.

“SkyFall in Kyiv is doing cutting edge drone manufacturing & changing modern warfare. Its innovation & new technologies are powering Ukraine’s fight against Russia's bloody slaughter,” wrote Blumenthal with an accompanying video on Twitter/X.

Blumenthal also met with children and families affected by Russian kidnappings while in Kyiv.

“Young children & their families hideously victimized by Russian kidnapping & other atrocities are awesome in their resilience & grace. The world must match their courage,” wrote Blumenthal on Twitter/X.

Blumenthal also visited Babyn Yar, a site honoring Jewish people killed there in massacres carried out by Nazi forces in World War II, and Independence Square, located in the center of Kyiv with memorials to those who have died in the ongoing war against Russia.

“A moving, solemn tribute at Babyn Yar to the 33,000 Jewish people killed there during the Holocaust. In the face of inhumanity, no one can be neutral—we must stop Putin’s savagery & cruelty,” wrote Blumenthal with an accompanying video on Twitter/X.

“At Independence Square, Ukrainians are honoring the brave lives tragically lost in Putin’s war of inhumanity & aggression. We join them in their sorrow & redouble our support for their fight to stop Russia’s slaughter,” wrote Blumenthal with an accompanying video on Twitter/X.

Blumenthal concluded his trip with a visit to Bucha, a city located on the northern front of the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

“Returning to Bucha reminds me why we should all be so passionate about Ukraine winning this war— Russia's criminal inhumanity & killing, & the steadfast strength of Ukraine,” wrote Blumenthal with an accompanying video on Twitter/X.

Blumenthal joined MS NOW’s Morning Joe to recap his trip to Ukraine and highlight the need for continued U.S. support for Ukraine in its fight against Russia’s bloody invasion.

“I visited the military hospital near the border, and that military hospital shows the face of courage and strength that President Zelenskyy echoed in what he said to me. He needs three priorities: the Russia sanctions bill, air defense—because his people have been slaughtered by Putin’s missiles and drones that are attacking civilian targets, not military—and he needs Starlink to target even deeper within Russia,” said Blumenthal on Morning Joe. “I said to him I would take those three priorities—most especially the Russia sanctions bill, because it passed the Senate by an 86 to 11 vote, completely bipartisan, after painstaking negotiations over several years by Senator Graham and myself with the White House, the U.S. Trade Representative, colleagues in Congress, and we are now at the cusp of passing it in the House. And it will make such a difference, because Putin's economy is on the cusp of major crisis, and stopping the flow of revenue from sales of oil and gas, as this sanctions bill would do, can have a real impact in throttling Putin's ability to wage war.”

Condemning Increased ICE Activity in Danbury

Blumenthal released a statement following reports of increased Immigration and Customs Enforcement activity in Danbury over the last few days.

“ICE’s cruelty and craven brutality has no limit. Snatching people off the streets as they walk their children to school or wait for a ride to work — such tactics are abusive, abhorrent, and illegal. I am in touch with state and local authorities and am ready to assist in any way possible.”

Responding to Nearly $17 Billion Meta Settlement in Case About Social Media Harms to Kids

Blumenthal and U.S. Senator Marsha Blackburn (R-TN), authors of the Kids Online Safety Act (KOSA), released the following statement in response to a nearly $17 billion settlement reached between Meta and a coalition of bipartisan state Attorneys General:

“This massive settlement shows how terrified Meta and Mark Zuckerberg are of accountability in open court. We applaud the bipartisan coalition of state Attorneys General for forcing Meta to start paying a real price for the harm its products have caused an entire generation of young people. The product design changes imposed under this settlement are a first step toward giving kids and parents the tools they need to take back control of their online lives, but they can be strengthened. Meta notes that these terms are only required to stay in place for 10 years—we must ensure permanent change. We also need safeguards that apply across the board—to all social media companies—not just Instagram and Facebook. This settlement once again demands that Congress pass the Kids Online Safety Act into law before the end of the year.”

On Twitter/X, Blumenthal further highlighted the need for increased protections for kids online.

“Meta is guilty of harming kids—& now it’s starting to pay a real price. This landmark settlement, staggering in penalties & important changes, only heightened the urgency & need for the Kids Online Safety Act to become law now,” wrote Blumenthal on Twitter/X.

Demanding Answers About DHS’s $464 Million Purchase of Luxury Jets & Planes via a No-Bid Contract

Blumenthal, Ranking Member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, and U.S. Senators Peter Welch (D-VT), member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, and Adam Schiff (D-CA), member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, demanded answers from Secretary of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Markwayne Mullin, about DHS’s wasteful purchase of 10 airplanes for $464 million via a no-bid contract. In a letter to Mullin, the Senators called out the Department’s growing and alarming reliance on no-bid contracts since the beginning of the second Trump Administration and raised concerns that the owner of the company that received the award also runs a company alleged to have solicited kickback payments to former DHS official Corey Lewandowski.

“Recent reporting reveals that, beginning in the fall of 2025, DHS pursued and eventually awarded a no-bid contract to purchase 10 aircraft, including three ‘luxury business jets’ and seven ‘Boeing 737 passenger jets,’ and that most of these aircraft have sat idle for months since DHS acquired them. Although DHS claims that the contract was undertaken during Secretary Noem’s tenure, contracting records indicate that the cost of the contract ‘increased by $303 million on the day that Mr. Mullin was sworn in as secretary,’” the Senators wrote.

The Senators continued, “DHS purchased the aircraft through a $464 million no-bid contract to Daedalus Aviation Corporation (Daedalus), a Virginia-based company led by chairman William Walters…In fact, Mr. Walters has allegedly created ‘a web of companies,’ that subsequently received government contracts despite having no prior government contracting experience. Companies with ties to Mr. Walters include Salus Worldwide Solutions Corporation (Salus), which, in 2025, received a hastily-awarded contract worth $915 million ‘for air operations to support the administration’s effort to persuade millions of undocumented immigrants to ‘self-deport.’ Public reporting alleges that a representative of Salus repeatedly approached a prospective subcontracting firm with proposals to undertake work for DHS only if the firm would direct millions in kickbacks to Corey Lewandowski or consulting firms connected to him.”

“Congress and the American people deserve the Department’s full and prompt transparency with respect to the shocking waste of taxpayer funds and potential corruption involved in the Department’s aircraft purchase and widespread no-bid contracting,” the Senators concluded.

The full text of the letter is available here.

Blumenthal Bulletin

Blumenthal slammed the Department of Justice’s decision undercutting one of FDA’s strongest enforcement tools against unauthorized tobacco products.

Blumenthal called out the craven political trashing of Stars and Stripes after the Pentagon fired leaders from the publication who criticized the Department of Defense’s interference.

Blumenthal visited the groundbreaking of Electric Boat’s new Waterford campus.

Blumenthal called for an end to misleading and deceptive food packaging with his Food Labeling Modernization Act.

title: Booker Concludes 2026 Annual 21-County Tour
text:
NEW JERSEY — Today, U.S. Senator Cory Booker concluded his 2026 Annual 21-County Tour, underscoring his commitment to fighting — and delivering — for New Jersey’s priorities in the Senate. Since launching the tradition 13 years ago, Senator Booker’s tours have spotlighted new federal investments, advanced local priorities, and strengthened partnerships with organizations, businesses, and industries across all 21 counties.

“Every stop on this tour reminded me why I love this job,” said Senator Booker. “I met extraordinary people in every corner of our state who are caring for their neighbors, lifting up their communities, and showing what is possible when we come together. I end this tour with deep gratitude and even more Jersey pride. It is the honor of my life to represent New Jersey in Washington, and I’ll never stop fighting for the people of our state.”

Senator Booker concluded his tour with stops in Atlantic, Cape May, and Cumberland Counties, highlighting federal investments, local economic development, and support for New Jersey farmers.

In Atlantic County, Senator Booker visited the Orange Loop, an Opportunity Zone neighborhood, where he met with local business owners and entrepreneurs for a roundtable discussion and driving tour. He heard directly about their experiences and saw firsthand how his Opportunity Zone legislation has helped spur economic development, support small businesses, and create new opportunities in historically underserved communities.

Also in Atlantic County, Senator Booker toured the AtlantiCare Trauma Center and helipad and presented AtlantiCare Health System with a ceremonial check commemorating the $1 million FY26 Congressionally Directed Spending award he secured for the hospital. He met with hospital leadership and frontline staff to discuss the importance of this federal investment in strengthening emergency response capabilities. The funding will help ensure New Jersey families have access to high-quality care when they need it most.

In Cape May County, Senator Booker toured the Cape May–Lewes Ferry Terminal’s three-vessel fleet and celebrated a $30 million Federal Transit Administration award he helped secure for the Delaware River and Bay Authority to purchase a new diesel-hybrid ferry. The award builds on a previous $20 million award he secured in 2024. He also discussed the $9.6 million FTA award to the Borough of Carteret and NJ TRANSIT’s Carteret Ferry Service Expansion Project, highlighting how the 2021 Bipartisan Infrastructure Law is delivering investments that will strengthen New Jersey’s transportation infrastructure, tourism, and economic development.

"For over 60 years, the Cape May–Lewes Ferry has been a vital crossing connecting New Jersey and Delaware, which is a significant contributor to our regional economy,” said Joel Coppadge, Executive Director of the Delaware River and Bay Authority. “This grant award is critical toward our efforts to modernize our fleet with cleaner, more efficient hybrid technology for the next generation. Beyond the environmental benefits, this investment safeguards an essential engine that drives more than $250 million in annual tourism and economic activity to the region. We are incredibly thankful for Senator Booker’s dedicated advocacy on behalf of the DRBA and the thousands of travelers who depend on our crossing every day."

In Cumberland County, Senator Booker ended the day with a visit to Cedar Rose Vineyards, where he saw firsthand the crop damage caused by the April freeze and met with farmers who suffered significant crop losses. He also received a briefing on the freeze’s impact across the state and discussed his efforts to secure federal disaster relief for farmers.

Senator Booker’s 2026 Annual 21-County Tour included:

Announcing the Rory Ahern Act in Ocean County, legislation to expand NARCAN training for first responders, school personnel, and substance use treatment professionals and help prevent overdose deaths.

Highlighting more than $33.5 million in federal investments he helped secure for New Jersey, including $2 million for Inspira Health Network, $1 million for AtlantiCare, $559,000 for Liberty Science Center’s new mobile planetarium, and $30 million for a new diesel-hybrid ferry for the Cape May–Lewes Ferry.

Honoring New Jersey veterans across Bergen and Monmouth Counties, includingpresenting medals and certificates to 57 veterans and hosting a Veterans Town Hallto listen directly to veterans and their families and stand up for the services and support they have earned.

Supporting New Jersey families facing food insecurity, including visits to theFranklin Food Bank in Somerset County, the Greater Mount Zion Food Pantry in Trenton, and Cathedral Kitchen in Camden County.

Meeting with researchers, students, and workers at Hackensack Meridian Health’s Center for Discovery and Innovation, Salem Community College’s Glass Education Center, and L’Oréal Groupe’s North America Research and Innovation Center to highlight scientific innovation, STEM education, and workforce development.

Supporting New Jersey farmers and small businesses, including visits to theHunterdon County 4-H & Agricultural Fair, Wharton’s Canal Day festival, Atlantic City’s Orange Loop, and the South Jersey Chamber of Commerce, as well as meeting with Cumberland County farmers facing significant crop losses from the April freeze and discussing federal disaster relief.
