title: LOCAL SPOTLIGHT: Cassidy Highlights Story of Faith and Unity Ahead of Hurricane Katrina’s 21st Anniversary
text:
(Click here to download.)

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Bill Cassidy, M.D. (R-LA), for his monthly Local Spotlight, commemorated the twenty-first anniversary of Hurricane Katrina by highlighting a story of two New Orleans churches that came together to serve one another in the aftermath of the storm. The lasting partnership between Franklin Avenue Baptist Church and First Baptist New Orleans illustrates the deep sense of community that binds Louisianans together.

Read his full August 2026 Local Spotlight below:

This month’s local spotlight commemorates the 21st anniversary of Hurricane Katrina, which forever changed our state.

We know of the destroyed homes, families displaced, how it tested our communities in ways we could not otherwise imagine, had we not lived through it.

But in the midst of all that loss and destruction, something remarkable occurred.

People showed up for one another.

Neighbors became families.

Churches became places of refuge, which they always were, but even more so now.

And Louisianans from every background put aside differences to help a complete stranger who is now their neighbor.

One story from that time captures the true spirit of our state.

When Hurricane Katrina flooded the majority of the city of New Orleans, and by the way, that included Franklin Avenue Baptist Church, 10 feet of flood water.

So, when Franklin Avenue lost its place of worship, just a few miles away was First Avenue Baptist Church, which was spared from the floodwaters.

How?

So, years earlier when building a new campus, church leaders went near an old train yard, and they started driving down to build their property, and they ran into something hard.

They assumed it was a buried boxcar.

They could either excavate the whole property, and pull out the boxcar, which could have cost a lot of money, or they could put more dirt on top and build a higher foundation.

They took the least expensive option and it turned out to be the best option.

When Katrina floodwaters rose, because they had built up, those floodwaters rose to the church’s steps, but it never entered the building.

Whoever buried that boxcar triggered a series of events in which the Baptist church here could host the Baptist church there.

Now, Franklin Avenue, Pastor Fred Luter, he was determined to reunite his congregation.

So, he calls First Baptist New Orleans Pastor David Crosby to ask if his church would share a facility with Franklin Avenue.

And Pastor Crosby said yes, immediately.

Beginning the very next Sunday, Franklin Avenue held services at 7:30 every morning, and First Baptist was at 9:30.

And the act of generosity, of hospitality, has grown to a long-lasting bond between the two churches, that friendship now two decades old.

They continue to worship together, serve communities together, and gather annually for prayer services and exchange pulpits as a reminder that although they may be different backgrounds, there is a unity of faith.

Today, church leaders see that partnership as more than a response to a natural disaster.

They see it as a lasting testament to faith, unity, and the power of serving one another.

First Baptist has long used the story of elevating their church building, ultimately saving it from taking on Katrina floodwaters, as a reminder of another kind of foundation.

That building a life rooted in faith, provides the strength to withstand life’s greatest storms.

So, 21 years after Hurricane Katrina, the story of First Baptist and Franklin Avenue Baptist reminds us that Louisiana’s greatest strength is not simply perseverance, but the way we come together to lift one another up.

Background

In July, Cassidy highlighted LSU student William Grand who founded the Giving Greek organization, turning one simple observation into a community effort that has donated more than 10,000 meals to a local Baton Rouge homeless shelter. His leadership and commitment to serving others demonstrate how one person can make a meaningful difference in their community.

title: Senator Collins Participates in Christening and Launch of UMaine’s 3D-Printed Vessel
text:
Click HERE, HERE, and HERE for individual photos.

HAMPDEN, ME – Today, U.S. Senator Susan Collins delivered remarks at the christening and launch of 3Dirigo-X, a 30-foot, 3D-printed vessel designed and manufactured by the University of Maine’s Advanced Structures and Composites Center (ASCC). Senator Collins joined University of Maine President Joan Ferrini-Mundy, University of Maine System Chancellor Dannel Malloy, ASCC Executive Director Dr. Habib Dagher, and Keith DeVries, Director of the Department of Defense Manufacturing Technology (MANTECH) Program, for the event at Hampden Marina. Following her remarks, Senator Collins helped christen the vessel and observed an in-water demonstration.

3Dirigo-X is the first large 3D-printed vessel designed to operate at high speeds in the challenging environment of the Atlantic Ocean. Developed through a Department of Defense-funded Accelerated Rapid Prototyping (ARP) program, it is engineered to withstand the static, dynamic, impact, vibration, and hydrodynamic forces associated with operating at speeds approaching 40 knots. The vessel builds on the ASCC’s 2019 production of 3Dirigo, a 25-foot patrol boat that was printed in 72 hours and set Guinness World Records for the world’s largest 3D-printed boat and largest 3D-printed object.

“Today, we launch 3Dirigo-X, the first large 3D-printed vessel designed to operate at high speeds in the challenging environment of the Atlantic Ocean. 3Dirigo proved that a boat could be printed. 3Dirigo-X will demonstrate that a vessel produced by this technology can perform in the demanding conditions of the high seas,” said Senator Collins during her remarks. “This significant advancement is the result of the expertise of researchers at UMaine’s Advanced Structures and Composites Center. My first official visit as a new senator in 1997 was to Dr. Dagher’s wood composites lab. Ever since, I have been proud to support the pioneering work done here by securing funding to support and strengthen its advanced manufacturing capabilities.”

Senator Collins has supported the ASCC since the beginning of her Senate service, and her first official visit as a senator in 1997 was to Dr. Habib Dagher’s wood composites laboratory. In 2019, she helped establish a partnership between UMaine and Oak Ridge National Laboratory focused on large-scale 3D printing with forest materials and in the past five years alone, she has secured more than $115 million in federal appropriations to support the ASCC’s Factory of the Future. This includes $35 million in fiscal year 2022 appropriations legislation to support the construction and advanced manufacturing capabilities of the ASCC’s Factory of the Future, and an additional $33 million in fiscal year 2023 to expand the facility, including the addition of a second manufacturing bay.

In April 2024, the ASCC unveiled the world’s largest polymer 3D printer, which is four times larger than its previous record-setting printer. The printer allows UMaine to accelerate and expand its research into applications including shipbuilding, affordable housing, and bridge construction.

title: Senator Collins Visits Penquis Bright Beginnings Child Development Center

BANGOR, ME – Today, U.S. Senator Susan Collins visited Penquis Bright Beginnings Child Development Center in Bangor to join Penquis President and CEO Kara Hay, Head Start and Childcare Director Mary Kay Hallett for a guided tour of the facility.

The center opened in May 2025 and includes 16 classrooms for infants, toddlers, and preschool-age children. Once fully operational, the center will serve nearly 200 children through its Head Start, Early Head Start, and child care programs.

“Bright Beginnings is helping more children get a strong start in life while giving parents access to the reliable, high-quality child care they need,” said Senator Collins. “I have long been a strong supporter of Head Start, and as Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, I will continue working to protect and strengthen this vital program for children and families in Maine and across the country.”

Senator Collins has long supported federal investments in Head Start, which provides early childhood education, health, nutrition, and family support services to children from low-income families. As Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, Senator Collins helped increase funding for Head Start nationally to $12.4 billion in the Fiscal Year 2026 Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies appropriations bill.

title: Senator Collins Warns $170 Million of Maine Goods Would Be Hit by Tariffs in New Letter to Administration
text:
BANGOR, ME – Today, U.S. Senator Susan Collins wrote to U.S. Department of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and U.S. Trade Representative Jameison Greer urging them to resume negotiations with Canada and to reach a fair trade agreement to prevent damaging tariffs from taking effect in order to protect Maine workers, employers, and communities from unnecessary economic harm.

She also shared new details quantifying the damage to Maine businesses if the tariffs continue as planned.

“The new 50 percent tariffs imposed by the Administration on certain Canadian imports and the retaliatory tariffs announced by the Canadian government will lead to higher costs, risk, and uncertainty for Maine families, small and large businesses, and our communities,” Senator Collins wrote. “For Mainers, commerce with Canada is a regular occurrence. Maine borders only one state, but shares a 611-mile border with Canada. The consequences of Canada’s retaliatory tariffs are severe for Maine businesses, including our heritage industries.”

“Approximately $170 million worth of goods would be subject to the announced Canadian tariffs, with roughly 62 percent coming from the forest products sector. Nearly 90 percent of Maine is covered by forest. This economic sector supports approximately 30,000 jobs and contributes more than $8 billion to the state’s economy,” she continued. “Two of Maine’s paper mills, which are the largest employers in their towns, have already contacted me about the crushing increased costs that they will incur and the potential impact on their employment levels.”

“I appreciate that the Canadian government has revised its initial announcement and removed seafood and fish products, including lobster, from its plan. This would have resulted in more than $200 million in tariffs on Maine’s lobster industry, with impacts felt all throughout the supply chain,” she added. “The tariffs will also impose significant hardships on Maine communities. For example, Maine municipalities rely on road salt from Canada to keep roads safe from snow and ice in the winter. Frenchville, a very small town on the Canadian border, will have to pay $10,000 more for road salt as a result of the new tariffs.”

“Maine’s economy is uniquely intertwined with Canada, and the consequences of an escalating trade dispute will be felt by American families, businesses, workers, and communities across the state. Thousands of American jobs and businesses across a variety of sectors are at risk. I urge the Administration to work urgently toward a negotiated resolution with Canada that removes the recently implemented American tariffs and prevents the Canadian tariffs from taking effect,” Senator Collins concluded.

The complete text of the letter can be read here.

+++

Senator Collins has repeatedly opposed broad tariffs on Canadian goods and worked to protect Maine businesses and communities from their negative effects.

Earlier this month, following the proposed 50 percent tariffs on more than 500 categories of Canadian imports, she wrote to the Commerce Secretary and the U.S. Trade Representative urging the Administration to provide Maine businesses with greater clarity and notice regarding the tariffs and to consider their expected negative impact on Maine’s economy before any potential implementation. She also met with Canadian Ambassador Mark Wiseman to discuss the tariffs and the broader economic relationship between the U.S. and Canada.

In April 2025, she delivered remarks on the Senate floor in support of a resolution to end the emergency declaration being used to impose tariffs on Canadian goods; joined a bipartisan group in introducing the Trade Review Act of 2025, which would reassert Congress’ constitutional authority over tariffs; and urged the Administration to exempt previously contracted fire truck orders from tariffs on Canadian steel and aluminum that were expected to increase the cost of each truck by $80,000 to $90,000.

In July 2025, she joined a bipartisan group in introducing the Creating Access to Necessary American-Canadian Duty Adjustments (CANADA) Act, which would exempt U.S.-owned small businesses from tariffs on Canadian imports.

In December 2025, she requested targeted tariff relief for Maine’s wild blueberry producers, including an exemption for specialized Canadian equipment used to harvest, process, and mow the crop.

title: After Years of Federal Investment, Duckworth, Durbin Celebrate Grand Opening of Fully-Accessible Southern Illinois Multimodal Station
text:
[CARBONDALE, IL] – U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) and U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL) today joined Governor JB Pritzker, Carbondale Mayor Carolin Harvey, Illinois Secretary of Transportation Gina Biagi and local leaders to celebrate the opening of the new Southern Illinois Multimodal Station (SIMMS), a project the Senators helped secure more than $18 million in federal funding for and championed for years. The new station features fully accessible facilities, including ramps and improved platforms, to make public transportation safer and more accessible for all riders while strengthening connections across Southern Illinois. Photos from the ceremony can be found on Senator Duckworth’s website.

“When public transportation is accessible, everyone benefits,” Duckworth said. “Today’s grand opening shows what we can accomplish when federal, state and local governments work together. The Southern Illinois Multimodal Station will make it easier for people with disabilities, parents with strollers and all travelers to get where they need to go safely and confidently, while expanding opportunity across the region. Together, we’ll keep fighting for the federal investments our transit systems need to remove barriers and modernize aging infrastructure.”

“Senator Duckworth and I helped to secure $18.3 million in federal funding for the Southern Illinois Multimodal Station to better connect families, students, and small businesses to local and national destinations,” Durbin said. “This federal investment will be a tremendous boost to Carbondale and Southern Illinois, with SIMMS acting as both an economic hub for the city and a modern regional transportation center.”

Duckworth and Durbin helped secure a total of $18.3 million in federal funding for the Southern Illinois Multimodal Station and have been long-time champions of the project on the federal level. The new station will serve as a connection point for Amtrak passenger rail, Greyhound bus service, mass transit service, bicyclists, pedestrians and allows for safer, easier and more reliable travel throughout the region.

title: Duckworth, Durbin Hold Roundtable with Illinois Health Care Provides on the Impacts of the Trump Administration’s Cuts
text:
[MARION, IL] – U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) and U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL) today held a roundtable with Illinois health care providers, leaders and advocates to discuss the challenges they’re facing in providing care to rural communities as a direct result of the Trump Administration’s harmful health care cuts. Since being signed into law last July, President Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill made the largest health care cuts in history, destabilizing the health care system with more than $1 trillion in cuts from Medicaid and the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act. Photos from the roundtable can be found on Senator Duckworth’s website.

“For many Illinoisans in rural communities, health care was already too expensive and too hard to get—and then came the Medicaid cuts,” Duckworth said. “Slashing Medicaid has not only put reliable health care coverage at even more risk for hundreds of thousands of Illinoisans but also added even more pressure on rural hospitals already struggling to keep their doors open. The Administration’s cuts will only make it harder for families to get care close to home when mere minutes can be life-saving—or stop access altogether. Senator Durbin and I will keep fighting to protect Medicaid, support our rural health care services and make sure every Illinoisan can get the care they need when they need it, no matter their zip code.”

“Senator Duckworth and I sent letters to Illinois hospitals last year and asked them how the so-called One Big Beautiful Bill Act and its devastating Medicaid cuts would impact their hospital, health care workforce, and the patients they serve,” Durbin said. “The 129 responses we received made it clear that this legislation will mean shuttering of services, layoffs, and even hospital closures—meaning patients will needlessly suffer. If you look at the numbers, 24 rural hospitals are at risk of closure in Illinois. I think we ought to make a commitment to rural hospitals and families struggling with the cost-of-living instead of slashing federal funding for health care in order to fund tax cuts for billionaires.”

The consequences of these policies will continue to be felt across our state, with an estimated 400,000 Illinoisans expected to lose health coverage by 2034. Illinois nursing homes and hospitals, primarily in rural areas, are at risk of closing and Medicaid cuts are predicted to result in more than 27,000 jobs cut across the state.

Yesterday, Duckworth hosted a women’s health care roundtable with local reproductive health clinics, obstetrics providers, federally qualified health centers and health departments to hear about the difficulties of providing reproductive and maternal care in rural Southern Illinois, where Carbondale has become a safe haven for women seeking care from across the region and surrounding states, and the impact of Trump Administration policies on access to care. Photos from the women’s health care roundtable can be found on Senator Duckworth’s website.

title: Duckworth Visits Southern Illinois Nursing School Expansion Made Possible by Federal Investment She Secured
text:
[CARTERVILLE, IL] – U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) today visited John A. Logan College (JALC) to see firsthand how the $1.2 million federal investment she successfully secured is expanding the school’s nursing program, building new classrooms, purchasing equipment and helping prepare students for careers in health and nursing. During the visit, Duckworth stressed the importance of programs like these in addressing the shortage of rural health care workers in Illinois and across the country—a crisis that’s being exacerbated by Trump and Republicans’ health care cuts. Photos from today’s visit are available on Senator Duckworth’s website.

“Rural Illinoisans were already dealing with extreme barriers to care, between a shortage of health care professionals and too many having to travel hours to the nearest hospital when mere minutes can mean life or death in an emergency. Now in the wake of Trump’s Medicaid cuts, those already-distant hospitals face the threat of losing key resources and being shuttered altogether,” said Duckworth. “This is a crisis our rural communities cannot afford to get worse. To help address these challenges, we must plan for the long-term and invest in training the next generation of health care professionals. After years of pushing for federal funding for this project, I’m proud to see this investment help us do just that.”

Duckworth long pushed for funding to expand rural health care access and support postsecondary programs across Illinois. Earlier this year, Duckworth’s bipartisan Improving Access to Care for Rural Veterans Act passed committee, which would make it easier for Veterans who live in rural areas to access the health care they’ve earned.

John A. Logan College is a public community college in Carterville, Illinois. The JALC Nursing Program offers three stand-alone nursing programs: Certified Nurse Assistant (CNA), Practical Nursing (PN) and Associate Degree Nursing (ADN).

title: Gallego, Kelly Statement on Trump Administration Lawsuit Targeting Arizona Dreamers
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senators Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) and Mark Kelly (D-AZ) released the following statement after the Trump administration sued Arizona over its policy allowing eligible Dreamers and other immigrant students who attended and graduated from Arizona high schools to qualify for in-state tuition.

“Dreamers are Americans in every way. They grew up here, went to our schools, and are contributing to communities across Arizona. They deserve the opportunity to get an education and build a future in the only country many of them have ever called home.

title: Gallego Leads Colleagues in Opposing Israeli Government’s E1 Settlement Tenders
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), led Senators Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Chris Coons (D-DE), Brian Schatz (D-HI), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Patty Murray (D-WA), Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Dick Durbin (D-IL), Jack Reed (D-RI), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Mark Warner (D-VA), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Ed Markey (D-MA), Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Gary Peters (D-MI), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Peter Welch (D-VT), Ben Ray Luján (D-NM), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE), Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), and Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD) in a joint statement opposing the Israeli government’s decision to issue tenders for the construction of 1,234 housing units in the E1 settlement project, following a joint effort with 45 Senators urging Prime Minister Netanyahu to immediately crack down on settler violence and settler expansion in the West Bank.

“Construction in the E1 area would sever East Jerusalem from major Palestinian population centers and make a viable contiguous Palestinian state under a two-state solution far harder to achieve. For decades, Republican and Democratic administrations have recognized that development in E1 would seriously jeopardize the prospects for a Palestinian state. That concern remains just as urgent today.

“At a time when settler violence — including violence against Palestinian Americans — is reaching unprecedented levels in the West Bank and severe restrictions continue to constrain Palestinian movement and the Palestinian economy, moving forward with construction in E1 risks further destabilizing the West Bank and making a negotiated resolution even more difficult.

“We urge the Israeli government to immediately rescind these tenders, halt settlement expansion in the West Bank, and take urgent action to rein in settler violence. Without a change in course, Israel risks weakening its international standing and undermining its prospects for long-term security. We also urge the Trump administration to make full use of its existing authorities, including targeted sanctions on individuals and entities.

“The United States must remain committed to a two-state solution that delivers lasting peace and security for both the Jewish, democratic State of Israel and for a future Palestinian state. Construction in E1 would take us further away from that goal.”

title: Gillibrand Statement On Disastrous Iran War Hitting 6 Months
text:
Today, Trump and Republicans’ war in Iran has now reached six-months. Over and over again, the American people have heard an endless parade of broken and shifting promises about the war from the president. We were told the war was a “total and complete victory,” “won’t be difficult,” was “projected [to last] four to five weeks”, was “winding down,” was ending “very soon,” was “ahead of schedule,” was going to end in “two or three weeks,” then “two to three days,” then “very close,” then again a “few days,” then “going to end really soon.” None of this has been true.

The war has cost tens of billions of taxpayer dollars, wounded hundreds and killed 18 American servicemembers, depleted our stockpile of long-range missiles, and cost New Yorkers billions at the gas pump.

Below is a statement on this anniversary from Senator Kirsten Gillibrand:

“Today marks six months since Donald Trump launched his disastrous war with Iran that congressional Republicans have fully supported.

“We were told this president and Republicans would bring peace and lower prices. Instead, they’ve wasted billions on war while leaving working families behind.

“This war was launched without a clear plan, executed without a coherent strategy, and has become a costly, self-inflicted disaster. Every justification we were given for this conflict has proven hollow.

“Our service members did not volunteer to be pawns in a chaotic, unauthorized war with no plan and no end in sight. Tragically, many have been wounded or lost their lives in this needless war.

“And here at home, New Yorkers have paid the price for this war as well– at the grocery store and the gas pump. This administration has unlimited money for bombs, ballrooms, and billionaires – but nothing for the American people: for their healthcare, their food, their housing, and for their lives.

“New Yorkers—and all Americans—deserve better. I pray for our troops and for the end to this war.”

title: In Buffalo And Troy: Gillibrand Continues Statewide Tour Addressing The Rising Cost Of Groceries, Lagging Consumer Confidence
text:
Today, standing alongside Upstate New York leaders and advocates in Buffalo and Troy, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand continued her statewide tour addressing the crushing impact of rising grocery and household goods prices on working families. The push follows a recent Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index report showing headline inflation surged to 4.2%, the sharpest 12-month increase since April 2023.

In Buffalo, Senator Gillibrand visited FeedMore WNY, an organization that provides food and skills training to Western New Yorkers in need. In Troy, Senator Gillibrand stood at Bargain Grocery, which offers fresh food at discounted prices, expanding food access and avoiding food waste.

“Donald Trump promised to tackle rising costs, but instead he has made life unaffordable for New Yorkers,” said Senator Gillibrand. “While Trump has poured billions of dollars into a forever war, New Yorkers cannot afford basic necessities as prices on groceries, gas, and essentials have skyrocketed here at home. I will continue to demand accountability and fight for all Americans being crushed by these unsustainable costs.”

“FeedMore WNY is proud to serve our neighbors and help keep our community nourished and thriving,”said Collin Bishop, Vice President of External Affairs for FeedMore WNY. “This includes our distributions and partnerships through our food bank distribution network, our home-delivered meal services supporting our older adults and homebound neighbors, and the fresh, affordable produce we offer through our Farm Market. However, high grocery prices combined with cuts and changes to SNAP have increased the strain on our community members, as well as the emergency food programs that are already operating at or beyond capacity. Access to affordable, nutritious food is a key element in the fight against hunger and maintaining safe, healthy, and robust communities throughout Western New York.”

“It is no secret that families are struggling here in New York, and I hear the same concerns from my colleagues on both sides of the aisle across the country,” said Assemblymember John T. McDonald III, RPh. “Federal policies, from tariffs to war continue to drive up the cost of everyday necessities like food and fuel. As one of the few health care professionals in the Legislature, I know firsthand how important access to healthy food is in preventing and managing conditions like hypertension and diabetes. But with rising grocery costs and changes to SNAP enacted by HR1, it is becoming increasingly difficult for families to afford nutritious food. We can and must do better. Every family should be able to afford healthy food and put a nutritious meal on the table.”

The spike in costs is hitting New Yorkers directly at the checkout counter, with the prices of staple items like fruits and vegetables climbing 6.1%, and nonalcoholic beverages up 5.8%. With average wage growth lagging significantly behind, working families are experiencing a severe gap in purchasing power, driving consumer confidence down as basic monthly expenses outpace paychecks.

Gillibrand blamed the rising costs directly on Trump’s ongoing war in Iran. She reiterated her commitment to curbing military actions abroad to shift the focus back to Americans struggling at home.

title: In Syracuse: Gillibrand Celebrates Pride And New Americans Day At The Great New York State Fair
text:
Today, U.S. Senator Kirsten E. Gillibrand visited the Great New York State Fair, where she gaggled with reporters and joined fairgoers to celebrate the two official themes of the day: Pride and New Americans Day. title: Grassley Completes 46th Annual 99 County Meetings
text:
LINN COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) concluded his 46th annual 99 county meetings across Iowa with a question-and-answer session with employees at Sub-Zero in Cedar Rapids. Earlier in the day, Grassley held a meeting with factory workers in Monticello. Grassley takes questions on any subject, and Iowans set the agenda.

“Meeting with Iowans face-to-face gives me the chance to meet with a cross section of people, which informs my work in Washington. Representative government is a two-way street, and having dialogue with constituents is what guides my policy priorities. Even though I’d like to, I can’t meet face-to-face with all three million Iowans. So, I always encourage people to get in touch with me by writing a letter, sending an email, or by calling or stopping by one of my offices,” Grassley said.

“My work to reach across the aisle in Washington, pass a five-year Farm Bill, make life more affordable for families and promote transparency and accountability in government are based on input I hear from my constituents in Iowa,” Grassley continued. “I look forward to many more question-and-answer sessions yet this year.”

Iowans who attended this year’s meetings raised comments on a variety of issues including pharmaceutical benefit managers, Social Security, foreign policy, election integrity, rural healthcare and the Farm Bill. They also shared support for bipartisanship in Washington, year-round E15 and the Working Families Tax Cuts Act.

For a full list of Grassley’s county meetings this year, visit his website. To view his photos and posts from the meetings, search #99CountyMeetings on X and Instagram. Grassley also posts meeting recaps on Facebook.

Background:

Grassley has held his annual county meetings since 1981, when he was first elected to the U.S. Senate. For the past 46 years, he has held at least one question-and-answer session in each of Iowa’s 99 counties every year and invites local media to attend his meetings and ask questions.

Grassley’s 99 county meetings consist of town halls, meetings with small businesses, farmers, students, healthcare professionals, factory workers, service clubs and more. Through this process, he hears from a wide range of Iowans, including those who are unable to take time off from work to attend his town meetings. Grassley’s tireless efforts to meet Iowans where they work, study and live continues to set the standard for representative government.

title: Grassley Joins Iowa Law Enforcement Officers for Roundtable Discussion
text:
BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) joined local and tribal law enforcement leaders from Poweshiek, Jasper, Iowa and Tama counties yesterday for a roundtable discussion in Toledo as part of Grassley’s 99 county meetings. The group discussed community mental health resources, federal public safety investments, no tax on overtime and more.

“Iowa’s brave law enforcement officers put their lives on the line to protect our communities. All Iowans, including myself, owe them a great debt of gratitude,” Grassley said. “I was honored to meet with local law enforcement leaders yesterday to discuss their successes, learn about challenges in their communities and answer their questions. I look forward to bringing these insights back to the policymaking tables in Washington.”

Download photos HERE.

Supporting law enforcement is one of Grassley’s top priorities as chairman of the Senate Judiciary Committee. This Congress, Grassley has advanced several bipartisan bills to back the blue, including legislation to improve officers’ access to mental health resources, speed up critical benefits determinations and stem the flow of contraband in federal prisons. He also spearheaded large sections of Republicans’ Working Family Tax Cuts, which eliminated tax on overtime and provided major investments for local law enforcement.

In Iowa specifically, Grassley has worked alongside community leaders and the U.S. Department of Justice to secure over $37.5 million in federal funds this Congress for the state’s law enforcement and public safety initiatives.

Background:

This is Grassley’s 46th straight year holding Q&As in each of Iowa’s 99 counties. Grassley has held at least one question-and-answer session in every county, every year since he was first elected to serve in the U.S. Senate. He takes questions on any subject; Iowans set the agenda.

Links to Grassley’s social media posts from this meeting can be found HERE and HERE. Follow along using #99countymeetings.

title: Grassley Welcomes Grant to Expand Iowa Veterans Cemetery
text:
BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) welcomed an announcement that the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) National Cemetery Administration (NCA) has awarded $1,358,525 in grant funding to the state of Iowa to expand the Iowa Veterans Cemetery in rural Dallas County.

The grant will fund 2,160 columbarium niches and landscaping. Grassley attended the cemetery’s dedication on July 3, 2008.

“We owe a deep debt of gratitude to our veterans, who sacrificed so much to protect our freedoms and liberties. The Iowa Veterans Cemetery provides a peaceful and meaningful resting place for those who have served our country in uniform. This new funding will ensure the cemetery can continue its mission to honor these heroes and their families,” Grassley said.

Background:

Since 1980, the VA Veterans Cemetery Grants Program has awarded 525 grants totaling over $1.187 billion to establish, expand, improve, operate or maintain 125 veterans cemeteries.

In 2025, VA grant-funded cemeteries interred 44,705 veterans and eligible family members, which is approximately 25% of the total annual interments in all national, state, tribal and territory cemeteries (174,398).

title: Q&A: Tax Law Boosts Workforce and Small Business
text:
Q: What is the Workforce Pell Grant?

A: It’s back to school season for families, students and teachers across the state. As students return to the classroom, schedules are filling up with homework and extracurricular activities and parents are off to the races juggling jobs, car pools and meal times. Many students are starting a new chapter with post-secondary education, including four-year colleges, community colleges and vocational programs. Studies show advanced training leads to job readiness, higher earnings and more opportunities.

However, too many students are pushed into burdensome debt seeking a four-year degree that doesn’t fit job market demands. For example, skilled trades are in growing demand and largely protected from artificial intelligence (AI) because the work can’t be replaced by automation. That’s where smart policymaking can help solve problems. I co-sponsored legislation to expand access to high-quality, short-term job training programs to help close the skills gap that I hear from employers at my annual 99 county meetings. During work on last year’s tax bill, I pushed successfully to include my bill called Promoting Employment and Lifelong Learning (PELL) Act in the final package. It amends the Higher Education Act of 1965 to provide for Workforce Pell Grants that allow eligible students to use Pell Grants for short-term, accredited programs that provide workforce-focused credentials that meet employer needs.

I’m pleased Iowa is the very first recipient of the nation’s first Workforce Pell Grant program. Eligible students at Iowa Central Community College in Fort Dodge can use federal Pell Grant dollars to enroll in its Emergency Medical Technician Program. The 14-week program prepares students for public safety jobs that will fill a critical need in local communities across the state. These students will start their jobs with little to no debt and have the training credentials to launch good careers, provide for their families and serve their neighbors.

Q: What are you hearing from small businesses at your county meetings?

A: No matter the size of the community, small businesses make up the lion’s share of employers across Iowa, and support nearly half the workforce. During my annual 99 county meetings, I regularly hold Q&As at small businesses, factories and manufacturing facilities so that I can hear directly from the workers and small business owners who can’t take time off to come to an open town meeting. I want to hear about challenges they face and learn what’s on their minds. From decades-old family-owned businesses to start-up businesses opening their doors, I’m always impressed with the entrepreneurism and hard work that Iowa workers and employers put in each and every day to climb America’s ladder of prosperity and serve their communities. I’ve also come to the conclusion that Iowans don’t brag enough about their high-quality products and services, so I’m particularly glad to get a first-hand look at these businesses. Iowans set a high benchmark for a strong work ethic and it shows with workforce productivity and state-of-the-art manufacturing and technology.

title: Hawley Op-Ed: Why I Am Investigating Flock
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Senator Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) penned an op-ed in The Daily Wire following the announcement of his investigation into companies like Flock, with its network of 120,000 AI-powered cameras across the United States. Senator Hawley raises concerns about how Flock’s collection of citizens’ data and personal information poses privacy threats and potentially violates existing laws.

Read the full op-ed here or below.

Every month, AI-powered cameras take 20 billion snapshots of cars in America. In almost every case, these photos capture drivers who did nothing wrong. These are regular folks on their way to work, picking up kids at school, or driving to church. Now, they are understandably asking what happens to the data captured by a network of more than 120,000 of these Flock cameras nationwide.

Even though this is new technology, it raises an issue older than our country itself. In 1761, a Boston lawyer named James Otis went to court to fight against something called writs of assistance, which gave customs officers virtually unlimited authority to search anywhere for smuggled goods. After the colonial court did not stop the writs, John Adams said American independence was born “then and there.” Otis never argued against law enforcement or the need for searches. He objected to open-ended authority without any limiting rules.

Today, Congress has not written any rules governing the data captured by national AI camera networks built by Flock Safety and similar companies. It may be governed by older statutes, and should have Fourth Amendment limits, but those are unsettled questions. For now, for practical purposes, the only privacy protections for hundreds of millions of Americans are those found in one company’s internal policies. I don’t know if Flock has broken the law, but I do know that technology is moving faster than Congress is keeping up. So I have opened an investigation in the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism, which I chair, into how this data is collected, retained, searched, and sold.

I heard about this issue in my home state of Missouri. The St. Charles County Police Department canceled its Flock contract this month, after an audit found a civilian employee running searches for personal reasons. Sadly, my state is not alone. In Milwaukee, prosecutors charged an officer with searching his girlfriend’s plate 124 times and her former boyfriend’s plate 55 times, typing the word “investigation” in the software’s justification field each time. Worse still, the system’s audit didn’t catch him; a private citizen did, after looking up his plate on a public website.

Adding insult to injury, the systems make mistakes. A Florida woman spent 13 days in jail on eight felony counts, three for vehicular homicide, after investigators searched Flock’s network for a vehicle description and arrested the owner. The prosecutors later dropped the charges because they had the wrong person. Los Angeles dropped its Flock contract after an audit found officers had stopped 161 drivers wrongly flagged as driving stolen cars. Another California police department found that 71 percent of its alerts were wrong.

Then we consider what happens to records generated by these cameras. Flock boasts an $8.3 billion valuation, which brings commercial pressures. Americans deserve to know whether and how their driving data is licensed, sold, and used. There are also concerns about whether data is sent or stored abroad. For example, reporters have described Flock using gig workers in the Philippines to classify data captured by cameras. Powerful AI models also automate parts of the process, supercharging these concerns.

All that said, I want police to have the tools they need. Cameras can help recover stolen cars, find missing children, and catch fleeing criminals. But people are concerned when private companies build unprecedented databases of personal information and want reasonable safeguards for that data. And the Supreme Court has found that people have a reasonable expectation of privacy against a “comprehensive” record of where they’ve been. Americans do not surrender all their privacy rights every time they leave the house.

So I have posed common-sense questions to Flock about how long it keeps data, who controls it, who can search it, what protections are in place, and who, if anyone, is buying what the cameras see.

I hope the company will commit to resolving these questions. But even if it does, Congress should not just take its word at face value; we should write protections into law. These safeguards must apply to every company and endure longer than the tenure of current CEOs. More fundamentally, the rules protecting Americans should be set by law and by the people, not by venture capital funds, AI executives, or big tech companies.

title: Heinrich, Colleagues Urge BLM to Stop Rollback of Waste Prevention Rule
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, joined U.S. Senator Michael Bennet (D-Colo.), and U.S. Representative Jared Huffman (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the U.S. House Natural Resources Committee, in opposing BLM’s proposal to overturn the 2024 Waste Prevention, Production Subject to Royalties, and Resource Conservation rule (the 2024 Waste Prevention Rule).

The BLM’s reversal of this commonsense rule will increase pollution on public lands, reduce domestic energy supply, expose nearby communities to avoidable health risks, and waste publicly owned natural gas, costing Americans tens of millions in foregone revenue.

“Reversing these common-sense standards will waste publicly owned natural gas, cost the American people tens of millions in foregone revenue, and increase pollution on our public lands,” the lawmakers wrote.

“We strongly urge BLM to reject this proposed rescission and maintain the 2024 Waste Prevention rule. The oil and gas resources on these lands belong to the American public and Tribal nations, and they deserve to benefit from the full value and benefits of responsible resource stewardship,” the lawmakers continued.

Read the full text of the letter HERE and below.

Dear Secretary Burgum and Director Pearce,

We write to express our strong opposition to the Bureau of Land Management’s (BLM) proposed rule to overturn the 2024 Waste Prevention, Production Subject to Royalties, and Resource Conservation rule (the “2024 Waste Prevention Rule”). Reversing these common-sense standards will waste publicly owned natural gas, cost the American people tens of millions in foregone revenue, and increase pollution on our public lands.

Between 2012 and 2021, operators lost an estimated 300 billion cubic feet of natural gas on federal lands to flaring and venting, valued at nearly $950 million, and resulting in a loss of between $76 and $135 million in potential taxpayer revenue. Routine venting and flaring of natural gas is unnecessary and harmful, turning natural gas into a waste product instead of a valuable energy commodity.

In addition to creating this financial loss, rolling back the 2024 Waste Prevention Rule would reduce our domestic energy supply and expose nearby communities to avoidable health risks. Methane is a greenhouse gas over 20 times as powerful as carbon dioxide. In addition to methane, the primary component of natural gas, venting and flaring releases volatile organic compounds that are carcinogenic, increase ground-level ozone, and lead directly to illness for both individuals and communities exposed.

Many states across the country have already demonstrated that limiting venting and flaring is compatible with robust energy production. Colorado adopted regulations in 2020 and New Mexico in 2021 that ended almost all venting and flaring. In addition, many major oil and gas producers have voluntarily agreed to avoid routine flaring on new wells by 2030. Furthermore, cost-effective technologies to detect and reduce methane waste, such as satellite monitoring, drones, and infrared cameras, are widely used across the oil and gas industry. Reversing the 2024 Waste Prevention Rule would prolong years of regulatory uncertainty, penalizing proactive operators that have invested in efficient operations while rewarding those that have not.

We strongly urge BLM to reject this proposed rescission and maintain the 2024 Waste Prevention rule. The oil and gas resources on these lands belong to the American public and Tribal nations, and they deserve to benefit from the full value and benefits of responsible resource stewardship.

Sincerely,

title: Heinrich Visits Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness, Meets with Local Nonprofits, Advocates, and Tribal Leaders, Vows to Continue to Fight to Protect Public Lands
text:
PHOTOS HERE

ELY, MINN. — Last week, U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, visited gateway communities to the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness (BWCAW), where he met with local advocates, volunteers, non-profit leaders, and the Three Chippewa Bands, on how Senate Republicans and President Trump’s plan to allow sulfide-ore copper mining near the BWCAW will open up the pristine wilderness to permanent pollution, harming Tribes, local communities, and businesses in the area. Heinrich saw the proposed mining sites firsthand and observed how the mining pollution would affect the community and the watershed.

Heinrich’s visit comes as Minnesota Governor Tim Walz announced that his administration is taking steps to constrain future sulfide-ore copper mining development in the Rainy River Headwaters, slowing Twin Metals’ path forward to mine near the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness.

“I come from a mining family. I'm not against every mine everywhere. My dad worked for Anaconda Copper, and my grandfather was a gold miner. But I learned, negotiating with big companies over natural resource damages, that there are smart places to put mines — and there are places where they really don't belong. And you don't know which is which unless you get out on the landscape and see it. I think it's really hard to look at maps and listen to rhetoric in Washington, D.C., and make a good decision,” said Heinrich.

Heinrich continued, “To put a mine where we went this week just seems insane to me. It would put at risk one of the last great wilderness areas in North America — not just the Boundary Waters, but the Boundary Waters, Quetico and Voyageurs. This is one of those last great landscapes in North America. I don't think these battles are ever won in one fell swoop. It takes decades. But I can tell from the passion of people on the ground, the polling I’m seeing in Minnesota, and the elected leaders who have stepped up and staked out a position that this is on a trajectory where I believe that the watershed is going to be protected. I want to say, from the bottom of my heart, as somebody who truly believes in the value and the importance of public lands and wilderness: thank you all for protecting this very special place.”

In April, President Trump signed into law H. J. Res 140, rolling back protections for the watershed, allowing for mining and mineral extraction in the headwaters of the wilderness area.

Heinrich has consistently pushed to protect the Boundary Waters from mining. In February, Heinrich called on Americans to use their voices and oppose H.J. Res. 140. In April, Heinrich delivered remarks on the Senate floor, urging his colleagues to oppose H.J. 140. When the resolution passed the Senate, Heinrich delivered remarks, blasting his colleagues for gutting protections for the Boundary Waters.

In his April remarks, Heinrich emphasized that the Boundary Waters are not simply a Minnesota issue, but an issue for the entire country, calling the area part of our “shared inheritance.” He also argued that there are many places where mining can be done responsibly, but that the Boundary Waters is not one of them.

Heinrich began his trip with a boat tour through Birch Lake and the proposed Twin Metals mining sites, where he spoke with staff from Voyageur Outward Bound School (VOBS), a nonprofit outdoor education organization that has been operating adjacent to the proposed sulfide-ore copper site since 1964, underscoring how mining in the area will adversely impact its operations.

U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, speaks to local nonprofit staff on how mining in the Boundary Waters will impact their operations, Wednesday, August 19, 2026.

Additionally, Heinrich toured YMCA Camp Widjiwagan, which provides wilderness experiences for youth, and met with the camp’s Executive Director, Ben Hoffman, to discuss the camp’s history and the extensive outdoor education opportunities that rely on the Boundary Waters.

U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, tours YMCA Camp Widjiwagan and speaks with camp Executive Director Ben Hoffman, Wednesday, August 19, 2026.

Next, Heinrich met with Tribal officials from the Three Chippewa Bands to discuss how mining in the Boundary Waters will threaten their treaty rights to hunt, fish, and gather in their ancestral homeland.

U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, meets with the Three Chippewa Bands about how mining in the Boundary Waters threatens Tribes and their ancestral homeland, Wednesday, August 19, 2026.

Following his meeting with Tribal leaders, Heinrich spoke at a dinner at Ely Folk School, a community center that provides learning experiences that celebrate the heritage, art, history, and culture of northern Minnesota, and thanked advocates for fighting to protect the Boundary Waters.

U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, speaks at dinner, thanking advocates for fighting to protect Boundary Waters, Wednesday, August 19, 2026.

After his visits on Wednesday, the Senator launched into the Boundary Waters from Snowbank Lake to Ima Lake, spending the next two days exploring the local ecosystem, hunting and fishing culture, and native history before paddling to Ensign Lake on Saturday.

title: Heinrich Visits Frijoles Fire Command Center, Meets with Firefighters and Incident Commanders
text:
PHOTOS and VIDEOS

SANTA FE, N.M. — This week, U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, visited the Frijoles Fire Command Center to receive a briefing on the operations and status of the fire and meet with Incident Commanders, firefighters, first responders, and support staff working to contain the blaze. The Frijoles Fire has burned 15,333 acres and is 59% contained, with 803 personnel currently engaged in the firefighting effort.

“I’m grateful to the firefighters, Incident Commanders, and support and medical crews who are working around the clock to protect New Mexico communities from the Frijoles Fire,” said Heinrich. “I also want to extend my deepest condolences to the family of Randy Lupe, who tragically lost his life supporting the response. Everyone who responds to wildfires puts themselves in harm’s way to keep our communities safe, and we have a responsibility to make sure they have the resources, equipment, and support they need to do their jobs safely and effectively.”

U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, meets with firefighters and emergency responders at the Frijoles Fire Incident Command Center, August 27, 2026.

During the visit, Heinrich received a briefing from the Southwest Complex Incident Management Team 4, which is managing the firefighting operations, and met with crews and support staff.

BACKGROUND:

Heinrich has led efforts to strengthen the nation’s wildland firefighting workforce, improve wildfire preparedness and response, and ensure New Mexico communities have the federal resources they need in wildfire emergencies.

Last month, Heinrich sent a letter urging the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to ensure that communities in New Mexico and nationwide receive the federal resources they need to respond to and prevent wildfires, including by promptly approving and distributing Fire Management Assistance Grant and post-fire mitigation funding.

In June, Heinrich introduced legislation to support the development of next-generation, PFAS-free protective gear to better protect firefighters from the dangers of their work.

In May, Heinrich criticized the Trump Administration’s cuts to the Forest Service workforce and its plans to reorganize federal firefighting efforts during wildfire season. He warned that losing staff who support incident command teams and wildfire response undermines the nation’s ability to prepare for and fight fires.

In February, Heinrich urged U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI) Secretary Doug Burgum to halt efforts to create the Department’s new U.S. Wildland Fire Service (USWFS), citing potential life-or-death consequences that could come as a result of decoupling wildfire management from land management agencies, and emphasizing a number of concerns related to recent reductions in staffing, combined with improperly severing wildfire management from land stewardship.

In February, Heinrich pressed Associate Chief of the U.S. Forest Service Christopher French about the impact of workforce cuts on wildfire preparedness and asked whether federal firefighters are paid enough. Heinrich pointedly asked French if firefighters were being paid enough; French acknowledged that they are not, citing longer fire seasons and growing demands on firefighters and their families.

Last December, Heinrich led his colleagues in demanding answers from the Forest Service about staffing cuts that had left the agency approximately 38% behind on hazardous fuels reduction work compared with recent years, warning that the decline posed serious risks to public safety and wildfire prevention.

Last September, Heinrich cosponsored the Honoring Our Fallen Heroes Act, bipartisan legislation that will expand health care coverage and benefits for first responders who become permanently disabled from service-related cancers and the families of those who pass away from these cancers.

Last August, Heinrich secured $1.1 million for Rio Arriba County to purchase radios and repeater towers for Rio Arriba County Volunteer Fire Departments to facilitate communications when firefighters are on duty.

Last July, Heinrich sent a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Secretary Brooke Rollins and DOI Secretary Doug Burgum following reports that staff reductions have required the deployment of fire personnel to fill administrative gaps, leaving fire crews understaffed and overwhelmed. In the letter, Heinrich urged the Departments of Agriculture and the Interior to provide adequate resources and support to wildland firefighters. .

In June of 2025, Heinrich’s Aerial Firefighting Enhancement Act of 2025, legislation to strengthen the aerial wildfire suppression fleet and better combat the year-round threat of catastrophic wildfire, was signed into law after passing the U.S. Senate in April.

In September 2023, Heinrich cosponsored the bipartisan Wildland Firefighter Paycheck Protection Act, legislation to permanently increase wildland firefighter pay and establish incident response premium pay to account for the 24/7 nature of the work.

In June 2022, Heinrich helped secure a temporary pay increase for the wildland firefighter workforce, funded by $600 million from the Infrastructure Law. He led calls for the administration to implement the pay increase, which ultimately raised federal wildland firefighter pay by up to $20,000 or 50% of base salary, whichever was less.

In May 2022, Heinrich secured over $15 million to improve wildfire response capabilities at Kirtland Air Force Base to upgrade facilities to allow the use of Very Large Air Tankers (VLATs) to fight wildfires throughout the state and region.

title: Hickenlooper Questions Trump’s Space Academy Announcement
text:
Hickenlooper: “Trump’s proposed plan is duplicative, costly, and unserious.”

OURAY – Today, U.S. Senator John Hickenlooper raised questions about President Trump’s new plan to create a U.S. Space Academy. President Trump announced plans to establish the academy earlier today at the Johnson Space Center in Houston, TX.

“President Trump’s proposed plan is duplicative, costly, and unserious.

Establishing a dedicated service academy for space may sound good on paper, but our nation already has an exceptional institution that trains tomorrow’s Space Force leaders: it’s called the U.S. Air Force Academy.

To duplicate that effort at a time when our national deficit is soaring, is reckless and makes a dire situation even worse.

Colorado Springs is already the epicenter of our national security and space efforts. This unnecessary proposal is yet another example of the president seeking to distract from his illegal war in Iran and the economic pain it has caused everyday Americans.”

Hickenlooper has consistently fought to protect Colorado’s role as the backbone of the nation’s space defense architecture. He denounced the Trump administration’s irresponsible and wasteful decision to move U.S. Space Command from Colorado to Alabama and joined a statement with the entire Colorado congressional delegation rebuking the relocation.

title: Hoeven Working to Advance $75 Million in Key Infrastructure for Bismarck, Lincoln & Other ND Communities
text:
BISMARCK, N.D. – As part of a roundtable with Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Region 8 Acting Regional Administrator Katherine Fox today, Senator John Hoeven outlined his efforts to advance $75 million in key infrastructure projects for Bismarck, Lincoln and other North Dakota communities. The projects support priorities such as flood control, disaster mitigation and recovery, with Hoeven working to:

Move the South Bismarck Flood Control Project forward.

In 2023, FEMA selected the City of Bismarck to receive $50 million in Flood Mitigation Assistance (FMA) funding to improve flood protection in South Bismarck.

Of this amount, FEMA has provided $7.3 million for Phase 1 preconstruction work, and the city plans to seek authorization this fall for $42.7 million in Phase 2 construction funding so construction can begin in 2027.

Once completed, the project is expected to remove approximately 1,000 structures from the floodplain under updated flood insurance maps, reducing the burden of flood insurance for impacted residents.

Support the University of Mary’s $9.1 million wastewater improvement project.

The university is seeking FEMA Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC) grant funding to replace its outdated lagoon facilities and restore the land currently used for septic lagoons.

Hoeven previously made the case to FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton for supporting the project, which has passed initial eligibility and is now undergoing review at FEMA headquarters.

Advance BRIC grants for communities across North Dakota. This includes:

A $7.76 million wastewater system regionalization project in Lincoln.

A $7 million water intake project in Washburn.

A $1.9 million wastewater lagoon project in Fessenden, which was officially awarded this week.

The senator expects the federal funding for these projects to be awarded beginning in September 2026 through next spring.

Ensure North Dakota communities have the federal support needed to recover from disasters.

Hoeven and roundtable participants discussed North Dakota’s request for a presidential major disaster declaration following severe storms, straight-line winds and tornadoes that impacted western and central North Dakota in June.

The senator also heard from state and county leaders regarding issues from previous major disaster declarations impacting residents and communities in Stutsman and Walsh counties.

“We appreciate Acting Regional Administrator Fox and her team being in North Dakota, as well as her ongoing efforts with us to advance $75 million in key infrastructure projects for the Bismarck area and communities across our state,” said Hoeven. “We’re working to advance BRIC-funded infrastructure projects in Fessenden, Lincoln and Washburn, as well as the University of Mary’s wastewater improvement project. We also need to keep the South Bismarck Flood Control Project moving forward so construction can begin next year, providing better flood protection while minimizing the burden of flood insurance on residents. At the same time, we continue working to ensure North Dakota communities have the federal support they need before, during and after disasters.”

-###-

title: Husted views storm damage in Reynoldsburg, meets with working families in Cincinnati
text:
“These conversations reinforce my priority as I serve in the U.S. Senate—to make sure Ohio families have more opportunities to save, spend and invest in the priorities that matter most to them.”

COLUMBUS – Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) today visited Reynoldsburg to receive an update on storm damage and recovery efforts before traveling to Cincinnati to host a roundtable with working Ohioans from southwestern Ohio to discuss ways to make life more affordable.

“Today, I had the chance to again see firsthand how our communities are recovering from the storms we faced earlier this month. I requested expedited federal assistance because Ohio communities deserve the resources they need to recover and rebuild as quickly as possible. I also had the opportunity to hear directly from working Ohioans in Cincinnati about what we can do to make life more affordable. These conversations reinforce my priority as I serve in the U.S. Senate—to make sure Ohio families have more opportunities to save, spend and invest in the priorities that matter most to them,” said Husted.

The Reynoldsburg visit comes after Husted wrote a letter to Federal Emergency Management Agency Administrator Cameron Hamilton and U.S. Small Business Administration Administrator Kelly Loeffler requesting they begin conducting damage assessments in Ohio as soon as possible due to the repetitive and ongoing storm impacts.

At the roundtable, Husted met with academic, business, faith and community leaders to discuss his work in the Senate to make life more affordable for working families.

Husted supported the Working Families Tax Cuts Act to put more money back into the pockets of hardworking Ohioans by including:

No tax on tips: More than 6 million taxpayers have benefited, providing relief for service workers who depend on gratuity.

No tax on overtime: More than 25 million taxpayers have claimed the provision, giving essential workers—factory workers, linemen, police officers, nurses, and more—a new break on their hard-earned extra hours.

A permanent 20% tax deduction for small businesses: Delivering $4,600 in average relief to 8 million entrepreneurs.

Enhanced deductions for seniors: More than 30 million seniors have claimed the provision.

An increased child tax credit of $2,200: More than 34 million families have claimed the provision.

A partially refundable adoption tax credit of up to $5,000.

Prevented a tax hike that would have cost the average family of four earning $80,000 about $1,700 MORE in federal taxes.

Husted introduced the Upward Mobility Act in January. The bill seeks to reform federal public assistance programs, end the benefits cliff and incentivize career growth. A benefits cliff occurs when Americans receiving federal public assistance experience a significant or complete loss of federal resources after a small increase in income. Americans receiving benefits may earn a raise or work more hours, but instead of increasing their total earnings, they end up worse off because their federal assistance drops sharply.

He also worked to pass the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act. This package is the largest housing bill to move through Congress in at least a decade.

The package reflects years of bipartisan, bicameral work and incorporates priorities from the U.S. Senate, U.S. House of Representatives and White House into a unified package to address America’s housing affordability crisis. The legislation focuses on the root cause of rising housing costs by cutting red tape, unlocking housing supply, lowering costs for families, protecting taxpayers and preserving local control.

title: Senator Justice Visits Bluefield State University in Support of the HBCU Arts Act and IGNITE HBCU Excellence Act
text:
BLUEFIELD, WV – Today, Senator Jim Justice visited Bluefield State University to meet with students and deliver remarks on the HBCU Arts Act and the IGNITE HBCU Excellence Act.

“HBCUs have been educating leaders, opening doors, and creating opportunities for generations. Bluefield State has already shown it can turn federal investment into results. IGNITE gives us a way to do more of that, faster. Along with the HBCU Arts Act, we are doing everything in our power to make sure students at HBCUs have the tools they need to succeed. Building up West Virginia’s HBCUs isn’t a partisan issue — it’s an investment in our workforce and our future,” said Senator Jim Justice.

“The HBCU Arts Act and the IGNITE HBCU Excellence Act are meaningful investments in our students, our campus and our community. As Senator Justice said, the arts are our soul, and this legislation would help Bluefield State preserve that soul while expanding opportunity. We are grateful for his longstanding advocacy for Bluefield State and America’s HBCUs,” said Keith Olson, Director of Communications, Bluefield State University.

BACKGROUND:

Senator Justice introduced the HBCU Arts Act with Senator Alsobrooks this May.

The HBCU Arts Act would increase investments in HBCU arts education by amending Section 323 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 to include provisions supporting arts programs at HBCUs.

Senator Justice is a co-sponsor of the IGNITE HBCU Excellence Act.

The IGNITE HBCU Excellence Act authorizes major federal investments in the infrastructure, technology, and research capacity of Historically Black Colleges and Universities.

title: Kaine, Colleagues Call for Senate Hearing on DOD’s Mismanagement of Illegal War in Iran and Its Effect on Servicemembers
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Tim Kaine (D-VA), the Ranking Member of the Senate Armed Services (SASC) Subcommittee on Seapower, joined a group of his colleagues in urging SASC Chairman Roger Wicker (R-MS) to hold a hearing with U.S. Department of Defense (DOD) leadership to investigate the Trump-Vance Administration’s failure to support servicemembers carrying out indefinite extended deployments in President Donald Trump’s foolish and illegal war in Iran.

In their letter, the senators emphasized how the Administration’s inability to end the conflict has taken a widespread physical, emotional, and mental toll on troops deployed to the region, even beyond the incidents reported aboard USS Abraham Lincoln, with dwindling supplies and deteriorating conditions taking hold aboard numerous ships and in numerous bases in the Middle East.

“The toll this unauthorized, disastrous war is taking on our troops is unconscionable,” wrote the senators. “Troops are suffering because of this Administration’s inability to end this war or make the environment safe enough for our servicemembers to be delivered the food, medication or supplies they need.”

“Military families and the American people deserve answers about when our heroes will come home and how DoD plans to restore military readiness that has been drained by this war. Supply shortages and unjustified extended deployments also have a real impact on our ability to recruit and retain our servicemembers – why would anyone sign up to fight when they fear they will be exploited and left without supplies, recourse, or support? Not only do we owe our troops the bare minimum respect and support they deserve, but it is a recruitment and retention imperative,” the senators continued.

“The stakes couldn’t be higher. The longer this Administration fails to articulate a plan to end this disastrous war, the longer our brave servicemembers will pay the price,” the senators concluded.

Along with Kaine, the letter is co-signed by Senators Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Angus King (I-ME), Mazie K. Hirono (D-HI), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Gary Peters (D-MI), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), and Elissa Slotkin (D-MI).

Full text of the senators’ letter is available here and below.

Dear Chairman Wicker:

We request that you convene a public Armed Services Committee hearing with Department of Defense (DoD) leadership regarding the poor planning and mismanagement of extended deployments to support Iran operations and the impact on our troops. Recent reports of sailors suffering from severe mental health issues amid deteriorating conditions on the USS Abraham Lincoln have only added to a disturbing pattern of failures to adequately plan and support our troops, who have been away from their families indefinitely as the Iran War drags on.

On August 11, Military Times reported that multiple sailors on board the USS Abraham Lincoln currently supporting Iran operations attempted to jump overboard, a heartbreaking decision in effort to escape the mental health toll of an extended deployment that was planned to end in May but is now at 9 months and counting. Horrifying messages from military families described other poor conditions onboard the Lincoln, including food rationing, rotten meals, shortages of supplies like water and soap, overflowing toilets, broken facilities and disrupted mail delivery. It took nine months for the Navy to relieve the Lincoln with the USS George Washington, after conditions had reached such severity that military families directly confronted the Acting Secretary of the Navy. This has revealed the real impact of unplanned deployment extensions on our ability to maintain and logistically support our ships in a contested environment.

This is not the first time during this war that we have seen the consequences of extended deployments onboard an aircraft carrier or even other ships. Sailors on the USS Ford experienced hundreds of broken toilets and significant damage from a non-combat fire that injured multiple sailors and affected 100 sleeping berths and forced it to redirect to Greece for emergency repair. After this emergency repair, the Ford was again sent back to the Red Sea to support Iran operations – eventually completing 11 months of deployment, even though the Navy tries to limit deployments to seven months. Military families of servicemembers on board the multiple ships as part of the Carrier Strike Groups (CSGs) in the region have reported emotional and financial strain from the unplanned extensions, struggling to balance work and childcare and caught in limbo with disrupted plans every time orders are extended.

Both the Lincoln and the Ford Carrier Strike Groups (CSGs) were redirected from their original missions to support President Trump’s illegal wars of choice. The Lincoln originally deployed in November to conduct routine patrols in the Indo-Pacific, but was redirected to the Middle East in January to support the start of the Iran operations. The Ford ultimately served a whopping 11 months at sea – redirected three times from an original mission to support deterrence in Europe, to operations in the Caribbean Sea and against Venezuela, to Iran operations. This Administration has failed to explain why it has insisted on stretching our sailors in this way without adequate planning – let alone for unauthorized wars of choice.

The strain on our troops is not confined to the Navy. In fact, our offices and press have heard story after story of Soldiers and Airmen, including National Guardsmen and Reservists, seeing their deployments extended with uncertainty about when they will be relieved by other units and can return home to their families. Bases in the Middle East originally designed to support a specific footprint have been stretched to support a much larger scale of units now stationed there – and conditions are deteriorating as too many people meet too little space and supplies.

The toll this illegal, disastrous war is taking on our troops is unconscionable. Troops are suffering because of this Administration’s inability to end this war or make the environment safe enough for our servicemembers to be delivered the food, medication or supplies they need.

All these developments strongly indicate a systemic failure of planning and adaptation by the Secretary of Defense and senior DoD leaders. It is appalling that in month seven of the Iran War, DoD still continues to fail to anticipate and plan for the second-order consequences of the President’s choices to continue this war with no end.

Military families and the American people deserve answers about when our heroes will come home and how DoD plans to restore military readiness that has been drained by this war. Supply shortages and unjustified extended deployments also have a real impact on our ability to recruit and retain our servicemembers – why would anyone sign up to fight when they fear they will be exploited and left without supplies, recourse or support? Not only do we owe our troops the bare minimum respect and support they deserve, but it is a recruitment and retention imperative.

The stakes couldn’t be higher. The longer this Administration fails to articulate a plan to end this disastrous war, the longer our brave servicemembers will pay the price.

We request a public hearing to help Congress and the public better understand how we got here and how the Department will ensure it never happens again. We call on the Department to explain to Congress, military families and the American people how it assesses and justifies the readiness impacts of these extended deployments, how it plans for relief rotations and what accounts for the systemic failures to provide troops with the support they need to do the mission the President has illegally asked of them. Importantly, the Department must justify and detail exactly how it plans to sustain our troops in this war indefinitely -- as the President’s negotiations continue to fail.

As Members of this Committee, we take seriously our responsibility to make sure the U.S. military is properly led, well-resourced, supported and able to conduct its missions. We believe it is critical that we conduct public oversight to ensure that whenever we ask the military to answer the Nation’s call, we will have their backs – not leave them stranded with no support. For these reasons, we urge the Committee to convene a hearing at the earliest opportunity to examine these issues directly with DoD leaders.
