title: Fulcher Signs On to Bill Protecting Idahoans’ Privacy
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Congressman Russ Fulcher (Idaho-01) released the following statement after co-sponsoring H.R. 9716, the Protecting Rights in Video and Equipment Acquired Discovery (PRIVACY) Act.

“I’m proud to sign on to this legislation to protect the privacy rights of Idahoans from increasingly intrusive surveillance data collection and to prohibit the widespread deployment of such surveillance tools with federal dollars,” said Congressman Fulcher. “It’s simple: if the federal government wants to access state and local systems’ data on citizens, they need to get a warrant.”

Specifically, the legislation safeguards the privacy of Americans by requiring federal law enforcement agencies to obtain a warrant from a Federal judge before accessing, receiving, querying, or otherwise obtaining surveillance data collected by state and local systems, such as:

Automated license plate readers (ALPRs);

Cameras that capture images of a vehicle’s occupants;

Long-range microphones;

Electronic fingerprint detection technology;

Any substantially similar technology determined appropriate by the Attorney General.

Bill Background

The PRIVACY Act:

Creates a list of intrusive technologies and requires federal law enforcement to obtain a warrant before accessing or querying data from those systems.

Limits the retention of data obtained under a warrant to 30 days, unless the data constitutes evidence in a prosecution or a court grants a limited extension.

Prohibits the use of federal funds to purchase or install such intrusive technologies, with limited exceptions.

title: Garbarino Brings Treasury Official, Long Island Business Leaders Together to Discuss Trump Accounts
text:
Bay Shore, NY — Last week, Congressman Andrew Garbarino brought together U.S. Department of the Treasury Assistant Secretary for Financial Institutions Luke Pettit, local small business owners, and chamber and business leaders for a roundtable discussion on Trump Accounts and how Long Island employers can take advantage of the new program.

Trump Accounts were established as part of the Working Families Tax Cut and provide a new tax-advantaged way for families to begin building long-term savings for their children. Eligible U.S. citizen children born between January 1, 2025, and December 31, 2028, may receive a one-time $1,000 contribution from the U.S. Treasury.

Beginning this year, employers can also contribute up to $2,500 annually to a Trump Account for an employee or an employee’s dependent, giving businesses a new option to invest in their employees and their families.

“Trump Accounts are a great way to help families start saving for their kids early and give them a head start for the future,” said Congressman Garbarino. “I was glad to welcome Assistant Secretary Pettit to Long Island and bring him together with local business leaders to talk about how this new program can benefit their employees and their families. I appreciate him coming out and everyone who joined us for the discussion.”

“Trump Accounts give families a revolutionary way of saving and investing for their children from day one,” said Luke Pettit, Assistant Secretary for Financial Institutions at the U.S. Department of the Treasury. “With the ability to contribute directly to employees and their childrens’ accounts, employers can play an important role in helping working families build long-term financial security. I appreciate Congressman Garbarino for convening Long Island’s small business leaders to help ensure as many employers and families as possible can take advantage of Trump Accounts, and for helping ensure they have the information they need to take advantage of this important new benefit.”

During the roundtable, Pettit provided local employers with an overview of Trump Accounts and how businesses can establish qualifying contribution programs. Local business leaders also had the opportunity to ask questions and provide feedback directly to Treasury.

The tax law that created Trump Accounts also included several priorities Garbarino supported to provide relief to Long Island families, including raising the State and Local Tax deduction cap to $40,000, providing a new deduction for seniors, establishing deductions for qualified tip and overtime income, and increasing the Child Tax Credit.

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer, Co-Chair of the Bipartisan Intelligence Committee 9/11 Review Task Force, Releases Report Marking 25th Anniversary of September 11th Attacks
text:
ABOVE: Gottheimer Visits Shanksville to Announce Report Marking 25th Anniversary of September 11th Attacks.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), Co-Chair of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence’s (HPSCI) bipartisan 9/11 Review Task Force, joined Committee Chairman Rick Crawford (AR-1), Ranking Member Jim Himes (CT-4), and Task Force Co-Chair Elise Stefanik (NY-21) to release the Committee’s report reviewing the federal government’s implementation of the 9/11 Commission’s recommendations, 25 years after the September 11th terrorist attacks.

Watch Gottheimer’s remarks here.

Over the past year, the bipartisan Review Task Force held hearings and briefings examining how the Intelligence Community carried out the reforms recommended in the original 2004 9/11 Commission Report — including the creation of the National Counterterrorism Center (NCTC) and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), which coordinates the nation’s intelligence agencies. The Task Force found that while many of the Commission’s reforms have made the country safer, dangerous gaps remain, and the threats facing the United States have grown far more complex, from great power competition with China and Russia to cyberattacks, foreign influence campaigns on social media, and the rise of artificial intelligence.

Based on its findings, the Task Force’s report offers 20 new bipartisan recommendations to close those gaps and prepare the intelligence community for the threats of the next 25 years — while continuing to protect Americans’ privacy and civil liberties.

“This morning, we had the heart-wrenching experience of visiting the Flight 93 Memorial and hearing from the first responders and family members of the heroes of Flight 93 – the brave forty men and women who put the lives of other Americans, and of our country, ahead of their own on the morning of September 11th,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), Co-Chair of the House Intelligence Committee’s 9/11 Review Task Force. “The fight against terror isn’t static – our adversaries and their weapons of war are always evolving, and we must evolve too. That is why, after the last year of work, we are proud to release our bipartisan twenty-five-year review of the original 9/11 Commission Report, and I’m proud to have led this effort with my colleague Representative Elise Stefanik.”

The Committee’s report reviews the 9/11 Commission’s original recommendations related to the Intelligence Community — including the creation of the NCTC and ODNI, along with reforms to congressional oversight and bolstering information sharing. The report also examines threats that did not exist in 2004, including great power competition with China and Russia, cyberattacks, foreign influence campaigns, economic espionage, drones, and the rise of artificial intelligence.

The report’s 20 bipartisan recommendations call on the nation’s intelligence agencies to operate as a single team by sharing information faster, training their people across agencies, and adopting new tools like artificial intelligence and open-source intelligence to keep pace with modern threats. They also aim to strengthen defenses against foreign spying and deepen partnerships with state, local, and private-sector partners to protect our communities. Twenty-five years after September 11th, the message of the report is simple: America must keep evolving to stay ahead of its enemies.

The full report is available here.

title: House Passes Congressman Hamadeh’s Kayleigh’s Law Bill to Protect Victims of Dangerous Crimes from Their Abusers
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Abraham Hamadeh (AZ-08) is grateful to his colleagues for their votes today in support of his legislation, known as Kayleigh’s Law, which protects victims of dangerous crimes from their abusers.

Congressman Hamadeh introduced Kayleigh’s Law in order to deliver stronger, lifelong protection to survivors of federal sex crimes and violent felonies by requiring courts to issue permanent no-contact injunctions against convicted offenders.

The goal of this legislation is to eliminate the "legal tug-of-war" where survivors must repeatedly face their attackers in court to maintain basic safety protections. Having passed at the state level in both Arizona and Wisconsin, this legislation, named after Kayleigh Kozak, a young mother from Arizona who was victimized as a child, prohibits all forms of direct or indirect contact with the victim for the rest of the guilty predator's life. The prohibition will remain in effect even after prison, probation, or supervised release ends.

“I want to thank my colleagues for their votes today. As I said on the floor today, Kayleigh’s Law started in Arizona. It works. In its first year alone, more than a thousand survivors in our state secured lifetime protection from the people who hurt them. H.R. 8481 would give every American victim of a federal sex crime or violent felony that same shield. This bill is simple. When a predator is convicted, federal courts must issue a lifelong no-contact injunction. Not until probation ends. Not until some judge decides the offender has “moved on.” For life. Victims should never again have to fill out another form, sit across from their abuser, or look over their shoulder because the sentence ran out and the system shrugged.”

“I have sat across from victims,” continued Congressman Hamadeh, a former prosecutor. “I know how vulnerable they are. I know how determined their predators are. And I know how often modern courts fail them, how they treat lifetime safety like an afterthought and force survivors back into a legal tug-of-war just to stay free of the person who hurt them. Kayleigh lived that failure. She should not have had to. Healing cannot begin if the abuser can show up again the day after release. Justice is not complete if the victim still lives in fear. Arizona already closed that gap. It is time the federal government did the same, so no American, no matter which state they live in, is left unprotected after a federal conviction.”

title: Congressman Pat Harrigan Co-Leads Bipartisan Bill to Track Self-Improving AI
text:
Contact: Lexi Kranich (814) 380-4408

WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, Congressman Pat Harrigan (NC-10) joined Congressman George Whitesides (D-CA-27) in introducing the bipartisan Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act, legislation to help the federal government better understand how quickly the most advanced AI systems are evolving, particularly their ability to conduct research and contribute to the development of new AI systems with limited human involvement.

“AI is moving incredibly fast, and we need a clear picture of what the most advanced systems can actually do,” said Congressman Harrigan. “As AI begins taking on more of the work involved in developing the next generation of AI, the pace of progress could accelerate dramatically. This bill makes sure we can track those developments without putting new mandates on American companies or getting in the way of innovation.”

The Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to monitor trends in the ability of advanced AI systems to conduct or assist with AI research and development. It also ensures that when frontier AI companies voluntarily partner with NIST on model evaluations, those agreements include sharing relevant metrics and estimates about how much AI is being used in their internal research and development, including work conducted without human review.

The legislation creates no new regulatory mandates and keeps participation with NIST voluntary. Congressman Harrigan will continue working to keep the United States at the forefront of artificial intelligence while ensuring policymakers have the information necessary to understand where this technology is headed and what it means for American innovation and national security.

title: House Passes Hinson Bill to Combat China’s Trade Crimes, Protect American Workers
text:
Washington, D.C. – Tonight, Congresswoman Ashley Hinson's (IA-02) bipartisan bill, the Protecting American Industry and Labor from International Trade Crimes Act, passed the House unanimously.

"China has spent decades finding ways to undermine American workers and our economy. My bill will finally give the DOJ real tools to stop these blatant violations and ensure penalties are meaningfully enforced. Today’s bipartisan passage is a huge win for American workers and domestic manufacturing — let’s make it the law of the land ASAP." — Congresswoman Ashley Hinson

“Today’s overwhelming bipartisan House passage of the PAIL Act is an important victory for American workers and manufacturers who have been forced to compete against companies based in the PRC that violate U.S. trade laws. Tariff evasion, illegal transshipment, forced-labor violations, and other trade crimes hurt American workers and undermine our industries. Our bipartisan bill gives the Justice Department dedicated resources and expertise to investigate and prosecute these crimes and hold repeat offenders accountable. The Senate should pass the PAIL Act without delay and send it to the President’s desk.” — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi

"This bipartisan legislation will arm the Department of Justice with the tools to stop trade crimes often perpetrated by China-backed companies. These crimes devastate American manufacturing, and they are a threat to the prosperity of every single American. Thanks to Congresswoman Hinson for her partnership and leadership on this legislation to fight back and protect American workers, and to our colleagues for their support today. Stopping China’s trade crimes and predatory trade practices is essential to the future of our country." — Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party Chairman John Moolenaar

Hinson’s bill would:

Establish a dedicated structure within the DOJ’s Criminal Division to investigate and prosecute trade-related crimes.

Strengthen coordination and training among federal, state, and local law enforcement.

Support expanded investigations and prosecutions and allow for parallel criminal and civil enforcement actions.

Require the Attorney General to report annually to Congress on DOJ’s efforts to combat trade crimes.

The legislation is strongly supported by various organizations, including: American Iron and Steel Institute, Coalition for a Prosperous America, American Medical Manufacturers Association, Alliance for American Manufacturing, Forging Industry Association, National Council of Textile Organizations, United Steelworkers, AFL-CIO, North American Die Casting Association, American Shrimp Processors Association, Southern Shrimp Alliance, American Mold Builders Association, Campaign for Uyghurs, America First Policy Institute, Kitchen Cabinet Manufacturers Association, Steel Manufacturers Association, Alliance for Trade EnforcementNOW, Committee on Pipe and Tube Imports, United States Oil Country Tubular Goods Manufacturers Association, EverRest US, Cold Finished Steel Bar Institute, American Wire Producers Association, and the Charlotte Pipe and Foundry Company.

title: Kaptur, Dingell, Lead Colleagues In Letter Urging President to Recognize Importance of the US-Canada Relationship
text:
Toledo, OH – Today, Democratic Co-Chairs of the bipartisan Congressional Great Lakes Task Force Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09) and Congresswoman Debbie Dingell (MI-06) led 86 of their House colleagues in urging President Trump to change his Administration’s diplomatic approach with Canada and recognize the importance of the US-Canada relationship. The effort follows further fraying in the two country’s relations amid President Trump’s escalating and chaotic use of trade barriers against Canada. In a letter to President Trump, the lawmakers specifically highlighted the risk to the American economy should the President continue to use demeaning rhetoric and implement damaging policies against Canada.

“Your Administration’s escalating and chaotic use of trade barriers against Canada is putting this relationship at serious risk. Recent tariffs, continued threats of additional trade restrictions, and increasingly adversarial rhetoric are creating uncertainty for businesses, workers, farmers, and consumers on both sides of the border. American exports to Canada declined in 2025, while Canadian exports to the United States also fell substantially following the implementation of US tariffs. Additionally, Canadian businesses are increasingly looking to diversify their supply chains and markets, which should concern your Administration,” the lawmakers wrote.

The lawmakers went on to describe the shared economic interests between the US and Canada and the risks a worsening relationship would have on the American people, especially for those across America's Heartland and in the Great Lakes region.

“Our economic relationship is too important to put at risk. Our manufacturers, farmers, producers, small businesses, and consumers depend upon Canada, as Canadian businesses and workers depend upon access to the United States. Materials, parts, and components routinely cross the border as part of shared North American supply chains. Disrupting these relationships increases costs for American businesses and consumers, undermines our competitiveness, and puts good-paying American jobs at risk. For example, the North American automotive industry relies on a highly integrated supply chain in which parts and materials can cross the US-Canada border multiple times before a vehicle reaches a customer. Similar integration exists across energy, agriculture, steel, aluminum, critical minerals, and manufacturing,” the lawmakers continued.

A full copy of the letter can be found by clicking here, or reading below:

Dear Mr. President:

This letter is to urge your Administration to change its diplomatic approach with our closest ally, Canada, and recognize the importance of the United States-Canada relationship.

Canada is not an adversary. Canada is a close friend, neighbor, ally, and economic partner whose security and prosperity is deeply intertwined with the United States. As you know, our countries share the longest international border in the world, generations of family and cultural ties, and deeply integrated economies and supply chains. We have stood together through war and peace and decades of cooperation. Our relationship is one of the world’s most enduring partnerships, built by generations of Americans and Canadians who work together, raise families, conduct business, travel, and share communities and culture.

Your Administration’s escalating and chaotic use of trade barriers against Canada is putting this relationship at serious risk. Recent tariffs, continued threats of additional trade restrictions, and increasingly adversarial rhetoric are creating uncertainty for businesses, workers, farmers, and consumers on both sides of the border. American exports to Canada declined in 2025, while Canadian exports to the United States also fell substantially following the implementation of US tariffs Additionally, Canadian businesses are increasingly looking to diversify their supply chains and markets, which should concern your Administration.

Our economic relationship is too important to put at risk. Our manufacturers, farmers, producers, small businesses, and consumers depend upon Canada, as Canadian businesses and workers depend upon access to the United States. Materials, parts, and components routinely cross the border as part of shared North American supply chains. Disrupting these relationships increases costs for American businesses and consumers, undermines our competitiveness, and puts good-paying American jobs at risk. For example, the North American automotive industry relies on a highly integrated supply chain in which parts and materials can cross the US-Canada border multiple times before a vehicle reaches a customer. Similar integration exists across energy, agriculture, steel, aluminum, critical minerals, and manufacturing.

To strengthen production and supply chains across North America, we must work with our American and Canadian partners. If our shared goal is to reduce dependence on China and other bad actors, treating Canada increasingly like an adversary is both counterproductive and dangerous. We should instead deepen economic cooperation with allies like Canada to increase domestic production and ensure critical goods and resources come from trusted partners.

We support fair and reciprocal trade and addressing legitimate trade barriers that disadvantage American workers and businesses. However, disagreements between close allies should be resolved through good-faith negotiations and established trade mechanisms, not through erratic trade policy, threats, and public disputes. Canada has already taken steps toward retaliation, demonstrating the real risk that continued escalation will harm American workers, businesses, farmers, and consumers and weaken the broader North American economy.

Our relationship with Canada also extends far beyond trade. We share vital defense and national security interests, energy resources, the Great Lakes, environmental responsibilities, agricultural markets, tourism, and millions of personal and economic ties across our border. We work together every day to protect North America, respond to emergencies, manage shared resources, and keep our communities safe. At a time of serious global economic and security challenges, we should be strengthening this partnership and the ties that make both countries safer, more prosperous, and more competitive.

We urge your Administration to treat Canada as the close ally, friend, neighbor, and economic partner that it is, and to resolve our differences through diplomacy while preserving and strengthening the relationship generations of Americans and Canadians have built. Just as a strong and prosperous United States is in Canada’s interest, a strong and prosperous Canada is also in America’s interest.

Thank you.

title: Congressman Kean and Commerce Secretary Lutnick Visit Magna-Power Electronics
text:
(August 31, 2026) RARITAN TOWNSHIP, NJ – Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) and Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick recently visited Magna-Power Electronics in Flemington.

Founded in 1981 by Ira Pitel, Magna-Power Electronics has deep roots in New Jersey. Today, all of its engineering and manufacturing operations are based at its Flemington facility, where they maintain vertically integrated, in-house production of high-power direct current power processing systems. Magna-Power maintains tight control over quality, cost, and lead times while serving national labs, industry, and universities worldwide.

“New Jersey is home to cutting-edge manufacturers like Magna Power that are proving American-made technology can compete with anyone in the world,” said Congressman Kean. “I am working to strengthen that advantage by supporting our manufacturers, growing well-paying jobs, and making sure the next generation of innovation is developed and built right here in America. Bringing Secretary Lutnick to Hunterdon County was an opportunity to showcase the incredible work being done in our district and reinforce my commitment to making New Jersey a leader in American manufacturing.”

“We chose the hard road forty-five years ago: make it yourself, in America,” said Magna-Power CEO Adam Pitel. “Today that decision is our biggest advantage. Vertical integration means our lead times, our quality, and our intellectual property stay in New Jersey. We were honored to show Secretary Lutnick and Congressman Kean what high-technology manufacturing looks like in New Jersey. They saw new machinery, growing headcount, and a backlog of American-made programmable DC power supplies. Good policy gave us room to invest, and we took it: new machinery, new hires, and a bigger R&D program, all right here.”

“Magna-Power is a great example of the innovation and advanced manufacturing happening right here in Hunterdon County,” said Hunterdon County Commissioner Director John E. Lanza. “Their continued growth and creation of highly skilled jobs demonstrate that world-class American manufacturing can thrive right here in Hunterdon County.”

“It was a privilege to join Congressman Kean and U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick for a tour of Magna Power here in Raritan Township. Visits like this provide an important opportunity to showcase the strength, innovation and skilled workforce that make Hunterdon County such an important part of New Jersey’s business community,” said Hunterdon County Chamber of Commerce President Christopher J. Phelan. “Bringing federal, state, and local leaders together with our business community is essential to understanding the opportunities and challenges facing employers today. We look forward to continuing to advocate for policies that strengthen our economy, support American manufacturing, and help Hunterdon County businesses compete and grow.”

“Having Secretary Lutnick on the floor at Magna-Power, with Congressman Tom Kean Jr., asking questions and hearing directly about the challenges manufacturers face, was incredibly valuable,” said New Jersey Manufacturing Extension Program, Inc. CEO Peter Connolly. “Magna-Power in particular is a great example of what American manufacturing can accomplish, with a supply chain that is exclusively Made in the USA. Congressman Kean has consistently supported NJMEP and the manufacturers in his district, and we appreciate him including us in this opportunity to engage directly with the Secretary. As the leader of the Department of Commerce, which oversees the MEP National Network, Secretary Lutnick’s willingness to listen and learn firsthand from manufacturers is especially important as we work together to strengthen manufacturing here in New Jersey and across the country.”

“It was great to see Congressman Tom Kean Jr. and U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick visit Magna Power Electronics in Raritan Township and see firsthand the incredible work being done right here in our community,” said Raritan Township Committeeman Scott Sipos. “Magna Power is truly a gem in Raritan Township. This family run New Jersey business is a great example of American innovation, manufacturing, and ingenuity while providing quality jobs right here in our community. This is what Made in America looks like, and we are proud to have it right here in Raritan Township.”

title: Keeping the Promise: Kennedy Urges Passage of Social Security 2100 Act
text:
Standing with Faith Leaders, Community Members, Elected Officials, Kennedy Calls on Congress to Expand Benefits, Protect Seniors from Trump-era Cuts, and Make the Wealthy Pay Their Fair Share

Social Security is Currently Projected to Begin Depletion in 2032, Decreasing Benefits

LACKAWANNA, N.Y. – Standing alongside faith leaders, community members, and elected officials at Mount Olive Missionary Baptist Church in Lackawanna, Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26) called on Congress to pass the Social Security 2100 Act, legislation that would expand Social Security benefits and strengthen the program’s long-term viability by making the wealthiest pay their fair share. The bill, introduced by Rep. John Larson (CT-01), would also reverse the Trump Administration cuts to Social Security Administration (SSA) staff and services. Critically, the legislation would eliminate the $184,500 payroll tax cap so higher income earners contribute above the current wage limit, ensuring the long-term solvency of the Social Security Trust Fund. According to the SSA, the Trust Fund is projected to be depleted by 2032, at which point benefits will be scaled back for retirees.1

“Social Security is not a handout – it’s a promise that is earned over a lifetime of work, and Western New York seniors have a right to expect that promise be kept, not broken,” said Congressman Kennedy. “For too long, future generations have stared down a weakened Social Security system that they won’t be able to depend on in their retirement years. The Social Security 2100 Act changes that. It makes the wealthy pay their fair share, boosts benefits, and undoes the damage the Trump Administration has inflicted on a critical agency that seniors rely on. I won’t stop fighting to save Social Security and ensure that future generations can receive the benefits they have paid into and have rightfully earned.”

“Social Security is a promise we must keep to our Americans who earned it,” said Erie County Legislator Lawrence Dupre. “The Social Security 2100 Act strengthens the program, asks the wealthiest Americans to finally pay their fair share, and protects the personal data of millions of Americans. Congress must act now to safeguard Social Security for current and future generations.”

“Social Security is more than a federal program—it is a promise our country made to generations of Americans who worked hard, paid into the system and now depend on it. Here in Lackawanna, many of our residents rely on Social Security for financial security and peace of mind. Therefore, we stand with Congressman Kennedy in his efforts to build support for the Social Security 2100 Act. This proposed bill keeps the promise to those who earned these benefits, protects current Social Security recipients, and ensures the program remains available for future generations,” said Mayor Annette Iafallo, City of Lackawanna.

“Social Security isn’t a handout—it’s an earned benefit and a promise to generations of working people who paid into it with every paycheck. After a lifetime of hard work, no retiree should have to wonder whether that promise will be there for them. The Social Security 2100 Act strengthens Social Security for today’s retirees and future generations while asking the wealthiest Americans to pay their fair share. UAW Region 9 is proud to stand with Congressman Tim Kennedy in protecting the retirement security working people have earned and deserve,” said Wence Valentin III, UAW Region 9 Political/Retiree Director.

“The Social Security 2100 Act recognizes that seniors face rising health care costs. By using an inflation measure that better reflects seniors’ medical expenses—and protecting Medicaid eligibility when Social Security benefits increase—we can strengthen retirement security without forcing vulnerable Americans to choose between financial stability and access to health care,” said Dr. Lavonne Ansari.

In addition to eliminating the payroll tax cap, the Social Security 2100 Act would add a 12.4% tax on investment income for those making more than $400,000 a year, adopt an improved cost-of-living adjustment that better reflects seniors’ true expenses, and strengthen the minimum benefit so no one who works a full career retires into poverty. The bill would also reverse the Trump Administration’s staffing cuts at the SSA, block future field office closures, and prevent DOGE-like entities and political appointees from accessing sensitive data systems.

title: Kennedy, Dingell, Morelle Introduce Hands Off Our Great Lakes Act to Block Trump’s Attempt to Rename Lake Ontario
text:
As Trump’s Tariffs Drive up Costs, Lawmakers Push Back on President’s Move to Turn Lake Ontario into a Distraction From His Affordability Crisis

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26), alongside Congresswoman Debbie Dingell (MI-06) and Congressman Joe Morelle (NY-25), introduced the Hands Off Our Great Lakes Act, legislation to block President Trump’s attempt to rename Lake Ontario as “Lake America” and prohibit the future renaming of any of the five Great Lakes.

“Americans are struggling to afford groceries, housing, and everyday essentials, and yet this President chooses to pick petty fights with our closest ally,” said Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26). “This unserious, unacceptable attempt to rename the historic, shared Lake Ontario adds insult to injury as Trump’s tariffs drive up costs, making an already difficult situation worse. Our families, workers, and businesses need an administration focused on lowering costs and strengthening our economy, not distractions. Renaming a lake won’t put food on the table, lower anyone’s bills, or create a single job. It is a pathetic attempt to distract from an affordability crisis that this President has failed to fix.”

“The Great Lakes are a shared treasure that generations of Americans and Canadians have worked together to protect. Canada is not our enemy. It is our neighbor, our ally, and one of Michigan’s most important economic partners. It is a friendship that no stroke of a pen should be able to erase,” said Congresswoman Dingell (MI-06). “By preventing President Trump from trying to divide us with distracting public relations stunts, maybe then he will turn his attention to his reckless trade war that is raising costs and threatening American workers.”

“Lake Ontario is Lake Ontario. President Trump can play games with a map all he wants, but I’m not going to stand by while he wastes the authority and resources of the federal government doing it,” said Congressman Joe Morelle (NY-25). “This is ridiculous, it’s embarrassing, and it’s exactly the kind of unserious distraction Americans are tired of.”

The legislation would prohibit the President, Secretary of the Interior, and federal officials acting under presidential authority from altering or renaming the official geographic names of Lake Superior, Lake Michigan, Lake Huron, Lake Erie, or Lake Ontario. The bill would also nullify Trump’s Executive Order renaming Lake Ontario, issued on August 27, 2026, and prohibits federal funds from being used to implement it or any substantially similar action.

title: $1.32 Million in Crisis Counseling Support
text: Last week, we got word that $1,320,108 in federal funding was awarded to the CNMI through FEMA’s Crisis Counseling Program following Super Typhoon Sinlaku. This funding will support crisis counseling and mental health services for individuals and communities in Saipan, Tinian, Rota as we continue to recovery from the storm. Recovery is about rebuilding homes and infrastructure, but also about supporting the well-being of our people. I’m grateful for the federal resources that will help ensure our communities have access to the support they need as we move forward together.

title: $236K to HSEM for Sinlaku Emergency Protective Measures
text: The CNMI Office of Homeland Security and Emergency Management (HSEM) has been awarded $236,605 in FEMA funding to support emergency protective measures following Super Typhoon Sinlaku. The funding is intended to help address immediate threats to public health, safety, and property resulting from the storm. These emergency measures are a critical part of the Commonwealth’s disaster response and recovery efforts, helping protect our communities while longer-term repairs and recovery projects move forward. I appreciate HSEM’s continued work to coordinate the CNMI’s disaster response and ensure our communities have the resources needed to recover from Sinlaku.

title: $300K Awarded to DPW for Sinlaku Recovery
text: Very happy to recognize the CNMI Department of Public Works for receiving $323,646.50 in FEMA funding to repair and replace fencing and other components damaged by Super Typhoon Sinlaku. DPW has been working across the Commonwealth to restore public infrastructure and help our communities recover from the storm. I appreciate their continued hard work and commitment to rebuilding the CNMI, and I will continue working to ensure our local agencies have the federal support they need to get the job done.

title: $948K to CPA for Sinlaku Emergency Protective Measures
text: I’m pleased to recognize the Commonwealth Ports Authority (CPA) for receiving $948,387.24 in FEMA funding to carry out emergency protective measures following Super Typhoon Sinlaku. The funding will support actions necessary to address immediate threats to public health, safety, and property caused by the storm. These emergency measures are an important part of protecting our critical port infrastructure and helping ensure that the CNMI’s ports can continue serving our communities during recovery. Our ports are essential to bringing in food, supplies, fuel, and other necessities, especially following a disaster. I appreciate CPA’s continued work to protect these vital assets and keep our Commonwealth connected.

title: Expanding Access to Financial Services
text: Over the last month, I have been looking into why CNMI residents continue to encounter problems opening brokerage accounts, obtaining credit cards, and accessing other financial services that are readily available elsewhere in the United States. One issue that keeps coming up is something very basic. We do not have standardized street addresses throughout much of the Commonwealth. I wrote to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent asking for help determining whether federal customer identification requirements are contributing to these problems and, if so, how existing alternatives for communities without conventional street addresses can be applied to the CNMI. People living in the Northern Mariana Islands should not be shut out of financial services simply because our addressing system looks different. I am looking forward to Treasury's response and, hopefully, identifying a practical path forward.

title: Joeten-Kiyu Public Library gets $208K for Sinlaku Repairs
text: The Joeten-Kiyu Public Library has been awarded $208,870.69 in FEMA funding to repair or replace heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems damaged by Super Typhoon Sinlaku. The award covers 90% of the eligible project costs and will help restore essential building systems at the library. These repairs will help ensure the facility remains a safe, functional, and comfortable space for the community. Libraries are so central to life in any community, and investments like this are an important part of rebuilding our public facilities and ensuring that community institutions remain operational and accessible.

title: A Lasting Connection Between the CNMI and Japan
text:
A recent Vision Times article highlights what many of us in the CNMI know well: the enduring legacy of Japanese craftsmanship can still be seen throughout our islands. From century-old homes, shrines, and structures to the former Japanese Hospital in Garapan, now home to the Northern Mariana Islands Museum of History and Culture, these structures remain tangible reminders of the deep historical connection between the CNMI and Japan. Our relationship with Japan is rooted in far more than geography. It is a connection shaped by history, family, culture, and enduring people-to-people ties. As we look towards the future of the CNMI-Japan relationship, I believe we should continue building on these connections while preserving and learning from the history that brought us together over a century ago.

title: Nogis sisters in DC
text: Janine Nogis-Rosario from our Saipan District Office and her sisters, Apollonia Borja and Natashia Tomokane, visited their congressional office in Washington on Wednesday. While Janine was in town for congressional management training, Apollonia and Natashia took the opportunity to tour the U.S. Capitol and explore some of Washington, D.C.’s other attractions. It was wonderful having them stop by. Thank you for visiting, ladies!

title: Pushing Back on New Postal Duty Requirements
text: Last week, I submitted formal comments to the U.S. Postal Service on new duty collection requirements affecting packages mailed from the CNMI and other U.S. territories to the rest of the United States. The new process could require CNMI residents to navigate customs classifications, determine whether goods qualify for exemptions, and pay duties and fees through a third-party customs broker before USPS will accept certain packages. We have already seen CNMI-made products incorrectly assigned tariff charges through the system being used to implement these changes. My comments ask USPS to suspend implementation in the territories until it can properly account for the CNMI's unique treatment under the Covenant. That includes ensuring qualifying CNMI-made goods receive the duty-free treatment they are entitled to, determining how duties and fees collected from CNMI residents will be returned to the Commonwealth Treasury as required by the Covenant, and creating a process that does not leave individual residents responsible for navigating complicated customs rules just to mail a package. The CNMI has a unique legal relationship with the United States, and federal policies have to account for it. I will continue working to make sure the rights and protections provided to our people under the Covenant are recognized when these policies are put into practice.

title: What Does the New Remittance Tax Mean for the CNMI?
text: I also wrote to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent last week seeking clarification on the new 1 percent excise tax on certain remittance transfers enacted under H.R. 1, The One Big Beautiful Bill Act. The CNMI operates under a mirror tax system, so we need clarity on whether this new federal tax applies to remittances originating from the Commonwealth and, if it does, how those revenues will be treated. CNMI residents send, on average, $82 million in remittances each year. If the tax applies and those revenues are required to be covered back to the Commonwealth, that could mean hundreds of thousands of dollars in additional annual revenue for the CNMI government. At a time when our government is facing exceptionally tight budgets, we need to make sure every dollar legally owed to the Commonwealth makes its way home. I have asked Treasury for clarification so we know exactly how this new provision applies to the CNMI and what revenues our government may be entitled to receive.

title: Krishnamoorthi Blasts FDA Decision to Authorize New JUUL2 Vaping Products
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), co-chair of the bipartisan Congressional Caucus to End Youth Vaping, today criticized the Food and Drug Administration’s decision to authorize the marketing of the JUUL2 e-cigarette device along with tobacco- and menthol-flavored pods.

The FDA announced Friday that it had authorized the three JUUL2 products after determining that their potential benefits for adults who completely switch from cigarettes outweighed the risks, including the potential appeal of the menthol-flavored product to young people. The decision follows the agency’s authorization of additional JUUL tobacco- and menthol-flavored products in July 2025.

“The FDA should be cracking down on products that hook kids on nicotine, not authorizing JUUL2, which even the agency acknowledges could appeal to young people. JUUL helped fuel a youth vaping epidemic, and that record cannot be ignored. At a time when the Trump Administration is weakening efforts to combat youth vaping, we should be strengthening protections for kids, not giving the tobacco industry new opportunities to addict them. I will keep fighting to hold Big Tobacco accountable and protect the next generation from nicotine addiction.”

title: U.S. House Unanimously Passes Bipartisan Krishnamoorthi Bill to Crack Down on CCP Trade Crimes
text:
WASHINGTON — The U.S. House of Representatives today unanimously passed the bipartisan Protecting American Industry and Labor from International Trade Crimes (PAIL) Act, legislation co-led by Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) to crack down on trade crimes that undercut American workers and manufacturers. The bill strengthens the Justice Department’s ability to investigate and prosecute tariff evasion, illegal transshipment, forced-labor violations, and other trade crimes.

“Today’s unanimous House passage of the PAIL Act is an important victory for American workers and manufacturers who have been forced to compete against companies based in the PRC that violate U.S. trade laws. Tariff evasion, illegal transshipment, forced-labor violations, and other trade crimes hurt American workers and undermine our industries. Our bipartisan bill gives the Justice Department dedicated resources and expertise to investigate and prosecute these crimes and hold repeat offenders accountable. The Senate should pass the PAIL Act without delay and send it to the President’s desk,” said Congressman Krishnamoorthi.

The PAIL Act would:

Establish a dedicated structure within the Justice Department’s Criminal Division to investigate and prosecute trade-related crimes;

Strengthen coordination and training among federal, state, and local law enforcement;

Support expanded investigations and prosecutions, including parallel criminal and civil enforcement actions; and

Require the Attorney General to report annually to Congress on the Justice Department’s efforts to combat trade crimes.

Krishnamoorthi co-led the bipartisan legislation with Congresswoman Ashley Hinson (R-IA), Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party Chairman John Moolenaar (R-MI), Congressman Ted Lieu (D-CA), and a broad bipartisan coalition of lawmakers.

“China has spent decades finding ways to undermine American workers and our economy. My bill will finally give the DOJ real tools to stop these blatant violations and ensure penalties are meaningfully enforced. Today’s bipartisan passage is a huge win for American workers and domestic manufacturing — let’s make it the law of the land ASAP,” said Congresswoman Hinson.

“This bipartisan legislation will arm the Department of Justice with the tools to stop trade crimes often perpetrated by China-backed companies. These crimes devastate American manufacturing, and they are a threat to the prosperity of every single American,” said Chairman Moolenaar.

The PAIL Act is supported by organizations representing American workers and manufacturers, including the United Steelworkers, AFL-CIO, American Iron and Steel Institute, Alliance for American Manufacturing, National Council of Textile Organizations, Steel Manufacturers Association, and Campaign for Uyghurs.

title: Congressman Langworthy Introduces American Quantum Competitiveness Act to Strengthen U.S. Leadership in Next Generation Technology
text:
Washington, D.C.—August 31st… Congressman Nick Langworthy today announced the introduction of the American Quantum Competitiveness Act, legislation designed to strengthen America’s position in the rapidly emerging quantum technology industry, protect critical domestic supply chains, and ensure the United States remains competitive with China and other foreign adversaries.

Quantum technology is poised to transform computing, communications, and sensing, with significant implications for both America’s economic competitiveness and national security. The legislation would establish the Department of Commerce as the federal lead for commercial quantum technology and develop a national strategy focused on manufacturing, investment, commercialization and trusted domestic supply chains.

In addition to its national and global implications, this legislation will play an important role in ensuring Western New York and the Southern Tier are at the forefront of this new frontier through its work with the I-90 tech corridor. New York’s 23rd Congressional District is poised to bring together world-class manufacturing, advanced technology, research institutions, and a highly skilled workforce.

“America cannot afford to wait until the next generation of technology has already been developed overseas before we decide we want to compete,” said Congressman Nick Langworthy. “The American Quantum Competitiveness Act is about getting ahead of the curve, strengthening our domestic supply chains and making sure the United States leads in quantum technology rather than becoming dependent on foreign adversaries. While this bill has broad national and global implications, it’s critical to our region as well, where we have the talent, manufacturing heritage, and research capabilities to be at the forefront of this next technological revolution.”

The legislation would:

Establish Commerce as the federal lead on commercial quantum technology, including manufacturing, deployment, investment and trusted supply chains.

Strengthen the domestic quantum ecosystem by identifying critical components, addressing barriers to investment and reducing supply chain risks and reliance on foreign adversaries.

Create a national quantum competitiveness strategy directing Commerce to coordinate with industry, researchers, federal agencies, states and trusted allies.

Support commercialization and domestic manufacturing, helping move quantum technologies from research and development into real-world applications.

Quantum technology will also create opportunities well beyond companies directly developing quantum systems. A robust domestic ecosystem will require critical suppliers in semiconductors, photonics, lasers, cryogenics, and other advanced technologies, creating new opportunities for American manufacturers and workers.

Congressman Langworthy has made strengthening the I-90 corridor a priority as part of a broader effort to position Western New York and the Southern Tier as a national hub for advanced manufacturing and emerging technologies. The American Quantum Competitiveness Act builds on that foundation by helping connect federally supported research with commercialization, investment, and domestic manufacturing.

The NY SMART I-Corridor Tech Hub, co-convened by the Buffalo Niagara Partnership, OneROC, and CenterState CEO, is strongly supportive of the legislation, saying, "A strategic, increased federal focus on innovation and commercialization for emerging quantum technologies supports the NY SMART I-Corridor's goals to help ensure our region and our country remain the global leader in this space. With our shared region's existing assets in the semiconductor and photonics industries, this legislation will deepen existing opportunities and create new ones to develop talent, technology, and domestic supply chains," said Regional Innovation Officer Dr. Joseph Stefko.

This legislation is also enthusiastically supported by the Quantum Industry Coalition, the leading voice of the U.S. quantum industry that includes major U.S. companies such as IBM, Microsoft and Google.

“The Quantum Industry Coalition supports the American Quantum Competitiveness Act, which will help strengthen U.S. commercial quantum policy, enhance the development of trusted, resilient quantum supply chains, and develop a national quantum competitiveness strategy. We appreciate Rep. Langworthy’s leadership in introducing this bill,” said Quantum Industry Coalition executive director Paul Stimers.

It is also supported by the state’s leading research institutions, including the Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), University of Rochester, University at Albany, University at Buffalo, Syracuse University, and Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (RPI), and by regional economic development organizations, including Greater Rochester Chamber of Commerce.

“Technology leadership is ultimately about more than winning a race for scientific breakthroughs,” Congressman Langworthy concluded. “It is about making sure those breakthroughs become American-made products, American companies and American jobs. We are perfectly positioned to take advantage of this enormous opportunity in Western New York and the Southern Tier, and I intend to make sure our region has a seat at the table.”

title: Lawler Demands CMS Reconsider 340B Payment Cuts to Safety Net Hospitals
text:
Washington, D.C. – 8/31/26… Today, Congressman Mike Lawler (NY-17) sent a letter urging Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Mehmet Oz to reconsider a proposed change to Medicare reimbursement for the 340B Drug Pricing Program, warning that the policy could put additional financial pressure on safety net hospitals and threaten access to care for vulnerable patients in New York.

Additional signers of the letter include Nick LaLota (NY-01), Andrew Garbarino (NY-02), Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11), Nick Langworthy (NY-23), Claudia Tenney (NY-24).

In a letter submitted Monday as part of the public comment process for CMS’s Calendar Year 2027 Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) and Ambulatory Surgical Center (ASC) Proposed Rule, Rep. Lawler and his New York colleagues raised concerns over the agency’s proposal to reduce Medicare reimbursement for certain 340B acquired drugs from the current rate of Average Sales Price (ASP) plus 6% to ASP minus 33.4%. This represents a nearly 40% reduction in payments to safety net hospitals.

CMS estimates the proposal would reduce Medicare spending on 340B-acquired drugs by approximately $4.55 billion in its first year. And while the agency plans to redistribute this money through increased payments for non-drug outpatient services, this approach will disproportionately affect the safety net hospitals that the 340B program is intended to support, cutting a critical source of funding for communities in need.

In New York, the proposed change is estimated to result in approximately $900 million in annual reductions to hospitals participating in the 340B program.

“Safety net hospitals that utilize 340B already operate under extremely difficult financial circumstances, and many don’t have the resources to compensate for the reductions in revenue on 340B drug payments. Our principal concern is that this steep payment change could ultimately impact their ability to maintain services and jeopardize access to care for patients,” wrote the lawmakers.

The full letter can be found HERE.

Congressman Lawler is one of the most bipartisan members of Congress and represents New York's 17th Congressional District, which is just north of New York City and contains all or parts of Rockland, Putnam, Dutchess, and Westchester Counties. He was rated the most effective freshman lawmaker in the 118th Congress, 8th overall, surpassing dozens of committee chairs.

title: Rep. Mike Levin Honors Encinitas Residents Cheryl H. Dean, Esq. & Nick Dean, Ph.D. as His August 2026 Co-Constituents of the Month
text:
Cheryl H. Dean, Esq & Nick Dean, Ph.D.

Encinitas, CA—Today, Rep. Mike Levin (CA-49) named Encinitas residents Cheryl H. Dean, Esq., and Nick Dean, Ph.D. as his August 2026 Co-Constituents of the Month for their work as documentary filmmakers bringing global attention to ocean conservation and the plight of the endangered North Atlantic right whale.

Nick and Cheryl are the co-founders of Spindrift Images, LLC, an independent documentary production company that has spent over a decade telling stories about the ocean, its wildlife, and the people whose lives are tied to it.[1] The BBC and the United Nations World Wildlife Day Film Showcase are among the outlets that have spotlighted their work, a reflection of the international audience their films have built.

Nick spent 25 years as a research scientist before turning to filmmaking in 2010. Cheryl has spent her career translating complex research for public audiences and has led San Diego's underwater photography community, serving as president of the San Diego UnderSea Film Exhibition since 2015.

In 2025, the couple founded the Spindrift Images Foundation to lead conservation campaigns protecting the North Atlantic right whale, a species clinging to survival with fewer than 400 animals left worldwide. Their latest film, The Right Whale: Tales of Resilience and Hope, is the product of six years of production and travel spanning four continents, capturing footage everywhere from remote whale nurseries in the far south to some of the world's most heavily trafficked commercial waters.

Through their combined expertise in science and storytelling, Nick and Cheryl Dean have turned their filmmaking into a platform for conservation advocacy, helping inspire public action to protect marine ecosystems around the world.

See below for Rep. Levin's statement recognizing Nick and Cheryl Dean in the Congressional Record:

“Mr. Speaker, it is my honor to recognize Nick and Cheryl Dean, residents of Encinitas, as my Co-Constituents of the Month for August 2026.

“For more than a decade, Nick and Cheryl have used the power of film to bring the wonders of the ocean, and the dangers facing it, into homes around the world. Their dedication took them across four continents over six years to document the North Atlantic right whale, a species with fewer than 400 animals left on Earth.

“Nick's background as a research scientist and Cheryl's gift for communicating science to the public have made them uniquely effective storytellers and advocates. Their foundation's work protecting the right whale and defending critical conservation laws reflects a deep commitment to our planet's future.

“I urge my colleagues to join me in celebrating Nick and Cheryl Dean for their extraordinary contributions to ocean conservation and environmental storytelling.”

title: Congressman Harris Celebrates Passage of H.R. 4499, His Sixth Bill to Pass the House
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Mark Harris (NC-08) celebrated the passage of H.R. 4499, legislation that makes technical corrections to federal statutes and updates references to provisions reclassified to Title 34 of the United States Code, which covers Crime Control and Law Enforcement. The bipartisan legislation is Congressman Harris’s sixth bill to pass the U.S. House of Representatives.

Rep. Harris’s remarks on H.R. 4499:

“I rise today in support of H.R. 4499, a bill that makes important technical corrections to our federal statutes and ensures that references in the United States Code remain accurate.

“The Office of the Law Revision Counsel, or OLRC, is responsible for preparing and publishing the United States Code, which organizes the federal laws enacted by Congress. In 2017, the OLRC moved various laws to Title 34 of the United States Code, which pertains to Crime Control and Law Enforcement. This was done to ensure that our nation’s laws are properly organized.

“H.R. 4499 updates references to these laws throughout the titles of the Code affected by their move to Title 34. While these may be technical changes, they are important for maintaining an accurate and accessible United States Code. I am grateful that Congress is taking action through my bill, as well as the other legislation being considered by the House today, to ensure that our laws accurately reflect the current Code.

“I would like to thank the Office of the Law Revision Counsel for all the work it does, as well as those on the Judiciary Committee who helped address these much-needed changes. I urge all my colleagues to support this important legislation.”

title: Congressman Menefee Highlights Work Across TX-18 During August Work Period
text:
HOUSTON, TX — As the August Work Period comes to a close, Congressman Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) released the following statement highlighting his work and meetings with constituents, community leaders, health care providers, and small businesses across Texas’s 18th Congressional District.

“As a first-term Member of Congress, it was a privilege to spend my first August Work Period back home in Houston, focused on what matters most to my work in Congress, the people of Texas’s 18th Congressional District,” said Congressman Menefee. “Being home gave me the opportunity to hear directly from the people I represent about what they are experiencing, what they need from their federal government, and what I can take back to Washington to fight for.”

Throughout the August Work Period, Congressman Menefee traveled across TX-18 to meet with constituents and hear directly about the issues affecting Houston families. He attended more than 10 back-to-school events across the district, including events at Texas Southern University, Marshall Middle Academy of Fine Arts and the Fifth Ward Multi-Service Center. These events provided students with free school supplies and other resources ahead of the new school year, while giving Congressman Menefee an opportunity to speak with parents, caregivers, educators, and community leaders about the rising costs families face when preparing their children to return to school.

Congressman Menefee also visited health care providers across the district, including HOPE Clinic during National Health Center Week and Garden Oaks Dialysis Center. During the visits, he met with health care professionals and community leaders to discuss the rising cost of health care, barriers to accessing care, and the importance of protecting federal investments that help providers continue serving Houston families.

As part of his continued focus on lowering costs and supporting Houston’s economy, Congressman Menefee met with local small business owners, including Pour Decisions and Common Bond Bistro & Bakery. The Congressman heard directly from business owners about rising operating costs and other challenges facing local entrepreneurs and discussed ways he can better support small businesses and expand access to resources and capital.

Congressman Menefee also participated in several roundtables and community discussions throughout the district focused on affordability, environmental justice, and other issues affecting TX-18. These conversations allowed the Congressman to hear directly from residents about rising household costs and longstanding environmental concerns in Houston communities and will help inform his work when Congress returns to Washington.

Throughout the August Work Period, Congressman Menefee’s district staff continued assisting constituents with federal casework and helping them navigate federal agencies. During the busy summer travel season, the office worked to resolve passport delays and other time-sensitive issues, helping more dozens of constituents with passport cases alone.

Congressman Menefee also continued calling for transparency and accountability following the death of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo during an encounter with federal immigration officers in Houston earlier this summer. In addition to assisting constituents with immigration-related casework, Congressman Menefee supported legislative efforts to protect immigrant communities, including the No TSA Data for ICE Act. He also joined a letter to Department of Homeland Security and Immigration and Customs Enforcement leadership raising concerns about health and safety conditions in ICE detention centers and calling for greater accountability which would help to curb ICE’s lawlessness and ensure greater transparency and accountability from federal immigration authorities.

As the 119th Congress enters its final stretch, Congressman Menefee is more determined than ever to deliver results for TX-18. He is also preparing for what comes next, so when Democrats take back the House, they are ready on day one to hold the Trump administration and congressional Republicans accountable for corruption, policies that have driven up costs, and decisions that have failed working families.

title: Reps. Mfume, Bell, Strickland Lead 70+ Congresspeople in Efforts to Stop Navy from Renaming Ship Honoring War Hero to instead Honor Donald Trump
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Last week, Representatives Kweisi Mfume (D-MD-07), Wesley Bell (D-MO-01), Marilyn Strickland (D-WA-10), led over 70 of their Democratic House colleagues in an effort pressing Department of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao to keep the name of the USS Doris Miller as is.

The letter follows recent reporting that the U.S. Navy is considering renaming the USS Doris Miller in honor of President Trump. Doris Miller was a sailor aboard the USS West Virginia when Japan began its attack on Pearl Harbor who placed himself in harm's way to help save his fellow sailors.

“Renaming this ship after a sitting President would be unprecedented and break longstanding tradition,” wrote the Representatives. “Most importantly, this would diminish the recognition of one of our country’s greatest military heroes. It was during President Trump’s first term that the Navy announced CVN-81 would bear Doris Miller’s name. Reversing that decision now would be a significant step backward in honoring the courage and sacrifice of those who have served our country.”

News broke last week about the Navy potentially renaming its ship, CVN-81, to honor Trump. During the president’s first term, the Navy had announced that CVN-81 would bear Doris Miller’s name, making it the first aircraft carrier to be named for an African American, as well as the first named in honor of an enlisted sailor.

Doris ‘Dorie’ Miller was serving aboard the USS West Virginia on December 7, 1941, when Japan began its attack. At the time, Miller was a Mess Attendant Third Class, and after his station came under fire, he took control of an anti-aircraft gun and fired at incoming aircraft. Even as the ship sank, he kept fighting until he ran out of ammunition, and assisted his fellow wounded sailors to reach safety.

“Doris Miller’s story is one of extraordinary bravery, service, and pure patriotism,” the Representatives continued. “When he served, segregation restricted the roles available to Black sailors and servicemembers. Yet, when his country came under attack, Miller did not hesitate to put himself in harms’ way to defend his fellow sailors and his nation. This story embodies the finest traditions of the United States Armed Forces.”

“There has never been a time when we have named a warship after a sitting president. Changing course and now to satisfy a sitting President’s ego, especially one who dodged service to his country, would be shamefully wrong. We urge you to reject this plan and ensure that CVN-81 bears the name USS Doris Miller. Our Navy must continue honoring the courage of those that answered their country’s call to service,” the lawmakers concluded.

In addition to co-leading this letter, Congressman Mfume has long led the congressional effort to secure federal recognition for Doris Miller. On March 25, 2025, National Medal of Honor Day, he introduced a pair of bills to honor Miller's heroism at Pearl Harbor:

H.R. 2335, which authorizes the President to award Doris Miller the Medal of Honor posthumously for acts of valor while serving in the Navy during World War II. The bill has 12 cosponsors and was referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.

The Doris Miller Congressional Gold Medal Act (H.R. 2336), which would posthumously award Miller the Congressional Gold Medal, the highest civilian honor bestowed by Congress. If enacted, Miller's family would receive the medal and it would be displayed at the Smithsonian. The bill was referred to the Committees on Financial Services and House Administration.

In introducing the bills, Congressman Mfume continued the work of the late Congresswoman Eddie Bernice Johnson, who fought since 2001 to see Miller awarded the Medal of Honor. The Medal of Honor legislation is endorsed by the National Association for Black Veterans (NABVETs) and the Dorie Miller Medal of Honor Committee.

Congressman Mfume represents Maryland's Seventh Congressional District and serves as Ranking Member of the House Oversight Subcommittee on Government Operations.

The letter was signed by: Reps. Gabe Amo, Yassamin Ansari, Joyce Beatty, Julia Brownley, Nikki Budzinski, Salud Carbajal, André Carson, Troy Carter, Ed Case, Joaquin Castro, Gilbert Cisneros, Emanuel Cleaver, Steve Cohen, Herb Conaway, Joe Courtney, Jason Crow, Diana DeGette, Christopher Deluzio, Mark DeSaulnier, Debbie Dingell, Sarah Elfreth, Dwight Evans, Shomari Figures, John Garamendi, Daniel Goldman, Maggie Goodlander, Josh Gottheimer, Steven Horsford, Chrissy Houlahan, Glenn Ivey, Sara Jacobs, Jonathan Jackson, William Keating, Timothy Kennedy, Ro Khanna, Greg Landsman, Stephen Lynch, April McClain Delaney, Jennifer McClellan, Christian Menefee, Dave Min, Gwen Moore, Seth Moulton, Jerrold Nadler, Donald Norcross, Eleanor Norton, Frank Pallone, Scott Peters, Brittany Pettersen, Mike Quigley, Patrick Ryan, Bradley Schneider, Robert Scott, Terri Sewell, Adam Smith, Eric Sorensen, Suhas Subramanyam, Shri Thanedar, Bennie Thompson, Dina Titus, Jill Tokuda, Ritchie Torres, Derek Tran, Gabe Vasquez, Marc Veasey, Eugene Vindman, Debbie Wasserman Schultz, Maxine Waters, George Whitesides, Frederica Wilson.

title: CONGRESSMAN JOE MORELLE LEADS LEGISLATION TO STOP TRUMP FROM RENAMING LAKE ONTARIO
text:
(Washington, D.C.)—Today, Congressman Joe Morelle introduced the Hands Off Our Great Lakes Act, legislation to stop President Donald Trump’s attempt to rename Lake Ontario and protect the historic names of all five Great Lakes.

The legislation, co-led by Congresswoman Debbie Dingell (D, MI-06) and Congressman Tim Kennedy (D, NY-26), comes after President Trump issued an executive order on August 27 attempting to rename Lake Ontario as “Lake America.”

“Lake Ontario is Lake Ontario. No executive order, proclamation, or presidential temper tantrum is going to change that,” said Congressman Joe Morelle. “Families are worried about paying their bills. Businesses are looking for certainty. Communities like ours are asking Washington to focus on the challenges that actually affect people’s lives. And Donald Trump is spending his time trying to rename a lake.

“This is ridiculous, it’s embarrassing, and it’s exactly the kind of unserious distraction Americans are tired of. President Trump can play games with a map all he wants, but I’m not going to stand by while he wastes the authority and resources of the federal government doing it.

“Here in Rochester, we’ll keep calling it Lake Ontario. And in Congress, I’m working with my colleagues to make sure it stays that way.”

The Hands Off Our Great Lakes Act would prohibit the President, Secretary of the Interior, or any other federal official acting under presidential authority from changing the official geographic names of Lake Huron, Lake Ontario, Lake Michigan, Lake Erie, or Lake Superior.

The legislation would also specifically nullify Executive Order 14422, issued by President Trump on August 27, and prohibit the federal government from implementing or enforcing the order—or any substantially similar action. It would further prohibit federal funds from being used to carry out the attempted renaming.

“The Great Lakes are a shared treasure that generations of Americans and Canadians have worked together to protect. Canada is not our enemy. It is our neighbor, our ally, and one of Michigan’s most important economic partners. It is a friendship that no stroke of a pen should be able to erase,” said Congresswoman Dingell. “By preventing President Trump from trying to divide us with distracting public relations stunts, maybe then he will turn his attention to his reckless trade war that is raising costs and threatening American workers.”

“Americans are struggling to afford groceries, housing, and everyday essentials, and yet this President chooses to pick petty fights with our closest ally,” said Congressman Tim Kennedy. “This unserious, unacceptable attempt to rename the historic, shared Lake Ontario adds insult to injury as Trump’s tariffs drive up costs, making an already difficult situation worse. Our families, workers, and businesses need an administration focused on lowering costs and strengthening our economy, not distractions. Renaming a lake won’t put food on the table, lower anyone’s bills, or create a single job. It is a pathetic attempt to distract from an affordability crisis that this President has failed to fix.”

title: Griffith Fights for Big Stone Gap, Announces Return of Postal Office Mailboxes
text:
Thanks to Congressional and local action, the United States Postal Service (USPS) has returned mailboxes to the Town of Big Stone Gap.

Earlier this August, employees with the USPS forcefully removed mailboxes from the historic C. Bascom Slemp Federal Building in Big Stone Gap, Virginia. The building, once owned by the General Services Administration (GSA), is now controlled by the Town and is under consideration for historical preservation projects.

U.S. Congressman Morgan Griffith (R-VA) worked with local officials and received support from Virginia’s U.S. Senators Mark Warner (D-VA) and Tim Kaine (D-VA) to secure a solution. The USPS activity to remove and confiscate the mailboxes was discovered to be unauthorized.

Following news of the mailboxes’ return, Congressman Griffith issued the following statement:

“I am glad to help secure the return of the Big Stone Gap Postal Office mailboxes! These mailboxes rightfully belonged to Big Stone Gap in the first place.

“The C. Bascom Slemp Federal Building is a historic site for Southwest Virginia and Wise County communities. The mailboxes, with beautiful designs and popular features, are iconic to the building, and that is a major reason why Big Stone Gap officials are working hard to make the mailboxes a centerpiece in preservation-related activities.

“I appreciate Senators Kaine and Warner for their help to secure this outcome. As always, I will continue to promote the rich history of Southwest Virginia.”

Town Manager Stephen Lawson provided the following comment:

“The Town of Big Stone Gap would like to extend our sincere appreciation to Congressman Morgan Griffith and his entire office for their assistance in helping secure the return of the historic post office boxes that were mistakenly removed from the C. Bascom Slemp Federal Building.

“These post office boxes are much more than a piece of the building’s history. For generations, they served as the centerpiece of the lobby and represented an important part of the character and identity of this beautiful historic building. When they were removed, it truly felt as though the heartbeat had been ripped out of the jewel of our downtown.

“Thanks to the efforts of Congressman Griffith and his staff, these historic boxes are being returned where they belong. Their return represents an important step in preserving the history, character, and legacy of the C. Bascom Slemp Federal Building for generations to come.

“We are deeply grateful to Congressman Griffith and his office for recognizing the importance of this historic treasure and for their willingness to help our community. Their support and dedication to the people of Southwest Virginia are sincerely appreciated.”
